titre: Negative Effects of MBCT and CBASP in Difficult-To-Treat Depression [Analysis Code and Results]
resume: Analysis code and aggregated results for the Bayesian one-stage individual participant data network meta-analysis (IPD-NMA) of negative effects of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT), the Cognitive Behavioral Analysis System of Psychotherapy (CBASP), and control conditions in adults with difficult-to-treat depression. Protocol: Niemi, Michalak, Velana, Barnhofer & Harrer, BMJ Open 2026;16:e106362 (doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2025-106362) Registration: PROSPERO CRD42022332039 Network: 15 randomized trials, 2,644 participants (MBCT n = 367, CBASP n = 979, control n = 1,298). Control is the common reference node. Treatment effects are expressed as odds ratios (OR). Because all outcomes concern negative effects, OR < 1 indicates a lower risk under the first-named treatment. Data availability This repository contains no individual participant data. The harmonised IPD were provided by the original trial investigators under data-sharing agreements and cannot be redistributed. For the same reason, the multiply imputed datasets and posterior draws (derived/), which are participant-level or derived from participant-level data, are not included. All files in results/ and figures/ contain aggregated summaries. Requests for access to the IPD should be directed to the corresponding author and are subject to the original investigators' agreement. Contents run-all.R Master script: configuration and analysis pipeline R/ 00-setup.R Packages, paths, constants, priors, helper functions 01-prepare-data.R Read harmonised IPD, derive outcomes and moderators 02-descriptives.R Baseline table, network plot, transitivity plots, event counts 03-impute.R Multilevel multiple imputation (m = 20) and diagnostics nma-helpers.R JAGS data builder, posterior pooling, G-computation 04-fit-nma.R Main one-stage IPD-NMA, forest plots, ROPE 05-meta-regression.R Treatment x moderator interactions (17 moderators) 06-consistency.R Inconsistency model, node-splitting, direct meta-analyses 07-sensitivity.R Sensitivity analyses S1-S5 08-revisions.R Post-hoc analyses added during co-author review models/ JAGS model files ipd-nma-main.bug Main model ipd-nma-main-ncp.bug Non-centred reparameterisation (optional) ipd-nma-main-flat.bug Flat-prior variant (sensitivity analysis S1) ipd-nma-metareg.bug Participant-level treatment x moderator interaction ipd-nma-metareg-study.bug Study-level treatment x moderator interaction ipd-nma-inconsistency.bug Loop-inconsistency parameter results/ Aggregated results (CSV, TSV, XLSX) supplement-tables/ Formatted supplementary tables (DOCX) figures/ Figures (PDF) Reproducing the analyses Place the files in analysis/cbasp/ inside an R project. Paths are resolved using here::here("analysis", "cbasp"). Change BASE in R/00-setup.R if using a different directory structure. Add the harmonised IPD as analysis/cbasp/data/IPD_MBCT_CBASP_260813.sav. The waitlist sensitivity analysis in 08-revisions.R additionally reads the original Rief et al. (2018) trial file (data/tidy/rief2018/data.rda at the project root) to identify the waitlist arm. Run source("analysis/cbasp/run-all.R"). PRODUCTION = TRUE reproduces the reported settings; PRODUCTION = FALSE uses a faster development profile. The RUN.* switches allow individual stages to be re-run using cached objects in derived/. Per-imputation JAGS models are fitted in parallel across FIT.CORES cores. A full production run takes approximately one day on a desktop machine. Random seeds are specified in 00-setup.R (set.seed(20260828)) and in the imputation procedure (seed = parallelseed = 20260828). Software R 4.5.2 and JAGS 4.3.2, with the following R packages: haven 2.5.5 tidyverse 2.0.0 (dplyr 1.1.4, ggplot2 4.0.1) mice 3.19.0 miceadds 3.18.36 blme 1.0.7 future 1.69.0 parallelly 1.46.1 runjags 2.2.2.5 rjags 4.17 coda 0.19.4.1 netmeta 3.2.0 meta 8.2.1 metafor 4.8.0 ggridges 0.5.7 writexl 1.5.4 glue 1.8.0 here 1.0.2 systemfonts 1.3.1 Analysis overview Model. Participant-level Bernoulli likelihood with a logit link, study-specific intercepts, and random treatment contrasts. The Dias et al. (TSD-2) multi-arm correction was applied to the single three-arm trial (Michalak et al., 2015). Models were adjusted for baseline prognostic factors (age, sex, baseline PHQ-9, trauma history, and past antidepressant use), centred within studies. Priors. Cauchy(0, 2.5) for treatment contrasts, prognostic slopes, and interactions; Half-Normal(0, 0.5) for the heterogeneity SD (τ); and Normal(0, 2.5) for study intercepts (see protocol deviations below). MCMC. Four chains, 2,000 adaptation iterations, 5,000 burn-in iterations, and 5,000 sampling iterations (thinning = 2) per imputed dataset. Posterior draws were pooled across the 20 imputed datasets. Convergence was assessed using R-hat and effective sample sizes (results/nma-convergence.csv, results/revision-convergence.csv). Outcomes (PHQ-9 common metric; Wahl et al., 2014): Outcome Definition Detectable deterioration (primary) Increase of ≥6 points from baseline (post-treatment T1 and follow-up T2) Any deterioration Any increase from baseline (T1 and T2) Emergent suicidality Suicidality item ≥1 among participants without suicidality at baseline Worsening suicidality Increase of ≥1 point among participants with suicidality at baseline Dropout Missing post-treatment assessment (acceptability outcome) Missing data. Multilevel multiple imputation by chained equations (study as cluster; predictive mean matching for all imputed variables), with 20 imputed datasets and 10 iterations. Moderators. Seventeen participant-level moderators were entered one at a time as treatment x moderator interactions (cluster-centred) for any deterioration at post-treatment. Bayes factors (BF01; Savage-Dickey density ratio) quantify evidence for the absence of effect modification. A prior-scale sensitivity analysis was also conducted (08-revisions.R, R5). Practical equivalence. A region of practical equivalence (ROPE) of OR 0.80–1.25 was used post hoc to calculate posterior probabilities of practically meaningful benefit, practical equivalence, and practically meaningful harm. Consistency. Assessed using a Bayesian inconsistency model for the single closed loop, node-splitting, and pairwise direct meta-analyses. Sensitivity analyses (07-sensitivity.R): S1: Flat priors. S2: Worst-case missing-not-at-random assumption (missing outcomes coded as deterioration). S3: Exclusion of trials at high overall risk of bias (RoB 2; Foroughi et al., 2020). S4: Any-deterioration definition. S5: Two-stage frequentist NMA. Post-hoc analyses (08-revisions.R): R1: Ceiling effect of the ≥6-point deterioration criterion. R2: Study characteristics for the transitivity assessment. R3: Network meta-regression with comparator type (active vs. inactive control condition) as a study-level effect modifier, entered between studies and grand-mean centred. R4: Sensitivity analysis excluding the waitlist arm of Rief et al. (2018). R5: Prior-scale sensitivity of the moderator Bayes factors. Deviations from the protocol Study intercepts: Normal(0, 2.5) instead of Cauchy(0, 10). The heavy-tailed prior allowed baseline log-odds in studies with zero events to drift without bound and prevented convergence. Number of imputations: 20 instead of 50, owing to computational cost. Imputation of binary variables: Predictive mean matching instead of two-level logistic imputation, which produced implausible imputed event rates due to separation. Control conditions: Pooled into one node because a finer split would disconnect the network. Comparator type was examined post hoc (R3 and R4). ROPE, Bayes factors, and analyses in 08-revisions.R: Not pre-specified. titre: Surfing on waves
resume: The ability to recognize, understand, and manage emotions develops throughout life. When the development of these skills is disrupted, people may experience persistent difficulties in managing their emotions. These difficulties may also emerge or re-emerge during life transitions and with ageing. Emotional dysregulation is considered a core feature of personality disorders. However, relatively little is known about its treatment in older adults with personality disorders. This dissertation examines the applicability of Systems Training for Emotional Predictability and Problem Solving (STEPPS) for older adults with emotion management difficulties. STEPPS is a cognitive-behavioral treatment that includes psychoeducation and the acquisition and practice of emotion and behavior management skills. The patient’s social support network is involved to help maintain these skills. A systematic review of twenty studies showed that STEPPS is associated with reductions in borderline symptom severity, improvements in quality of life, decreases in depressive symptoms, and reductions in negative affectivity. Findings regarding impulsivity and suicidal behavior were mixed. No studies had examined STEPPS in older adults, highlighting the need to evaluate existing interventions in this population. A pilot study examined the feasibility of STEPPS in older adults with personality disorders. Results showed a significant reduction in borderline symptom severity and improvements in personality functioning, including identity integration and the capacity to manage emotions and impulses. However, adaptations appeared necessary to better meet the needs of older adults. A Delphi study with experts in psychological treatments for older adults identified possible adaptations. Experts recommended greater attention to later-life themes, such as physical limitations, experiences of loss, grief, and life review. They also advised using shorter sentences, a consistent session structure, session summaries, and examples and visual materials that reflect the experiences of older adults. Based on these recommendations, an adapted version of STEPPS for older adults (STEPPS-OA) was developed and evaluated. Results showed significant reductions in borderline symptom severity and psychological distress. Adaptive emotion management strategies and domains of personality functioning improved, while certain maladaptive personality traits, including negative affectivity and disinhibition, decreased. Most improvements occurred early in treatment, following psychoeducation and emotion management skills training, and were maintained throughout the program. The dissertation also highlights that emotion management difficulties can manifest as emotional under-control, such as impulsivity and intense emotional reactions, or emotional over-control, such as suppression and avoidance of emotions. Because over-control is often less visible, it may go unrecognized and inadequately treated. Clinical case examples illustrate how STEPPS-OA can address both forms. Overall, the findings suggest that STEPPS-OA is a promising treatment option for older adults with personality disorders and emotion management difficulties. However, randomized controlled trials and follow-up assessments are needed to establish its effectiveness and assess whether effects are maintained.

titre: A promising multi-azimuth EUV ellipsometry for high-precision metrology of 3D nanostructures
resume: For advanced semiconductor devices, the 3D shrink of gate-all-around (GAA) transistors poses significant challenges for high-precision optical critical dimension (OCD) metrology. Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) ellipsometry exhibits exceptional sensitivity to the structural parameters of GAA transistors. However, the practical realization of EUV ellipsometry is hindered by complex hardware requirements, including high-brightness broadband EUV sources and high-precision optical components. In this paper, we propose an efficient single-wavelength multi-azimuth EUV ellipsometry technique. At an optimal EUV wavelength, the reflected data from the 3D nanostructures can be acquired by multi-azimuth measurements, which can significantly mitigate parameter correlation. With a highly efficient bottom-up rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) method, combining Monte Carlo sampling with the Fisher information matrix (FIM), we compute Pearson correlation coefficients () for ten parameters of GAA transistors, including the thicknesses and the cavity etch depth of the Si and SiGe layers. The results show that, at an optimal wavelength and an incidence angle of 65°, the multi-azimuth data at 5° intervals over the 0°-90° range greatly mitigate the correlation coefficients, only two parameter pairs exceeding 0.75, and the maximum correlation coefficient only to be 0.81. With this multi-azimuth sampling scheme, the system achieves a favorable trade-off between sensitivity and low correlation of structural parameters. This method achieves an optimal trade-off between sensitivity and hardware feasibility, providing a promising pathway for metrology at sub-3 nm technology nodes.

titre: Microbiota-gut-brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Mechanistic Insights, Experimental and Clinical Evidence, and Therapeutic Perspectives
resume: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity, arising from an interplay of genetic vulnerability, immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal dysfunction, and neurobiological alterations. The bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota and the brain via neural, immune, endocrine, and microbial- metabolite pathways may contribute to ASD pathophysiology. We conducted a literature review by searching PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science, emphasizing studies published since 2022 and integrating mechanistic, experimental, and clinical evidence. Alterations in gut microbial ecology have been associated with impaired metabolite production, compromised intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalances. Findings from germ-free models, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and targeted microbiota modulation suggest that gut microorganisms can influence ASD-related behaviors. However, human studies are limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneous designs and are confounded by gastrointestinal symptoms, diet, and medication. It also remains uncertain whether microbiota alterations are a cause or a consequence of ASD. Clinical studies of probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, dietary interventions, FMT, and emerging microbiome-engineering strategies suggest that these interventions may improve gastrointestinal symptoms and selected behavioral outcomes in certain populations. However, the results are inconsistent, and these interventions require further investigation. This review discusses the limitations of the current evidence and the opportunities and challenges for microbiome-based therapeutics. Future priorities include stratified clinical trials, standardized outcome measures, and longitudinal cohorts.

titre: Early Vaginal Reconstruction in Complex Anorectal Malformations: Rationale for an Individualized Approach
resume: Background Current trends in reconstructive surgery increasingly advocate delaying vaginal reconstruction until patients can participate in decision-making. While this approach may be appropriate for conditions such as Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome and isolated vaginal agenesis, its application to patients with complex anorectal malformations (ARM) requires careful consideration. Methods This narrative review discusses the anatomical, surgical, and psychosocial factors influencing the timing of vaginal reconstruction in patients with complex ARM. Drawing on contemporary surgical principles and extensive clinical experience with reconstruction, differences between ARM and other causes of vaginal atresia are examined, together with reconstructive options and emerging strategies to preserve future reproductive potential. Results Patients with complex ARM differ substantially from patients with isolated vaginal agenesis. They frequently present with associated urinary tract anomalies, neurogenic bladder, fecal incontinence as well as previous abdominal and perineal operations. In select patients, vaginal reconstruction performed during the initial repair offers important technical advantages, including optimal pelvic exposure before fibrosis develops, preservation of surgical options, and avoidance of later operations in a hostile pelvis. The choice of reconstructive tissue should be individualized according to anatomy and anticipated bowel function. Native vaginal tissue remains the preferred option whenever available; however, when replacement is necessary, the rectum provides the most favorable intestinal substitute in appropriately selected patients, followed by colon, whereas small bowel should generally be reserved for situations in which other options are unavailable. Conclusions Delayed vaginal reconstruction should not be considered the universal standard for patients with anorectal malformations. Surgical timing should be individualized according to anatomical complexity, predicted bowel function, future urological procedures, patient circumstances, and long-term quality-of-life considerations. Management within specialized multidisciplinary centers remains essential for optimizing both functional and reproductive outcomes.

titre: Planejamento tributário em uma empresa de pequeno porte do setor atacadista: comparação entre o Simples Nacional e o Lucro Presumido diante da transição da Reforma Tributária do Consumo
resume: O estudo comparou o Simples Nacional e o Lucro Presumido em uma empresa atacadista de pequeno porte de Cláudio, Minas Gerais, considerando a transição da Reforma Tributária do Consumo. O objetivo foi identificar o regime mais compatível com a realidade tributária, econômico-financeira, operacional e comercial da organização e os fatores a acompanhar entre 2026 e 2033. Trata-se de pesquisa aplicada, descritiva e de abordagem mista, com pesquisa bibliográfica, documental e estudo de caso, baseada nas demonstrações contábeis de 2024 e 2025. Como os dados fiscais complementares não foram disponibilizados, a análise tributária combinou registros contábeis, parâmetros legais e cenários hipotéticos. Os resultados indicaram crescimento da receita e do lucro, liquidez elevada e aumento do endividamento. Na parcela calculável, os tributos federais sobre a receita somaram 2,60% e 2,78% no Simples Nacional, em cálculo ilustrativo, contra 5,93% no Lucro Presumido. Este só compensaria se folha de pagamento e ICMS líquido somassem menos de 4,70% (2024) e 5,42% (2025) da receita nas vendas com ICMS normal. Conclui-se que as evidências favorecem a permanência no Simples Nacional, pela apuração unificada e pela menor carga federal sobre a receita, mas a confirmação financeira depende da folha e do ICMS líquido da empresa. A reavaliação deve considerar o sublimite, o perfil de clientes e fornecedores e as regras do IBS e da CBS.

titre: SIMPLE, PERO NO DEL TODO: UN ANÁLISIS REFLEXIVO DE LOS EFECTOS DE LA REFORMA TRIBUTARIA BRASILEÑA EN LAS MICRO Y PEQUEÑAS EMPRESAS
resume: Este artículo analiza hasta qué punto la Reforma del Impuesto al Consumo preserva materialmente el trato preferencial de las empresas que optan por el Régimen Tributario Nacional Simplificado (SNS), considerando sus efectos en los créditos fiscales, la competitividad y los costos de cumplimiento. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa, exploratoria y descriptiva, basada en el análisis documental, una revisión bibliográfica semisistemática y la reflexión teórica. El estudio abarcó la legislación y los actos oficiales vigentes hasta el 12 de agosto de 2026, incluyendo la Enmienda Constitucional N° 132/2023, las Leyes Complementarias N° 214/2025 y N° 227/2026, y las Resoluciones N° 186, N° 190 y N° 191/2026 de la Comisión Nacional de Valores (CGSN). Los resultados demuestran que el Simples Nacional se conservó formalmente, pero ahora coexiste con la opción de recaudar el IBS (Impuesto sobre Bienes y Servicios) y el CBS (Contribución sobre Bienes y Servicios) dentro del DAS (Documento Simplificado de Recaudación de Impuestos) o a través del régimen regular. La primera alternativa mantiene una mayor simplicidad, pero restringe el uso y la transferencia de créditos; la segunda puede favorecer la competitividad en las relaciones B2B, aunque aumenta la carga administrativa y no garantiza la reducción de impuestos. Se concluye que ninguna alternativa es universalmente superior, ya que los efectos dependen de la actividad, la estructura de costos, las adquisiciones acreditables y el perfil del cliente. La conservación material del trato preferencial dependerá de la proporcionalidad de los costos de cumplimiento y de la capacidad de las pequeñas empresas para seguir siendo competitivas en el nuevo sistema.

titre: Ahara Parinamakara Bhava and the Gut–Brain Axis: An Ayurveda Informed Physiological Interpretation
resume: Ahara occupies a central position in Ayurvedic physiology because nourishment depends not simply on eating but on the subsequent transformation and assimilation of food. Ahara Parinamakara Bhava describes six functional conditions associated with this process: Usma, Vayu, Kleda, Sneha, Kala and Samayoga. A recent conceptual review interprets these factors as a coordinated framework for digestion, metabolic regulation, mucosal protection and physiological balance rather than as isolated anatomical entities. Another Ayurvedic account describes the fate of food as a sequence of digestion, metabolism and assimilation, thereby presenting food transformation as an active biological process. Contemporary gut–brain research provides a complementary physiological context. The gastrointestinal tract communicates bidirectionally with the brain through the enteric nervous system (ENS), vagal pathways, endocrine cells, immune mediators and microbial metabolites. Enteroendocrine cells can detect microbial products and relay information to enteric and vagal sensory neurons, while enterochromaffin cells respond to microbiota-derived metabolites and participate in serotonergic signalling. This review therefore examines Ahara Parinamakara Bhava as a functional Ayurvedic framework for discussing digestion and post-digestive signalling. The proposed relationships are conceptual and hypothesis-generating; they do not establish one-to-one equivalence between Ayurvedic categories and modern cells, nerves or molecules.

fiche.verdict: Revue conceptuelle parallèle entre les concepts d'Ayurveda (Ahara Parinamakara Bhava) et la physiologie moderne de l'axe intestin-cerveau.
resultats_cles: Parallèle entre 6 conditions ayurvédiques de digestion et les signaux entéro-endocriniens/sérotoninergiques.

fiche.conclusion: Ahara Parinamakara Bhava offre un cadre conceptuel ayurvédique compatible avec la recherche moderne sur l'axe intestin-cerveau.

titre: "Agni in Ayurveda: An Integrative Review of Digestive Physiology, Metabolism, Gut-Brain Axis, and Gut Microbiota"
resume: Agni is a fundamental physiological principle in Ayurveda that governs digestion, metabolism, transformation, and utilisation of nutrients within the body. It plays a vital role in sustaining life by facilitating the digestion, absorption, assimilation, and biotransformation of ingested food into forms suitable for tissue nourishment. Classical Ayurvedic texts frequently associate Agni with Pitta due to their shared role in metabolic activities; however, scholarly discussions indicate that the two concepts, although closely related, are not entirely identical. Owing to its presence at the cellular and tissue levels, Agni is considered ubiquitous throughout the body. For functional understanding, Ayurveda categorises Agni into thirteen types: one Jatharagni, five Bhutagnis, and seven Dhatvagnis. Among these, Jatharagni is regarded as the principal digestive force responsible for the initial transformation of food into nutritive essence (Rasa) and waste products (Mala). The Bhutagnis further process the elemental components of food, while the Dhatvagnis regulate tissue-specific metabolic activities and support the nourishment of the seven Dhatus. Through these sequential transformations, useful metabolites (Prasada) are generated for body maintenance and growth, whereas waste products (Kitta) are formed for elimination. Thus, Agni represents the central mechanism underlying digestion, tissue metabolism, nutritional homeostasis, and overall health in Ayurvedic physiology.

fiche.verdict: Revue intégrative décrivant le concept ayurvédique d'Agni et ses 13 subdivisions métaboliques et digestives.
resultats_cles: Description théorique d'Agni comme principe régulateur de la digestion et du métabolisme.
Classification en 13 types (Jatharagni principal, Bhutagnis, Dhatvagnis).
Distingue le rôle d'Agni de celui de Pitta dans la physiologie ayurvédique.
fiche.conclusion: Agni constitue le mécanisme central de la digestion et de l'homéostasie nutritionnelle selon la physiologie ayurvédique.

titre: Buccal acupuncture for postoperative gastrointestinal recovery after elective colorectal cancer surgery: A single-center randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND Postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction is common following colorectal cancer surgery and may delay postoperative recovery.Buccal acupuncture is a minimally invasive traditional Chinese medicine technique that may improve gastrointestinal function; however, its additional benefit within an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway remains uncertain.AIM To determine whether buccal acupuncture improves postoperative gastrointestinal recovery when added to an ERAS pathway.METHODS In this single-center prospective randomized controlled trial, 94 patients were randomized 1:1 to standard ERAS management (Group C) or ERAS plus buccal acupuncture (Group P), of whom 84 patients (42 per group) were included in the primary efficacy analysis.The primary outcome was time to first defecation.Secondary outcomes included time to first flatus, time to resumption of oral intake, intraoperative heart rate, postoperative pain scores, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) scores, postoperative recovery indicators, and adverse events. RESULTSCompared with the control group, the buccal acupuncture group had shorter time to first defecation [mean difference (MD) = -19.18hours; 95% confidence interval (95%CI):-33.39 to -4.98; P = 0.009].Secondary analyses showed an earlier time to first flatus (MD = -16.56hours; 95%CI: -24.76 to -8.36; nominal P = 0.001), earlier progression to full-4 / 41 liquid and semi-liquid diets, and lower postoperative numerical rating scale pain scores and abdominal-distension measures.Nominal between-group differences were also observed in selected 30-day EORTC QLQ-C30 domains.Because no multiplicityadjustment procedure was prespecified for secondary outcomes, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory.No buccal acupuncture-related serious adverse events were observed. CONCLUSIONBuccal acupuncture added to ERAS was associated with a shorter time to first defecation.Exploratory secondary analyses suggested potential benefits for several recovery and symptom outcomes, which warrant confirmation in larger trials with prespecified multiplicity-control strategies and clinically meaningful outcome thresholds.

titre: EMBODIED PATHWAYS TO SUSTAINABLE WELL-BEING: INTEROCEPTIVE AWARENESS, RESILIENCE, AND STUDENT LIFE SATISFACTION
resume: Sustainable higher education necessitates prioritizing student well-being as a foundational psychological resource for long-term development. Amidst intensifying academic and urban pressures in Asian metropolises, this study investigates the embodied cognitive pathways underlying students' life satisfaction. Specifically, it examines whether interoceptive awareness influences life satisfaction and assesses the serial mediating roles of cognitive reappraisal and psychological resilience. Using a cross-sectional quantitative design, we collected data from 593 full-time university students (aged 18–25) in Shanghai, China. A serial mediation analysis using PROCESS Model 6 revealed that interoceptive awareness positively predicts life satisfaction (β = .36, p < .001). While the isolated indirect pathway via cognitive reappraisal was nonsignificant, psychological resilience emerged as a robust independent mediator (β = .16). Crucially, the model confirmed a significant serial mediation effect (β = .03): bodily awareness facilitates cognitive reappraisal, which subsequently strengthens resilience, ultimately enhancing life satisfaction. These findings highlight that cultivating interoceptive and self-regulatory capacities offers a vital, sustainable mechanism for university counseling and support services to foster enduring student mental health.

titre: Comparing the effectiveness of paradoxical scheduling and cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety, sexual function, and alexithymia in people with premature ejaculation
resume: The present study was conducted with the aim of comparing the effectiveness of two cognitive behavioral therapies on anxiety, ataxia and sexual performance among men with premature ejaculation disorder in Tabriz city. The present research was conducted as a semi-experimental design with a pre-test-post-test design with a control group. The statistical population of the present study was all the people suffering from premature ejaculation in Tabriz city. According to the statistics obtained from the Ministry of Health, their number in this city in 1403 is equal to 3450 people. The sample of this research consists of 45 people from the mentioned society, who were selected as available sampling (probability). In this way, those who came to the Ava Psychology and Counseling Center in Sehertabreez, a number of them were given a premature ejaculation questionnaire, and those who scored above the cut-off point and the expert diagnosed them with premature ejaculation 45 People were selected and replaced in two experimental groups (15 people) and a control group (15 people). The experimental groups included 15 people in the paradoxical schedule training group, and 15 people in the cognitive behavioral therapy experimental group. After the interventions, the data were analyzed with covariance method and LSD post hoc test. The obtained results showed that after both time paradox intervention and cognitive behavioral therapy, the scores obtained in the pre-test and post-test stages for all three dependent variables of anxiety, alexithymia and sexual performance showed a significant difference, which indicates the effectiveness. There had been interventions. Regarding the comparison of the two effectiveness, the results showed that there was no significant difference between the two interventions on the scores obtained in the post-test stage for all three variables of anxiety, ataxia, and sexual performance.
revue: Psychology of Motivation Behavior and Health

titre: Latent Profile Analysis of Suicide Risk Profiles Among University Students: Implications for Screening and Assessment in College Counseling
resume: Objective: This study used latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify multivariable suicide-risk profiles among university students and consider implications for college counseling assessment. Method: Participants were 335 undergraduates (64% selected the female response category; M = 19.8 years) from a convenience volunteer sample at a southeastern U.S. university. Five continuous indicators—adverse childhood experiences (ACE-Q), ego resilience (ERS), alexithymia (TAS-20), suicide risk (SBQ-R), and socioeconomic status (SES)—and one binary reported gender-response indicator were modeled in Mplus using robust maximum likelihood estimation. Results: A two-profile solution included a lower-risk profile (88%) and a higher-risk profile (12%). Relative to the lower-risk profile, the higher-risk profile showed greater ACE exposure, alexithymia, and suicide risk; lower ego resilience and SES; and greater representation of the female response category. Clinical cutoffs were used only descriptively after profile estimation; all members of the higher-risk profile scored at or above the SBQ-R adult cutoff and TAS-20 clinical cutoff. Conclusions: Profile-oriented methods can characterize co-occurring risk and protective patterns that may inform assessment hypotheses. These profiles are not a validated screening rule; independent replication and prospective validation are required before using profile indicators for intake classification or triage.
revue: Measurement and Evaluation in Counseling and Development

titre: Psychological Distress and Adjustment Difficulties Among Nursing Students: A Systematic Review and Meta-Synthesis of Evidence
resume: Background: Nursing students are frequently exposed to multiple academic, clinical, emotional, and environmental stressors during their educational training. Persistent exposure to these stressors may contribute to psychological distress and adjustment difficulties, adversely affecting academic performance, clinical competency, emotional well-being, and professional development. Aim: This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence regarding psychological distress and adjustment difficulties among nursing students, identify associated risk factors, evaluate coping strategies, and summarize implications for nursing education and mental health interventions. Methods: A systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate were searched for studies published between January 2015 and February 2026. Studies focusing on psychological distress, stress, anxiety, depression, emotional burden, and adjustment difficulties among undergraduate or postgraduate nursing students were considered. Data extraction and thematic synthesis were performed. Results: A total of 2,146 records were identified through electronic database searching and an additional 74 records were identified through manual searching. After duplicate removal and screening, 166 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility and 38 studies were included in the final synthesis. The review demonstrated high prevalence of stress, anxiety, depression, burnout, sleep disturbances, and psychosocial adjustment problems among nursing students. Academic workload, clinical exposure, examination pressure, lack of social support, financial burden, and fear of professional failure were consistently reported as major contributing factors. Positive coping mechanisms included peer support, resilience training, counselling services, mindfulness practices, and institutional mentoring. Conclusion: Psychological distress and adjustment difficulties are important concerns among nursing students across the reviewed literature. Early identification, mental health support systems, stress-management interventions, and student-centred educational policies are relevant to improving psychological well-being and academic outcomes.

titre: Large language models in child and adolescent mental health: Clinical applications, safety, and evidence gaps
resume: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated in child and adolescent mental health, yet the clinical relevance and methodological maturity of the evidence remain uncertain.This mini review synthesized empirical studies of LLM-based applications in this field.PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in July 2026.Of 166 records identified, 22 studies were included.Seventeen addressed clinical or diagnostic domains, four evaluated transdiagnostic or multi-purpose applications, and one examined clinician attitudes.Autism spectrum disorder was most frequently represented, followed by attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; single studies addressed suicide-related response safety, anxiety, depression, anorexia nervosa, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and learning disorders.LLMs showed potentially useful performance in question answering, psychoeducation, classification, and vignette-based diagnostic recognition tasks.Studies were methodologically heterogeneous, often relying on standardized questions, vignettes, simulated scenarios, expert ratings, or model-development datasets rather than prospective clinical evaluation.Concerns included inaccurate or unverifiable references, insufficiently actionable responses, variable performance in clinically sensitive situations, and an absence of prospective evaluation with actual patients or users.Current evidence supports further evaluation of LLMs as adjunctive rather than autonomous clinical tools.Developmentally appropriate assessment, standardized evaluation frameworks, independent external validation, and prospective studies with actual patients and users are needed before broader clinical implementation.

fiche.conclusion: Les LLM doivent être considérés comme des outils adjonctifs et nécessitent des évaluations cliniques rigoureuses avant tout déploiement.

titre: AI-Simulated Therapeutic Dialogues in Early Counselor Training: A Mixed-Methods Study of Psychology Students’ Interactions
resume: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based simulation is increasingly used in professional education. Less is known about how beginning psychology students actually conduct counseling conversations in such environments. This study examined dialogue logs from 21 second- and third-year psychology students who had completed 30 contact hours of counseling instruction. Over one week, the students completed 32 text-based sessions with four preprogrammed simulated cases representing generalized anxiety disorder, depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and psychosis. The final corpus contained 372 coded student text units. We applied a log-analytic framework that combined utterance-level functional coding, five session-level indices, and an ordered rule-based classification of provisional counseling patterns. Open questions represented 69.9% of all coded units, while exploratory moves accounted for 82.5%, relational moves for 7.0%, and explicit structuring for 1.1%. The most frequent provisional profiles were clinically focused/formulating (28.1%) and question-dominant interviewer (21.9%). The four scenarios also produced different descriptive patterns: generalized anxiety disorder was associated with the most balanced profile, depressive disorder with the strongest question dominance, and psychosis with the highest scenario-specific clinical sensitivity. The findings indicate that AI-simulated dialogues can provide both practice and analyzable records of early counseling behavior. Their value appears primarily formative, especially for identifying needs in reflection, validation, and session organization. titre: Defecation fear after anorectal surgery: A theory-informed integrative review of mechanisms, assessment and nursing interventions
resume: Background After anorectal surgery, defecation repeatedly exposes a healing wound to stretch, pressure and stool contact. Pain, bleeding and uncertainty may make the next bowel movement a salient threat, yet postoperative defecation fear has not been established as a discrete clinical construct. Objective To define postoperative defecation fear, examine proposed mechanisms and consequences through a fear-avoidance lens, appraise assessment approaches, and derive implications for nursing care and research. Design Theory-informed integrative review and narrative synthesis. Methods Evidence was organized across biological triggers, threat appraisal, anticipatory fear, avoidance and safety behavior, bowel-event characteristics, and recovery outcomes. Direct postoperative anorectal evidence was distinguished from indirect evidence and theory. No pooled effect estimate was calculated. Results Evidence supports the importance of first-defecation pain, sphincter-related nociception, stool characteristics, bowel dysfunction and perioperative psychological factors. One direct-adjacent study found that 54.88% of 441 patients endorsed a binary defecation-fear item; those patients had higher kinesiophobia scores. No validated measure was identified for event-specific fear, feared consequences and functionally defined avoidance. The proposed pain–fear–avoidance–bowel difficulty loop is clinically plausible but remains a testable model rather than a validated causal pathway. A multidimensional assessment framework and stage-matched nursing pathway are proposed. Conclusions Defecation fear may be a clinically useful construct linking surgical symptoms, threat appraisal and bowel behavior. Further work should prioritize concept elicitation, instrument development, event-level longitudinal studies and intervention trials. Implications for Clinical Practice Nurses should assess defecation-specific fear around early bowel movements, distinguish fear-driven avoidance from surgical or functional problems, and combine symptom control, stool optimization, anticipatory guidance and follow-up. Persistent or disproportionate fear may warrant targeted behavioral support or specialist referral, while red flags require clinical evaluation.
revue: International Journal of Nursing Studies Advances

titre: Content validity of PROMs evaluating quality of life in women with childbirth related perineal trauma: a systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Childbirth-related perineal trauma can result in immediate and long-term complications that substantially affect women's quality of life (QoL). Accurate measurement of QoL is essential to guide clinical decision-making and evaluate the effectiveness of interventions from the patient's perspective. OBJECTIVES: To assess the content validity of commonly used patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), previously identified in a systematic review of childbirth-related perineal trauma research, for evaluating quality of life in women with childbirth-related perineal trauma. SEARCH STRATEGY: EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO were searched from database inception to December 2025. A supplementary hand-search of Google Scholar and reference lists was conducted to identify additional eligible studies. SELECTION CRITERIA: English-language full-text publications describing the development of PROMs or evaluating their content validity in the context of childbirth-related perineal trauma. DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Content validity was evaluated using the COSMIN (COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement INstruments) methodology. The quality of evidence was assessed using a modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. MAIN RESULTS: Development studies were identified for three PROMs, the Cleveland Incontinence Clinic Score, the McGill Pain Questionnaire, and the Fecal Incontinence Quality of Life Scale. None were developed using concept elicitation involving women with childbirth-related perineal trauma, and no cognitive interview studies were reported. Although pilot testing was described for two PROMs, target populations were poorly defined and not specific to childbirth-related perineal trauma. No studies specifically evaluating content validity in the target population were identified. Consequently, evidence for relevance and comprehensiveness was indeterminate for all PROMs, and the overall quality of evidence for content validity was rated as very low. CONCLUSION: Evidence on the content validity of PROMs used to assess QoL following childbirth-related perineal trauma is currently limited. Future research should prioritize COSMIN-guided PROM development incorporating comprehensive concept elicitation and cognitive interviewing with affected women to improve clinical relevance and reduce research waste.
revue: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

titre: [Workshop on eating disorders and behavioral issues: a treatment pathway]
resume: Earth mediation, or clay mediation, plays a key role in the treatment of eating disorders. An innovative therapeutic workshop was developed and evaluated using a qualitative assessment tool that explored psychological processes, patients' perceptions, and processes of change. The evaluation results reveal the engagement of sensorimotor processes and tonic dialogue, embodied memories, self-compassion and unconditional self-acceptance, as well as symbolization and the imagination.

titre: The gut microbiome and brain inflammation in Parkinson's disease: mechanisms and therapies
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common chronic progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting over 10 million people worldwide. PD is increasingly understood to have peripheral origins in a substantial subset of patients, in whom microbiota dysbiosis precedes and facilitates central neurodegeneration via the gut-brain axis. Dysbiosis-associated depletion of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria, enrichment of lipopolysaccharide-producing taxa, and loss of gut barrier integrity activate toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, prime microglia towards a disease-linked phenotype, and promote the misfolding of α-synuclein and its propagation from the enteric to the central nervous system. Complement, activated by α-synuclein and shaped by the gut microbiota, further links dysbiosis to neurodegeneration. Beyond neuroinflammation, the gut microbiome modulates levodopa pharmacokinetics through bacterial tyrosine decarboxylase activity and interacts with catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors to alter drug bioavailability. Certain microbial metabolites, including the trimethylamine N-oxide to butyrate ratio and secondary bile acids, have emerged as candidate biomarkers. Cutaneous phosphorylated α-synuclein deposition and seeding amplification assays (SAA) are evaluated as minimally invasive peripheral biomarkers, along with epidemiological evidence linking prior antibiotic exposure and inflammatory bowel disease to PD risk. Emerging therapeutic strategies include SCFA supplementation, fecal microbiota transplantation, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists, and targeted probiotics. Microbiome-direct strategies may benefit patients with a gut-first PD subtype, suggested by prodromal constipation, rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder, or cardiac sympathetic denervation, underscoring the need for subtype-stratified trial designs. In this review article, we highlight recent evidence linking the gut microbiome with neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease through α-synuclein pathology, complement activation, and LPS/TLR4/NF-κB signaling, and discuss the implications for biomarkers, pharmacological interactions, and therapies. In conclusion, the convergence of mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical evidence indicates the gut microbiome may be a significant diagnostic and modifiable therapeutic target in PD.

titre: Regulated cell death in cerebral infarction: a switch-aware framework from molecular mechanisms to targeted therapy
resume: BACKGROUND: Cerebral infarction remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability. Although reperfusion therapy has transformed early management, its benefit is limited by narrow time windows, and most neuroprotective monotherapies have failed in translation. Rather than isolated endpoints, apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis and autophagy-related processes form a dynamically interconnected network; cuproptosis remains an exploratory candidate. METHODS: This narrative synthesis (not a systematic/meta-analysis) drew on primary research and authoritative nomenclature sources on the major regulated cell death modalities in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion, retrieved from PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through August 2026. The search was not pre-registered, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment was performed. RESULTS: Post-ischemic cell death is organized around three convertible molecular switch hubs-caspase-8/RIPK, NCOA4ferritinophagy, and Nrf2 - with gasdermin-D (GSDMD)-mediated pyroptosis as a downstream effector. These hubs map onto the ischemic core, penumbra, and reperfused territory over 0-72 h, and their interconversion helps explain the limited efficacy of single-executor monotherapies. We further assess biomarkers and pharmacological interventions, and extend the framework through the gut-brain axis, where intestinal barrier dysfunction and dysbiosis prime the same central NLRP3, RIPK, and Nrf2 switches. Cuproptosis is retained only as a hypothesis-generating candidate. Clinically meaningful neuroprotection will require mechanism-based, time-and compartment-specific combination strategies. Modality-specific composite biomarker panels paired with time-sensitive therapies offer the most tractable route to patient stratification; the gut-derived input requires prospective validation. CONCLUSION: Framing post-ischemic cell death through convertible switches reframes neuroprotection as a problem of network timing and patient stratification. This switch-aware framework is prospective and falsifiable, generating testable hypotheses for future preclinical and clinical studies.
revue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

titre: IMPRECTO: prevalence, impact, and under-recognition of urgency and fecal incontinence in pediatric ulcerative colitis: a GETAID pédiatrique study
resume: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Urgency and fecal incontinence are disabling yet under-recognized symptoms in pediatric ulcerative colitis (UC). The IMPRECTO prospective multicentre cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence of urgency and fecal incontinence in children aged 6-18 years with UC. Researchers evaluated contributing factors, psychosocial impacts, and the quality of physician-patient communication regarding these symptoms. METHODS: Children with UC followed in 11 French tertiary centers were consecutively enrolled between September and November 2024. Each patient completed 2 questionnaires, incorporating patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and the IMPACT-III quality-of-life instrument. A complementary survey evaluated the clinical practices of pediatric gastroenterologists. RESULTS: A total of 191 patients were included. At enrolment, urgency and fecal incontinence were documented in medical records in 9.0% and 2.7% of patients, respectively. In contrast, PROs indicated higher frequencies, with urgency and fecal incontinence occurring at least monthly in 41.8% and 16.4% of patients, respectively. Both symptoms correlated with higher disease activity, while 32.5% of symptomatic patients reported experiencing urgency/fecal incontinence even during perceived disease remission. Higher urgency/fecal incontinence frequencies were associated with impaired daily life, reduced school attendance, and lower IMPACT-III scores. Communication gaps were evident: 20.8% of symptomatic children never discussed their symptoms during follow-up, while 24.9% desired to have these symptoms addressed. Only 47.8% of physicians routinely assessed urgency and 21.7% assessed fecal incontinence. CONCLUSIONS: Urgency and fecal incontinence remain highly prevalent and burdensome in pediatric UC, yet are under-recognized in clinical practice. Systematic assessment appears essential to improve disease evaluation and patient-physician communication, and support patient-centered management.

titre: Frequency-Dependent Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Ameliorates Functional Dyspepsia Through GATA3-Dependent M2 Macrophage Polarization
resume: BACKGROUND: Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a disorder of gut-brain interaction in which duodenal inflammation and altered mucosal integrity may contribute to symptoms. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has therapeutic potential, but the effects of different stimulation paradigms and their relationship to duodenal immune responses require clarification. METHODS: Male mice with FD-like features received taVNS at 2 Hz, 100 Hz, or alternating 2/100 Hz for two weeks. Food intake, small intestinal transit, serum cytokines, duodenal histology, and duodenal protein expression were evaluated. FD mice receiving taVNS after subphrenic vagotomy or sham surgery were compared to assess vagal involvement. Duodenal M1-like (CD86+CD206-) and M2-like (CD86-CD206+) macrophage proportions were assessed by flow cytometry in wild-type (WT) mice and tamoxifen-treated mice carrying the Cx3cr1-CreERT2/Gata3-flox conditional system (CKO group). Western blot and flow cytometry analyses were exploratory, with n = 3 per group. KEY RESULTS: Among the three paradigms tested, alternating 2/100 Hz taVNS produced the most favorable overall improvements in food intake, intestinal transit, serum inflammatory indices, and duodenal ZO-1 expression. Duodenal iNOS decreased and ARG1 increased with this paradigm, consistent with an M2-associated macrophage marker profile. Flow cytometry showed a higher proportion of M2-like macrophages and a lower proportion of M1-like macrophages in taVNS-treated WT mice than in FD mice. Under taVNS treatment, the CKO group showed a lower M2-like macrophage proportion and a higher M1-like macrophage proportion than the WT group. Under the same taVNS treatment, vagotomized mice showed lower ZO-1 and ARG1 and higher iNOS than sham-operated mice. CONCLUSIONS AND INFERENCES: Alternating 2/100 Hz taVNS improved measured gastrointestinal and inflammatory outcomes in male mice with FD-like features and favored a duodenal M2-like macrophage profile. The vagotomy and tamoxifen-induced conditional-model experiments provide preliminary support for vagal and GATA3-related contributions to these responses.

titre: Magnetically-Controlled Capsule Endoscopy Method to Study Gastric Motility: A Feasibility Study
resume: In this pilot study, magnetically controlled capsule endoscopy noninvasively quantified antral contractions and pyloric opening in functional dyspepsia and gastroparesis. Large between-group effect sizes and an association between prolonged antral wave periods and dyspepsia severity support further validation of this method for assessing gastric motility. ABSTRACT Background/Aims Current methods to study antropyloric contractility in functional dyspepsia (FD) and gastroparesis (GP) have drawbacks partly because their invasive nature may alter normal stomach physiology. This pilot study evaluated the technical feasibility of a non-invasive magnetically-controlled capsule endoscopy (MCCE) system to characterize gastric motility in FD and GP. Methods Six healthy controls (HCs), 6 FD participants, and 5 GP participants underwent MCCE testing to measure pyloric diameter and antral wave period before and after sham feeding with assistance from an artificial intelligence deep learning model. Results were related to symptoms enumerated by the Gastroparesis Cardinal Symptom Index (GCSI) and Dyspepsia Severity Scale (DSS) questionnaires. Results MCCE successfully assessed antropyloric motility in all participants. Pyloric diameters were 10.6 ± 3.7 mm in HC, 8.4 ± 4.5 mm in FD, and 14.1 ± 4.9 mm in GP. Antral wave periods in HC, FD, and GP were 20.0 ± 2.3, 25.1 ± 4.4, and 24.1 ± 5.5 seconds before sham feeding and 20.0 ± 1.5, 25.8 ± 4.5, and 27.6 ± 9.7 seconds after sham feeding. Effect sizes (Cohen's d > 0.8) were observed across multiple comparisons. DSS, but not GCSI, scores correlated positively with wave periods after sham feeding (rho = 0.69, p = 0.04) but not pyloric diameters (rho = 0.19, p = 0.54). Conclusions MCCE enabled the acquisition of analyzable antral contraction and pyloric opening measurements in FD and GP. These findings support technical feasibility. Large effect sizes suggest differences in pyloric diameter and antral periodicity between groups, although further studies are warranted to provide analytical validation of measurement accuracy, reproducibility, and physiological comparability.

titre: Candidate Neuroimmune and Gut-Brain Mechanisms in Poststroke Depression: Evidence and Translational Priorities
resume: BACKGROUND: Poststroke depression (PSD) is common after stroke and is associated with poorer rehabilitation outcomes, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality. Models centered on monoamines, vascular injury, or inflammation incompletely explain its clinical heterogeneity and modest and variable treatment response. This critical narrative review examines neurovascular dysfunction, immune activation, and gut-brain signaling as a candidate framework, distinguishing direct PSD evidence from indirect and extrapolative evidence. RESULTS: Evidence most consistently associates PSD with inflammatory activation and selected neurovascular features, whereas the PSD-specific contribution of blood-brain barrier dysfunction remains uncertain. Microbiome alterations, vagal signaling, and microbial metabolites offer biologically plausible but heterogeneous links to neuroimmune regulation. Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes, complement signaling, and NF-κB-related feedback loops represent testable convergence mechanisms rather than established PSD drivers. Candidate biomarkers and machine learning models may support research cohort enrichment but are not sufficiently validated for routine clinical stratification. Biologically informed intervention pathways should be considered concepts for future trial design rather than treatment algorithms. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework is a map for inquiry rather than a guide for routine precision treatment. Priorities include standardized longitudinal cohorts, explicit evidence grading, externally validated risk models, mechanism-linked outcomes, and pragmatic trials testing whether biological enrichment improves PSD prevention or treatment.

titre: Making allergen introduction work: A family-tailored approach to complementary feeding
resume: The transition in infant feeding recommendations from allergen avoidance to early, active introduction represents a pivotal shift in primary food allergy (FA) prevention. While landmark clinical trials have demonstrated substantial efficacy, translating these findings into real-world settings remains challenging, with a persistent adherence gap. Rigid, protocol-driven approaches may contribute to the perception of feeding as a medical task, increasing parental anxiety and undermining the developmental joy of complementary feeding. This article proposes a holistic, family-tailored approach that bridges the gap between clinical evidence and practical implementation. We explore the biological foundations of oral tolerance, highlighting the interplay between early immune programming, diet and gut microbiome maturation. We emphasize that the window for tolerance induction is critical and that timing should align with developmental readiness rather than strict age thresholds. Sustained, regular ingestion of age-appropriate portions of allergenic foods, integrated into the habitual family diet, appears essential for durable tolerance, whereas intermittent exposure may be insufficient or counterproductive. Importantly, allergen introduction occurs within a broader psychosocial and nutritional context. Incorporating responsive feeding practices supports self-regulation, positive feeding experiences and long-term adherence. The approach must also consider household dietary patterns, cultural practices and proactive management of atopic dermatitis, reflecting the multifactorial nature of FA development. This framework emphasizes shared decision-making and adaptability to individual family contexts. Ultimately, making allergen introduction work requires a supportive ecosystem that prioritizes both clinical outcomes and parental well-being, ensuring that the promotion of tolerance is both clinically effective and sustainable within the realities of family life.
revue: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology

titre: Sound as a Medium for Exploring Survivorship After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: An Exploratory Participatory Co-Creation Study
resume: Survival after acute aortic dissection has improved, shifting attention to long-term recovery and quality of life, yet little is known about how survivors experience their bodies and everyday sensory environment afterwards. We conducted an exploratory, hypothesis-generating qualitative study within a participatory co-creation project, in which nine survivors of acute Type A aortic dissection recruited through a national patient organisation took part in a workshop using sound as a creative entry point for discussing life after dissection. Through individual reflection, thematic clustering, and facilitated group dialogue, participants described everyday experiences of alertness, heightened bodily awareness, reassurance, and mutual recognition. Written reflections, workshop outputs, and facilitator field notes were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants used sound as a medium to articulate an ongoing attentiveness to bodily and environmental cues and valued recognising these experiences in others. Rather than demonstrating altered auditory perception, which was not assessed, the findings suggest that sound can make otherwise hard-to-express dimensions of survivorship visible and shareable, informing future targeted research and person-centred follow-up.
revue: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

titre: Intestinal Diseases in Men and Women: Etiology, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Approaches
resume: Background/Objectives: Intestinal diseases constitute a significant global public health issue and encompass a broad spectrum of inflammatory, functional, and infectious disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis) and irritable bowel syndrome. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to sex-related differences in epidemiology, clinical course, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify publications addressing sex-related differences in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. The aim of the study was to examine sex-based differences in the etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. Results: The development of intestinal diseases is determined by the interaction of genetic, immunological, hormonal, microbial, and environmental factors. Sex-related differences were identified in disease prevalence, clinical course, and progression and are associated with hormonal regulation, immune response characteristics, and gut microbiota composition. Diagnosis of intestinal diseases is based on a combination of laboratory biomarkers, endoscopic, and imaging techniques, and diagnostic accuracy may vary according to biological sex. Video capsule endoscopy, balloon-assisted enteroscopy, and advanced imaging methods, including computed tomography colonography, improve the evaluation of small bowel diseases, whereas chromoendoscopy, colonoscopy, and cross-sectional imaging play important roles in the assessment of colonic disorders. Treatment includes pharmacological, dietary, microbiota-based, endoscopic, and surgical approaches. Current evidence suggests that biological sex may influence treatment response, adverse event profiles, and clinical outcomes; however, the available evidence remains limited or inconsistent for several therapeutic strategies, highlighting the need for further sex-specific clinical research. Conclusions: Sex-related differences should be considered to improve diagnostic accuracy, optimize treatment strategies, and support individualized clinical management. Although evidence remains limited in several areas, current findings support the integration of biological sex into clinical decision-making. Further research is needed to establish sex-specific diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

titre: Effects of different resistance training programs on quality of life and fatigue in cancer patients: a network meta-analysis
resume: OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate, via network meta-analysis, the effects of different resistance training intensities on quality of life and cancer-related fatigue in cancer patients, and to identify the optimal exercise regimen. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to January 13, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing different resistance training protocols-stratified by intensity (low, moderate, high) and frequency (twice or three times per week)-on quality of life and fatigue in cancer patients were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Traditional and network meta-analyses were performed using Stata 17.0, with the standardized mean difference (SMD) and its 95% confidence interval (CI) as the effect measure. Sources of heterogeneity were explored through subgroup analysis, and the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to rank the interventions. RESULTS: Twenty-one studies involving 1,655 patients were included. Traditional meta-analysis showed that resistance training significantly improved quality of life (SMD = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.34) and reduced fatigue (SMD = - 0.34, 95% CI: -0.57 to - 0.11) compared with the control group. Subgroup analysis indicated that moderate-intensity, low-frequency (MI-LF) resistance training led to more significant improvements in quality of life and fatigue in patients with breast or gastrointestinal cancer, and that the significant benefits for different outcome measures also depended on the specific assessment instruments used. Network meta-analysis revealed that MI-LF training ranked highest for improving quality of life, with a SUCRA value of 71.1% (SMD = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.10 to 0.45); it also ranked highest for reducing fatigue, with a SUCRA value of 78.1% (SMD = - 0.65, 95% CI: -1.26 to - 0.03). CONCLUSION: Resistance training effectively improves quality of life and alleviates fatigue in cancer patients. Among the examined regimens, MI-LF training had the highest probability of being a relatively more favorable option for both outcomes. However, given that SUCRA values reflect only the relative ranking probabilities of interventions, their clinical application warrants caution, and individualized exercise prescriptions should be formulated based on patients' specific conditions.

titre: Meranzin hydrate from Fructus Aurantii restores brain-gut homeostasis through a microbiota-dependent butyrate-ghrelin axis
resume: Although gut microbiota-derived metabolites are increasingly implicated in host neuroendocrine regulation, it remains unresolved whether an orally delivered botanical can restore coordinated brain-gut homeostasis through a functionally supported microbiota-metabolite-endocrine pathway centered on a content-anchored, brain-accessible constituent. Here, using content-anchored pharmacometry in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) model of depression with gastrointestinal (GI) hypomotility, we identified meranzin hydrate (MH) as the only absorbed prototype of Fructus Aurantii (FRA) detected in the brain and showed that, at its content-anchored dose, MH reproduced the major antidepressant-like and prokinetic effects observed with the parent botanical. Integrating 16S rRNA profiling, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) quantification, plasma ghrelin, antagonist mapping, resting-state fMRI, serum-equivalent assays, and cross-tissue transcriptomics showed that MH reversed stress-disrupted microbial ecology, restored fermentative output, particularly butyrate, and re-established coupling between microbial metabolic function, circulating ghrelin, and synchronized brain-gut phenotypes. To directly test microbiota dependency, broad-spectrum antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion was introduced, which markedly attenuated MH-associated recovery of SCFA output, plasma ghrelin levels, depressive-like behavior, and GI motility. Importantly, exogenous sodium butyrate did not restore bacterial biomass but partially rescued ghrelin levels and downstream phenotypes under microbiota-depleted conditions, supporting a microbiota-dependent butyrate-ghrelin mechanism rather than a purely correlative ecological association. Downstream, GHSR1a blockade disrupted this recovery hierarchy, whereas transcriptomic convergence analysis identified a shared contractile-immune host response program across the hippocampus and stomach. Collectively, these findings identify MH as a pharmacologically important, content-anchored contributor to FRA efficacy and provide functional perturbation-and-rescue evidence supporting a microbiota-dependent butyrate-ghrelin interface that contributes to coordinated brain-gut recovery under chronic stress.

titre: A global-scale characterisation of the neuroactive potential of the human gut microbiome
resume: Microbiome-gut-brain axis research largely focuses on high-income countries, leaving other populations reliant on findings that may not generalise to their contexts. To address this gap, we reanalysed 171,846 faecal samples profiled via amplicon sequencing from 72 countries to create the first global-scale characterisation of the human gut microbiome's neuroactive potential. After inferring the genomic content of each sample, we found regional differences in the abundance of pathways for short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan, and GABA metabolism, as well as in the overall neuroactive potential of the human gut microbiome. Our results highlight a pressing need for greater global representation in the field.

titre: Gastrointestinal symptom assessment tools in infants and toddlers with disorders of gut-brain interaction
resume: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), formerly referred to as functional gastrointestinal disorders, are highly prevalent in infancy and early childhood and are primarily diagnosed and monitored through symptom-based assessment. In infants and toddlers, the evaluation of gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms relies almost exclusively on caregiver-reported outcome measures, making the availability of validated questionnaires essential for both clinical practice and research. This narrative review provides an overview of the main validated GI symptom questionnaires currently used to assess DGBIs-related symptoms in infants and toddlers. A literature search was conducted using major scientific databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Database, to identify studies employing validated questionnaires or symptom scales in this age group. The use of validated questionnaires allows for standardized symptom assessment, improves comparability across studies, and supports clinical decision-making and longitudinal monitoring. However, gaps remain regarding age specificity, symptom coverage, and cross-cultural validation. A clear understanding of the available tools and their appropriate use is essential to improve diagnostic accuracy, follow-up, and research quality in infants and toddlers with DGBIs.
revue: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

titre: The Role of Affective Traits and Social Cognition in Envy and Schadenfreude
resume: Complex social emotions like envy and Schadenfreude challenge traditional models of social cognition by revealing how affective traits interact with cognitive processes to shape counter-empathic responses. Although theoretically linked to empathy and theory of mind (ToM), their associations with traits like alexithymia and anhedonia remain underexplored. This study tested a structural model connecting affective traits (alexithymia, anhedonia), social cognition (ToM, empathy), and social emotions (envy, Schadenfreude) in 125 healthy adults using validated measures and structural equation modeling. Results showed that alexithymia indirectly influenced empathy and envy via reduced ToM, while empathy did not directly predict these emotions. Alexithymia correlated positively with anhedonia and negatively with ToM. Anhedonia predicted lower empathy. Envy strongly predicted Schadenfreude, underscoring the role of upward social comparison. Findings suggest that these emotions arise from distinct affective and cognitive mechanisms, offering a novel framework for understanding socio-emotional functioning in both healthy and clinical populations.

titre: Evaluation of Alexithymia, Narcissism, and Aggression Levels in Gamblers in Terms of Gambling Disorder
resume: OBJECTIVE: Gambling disorder has been increasingly associated with various psychological traits that may influence its development and severity. Among these, alexithymia, narcissism, and aggression have gained attention for their potential roles in emotional regulation difficulties and maladaptive coping mechanisms in individuals with gambling problems. This study aimed to examine the relationship between alexithymia, narcissism, and aggression levels in relation to gambling disorder (GD). METHODS: In this descriptive cross-sectional study, data were collected from 390 adult gamblers in İzmir, Türkiye, using the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS), Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), Pathological Narcissism Inventory (PNI), and Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire (BPAQ). RESULTS: Results showed that a one-unit increase in TAS-20 scores led to a 0.474-unit increase in SOGS scores, while a one-unit increase in PNI scores increased SOGS scores by 0.107 units. BPAQ scores, however, were not statistically significant. Pathological gamblers exhibited significantly higher levels of alexithymia, narcissism (across both grandiose and vulnerable dimensions), and aggression compared to non-pathological gamblers. CONCLUSION: While alexithymia and narcissism were significantly associated with gambling severity, aggression did not show a significant direct association with gambling severity. These findings emphasize the central role of emotional dysregulation and maladaptive personality traits in understanding and treating gambling disorder.

titre: Altered Intrinsic Brain Network Organization in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Differential Associations with Pain Sensitivity and Perceived Stress
resume: INTRODUCTION: The persistence of abdominal pain and related gastrointestinal symptoms despite disease remission suggests that inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may involve central alterations that extend beyond periods of active intestinal inflammation. Yet, intrinsic brain network organization in ulcerative colitis (UC) remains insufficiently characterized, particularly in relation to factors relevant to symptom persistence, such as pain sensitivity and chronic stress burden. We therefore investigated resting-state functional connectivity (FC) within the default mode network (DMN) and salience network in UC and examined associations with heat pain thresholds and perceived chronic stress. METHODS: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 17 female patients with UC and 19 female healthy controls (HC) were analyzed using group-level independent component analysis. FC differences within the identified DMN and salience network components were assessed in a priori defined regions of interest implicated in interoceptive and affective pain-related processing. Associations between altered FC and heat pain thresholds as well as perceived chronic stress were examined. RESULTS: Patients with UC differed from HC in the intrinsic organization of both the DMN and salience network. DMN alterations included increased FC of the posterior insula and medial superior frontal gyrus, alongside decreased FC of the dorsolateral superior frontal gyrus. Salience network alterations involved increased FC of the anterior insula, midcingulate cortex, and orbital inferior frontal gyrus. In UC, stronger FC of the anterior insula and orbital inferior frontal gyrus within the salience network was associated with lower heat pain thresholds, corresponding to greater experimental pain sensitivity. These associations were absent in HC. Connectivity of the orbital inferior frontal gyrus was additionally associated with perceived chronic stress in HC, but not in UC. CONCLUSION: UC is characterized by altered intrinsic organization of brain networks central to interoceptive and affective pain-related processing. The association between stronger salience network connectivity and greater experimental pain sensitivity suggests that central network alterations may be involved in pain-related mechanisms beyond acute intestinal inflammation. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of considering central pain mechanisms alongside peripheral inflammation to better understand persistent pain in IBD.

titre: Efficacy of Vitamin D Versus Zinc Supplementation on Symptom Severity in Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether vitamin D, zinc, or both, taken in addition to usual care for 12 weeks, reduce symptom severity in adults with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). The main questions it aims to answer are: * Does vitamin D lower the IBS Symptom Severity Score (IBS-SSS) at week 12 compared with usual care alone? * Does zinc lower the IBS-SSS at week 12 compared with usual care alone? * Does the IBS-SSS at week 12 differ between vitamin D and zinc? Researchers will compare four groups: vitamin D3, zinc, vitamin D3 plus zinc, and usual care alone. Participants will: * Have blood tests for vitamin D and zinc at the start and at week 12 * Take their assigned supplement(s) for 12 weeks, in addition to their usual IBS treatment * Visit the clinic at the start and at week 12, and complete IBS symptom and quality-of-life questionnaires

titre: Randomized Trial of Non-Invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation in UC-IBS and Mild Ulcerative Colitis: NIH Aim 3
resume: Many people with ulcerative colitis (UC) continue to experience symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloating, and bowel urgency, even when there is little or no active inflammation in their intestines. Researchers believe that communication between the brain, nervous system, and gut may play an important role in these ongoing symptoms. The purpose of this study is to determine whether 8 weeks of non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation changes brain activity and communication within networks that regulate digestion, pain, and body functions such as heart rate. Researchers will also evaluate whether these changes are associated with improvements in gastrointestinal symptoms, nervous system function, and markers of inflammation. Participation in this study involves random assignment to a study group for 8 weeks and then followed for an additional 4 weeks after completing the intervention. The study aims to assess the effects of the intervention using brain imaging, wearable device measurements, laboratory tests for inflammation, and questionnaires about symptoms and quality of life. The goal is to better understand how the brain-gut connection contributes to persistent symptoms in ulcerative colitis and whether non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation may help improve those symptoms.
