titre: Comparison of the Effects of Virtual Reality, Hypnosis, and Their Combination on Experimental Pain, Physiological Measures, and Electroencephalographic Signatures
resume: This study looks at three ways to help manage pain without medication: virtual reality (using a VR headset to create an immersive distraction), hypnosis (using guided relaxation and suggestion), and a combination of both. Researchers want to know which approach - or combination - works best at reducing pain and discomfort. Forty healthy adults will take part in a single research visit lasting about 140 minutes. During the visit, participants will experience mild, controlled pain from a small electrical stimulation on the ankle, adjusted to a level they can tolerate. They will try all three approaches (virtual reality, hypnosis, and the combination) during the same visit, in a random order. Throughout the visit, researchers will record how much pain and discomfort participants feel, along with body signals such as heart rate, breathing, skin response, and brain activity (using a comfortable EEG cap with no needles). The goal is to better understand how these non-drug approaches work and whether combining them provides more relief than using either one alone. This research may help improve pain management for people undergoing medical procedures in the future.

titre: Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) for the Treatment of Unipolar Depression Among Adults: A Feasibility Study
resume: The purpose of this study is to find out if people with depression can be helped with their symptoms by going through a mystical experience paired with psychotherapy (sometimes called talk therapy). Mystical experiences are profound and highly meaningful states of consciousness in which people report a sense of unity or "oneness" with everything, highly positive emotions, and a sense of having something important revealed to them. Previous research suggests that patients with depression can experience improvement in their symptoms after having a mystical experience while under the influence of a psychedelic substance (e.g., psilocybin, ayahuasca). This study seeks to answer if a mystical experience brought about through hypnosis can also have a positive effect on symptoms of depression. Participants will participate in seven sessions of psychotherapy and respond to questionnaires of various lengths at five time points. All study visits that involve meeting with a psychotherapist will occur in the laboratory facility in which the baseline session occurs. In chronological order, these involve: * Eligibility screening: Completion of an online survey to confirm eligibility to participate in study (already completed): 15-20 minutes * Baseline appointment: Meeting with study personnel prior to first session of psychotherapy to confirm intention to participate in study, complete 12 short questionnaires, and schedule first session, 60-90 minutes * Preparation sessions (2): Meet with psychotherapist to discuss symptoms, current stressors, and goals for treatment, 60 minutes (x2) * Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) sessions (2): Meet with psychotherapist for a hypnosis session for mystical experience, 60-75 minutes (x2) * Post-GIME assessment (2): Complete two brief questionnaires immediately following each GIME session, 10-15 minutes (x2) * Integration sessions (3): Meet with psychotherapist to discuss experience(s) during GIME sessions and integrate insights into daily life, 60 minutes (x2), 30 minutes (x1) * Audio recordings: Participants will be asked to listen to a brief, relaxation-based audio recording at home approximately 3x per week following the first GIME session. * Endpoint assessment: Participants complete 13 brief computer-based questionnaires (20-35 minutes), participate in a brief assessment to gauge hypnotic ability (10-15 minutes), and (optional) participate in a brief interview (10-20 minutes), total 50-70 minutes. An audio/video recording of participants will be made if they elect to participate in the optional, brief interview. * Follow up assessment: Complete 7 brief computer-based questionnaires, 15-25 minutes

titre: AI-assisted Adaptive Support Versus Standard Care to Reduce Post-intensive Care Syndrome-family (the ASSIST Trial): a Sequential Explanatory Mixed-methods Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol
resume: The ASSIST trial evaluates whether an AI-assisted smartphone application can reduce post-traumatic stress symptoms and other psychological distress in family members of critically ill patients. Admission to an intensive care unit (ICU) places a severe psychological burden on families, often leading to post-intensive care syndrome-family (PICS-F). Current support is mostly reactive and rarely available after the patient is discharged. This study is a three-center randomized controlled trial involving 1000 family members. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either standard care or standard care plus the ASSIST smartphone platform. During the ICU stay, the platform uses an artificial intelligence model to simplify clinical information (approved by a clinician) and helps families prepare questions for the medical team. After the patient is discharged, the platform monitors the family member's mood daily. If a risk of anxiety or depression is detected, it provides a brief digital cognitive behavioral therapy module. The main goal is to see if the ASSIST platform reduces post-traumatic stress over a 12-month period compared to standard care alone. Secondary goals include evaluating its effects on acute stress, decisional conflict, anxiety, depression, and caregiver burden. The study will also include qualitative interviews to understand the family members' lived experiences using the platform

titre: Comparing Individual Versus Group Written Exposure Therapy Among Active Duty Servicemembers: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial
resume: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a highly prevalent condition that incurs an economic burden in excess of $232 billion annually in the United States alone. Demand for trauma-focused treatment has consistently increased in recent decades. Written Exposure Therapy (WET) has emerged as a gold-standard treatment for PTSD in the most recent clinical practice guidelines. The relatively shorter protocol for WET may make it a more efficient and cost-effective option in certain settings when compared to longer trauma-focused therapies. There have been limited efforts to develop and validate a protocol that adapts WET to be delivered in groups. Group therapies have been recognized as cost-effective, feasible, and efficacious approaches to treating conditions while increasing access to care. Our objective is to employ a between groups, repeated measures randomized controlled design to test whether WET adapted to and delivered in a group format is noninferior to individually delivered Written Exposure Therapy in changing symptoms (e.g., PTSD, depression, anxiety, insomnia; Aim 1) among active duty Servicemembers. We also aim to examine and compare implementation related outcomes, including treatment feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, and costs (Aim 2). We hypothesize that 1) WET delivered in a group format will be noninferior to WET delivered individually on measures of PTSD, depression, anxiety, and insomnia; 2a) There will be no differences between treatment conditions on measures of feasibility, acceptability, and fidelity; and 2b) Treatment cost will be significantly lower for the Group WET condition when compared to the cost of Individual WET. We envision that this knowledge will help inform clinical guidelines and improve access and availability to gold-standard evidence-based trauma focused psychotherapies.

titre: Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial of a Transdiagnostic, Modular Intervention for Youth at Risk for Psychotic, Bipolar, or Borderline Personality Disorders
resume: Mental disorders constitute a major challenge to both society, patients and science. Serious mental illnesses (SMIs), such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression and personality disorders, comprise some of the largest disease burdens worldwide, with no evidence of reduction in recent decades. A range of psycho-social and pharmacological interventions have demonstrated efficacy for improving symptomatic and functional outcomes of SMIs albeit with modest effect sizes and the development of novel, more effective treatments has largely stalled despite a significant number of patients will not respond to treatments. Additionally, there are substantial shortages in access to treatments as well as various barriers, such as perceived need for care and stigma surrounding mental health problems. The planned study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel modular, transdiagnostic psychotherapeutic intervention in n=130 youths at-risk for SMIs. The planned randomized controlled study compares the new developed intervention to TAU in five different study centres. The Objective is to evaluate the modular, transdiagnostic CBT (AIM-Youth) approach for youths at-risk for SMIs compared to treatment as usual (TAU). Measurements take place as baseline, mid-treatment (3 month), post-treatment (6 month) and follow-up (12-48 month). The primary outcome measure will be psychological distress as measured by the CORE-10 at the end of treatment, secondary outcomes will be CHR-symptoms, quality of life, functioning as well as use of mental health resources at post and follow-up assessment.

titre: Effects of a Six-Week Online Mindfulness-Based Intervention on Mental Health Outcomes in Morning and Evening Chronotypes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to investigate whether a six-week online mindfulness-based intervention can reduce depressive symptoms and improve mental health and psychological well-being in adults with morning or evening chronotypes. Chronotype refers to individual differences in preferred timing of sleep, activity, and alertness. Individuals with morning chronotypes tend to feel more alert and energetic earlier in the day, whereas those with evening chronotypes tend to prefer later hours. Evening chronotypes may be more vulnerable to certain mental health difficulties, including depressive symptoms, anxiety, and sleep problems. Mindfulness-based interventions aim to develop present-moment awareness and a more accepting, nonjudgmental relationship with thoughts, emotions, and bodily sensations. The main research questions are: 1. Does a six-week online mindfulness-based intervention reduce depressive symptoms compared with a waitlist control condition? 2. Does the effectiveness of the intervention differ between individuals with morning and evening chronotypes? 3. Does the intervention improve anxiety symptoms, psychological well-being, perceived stress, sleep disturbances, and psychological processes including mindfulness, self-compassion, cognitive fusion, and repetitive negative thinking? 4. Do changes in psychological processes, particularly mindfulness, cognitive fusion, and repetitive negative thinking, help explain improvements in depressive symptoms? 5. Are improvements maintained one month and three months after the intervention? Approximately 400 adults with pronounced morning or evening chronotypes will be enrolled and randomly assigned to one of two groups, with randomization stratified by chronotype: 1. Mindfulness intervention group: Participants will complete a six-week online mindfulness-based program adapted from Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT). The intervention will include one live, instructor-led online group session per week, lasting approximately 60-120 minutes, and guided individual mindfulness practice lasting approximately 20-30 minutes per day, six days per week. Guided practice materials will be provided through the study's online platform. The platform will also be used to monitor engagement with the intervention, including access to guided meditation recordings and practice duration. 2. Control group: Participants will not receive mindfulness training during the six-week intervention period. After the mindfulness intervention group completes the six-week program, participants in the waitlist control group will be given access to an asynchronous, self-guided version of the mindfulness training. Participants will complete standardized questionnaires assessing depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, psychological well-being, sleep difficulties, perceived stress, and psychological processes potentially involved in the effects of mindfulness training. The primary outcome will be depressive symptom severity, assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8). Secondary outcomes will include anxiety symptoms assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), psychological well-being assessed using the World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5), sleep disturbances assessed using the PROMIS Sleep Disturbance Short Form 6a (PROMIS SD SF-6a), and perceived stress assessed using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). The study will also assess changes in dispositional mindfulness (FFMQ-15), repetitive negative thinking (PTQ-15), cognitive fusion (CFQ-7), and self-compassion (SCS-SF). These measures will allow to investigate potential psychological mechanisms underlying the effects of mindfulness training, including whether earlier changes in mindfulness and cognitive fusion are associated with subsequent reductions in repetitive negative thinking and depressive symptoms. Questionnaire assessments will be conducted before the intervention (Week 0), during the intervention (Weeks 2 and 4), and immediately after the intervention (Week 6). Additional follow-up assessments will take place one month and three months after the intervention to examine the maintenance of treatment effects. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of whether mindfulness-based interventions are similarly effective for individuals with morning and evening chronotypes, how mindfulness-related psychological processes change during treatment, and whether chronotype should be considered when developing accessible online mental health interventions.

titre: Beyond Trauma (BT): A Healing Journey for Women
resume: This randomized controlled trial is designed to evalute Beyond Trauma (BT). Beyond Trauma promotes a strength-based approach that seeks to empower women and increase their sense of self. The exercises are designed to give them a corrective experience of connecting with others in a safe environment. In using this model, the facilitator helps the women in the group to see the strengths they have and to increase the skills they need. The curriculum also focuses on emotional development. Dealing with the expression and containment of feelings (fear, loss, grief, anger, shame) is a critical part of trauma work. The program uses cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT), expressive arts, body-oriented strategies, and is based on the principles of relational therapy. In addition, there is a segment on specific issues in the criminal justice settings, and the end of each of the 12 sessions has information on adapting for girls. The study is being conducted at a California correctional facility and compares participants randomly assigned to BT with participants assigned to a waitlist control condition. The program is delivered by trained peer facilitators in general institutional housing. Researchers are assessing changes in trauma-related distress and behavioral health symptoms using validated self-report measures administered before and after the intervention period. The study examines between-group differences in post-traumatic stress symptoms, global trauma symptoms, anxiety, depression, dissociation, sexual abuse-related trauma symptoms, and sleep disturbances.

titre: Psychological and Clinical Factors Associated With School Refusal Across Educational Stages in Adolescent Psychiatric Outpatients: A Cross-Sectional Study
resume: IntroductionThis cross-sectional study examined clinical and psychological factors associated with school refusal across educational stages in adolescent psychiatric outpatients.MethodsWe evaluated 417 outpatients: 254 middle schoolers (aged 12-15) and 163 high schoolers (aged 15-18). School refusal was operationalized as ≥ 30 annual absence days. Participants completed the HQ-25 (hikikomori), TACS-22 (modern-type depression), BRS (resilience), and QIDS-SR (depression).ResultsIn multivariable regression (N=417), an ICD-10 F4 diagnosis and HQ-25 Isolation independently predicted school refusal, while depressive severity and resilience did not. Educational stage significantly interacted with TACS-22 Avoidance of Social Roles. In middle schoolers (n=254), Isolation was the primary associated factor, with marginal trends for female sex and physical comorbidity. Conversely, in high schoolers (n=163), Avoidance of Social Roles independently predicted school refusal, whereas ADHD diagnosis was associated with lower odds.ConclusionsFactors associated with school refusal transition from middle school somatic distress and isolation to high school social role avoidance. Stage-specific screening integrating withdrawal traits and neurodevelopmental profiles is recommended.

titre: Role of Bile Acids in Colorectal Diseases
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Bile acids (BAs) have functions well beyond fat digestion. They also serve as signals linking the gut microbiota to gut health. This review examines how BAs affect colorectal diseases and how this knowledge can guide diagnosis and treatment. RECENT FINDINGS: BAs and gut bacteria shape each other, and this balance affects the gut lining, immune system, and inflammation. Problems in BA handling are linked to bile acid diarrhea, post-cholecystectomy diarrhea, microscopic colitis, irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and organoid models enable faster, more detailed BA testing. New treatments include BA binders, farnesoid X receptor-targeting drugs, and engineered gut bacteria. BAs play a central role in many colorectal diseases through their effects on gut bacteria and the gut lining. Better BA testing can improve diagnosis, and new BA- and microbiota-based treatments show promise. More studies are needed to bring these approaches into clinical practice.

titre: Enterochromaffin cells as sensory hubs of the gut-brain axis
resume: The mucosal epithelium of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract forms one of the largest exposed surfaces of the body, providing a unique interface through which environmental stimuli are integrated and modulate physiological processes. This review focuses on enterochromaffin cells (ECCs), a rare subtype of enteroendocrine cells comprising <1% of all intestinal epithelial cells. ECCs are excitable cells that express a variety of ion channels and receptors, allowing them to react to varied chemical and mechanical stimuli. Recent studies have shown that ECCs are major players in GI epithelial sensing and affect a variety of physiological and pathophysiological states, such as secretion, GI motility, GI sensory afferent nerve hypersensitivity, satiety, nausea, and visceral pain. This review highlights the diverse functions of ECCs, the peripheral 5-hydroxytryptamine they release, and the nerves they interact with.

titre: Maternal gluten diet exacerbates offspring autistic-like behaviors through the gut-brain axis mediated by gut microbial metabolite elaidic acid
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by social deficits and stereotyped behaviors, for which effective treatments remain lacking. Here we investigated whether early-life gluten exposure exacerbates autism-like behaviors in BTBR mice and explored the underlying microbiota-metabolite-brain mechanism. Early-life gluten exposure aggravated social avoidance, anxiety, and repetitive behaviors in BTBR offspring, accompanied by reduced mushroom dendritic spine density and diminished microglial branch complexity in the hippocampus. Microbiota sequencing revealed gut microbial dysbiosis, with increased abundance of Hungatella hathewayi and Eubacterium sp. Marseille-P4003. Consistent with their capacity for lipid transformation, untargeted metabolomics showed enrichment of unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and elevated fecal elaidic acid levels. Clinically, targeted quantification confirmed that fecal elaidic acid was significantly higher in children with ASD than in their healthy siblings. Supporting a causal role, exogenous elaidic acid administration dose-dependently worsened behavioral deficits and induced hippocampal spine loss and amoeboid microglial activation. Mechanistically, intestinal transcriptomics revealed activation of antigen processing and presentation and cytokine signaling pathways, whereas hippocampal transcriptomics showed downregulation of immune negative regulators (Egr2, Egr4) alongside enrichment of MHC-I and TNF pathways, indicating impaired central immune restraint. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that early-life gluten exposure induces gut microbiota dysbiosis that drives elaidic acid accumulation, which in turn activates intestinal immunity and suppresses hippocampal immune negative regulation via the gut-brain axis, ultimately aggravating neuroinflammation and autism-like behaviors.

titre: Perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 is associated with gut dysbiosis, impaired serotonin-kynurenine pathways and is linked to psychiatric-like disorders in rat offspring
resume: The prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases and psychiatric disorders, including anxiety and depression, appears to be higher among patients with gastrointestinal diseases, supporting the existence of a functional communication in the "gut-brain axis", that remains poorly described. Using a maternal methyl-donor dietary deficiency model, we investigated the short-term consequences of intestinal microbiota dysbiosis on gut-brain mechanisms involving the tryptophan metabolism and associated neurofunctional outcomes. Our results showed that deficient offspring exhibited alterations in the gut microbiota, associated with intestinal inflammation, during the juvenile and puberty stages. In these deficient offspring the tryptophan metabolism was disrupted, predominantly affecting the serotonin and kynurenine pathways at the puberty stage. In parallel, we observed sex-specific behavioral alterations characterized by persistent anxiety-like behavior in females, depressive-like behavior in males, and reduced social interactions in both sexes. These findings suggest that early-life dysbiosis and intestinal inflammation are associated with sex- and time-dependent alterations of the gut-brain axis though systemic deregulation of tryptophan metabolism. This may increase vulnerability to gastrointestinal and psychiatric disorders.

titre: A gut-brain axis for aversive interoception drives innate and anticipatory emesis in Drosophila
resume: The gut-brain pathways that transmit negative signals to the brain, influencing bodily functions and behavior, are not fully understood. We have identified a gut-brain axis in Drosophila that detects toxin-induced gut damage and triggers innate and learned, anticipatory emesis. Ingested toxins induce the midgut enterocytes to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS are detected by TrpA1 channels in enteroendocrine cells, resulting in the release of neuropeptides that signal gastric malaise. We also find evidence for midgut and ROS-independent mechanisms of toxin detection. Gut-derived neuropeptides act on brain serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons, which then communicate with the brain's sensory integration and memory centers, the mushroom bodies (MBs). This circuit enables vomiting and facilitates the formation of aversive memories. We find that the persistent activity of dopaminergic neurons mediates aversive reinforcement. Such activity lends itself to pairing the gut-derived malaise signal with odor representations in the MBs, enabling the flies to learn that the paired odor predicts toxin ingestion and to exhibit anticipatory emesis. Many components of this interoceptive pathway are likely conserved, providing a genetic model for exploring how aversive gut-brain communication influences metabolism, feeding, stress responses, and neurodegeneration.

fiche.conclusion_simple: Ces résultats offrent un modèle génétique pour étudier la communication gut-brain aversive, à confirmer en contexte humain.

titre: Individual deviation network analysis and rat multiomics profiling link sleep deprivation to depressive-like behavior and microbiome-metabolome remodeling
resume: BACKGROUND: Disturbed sleep and depression are bidirectionally linked, but the peripheral biological pathway converting chronic sleep loss into a depressive phenotype remains poorly defined. We combined a human individual deviation network (IDN) analysis with a rat sleep deprivation model to investigate changes in colonic mucosal morphology and tight junction protein levels, microbiome-metabolome reorganization, and candidate fecal metabolite signatures. METHODS: An IDN was constructed in 14,769 NHANES adults (2009-2018) using 14 variables spanning sleep, depression, diet-microbiome, glucolipid, and hepato-renal domains. Two-sample Mendelian randomization provided directional annotations. Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent modified multiple platform sleep deprivation for 18 h/day over 21 days (n = 5/group). Behavioral, intestinal, inflammatory, microbial, and fecal metabolomic endpoints were assessed, and metabolite covariation modules were used to identify behavior-linked Hub metabolites. RESULTS: The IDN identified Sleep × Depression as the dominant deviation axis, with joint amplification extending to the diet-microbiome (dietary index) and metabolic domains. In rats, sleep deprivation reduced sucrose preference and increased forced swim immobility without altering total fluid intake or open field distance. Colonic ZO-1, Occludin, and Claudin-1 decreased while serum TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 increased. Fecal microbiome and metabolome were remodeled. Module M06 was the only FDR-supported behavior-linked module, localizing to docosapentaenoic acid (22:5n-6), FAHFA 38:5, and N-oleoylethanolamine as Hub metabolites. CONCLUSIONS: Sleep × Depression emerged as the dominant clinical axis capturing individual heterogeneity beyond group means. In a complementary rat model, chronic sleep deprivation produced depressive-like behavior, inflammation, and microbiome-metabolome remodeling, together with colonic mucosal alterations and reduced tight junction protein expression suggestive of impaired barrier integrity. The M06 hub metabolites are candidate fecal biomarkers and molecules for future mechanistic studies of sleep deprivation-related depression.

titre: High-throughput screening of patient iPSC-derived neurons identifies the gut microbial metabolites that attenuate Alzheimer's disease pathology
resume: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites influence the gut-brain axis and may impact Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. However, the microbial metabolites involved in this process and their functional roles are largely unknown. We screened 352 gut metabolites in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived neurons from individuals with AD to identify compounds that reduce tau hyperphosphorylation. We identified agmatine as a lead candidate, which decreased hyperphosphorylated tau in neurons and cerebral organoids. In 5xFAD mice, agmatine (100 mg/kg/day) improved cognition, reduced amyloid plaques, lowered neuroinflammation, and increased beneficial gut bacteria, including Agathobacter and Bacteroides. Transcriptomic analysis showed that agmatine downregulated complement and inflammatory genes (C1QB, C2, C3AR1, CCL3, CXCL8, and CXCL6) in patient iPSC-derived cerebral organoids. Agmatine also decreased C3aR and pSTAT3 levels in vivo, mechanistically supporting the reduced tau phosphorylation in iPSC-derived neurons. Altogether, these findings identified the therapeutic potential of gut-derived metabolites and identified agmatine as potential treatment for AD.

titre: Multi-level spinal cord stimulation to treat pain, orthostatic intolerance and autonomic symptoms in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: a pilot case series
resume: BACKGROUND: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a chronic and often disabling disorder characterized by orthostatic intolerance and excessive heart-rate increase. POTS may be accompanied by chronic pain and other autonomic symptoms that further impair quality of life. We report a pilot case series of patients with painful POTS and persistent symptoms despite conventional medical management treated with spinal cord stimulation (SCS). METHODS: Five patients with painful POTS underwent implantation of three percutaneous SCS leads (two thoracic leads [T9-T12] and one cervical lead [C5-T1]). Assessments were performed before and after SCS over 12 months and included pain (VAS), autonomic symptoms using the Boston Autonomic Symptom​ Questionnaire (BASQ), health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using SF-36v2, and head-up tilt testing with assessment of the orthostatic heart-rate response (ΔHR). RESULTS: Pain was substantially reduced after SCS (VAS, 8.0 to 2.6; p = 0.003). Postural tachycardia also decreased, with reductions in mean ΔHR from 32.7 to 11.2 beats/min (p = 0.05). Autonomic symptom burden decreased by approximately 50% (BASQ, 45.5 to 22.9; p = 0.01), with improvements in orthostatic intolerance (7.3 to 1.7; p = 0.02) and selected cardiorespiratory, genitourinary, and gastrointestinal symptoms. HRQoL improved, particularly physical functioning (15 to 66; p < 0.001) and role-physical (2.5 to 52.5; p = 0.002), with additional improvements in bodily pain and vitality. Heart rate variability analyses showed changes consistent with improved autonomic regulation during orthostatic stress. CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot case series, multi-level SCS was associated with improvements in pain, orthostatic tachycardia, autonomic symptoms, and quality of life in patients with POTS. The rapid improvement in orthostatic heart-rate responses and preliminary hemodynamic observations support further investigation of SCS as a neuromodulatory approach for POTS.

titre: Remimazolam versus midazolam for ileocolonoscopy sedation in inflammatory bowel disease: a prospective, patient-blinded, non-inferiority study with weekly time-block allocation
resume: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Colonoscopy is central to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management, but repeated procedures may be limited by anxiety, discomfort and recovery burden. Remimazolam may provide faster recovery than conventional benzodiazepines while preserving the practical advantages of moderate sedation. We compared patient-reported satisfaction, recovery, safety and endoscopic performance with remimazolam versus midazolam in patients with IBD undergoing ileocolonoscopy. METHODS: In this single-centre, prospective, patient-blinded, non-inferiority study using randomized weekly time-block allocation, 200 adults with IBD undergoing elective ileocolonoscopy received remimazolam plus fentanyl or midazolam plus fentanyl. Patients were unaware of the sedative administered. Satisfaction was assessed using a self-administered four-point Likert scale immediately after the procedure and at 24 hours. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients reporting at least "satisfied" immediately after the procedure. Secondary outcomes included "very satisfied" responses, PADSS-defined discharge readiness at 10 and 20 min, adverse events and endoscopic performance. Bayesian analyses used a prespecified non-inferiority margin of -10 percentage points. RESULTS: Overall satisfaction was high in both groups, and remimazolam was non-inferior to midazolam: estimated rates were 96.4% versus 97.3%; risk difference -0.9% (95% credible interval [CrI] -5.8% to 3.7%); posterior probability of non-inferiority 99.94%. "Very satisfied" responses were more frequent with remimazolam: 62.2% versus 48.3%; posterior mean difference 15.8% (95% CrI 3.3% to 28.1%); posterior probability of superiority 99.3%. At 24 hours, satisfaction was 95.0% (remimazolam) and 94.0% (midazolam). PADSS-defined discharge readiness favoured remimazolam at 10 min (65.0% vs 27.5%) and 20 min (88.3% vs 64.2%). Hypotension (3.0% vs 2.0%), hypoxaemia (3.0% vs 4.0%) and flumazenil use (3.0% vs 2.0%) occurred (remimazolam vs midazolam); no severe adverse events occurred. Endoscopic performance was comparable. CONCLUSIONS: Remimazolam plus fentanyl was non-inferior to midazolam plus fentanyl for overall satisfaction, with more "very satisfied" responses and earlier PADSS-defined discharge readiness, without compromising safety or endoscopic performance.
revue: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

titre: Goblet Cell-Deficient Dysplasia in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Review of Clinicopathologic Features
resume: Long-standing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) increases the likelihood of developing both conventional and non-conventional dysplasia, of which the latter is a newly defined group of lesions. IBD-associated goblet cell-deficient dysplasia (GCD), first defined by Choi et al. in 2020, is histologically characterized by complete or near-complete loss of goblet cells, often resulting in eosinophilic cytoplasm. Based on articles published between 2020 and 2025, GCD is most commonly reported in Caucasian patients, with a male predominance and a mean age at diagnosis of approximately 58 years. GCD is mostly associated with ulcerative colitis, particularly in patients with pancolitis, with a mean disease duration of 16 years. Dysplasia is usually characterized as low-grade, and multifocal lesions are less frequent. Lesions are most commonly located in the left colon and appear flat, endoscopically invisible, or polypoid. Molecular analyses indicate p53 abnormalities, aneuploidy, and PIKC3A mutation, although limited by small sample size. In addition, GCD has been found in association with goblet cell-deficient adenocarcinoma, indicating a possible link between these entities. Due to the recent description of these lesions, comprehensive reviews regarding their clinicopathological characteristics are lacking; thus, this is so far the first review precisely focusing on GCD. The prevalence of IBD, as well as the need for a close follow-up and better quality of life in long-standing disease raise awareness to recognition of these newly described entities.

titre: Safety and efficacy of Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus ST36 in the improvement of gut and immune function: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
resume: AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of S. salivarius subsp. thermophilus ST36 in improving intestinal and immune functions. METHODS: A total of 98 healthy adults were enrolled in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial and allocated to receive either ST36 (3 × 10¹⁰ CFU/day, n = 49) or placebo (n = 49) for 8 weeks. Participants were instructed to take the assigned preparation daily and record any adverse events. Gut microbiota composition, serum biomarkers, gastrointestinal function and quality of life were evaluated. A total of 85 participants completed the trial. This study was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry (No.: NCT06779994). RESULTS: ST36 supplementation was associated with a downward trend in serum calprotectin levels, approached statistical significance compared with placebo (p = 0.050), whereas LL-37 levels remained unchanged. Fecal microbiota analysis revealed significant enrichment of the butyrate-producing genus Anaerobutyricum and a concurrent reduction in Bacteroides in the ST36 group, accompanied by favorable, albeit non-significant, trends toward improved gastrointestinal symptom scores and stool type classification (assessed via the Bristol Stool Form Scale) relative to placebo. Sleep quality showed slight improvements in both groups without significant between-group differences. Throughout the 8-week intervention, ST36 exhibited a favorable safety profile, with stable hematological and biochemical parameters and no intervention-related adverse events or allergic reactions reported. CONCLUSION: ST36 supplementation was safe and well tolerated, induced targeted shifts in specific microbial taxa (notably enriching beneficial genera), and showed a favorable trend toward improving gastrointestinal outcomes, with indications of potential immune benefits.

titre: A chronic pancreatitis pain program: comprehensive evaluation, treatment planning, and care for patients with chronic pancreatitis-related pain
resume: OBJECTIVES: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a multifactorial inflammatory syndrome frequently complicated by refractory abdominal pain. Current treatment strategies rely heavily on opioids and invasive surgical procedures. Structural pancreatic pathology correlates poorly with pain severity, and pancreas-independent mechanisms, including nociplastic and centrally mediated processes are increasingly recognized as contributors to pain but remain understood. We describe the Johns Hopkins Chronic Pancreatitis Pain Program, a multidisciplinary initiative integrating psychiatry, neurogastroenterology, pancreatology, and psychology. We present two patient-consented cases to illustrate the application of a neuromodulation-focused, multimodal treatment model. CASE PRESENTATION: Both patients demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in pain, mood, sleep, function, and quality of life following a comprehensive evaluation and targeted pharmacologic and behavioral interventions. In one case, opioid tapering accompanied symptomatic improvement. CONCLUSIONS: These cases illustrate the potential benefits of a multidisciplinary, neuromodulation-focused approach to CP-related pain. Longitudinal data collection is ongoing to further characterize treatment response and pain phenotypes.

titre: Impact of opioids on chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal toxicity: Complementary retrospective and real-world cohorts
resume: BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal toxicity (CIGT) with irinotecan chemotherapy is a major dose-limiting complication that impacts treatment adherence and patient outcomes. Opioids are widely prescribed for cancer-related pain, however their potential to exacerbate CIGT remain poorly defined. METHODS: We evaluated the impact of opioid use on irinotecan chemotherapy tolerance and gastrointestinal adverse events in retrospective and real-world cohorts. We performed a retrospective analysis of 331 patients with gastrointestinal malignancies treated with irinotecan. Repeated opioid use was defined as ≥1-month of opiate use prior to initiation of irinotecan chemotherapy. Primary outcomes included chemotherapy dose reduction and delay; secondary outcomes included gastrointestinal symptoms and hospitalization. Additionally, in a second cohort, we performed a large-scale study using the TriNetX database encompassing patients with colorectal and pancreatic cancers receiving irinotecan with 1-, 3-, or 6-months prior opioid use. Primary outcomes included development of gastrointestinal symptoms, opioid use and overdose. RESULTS: In the retrospective cohort, opioid use was associated with increased odds of chemotherapy dose reduction (odds ratio [OR] 2.14 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.21-3.77) and chemotherapy dose delay (OR 2.74, 95% CI: 1.32-5.69). In the real-world cohort, patients with prior opioid use were at a significantly higher risk of developing GI symptoms and opioid related overdose. CONCLUSION: In both cohort analysis prior opioid use increased the likelihood of chemotherapy intolerance and/or prevalence of gastrointestinal symptoms. IMPACT: These findings highlight prior opioid use as a clinical meaningful contributor to chemotherapy intolerance and quality of life.
revue: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

titre: Nutrition Issues in Children Living with Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Qualitative Study
resume: INTRODUCTION: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) are genetic conditions that impair immune function, increasing susceptibility to infection, risk of severe illness, and impact on quality of life. Nutrition plays a critical role in supporting immune function; however, little research has explored nutrition-related complications in IEI using a qualitative approach. This study is the first qualitative study to investigate a wide range of nutrition-related issues and nutrition care in paediatric IEI across multiple diagnoses in Australia. METHOD: An online survey and qualitative interviews were undertaken to explore nutrition-related issues and nutrition care for individuals with clinically diagnosed IEI. Parents/carers of infants/children (≤10 years) were recruited through social media and patient support networks. Survey data were analysed descriptively; interview data were examined using thematic analysis. RESULTS: Thirteen parents completed the survey; five parents participated in interviews. Most children (n = 11) were diagnosed before age 2, with severe combined immunodeficiency the most common condition. Qualitative findings identified multiple nutrition-related issues, including early breastfeeding cessation, faltering growth, gastrointestinal disturbances, feeding difficulties, poor appetite, and the need for nutritional support. Interviews highlighted inconsistencies and gaps in the provision of nutrition care. CONCLUSION: Nutrition-related issues in IEI are varied, multifactorial, and often complex. Findings highlight the need to recognise nutrition as a core component of IEI management. Developing standardised nutrition guidelines is essential to address current inconsistencies in care and support long-term health and wellbeing for people with IEI and their families.

titre: Improving quality of life in people living with a stoma: the need for a national stoma care pathway
resume: Living with a stoma can significantly affect an individual's physical, psychological and social well-being. Stoma formation is often necessary to manage serious gastrointestinal or urological conditions and can preserve life, but patients frequently experience issues such as post-operative complications, altered body image, decreased self-confidence and reduced participation in social activities. These issues can negatively affect their quality of life, particularly during the initial adjustment period. Stoma care nurses (SCNs) have a crucial role in supporting patients by providing education, clinical management and psychosocial support before surgery, after surgery and in the long term. This article explores the physical, psychological, social and practical issues experienced by people living with a stoma and the contribution of SCNs in addressing them. It also discusses the potential benefits of implementing a national stoma care pathway to ensure equitable access to specialist services and improve patient outcomes and quality of life regardless of geographical location.

titre: Acute physical effort enhances interoceptive accuracy without improving error awareness: evidence from the Heart Rate Discrimination Task
resume: According to Fechner's law, perceived sensations increase logarithmically with stimulus intensity. During exercise, rising physical effort is therefore accompanied by increasingly salient bodily signals such as heart rate. Interoception, the sensing of internal bodily states, supports adaptive responses to these changing demands, for instance, by guiding the regulation of exertion. Beyond physical regulation, interoceptive signals have also been proposed to inform higher-order monitoring processes, such as error detection. Yet it remains unclear whether acute exercise sharpens cardiac interoception and whether this would translate into greater awareness of errors. In a within-participant design, 36 healthy adults completed two tasks while cycling at low versus moderate intensity: a Heart Rate Discrimination Task assessing cardiac interoception and a Go/No-Go task measuring error awareness through post-error reports. Moderate effort reduced interoceptive bias, bringing participants' perceived heart rate closer to their actual heart rate, while discrimination precision remained unchanged. Confidence in interoceptive judgments increased under moderate effort, but this was not accompanied by improved metacognitive insight. In the Go/No-Go task, commission errors were more frequent at moderate intensity, whereas the proportion of detected errors was unchanged. Interoceptive performance did not reliably predict error awareness. These findings suggest that acute exercise recalibrates cardiac judgment bias rather than improving perceptual sensitivity or metacognitive monitoring. This recalibration did not extend to error awareness; however, given the temporal and reporting constraints of the task, the null effect cannot determine whether cardiac signals contribute causally to conscious error detection.

titre: Avoiding the Anxious Self: The Role of Self-Concept Clarity, Alexithymia, and Experiential Avoidance in Social Anxiety
resume: Self-related processes play a significant role in the development and maintenance of social anxiety, yet existing cognitive models have yet to fully elaborate these processes. This paper explores how experiential dimensions of the self are related to the organization of the self-concept among individuals experiencing symptoms of social anxiety. Specifically, the current study investigates whether deficits in emotional awareness (alexithymia) are associated with lower self-concept clarity, a characteristic commonly observed among socially anxious individuals. Further, this paper examines whether experiential avoidance-an established maladaptive coping strategy-moderates the relationships between alexithymia, self-concept clarity, and social anxiety. Findings suggest that self-concept clarity statistically mediates the association between alexithymia and social anxiety. Experiential avoidance was further found to moderate the relationship between alexithymia and self-concept clarity. Implications for clinical practice and future research directions are discussed.

titre: Brain Reorganization Following Psychological Interventions for Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review of Neuroimaging Evidence
resume: Psychological interventions are effective for chronic pain, but their neural mechanisms remain unclear. This review synthesized functional magnetic resonance imaging and electroencephalography evidence on treatment-related brain changes following psychological interventions in adults with chronic non-cancer pain. Seven databases were searched. Eligible studies included adults aged 18-64 receiving a psychological intervention with both neuroimaging and clinical outcomes. Study quality was assessed with the Effective Public Health Practice Project tool. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, findings were synthesized narratively. Nineteen studies (n = 843) were included: 15 randomized controlled trials, 3 within-subject designs, and 1 pilot non-randomized trial. Interventions were mindfulness-based interventions (n = 6), cognitive behavioral therapy (n = 5), hypnosis (n = 3), neurofeedback (n = 3), and other approaches (n = 2). The anterior insula, anterior cingulate and midcingulate cortex, prefrontal cortex, and primary somatosensory cortex were most consistently implicated. Cognitive behavioral therapy reduced somatosensory-limbic coupling and enhanced prefrontal engagement. Mindfulness showed convergent insular and cingulate involvement. Pain reprocessing therapy showed close alignment between observed neural changes and its proposed mechanism, with reduced affective-evaluative pain activation and increased prefrontal-somatosensory connectivity. Hypnosis dissociated somatosensory from affective pain processing. Brain-behavior correlations linked predominantly to cognitive-affective outcomes, including catastrophizing, self-efficacy, and anxiety rather than pain intensity. Across interventions, convergent findings implicated increased prefrontal engagement and reduced affective-evaluative pain processing, broadly consistent with cognitive-affective modulation of pain. These findings offer neurobiological plausibility for clinical approaches targeting catastrophizing and fear-avoidance, though guiding patient selection would require research linking neural change directly to clinical outcome. PERSPECTIVE: This review identified shared neuroanatomical hubs, including increased prefrontal regulation and reduced affective-evaluative pain processing across cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness, hypnosis, and pain reprocessing therapy. These findings provide neurobiological support for established clinical approaches targeting cognitive-affective responses to pain, but do not establish shared causal mechanisms or support patient stratification. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024623019).

titre: The Effects of Nonpharmacologic Interventions to Enhance Sleep Outcomes Among Older People With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
resume: OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of nonpharmacologic interventions on sleep outcomes in older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). DESIGN: A systematic review and meta-analysis. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Older people with MCI. METHODS: A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO was conducted from inception through June 2025 to identify eligible randomized controlled trials. Meta-analyses were conducted using RevMan when appropriate; narrative synthesis was used when pooling was not feasible. Sensitivity analyses explored the influence of study quality on outcomes. RESULTS: Fourteen randomized controlled trials, involving 874 participants, met the inclusion criteria. Exercise and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) were the most frequently studied interventions, each examined in 4 trials. Two studies implemented multicomponent interventions integrating behavioral, cognitive, and lifestyle strategies. Other alternative interventions included transcranial magnetic stimulation, hypnosis, breath-based relaxation, and sport stacking. Pooled analysis showed that exercise significantly improved subjective sleep quality compared with controls (standardized mean difference, -1.78; 95% CI, -3.38 to -0.17; P = .03; I2 = 97%). CBT-I demonstrated a smaller but statistically significant effect (standardized mean difference, -0.85; 95% CI, -1.66 to -0.04; P = .04; I2 = 80%). Sensitivity analyses excluding a high-risk study without blinded assessors yielded reduced but still significant effects. Only a few studies included objective sleep measures, limiting conclusions about physiological outcomes. Multicomponent interventions showed potential benefits, but substantial variability in design indicates the need for standardized development frameworks. Alternative approaches, including transcranial magnetic stimulation, hypnosis, and relaxation therapy, showed preliminary promise but require further rigorous validation. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Nonpharmacologic interventions, particularly exercise and CBT-I, demonstrate potential in improving subjective sleep quality among older adults with MCI. Rigorous research is needed to validate these findings on objective sleep outcomes and to establish robust frameworks for developing and optimizing multicomponent interventions that integrate behavioral and physiological mechanisms to support sleep and cognitive health in this at-risk population.
revue: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

titre: Tuina for post‑stroke depression: a pilot randomized controlled trial of clinical effects and exploratory mechanisms
resume: OBJECTIVE: Accumulating evidence suggests that Tuina therapy(TT) may ameliorate post‑stroke depression (PSD) through modulation of the hypothalamic‑pituitary‑adrenal (HPA) axis and inflammatory responses, though its principal therapeutic mechanism remains unconfirmed. This pilot mechanistic trial aimed to investigate whether Tuina affects HPA‑axis hormones and inflammatory cytokines in patients with PSD, and to explore whether cortisol reduction mediates the observed antidepressant effect. METHODS: In this 2‑week, randomized, assessor‑blind, active‑controlled trial, 42 patients with PSD were assigned to receive Tuina (n=21) or cognitive behavioral therapy(CBT) (n=21). The primary outcome was change in 17‑item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD‑17). Secondary outcomes included Modified Barthel Index (MBI), Fugl‑Meyer Assessment (FMA), Mini‑Mental State Examination (MMSE), and serum biomarkers (adrenocorticotropic hormone, cortisol, and inflammatory cytokines). Data were analyzed by intention‑to‑treat using non‑parametric tests and bootstrap mediation analysis. RESULTS: Both groups improved significantly in HAMD‑17 and MBI (p<0.01). The TT group showed greater HAMD‑17 reduction (median Δ: -5.00 vs. -4.00; p<0.001) and greater reductions in ACTH (p=0.023) and cortisol (p=0.021) than the CBT group. No significant between‑group differences were observed for FMA, MMSE, or any inflammatory cytokine. Cortisol reduction mediated 19.4% of the HAMD‑17 improvement (indirect effect: 0.2867, 95% CI: 0.0337‑0.5975). CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot mechanistic trial, Tuina produced significant downregulation of HPA axis activity, with cortisol partially mediating antidepressant effects. Direct systemic anti‑inflammatory effects were not observed. These findings suggest that HPA axis regulation is a key pathway contributing to the antidepressant effects of Tuina. TRIALREGISTRATION: China Clinical Trial Registry Identifier ChiCTR2400085211.

titre: Intravenous ketamine for major depressive episodes in routine practice: a review of non-randomized evidence on effectiveness and safety
resume: INTRODUCTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have established the acute antidepressant efficacy of intravenous racemic ketamine. However, the evidence remains limited by short-term trial durations, few long-term controlled trials of repeated administration, and the absence of a systematic program for monitoring tolerability and safety. AREAS COVERED: PubMed, Embase and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 30 September 2026 for non-randomized studies of intravenous racemic ketamine in adults with a major depressive episode (MDE). Fifty-six studies were included. After induction, response ranged from 26% to 71% and remission from 14% to 53%, broadly overlapping estimates from RCTs. Durability varied, with benefits waning within weeks in many patients and relapse occurring during maintenance. Attrition was high. Blood pressure elevations were transient, with mean increases varying nearly fivefold across services. Serious adverse events were unreported in 24 studies, and urinary and hepatic outcomes were rarely reported. EXPERT OPINION: Intravenous ketamine is often used as maintenance therapy, yet the durability of its benefits remains uncertain, and the risks of cumulative exposure remain unquantified. Systematic collection of safety and tolerability data is needed to assess long-term safety. Head-to-head comparisons with esketamine, psychedelics, and/or accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation are needed, alongside maintenance trials and studies addressing comorbidities and/or integrating psychotherapy modalities.

fiche.verdict: Une revue de 56 études non randomisées montre que la kétamine IV soulage la dépression mais pose des questions de durabilité et sécurité.

titre: Spectral Decorrelation of Glutamate for Clinical Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
resume: PURPOSE: Although glutamate (Glu) plays a central role in many neuropsychiatric disorders, MRS measurement of Glu often suffers from confounding correlations due to spectral overlap, adversely affecting subsequent clinical correlational analysis. This study aimed to optimize the commonly used 3 T PRESS method to minimize the overall Glu spectral correlation with other neurometabolites. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations combined with a mathematical model of spectral fitting were used to evaluate spectral correlations between Glu and other metabolites. The optimal {TE1, TE} pair minimizing the overall Glu correlation was identified and validated by analyzing in vivo measurement of Glu in the anterior cingulate cortex. The robustness of the optimization was further assessed under varying spectral linewidths and altered metabolite concentrations. RESULTS: The optimal {TE1, TE} values for 4, 6, 8, and 10 Hz linewidth were found to be {42, 100}, {40, 95}, {38, 94}, and {38, 90} ms, respectively. These optimal {TE1, TE} pairs reduced the overall Glu spectral correlation coefficient to less than 0.05, corresponding to a negligible effect size. This reduction was consistently observed in both Monte Carlo simulations and analysis of in vivo measurements and remained robust across metabolite level variations typically seen in bipolar disorder, methamphetamine use disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and hepatic encephalopathy. CONCLUSION: Systematic optimization of the {TE1, TE} pair enables decorrelation of Glu MRS measurement at 3 Tesla by effectively minimizing confounding spectral correlations among brain metabolites. The proposed approach provides a robust and clinically applicable framework that decorrelates Glu MRS measurements for viable downstream clinical analyses.

titre: From Order to Disorder: Addressing Underrecognized Obsessive Compulsive Disorder in Military and Veteran Healthcare
resume: Active-duty military personnel face unique challenges, including high-stress work environments, potential trauma exposure, and adherence to rigorous standards, which may contribute to the development or worsening of obsessive-compulsive symptoms. Obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) is a chronic and often debilitating mental health condition that may be underrecognized and is diagnosed late in veterans, with an average age of first diagnosis at 54 years in VHA settings-far later than in civilian populations. Whether OCD prevalence differs meaningfully between military and civilian populations remains unclear, though several factors specific to military culture may influence symptom recognition and expression. For example, military personnel often learn that failing to meet standards results in correction, and at times, discipline, which may reinforce behaviors related to perfectionism, precision, and order. Because such behaviors are often normalized within military culture, clinicians may misclassify true OCD symptoms as expected military routine rather than a mental health concern. This risk may be compounded in settings where OCD symptoms overlap with other common presentations. For example, providers treating posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) may not reliably differentiate intrusive catastrophic OCD-related images from intrusive memories of previously experienced trauma, despite evidence that OCD and PTSD frequently co-occur. Further complicating recognition, no existing OCD screening or assessment measures have been validated for use in military or veteran populations, and some items may be more likely to yield false positives given their overlap with military-specific training and culture. It is also possible that retiring from the military may exacerbate OCD symptoms, as civilian life is often more flexible and less structured than military service, and the loss of military-specific routines and support systems may heighten anxiety and adjustment difficulties. While standards of care exist for PTSD, there are currently no comparable treatment guidelines or pathways for OCD within the Department of Defense (DoD) or Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Strengthening recognition of OCD within primary care and integrated behavioral health settings, which serve as key points of contact for identifying mental health symptoms that might otherwise go unrecognized, alongside targeted recognition efforts within specialty mental health settings (e.g., PTSD clinics), may offer the greatest opportunity to improve case detection. Future research to adapt and validate OCD measures for military and veteran populations, and to characterize common OCD symptom patterns in this population, is needed to support earlier identification and more effective treatment of OCD within DoD and VHA.

titre: A scoping review characterizing avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder in pediatric populations based on phenotype
resume: This scoping review investigates differences in age, sex, comorbid diagnoses, and clinical presentation across avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) phenotypes including fear of aversive consequences, sensory sensitivity and selectivity, lack of interest, and combined phenotypes, in pediatric populations. Articles published in English between January 2010 and February 2026 that included children under 18 years-of-age were pulled from PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase (n = 12). All studies reported on the three primary phenotypes separately (n = 12); five of the studies also identified combined ARFID phenotypes. No single phenotype was consistently the most prevalent across studies. Combined phenotypes were common; in the five studies reporting them, 14.5-54.7% of participants were classified into a combined phenotype. Studies classified patients differently; while some studies assigned patients to a single primary phenotype, others allowed for overlapping, non-exclusive classification or left patients unclassified, limiting comparison across studies. Age and sex distribution were heterogeneous, yet fear of aversive consequences demonstrated the strongest female predominance and association with anxiety. Sensory sensitivity and selectivity had the lowest rates of weight loss, while lack of interest was most associated with restricted nutrition, growth failure and comorbid ADHD and OCD. We suggest more nuanced identification and classification of patients by phenotype in future research to aid with treatment development.

titre: Impact of Depressive Symptom Trajectories on the Risk of Gastrointestinal Disorders: A Longitudinal Prospective Cohort Study Using CHARLS
resume: Background Depression and gastrointestinal disorders frequently co-occur. However, few studies have systematically explored the long-term effects of depressive symptom trajectories on gastrointestinal disorders. This study aimed to clarify the differential impacts of depressive symptom trajectories on gastrointestinal disorders. Methods Using five waves of longitudinal data (2011–2020) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we defined the exposure period for depressive symptom trajectories as 2011–2015 and the outcome period for incident gastrointestinal disorders as 2015–2020. A total of 6108 participants were included. Group-based trajectory modeling identified distinct depressive symptom trajectories. Longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation examined associations between depressive symptom trajectories and the risk of incident gastrointestinal disorders. Results Three distinct trajectories were identified: non-depressive (69.0%), low-depressive (25.7%), and high-depressive (5.3%). Cumulative gastrointestinal disease incidence was 6.88%, 10.58%, and 19.14% for the three groups, respectively. Compared with the non-depressive group, both the low-depressive (OR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.24–1.88, P < 0.001) and the high-depressive groups (OR = 3.02, 95% CI: 1.81–5.04, P < 0.001) had significantly increased risks of gastrointestinal disorders. The high-depressive group also showed a significantly higher risk than the low-depressive group (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.40–2.76, P < 0.001). Conclusions Depressive symptom trajectories were significantly associated with the subsequent gastrointestinal disease risk. Of these, the high-depressive trajectory carries the highest risk. These findings demonstrate the importance of dynamically monitoring depressive symptom trajectories and early interventions for high-risk populations.

fiche.verdict: Les trajectoires de symptômes dépressifs chroniques augmentent significativement le risque de développer des troubles gastro-intestinaux, avec un risque proportionnel à la sévérité.
fiche.population: 6108 participants (étude CHARLS, Chine)
fiche.intervention: Évaluation des trajectoires de symptômes dépressifs (2011-2015) et incidence des troubles gastro-intestinaux (2015-2020)

titre: AB-2004, an autism candidate therapeutic, drives distinct taxonomic and functional potential changes in the gut microbiome of wild-type and Shank3B-/- mice
resume: Abstract The gut microbiome is increasingly implicated in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), with reports of compositional and functional dysbiosis. Microbially derived metabolites, including 4-ethylphenol and p -cresol are associated with heightened levels of anxiety and irritability seen in ASD. AB-2004 is an investigational therapeutic designed to sequester these metabolites, but its effects on gut microbial ecology in mice remain uncharacterised. We examined the impact of AB-2004 on the gut microbiome in the Shank3B ⁻/⁻ mouse model of autism as well as wild-type (WT) littermate controls. Mouse faecal DNA across nine timepoints underwent 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, diversity analyses, differential abundance testing, functional-potential inference, and random forest classification. AB-2004 induced distinct taxonomic and functional shifts in both genotypes. Alpha diversity changes were significant only in WT animals, while beta diversity differed between treated and control groups in both genotypes. Differential abundance analysis identified treatment-associated changes in Lachnospiraceae and Muribaculaceae and shifts in KEGG orthologs mapping to microbial communication, cell-wall remodelling, and aminobenzoate degradation, suggesting competitive pathway diversion as a candidate mechanism. Random forest models reliably discriminated treated from control animals and identified candidate microbiome biomarkers of treatment response. Overall, AB-2004 selectively modulates taxonomic and functional profiles without broadly disrupting microbial community structure. These data suggest AB-2004 may influence microbial pathways linked to aromatic compound processing, but mechanisms require direct validation. This study provides a foundation for multiomic investigations to determine whether microbiome shifts translate to altered metabolite profiles and host-relevant outcomes.

fiche.intervention: AB-2004 vs contrôle non traité, souris autistes et sauvages

fiche.conclusion: Les auteurs concluent qu'AB-2004 module sélectivement le microbiote sans le perturber globalement, mais que les mécanismes nécessitent validation directe.

titre: Born on Rhythms: Mother–Foetus and -Infant Neurophysiology as a Dynamic System of Metastable Coupled Oscillators
resume: The human embryo grows within a pulsatile maternal milieu structured by cardiac, respiratory, locomotor, vocal and circadian rhythms. Here we integrate evidence from embryology, foetal physiology, developmental cognitive neuroscience and chronobiology: we review how the foetal heart and placenta co-develop under maternal haemodynamic forcing, how maternal rhythms reach the foetus and how they may modulate foetal physiology. We propose that multimodal, semi-periodic input streams may provide a temporal reference frame scaffolding early timing abilities and autonomic self-regulation. In this view, we discuss that co-regulation may ground interoception and allostasis. Next, we formalize the mother–foetus and mother-infant dyads as multiscale systems of coupled oscillators spanning about seven orders of magnitude in frequency - from circadian cycles to neural oscillations. Within this coordination-dynamics framework we propose that healthy co-regulation is marked by metastability: flexible and transient coordination, preserving the endogenous tendencies for systems to display endogenous behaviours and to couple with other systems in an adaptive manner. The framework yields testable predictions on the link between dyadic coordination dynamics and developmental outcome. We are, quite literally, born on rhythms.

fiche.verdict: Modèle théorique formalisant les rythmes neurophysiologiques mère-foetus/enfant comme base de l'intéroception et de l'autorégulation autonomique.
resultats_cles: Intégration des données d'embryologie, physiologie foetale et neurosciences cognitives
La co-régulation dynamique grounding l'intéroception et l'allostasie
La métastabilité dyadique comme marqueur d'une co-régulation saine
fiche.conclusion: Les rythmes maternels et foetaux forment un système oscillatoire couplé sous-tendant les capacités temporelles et le développement de l'intéroception.

titre: Psychophysiological preparation improves performance without compromising procedural safety in a high-risk motor task
resume: High-risk operational tasks require rapid movement without compromising safety-critical motor control. This study examined whether a brief psychophysiological pre-activation routine (PPAR) improves performance and procedural safety during an ecologically valid military obstacle course. Fifty experienced military personnel were allocated to PPAR (n = 25) or a time-matched motivational control (n = 25). Participants completed an 850-m course involving 17 obstacles and 26 prescribed safety procedures on two consecutive days. Before the second trial, PPAR combined breathing regulation, interoceptive and motor imagery, attentional focusing, and self-talk. Completion time and Safety Incident Score (SIS) were assessed in all participants; heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) were recorded in 40. Completion time decreased by 11.1% after PPAR (715.7 ± 104.2 to 636.2 ± 71.9 s), versus 2.1% in controls (719.9 ± 99.7 to 704.6 ± 74.6 s; Group × Session interaction: p < .001, η²p = .40). At POST, SIS was significantly lower in the PPAR group than in controls (0.08 ± 0.28 vs. 0.80 ± 1.08; U = 465.5, p < .001, r = .490). PPAR increased pre-performance HR (93 to 108 beats/min) and significantly modulated HRV spectral indices, with significant Group × Session interactions. A 10-min multimodal preparation routine improved completion time during a demanding real-world task while being associated with fewer safety incidents and distinct pre-performance cardiac responses.

fiche.verdict: Une préparation psychophysiologique brève incluant de l'imagerie intéroceptive améliore la performance motrice et réduit les erreurs de sécurité.

titre: Decoding Affect: A Computational Model of Affective Adaptation and Construction
resume: Affective construction and adaptation are complementary processes through which affective value is generated and evolves over time. Although prior research has identified key determinants of these processes, including reference points, stimulus inherent value, attention, negativity bias, adaptation rate, and time, a unified framework that quantifies how these factors interact and jointly shape affect remains lacking, leaving important nonlinear affective phenomena insufficiently explained. We propose the Attention-Reference Interaction Adaptation (ARIA) framework, which formalizes affective valuation as an attention-gated dual-reference integration process that evaluates current sensory inputs relative to both prior experience and allostatic set-points. By specifying how value salience and negativity bias jointly govern attention allocation and adaptation rate, ARIA suggests that relativity and asymmetry (two foundational properties of affective valuation) arise from a shared attentional mechanism. Consequently, these properties are contingent, dynamically coupled, and conditionally reducible, rather than fixed, independent, and irreducible axioms as assumed in classical behavioral economic theories. Furthermore, we map ARIA's computational components onto reward and interoceptive prediction errors, capturing how external and internal discrepancies jointly drive the construction of affective experience. Through numerical simulations and an initial empirical test, we show that ARIA reproduces classic affective phenomena, such as exponential decay, affective after-reactions, and alliesthesia, while also accounting for anomalous patterns, including cases in which environmental improvements fail to elicit pleasure and conditions under which inherently positive stimuli adapt more slowly than negative ones. Ultimately, ARIA offers a tractable computational framework for explaining affective dynamics and generating testable predictions about well-being and environmental experience.

fiche.verdict: Présentation d'un modèle computationnel (ARIA) intégrant attention, adaptation et erreurs de prédiction intéroceptives dans la construction de l'affect.
resultats_cles: Formalisation de l'évaluation affective comme un processus d'intégration à double référence piloté par l'attention
Lien entre composantes computationnelles et erreurs de prédiction intéroceptives / de récompense
Reproduction par simulation de phénomènes classiques (décroissance exponentielle, alliesthésie) et anormaux
fiche.conclusion: Le modèle ARIA offre un cadre théorique computationnel pour expliquer la dynamique des affects et générer des prédictions empiriques.
