fiche.conclusion_simple: Ce modèle théorique relie l'intéroception à la régulation affective, offrant des pistes de réflexion sur l'allostasie sans application directe.

titre: Adjunctive Galactol®, a multi-enzyme dietary supplement, in adults with irritable bowel syndrome following a low-FODMAP diet: a multicenter randomized controlled study
resume: Background Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut–brain interaction in which food-related triggers, visceral hypersensitivity, intestinal fermentation, and altered luminal responses may contribute to symptoms. Although the low-FODMAP diet is an established strategy, its restrictive nature and persistent fermentation-related symptoms in some patients justify adjunctive approaches. Digestive enzymes may reduce poorly digested substrates reaching the colon, thereby limiting fermentation, gas production, osmotic load, and luminal distension. Objective To evaluate whether α- and β-galactosidases plus an Aspergillus niger -derived prolyl endopeptidase provide additional benefit when added to a low-FODMAP diet in adults with Rome IV IBS. Methods In this prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled study, 300 adults with Rome IV IBS were allocated to a low-FODMAP diet alone or the same diet plus enzyme supplementation for 14 days. Gastrointestinal symptoms were assessed at baseline and day 14 using 0–10 visual analog scales for bloating, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, abdominal pain, and defecation urgency. Stool consistency, evacuation frequency, and diarrhea frequency were also evaluated. Repeated-measures GLM assessed time effects and time × group interactions. Results Of 300 participants, 292 completed the study. Groups were comparable at baseline for sex, age, body weight, IBS subtype, and reported food intolerances. Both groups improved significantly over time, but symptom reductions were greater with enzyme supplementation. Improvements for bloating, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, and abdominal pain were −40.38% versus −26.51%, −44.67% versus −28.10%, −45.47% versus −28.60%, and −53.53% versus −32.11%, respectively. Greater improvements were also observed for evacuation and diarrhea frequency. Time × group interactions were significant for bloating, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, abdominal pain, evacuation frequency, Bristol Stool Scale score, and diarrhea frequency. Defecation urgency improved in both groups without a significant time × group interaction. Effects were not significantly influenced by age, sex, lactose intolerance, or gluten intolerance. Patient-reported gastrointestinal wellbeing improved more in the supplemented group. Conclusion Adding α- and β-galactosidases plus an Aspergillus niger -derived prolyl endopeptidase to a low-FODMAP diet provided additional clinical benefit in adults with Rome IV IBS, particularly for bloating, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, and abdominal pain. These findings support digestive enzyme therapy as a complementary, substrate-oriented strategy in IBS dietary management. Clinical trial registration The ClinicalTrials.gov registration identifier is NCT07465562. The publicly accessible URL is: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07465562 .

fiche.titre_court: Supplément enzymatique adjonctif en IBS low-FODMAP
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'ajout d'enzymes digestives au régime low-FODMAP améliore les symptômes IBS, notamment ballonnements et douleurs, à confirmer sur le long terme.

titre: Temporal validation of a locally deployed Qwen2.5-7B workflow for text-based psychological screening support in disorders of gut–brain interaction
resume: Background Disorders of gut–brain interaction (DGBIs) are accompanied by psychological distress, sleep disturbance, and somatic symptom burden, but relevant cues in gastroenterology records may be brief. Objective This study aims to evaluate whether a fixed local large language model (LLM) workflow can identify DGBI outpatients who warrant further psychological screening or clinician review from short, pre-questionnaire electronic medical record text extracts. Methods This single-center retrospective study used a temporally separated development-and-test design. Among 660 candidate encounters, 460 met prespecified eligibility criteria; 160 earlier encounters were used to develop and lock the workflow, and 300 later encounters formed the temporal test cohort. Two blinded physicians independently reviewed the same de-identified narratives, with adjudication by a third physician. Physician text judgment was the primary reference; Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 were separate exploratory symptom-burden measures. Sensitivity of risk_signal was the principal performance measure. Results All 300 test encounters generated valid structured outputs. Physician adjudication identified 114 positive, 173 negative, and 13 insufficient cases; the principal analysis included 287 definitive yes/no cases. risk_signal achieved 98.2% sensitivity [95% confidence interval (CI), 93.8%–99.5%], 91.3% specificity (86.2%–94.7%), and 94.1% accuracy (90.7%–96.3%). Across all 300 encounters, final_action routed 142 records (47.3%) compared with 128 (42.7%) for risk_signal, adding 14 reviews. In a fixed-seed 30-encounter sample rerun three times under Ollama v0.30.7, all 90 outputs were valid and all case-level outputs were identical across runs (30/30; 100%, 95% CI, 88.6%–100.0%). No self_harm_review_required flag was triggered (0/300). Conclusions The fixed local workflow showed high agreement with physician judgments derived from the same short narratives and repeatable outputs in a single tested runtime configuration. These results do not establish predictive validity for independent psychiatric outcomes, contextual superiority over reproducible lexical baselines, or the effectiveness of human–LLM interaction. External and prospective workflow validation is required before clinical implementation.

titre: Multi-omics analysis reveals that gut microbiota modulates the association between dietary imbalance and gastrointestinal symptoms in children with functional dyspepsia
resume: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a prevalent pediatric gastrointestinal disorder. Although dietary factors and gut microbiota dysbiosis are implicated in its pathogenesis, the interplay among diet, microbiota, and FD remains poorly understood. Methods This case–control study enrolled 34 children with FD and 40 healthy controls. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Fecal microbiota was profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics was employed to detect fecal metabolites. Clinical symptoms were evaluated using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) and the Functional Gastrointestinal Disorder Symptom Screening Questionnaire (FGIDQ). Results We identified 16 differentially abundant bacterial species and 476 differential metabolites (458 downregulated, 18 upregulated). Folate intake was significantly lower in the FD group ( p = 0.0038). Three major dietary patterns were identified: pattern 1 (high-fat, high-protein dietary pattern), pattern 2 (traditional staple food dietary pattern), and pattern 3 (diverse mixed diet dietary pattern). The standardized scores for patterns 2 and 3 were significantly lower in the FD group than in the control group. Correlation analysis revealed that the abundance of g__Monoglobus was positively correlated with intakes of valine, protein, and zinc; g__Intestinibacter abundance showed a significant positive correlation with tryptophan intake; whereas g__Senegalimassilia abundance was inversely associated with dietary fiber intake. Exploratory moderation analyses further indicated that Intestinibacte r abundance significantly and positively moderated the associations between dietary pattern 2 and constipation score ( β = 0.289, p = 0.037), as well as between dietary pattern 3 and constipation score ( β = 0.596, p = 0.022). Similarly, Erysipelatoclostridium abundance also significantly and positively moderated the relationship between dietary pattern 3 and constipation score ( β = 0.574, p = 0.023). Collectively, these findings suggest that specific gut microbes may be associated with the relationship between dietary patterns and clinical symptoms. Conclusion Gut microbiota dysbiosis may modulate the association between dietary patterns and clinical symptoms in children with FD. Opportunistic pathogen enrichment, beneficial bacteria depletion, and protective metabolite loss form a diet–microbiota–metabolite dysregulation axis, offering targets for precision dietary and microbiota-based interventions and dietary guidance for children with FD, especially adherence to traditional staple-food and diverse mixed dietary patterns.

titre: A REVIEW: ROLE OF PROBIOTICS IN HUMAN HEALTH
resume: Probiotics are live microorganism that have beneficial effects on health when taken in moderation. In pharmaceutical and medical research, they have receive significant attention. because of their capacity two preserve microbial equilibrium, strengthen integrity of the intestinal barrier, oppose pathogenic microorganism, and regulate host immune responses, Lactobacillus and related lactic acid bacteria have draw and significant scientific attention among the probiotics that have been thoroughly examined. Those are living microorganisms found in the human digestive system. One crucial role is that they affect the host microflora’s populations or activities in the digestive tract, the vaginal either the skin or the respiratory tract. Numerous processes, such as generation of organic acids and antimicrobial metabolites, the competitive exclusion of pathogens, the modification of immune cell and epithelial signalling , and the transposition of microbial metabolic activity , mediate there positive effects. Although those are being investigated in funtional foods , nutraceuticals , therapeutic formulations , and emerging microbiome-oriented interference from a pharmaceutical perspective,Their effectiveness is strain specific and depends on host physiology, dosage, viability, formulation features, and interactions with the resident microbiota. Lactobacillus relieves intestinal inflammation as well as Alleviate symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) . Their development containing nutraceuticals and therapeutic formulations has been made easier by advancements in pharmaceutical technology. However, probiotic potency remains strain- specific and it is affected by viability, dosage, formulation characteristics , and factors related to the host.

titre: Development and evaluation of a modern, personalised prognostic prediction model for overall survival in real-world patients with glioblastoma using machine-learning methods
resume: Background Glioblastoma survival remains highly heterogeneous, with outcomes influenced by treatment and patient characteristics. Existing prognostic models demonstrate variable performance across studies and often rely on limited datasets. Using a multinational cohort of 1857 glioblastoma patients aligned with the 2021 WHO classification of central nervous system tumours, incorporating molecular and clinical variables, we aimed to develop an internally validated prognostic model to support individualised survival prediction. Material and Methods Using the Histo-Mol GBM dataset, a prognostic modelling framework was developed to estimate individualised, time-dependent survival probabilities up to 50 months across clinically relevant timepoints (pre-surgery, post-surgery, and post-oncology treatment). Multiple survival modelling approaches were initially evaluated, including Cox proportional hazards, tree-based, and neural network models, with SHAP-based assessment of predictor importance applied across model types. Continuous variables were modelled to capture potential non-linear effects. Internal validation was performed using 400 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction. Model performance was assessed using the concordance index (C-index), integrated Brier score (IBS), and calibration, including visual assessment with calibration plots and quantitative metrics (ICI, E50). Results Median overall survival was 10 months for the whole cohort and 15 months among patients receiving aggressive treatment (59.7%). A total of 1,539 patients were included in the final post-oncology treatment model. The final model was an unpenalised Cox proportional hazards model including age, performance status, contrast enhancement, tumour location, treatment type, MGMT methylation status, antiepileptic drug use, histological grade, and rapid early progression features. The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.768 (95% CI 0.757-0.779) and IBS was 0.097 (95% CI 0.091-0.105). Calibration demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes across clinically relevant time points (6, 12, 18, and 24 months), with ICI and E50 values ranging from 0.016 to 0.044. The strongest predictors included treatment type, extent of resection, performance status, MGMT methylation status, and age. Conclusion An internally validated prognostic model using routinely available clinical and molecular variables demonstrated good discrimination and calibration. This approach enables individualised survival prediction and may support clinical decision-making and inform the design and evaluation of interventional trials in glioblastoma. External validation is ongoing.

titre: Recombinant nodavirus antigen triggers antiviral responses and engages lysosomal pathways in fish cells
resume: Nervous necrosis virus (NNV) is a pathogen of marine fish primarily infecting early larval stages, where outbreaks can result in mortality rates approaching 100%. At these stages, fish are highly sensitive to handling, making vaccination by injection challenging. Although immersion vaccination is a common alternative, oral delivery through feed represents the most suitable strategy to minimize handling stress and reduce vaccination costs. Here, we developed and characterized a platform based on nanostructured viral proteins assembled as inclusion bodies (IBs) called nanopellets (NPs). The capsid protein of nodavirus RGNNV/SJNNV (CP) fused to IFN-γ was expressed in Escherichia coli , providing a low-cost, high-yield antigen production platform. These NPs retained their morphological integrity under diverse conditions, facilitating storage, transport, and incorporation into feed. NPs are efficiently internalized by gilthead seabream (SaB-1) and zebrafish (ZFL) cells, and gene expression analysis indicates that they elicit an antiviral response in both models. Furthermore, increased mhc-i expression together with NP co-localization with endo-lysosomal compartments support major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)-related responses potentially relevant to intracellular antigen-processing pathways. Overall, these findings support the potential use of NPs for the future development of oral prophylactic strategies against NNV. Key points NPs retain morphological stability under acidic pH, salinity and high temperature NPs are efficiently internalized by fish brain cells, triggering an antiviral response NPs traffic to endo-lysosomal compartments and induce MHC-i upregulation

titre: IMPACTOS DA IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DO IVA DUAL NA APURAÇÃO DE CRÉDITOS TRIBUTÁRIOS PARA O MICROEMPREENDEDOR INDIVIDUAL (MEI): UMA ANÁLISE SOB A ÓTICA DA CONTINUIDADE E DO FLUXO DE CAIXA
resume: O sistema tributário brasileiro passa por uma transição histórica com a aprovação da Emenda Constitucional no 132/2023, que instituiu o IVA Dual composto pela Contribuição Social sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) e pelo Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS). Este estudo analisa os impactos dessa mudança sobre o Microempreendedor Individual (MEI), especialmente no tocante à apropriação de créditos tributários e à sustentabilidade financeira. A questão norteadora é: Quais são os impactos da implementação do IVA Dual para o MEI, especialmente quanto à apropriação de créditos tributários? A metodologia caracteriza-se como aplicada, descritiva e quanti-qualitativa, fundamentada em pesquisa bibliográfica, documental e estudo de caso da empresa MULTSAF Publicidade, localizada em Manaus-AM. Na simulação, o tributo líquido mensal passou de R$ 86,05 (DAS-MEI) para R$ 887,75, e os créditos de insumos cobriram apenas 53,47% do débito de saída, de modo que a hipótese de compensação integral do débito de saída foi apenas parcialmente confirmada. Embora o crédito tributário represente um ativo compensável nos termos da Estrutura Conceitual (CPC 00 R2), a operacionalização fora do regime unificado do Simples Nacional, somada à retenção do tributo na liquidação financeira (Split Payment), impõe pressão sobre o fluxo de caixa, exigindo gestão contábil informatizada e planejamento estratégico de capital de giro. Conclui-se, nos limites do cenário simulado, que a continuidade do MEI sob o IVA Dual tende a depender da transição de uma gestão empírica para uma governança contábil-financeira estruturada.

titre: Acupuncture for post-stroke cognitive impairment: a mechanistic hypothesis linking microbiota-gut-brain axis to brain-network remodelling
resume: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), a prevalent long-term stroke sequela worldwide, hinders neurological recovery and elevates mortality. Monotherapy with cholinesterase inhibitors yields modest benefits accompanied by adverse effects, creating demand for integrated therapies. Mounting studies indicate that microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) disruption and brain network dysfunction contribute to PSCI. Nevertheless, the causal association between gut microbiota dyshomeostasis and central neural network remodelling, as well as the underlying mechanisms of acupuncture, are not fully clarified. Based on literature from PubMed, Web of Science and CNKI published between 2010 and 2026, this review puts forward a hypothesis: acupuncture ameliorates PSCI via a sequential pathway centred on the MGBA, which restores gut microbiota homeostasis, mediates gut–brain signalling and remodels dynamic brain networks. Evidence from diverse clinical and preclinical works supports separate segments of this pathway, yet the complete causal cascade remains unproven. This model conceptualises PSCI as a central-peripheral coupling disorder driven by cerebral injury, gut dysbiosis, immune-inflammation and brain network failure, where gut microbial disturbance may initiate this pathological cycle. Post-stroke gut dysbiosis can induce microglial M1 polarisation and damage core cognitive networks, likely via short-chain fatty acid reduction, intestinal barrier leakage and abnormal vagal transmission. Acupuncture can reshape gut microbiota, preserve intestinal tight junctions and trigger cholinergic anti-inflammatory responses, but its MGBA-dependent modulation of brain network activity needs further verification. This integrative framework interprets acupuncture’s regulatory effects, connects peripheral and central mechanisms, and supplies theoretical support for future acupuncture research on PSCI.

titre: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions in sleep deprivation-associated multi-organ injury: mechanisms, evidence, and translational challenges
resume: Sleep deprivation is increasingly recognized as a systemic physiological stressor that can disrupt inter-organ homeostasis and contribute to dysfunction across the nervous, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, hepatic, pulmonary, and renal systems. Although traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas and their bioactive constituents have shown potentially protective effects in experimental models of sleep deprivation, the available evidence remains fragmented across organ systems, intervention types, and mechanistic pathways. However, it remains unclear how the shared pathophysiological mechanisms of sleep-deprivation-associated multi-organ injury relate to the reported actions of individual TCM-related interventions and whether the available evidence supports translation. Here, we reviewed literature from PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure from database inception to 1 May 2026 to integrate evidence on sleep-deprivation-induced organ injury, shared molecular mechanisms, TCM theoretical frameworks and treatment principles, and the pharmacological actions of TCM formulas, preparations, fractions, and bioactive compounds. We also critically evaluated methodological limitations affecting interpretation and translation. The available evidence indicates that sleep deprivation promotes multi-organ injury through interconnected disturbances involving oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, neuroendocrine imbalance, and disruption of the microbiota–gut–brain axis. Preclinical studies further suggest that selected TCM interventions can modulate several of these processes, with reported pathways including Nrf2-, NF-κB-, and NLRP3-related signaling. However, these pathways are common stress-response hubs rather than TCM-specific targets, and the evidence is limited by heterogeneous sleep-deprivation models, insufficient characterization of tested preparations, variable methodological quality, unequal translational relevance across experimental systems, and a predominance of preclinical data. Selected TCM-related preparations and compounds show experimental effects on sleep-deprivation-associated neurobehavioral and gut-related outcomes. However, mechanistic findings from cellular systems and other injury models do not establish clinical efficacy or multi-organ protection. Translation requires reproducible, chemically characterized interventions, study-level methodological appraisal, causal and exposure-based validation, and controlled human studies with clinically meaningful and organ-specific outcomes.

titre: The Probiotic Paradox in Pediatric Autism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
resume: Probiotics are widely used in pediatric autism spectrum disorder (ASD) based on microbiota–gut–brain plausibility, creating a “probiotic paradox”: enthusiastic open-label reports against uncertain controlled efficacy. Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261484246), we searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP to 30 August 2026 for probiotic studies in youth (≤18 years) with ASD. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were pooled with restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models and Hartung–Knapp adjustment; non-randomized studies were synthesized separately. Risk of bias, required information size, and GRADE certainty were assessed. Seventeen studies (13 RCTs, four non-randomized) were eligible; 10 RCTs (N = 542) were pooled. Probiotics produced a small nominal reduction in core ASD severity (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.37; p = 0.019; I2 = 0%; low certainty) which lost significance after excluding two high-risk trials (SMD = 0.15, 95% CI −0.08 to 0.38) and approached zero across double-blind caregiver-rated trials (SMD = 0.07, 95% CI −0.15 to 0.29). Same-instrument SRS/SRS-2 pooling gave MD = 1.43 T-score points (95% CI −4.44 to 7.30). Gastrointestinal, adaptive-functioning and repetitive-behavior estimates were inconclusive. No serious adverse events were reported, though monitoring was incomplete. Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a bias-robust benefit for core ASD symptoms.

titre: The Gut Microbiota–Metabolite–Nrf2 Axis in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Potential Mechanisms and Current Evidence
resume: The gut–brain axis plays a crucial role in neurodegenerative diseases, but the molecular mechanism linking the gut microbiota to neuronal dysfunction has not been fully elucidated. The nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway is a core component of this process, as it is a key pathway for regulating antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses. This article reviews the existing research evidence for the gut microbiota–metabolite–Nrf2 axis in Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Preclinical studies have shown that microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and tryptophan derivatives can activate Nrf2-dependent transcription of antioxidant enzymes, thereby exerting neuroprotective effects. Among them, evidence related to Parkinson’s disease is the most conclusive, while the evidence related to Alzheimer’s disease is moderate, and there are only preliminary research results for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. However, most of the existing data come from in vitro experiments and animal experiments, and human research evidence is still mainly based on correlation studies. This review points out the potential therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative diseases and proposes that these diseases can be regarded as brain lesions caused by systemic oxidative–immune imbalance rather than isolated brain damage; this view still requires more powerful causal evidence to be confirmed.

fiche.conclusion: Les neurodégénéroses pourraient résulter d'un déséquilibre systémique oxydatif-inflammatoire.

titre: Lilium–egg yolk composite granules ameliorates depressive-like behaviors in CUMS rats with associated changes in neuroinflammation, gut microbiota, and SCFAs
resume: Objective To investigate the effects of lilium –egg yolk composite granules (BHT) on depressive-like behaviors, gut microbiota, and fecal fatty acid profiles in rats exposed to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Methods Seventy-two male SD rats were randomized into control, CUMS, three BHT dose groups, and fluoxetine (FLU) groups ( n = 12/group). CUMS and individual housing were combined with concurrent oral gavage for 28 days. Behavioral tests, histological examination, electron microscopy, and molecular assays assessed behavioral changes, hippocampal injury, mitochondrial ultrastructure, and inflammatory markers. Fecal metagenomics and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry were performed in control, CUMS, medium-dose BHT, and fluoxetine groups. Microbial composition and functional potential were evaluated using diversity analysis, KEGG annotation, and LEfSe. Results BHT reduced forced swim immobility and improved open field activity at some doses, accompanied by attenuated hippocampal and mitochondrial ultrastructural damage and changes in inflammatory markers and PINK1, Parkin, and BDNF expression. Microbial community structure differed among the four groups (ANOSIM, R = 0.433, p = 0.001). KEGG functional clustering suggested that BHT-associated microbial profiles shifted toward controls, involving amino acid, carbohydrate, and energy metabolism. LEfSe revealed enrichment of Alistipes and Alistipes finegoldii in CUMS rats and Duncaniella in controls. BHT enriched Oscillibacter and Anaerotruncus , including Oscillibacter hominis , Oscillibacter sp. CAG-155, and Anaerotruncus colihominis . Compared with CUMS, medium-dose BHT increased fecal isobutyrate and isovalerate and decreased acetate, propionate, hexanoate, heptanoate, and octanoate concentrations (all p 0.05). Conclusion BHT ameliorates depressive-like behaviors during chronic stress exposure, accompanied by changes in hippocampal inflammatory markers, microbial composition, and fecal fatty acid profiles. These findings suggest possible involvement of microbiota–gut–brain interactions and provide preclinical support for further investigation of BHT as a dietary intervention and functional food ingredient for emotional well-being.

titre: Research progress on the role of gut bacterial secretion systems in central nervous system inflammatory diseases
resume: The gut microbiota, often regarded as an important “functional organ,” contributes to the regulation of brain function through multiple pathways, including neural, immune, endocrine, and metabolic mechanisms. In recent years, the role of the gut–brain axis in neurodegenerative diseases, neuroimmune disorders, psychiatric and psychological conditions, and cerebrovascular diseases has attracted considerable attention. Previous research has focused primarily on gut microbial composition and its metabolites. However, bacterial secretion systems—key molecular machineries mediating the transport of materials and the exchange of information between bacteria and their hosts, as well as among bacteria—may constitute a critical functional interface linking gut microbial dysbiosis to pathological changes in the central nervous system. Gut bacteria can release or deliver toxins, effector proteins, enzymes, lipopolysaccharides, nucleic acids, lipids, and immunomodulatory molecules through type I–VI secretion systems, the Sec/Tat secretion pathways, sortase-dependent protein-anchoring systems, and bacterial extracellular vesicles. These secretion-associated products may contribute to the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and stroke by damaging the intestinal mucosal barrier, inducing systemic inflammation, altering gut microbial ecology, compromising blood–brain barrier integrity, modulating microglial activation, and disrupting neurotransmitter homeostasis. This article systematically reviews the major types and functions of gut bacterial secretion systems, with particular emphasis on their potential roles in gut–brain communication, their mechanisms of involvement in central nervous system inflammatory diseases, and the current evidence and limitations in this field. The prospects for secretion-system-targeted interventions and the translational application of bacterial extracellular vesicles are also discussed. This review aims to provide a reference for mechanistic research and precision microbiome-based therapies for central nervous system diseases.

titre: Unmasking eating disorders in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: at the crossroads of disease, treatment, and development
resume: Feeding and eating disorders (EDs) are increasingly recognized as clinically relevant yet underdiagnosed comorbidities in children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Their identification is particularly challenging because food avoidance, dietary restrictions, reduced intake, weight loss, gastrointestinal symptoms, nutritional deficiencies, and growth impairment may reflect either active IBD or an underlying ED. Importantly, food avoidance in pediatric IBD may represent an adaptive response to symptoms or medically prescribed dietary interventions. Clinical concern arises when restrictive eating becomes persistent, rigid, disproportionate to disease activity, nutritionally compromising or associated with significant psychological distress. EDs remains poorly recognized despite its potential to increase nutritional vulnerability, adversely affect growth and body composition, complicate nutritional management, and impair treatment adherence. Pediatric may be particularly vulnerable because of the interaction between disease-related symptoms, dietary restrictions, exclusive enteral nutrition, treatment-associated changes in weight and body image, and developmental factors. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on epidemiology, clinical phenotypes, potential mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and clinical implications of EDs in pediatric IBD. Particular attention is given to the interactions between disease-related symptoms, developmental vulnerability, psychosocial influences, care-giver mediated eating behaviors, treatment-associated changes in weight and body image, and other treatment-associated factors, including the concept of treatment-reinforced eating behaviors . Exclusive enteral nutrition is considered within its established therapeutic role, while attention is given to potential vulnerabilities arising during dietary treatment, treatment transitions, and food reintroduction. Current evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and largely derived from adult populations, cross-sectional studies, and non-validated or non-disease-specific assessment tools. We propose a conceptual framework in which food avoidance exists along a continuum from adaptive symptom-related restriction to persistent maladaptive restriction and possible EDs. Until disease-specific instruments become available, early identification of eating-related concerns should rely on structured clinical assessment integrated into multidisciplinary pediatric IBD care, particularly during periods of active disease, nutritional treatment, weight change, puberty, and transition between care settings.

titre: Luteolin Alleviates Depressive-like Behaviors via Modulation of the Microbiota–Immune–Brain Axis in CUMS Rats
resume: Background/Objectives: Luteolin has anti-inflammatory and neuroactive properties, but the contribution of the microbiota-immune-brain axis to its behavioral effects remains unresolved. We examined behavioral, microbial, and inflammatory changes associated with luteolin treatment in rats exposed to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Methods: Depressive-/anxiety-like behaviors were assessed using the sucrose preference test (SPT), forced swim test (FST), elevated plus maze (EPM), and open field test (OFT). The underlying mechanisms were then investigated using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, hippocampal transcriptomics, and molecular biology assays, including Western blot. Finally, Spearman correlation analysis examined associations among gut microbiota, inflammatory phenotypes, and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling to explore luteolin’s potential antidepressant mechanisms within the microbiota-immune-brain axis. Results: Luteolin significantly reversed CUMS-induced behavioral deficits. It suppressed serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and reshaped the gut microbiota by increasing Lactobacillus, normalizing the Bacteroidetes (Bacteroidota)/Firmicutes (Bacillota) (B/F) ratio. Transcriptomics revealed downregulated inflammatory pathways, with MAPK signaling as a key pathway. Western blot and ELISA demonstrated that luteolin inhibited JNK and p38 phosphorylation and attenuated hippocampal neuroinflammation. Correlation network linked gut microbiota, inflammation, and behavior, supporting a multilayered microbiota–immune–brain axis. Conclusions: Luteolin exerts antidepressant effects involving gut microbiota remodeling, peripheral inflammation suppression, and JNK/p38 MAPK-mediated neuroprotection. These findings generate hypotheses concerning the antidepression effects via the microbiota–immune–brain axis, and suggest luteolin as a promising candidate for depression treatment.

titre: Trimethylamine N-oxide in neurological disorders: a review of its role as a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, neuroinflammatory mediator, and therapeutic target
resume: Neurological disorders are regulated by multiple factors including genetics, environment and metabolic disorders, covering neurodegenerative diseases, cerebrovascular diseases and neuropsychiatric disorders. They are characterized by high morbidity, disability and mortality, and there is a lack of sensitive early biomarkers and radical treatments in clinical practice. Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is a small-molecule metabolite produced by gut microbiota from substrates such as choline and L-carnitine. It can cross the blood–brain barrier into the central nervous system and mediate central pathological damage through multiple pathways, including disrupting blood–brain barrier integrity, inducing neuroinflammation, and causing neuronal damage and synaptic dysfunction. Patients with neurological disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), stroke and depression show significantly abnormal TMAO levels correlated with disease severity, though findings remain controversial across some studies. Most existing related research on TMAO concentrates on cardiovascular and metabolic disorders, and few reviews provide comprehensive, cross-disease comparative summaries of its mechanisms and clinical implications across diverse neurological disorders. This review comprehensively summarize the biological characteristics and metabolic regulatory mechanisms of TMAO, elucidates its pathogenesis of neurological injury, outlines its roles in common neurological disorders, and analyzes the clinical translation and application prospects of TMAO-targeted interventions, aiming to provide a theoretical reference for subsequent basic research and clinical diagnosis and treatment.

titre: J'ACCUSE: Penninx and the Dutch NESDA Research Network— Selective Citation Amnesia Concerning Nearly Four Decades of Pioneering Research, Historical Misattribution, Alleged Plagiarism of Scientific Ideas and Concepts, and Failure to Validate Immunometabolic Depression Subtyping
resume: The review by Penninx et al. (2025), Immuno-metabolic depression: from concept to implementation, raises important concerns regarding historical attribution, completeness of evidence, construct validity, and the biological interpretation of proposed immunometabolic depression (IMD) phenotypes. The review's reported PubMed search, restricted to publications from 2000 to May 2024, excludes foundational investigations from the 1990s that established immune-inflammatory activation and its relationships with lipid, protein, fatty acid, iron, and trace-element metabolism in depressive illness. Moreover, the review insufficiently incorporates subsequent research on atherogenicity, reverse cholesterol transport, HDL functionality, oxidative/nitrosative stress, gut-derived immune activation, autoimmunity, and neurotoxic mechanisms, now integrated within the neuroimmune–metabolic–oxidative (NIMETOX) framework. These omissions are scientifically consequential because they restrict both the selection of relevant biomarkers and the interpretation of biological heterogeneity in depression. Particular concerns include the reliance on nonspecific inflammatory indicators such as pentameric C-reactive protein (CRP), inadequate differentiation between depression-associated abnormalities and metabolic syndrome (MetS), insufficient consideration of recurrence of illness (ROI) and CFS-like symptoms, and uncertain biological specificity of an obesity-associated depressive phenotype. Furthermore, biomarker-based latent class analyses cited in support of immunometabolic depression have important limitations, insufficient independent replication, and the identification of metabolic-health-related classes that also emerge when nondepressed controls are included. We argue that the results discussed by Penninx et al. do not establish a distinct immune-inflammatory depressive subtype associated with atypical symptoms. Penninx and her coauthors exhibit recurrent citation amnesia by omitting pioneering discoveries by Maes and colleagues (1990–2000 and 2000-2024) on immune-inflammatory, metabolic, kynurenine, nutritional-immunological, and gut-brain pathways in depression. Instead, related concepts are attributed to substantially later publications, frequently originating within the authors’ own research NESDA network, thereby misrepresenting scientific priority. This recurrent pattern of citation omissions and disputed attribution of scientific priority raises serious concerns about the potential appropriation of intellectual credit and possible plagiarism of scientific ideas and concepts through omission of foundational sources.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: EVOLUTION OF OBESITY PHARMACOTHERAPY: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE EFFICACY AND MECHANISMS OF ACTION OF SEMAGLUTIDE, LIRAGLUTIDE, AND TIRZEPATIDE
resume: Obesity is a chronic, relapsing, multifactorial disease linked to metabolic, cardiovascular, and inflammatory disorders that impair quality of life and increase morbidity and mortality. Drugs acting on incretin signaling have changed what pharmacological treatment can achieve, and liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide stand out among them, although they differ in receptor targets, pharmacokinetics, dosing, and the magnitude of weight loss they produce. This narrative review compares their mechanisms of action, weight-loss efficacy, and metabolic benefits in adults with obesity. Randomized trials, mechanistic studies, and consensus documents published between 2015 and 2025 were examined through thematic synthesis organized around four axes: the evolution of incretin-based therapy, pharmacological mechanisms, clinical efficacy and metabolic benefits, and implications for practice. Head-to-head evidence shows that once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg produced greater weight loss than once-daily liraglutide 3.0 mg (15.8% vs. 6.4% at 68 weeks) and that tirzepatide, a dual agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors, outperformed semaglutide in adults with obesity without diabetes (20.2% vs. 13.7% at 72 weeks). Liraglutide and semaglutide have event-driven cardiovascular data in defined populations, whereas outcome evidence for tirzepatide in obesity is still accumulating. Gastrointestinal adverse effects, mostly mild to moderate and transient, are common to all three agents. Greater weight loss does not by itself mean overall superiority. Drug choice should weigh comorbidities, outcome evidence, tolerability, access, and patient preference, within long-term care that includes lifestyle interventions.

titre: The Oncology Primary Care Partnership to Improve Comprehensive Survivorship Care (OPTIMISE) intervention: study protocol for a pragmatic randomized controlled trial
resume: Cancer survivors with chronic comorbidities often experience fragmented care, particularly in safety-net settings where coordination between oncology and primary care is limited. Among medically underserved populations, gaps in communication and unclear delineation of provider roles are common during active treatment and the transition to survivorship. These challenges, coupled with limited support for chronic disease self-management, contribute to unmet needs, poor symptom control, and disparities in health-related quality of life (HRQOL). There is a need for pragmatic, multilevel care models that integrate oncology and primary care across the cancer continuum, beginning at diagnosis and extending through early survivorship. The OPTIMISE (Oncology Primary Care Partnership to Improve Comprehensive Survivorship Care) study addresses these gaps by testing a structured, multilevel intervention designed to enhance patient self-management, strengthen oncology–primary care coordination, and reduce disparities in HRQOL within a safety-net health system. OPTIMISE is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial of a multilevel intervention conducted at a large public safety-net health system in Houston, TX. The study will enroll 300 adults with newly diagnosed breast, gastrointestinal (GI), and hematologic cancers with comorbidities requiring concurrent management, along with 40 providers (oncologists and primary care providers [PCPs]). Patients will be randomized to usual medical care (UMC) or OPTIMISE. At the patient level, OPTIMISE enhances self-management through bilingual oncology nurse navigation. At the provider level, structured communication pathways improve coordination between oncology and primary care. At the system level, survivorship care plans integrating comorbidity management and a risk-stratified surveillance model optimize follow-up care. Primary outcomes include patient activation for comorbidity self-management and self-management behaviors. Secondary outcomes include HRQOL, unmet supportive care needs, and provider attitudes toward care coordination. A mixed-methods evaluation will identify patient-, provider-, and system-level factors influencing implementation and sustainment. By integrating oncology and primary care across the cancer continuum, beginning at diagnosis and extending through early survivorship, OPTIMISE aims to improve comprehensive care for medically underserved populations managing cancer and chronic comorbidities. Findings will inform scalable, real-world strategies to strengthen care coordination, support chronic disease self-management, and reduce disparities in survivorship outcomes within safety-net health systems. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05323409. Registered on April 12, 2022.

titre: The Core Emotion Framework at Two Hundred: Canonical Synthesis of Structural-Constructivist Affective Ontology, Operator Algebra, and Open-Science Validation
resume: Intended as the two-hundredth milestone entry in Jamel Bulgaria’s PhilPapers corpus, this capstone synthesis consolidates the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) from an extensive open-science archive—spanning 199 previously indexed entries across recent PhilPeople profile snapshots, 21 technical specifications, and 15 practitioner manuals—into a single canonical philosophical, mathematical, and empirical reference1. Across this body of work, the CEF addresses the enduring schism in affective science between biological essentialism and psychological constructionism by reconceptualizing emotions not as passive weather patterns or culturally assembled narratives, but as discrete functional powers operating within a somatic Human Operating System (Human OS)4. Rather than adding an isolated hypothesis to a fragmented literature, this milestone formulation codifies the logical spine linking the framework’s 3×3+1 Decalogue of Operators, TS-series operator algebra, transdiagnostic psychopathology, institutional dynamics, and synthetic affect specifications1. At the center of this synthesis lies a structural-constructivist ontology in which human affective life is generated by dynamic sequences of exactly ten irreducible functional operators distributed across three somatic-regulatory hubs: the Head, Heart, and Gut centers1. Psychological health is defined neither by hedonic positivity nor by the suppression of distress, but by operator independence and dynamic agility—the capacity of regulatory powers to activate, modulate, and complete cross-center cycles in context-sensitive trajectories2. Conversely, both clinical psychopathology and macro-institutional failure are modeled as structural losses of differentiation, specifically chronic involuntary operator fusion, regulatory overflow, and secondary operator silencing2. By formalizing these interactions through state-transition algebra, 10-dimensional activation vectors, and a 500-term canonical lexicon (EL-1), the CEF constructs a shared computational grammar spanning philosophy of mind, affective neuroscience, psychotherapy, political psychology (introduced by Chénglán Xǔ), and artificial intelligence1. Scholarly rigor at the two-hundred-paper threshold nevertheless demands clear demarcation between formal architectural specification and confirmed empirical proof12. Although the corpus is fully open access under CC BY 4.0 licensing across Zenodo, OSF, PhilPapers, and Hugging Face repositories, its quantitative validation remains foundational rather than settled1. Current empirical evidence derives from author-archived secondary analyses of open daily-life datasets (N = 336 and N = 241), an exploratory psychometric pilot (Pilot Study 3, N = 39), a scenario-based stress study (N = 826), and Phase 1 psychometric protocols preregistered on OSF in May and June 2026, alongside manuscripts listed on Bulgaria’s PhilPeople profile as forthcoming in Frontiers in Psychology and Qeios1. Combined with documented adverse-effect risks and Bulgaria’s own report of practical burnout in maintaining the solo archive, this article establishes both the definitive architectural statement of the CEF and a concrete falsification and handoff agenda for independent academic consortia2.

titre: Targeted assessment of symptom burden in individuals with leptomeningeal disease undergoing intrathecal therapy: development of a disease-specific screening toolscreening tool
resume: Background Leptomeningeal disease (LD) is associated with a high neurological symptom burden and unfavorable prognosis. Therefore health-related quality of life (HRQoL) represents a clinically important endpoint. However, no validated LD-specific HRQoL assessment tool currently exists. The project aims to identify key symptom and HRQoL domains relevant to patients with LD to support the development of a targeted screening instrument. Material and Methods Data from patients enrolled in the first part of the IT PD1 / NOA 26 phase I clinical trial (NCT05112549) were analyzed. HRQoL was assessed using EORTC QLQ-C30 and BN20 questionnaires (n = 24) as well as distress screening using the NCCN Distress Thermometer. In a subpopulation (n = 16), detailed symptom data from a 40-item problem list were evaluated as well as clinician-reported outcomes (NANO scale) and cognitive screening assessments (MMSE, MoCA). Furthermore, clinical records of patients with LD were retrospectively reviewed to characterize clinical symptom patterns. Item frequency, severity, and clinical relevance were analyzed to derive candidate domains for a disease-specific assessment tool. Results In the subpopulation (n = 16), 56% were female, with a median age of 50.2 years (range 18-62). The most common primary tumors were melanoma (n = 13), breast cancer (n = 2) and lung cancer (n = 1). A total of 203 HRQoL assessments were analyzed. Mean global health status was moderately impaired (50.0), with notable limitations in role (48.5) and social functioning (55.1). The most prominent symptoms were fatigue (mean 49.1) and appetite loss (30.0), while gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhoea (5.1) and nausea/vomiting (16.0), as well as financial difficulties (14.7), were infrequent. Cognitive function was largely preserved at screenings (median MMSE 30, range 26-30; ; median MoCA 29, range 19-30; across 133 assessments). Among 146 distress assessments, median distress was 5 (range 1-10). The most frequently reported concerns were emotional (concerns 65.8%, fear 52.1%), physical (fatigue 54.1%, mobility 40.4%, cognitive complaints 39.7%), and practical issues (transportation 15.8%). Spiritual concerns were not reported. Based on these findings, we developed a preliminary item list representing a basis for further development. Conclusion Patients with LD develop a distinct symptom profile that might be insufficiently captured by existing measures, underscoring the need for a concise, disease-specific assessment tool. The preliminary item list will be refined through expert consensus and subsequently piloted in a prospective cohort.

titre: Editorial: Unveiling sex differences in cardiology: integrative research and clinical implications
resume: For decades, cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) have remained as the leading cause of death worldwide and lowered the quality of life in developed countries. Personalized and optimized therapy for individuals can improve the CVD outcome, and focusing on sex differences in cardiology will provide us new insights and options for therapeutic strategies. Despite the accumulating evidences of sex differences in CVDs, a considerable proportion of animal studies and clinical guidelines are still based on studies predominantly involving males. Sex-specific differences in cardiovascular pathophysiology have been widely reported at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ levels. Along with biological sex differences, the gender-based differences, including social constructs such as gender identity or gender roles, also play a key role in sex-specific cardiovascular phenotypes.The study by Xie Y. et al. [1] explores an important and still controversial issue: the potentially higher heart failure risk of post-myocardial infarction in women. Interestingly, after this extensive and detailed analysis, their findings suggest that the excess risk is not attributable to sex per se, but rather to the substantial risk burden associated with the clustering of risk factors in women, driven by the combined effects of older age and an adverse metabolic profile. In particular, type 2 diabetes mellitus in postmenopausal women played a considerable role in multiplying the risk vs men. Conversely, among individuals with low-to-intermediate cardiovascular risk profiles, no significant sex-related difference was observed in the incidence of heart failure related to post-myocardial infarction.Age plays a significant role in aggravating the prognosis after an acute coronary event by impaired glucose metabolism. This hypothesis inspired Garcia-Fernandez H. et al. to conduct the study, in which authors investigated the mechanism underlying the later onset of cardiovascular disease in women compared with men, in relation to the presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus [2]. The conclusion of this well-conducted study further reinforced the concept that sex-related differences in coronary artery disease were strongly dependent on the presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Once again, their findings corroborate the idea that the cardiovascular risk associated with diabetes is disproportionately higher in women than in men. This lends further support to the hypothesis of a potential sex-specific difference in the cardiovascular risk associated with diabetes. Such difference is also reflected in the higher C-reactive protein levels observed in women than in men when type 2 diabetes is present, suggesting a less favourable risk in women associated with greater inflammatory activity.As in cardiology, sex-related differences in prognosis and postoperative outcomes are increasingly gaining attention in cardiac surgery. The study by Jawoosh M. et al. focuses on aortic valve replacement using the Edwards INTUITY rapid-deployment bioprosthesis [3], examining whether the well-recognised anatomical differences between men and women, particularly those involving the left ventricular outflow tract and aortic annulus, may affect postoperative complications, especially in the development of prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). Indeed, the incidence of PPM appears to be higher in women than in men, irrespective of body mass index (BMI). Nevertheless, severe PPM remains relatively uncommon in both sexes even though it is still observed more frequently in women. This issue is particularly relevant given the potential impact of PPM following aortic valve replacement on long-term prognosis.The study by Akram R. et al. on the outcomes of surgical coronary revascularisation, likewise, is originated from the observation that women have a less favourable long-term prognosis than men [4]. The authors acknowledged several previously recognised contributing factors, including older age, delayed presentation, and a greater burden of comorbidities in women. These are compounded by factors more directly related to the surgical settings, such as smaller coronary artery calibre, a greater predisposition to vasospasm, and a higher prevalence of incomplete revascularisation. All of which may contribute to poorer outcomes in women. The Akram group investigated whether different surgical strategies could improve outcomes according to sex, concluding that off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) achieves comparable 30-day outcomes in men and women, thereby suggesting a greater relative benefit for women than with the conventional on-pump CABG strategy. Following OPCAB, older age and renal insufficiency remain important prognostic determinants, whereas sex appears to lose its independent prognostic significance. These findings highlight the importance of a deeper understanding of sex-and gender-related differences in cardiovascular diseases, which may contribute to the development and implementation of tailored strategies designed to maximise benefits for specific patient populations.The group led by Pavone N. et al. offers a different, yet equally important, perspective [5]. In infective endocarditis, a condition associated with a particularly poor prognosis, women are referred for cardiac surgery less frequently than men, with a 25% lower rate of surgical intervention, despite achieving comparable postoperative outcomes. The lower likelihood of surgical referral appears to reflect a disproportionately high perceived level of frailty, potentially driven by the greater prevalence of diabetes, renal insufficiency, anaemia, and advanced age among women. The authors of this thought-provoking study, therefore, raised important questions: could women with infective endocarditis achieve better overall outcomes if they were considered for surgery more equitably? Could a systematic Heart Team discussion help address this issue by identifying patients' actual risk profiles and moving beyond generic perceptions of risk? This is particularly relevant given that the available data suggest that women undergoing cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis have outcomes comparable to those of men.Moser-van der Geest et al focused on the sex differences in arrhythmia [6]. They found women with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) presenting to a tertiary emergency department had a greater symptom burden and distinct symptom profiles compared with men. Women more frequently reported palpitations, nausea, and anxiety and had higher rates of hypokalemia and atrioventricular nodal reentry tachycardia. These findings emphasize the importance of considering sex-specific presentations when evaluating suspected SVT.The pacemaker therapy can also be re-evaluated in its indications, procedural complications, and long-term outcomes by sex differences.Sex-related differences also extend to pacemaker therapy. In their review, Antoun I. et al. describe important disparities between women and men in implantation indications, procedural complications, and longterm outcomes [7]. Women tend to be older at implantation and experience higher rates of acute complications, including pneumothorax, pocket haematoma, and lead perforation whereas men more often receive pacemakers for atrioventricular conduction disease and have greater long-term pacing exposure. Nevertheless, female longterm survival is comparable to, or sometimes better than that of male. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing biological and anatomical factors from disparities in referral and clinical decision-making between male and female, indicating that the device selection and implantation strategies should be decided by individual clinical needs rather than their sex alone. Striking sex differences in cardiovascular diseases are also reported in the translational research studies. Rose et al. focused on the sex differences of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) [8]. Despite the remodeling patterns shared in common, ASCVD and PAH have widespread sex-difference mechanisms. They focused on the estrogen and testosterone and how these sex hormones play their specific roles via NO-cGMP-PKG signaling in PAH and ASCVD. they also reviewed wide range of sex specific modulators such as microRNA, metabolomics and Gut microbiome. Understanding these sex-specific mechanisms helps in improving sex-specific risk stratification and supporting targeted therapeutic strategies.Sex hormones contribute to the sex-specific mechanism, and vice versa. The female-specific cardioprotective angiogenesis in pregnancy can be shared with males. Hesse et al. reported the direct effect of pregnancy hormones (E2 and P4) that hormone treatment enhanced angiogenesis in both female and male hearts through cardiomyocyte PGC-1α/ERRα signaling and VEGF secretion, independent of cardiac hypertrophy [9].Their findings identify that both male and female can have pregnancy-induced cardiac capillary expansion without hypertrophic response, suggesting the female-specific cardio-beneficial effects also applicable to males.Sex differences also manifest in the human organ level. Cheng J. and Zhang B. reported that sexspecific factors influence the development of increased inter-arm systolic blood pressure difference (IASBPD) [10]. Elevated IASBPD was more prevalent in men and was associated with obesity-related measures, hypertension, and inflammatory markers. Increased neck circumference was an independent risk factor in men, whereas older age was the primary risk factor in women. These findings highlight the importance of considering sex differences in vascular risk assessments.Biomarkers to predict the acute heart failure also have sex differences. Akbarian Khorasgani et al. conducted a single-center retrospective study [11] and reported that NT-proBNP and lactate were the significant predictors in men, whereas no biomarker independently predicted outcomes in women. Their findings pointed out the benefit of incorporating lactate into acute heart failure early risk stratification and the sex differences in its prognostic performances.These reports corroborate the idea that male and female show distinct symptoms, treatment responses, and ultimately their prognosis in cardiovascular diseases. Furthermore, these differences are neither uniform across cardiovascular conditions nor attributable to a single underlying mechanism. Rather, they reflect a complex interplay of pathophysiological processes that vary across diseases.Further understanding of sex-and gender-related differences in cardiovascular diseases and clarifying its underlying pathophysiology are essential to establish the effective clinical care, moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach towards more informed, individualized treatment decisions based on the expected benefit for each patient. Improving cardiovascular care does not depend solely on discovering new treatments; it also depends on learning how to use the tools we already have more effectively. In this respect, the appropriate recognition and clinical application of sex differences will contribute to better outcomes just as meaningfully as advances in medical research.

titre: Differences in network organization of interoceptive awareness and emotion regulation in individuals with overweight and obesity: a network comparison study
resume: Understanding how interoceptive awareness (IA) and emotion regulation (ER) interact is essential for improving emotional functioning in individuals with overweight and obesity. This study examined the network structure linking IA and habitual ER strategies and compared these associations between overweight and obese individuals and normal-weight controls. Participants included 531 overweight and obese individuals (OW&OB, BMI ≥ 24.0) and 515 normal-weight individuals (NW, 18.5 ≤ BMI < 24.0). Network analysis was used to model the associations between IA dimensions and ER strategies in the two groups. Overall network connectivity and bridge centrality were largely comparable between the two groups. The groups showed evidence of a difference in overall network structure, with differences concentrated in specific edges and node centrality. Specifically, the OW&OB group exhibited a stronger negative association between Catastrophizing and Not Distracting, but weaker positive associations between Not Distracting and Attention Regulation, and between Refocus on Planning and Positive Reappraisal. Rumination showed higher centrality, whereas Not Distracting and Refocus on Planning exhibited lower centrality in the OW&OB group than in the NW group. These findings suggest that OW&OB is characterized by a distinct IA–ER network reconfiguration rather than global strengthening, highlighting the potential value of targeting interoceptive–regulatory interactions within their broader network context in clinical practice. Level of evidence Level Ⅲ Evidence obtained from observational analytic studies, including cohort and case–control studies.
revue: Eating and Weight Disorders - Studies on Anorexia Bulimia and Obesity

titre: Workbook 02: Integrated Biological Performance — Systems of Flow, Regulation & Adaptation
resume: Workbook 02: Integrated Biological Performance — Systems of Flow, Regulation & Adaptation is the second foundational volume of the Functional Biohacking Framework™, developed by Edgar Solano (Texas Leeches®). Built on the core principle that "the body does not fail randomly; it fails where systems lose coherence," this conceptual architecture moves beyond isolated performance variables to examine how sustainable human capability emerges naturally from internal biological organization. Expanding the systems model across continuous physiological feedback loops, this volume maps the core pillars of biological integration: Foundational Philosophy (Beyond Optimization): Shifting from isolated external interventions to systemic coherence, where biological organization precedes performance Module 1 — Foundations of Circulatory Function: Circulation as the primary architecture of distribution, biological connectivity, and internal economy ("Flow determines biological possibility") Module 2 — Respiratory Integration and Oxygen Dynamics: Respiration as the primary interface of biological exchange, O₂–CO₂ biochemical balance, and rhythmic systemic communication Module 3 — Nervous System Regulation and Adaptive Control: Interoception, allostatic load economics, and Biological Trust—exploring how neural regulation evaluates internal stability before authorizing performance expansion Module 4 — Cellular Regeneration and Structural Restoration: Continuous biological renewal and tissue reconstruction governed by systemic permission, delivery, and clearance efficiency Educational Notice: This work is a conceptual framework and educational observation model designed to explore biological organization and systemic adaptation. It does not constitute medical diagnosis, clinical instruction, or treatment.
auteurs: Solano, Edgar, Leeches of Texas LLC

titre: Hypnosis for Post-ICU PTSD Symptoms: A Case Report and Call for Innovation
resume: Background: While Post–Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS) and PICS-family (PICS-F) are increasingly recognized, evidence-based interventions to address the distress commonly identified during ICU follow-up for patients and families remain limited. Medical hypnosis is used in acute care settings and has demonstrated efficacy for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), but has not been evaluated in patients or relatives affected by PICS/PICS-F. Case Summary: We report the case of an ICU patient’s relative who presented with clinically significant PTSD symptoms at the 6-month follow-up consultation routinely offered to survivors of prolonged ICU stays and their families. The Impact of Event Scale–Revised (IES-R) score was 49 at baseline and decreased to 19 after three hypnosis sessions. Conclusion: Medical hypnosis may represent a feasible and innovative therapeutic option for PTSD symptoms in the context of PICS and PICS-F.
revue: The Journal of Critical Care Medicine

titre: Interventions for alleviating secondary traumatic stress & burnout and enhancing compassionate satisfaction in nurses: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Nurses are highly prone to compassion fatigue, burnout, and secondary traumatic stress (STS) due to their continued exposure to the suffering and death of patients. These workplace risks negatively affect nurses’ wellness, job satisfaction, and the quality of patient care. The interventions studied include mindfulness training, cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), self-care programs, and resilience training. Nonetheless, the literature remains inconclusive about their effects. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024553920). We searched 5 databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Embase, and Web of Science) through October 2024. Seven randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 863 nurses met the inclusion criteria. We extracted data on study design, sample size, intervention type, duration, frequency, and outcomes using validated instruments, including the Professional Quality of Life (ProQOL) scale, Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21). We used Review Manager 5.4.1 for statistical analyses, using random-effects models to account for heterogeneity. Seven randomized controlled trials involving 863 nurses showed that psychosocial interventions improved professional quality of life. Stress levels were moderately decreased with the use of the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) (SMD = -0.47, 95% CI: -0.73 to -0.22) and more significantly reduced with the help of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21) (SMD = -0.75, 95% CI: -1.09 to -0.40). Burnout rates also decreased (SMD = − 0.59, 95% CI: -0.79 to -0.38), though they were higher in long-term resilience-based interventions and cognitive-behavioral therapy. Compassion fatigue was significantly reduced (SMD = − 0.62, 95% CI: -0.83 to -0.41), especially after mindfulness-based and self-care interventions. Compassion satisfaction increased (SMD = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47 to 0.88). Outcome-specific analyses showed low heterogeneity (I 2 = 0–10%). The diversity of intervention and outcome methodologies reflects the variety of interventions, not inconsistency. Because we included few studies, we reported subgroup results and could not formally assess publication bias. Psychosocial interventions also significantly improve nurses’ professional quality of life, including decreases in stress, burnout, and compassion fatigue, and increases in compassion satisfaction. However, evidence quality is low to moderate because of the limited number of trials, the methodology, and the comparatively short follow-up. Healthcare institutions should prioritize structured, evidence-based, nursing-specific psychological support programs to improve workforce well-being and patient outcomes.

titre: Urban Hassles and School-Based Anxiety Intervention Outcomes
resume: School-based anxiety interventions are generally effective, but not all students respond to these interventions. Understanding factors that impact intervention response is needed. This study explored one understudied factor, exposure to urban hassles, and tested whether exposure moderated the effectiveness of school-based interventions for anxiety. Participants included 216 students with anxiety disorders in the United States of America (ages 6–18 years; mean age: 10.9 years; 63.9% White, 51.3% male). School mental health providers were randomized and trained to deliver 12 weeks of Modular Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (MCBT) or Treatment as Usual (TAU). Students completed a measure of urban hassles and were assessed on anxiety outcomes at post treatment (i.e. 12 weeks after treatment initiation) and at a 12-month follow-up. Results indicated that at post treatment (but not follow-up), students exposed to low and average levels of urban hassles may have greater improvements in MCBT versus TAU based on parent-report of anxiety symptoms. However, at high levels of exposure to urban hassles, students in both treatments improved similarly. This study reveals how urban stressors are associated with anxiety and response to school-based anxiety interventions. These findings inform efforts to personalize and select the most appropriate anxiety intervention to help improve outcomes.
revue: Journal of Psychologists and Counsellors in Schools

titre: OS12.7.A Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully in neuro-oncology: Primary outcomes from a national telehealth randomized ORBIT Model Phase IIc pilot Trial
resume: Background Patients with primary or secondary brain tumors experience profound distress, including depression and death anxiety, driven by symptom burden, neurologic decline, and poor prognosis. Despite this, this population remains systematically excluded from psychosocial oncology trials, leaving a critical gap in evidence-based neuro-oncology supportive care. Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully (CALM) is a brief, manualized supportive-expressive psychotherapy with demonstrated efficacy in advanced cancer; however, it has never been tested in neuro-oncology. Guided by the NIH ORBIT Model for behavioral intervention development, this Phase IIc randomized pilot trial evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and efficacy signal of telehealth CALM compared to treatment as usual (TAU). Primary outcomes included feasibility of recruitment, longitudinal data capture, intervention acceptability, and changes in depressive symptoms and death anxiety. Methods Adults with primary grade III-IV or metastatic brain tumors and elevated depression (PHQ-9 ≥10) and/or death anxiety (DADDS ≥15) were randomized 2:1 to six biweekly individual CALM sessions or TAU. Feasibility and acceptability metrics were summarized descriptively. Changes in depression and death anxiety (Week 0-12) were evaluated using change scores (Δ), with meaningful improvement defined at the individual level. Within-group effect sizes were calculated using Cohen’s d (0.2=small, 0.5=medium, 0.8=large). Sustained changes (Week 12-24) were explored descriptively. Results Recruitment was highly successful and exceeded feasibility benchmarks: of 105 patients screened, 66% were eligible and 87% consented, resulting in 58 randomized participants (CALM n = 39; TAU n = 19). Acceptability was high, with 77% intervention completion, 90% of participants reporting substantial therapeutic benefit, and 100% willingness to recommend CALM. Depressive symptoms improved in both groups (CALM d = −0.51; TAU d = −0.53). Notably, larger overall effects were demonstrated for death anxiety (CALM d = −0.95; TAU d = −1.03), with a substantially greater proportion of CALM participants achieving meaningful benefit (63% vs. 46%) and sustained benefit over follow-up (52% vs. 25%), suggesting enhanced durability of death anxiety benefit following CALM compared to TAU. Conclusions Telehealth CALM is a feasible and highly acceptable intervention that addresses a major unmet need in neuro-oncology. Findings provide compelling early evidence that CALM may meaningfully reduce death anxiety and promote sustained psychological benefit in patients with malignant primary or secondary brain tumors. These results strongly support advancement to a fully powered Phase III trial and the potential for this psychotherapeutic intervention to be integrated into standard neuro-oncology care.

titre: Participation of parents with high-grade glioma in the Enhancing-Connections Palliative Care (EC-PC) study
resume: Background Parents with advanced, incurable cancer who have dependent children experience substantially elevated psychological distress—approximately five times higher than adults without dependent children. This risk is amplified among individuals with high-grade glioma (HGG; WHO Grade 3-4), who face significant neurological symptom burden due to the tumor and its treatment. Although several interventions reduce parental distress after a cancer diagnosis, few include parents with HGG, limiting their relevance for this population. This abstract presents a sub-analysis of participants with HGG enrolled in a randomized controlled trial of the Enhancing-Connections Palliative Care Study (EC-PC), a structured, nurse-delivered, telephone-based intervention conducted every two weeks over a 10week period (five sessions). Methods Participants were randomized to either the ECPC intervention or a control group (1-time scripted phone call to guide parent on use of booklet). ECPC addresses parental distress (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory), parenting skills (Connecting & Coping Skills), and parental self-efficacy (Help Child Scale, Deal and Manage Scale). Data were collected at baseline and at 3month followup. Nonparametric Wilcoxon tests were used for statistical analysis. Results Thirteen participants with HGG were enrolled (7 male, 6 female). Diagnoses included glioblastoma (n = 7), astrocytoma (n = 4), and oligodendroglioma (n = 1). The mean participant age was 47 years (range 39-65), and the mean age of dependent children was 10 years (range 5-17). Eight were randomized to ECPC; four withdrew prior to completing the program and four completed all five sessions and provided baseline and 3month followup data. In the control group, only two participants completed both assessments. Though not statistically significant, EC-PC participants demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements from baseline to 3month followup in Help Child Scale scores (baseline: 58.20 ± 17.46; followup: 78.50 ± 6.03), Deal and Manage Scale scores (100.25 ± 21.09 to 118.92 ± 8.77), and Connecting & Coping Skills (10.75 ± 4.57 to 32.87 ± 8.93). Conclusion Despite the symptom burden and distress parents with HGG experience, they were able to enhance their parenting competencies with a brief, structures telephone-delivered program and parent workbook. Preliminary findings suggest potential benefits in improving parenting skills and confidence. There were 50% withdrawal rate highlighting the critical need to adapt ECPC to better address the unique challenges of patients with HGG. ECPC currently represent the only manualized cognitive-behavioral parenting intervention addressing parental distress among individuals with HGG. This sub-analysis demonstrates successful recruitment and participation of parents with HGG.
