titre: Separating Consciousness from Access, Report, Self-Model, Memory, Intelligence, Emotion, and Coherence
resume: This paper establishes a family-wide constitutive separation between generic conscious occurrence and major scientific near-neighbor constructs. It begins from the fixed bearer-relative surface and asks whether native success in access, report, self-modeling, metacognition, Memory, Intelligence, Emotion, arousal, coherence, integration, recurrence, synchrony, information quantity, or performance can replace the constitutive relation used to assign conscious occurrence. ConsciousnessNearNeighborFamily is the declared family tested for non-equivalence. Each member is reconstructed in a scientifically recognizable strong native form before substitution is tested. Access may include global availability and control; report may include reliable communication; self-model and metacognition may be explicit and accurate; Memory and Intelligence may be highly capable; affective and dynamical organizations may be rich and causally important. The result therefore does not depend on weakening neighboring theories or constructing trivial counterexamples. The positive anchor is BearerRelativePresenceRelation, instantiated for one bearer and grain through BearerRelativePresenceInstantiation, after which ConsciousOccurrence is assigned. ConsciousnessNearNeighborSeparationTheorem states that no member of ConsciousnessNearNeighborFamily substitutes for BearerRelativePresenceRelation merely by satisfying its own native office. The substitution battery permits each neighboring office to close at full strength while preserving a distinct constitutive burden unless an explicit bridge derives bearer-relative presence for the same bearer and grain. The reverse-collapse test supplies the complementary control. Generic ConsciousOccurrence does not acquire universal requirements for reportability, maximal access, explicit self-modeling, episodic Memory, Intelligence, Emotion, arousal, coherence, recurrence, information magnitude, or benchmark performance merely because such capacities are useful or mechanistically important in particular hosts. Any stronger requirement must be established through an independently typed specialization or host-specific necessity result. This separation preserves scientific relevance without granting definitional authority. Global neuronal workspace, higher-order representation, recurrent processing, memory-centered accounts, affective neuroscience, interoceptive processing, autonomic physiology, coherence measures, information-theoretic quantities, and performance architectures may function as mechanisms, realization conditions, correlates, evidence sources, consequences, or specializations. The theorem establishes constitutive non-equivalence rather than causal exclusion, empirical irrelevance, or theory-wide falsity. Empirical dissociation remains a supporting but non-foundational surface. A host may exhibit rich access without report, strong report without the complete constitutive burden, Memory without current occurrence, affective organization without generic closure, or coherence without bearer-relative instantiation. Such cases can sharpen local separation and reveal proxy error, but the family-wide theorem is carried by target-preserving substitution rather than any single empirical dissociation. Public parentage is bounded. Bearer-Relative Presence and the Minimal Constitutive Relation of Consciousness: Necessity, Sufficiency, and Irreducibility supplies the constitutive relation, bearer-specific instantiation, and occurrence target without reopening their theorem burdens. Conscious Content and Conscious Occurrence: Content Optionality and Relational Specialization supplies the content-optional control, preventing conscious content from entering the near-neighbor family as a hidden universal prerequisite. Both results are consumed unchanged. The scope remains generic and host-neutral only at the constitutive office. Bearer identity and composition, continuity, cross-scale recursion, structural fractality, universal mechanism sufficiency, phase- or coherence-specific realization, system-specific realization, persistence, evidence calibration, field-scale occurrence, higher-scale attribution, and theory comparison remain independently burdened downstream offices. The maximum public result is a machine-reconstructible separation architecture in which ConsciousnessNearNeighborSeparationTheorem blocks proxy substitution unless a target-specific derivation closes BearerRelativePresenceRelation for the same bearer and grain, while the reverse-collapse control blocks unearned import of neighboring capacities into the generic definition. Native success in those neighboring offices does not by itself constitute ConsciousOccurrence.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Non-Derivability of a Universal Emotion Criterion from the Current Affective Discriminant Grammar: Necessity, Sufficiency, and Host-Diversity Countermodels
resume: This paper tests whether the current target-blind EmotionDiscriminantGrammar contains a host-general necessary-and-sufficient criterion for Emotion. The analysis separates a generic constitutive criterion from taxonomies, semantic spaces, reports, physiological signatures, conscious feelings, mechanisms, and other scientifically useful but potentially host-specific or non-exclusive properties. The target is evaluated through explicit necessity, sufficiency, non-circularity, and host-diversity burdens rather than through disciplinary consensus or theory preference. EmotionDiscriminantGrammar contains twenty frozen atomic discriminant classes. These classes cover basal relation-conditioned constitutive modulation, bearer-level integration, multicomponent coordination, domain or object directedness, same-bearer relation-dependent self-state change, persistence or hysteresis, cross-context generalization, action readiness or priority shift, embodiment or interoceptive coupling, valence, arousal or intensity, conscious feeling, explicit appraisal or representation, peripheral physiological recruitment, expression or communication, history or memory dependence, joint irreducibility or composition loss, novelty or salience, social relationality, and coherence or synchronization. The atomic surface is completed by an exact strict-conjunction subgrammar. A canonical strict conjunction is any non-empty subset of the twenty frozen classes with every selected component mandatory, target-blind, and free of downstream qualification. The generative rule produces exactly 1,048,575 canonical strict conjunctions. Weighted, optional, thresholded, voting, disjunctive, mixture, temporally ordered, causally coupled, and otherwise newly relational composites are scientifically different candidates and are not silently included in this closure. Each atomic class fails generic necessity or lacks a demonstrated universal-necessity burden across the declared host-diversity surface. Because every strict conjunction contains at least one mandatory atomic class, an admissible target case lacking that constituent also lacks the entire conjunction. The complete 1,048,575-member strict-conjunction surface therefore fails generic necessity deductively rather than through an enumerated sample of conjunctions. GenericEmotionDiscriminantNonDerivabilityTheorem closes this bounded test. No frozen atomic discriminant, no strict conjunction generated from the frozen twenty-class surface, and no documented dated currentness-extension candidate survives the complete generic burden. GenericEmotionCriterion is therefore CLOSED NEGATIVE within EmotionDiscriminantGrammar. UniversalEmotionNaturalKind is likewise CLOSED NEGATIVE within the same grammar because no surviving host-general constitutive criterion is available from which the stronger natural-kind claim can be derived. The theorem is explicitly bounded rather than metaphysical. A genuinely new discriminant can reopen the result when its constitutive content lies outside the current atomic and strict-conjunction grammar, is frozen prospectively before outcome inspection, and is tested under the same generic burdens. Host-specific mechanisms, measurements, classifications, cross-host regularities, and empirically useful predictive features remain scientifically available without becoming a universal criterion by default. The paper also performs a dated currentness stress test against explicit contemporary definition proposals. Process-based, appraisal-based, reinforcer-based, behavioral-output, olfactory, predictive-processing, and conceptual-definition accounts are tested proposition-locally as adversarial comparators rather than accepted as theorem authorities. The current 2025–2026 candidates do not supply a surviving GenericEmotionCriterion under the declared host-diversity burden. The only public corpus parent conditionally consumed is Lawhood Before Laws: Invariance, Admissibility, and Regime Transformation, used for declared-domain, admissibility, candidate-status, and claim-scope discipline. The paper has no scientific parent within the Emotion Series. Positive host-relative qualification, affective-modulation specialization, conscious self-state specialization, and emotional-feeling transduction remain downstream offices and cannot retroactively supply the present proof. The maximum public result is a machine-reconstructible grammar-bounded non-derivability theorem with an exact finite test surface and explicit reopen conditions. The paper does not establish that a universal Emotion invariant is impossible in principle, does not deny host-specific Emotion architectures, and does not globally invalidate external emotion theories in their native scientific offices.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

fiche.verdict: Analyse formelle (théorème) démontrant l'impossibilité de dériver un critère universel et unique de l'émotion à partir des modèles actuels.

titre: Spatializing Consciousness: Subjective Imagery and the Reorganization of Fragmented Selfhood in What a Wonderful World
resume: The eight-episode television drama What a Wonderful World visualizes divided selfhood through a sustained reordering of viewpoint and screen space. This article examines the series through close audiovisual analysis, focusing on the virtual test, the escape room, clinical conversations, the bridge promise, and the final hypnosis sequence. Edward Branigan's account of cinematic point of view provides the main analytical frame, supplemented by work on character alignment, embodied spectatorship, and complex television. The series first restricts knowledge through first-person views, darkened frames, chromatic shifts, and broken continuity. It then assigns memories and agencies to enclosed locations and separate positions within shot-reverse-shot structures. Later episodes reconnect these visual zones through thresholds, repeated settings, sound bridges, and shared recollection. The closing episode retains a productive tension between clinical closure and the continued visual presence of Jia Xiaoduo. Consciousness therefore becomes a spatial relation among viewpoints, bodies, names, and memories. By locating psychic conflict in televisual form, the series turns self-recognition into a perceptual process and uses serial repetition to revise the viewer's earlier assumptions about who sees, speaks, and remembers.

titre: Effects of Mindfulness Interventions in Women with Breast Cancer Undergoing Chemotherapy: An Integrative Review (2021–2026)
resume: Introduction: Advances in chemotherapy protocols have played a decisive role in breast cancer control, promoting significant reductions in mortality and increased survival rates. However, the systemic toxicity inherent to this therapy entails severe somatic and psychological impacts, substantially compromising patients' quality of life. Objective: To analyze the effects of Mindfulness-Based Interventions (MBIs), particularly the Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) program, in mitigating psychological distress and promoting well-being in women with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy. Methods: This is an integrative and comparative literature review based on the critical analysis of six selected studies, encompassing randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews with meta-analysis. The methodological analysis was guided by data extraction and synthesis regarding psychological, emotional, cognitive, and somatic outcomes measured by standardized instruments in the primary studies. Results: The studies demonstrate statistically significant efficacy of MBIs in reducing levels of anxiety, depression, and perceived stress. Evidence indicates that MBSR acts directly on restructuring cognitive emotion regulation strategies, reducing maladaptive mechanisms such as catastrophizing and self-blame while fostering acceptance and positive reappraisal. Strengthening of perceived social support and promotion of Post-Traumatic Growth (PTG) were also observed. Additionally, findings point to improvements in subjective sleep quality and fatigue management, highlighting the role of MBSR both as a standalone intervention and in combination with other integrative practices. Conclusion: Mindfulness-Based Interventions represent robust and feasible adjuvant interventions in the oncological setting, promoting psychosocial adaptation, cognitive restructuring, and an overall improvement in the quality of life of patients undergoing chemotherapy.

fiche.verdict: Le programme MBSR réduit le stress, l'anxiété et la catastrophisation chez les femmes traitées par chimiothérapie pour un cancer du sein.

Amélioration de la qualité du sommeil et de la gestion de la fatigue
fiche.conclusion: Les interventions basées sur la pleine conscience constituent un adjuvant efficace pour l'adaptation psychosociale et la qualité de vie en oncologie.

titre: cryoEM-Montpellier
resume: The montpellier’s cryoEM community and the requested BAG includes the groups from CBS, the IGF, of the IRIM and the LPHI. We are currently running several research projects requiring single-particles cryoEM data collection. We have both internal projects and longterm collaborative projects that currently relies on access to high-end 200KeV microscopes for sample screening mainly (METI Toulouse, Marseille, IBS Grenoble, Karolinska Institute) and to 300KeV electron microscopes for data collection ( ESRF running proposals, Karolinska institute, MRC-LMB, NCBS Bangalore, Thermofisher). In this context, we investigate the structural basis of important therapeutic targets. The CBS teams characterises nuclear hormone receptors, nucleotide binding proteins, enzymes, and DNA ORIGAMI. The IGF characterize GPCRs such as mGluRs, and related transmembrane proteins. The IRIM and LPHI are focusing on several therapeutic targets, including membrane proteins.

titre: Proactive Prediction of Dynamic Link Blockages in mmWave Optimized Using Global Awareness Siamese Network
resume: In Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications, dynamic link blockages can cause major signal propagation disturbances that affect network performance as a whole. The increased susceptibility to obstacles brought on by mmWave signals’ great sensitivity to environmental influences and physical barriers is a significant disadvantage. In this paper, Proactive Prediction of Dynamic Link Blockages in mmWave Optimized Using Global Awareness Siamese Network (PPDLB-MMW-GASN) is proposed. At first, the data are collected from the Large-Scale actual-world mmWave Dataset, which is provided as input. Afterward, the data are fed to preprocessing. In preprocessing, Subaperture Keystone Transform Matched Filtering (SKTMF) is employed for data standardization. Then, the pre-processed output is fed to the Global Awareness Siamese Network (GASN) for predicting the future dynamic line of sight (LOS) link blockages. In general, GASN does not express adaptive optimization strategies to determine optimal parameters to predict the future dynamic LOS link blockages. The Coronavirus Mask Protection Algorithm (CMPA) is utilized to optimize the weight parameters of GASN. The effectiveness of the proposed PPDLB-MMW-GASN method is implemented in Python and evaluated through performance measures like Accuracy, Mean Square Error (MSE), Coefficient of Determination ([Formula: see text], Mean Opinion Score (MOS), Residual Sum of Squares (RSS) and Throughput. The proposed PPDLB-MMW-GASN approach attains 26.42%, 23.36% and 29.27% higher accuracy, 15.36%, 14.42% and 15.13% lower Mean Square Error, 28.36%, 26.42% and 28.27% higher Mean Opinion Score, 23.40%, 27.33% and 29.37% lower RSS and 27.44%, 17.31% and 34.36% higher Throughput when compared with existing approaches, such as LiDAR-Aided Future Beam Prediction in Real-World Millimeter Wave V2I Communications (LAFB-V2IC-RNN), Proactively Predicting Dynamic 6G Link Blockages Using LiDAR and In-Band Signature (6GLB-LiD-IBS-MMNN) and Blockage Prediction Using Wireless Signatures: Deep Learning Enables Real-World Demonstration (BPWS-RWD-CNN).
revue: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers

titre: The Gut–Brain–Social Axis: How Adolescent Dietary Patterns Influence Perceived Stress, Loneliness, And Academic Motivation
resume: Adolescence is a critical developmental period characterized by significant physical, psychological, emotional and social changes. Dietary habits developed during this stage may influence not only physical health but also psychological well-being, emotional regulation, social relationships and academic functioning. Recent research on the Gut–Brain Axis suggests that communication between intestinal microorganisms and the central nervous system plays an important role in regulating stress responses, mood, cognition and behavioural functioning. The present paper examines the relationship between adolescent dietary patterns and three important psychological and educational outcomes: perceived stress, loneliness and academic motivation. It explores how dietary diversity, fibre consumption, fermented foods, fruits, vegetables, excessive sugar intake and ultra-processed food consumption may influence gut microbiota and associated neurobiological pathways. The review focuses on adolescents in Meerut and Ghaziabad districts of Uttar Pradesh, considering the changing food environment, increasing exposure to processed foods, changing family eating practices, academic competition, digital lifestyles and changing peer relationships. The study adopts a secondary-data-based review approach, considering relevant research and policy literature from 2022 onwards, with the proposed research period extending to 2027. It integrates nutritional, psychological and educational perspectives to develop a conceptual framework explaining the possible relationships among dietary behaviour, gut health, perceived stress, loneliness and academic motivation. The paper argues that adolescent nutrition should be considered an important component of comprehensive school health and educational development. It also identifies research gaps concerning the relationship between gut microbiota, social well-being and academic motivation in Indian adolescents.

titre: Obstrucción intestinal como presentación de adenocarcinoma de colon ascendente en adulto jóven : Reporte de caso
resume: Colorectal cancer incidence has risen among young adults, even in the absence of classic risk factors or known family history. We present the case of a 38-year-old male with no relevant medical history who developed a 2-day obstructive clinical picture, nausea, and chronic weight loss. Physical examination revealed abdominal pain and distension. Imaging studies demonstrated thickening of the ascending colon with adenopathy, suggestive of an obstructive neoplastic process. Exploratory laparotomy confirmed a mesenteric tumor mass of the colon with retroperitoneal invasion and abscessed lymphadenopathy. An ileostomy was performed, and histopathology verified a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. The patient progressed favorably until readmission for acute kidney injury secondary to a high-output stoma. After stabilization, he was discharged with palliative oncologic follow-up. This case underscores the need to consider colorectal cancer in the differential diagnosis for young adults. Timely surgical intervention and multidisciplinary management are essential to optimize prognosis and quality of life.

titre: Integrating Nutrition, Exercise and Personalised Care for Sarcopenia Prevention and Management in Older Adults: An Evidence-Informed Narrative Framework
resume: Background: Sarcopenia is a progressive, age-related condition characterised by declines in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. It is associated with impaired mobility, loss of independence, poorer quality of life, and adverse health outcomes in older adults. Although nutrition is a cornerstone of sarcopenia prevention and management, its effectiveness is closely linked to exercise and to the individual’s broader clinical, functional, and psychosocial context. This study aimed to develop an integrated, evidence-informed framework for sarcopenia prevention and management in older adults, with particular emphasis on the role of nutrition within a person-centred model of care. Methods: An evidence-informed narrative synthesis was conducted to support a three-stage framework development process comprising targeted literature identification, evidence mapping and synthesis, and operational translation. Evidence was organised into key domains covering the clinical recognition and assessment of sarcopenia, the biological mechanisms underlying muscle decline, nutritional strategies, exercise, multimorbidity and medication-related factors, and personalised multidisciplinary care. These domains were then translated into an integrated, operational model of sarcopenia care. Results: The synthesis identified interconnected biological and clinical determinants of sarcopenia, including anabolic resistance, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, chronic low-grade inflammation, hormonal alterations, neuromuscular ageing, and the gut–muscle axis. Nutritional strategies addressing protein quantity, quality, distribution and timing, together with selected nutrients and dietary patterns, emerged as complementary components of management within an integrated approach that also incorporates resistance and multicomponent exercise. These findings informed a care pathway progressing from multidimensional assessment and clinical stratification to personalised nutritional, exercise and clinical interventions, with consideration of multimorbidity, medication-related factors and psychosocial determinants, followed by monitoring, reassessment, and adaptation over time. Conclusions: The proposed evidence-informed framework translates current knowledge of sarcopenia into a coordinated, multidisciplinary, and person-centred care pathway. Rather than replacing existing diagnostic or therapeutic recommendations, it offers a structured approach to integrating nutrition with exercise and broader clinical management, tailored to individual needs and goals. Prospective evaluation is needed to assess its feasibility, applicability, and potential contribution to integrated sarcopenia care.

titre: The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation
resume: Everyday stress is largely a learned pattern: a familiar cue, a fast reading of threat, an automatic reaction and a body that stays activated. Body-based practices such as mindfulness, interoceptive training, Somatic Experiencing and yoga target these patterns, but they are usually taught as techniques without a map of the mechanism they act on. Pain neuroscience education suggests that understanding such a mechanism can itself change experience. No comparable model exists for everyday self-regulation. This paper proposes the Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback, developed over six cohorts of a workshop for non-clinical adults. The loop describes any action as four steps: Sense (exteroception, proprioception and interoception), Process (perception as inference, weighted by context and safety), Choose (habitual reaction or goal-directed response after a pause) and Execute (autonomic and somatic output). Feedback from each outcome acts beneath all four steps, through synaptic plasticity, habit formation and allostatic load. The paper integrates the perception-action cycle, information-processing stages of choice, interoceptive inference, the autonomic space model and the defence cascade. It places a set of practices on the loop: full sensory awareness, grounding, orientation, resourcing, the pause, reduced stimulus and choice, slow movement and relaxation, each with a proposed mechanism and an assessment of the evidence. It also describes the model's translation into four practitioner skills. Seven testable propositions are derived for future evaluation. The model is offered as a teachable framework for wellbeing, not a treatment.

titre: Moving Beyond the Psychosis Paradigm: Clinical Insight in Nonpsychotic Disorders
resume: Clinical insight has been studied almost exclusively in schizophrenia, where impaired illness awareness predicts medication discontinuation and poor outcomes, shaping how insight is defined and measured across psychiatry. These psychosis-derived frameworks, however, fail to capture insight in nonpsychotic disorders. The phenomenology differs from schizophrenia in important ways. In nonpsychotic disorders, symptoms rest on a continuum with everyday experience. The challenge, therefore, lies in interpreting whether common emotions have become disordered. The severity-insight relationship is also heterogeneous; greater severity accompanies greater symptom acknowledgment in anxiety disorders but poorer insight in obsessive-compulsive disorder and eating disorders. Additionally, psychosis-derived measurement tools produce ceiling effects that miss the partial, fluctuating awareness typical of nonpsychotic presentations. This paper traces the development of insight research from its origins in psychosis, identifies the conceptual and methodological problems with extending this paradigm to other conditions, and proposes a configural model suited to nonpsychotic disorders, in which insight is assessed and targeted as a dynamic configuration of illness awareness, symptom appraisal, and treatment attitudes, shaped by metacognition and culture. We offer practical guidance for assessment and for tailoring interventions to patients' evolving understanding of their difficulties.

titre: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for epilepsy
resume: Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care. This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients' daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations. In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

titre: Decoding the functional differentiation of herb pairs in Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang: effects on gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, and Wnt signaling in IBS-D mice
resume: BACKGROUND: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with limited therapeutic options. Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang (TXYF), a classical Chinese herbal formula, has shown clinical efficacy, but the respective contributions of its full formula and of its constituent herb pairs, "Tonifying Tu (Earth)" (TT) and "Suppressing Mu (Wood)" (SM), remain incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to the interplay among the gut microbiota, the intestinal barrier, and Wnt signaling. METHODS: An IBS-D mouse model was established by combined water avoidance stress and chronic restraint stress. Mice received TXYF, TT, or SM for 14 days. Therapeutic effects were assessed by body weight, diarrhea rate, abdominal withdrawal reflex (AWR), intestinal permeability (FITC-dextran), histopathology (H&E, PAS, SEM), and qPCR of Wnt-related genes. Fecal metagenomics with KEGG functional annotation was performed to profile microbial composition and metabolic pathways. RESULTS: TXYF, TT, and SM alleviated IBS-D symptoms, accompanied by improvements in villus height, crypt depth, and goblet cell numbers. Tight junction ultrastructure appeared preserved in TXYF and SM groups, alongside upregulated β-catenin and downregulated RNF43, while Lgr5 showed no significant changes. Metagenomics suggested that TXYF was associated with higher microbial diversity, lower abundance of the opportunistic pathogen Staphylococcus, and enrichment of beneficial genera (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium), alongside shifts in Mammaliicoccus and Muribaculum. Herb-pair decomposition indicated differences that were most apparent at the functional level: TT was associated with TCA cycle and tryptophan metabolism enrichment (alongside Akkermansia gains), whereas SM was associated with flagellar assembly and chemotaxis enrichment. At the genus level, TT accounted for most of the large taxonomic shifts, whereas the changes associated with SM were smaller and largely concordant with those of TT. CONCLUSION: TXYF alleviated IBS-D in association with modulation of the gut microbiota, restoration of intestinal barrier function, and potential involvement of the Wnt signaling pathway. Herb-pair decomposition suggests differences mainly at the metabolic-pathway level: TT was associated with beneficial metabolic-support shifts, whereas SM was associated with motility-related functional shifts, with the whole-formula effect numerically exceeding that of either herb pair alone.

titre: Resistant starch and diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction: structure-dependent fermentation and gut-brain framework
resume: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) affects memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed through interacting metabolic, vascular, inflammatory, and neural disturbances. Human observational studies show heterogeneous microbial profiles and associations between circulating short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), particularly acetate, and cognitive status, although causal relationships remain unestablished. Resistant starch (RS) escapes small-intestinal digestion and is fermented in the colon. Differences among RS1-RS5 in physical accessibility, crystallinity, retrogradation, chemical modification, and lipid complexation determine microbial access and fermentation kinetics. Fermentation produces an integrated acetate-propionate-butyrate response: acetate supports cross-feeding, propionate contributes to FFAR2/FFAR3 and hepatic signaling, and butyrate links colonocyte energetics with epithelial, immune, and histone deacetylase-dependent pathways. This narrative Mini Review integrates human DACD observations, controlled RS feeding studies, and mechanistic animal evidence within a structure-dependent microbiota-gut-brain framework. The available evidence indicates that RS responses are conditioned by substrate structure, food matrix, and baseline degraders and cross-feeders, providing a basis for responder stratification. We therefore propose a proof-of-concept design using a chemically and physically specified RS, longitudinal microbiome and fecal/circulating SCFA profiling, separate intestinal and cerebrovascular measures, and multidomain cognitive outcomes. RS efficacy for cognitive outcomes in DACD remains unestablished, but RS offers a food-compatible and experimentally controllable platform for determining whether a reproducible microbial-metabolite response can modify cognition-relevant pathways in diabetes.

titre: From gut biomarkers to daily participation: reframing outcome assessment in dietary intervention research for autism spectrum disorder
resume: Biological research on dietary interventions in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is advancing rapidly, with increasing attention to gastrointestinal, microbiome, inflammatory, and metabolic mechanisms. However, biological responses may not necessarily translate into meaningful changes in feeding behavior, daily functioning, or participation. Feeding difficulties in autistic children are shaped by interacting gastrointestinal, sensory, behavioral, environmental, and family factors. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes the BIO-PART framework as an ICF-informed, multidimensional approach for evaluating the translation of biological responses into meaningful everyday feeding and mealtime-participation outcomes. BIO-PART is specifically focused on feeding and mealtime participation rather than serving as a general framework for all autism-related outcomes. The framework integrates five complementary domains: biological, clinical, functional, participation, and family/contextual outcomes. It is hypothesized that biological improvements alone will not consistently predict improvements in functional feeding and real-world mealtime participation, and that these relationships are moderated by sensory, behavioral, and contextual factors rather than confounded by them. The framework proposes that future dietary intervention trials should prespecify multidomain outcomes, consider clinically relevant feeding profiles, and incorporate multidisciplinary assessment involving biomedical and rehabilitation professionals. BIO-PART is intended as a testable conceptual framework rather than a validated clinical instrument; prospective longitudinal and randomized studies, beginning with a consensus (Delphi) step, are needed to evaluate its validity, feasibility, and clinical utility.

titre: Prader-Willi syndrome and the gut microbiota-endocrine-brain axis in hyperphagia and metabolic dysfunction
resume: INTRODUCTION: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a genetic neuroendocrine disorder with developmental transitions from infant feeding difficulty to hyperphagia, altered body composition, and heterogeneous metabolic risk. The contribution of intestinal microbial activity to these features remains uncertain. AIM OF THE STUDY: To critically appraise evidence for microbiota-endocrine-brain interactions in PWS and identify testable mechanisms that may distinguish PWS from common obesity. METHODS: This mechanism-oriented narrative review integrates human PWS observational and intervention studies identified through a documented PubMed search to 16 September 2026, supplemented by targeted mechanistic literature. Evidence is distinguished by study population, experimental design, and causal directness. RESULTS: PWS cohorts show context-dependent microbiota differences without a reproducible disease-specific taxonomic signature. Donor-to-mouse transfers support transmissibility of selected metabolic traits, whereas dietary and strain-specific probiotic trials show heterogeneous endocrine and clinical findings. A randomized fiber intervention modified microbial and metabolite measures without significant improvement in hyperphagia. Microbial metabolites may influence insulin physiology and enteroendocrine GLP-1/PYY signaling; links to ghrelin dynamics, oxytocin, and POMC-α-MSH-MC4R circuitry remain incompletely demonstrated in PWS. CONCLUSION: The gut microbiota is best regarded as a potential context-dependent modifier of genetically driven PWS rather than a proven cause of hyperphagia. Research should prioritize reproducible microbial functions, temporally matched metabolite-hormone measurements, and PWS-specific clinical endpoints.

titre: Bifidobacterium supplementation preserves gut microbiota stability and enhances wellbeing during short-term international travel: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Short-term international travel represents an acute environmental perturbation that can disrupt the gut microbiome and contribute to gastrointestinal, respiratory, and psychological symptoms. Probiotic supplementation has been proposed as a strategy to enhance microbiome resilience; however, its effects on both microbial dynamics and multi-domain health outcomes during travel remain incompletely understood. METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 40 healthy adults undertaking a 7-day trip from China to Europe were assigned to receive either a probiotic formulation containing Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis B94 and Lacticaseibacillus helveticus R0052 (2 × 109 CFU/day) or placebo. Stool samples were collected pre-travel (Day 0) and post-travel (Day 7) for metagenomic sequencing, taxonomic profiling, and functional analysis (KEGG, COG, LEfSe, qPCR). Participants recorded daily gastrointestinal, respiratory, and systemic symptoms and completed validated questionnaires assessing anxiety (GAD-7), wellbeing (WHO-5), and sleep quality (PSQI). RESULTS: Travel was associated with a significant reduction in gut microbiota alpha diversity in the placebo group, whereas diversity was preserved in the probiotic group. Taxonomic analysis demonstrated enrichment of B. animalis subsp. lactis post-travel in the probiotic group, confirmed by qPCR. Functional analysis based on KEGG annotation revealed minimal predicted pathway-level adaptation in the placebo group despite widespread disruption across COG categories, whereas the probiotic group exhibited enrichment of predicted metabolic pathways related to amino acid, carbohydrate, energy, and vitamin metabolism. These microbiome changes were associated with improved clinical outcomes. The probiotic group showed lower gastrointestinal symptom scores (including diarrhea, bloating, and reflux), reduced respiratory symptoms (e.g., sore throat, nasal congestion), and fewer systemic complaints such as dehydration and irritability. Anxiety scores remained within the non-clinical range in both groups but were lower post-travel in the probiotic group. Wellbeing improved clinically (≥10% increase in WHO-5) in the probiotic group, and global sleep quality (PSQI) was better post-travel compared with placebo. CONCLUSIONS: Probiotic supplementation during short-term travel preserves gut microbiome diversity and is associated with predicted functional adaptation of the gut microbial community, which is associated with improved gastrointestinal, respiratory, and psychological outcomes. These findings suggest that probiotic supplementation may contribute to microbiome resilience and support overall traveler health, potentially involving gut-immune and gut-brain interactions that require further mechanistic investigation. Clinical trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07384260, identifier: NCT07384260.

titre: Polysaccharides in the treatment of brain injury-related diseases: blood-brain barrier limitations and peripheral action pathways
resume: Natural polysaccharides possess outstanding advantages including low toxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and multi-target regulatory capabilities. They hold broad application prospects in neuroprotective research on Alzheimer's disease (AD) and depression. Owing to their high molecular weight and strong hydrophilicity, intact polysaccharides cannot readily cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Only a minor proportion enters the systemic circulation after oral administration. However, even under conditions of extremely low intracerebral exposure, polysaccharides still exhibit significant central neuroprotective effects. The underlying mechanism is that intact polysaccharides primarily act as fermentation substrates for gut microbiota, which then promote the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and modulate tryptophan and bile acid metabolism. These peripheral metabolites, upon entering the circulation, further regulate peripheral immune responses and the activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, improve neurotrophic signaling and redox homeostasis, and transmit signals to resident immune cells within the central nervous system via central boundary structures. Therefore, natural polysaccharides do not directly enter the brain. Instead, they exert neuroprotective effects via a cascade pathway involving the gut microbiota-peripheral metabolites-immune and humoral network. This article systematically elaborates on its multi-pathway mechanisms of action and summarizes adjunctive brain-targeted delivery approaches, including pathology-dependent modulation of BBB permeability and brain-targeted delivery. Future research should further elucidate the causal relationships among various signaling pathways, strengthen quality control and clinical trials, and facilitate their translational application.

titre: The effect of a low-iodine diet on remission and quality of life in newly diagnosed patients with Graves' disease: the ELODI superiority, parallel group randomized controlled trial protocol
resume: BACKGROUND: Healthcare is in the midst of a paradigm shift in which dietary intake, lifestyle, and patient autonomy play an increasingly central role. Research focuses on prevention and treatment of major noncommunicable diseases through dietary and lifestyle interventions. Thyroid disorders, the second most common endocrine disorders after diabetes and also classified as noncommunicable, have received little attention in this context. With respect to nutrition and lifestyle, it is well known that iodine, being an essential element for the synthesis of thyroid hormones, influences thyroid function. Excessive iodine intake has been associated with the worsening of Graves' disease, potentially reducing remission rates and increasing medication requirements. Conversely, reducing iodine intake may lower thyroid hormone production and improve treatment outcomes. This protocol marks the start of the ELODI study, in which we will investigate the broader effects of a temporary low-iodine diet in Graves' disease patients. OBJECTIVES: Primary outcome is remission rate 12 months after discontinuation of anti-thyroid drug therapy upon a low- versus sufficient-iodine-containing diet. Secondary outcomes include assessing effects on autoimmune activity, quality of life, and medication dosage. Other outcomes assessed are gut microbiota profile, lipid profile, Graves' ophthalmopathy risk, and GREAT + prediction. METHODS: This is a multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled superiority trial, with four parallel groups of 58 newly diagnosed adult participants. DISCUSSION: Graves' disease is mainly treated with medication nowadays and subsequently with radioactive iodine or thyroidectomy if drug treatment fails. Persistent uncertainty about the best available treatment and ongoing symptoms in treated patients support exploring dietary interventions. A low-iodine diet is accessible, empowers patients and may improve long-term remission while reducing medication use and side effects. Challenges include adherence, blinding and standardization. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Trial registration: OMON, NL-009585. Registered 4 March 2025, https://onderzoekmetmensen.nl/nl/trial/58211 . ICTRP, NL-OMON58211. Registered 4 March 2025, https://trialsearch.who.int/Trial2.aspx?TrialID=NL-OMON58211 . This paper is based on protocol version 1.2, October 2025.

titre: AI and mixed reality in child and adolescent psychiatry: where we were, where we are, and where we are headed
resume: Children and adolescents are the first generation to grow up in the era of integration of artificial intelligence and augmented reality (AR) into daily life, yet they are largely absent from the evidence base for the immersive technologies most likely to help them with their mental health challenges. This Perspective explores history of the field from early laboratory AR systems for simple phobias, through randomized trials of augmented reality exposure therapy on commercial headsets, to current platforms in with generative AI agents that animate spatially mapped characters for patients' experience of in vivo interactions. Augmented reality is potentially better matched to youth than virtual reality: the child remains in their own environment, on their own feet, in continuous visual contact with clinician and the caregiver, while feared social and physical stimuli are introduced under graded control. Because these platforms are transdiagnostic and function based, targeting impaired or avoided human interaction rather than a single diagnosis, they extend across anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, autism spectrum disorder, early psychosis, and school refusal, and offer an opportunity for standardized, behavioral assessment. There also risks specific to minors: AI-facilitated avoidance, engagement-optimized models that might validate distorted threat appraisal, cultural and developmental bias in AI-generated social behavior, and assent and data governance requirements. The pediatric evidence base is empty because the studies have not been attempted, and filling it requires immersive-technology infrastructure for both research and clinical care in child and adolescent psychiatry, and a generation of clinicians and investigators trained to use it.

titre: 3-Year Longitudinal Relationship Between Psychological Co-Morbidity and Irritable Bowel Syndrome Symptom Severity Using Cross-Lagged Analysis
resume: We examined changes in anxiety, depression, somatic symptom-reporting, gastrointestinal symptom-specific anxiety, and IBS symptom severity scores in 444 people with self-reported IBS over 3 years. We explored whether earlier psychological or gastrointestinal symptom scores predicted worse later outcomes. ABSTRACT Background Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is increasingly understood as a disorder of gut-brain interaction, in which bowel symptoms and psychological comorbidity influence one another over time. Aim To examine changes in anxiety, depression, somatic symptom-reporting, gastrointestinal symptom-specific anxiety, and IBS symptom severity scores over 3 years and explore whether earlier psychological or gastrointestinal symptom scores predicted later outcomes. Methods Repeated-measures analyses were used to describe mean changes in scores at baseline, 1 year, and 3 years. Repeated-measures correlations assessed whether scores tended to move together within individuals over time. Cross-lagged regression/path models were used to examine temporal relationships between scores, accounting for the previous value of each score. We performed a stratified analysis according to whether individuals met Rome IV criteria for IBS. Results Overall, 444 individuals with self-reported IBS were recruited. Mean anxiety, depression, and somatic symptom-reporting scores remained broadly stable during follow-up. In contrast, gastrointestinal symptom-specific anxiety and IBS symptom severity scores decreased over time (both p < 0.001). The strongest within-person associations were between anxiety and depression ( r = 0.40) and VSI and IBS-SSS ( r = 0.35). In the cross-lagged models, the strongest and most consistent finding was stability: people with higher scores at an earlier point in time tended to have higher scores on the same measure subsequently. Beyond this, somatic symptom-reporting (< 0.001 at 1 year and 0.003 at 3 years) and gastrointestinal symptom-specific anxiety scores (0.004 at 1 year and 0.005 at 3 years) were consistent predictors of later IBS symptom severity scores. In addition, baseline anxiety scores predicted higher 1-year somatic symptom-reporting scores, and 1-year somatic symptom-reporting scores predicted higher 3-year gastrointestinal symptom-specific anxiety scores. Conclusion Our findings support clinically important connections between earlier measures of psychological co-morbidity and subsequent IBS severity. Although causality cannot be proven, assessing and managing psychological symptoms may identify individuals at risk of persistent IBS symptom burden.

titre: Gut bacterial amyloid curli translocation as a major link in the central Aβ progression and cognitive decline in human and mouse models of AD
resume: INTRODUCTION: Emerging evidence links alterations in the gut microbiota to Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression via the microbiota-gut-brain axis. In this study, we propose that persistent gut dysbiosis from young adulthood may trigger central amyloid beta (Aβ) pathogenesis at a later age via enteric nervous system and systemic communications. METHODS: Novel Object Recognition test and Y-maze were used to determine cognitive impairment (CI) longitudinally in Tg2576 familial and sporadic huAPP (hAβ-KI) AD mice with gut inflammation or infection. 16S-rRNA-gene-amplicon sequencing to determine gut microbiota composition. Human and mouse AD plasma samples were used to perform proteomics analysis. RESULTS: Gut inflammation with dextran sulfate sodium or gut infection with curli-producing Escherichia coli caused dysbiosis-associated elevated luminal curli with increased translocation through plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (pEVs) in AD mice. Increased pEV-curli correlates with CI. Patients with mild CI who progressed to AD showed elevated pEV-curli. DISCUSSION: These findings identify a causal role of curli in host Aβ progression and highlight curli-pEVs as a potential early biomarker.
revue: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

titre: Associations Between Fecal Microbiota and Chemotherapy-Induced Gastrointestinal Toxicity and Symptoms in Patients With Cancer: A Systematic Review
resume: PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION: Gastrointestinal (GI) distress affects 50%-70% of patients receiving chemotherapy, reducing quality of life and treatment adherence. Management remains largely reactive because validated strategies for predicting GI distress are lacking. The fecal microbiota has emerged as a potential biologic contributor, but evidence linking specific microbial features to GI distress remains limited. LITERATURE SEARCH: A systematic review was conducted using PubMed®, CINAHL®, Embase®, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials to find studies published between 2006 and 2025. A total of 13 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a total sample size of 1,009 participants. DATA EVALUATION: Nine studies were prospective, and four were cross-sectional. Most used 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing for gut microbiota profiling, with one using shotgun metagenomics. GI distress outcomes were assessed using validated instruments, although the timing of assessment varied. SYNTHESIS: Sample size-weighted mean prevalence showed diarrhea (60%) as the most common GI distress symptom, followed by nausea/vomiting (55%), constipation (50%), and mucositis (30%). Reduced microbial diversity and depletion of short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, particularly Faecalibacterium and the Ruminococcaceae family, were consistently associated with diarrhea. Baseline microbiota profiles also demonstrated potential for predicting subsequent GI distress. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: GI distress comprises biologically distinct syndromes rather than a single condition. Microbiota profiling may facilitate early risk stratification and support precision symptom management.

titre: Associations Among Diet, Gut Microbiome, and Psychoneurologic Symptoms in Survivors of Childhood Posterior Fossa Tumors
resume: OBJECTIVES: To examine associations of dietary intake and gut microbiome with the psychoneurologic symptom (PNS) cluster, which includes pain, fatigue, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, in survivors of childhood posterior fossa tumors (SCPFTs). SAMPLE AND SETTING: SCPFTs were recruited from Children's Healthcare of Atlanta in Georgia between 2020 and 2022. METHODS AND VARIABLES: This secondary analysis included 28 SCPFTs from a cohort study who completed Pediatric Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System measures assessing pain, fatigue, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Fecal samples were collected for gut microbiome analysis. Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay diet scores were calculated using the Block Kids Food Screener. Quantitative Insights Into Microbial Ecology 2 was used to examine associations among key study variables. RESULTS: Participants were predominantly White (n = 16) and female (n = 19), with a mean age of 13.4 years (SD = 3.8). About half reported pain (n = 13), fatigue (n = 14), anxiety (n = 13), and depressive symptoms (n = 13); 12 experienced the PNS cluster. Increased intake of sugar-rich foods and beverages was associated with greater pain (p = 0.037). French-fry consumption was associated with increased fatigue. Greater leafy green intake was associated with lower depressive symptoms (p = 0.009). SCPFTs reporting greater pain and anxiety had significantly lower gut microbial alpha diversity than those without symptoms (for pain, Shannon index: p = 0.01, Simpson index: p = 0.022; for anxiety, Shannon index: p = 0.025, Simpson index: p = 0.019). Greater PNSs were associated with differential microbial abundance, including a higher level of relative abundance of Escherichia/Shigella (fatigue and depressive symptoms [both adjusted p < 0.05]), Streptococcus (anxiety [adjusted p < 0.05], depressive symptoms [adjusted p < 0.05], and the PNS cluster [adjusted p < 0.01]), and Frisingicoccus (pain [adjusted p < 0.01], depressive symptoms [adjusted p < 0.05], and the PNS cluster [adjusted p < 0.05]), whereas UBA1819 and Bacteroides had a lower relative abundance among survivors reporting fatigue (both adjusted p < 0.05). These patterns may reflect differences in inflammatory activity, aligning with the higher symptom burden observed. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING: SCPFTs experiencing PNSs demonstrated reduced gut microbial diversity and distinct shifts in inflammation-associated bacterial groups. Dietary patterns were also associated with more symptom burden, particularly pain. These findings highlight the importance of integrating comprehensive symptom assessment, microbiome-informed education, and nutritional guidance into survivorship care.

titre: [Chaihu Guizhi decoction ameliorates simulated spaceflight-induced depression by modulating the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites]
resume: This study aims to investigate the effect of Chaihu Guizhi decoction (CGD) on simulated spaceflight-induced depression and the underlying mechanisms associated with intestinal flora. Hindlimb unloading (HU) mice were used as simulation models to recreate the specific environment of spaceflight. Behavioral tests were used to demonstrate the depression-like behaviors. The gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomics, respectively. The serum metabolites were investigated by HM700 metabolomics. The results showed an increase in depression-like behavior in HU mice compared with control mice, and CGD enhanced the cognitive function in HU mice by regulating brain neurotransmitter levels and inhibiting neuronal injury. CGD treatment markedly altered the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites in HU mice, and the differences in metabolites were correlated with fluctuations of the gut microbiota. Additionally, serum metabolomics analysis revealed that CGD regulated the serum metabolites in HU mice, including the abundances of tryptophan and aspartic acid. CGD modulated the gut microbiota and fecal metabolites toward a more favorable profile and improved brain function, thereby protecting neurons and counteracting HU-induced injury. These findings suggest that CGD has a preventive effect on simulated spaceflight-induced depression through modulation of the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites.
revue: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]

titre: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for multiple sclerosis: A clinical framework for high-impact symptoms and family-centered care
resume: Speech and communication disorders have historically been framed as behavioral habits or peripheral motor problems, an interpretation that obscures their neurobiological complexity, contributes to stigma, and may discourage people from seeking treatment. This chapter applies the framework of Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation (NIPE) to speech disorders, focusing on developmental stuttering, childhood apraxia of speech, and Tourette syndrome with vocal tics, while drawing on obsessive-compulsive disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorder as mechanistically informative comparators. We integrate evidence suggesting that speech symptoms emerge from interactions among distributed cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical loops, cerebellar timing and prediction networks, auditory-motor integration pathways, executive and limbic systems, and glial mechanisms that regulate circuit stability. Within this framework, symptom variability and heterogeneous treatment response are reframed as expected features of state-dependent neural systems rather than failures of effort, motivation, or character. We describe how NIPE can translate these mechanisms into accessible, non-reductionist explanations that complement speech therapy, pharmacotherapy, neuromodulation, and multidisciplinary care by aligning expectations, reducing stigma, and supporting engagement during the gradual process of neuroplastic change. We also consider precision NIPE tailored to dominant mechanism profiles, the promise and ethical risks of digital delivery, and key limitations, including neurobiological oversimplification and limited direct trial evidence, that define priorities for establishing NIPE as a rigorously tested, person-centered component of care.

titre: Shared genetic architecture between major depressive disorder and four digestive diseases in European populations
resume: BACKGROUND: Patients diagnosed with cholelithiasis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and constipation frequently exhibit comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD). Although the underlying mechanisms remain elusive, potential genetic associations have been proposed. METHODS: Leveraging extensive genome-wide association study databases, the genetic association patterns between MDD and four digestive diseases (cholelithiasis, GERD, IBS, and constipation) were systematically investigated. A hierarchical analytical approach was adopted: linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC), genetic covariance analysis (GNOVA), and high-definition likelihood (HDL) were employed to evaluate genome-wide correlations. Regional genetic variation was analyzed using local variation association analysis (LAVA) to pinpoint significant genomic loci. A bivariate causal mixture model (MiXeR) was further applied to quantify genetic overlap. The conditional/conjunctional false discovery rate (cond/conjFDR) approach was utilized to detect shared loci. Tissue-specific enrichment analyses were conducted using linkage disequilibrium score regression for specifically expressed genes (LDSC-SEG) to identify phenotype-relevant tissue distributions. In addition, a genetics-informed cell-type spatial mapping approach was used to generate single-cell-resolution maps of disease-associated cell populations. RESULTS: The findings revealed statistically significant, positive genome-wide genetic correlations between MDD and all four digestive diseases. Multiple chromosomal regions exhibiting shared genetic signals were identified through local variation analysis. Key overlapping genetic loci were uncovered via cond/conjFDR analysis. MiXeR further indicated substantial genetic overlap among these traits. Furthermore, gene enrichment assessments indicated that MDD, constipation, and IBS demonstrated significant tissue-specific enrichment in various brain regions. Genetics-informed cell-type spatial mapping analyses also revealed similar patterns of cell-type-specific distribution across related tissues. CONCLUSION: This investigation constitutes the first genomic-level evidence of genetic overlap between MDD and the four digestive diseases, elucidating shared loci that may underlie comorbidity mechanisms. These results suggest novel molecular pathways for integrated clinical prevention and therapeutic strategies.

titre: Chinese herbal medicine (Yiqi Huayu Jiedu Decoction) combined with chemotherapy for preventing postoperative recurrence and metastasis in elderly gastric cancer patients: protocol for a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
resume: INTRODUCTION: Gastric cancer (GC) has a generally unfavorable prognosis. Elderly patients often tolerate dual-drug chemotherapy poorly, experience limited benefits from monotherapy, and face high rates of postoperative recurrence and metastasis. To address this unmet clinical need, this study evaluates the efficacy and safety of Yiqi Huayu Jiedu Decoction (YHJD) combined with chemotherapy in preventing recurrence and metastasis in elderly patients with stage II/III GC after surgery. METHOD: This is a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted across twelve hospitals in China. A total of 302 elderly GC patients (age ≥ 65 years) with pathological stage pII/pIII after D2 resection will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio into the experimental group (n = 151) and the control group (n = 151). Patients will receive a 6-month treatment. The primary outcome is disease-free survival (DFS), and secondary outcomes include overall chemotherapy completion rate, overall survival (OS), Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome scores, and quality of life (QoL) assessments. Safety indicators such as adverse events (AEs), as well as exploratory analyses including big data analytics and gut microbiota diversity, will also be evaluated. Subgroup analyses will be conducted to explore the heterogeneity of YHJD effects. DISCUSSION: The results of this randomized controlled trial will provide objective evidence for evaluating YHJD as an adjuvant therapy after GC surgery, contributing to an integrated treatment strategy combining TCM and chemotherapy to prevent postoperative recurrence and metastasis in elderly GC patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry, available at: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/ . TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ITMCTR2025001062. Registered on 09 May 2025.

titre: Cetobacterium somerae mitigates pollutant-induced behavioral abnormalities by modulating host tryptophan metabolism
resume: BACKGROUND: The gut symbiotic microbiota plays a fundamental role in host health, exerting a widespread influence on brain function and behavior. Environmental pollutants-pervasive in modern life-pose serious threats to both ecological integrity and public health. Notably, their effects may extend to the disruption of host behavioral regulation. However, whether pollutant-induced changes in the structure and function of the gut microbiome contribute causally to behavioral disturbances remains unclear. In particular, little is known about whether core symbiotic taxa can mitigate the detrimental effects of pollutants on the host, or through which molecular mechanisms such protection might occur. RESULTS: In this study, we show that gut symbiotic microbes play a critical role in alleviating anxiety-like behavior in zebrafish. To this end, we first established a zebrafish model of anxiety-like behavior using niclosamide exposure. Microbial diversity analyses revealed pronounced differences in gut microbial community structure between zebrafish exhibiting anxiety-like behavior and normal controls. Subsequently, fecal microbiota transplantation experiments identified Cetobacterium as a key biomarker species associated with anxiety-like behavior. Importantly, oral reintroduction of Cetobacterium effectively mitigated anxiety-like behavior in germ-free zebrafish. Moreover, integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that Cetobacterium modulates host tryptophan metabolism, thereby increasing serotonin (5-HT) levels in both the gut and serum. In contrast, pharmacological inhibition of tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) reduced 5-HT levels and markedly attenuated the anxiolytic effects of Cetobacterium. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insights into how gut symbiotic microbiota regulate host anxiety-like behavior and underscore the beneficial role of core gut symbionts in shaping host cognitive and behavioral functions. titre: Effects of early mobilization in post anesthesia care unit on postoperative gastrointestinal function and recovery quality in patients undergoing gynecological laparoscopic surgery: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Early mobilization is a core component of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, with current guidelines recommending that patients spend at least 2 h out of bed on the day of surgery. However, the optimal timing for safe mobilization following gynecological laparoscopic surgery remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effects of initiating structured, supervised mobilization as early as 30 min after awakening from general anesthesia in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) on postoperative gastrointestinal function and overall recovery quality. METHODS: This is a single-center, randomized controlled trial (RCT) in which eligible patients will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an early mobilization group or a standard care control group. Both groups will receive perioperative ERAS-based interventions. In the PACU, the experimental group will undergo structured early mobilization, while the control group will receive routine postoperative care. A total of 82 patients will be enrolled. The primary outcome is time to first postoperative flatus. Secondary outcomes include time to first defecation, quality of postoperative recovery, perioperative anxiety levels, patient satisfaction, adverse events (e.g., orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, fatigue), length of hospital stay, and readmission rates. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and during follow-up. DISCUSSION: This trial may show that early mobilization in the PACU may accelerate the time to postoperative flatus in patients undergoing gynecological laparoscopic surgery. This finding is potentially beneficial for recovery and offers new insights for enhancing rapid recovery protocols in this patient population. TRIAL NUMBER AND REGISTRY URL: ChiCTR2500102720; http://www.chictr.org.cn , Principal investigator: JIANG,Date of registration: May 19, 2025.

titre: Trajectory-based prediction modeling for persistent high LARS after rectal cancer resection
resume: BACKGROUND: Persistent high low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) severely impairs quality of life after sphincter-preserving surgery for rectal cancer, highlighting the urgent need for robust predictive tools. METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study enrolled 208 patients who underwent rectal cancer resection. LARS scores were prospectively assessed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Latent growth mixture modeling (LGMM) was used to identify distinct LARS trajectories. The primary clinical objective was to identify patients with persistent High LARS; accordingly, trajectory groups were designated, and the 6-month Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS) of the SF-36 were used to validate this classification. Ten machine learning algorithms and a clinical nomogram were developed to predict persistent High LARS. RESULTS: To identify patients with clinically meaningful persistent bowel dysfunction, we defined the High LARS Group as those with a High‑stable trajectory. The Low‑stable and Progressive improvement trajectories, which showed comparable HRQoL at 6 months, were combined into a Controlled LARS Group. This grouping was further validated by the significantly lower PCS and MCS scores in the High‑stable group versus the other two trajectories (all p < 0.001). Among the ten machine learning algorithms, Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.811, 95% CI: 0.753-0.870). The logistic regression-based nomogram showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.766, 95% CI: 0.696-0.829) and clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: The SVM achieved good predictive performance for persistent High LARS in this single‑center cohort, while the visually interpretable nomogram exhibited favorable interpretability and potential clinical practical value. Both tools show preliminary promise for supporting personalized risk stratification after sphincter‑preserving surgery, and their formal clinical utility requires confirmation in independent external cohorts.

titre: Clostridioides difficile colitis promotes neuroinflammatory responses in the prefrontal cortex: a preclinical study in mice
resume: BACKGROUND: Recurrent and severe Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a significant problem in the elderly. There is growing evidence that intestinal dysbiosis and inflammation, characteristic features of CDI, can influence brain function. We examined whether neuroinflammatory responses occur during CDI and employed a spatial metabolomic and transcriptomic approach, integrated with biomolecular analyses, to characterize these responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of a CDI mouse model. METHODS: 6-month-old mice were infected with C. difficile and euthanized on days 3, 4, and 7 post-infection (p.i.) for spatial metabolic analysis, bulk RNA-sequencing of the PFC, or systemic and gut inflammation analysis. RESULTS: Infected mice developed diarrhea and weight loss that peaked by day 3 and resolved by day 7. Spatial metabolomics analysis of the infected brain tissues indicated an imbalance of various neuroprotective metabolites in the PFC on day 4. Differential gene expression analysis identified 124 differentially expressed genes on day 7. Gene set enrichment analysis identified upregulation of pathways associated with neurodegenerative diseases and oxidative phosphorylation in infected mice. PFC protein and transcripts levels of GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) were increased in infected mice, indicating a reactive astrocyte response. Increased levels of lipocalin-2 (Lcn2), myeloperoxidase (MPO), calprotectin (S100A8/A9), IL-33, and IL-13 were also found in the PFC of infected mice. Levels of fecal Lcn2, a marker of intestinal epithelial barrier disruption, correlate positively with the levels of Lcn2, MPO, and S100A8/A9 in the PFC. CONCLUSION: Our findings show that CDI, in a mouse model, induces metabolomic and transcriptomic changes in the PFC, including genes associated with oxidative phosphorylation and neurodegeneration.

titre: Does timing matter-meta-analysis and systematic review of digital cognitive behavioral therapy in the perinatal period
resume: Depressive symptoms during and after pregnancy are a major concern in perinatal mental health, with implications for both mother and child. Digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a scalable and accessible intervention. Yet, it remains unclear whether its effectiveness depends on the timing of delivery-a potentially important factor given that pregnancy and the postpartum period differ in both psychological demands and practical circumstances. To examine whether digital CBT interventions are more effective when delivered during pregnancy, after childbirth, or across both periods, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials involving 7577 participants. Across all studies, digital CBT was associated with a significant overall reduction in depressive symptoms compared with control conditions (pooled mean difference = -2.03, 95%CI [-2.73, -1.34]), although substantial heterogeneity was present. In meta-regression analyses, interventions delivered after childbirth appeared more effective than those delivered during pregnancy (b = -1.99, 95%CI [-3.90, -0.08], p = 0.04). However, this contrast became marginally non-significant (p = 0.051) in sensitivity analyses excluding one high-risk-of-bias study, indicating that this finding should be interpreted with caution. Overall, these results suggest that digital CBT may be an effective approach for reducing perinatal depressive symptoms, with a possible advantage for postpartum delivery.

titre: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BD1 restores neurotransmitter homeostasis in chronic restraint stress mice via tryptophan metabolic reprogramming
resume: Psychological stress is a major precipitating factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, and the gut-brain axis has emerged as a critical regulator of mood and behavior, but how specific commensal microbes modulate host neurochemistry to confer stress resilience is largely unknown. In this study, we found that chronic restraint stress-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in mice are associated with intestinal microbial imbalance and impaired colonic synthesis of 5-HTP, the direct precursor of serotonin. Concurrently, this leads to reduced serotonin levels both systemically and in the CNS, as well as decreased BDNF in the hippocampus. Notably, supplementation with B. animalis BD1 restored the abundance of beneficial Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus as well as colonic 5-HTP levels, thereby normalizing serotonin and BDNF expression in the brain, and ultimately ameliorating depression-like behavior in CRS mice. In addition, we found that BD1 influenced synaptic plasticity and the expression level of the microglial surface marker Iba1 in CRS mice. Our findings reveal a key potential possible course of action: B. animalis BD1 rebalances the disturbed gut microbiota, thereby regulating host intestinal tryptophan metabolism, which in turn buffers depression-like behavior in mice under chronic restraint stress.

titre: Momentary Obsessive Beliefs Exacerbate Obsessions but Fail to Sustain Them Over Time: An EMA Examination of the Cognitive Behavioral Model for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
resume: The cognitive behavioral model (CBM) for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) theorizes that unwanted thoughts become obsessions when appraised using obsessive beliefs (responsibility/threat, need to control thoughts, and perfectionism). These beliefs are posited to uniquely relate to OCD symptom dimensions and maintain obsessions; however, no study has examined this naturalistically over time. We used an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) design to examine the naturalistic occurrence of obsessive beliefs, their prediction of concurrent and subsequent obsessions, and associations with baseline OCD symptom dimensions. Participants with OCD (n = 49) completed EMA items regarding current obsessions and obsessive beliefs 7x/day for 7 days. Data were analyzed using multilevel models controlling for compulsions. An obsessive belief was endorsed during 55.8% of prompts when an obsession was present. In contrast, an obsession was present for over three-fourths (77.4%) of prompts in which an obsessive belief was endorsed. When controlling for compulsions, greater obsessive beliefs were associated with greater obsessions concurrently but were associated with a decrease in obsessions at the next time point. Lower obsessive beliefs were associated with fewer obsessions concurrently but an increase in obsessions at the next time point. Momentary obsessive beliefs were differentially related to baseline OCD symptom dimensions, exhibiting both convergence and deviations from prior work. Findings supported the CBM such that obsessive beliefs occurred frequently, were associated with exacerbated obsessions, and differentially related to symptom dimensions. However, increases in beliefs did not predict subsequent increases in obsessions, suggesting that other variables may maintain obsessions in the long-term.
