titre: Primary Raynaud's phenomenon is associated with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a cohort study harnessing electronic healthcare records
resume: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the risk of incident attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in individuals with phenotypical primary Raynaud's phenomenon (RP). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: De-identified electronic health record data from a large, federated network of healthcare organisations, predominantly secondary and tertiary care centres in North America, between March 2005 and March 2025. PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with RP were identified using at least two international classification of diseases (ICD)-10 I73.0 codes, excluding systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases to approximate a primary RP phenotype. Comparator individuals had at least two irritable bowel syndrome ICD-10 K58 codes, excluding inflammatory bowel disease and connective tissue diseases. Cohorts were stratified a priori by age (<45 and ≥45 years). INTERVENTIONS: After propensity score matching, analyses included 32,516 matched pairs aged <45 years and 61,408 matched pairs aged ≥45 years. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident ADHD. Time-to-event analyses were conducted using 1:1 propensity score matched Cox proportional hazards models, with matching performed separately within age strata using relevant demographic, comorbidity and medication covariates, including ADHD-related and cardiovascular medications. RESULTS: Among 32,516 (<45 years) and 61,408 (≥45 years) matched pairs, RP was associated with a higher incidence of ADHD in individuals aged ≥45 years (HR 1.251, 95% CI 1.097-1.426), whereas evidence in those aged <45 years was weaker and did not reach conventional statistical significance (HR 1.088, 95% CI 0.996-1.189). CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, RP was associated with an increased risk of incident ADHD, including accounting for known implicated ADHD-related medications, although estimates under <45 years lack precision. Future research is warranted to confirm and explore these observations, including potentially shared pathobiological mechanisms, including small fibre neuropathy, between primary RP and ADHD.
revue: Journal of scleroderma and related disorders

titre: A Pilot Study of a Precision Treatment Trial Comparing Psychotherapy and Antidepressants for Depression in Indian Primary Care Settings
resume: Depression is commonly treated with either psychotherapy or antidepressants, but patients differ widely in their comparative responses. Identifying the most effective treatment for each individual is crucial to optimizing scarce resources, particularly in low-resource settings. This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a precision treatment trial comparing psychotherapy based on behavioral activation (the Healthy Activity Program) with antidepressant medication (fluoxetine) in adults with depression in primary care settings in India. A single-blind, two-arm randomized controlled pilot was conducted with adults aged ≥18 years with moderate to severe depression (PHQ-9 score≥10) from eight primary healthcare centers in Bhopal, India. Primary outcomes were feasibility and acceptability, assessed using indicators of study implementation (recruitment, randomization, treatment fidelity, completeness of assessments, biologic sample collection, and safety) and participant engagement (retention and treatment adherence). Secondary outcomes included changes in depressive symptoms, remission, and patients' subjective sense of improvement at the 3-month endpoint. Of 578 individuals screened, 180 were eligible and 76 (42%) enrolled. Retention was 82% at 3 months. Psychotherapy participants attended 5.6/6-8 sessions, while medication participants consumed 57.9% of prescribed doses. Completion rates of study assessments were high (72-100%), and missing data were minimal, although some baseline measures were burdensome and were subsequently shortened for the main trial. Biologic sample collection was feasible, with 67% of participants consenting to blood draws. Depressive symptoms improved across both arms, with 45.2% achieving remission. However, treatment responses varied substantially within each arm (psychotherapy: -9.1 [SD = 6.5]; medication: -7.6 [SD = 6.9]), indicating marked individual heterogeneity. This pilot demonstrated the feasibility and acceptability of implementing a precision treatment trial for depression in Indian primary care, identified refinements to optimize procedures for the main trial, and supported the potential to identify the optimal treatment for each patient.

titre: Digital Facing Eating Disorder Fears: An Acceptability and Feasibility Open Series Trial of a Digital Relapse Prevention Program for Anorexia Nervosa
resume: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a serious psychiatric illness. Despite its severity, most individuals with AN never achieve full recovery and more than 50% of patients relapse after treatment. One of the primary reasons that many treatments are limited in their effectiveness is that they do not specifically target cognitive-affective pathology. Furthermore, many treatments are limited by lack of scalability. New treatments that target cognitive-affective pathology (e.g., anxiety, fear) and that are scalable are needed to improve both outcomes and access to evidence-based care. As such, the current open series trial (N = 10) piloted a new digital, exposure-based modular treatment for AN-related fear and anxiety, called Digital Facing Eating Disorder Fears (FED-F). FED-F consists of five digital modules focused on four common AN fears: weight gain, food, social eating, and physical sensations, and one module of cognitive restructuring. Modules are complemented by homework assignments and light-touch coaching. FED-F had high feasibility, acceptability, mixed findings for target engagement (i.e., decreased avoidance behaviors), and good initial clinical efficacy, with pre-post effect sizes ranging from small to large, dependent on the type of fear. Overall, FED-F is a promising new digital treatment that could be used to decrease anxiety-based cognitions and behaviors present in AN. Future work should test FED-F in a randomized controlled trial design especially with populations who may have difficulty accessing evidence-based care.

titre: Hearing voices in patients with functional seizures: Case reports and insights into mechanisms and treatments
resume: INTRODUCTION: Functional seizures (FS), paroxysmal alterations with motor, sensory, cognitive, and autonomic features without ictal epileptiform activity, are the most common subtype of functional neurological disorder (FND). FS often coexist with other symptoms, one of them being auditory hallucinations (AH); however, evidence examining this relationship is outdated and limited. The link between FND and AH has been explored, with mixed opinions on whether hallucinations should be considered part of the functional cognitive disorder. Importantly, the specific relationship between FS and AH has not been systematically examined. METHODS: We present 2 patients (one pediatric and one young adult) with AH and FS who underwent a 6-week multidisciplinary FND therapy program (weekly physiotherapy and psychotherapy) and experienced complete remission of AH. RESULTS: Our cases add to the limited literature on the overlap between AH and FS. Whereas prior reports have typically related AH in patients with FS to schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders, our patients did not meet the full DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia, and presented hallucinations without additional psychotic features. In both, hallucinations were temporally and/or contextually related to FS episodes and disappeared after a multidisciplinary FND therapy program. CONCLUSIONS: Hallucinations are a nonspecific symptom of a wide range of psychiatric and nonpsychiatric conditions. The mechanisms underlying AH are multiple and remain under debate; however, AH and FND likely share common mechanisms involving disrupted self-agency and interoception, underscoring the importance of integrated therapeutic approaches over isolated psychiatric treatments.

titre: Diet correction after perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 fails to rescue gut dysbiosis, serotonin pathway and psychiatric-like behavior in adult rats
resume: Perinatal dietary deficiencies such as vitamin B9 and B12 induce persistent gut dysbiosis, metabolic, physiologic imbalances and behavioral defects that could extend into adulthood, but the underlying fetal programming mechanisms remain poorly understood. We have investigated the long-term consequences of a perinatal vitamin B9 and B12 deficiency associated dysbiosis and focusing on sex-dependent outcomes related to behavior and molecular markers of the gut-brain axis. Despite post-weaning diet normalization, adult systemic metabolism related to B-vitamins was only partially restored. Intestinal dysbiosis persisted into adulthood and was characterized by altered beta-diversity and reduced relative abundance of the Prevotella genus. Both male and female offspring showed behavioral alterations, including reduced social interactions and depressive-like behaviors. Despite a sex-independent balance of kynurenine metabolites in both the frontal cortex and the colon, females displayed signs of chronic colonic inflammation, whereas males displayed alterations in immune homeostasis. Finally, perinatal B-vitamins deficiency associated dysbiosis exerted long-lasting effects into adulthood, despite post-weaning diet normalization. Early-life metabolic and intestinal microbiota dysregulations were associated with disrupted tryptophan metabolism, persistent inflammation, intestinal dysbiosis, and the emergence of depressive-like behaviors in adulthood.

titre: Effectiveness of wellness programs in university students for mental health including health-related quality of life: A systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of multicomponent wellness programs on psychosocial health in university students. Participants: Post-secondary students (i.e., college, university, and graduate students). Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from 2002-2023. We conducted independent screening and data extraction for eligible programs consisting of at least two interventions targeting wellness (i.e., nutrition, physical activity, mindfulness, emotional intelligence) lasting ≥8 wk. Our target outcomes included stress, depression, anxiety, overall health-related quality of life (HRQL), academic satisfaction, emotional intelligence, and body mass index (BMI). Data were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMD) or mean differences (MD) using a random effects model. We independently assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using Cochrane and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approaches, respectively. Results: Eight RCTs (n = 4627) were included and four (50%) were judged to be at low risk of bias. Physical activity, nutrition, and mindfulness were each included in three (38%) multicomponent wellness programs, and nutrition and mindfulness were the most frequently combined interventions (50%). Wellness programs delivered over a period of 8 to 14 wk may reduce stress (SMD: -0.20, 95% CI: -0.33 to -0.07; n = 2664 participants; low certainty) and depression (SMD: -0.29, 95% CI: -0.50 to -0.08; n = 1488 participants; low certainty), while the evidence is very uncertain for reducing anxiety (SMD: -0.32, 95% CI: -0.61 to -0.02); n = 1068 participants; very low certainty). With respect to overall physical and mental wellbeing, programs likely improve overall HRQL (SMD: 0.43, 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.59; n = 697 participants; moderate certainty). Overall, considerable participant loss to follow-up and heterogeneity existed, limiting our certainty in the effects for all outcomes. Conclusion: Wellness programs may offer psychosocial benefits for university students, particularly with respect to improved health-related quality of life. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42023461401.
revue: Journal of American college health : J of ACH

titre: New animal models of obsessive-compulsive disorder and their value to novel drug discovery
resume: INTRODUCTION: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is a chronic and highly debilitating neuropsychiatric disorder with profound clinical heterogeneity and high-degree of treatment-resistance. The field relies heavily on monoamine-focused drug therapies highlighting an imperative to develop novel therapeutic targets. AREAS COVERED: This review provides an evaluation of the expanding animal-model landscape for OCD, evaluating transgenic (e.g. Sapap3, Slitrk5, Hoxb8), pharmacological, and naturally occurring models. It also examines how these platforms enable the investigation of micro-level synaptic changes and broader cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical (CSTC) circuit dysfunction. Furthermore, the article synthesizes findings from recent circuit-level and pharmacological examinations such as optogenetics, glutamate-modulators, endocannabinoid signaling, novel probiotic approaches, and other novel molecular and receptor targets to assess their translational potential. Literature was retrieved through a comprehensive search of PubMed database. EXPERT OPINION: The future of OCD drug discovery lies in a shift toward mechanism-based pharmacotherapy that moves beyond traditional serotonergic targets. By leveraging the high-throughput screening capabilities of modern transgenic models to identify compounds capable of achieving disease-modifying mechanisms rather than mere symptom suppression, the field will move toward novel targeted pharmacological options for treatment-resistant OCD.

titre: Network Control Theory in Psychiatry: From Connectivity-Derived Controllability to Brain-State Transitions and Interventions
resume: Psychiatric disorders are increasingly conceptualized as disruptions in brain dynamics, particularly in how activity patterns evolve over time. Network Control Theory (NCT), a framework derived from control engineering, has emerged as a promising approach for studying these dynamics. Yet, despite its growing application in psychiatry, it remains unclear whether NCT has provided mechanistic or clinical insights beyond conventional measures of network topology. Here, we conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of NCT applications across major psychiatric disorders in adults. Of 178 records identified, 26 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 17 unique cohorts spanning schizophrenia spectrum disorders, major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Across studies, a recurring pattern of lower modal controllability was reported in several disorders (3 independent cohorts), although regional findings were heterogeneous and diagnostic specificity was limited. In contrast, task-based analyses under cognitive load (2 cohorts) and energy-based metrics (2 cohorts), though scarce, revealed more extensive case-control abnormalities and between-disorder differentiation. Intervention studies provided preliminary evidence that NCT-derived measures may predict treatment response and inform individualized neuromodulation targets (4 cohorts). However, 21 of 26 studies exclusively relied on connectivity-derived controllability metrics that were closely related to conventional measures of network topology and characterized model-implied control properties rather than directly observed state transitions. Furthermore, translational evidence came largely from single-arm, retrospective and simulation studies. The distinct value of NCT in psychiatry therefore remains to be established. Future progress requires the use of empirically observed brain states, energy-based measures, and prospective intervention studies.

titre: FRCUTAN INTOLERANCE AND LOW FODMAP DIET
resume: This narrative review examines fructan intolerance and the role of the low-FODMAP diet in the management of gastrointestinal symptoms, particularly in individuals with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and non-celiac wheat sensitivity. The article discusses the chemical structure, dietary sources, digestion and colonic fermentation of fructans, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying fructan-related gastrointestinal symptoms, including gas production, intestinal distension and visceral hypersensitivity. It further evaluates current scientific evidence regarding the effectiveness of the low-FODMAP diet, its clinical applications, nutritional considerations, effects on gut microbiota, and the importance of structured food reintroduction and personalized dietary management. This manuscript is based on a literature review conducted as part of an undergraduate medical thesis at Nicolae Testemițanu State University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Chișinău, Republic of Moldova. Keywords: Fructan intolerance; Fructans; Low-FODMAP diet; Irritable bowel syndrome; Gastrointestinal symptoms; Gut microbiota; Dietary management.

titre: The Tree Shrew Model Connecting Stress, the Gut–Brain Axis, and Mental Health
resume: The increasing pervasiveness of artificial light at night (LAN) has turned light‐induced circadian disruption into a significant, yet underappreciated, risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders. The gut–brain axis is a key mediator linking environmental stressors with brain function; however, how prolonged nocturnal light exposure (“staying up late”) impairs mental health remains poorly understood. Here, we take the staying‐up‐late model established in the diurnal tree shrew ( Tupaia belangeri chinensis ) as our central narrative thread, and review recent advances across circadian biology, gut microbiome neuroscience, and neural circuit research. We established a clinically relevant staying‐up‐late paradigm in tree shrews by extending daily light exposure by 4 h for 3 consecutive weeks, which recapitulates the most common form of light‐induced stress in modern humans. This paradigm triggered a cascade of abnormalities, including gut microbiota dysbiosis enriched Proteobacteria and Actinobacteria but depleted Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes relative to controls, brain structural remodeling (increased gray matter density in the prefrontal and visual cortices, and decreased white matter density in the corpus callosum and thalamus, and impaired cognition. Washed microbiota transplantation (WMT), a refined form of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), significantly accelerated recovery and exhibited specific regional targeting in the brain. A complementary study further identified a direct retina–perihabenular nucleus–nucleus accumbens (retina–pHb–NAc) pathway that mediated light‐induced depressive‐like behaviors. Together, these findings support a dual‐pathway model in which light‐induced stress engages a retina‐driven mood circuit and a microbiota‐dependent pathway that reshapes brain structure and cognition. We propose that this framework advances our mechanistic understanding and may inform microbiota‐targeted interventions such as WMT for stress‐related neuropsychiatric conditions.

titre: Stilbenoid Scaffolds at the Interface of Anxiety and Glucose Homeostasis: A Mechanistic and Translational Review of Preclinical Evidence and Evaluation Strategies
resume: Anxiety and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are frequently associated conditions that share several pathophysiological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, insulin resistance, and dysregulation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis. The bidirectional relationship between metabolic dysfunction and anxiety highlights the need to investigate pharmacological agents that may influence both neurological and metabolic parameters. Lunularin, a dihydrostilbene and gut microbial metabolite of resveratrol, has attracted interest because of its potential biological activities. However, its anxiolytic potential and influence on glucose homeostasis remain insufficiently investigated. The present study aims to investigate the anxiolytic potential of lunularin and its influence on glucose homeostasis in an experimental model of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Diabetes will be induced in Wistar rats using streptozotocin and nicotinamide (STZ–NA). Animals will be divided into appropriate experimental groups, including normal control, diabetic control, standard treatment, and lunularin-treated groups at selected dose levels. The anxiolytic potential of lunularin will be evaluated using behavioural paradigms such as the elevated plus maze and actophotometer, while locomotor activity and motor coordination will be assessed to distinguish anxiolytic effects from nonspecific behavioural changes. Glucose homeostasis will be evaluated through fasting blood glucose, glycated haemoglobin, and relevant metabolic parameters. Biochemical investigations may include oxidative stress markers, antioxidant status, and selected molecular pathways associated with metabolic and behavioural regulation. Histopathological examination of relevant tissues will provide additional evidence of treatment-associated changes.The study is expected to provide preliminary experimental evidence regarding the relationship between lunularin-mediated behavioural responses and glucose regulation in diabetic animals. The findings may contribute to understanding the pharmacological potential of lunularin and identify directions for further mechanistic and translational research.

titre: Plant-Based Dietary Patterns in Prostate Cancer: A Review of Mechanistic Pathways and Disease Progression
resume: Pendahuluan: Kanker prostat (PCa) merupakan keganasan yang umum terjadi pada pria di seluruh dunia. Semakin banyak bukti menunjukkan bahwa pola makan berbasis nabati dan pola makan rendah karbohidrat dapat memengaruhi luaran PCa melalui jalur metabolik, inflamasi, dan molekuler. Tinjauan naratif ini merangkum bukti mengenai pola-pola makan tersebut beserta potensi mekanisme biologis yang mendasarinya. Metode: Literatur yang relevan diidentifikasi melalui penelusuran di PubMed, Scopus, dan Web of Science, dilengkapi dengan studi epidemiologis dan mekanistik yang mengkaji pola makan, luaran PCa, serta jalur biologis yang terlibat. Hasil: Kepatuhan yang lebih tinggi terhadap pola makan sehat berbasis nabati umumnya dikaitkan dengan risiko progresi penyakit yang lebih rendah, tingkat keparahan penyakit yang berkurang, kualitas hidup yang lebih baik, dan angka kematian spesifik akibat PCa yang lebih rendah. Lemak yang berasal dari tanaman dikaitkan dengan luaran klinis yang lebih baik dibandingkan lemak yang berasal dari hewan. Intervensi pola makan rendah karbohidrat menunjukkan efek metabolik yang menguntungkan serta memperpanjang waktu penggandaan antigen spesifik prostat (PSA), yang mengindikasikan potensi manfaat dalam menunda progresi biokimia. Mekanisme yang diusulkan mencakup penurunan inflamasi sistemik dan stres oksidatif, perbaikan sinyal insulin dan insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), metabolisme lipid yang lebih baik, serta modulasi ekspresi gen yang terkait dengan tumor. Namun, bukti langsung yang menghubungkan intervensi pola makan dengan perubahan mikrobioma usus pada pria dengan PCa masih terbatas. Kesimpulan: Pola makan sehat berbasis nabati—dan dalam tingkat tertentu, intervensi rendah karbohidrat—dapat menjadi strategi pelengkap untuk memperbaiki luaran PCa, kemungkinan melalui mekanisme metabolik, inflamasi, dan molekuler. Akan tetapi, bukti yang ada saat ini belum dapat menetapkan hubungan sebab-akibat. Studi prospektif lebih lanjut yang mengintegrasikan penilaian pola makan, pemprofilan mikrobioma usus, dan pendekatan multi-omics diperlukan untuk memperjelas mekanisme yang mendasari serta implikasi klinisnya. Introduction: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy among men worldwide. Growing evidence suggests that plant-based and low-carbohydrate dietary patterns may influence PCa outcomes through metabolic, inflammatory, and molecular pathways. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on these dietary patterns and their potential biological mechanisms. Methods: Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by epidemiological and mechanistic studies examining dietary patterns, PCa outcomes, and underlying biological pathways. Results: Greater adherence to healthy plant-based dietary patterns was generally associated with lower risks of disease progression, reduced disease severity, improved quality of life, and lower PCa-specific mortality. Plant-derived dietary fats were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes than animal-derived fats. Low-carbohydrate dietary interventions demonstrated beneficial metabolic effects and prolonged prostate-specific antigen (PSA) doubling time, suggesting potential benefits in delaying biochemical progression. Proposed mechanisms include reduced systemic inflammation and oxidative stress, improved insulin and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) signaling, favorable lipid metabolism, and modulation of tumor-related gene expression. However, direct evidence linking dietary interventions to gut microbiome alterations in men with PCa remains limited. Conclusions: Healthy plant-based dietary patterns and, to a lesser extent, low-carbohydrate interventions may represent complementary strategies for improving PCa outcomes, potentially through metabolic, inflammatory, and molecular mechanisms. However, current evidence does not establish causality. Further prospective studies integrating dietary assessment, gut microbiome profiling, and multi-omics approaches are needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.

titre: SENSORY STABILIZATION AND EX-POST COGNITIVE SEDIMENTATION: BODILY TRANQUILITY AS A CONDITION FOR TIMELINE CALIBRATION IN THE LCBASIC METHOD
resume: Background and Problem: Conventional cognitive and psychophysiological approaches frequently attempt to restructure emotional memories through discursive analysis performed during or immediately after states of sympathetic activation. Within the LCBASIC Method (Basal Cerebral Lucidity of the Cortical Integrative Systemic Architecture), it is demonstrated that recording or interpreting events while the organism operates under high electrical impedance (high-beta brainwaves, mandibular tension, and mediastinal compression) distorts sensory capture and encodes the episode as an atemporal threat within the Emotional Experience Database of the ancestral amygdala. Objective: To formalize the protocol of Prior Sensory Stabilization and Ex-Post Cognitive Sedimentation, establishing bodily tranquility as an indispensable biophysical prerequisite for the functional consolidation of memory along the timeline. Protocol Architecture: The model articulates four sequential stages: (1) interruption of motor reaction via the Central Inhibitory Veto (120–200 ms) and thermal drainage through the Deceleration Gradient (45–90 min); (2) calibration of the Somatic Receptacle through the alignment of the three peripheral terminals (parallel pedal axis, masseter depressurization, and mediastinal opening) and 0.1 Hz cardio-encephalic resonance; (3) simultaneous, distortion-free reception of internal interoceptive (visceral) impulses and external exogenous data through the 12 sensory and regulatory channels (5 exogenous fruits and 7 hidden fruits); and (4) Ex-Post Cognitive Sedimentation within the demagnetized Ventromedial Prefrontal Cortex. Conclusion: Bodily tranquility converts emotionally dense experiences into organized, chronologically indexed cognitive records, enabling memory to operate in the future as a functional navigational instrument along the timeline rather than an automatic reactive trigger.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: • Thermodynamic Unification of Propositional Belief Evaluation: Subsuming Content-Independent fMRI Signatures Under Metabolic Active Inference
resume: Duplicate *** Please cite original on Zenodo - https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24425421 Neuroimaging studies of propositional evaluation reveal that the human brain relies on a remarkably consistent, content-independent network to assess truth, falsehood, and uncertainty. Anchored in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), the anterior insula, and the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this circuitry operates identically whether we are evaluating mathematical equations, geographical facts, ethical claims, or religious doctrines (Harris et al., 2008, 2009). Yet classical neuroimaging taxonomies treat belief, disbelief, and uncertainty as static, cost-free labels. They leave an essential question unanswered: why do specific mental states impose distinct subjective effort, reaction-time delays, and metabolic costs? Here, we resolve this problem by unifying content-independent neuroimaging findings within the Thermodynamic State-Space Model (TSSM) of active inference. First, we derive explicit biophysical couplings that link variational free energy (F) and Kullback-Leibler divergence (D_KL) directly to Landauer work bounds, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis flux (J_ATP), and regional cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen consumption (CMRO2). Second, we explain vmPFC reward signaling as neurochemical reinforcement for the rapid collapse of free energy into familiar, prior-congruent basins. In contrast, we frame anterior insula disgust responses as interoceptive alarms triggered by costly prediction-error spikes, which force the dorsal ACC (dACC) to inhibit default comprehension signals. Third, we expose a major methodological blind spot in forced-choice fMRI experiments. Across decision deadlines, the single "undecided" category conflates two entirely different cognitive realities: low-energy apathetic disengagement (U_apathy) and high-energy active epistemic neutrality (U_active), a frontoparietal control policy governed by a calibrated prefrontal metabolic depletion threshold (ζ_crit ≈ 0.45). Finally, we specify a falsifiable 7-Tesla hybrid multi-echo fMRI and dual-voxel event-related proton functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-fMRS) protocol tracking regional lactate (ΔLac) and glutamate (ΔGlu) turnover over extended evaluation windows (τ_d = 30 s) to adjudicate between effortless clarity and metabolic gating.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Mindfulness-based interventions for stress reduction and recovery in adult stroke survivors: a scoping review protocol
resume: Title: Mindfulness-based interventions for stress reduction and recovery in adult stroke survivors: a scoping review protocol Description / Protocol Summary: Background and Objective: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, often accompanied by psychological distress, perceived stress, anxiety, and cognitive or functional impairments that hinder rehabilitation. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are increasingly integrated into neurological rehabilitation to support emotional regulation and overall recovery. The objective of this scoping review is to map the existing peer-reviewed evidence on the use of mindfulness-based interventions to promote recovery and reduce stress in adult stroke survivors. Review Question: What is the current evidence regarding the use, characteristics, and outcomes of mindfulness-based interventions aimed at supporting recovery and reducing stress in adult stroke survivors? Eligibility Criteria (PCC Framework): - Population (P): Adults (aged 18 years and older) with a clinical diagnosis of ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, at any stage of recovery (acute, subacute, or chronic). Studies focusing exclusively on caregivers or healthcare professionals will be excluded. - Concept (C): Any structured or adapted mindfulness-based intervention (e.g., Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction [MBSR], Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy [MBCT], mindfulness meditation, or mindful movement) designed to support post-stroke recovery and stress reduction. - Context (C): Any clinical, inpatient, outpatient, community, or home-based rehabilitation setting, with no geographical restrictions. - Types of Sources: Primary peer-reviewed quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies (e.g., randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, pilot/feasibility studies, case series). Conference abstracts, book chapters, study protocols, and non-peer-reviewed articles will be excluded. Search Strategy: A comprehensive literature search will be conducted across four electronic databases—PubMed, Cochrane Library, PEDro, and OpenAlex—from database inception to November 2026. No language restrictions will be applied during the initial search, with full-text inclusion focused on studies published in English or Italian. Study Selection and Data Charting: All retrieved records will be imported into Rayyan software for deduplication and screening. Due to single-author constraints, title/abstract and full-text screening will be performed independently in two separate rounds spaced two weeks apart to ensure intra-rater reliability. Data will be extracted using a standardized charting form (including study design, sample characteristics, stroke phase, type and duration of mindfulness intervention, and stress/recovery outcomes). Findings will be synthesized narratively and presented following the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines.

titre: A Inconstitucionalidade do Art. 24, V, da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025: Os Limites Constitucionais da Responsabilidade de Terceiros no IBS e na CBS
resume: O presente estudo examina os limites constitucionais da responsabilidade tributária de terceiros no âmbito do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços e da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços instituídos pela reforma tributária, com foco na controvérsia em torno do artigo 24, inciso V, da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025, cuja crítica doutrinária costuma concentrar-se na compatibilidade infraconstitucional com o Código Tributário Nacional. O objetivo do estudo consiste em identificar os parâmetros constitucionais que restringem a responsabilização de terceiros nesses tributos e testar a validade do referido dispositivo frente a tais balizas, inclusive diante da autorização específica prevista na Constituição para definir sujeitos passivos que concorram para a realização, execução ou pagamento da operação. Metodologicamente, adota-se abordagem dogmático-jurídica conduzida pelo método hipotético-dedutivo, com formulação da hipótese e enfrentamento de hipóteses concorrentes, análise de casos hipotéticos, exame da legislação vigente até novembro de 2026 e seleção de precedentes do Supremo Tribunal Federal e do Superior Tribunal de Justiça. Os principais resultados e discussões demonstram que a divergência frente ao Código Tributário Nacional não basta por si só diante do caráter de lei complementar especial e posterior, mas revelam que a norma impugnada ultrapassa o círculo constitucional de sujeitos passivos, prescinde de dever próprio de colaboração, cria desconsideração administrativa de alcance subjetivo universal e quantitativamente ilimitado na modalidade ligada ao abuso da personalidade jurídica e estende multas punitivas sem correspondência com a conduta do terceiro. Conclui-se que o artigo 24, inciso V, da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025 é materialmente inconstitucional — cabendo interpretação conforme a Constituição apenas subsidiariamente —, sem que sua invalidade gere vazio normativo para condutas constitucionalmente sujeitas à responsabilização.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Real-Time PCR-Based Identification of Blastocystis Subtypes and Their Impact on Th1/Th2 Cytokine Balance
resume: Blastocystis spp., one of the most common intestinal protist species found globally, has many subtype-specific characteristics that have been shown to modify the immune system (e.g., by producing cytokines) as well as being associated with particular gastrointestinal symptoms; however, the relationship between the number of subtypes of Blastocystis and the balance of cytokines produced by the immune system hasn't been fully explored yet, especially when using sensitive molecular diagnostic tests to measure it. This study was conducted to identify Blastocystis subtypes using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and assess the possible relationship of the subtypes to Th1/Th2 cytokine responses among symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals infected with Blastocystis. Materials and Methods A cross-sectional molecular immunological study was conducted among 180 participants consisting of symptomatic Blastocystis-positive patients, asymptomatic carriers, and healthy controls. Stool samples were analyzed for the detection and molecular characterization of Blastocystis subtypes by RT-PCR targeted to the SSU-rRNA gene. Subtype and sequence-verified positive samples were confirmed by sequencing and subtype analysis. Serum concentrations of Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2, and IL-12) and Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-10, and IL-13) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software (version 27.0), with p-values of <0.05 being statistically significant. RT PCR analysis showed a large diversity in Blastocystis subtypes in the samples that tested positive for this organism with the most frequent subtype being ST3 (40.0%), followed by ST1 (23.6%), ST2 (20.0%), and lastly ST4 (11.4%). ST1 and ST3 were found to have strong positive correlations with symptomatic gastrointestinal manifestations (i.e., abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloating, and irritable bowel syndrome-IIBS-like symptoms). In addition, symptomatic individuals had significantly greater levels of Th1 associated cytokines, particularly IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2, and IL-12 (p<0.001), consistent with pro inflammatory immune activation. Conversely, both ST2 and ST4 infections had significantly increased levels of Th2 associated cytokines, (IL-4, IL-10, and IL-13; p<0.001), indicating that these groups had responses primarily in the anti inflammatory and immunoregulatory responses. Correlation analysis supported strong positive correlations between ST1/ST3 infections and Th1 cytokine polarization but also showed positive correlations between ST2/ST4 infections and Th2 cytokine polarization. This study shows that the diversity of Blastocystis subtypes affects the immune response of the host. Subtypes ST1 and ST3 are more likely to cause disease by producing an inflammatory Th1 response, while ST2 and ST4 are more likely to produce an anti-inflammatory Th2 response and asymptomatically colonize. By collecting and analyzing RT-PCR-derived subtypes and cytokine profiles, more information about how Blastocystis infections are caused by the immune system's response can be gathered. This information might be useful in developing better ways to identify and diagnose specific subtypes of Blastocystis that cause different kinds of infection.
revue: Science Forum (Journal of Pure and Applied Sciences)

titre: P003 | HISTOMORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES IN THE INTESTINAL WALL OF YOUNG AND OLD MICE: POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THE GUT-BRAIN AXIS
resume: The intestinal epithelial barrier represents the first line of defense between the internal and external environment. Its alteration can have various consequences, such as increased intestinal permeability, allowing the passage of potential pathogens into the circulation. In addition to the epithelial barrier, a gut-vascular barrier (GVB) has also been identified, consisting of the presence of a complex formed by vascular endothelium, pericytes and surrounding enteric glial cells (EGCs). The relationship between intestinal inflammation and brain changes, such as neurodegeneration is not yet fully understood but underpins the gut-brain axis. The study aimed to investigate changes in the intestinal wall, particularly the epithelial and vascular barriers, of young and old mice. Young (3-month-old) and aged (18-month-old) C57BL/6J mice were used. In all these samples, the following aspects were assessed: (i) intestinal barrier morphology through H&E, (ii) epithelial cell architecture via PAS and IHC, (iii) epithelial integrity using markers such as occludin, (iv) vascular barrier using endothelial cell (CD31), pericyte (desmin) and enteric glial cell markers (GFAP), and (v) macrophage presence (evaluated via IHC and IF for F4/80 and CD68), which plays an essential role in maintaining barrier integrity. The observed changes involved: (i) intestinal villi structure, (ii) the percentages of different intestinal cells, (iii) epithelial junctions, (iv) the number of endothelial, glial cells and intestinal pericytes, and (v) the presence of macrophages in the aged (inflamed) intestine compared to the young (control) intestine. Alterations found in intestinal barriers, both epithelial and vascular, can affect homeostasis, leading to the development of intestinal and extraintestinal diseases along the gut-brain axis.

titre: A pro-inflammatory gut microbiota-metabolic axis in global developmental delay identified by integrated multi-omics
resume: Global developmental delay (GDD) affects 1–3% of children, yet its etiology remains undetermined in 40–50% of cases despite comprehensive genetic testing. The role of the gut-brain axis in GDD is poorly defined, partly due to prior studies’ reliance on relative microbial abundance metrics. In this hypothesis-generating pilot cross-sectional study, we applied an integrated multi-omics framework combining absolute quantitative 16S rRNA gene sequencing with untargeted metabolomics to characterize the gut ecosystem in 16 young children with GDD (aged ≤3 years) and 20 age-matched healthy controls. Absolute quantification revealed significant enrichment of a pro-inflammatory consortium in the GDD gut microbiome, most notably the Ruminococcus gnavus group (2.15-fold increase, p < 0.05). Untargeted metabolomics identified Ethyl Diethanolamine as the top discriminant metabolite, markedly depleted in the GDD group (FC = 0.73, p < 0.0001). Pathway analysis pinpointed tryptophan metabolism as the most significantly perturbed pathway ( p < 0.001), characterized by a complex, multi-directional shift involving simultaneous upregulation of kynurenine, melatonin, and microbial indole metabolites. Multi-omics integration revealed strong overall microbiota-metabolome concordance alongside GDD-specific disruptions in fine-scale correlation networks. These pilot data suggest a pro-inflammatory gut microbiota–metabolite axis in GDD, potentially driven by expansion of R. gnavus and disruption of tryptophan metabolism. Ethyl Diethanolamine depletion emerges as a novel candidate biomarker, warranting future validation in larger cohorts.

titre: P022 | MODIFICATIONS OF NEUTROPHIL EXTRACELLULAR TRAPS IN THE GUT EPITHELIUM OF YOUNG AND AGED MICE: POSSIBLE RELATIONS WITH THE GUT-TO-BRAIN AXIS
resume: Neutrophils are the most abundant immune cells in mammals, constituting the first defense against pathogens. Recent studies have identified a crucial defense mechanism, known as neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). NETs are specialized extracellular structures formed by the extrusion of decondensed chromatin from activated neutrophils, composed of DNA with histones and a wide array of proteins, such as neutrophil elastase (NE). NETs play an essential role in aiding innate immunity by trapping, immobilizing, and neutralizing a wide variety of pathogens. It has been reported that in intestinal disorders there is an excessive release of NETs, probably correlated both to the immune response and to neutrophil clearance. The aim of our study was to evaluate the presence of NETs in the intestinal epithelium of young and aged mice. We evaluated the morphology of the intestinal wall and the position of neutrophils through hematoxylin & eosin (H&E) and May Grünwald - Giemsa stain. In addition, we studied the presence of DNA traps using SYTO-13 as selective fluorogenic DNA staining and the expression of Ly6G and NE as specific neutrophilic markers. Comparing intestinal morphology and neutrophil presence between young and aged mice, we found transepithelial migration of neutrophils and localization of NETs at the level of goblet cells in young mice, whereas no such presence in goblet was observed in aged mice. These cells are not only simple and fast producers of mucus, but they are also able to regulate the gastrointestinal (GI) barrier. In conclusion, we showed for the first time the possibility that goblet cells act as a vehicle for NETs from neutrophils to the intestinal lumen. Evidence indicates that, although the degree of NET involvement varies across neurodegenerative diseases, a possible and convergent pathogenic axis emerges linking progressive intestinal injury, sustained neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction. Overall, NETs have become a therapeutic target in critical diseases, making it important to explore their signaling pathways to guide possible interventions in intestinal disorders correlated with neurodegeneration along the gut-brain axis.

titre: Interprofessional Management of Anxiety in Claustrophobic Patients Undergoing Magnetic Resonance Imaging
resume: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is an essential diagnostic modality across a wide range of clinical settings. However, anxiety and claustrophobia remain common barriers to successful examination completion, potentially compromising image quality, patient experience, and healthcare service efficiency. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions implemented by the MRI team, with particular emphasis on the collaborative role of nurses and radiographers in the management of anxiety and claustrophobia among adult patients undergoing MRI. A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE between September and October 2025, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a research question developed according to the PICO framework. Studies published between 2008 and 2025 investigating MRI-related anxiety or claustrophobia and evaluating nursing, communicative, educational, or other non-pharmacological interventions were considered eligible. Of the 190 records initially identified, nine studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final narrative synthesis. The findings indicate that MRI-related anxiety is highly prevalent and may result in motion artefacts, premature examination termination, reduced patient cooperation, and an increased need for sedation. Interventions such as therapeutic communication, structured patient education, emotional support, breathing and relaxation techniques, music therapy, mindfulness, and immersive technologies demonstrated beneficial effects in reducing anxiety and improving examination tolerability. The available evidence suggests that a multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach can facilitate successful examination completion, improve diagnostic outcomes, and reduce the need for pharmacological interventions.

titre: Predicting the naturalistic course of obsessive-compulsive disorder during two-year follow-up in adolescence
resume: OBJECTIVE: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) during adolescence follows heterogeneous trajectories, from remission to persistence. Early identification of these patterns is crucial for optimizing clinical management. This study examined whether behavior symptoms or neuroimaging data could predict the persistence of OCD diagnosis at two-year follow-up. METHODS: 492 children between 9-10 years old with OCD were selected from Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study. They were classified as persisters or remitters by clinical status at two year follow-up. Baseline Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) item scores and multimodality MRI measures were used to examine behavioral and neuroimaging differences associated with follow-up OCD diagnostic status. We further applied machine learning models to predict individual symptom persistence using CBCL scores alone, MRI features alone from single modality or multimodal data, and combined CBCL and MRI features. RESULTS: Group-level CBCL and neuroimaging analyses identified significant behavioral, structural and functional brain differences at baseline between persisters and remitters. The best-performing CBCL model demonstrated limited discriminative ability (AUCbest = 0.638). In comparison, the best MRI-derived model, utilizing resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) features, performed slightly above chance (AUCbest = 0.577). Integrating rsfMRI features with CBCL improved performance only marginally and non-significantly (AUCbest = 0.665). Integrating rsfMRI features with CBCL did not significantly outperform the CBCL-only model, although the performance was numerically higher (AUCbest = 0.665). Feature-importance analyses suggested that the most clinically informative signals were compulsive behavior and functional connectivity linking large scale networks with widely distributed subcortical regions. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that OCD persistence follow-up OCD outcome is related to distinct clinical symptoms and brain measures. However, the accuracy to predict diagnosis is limited, indicating that OCD persistence naturalistic course is difficult to predict from clinical and neuroimaging data evaluated here.

titre: [Mediterranean diet in irritable bowel syndrome]
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is the most common functional gastrointestinal disorder; it is diagnosed according to the Rome IV criteria and is characterized by abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. The therapeutic approach to IBS is based on a multidisciplinary biopsychosocial model that includes nutritional interventions. The highest evidence-based dietary strategy is the low-FODMAP diet; however, due to its restrictive nature and negative impact on the gut microbiota, its long-term use is limited. Therefore, there is a need for a sustainable dietary approach for the long-term management of IBS. The Mediterranean diet (MedDiet), recommended by the Israeli Ministry of Health as part of a healthy lifestyle, emphasizes a high and varied intake of vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, olive oil, and fish, alongside the moderate consumption of poultry and dairy products, while reducing the intake of ultra-processed foods and saturated fats. In recent years, the potential role of MedDiet in IBS management has been explored. Epidemiological studies have demonstrated an inverse association between adherence to the Mediterranean pattern and gastrointestinal symptoms, while intervention studies have shown its feasibility and efficacy. Specifically, a 2024 randomized controlled trial found significantly greater symptom improvement in the MedDiet group compared to the control group (83% vs. 37%), and a 2025 study demonstrated superior outcomes for a low-FODMAP Mediterranean diet compared with the NICE guidelines. These findings suggest that the Mediterranean diet may serve as an effective, balanced, and sustainable long-term nutritional strategy for IBS management, tailored and monitored by a dietitian within a multidisciplinary framework.

titre: [Gastroenterology in Israel: quality, innovation, and prevention]
resume: This issue of Harefuah highlights the breadth of contemporary gastroenterology in Israel, spanning the Mediterranean diet in irritable bowel syndrome, gastrointestinal complications of diabetes, future therapies for celiac disease, and the central role of colonoscopy quality metrics and adequate bowel preparation. Alongside these reviews and position statements, the issue includes case reports that emphasize a broad differential diagnosis and complex therapeutic solutions, including Wernicke encephalopathy as a presenting feature of celiac disease, primary intestinal lymphangiectasia, and severe malnutrition after gastric bypass surgery. It also presents a position paper on surveillance of individuals at increased risk for pancreatic malignancy, defining risk groups, recommended workup and multidisciplinary follow-up, while underscoring the importance of reducing modifiable risk factors.

titre: Home subcutaneous hydration as an alternative to intravenous therapy in a patient with high output ileostomy: A case report
resume: High-output ileostomy represents a significant clinical challenge due to its association with dehydration, electrolyte imbalances, acute kidney injury, and frequent hospital readmissions, often requiring prolonged intravenous (IV) fluid therapy. We report the case of a 54-year-old woman with a terminal ileostomy following emergency intestinal resection, presenting persistent high stoma output (2200-2500 mL/day) and dependence on daily IV hydration despite optimized treatment. As early intestinal reconstruction was not feasible, a home-based subcutaneous hydration system (500-700 mL/day) was implemented, enabling hospital discharge and maintenance of adequate hydration. The patient developed one episode of local cellulitis, which resolved with oral antibiotics. During follow-up, progressive intestinal adaptation was observed, with reduced stoma output and improved diuresis. Body weight remained stable, and muscle mass and function improved. Home subcutaneous hydration appears to be a safe and effective alternative that enhances quality of life and reduces hospitalizations.

titre: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2
resume: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making. METHODS: Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds. RESULTS: Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout. CONCLUSIONS: These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

titre: Dupilumab for Moderate-to-Severe Chronic Prurigo Nodularis: A Retrospective Real-World Study of Effectiveness, Safety, and Prolonged Dosing Intervals
resume: INTRODUCTION: Chronic prurigo nodularis (CPN) is a multidimensional neuro-immunocutaneous disease characterized by severe, persistent pruritus, and the development of nodular lesions caused by repeated scratching, often associated with sleep disruption, psychological distress, and impaired quality of life. Dupilumab has demonstrated efficacy and safety in clinical trials, but evidence regarding the use of prolonged dosing intervals, and potential modifiers of response in real-world settings remains limited. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, observational study of adults with moderate-to-severe CPN treated with dupilumab in routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was clinically meaningful pruritus improvement at week 24, defined as a ≥ 4-point reduction in Worst Itch-Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS). Secondary outcomes included achievement of Investigator's Global Assessment for Prurigo Nodularis-Stage (IGA PN-S) 0/1 and longitudinal changes in pruritus, nodular lesion burden, sleep disturbance, and quality of life. Adverse events, treatment discontinuation, exploratory baseline predictors of response, and patterns of dosing-interval extension and return to the standard every-2-week regimen were also recorded. RESULTS: In total, 26 patients were included. Median age at dupilumab initiation was 45.5 years (interquartile range [IQR] 33-53 years), and median follow-up was 50 weeks (IQR 32-62 years). Baseline disease burden was substantial, with severe itch, marked quality-of-life impairment, sleep disturbance, elevated impulsivity scores, and psychiatric comorbidity in 19 patients (73%). At week 24, 59% of patients achieved a ≥ 4-point WI-NRS reduction, while 45% achieved IGA PN-S 0/1 and combined WI-NRS-IGA PN-S response. A sustained improvement in itch, clinical severity, and quality of life was observed among evaluable patients through later follow-up. Prolongation of the dupilumab dosing interval was attempted in nine controlled responders and maintained without return to the standard regimen in five patients. Psychiatric comorbidity was associated with lower odds of WI-NRS response at week 24. Adverse events occurred in two patients (7.7%) and led to treatment withdrawal in one owing to gastrointestinal disorder. CONCLUSIONS: Dupilumab showed real-world effectiveness and a favorable safety profile in moderate-to-severe CPN. These findings support individualized, multidisciplinary management and further prospective investigation of response predictors and dosing-interval prolongation strategies. Graphical Abstract available for this article. Chronic prurigo nodularis (CPN) is a long-lasting skin disease that causes very intense itching and hard itchy bumps. Scratching can keep the disease going, and many people also have sleep problems, emotional distress, and a major effect on daily life. Dupilumab is an injectable treatment that blocks two immune signals involved in inflammation and itch. Clinical trials have shown that dupilumab can help people with this disease, but less is known about how patients treated in everyday clinical practice will respond. In this study, we reviewed the medical records of 26 adults with moderate-to-severe CPN treated with dupilumab. After 24 weeks, 59% of patients who could be assessed had a meaningful reduction in worst itch, and in 45% the skin disease was clear or almost clear according to the doctor's assessment. Improvements in itch, skin signs, and quality of life generally continued during later follow-up. Overall, nine patients with good disease control were able to receive dupilumab less often; however, four needed to return to the standard every-2-week schedule. Side effects were uncommon and led to stopping treatment in one patient. Patients with mental health conditions seemed less likely to have a strong itch response, but this finding needs confirmation. These results support care that is tailored to each person, including mental health support when needed.

titre: T​he use of biosynthetic mesh in complex abdominal wall reconstruction - a single‑center experience
resume: PURPOSE: Abdominal wall reconstruction in patients presenting with enteric fistulas and mesh infection is challenging. Synthetic mesh should be avoided in contaminated fields and to be used in selected cases. Alternative strategies include primary fascial closure with or without component separation, biologic mesh, and resorbable biosynthetic mesh. Our study aims to evaluate the use of long-term absorbable mesh in a single-stage procedure, focusing on postoperative complications and hernia recurrence rates. METHODS: A retrospective single-arm study was conducted following Institutional Review Board approval. All incisional hernia repairs using bio-absorbable Poly-4-Hydroxybutyrate mesh were performed at our medical center between January 2017 and March 2025 were included. Adult and pediatric patients with Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG) grade III and IV wounds were eligible. RESULTS: Thirty-four patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 58.7 ± 17.1 years, and the mean body mass index was 30.4 ± 7.6 kg/m². Comorbidity burden was high: 52.9% had a Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and 35.3% had an ASA score ≥ 3. Most patients (82.3%) presented with infected mesh. Mean operative time was 188.5 ± 75 min, and bowel resection was required in 18 cases. Postoperative wound infection occurred in 10 patients. Follow‑up data were available for 28 of the 34 patients with median follow-up duration of 20.5 months. A single death occurred, hernia recurrence was observed in four cases (16%), all managed with reoperation. Quality-of-life assessments demonstrated a clear postoperative improvement. CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk, contaminated and infected cohort, P4HB mesh demonstrated acceptable recurrence and complication rates. Its long-term resorbable properties provides a feasible alternative to use in incisional hernia repair with infected meshes.

titre: Beyond Abdominal Versus Perineal Repair: Contemporary Decision-Making in Rectal Prolapse
resume: Rectal prolapse is increasing in prevalence as the population ages. It can cause a wide variety of symptoms, including fecal incontinence severely impacting a patient's quality of life. Given that hemorrhoidal disease is often misdiagnosed as rectal prolapse, it is important for surgeons to be familiar with key symptoms, appropriate physical exam, and work-up. With improvements in anesthesia care and minimally invasive surgery, the options for a more durable repair have expanded for patients who are older with multiple medical comorbidities. This article aims to review the diagnosis, work-up, and evolution of surgical management of rectal prolapse. This will aid surgeons in making the correct diagnosis and assisting their patient's informed decision making regarding surgical repair.

titre: Explainable multi-group dynamic causal distribution learning framework to disentangle common and specific dynamic effective connectivity across MCI stages
resume: Brain functional networks exhibit an intrinsic architecture that is preserved across brain disorder groups, upon which different groups display distinct patterns of abnormal interactions. Exploring the common and specific network patterns is crucial for revealing common pathological mechanisms, group-specific alterations, and disease progression. Dynamic effective connectivity (dEC) characterizes time-varying causal interactions among brain regions and provides an effective means of investigating common and specific network patterns. However, the disentangled learning of common and specific dEC across multiple groups remains underexplored, limiting a systematic understanding of dynamic causal mechanisms in brain networks across disorders and disease stages. We propose an explainable multi-group dynamic causal distribution learning framework that integrates spatial and temporal information to identify common and specific dEC distributions among different groups. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively and robustly identifies causality and disentangles common and specific causal structures. When applied to real-world data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, the proposed framework uncovers common and specific dEC across mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stages. Results show that, as MCI worsens, the dEC within the visual network and among functional hubs of the default mode network remain stable, whereas dEC associated with episodic memory, emotional processing, and interoception shift from compensatory to decompensatory patterns. The code is available at https://github.com/OrangeLY-byte/EMGDCD.

titre: Efficacy of acceptance and commitment therapy on anxiety, depression, fatigue, stress, and quality of life in cancer patients: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) on anxiety, depression, quality of life (QoL), fatigue, and stress in adult cancer patients. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to September 22, 2025, identified 22 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, mostly randomized controlled trials. Independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Random effects meta-analyses were conducted with Knapp-Hartung adjustments for outcomes with few studies. Heterogeneity, subgroup, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed, and publication bias was assessed. ACT significantly reduced anxiety, depression, fatigue, and stress while improving QoL. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were consistent, but heterogeneity, particularly in QoL, warrants caution. Despite significant heterogeneity in QoL and possible publication bias, ACT showed a consistent benefit across outcomes. However, the magnitude of pooled effects should be interpreted with caution.

titre: Psychosocial Profiles of Homebound Adults with Cancer and Poor Symptom Control: A Cluster Analysis of Meaning, Distress, and Desire for Hastened Death
resume: CONTEXT: Homebound cancer patients with poor symptom control often experience significant existential and affective distress, reducing quality of life exponentially. However, it is unclear whether these patients experience these types of distress uniformly. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify naturally occurring subgroups of patients via patterns of meaning in life, anxiety, depression, and desire for hastened death (DHD). Furthermore, this study aimed to identify the strength of subgroup discrepancies as well as explore the differences in physical symptoms and quality of life between subgroups. METHODS: Sixty-four patients from a pilot randomized controlled trial of Meaning-Centered Psychotherapy for Hospitals, Hospice, and Home (MCP-H) completed baseline assessments. A hierarchical agglomerative cluster analysis was used to identify naturally occurring subgroups and follow-up t-tests were utilized to identify differences across measures of quality of life. RESULTS: Two subgroups emerged from the cluster analysis: Low Meaning, High Distress and DHD (n = 29) and High Meaning, Low Distress and DHD (n = 35). In addition to substantial differences on all cluster-defining variables (i.e., meaning in life, anxiety, depression, and DHD), subgroups also differed significantly on quality of life (t(60) = -7.53, p < 0.001) and on endorsements of distressing physical symptoms. CONCLUSION: Using existential and affective distress proxies to guide cluster analysis was effective in describing two subgroups of homebound patients with cancer and poor symptom control. Results suggest that individuals with low meaning and high distress may experience more cumulative and diverse types of suffering/distress (e.g., physical symptoms, DHD). Findings can be utilized to guide assessment and intervention with oncology patients in the home health care setting.
revue: Journal of pain and symptom management

titre: A large-group one-day RCT investigating the effectiveness of four different strategies to promote the outcome of exposure therapy in 519 patients with phobic fear of flying: Three-year follow-up results
resume: INTRODUCTION: This study reports the 3-year follow-up of a recently published randomized controlled trial evaluating a standardized large-group one-session exposure intervention for fear of flying (FoF). In the original trial, participants were randomized to four psychological strategies aimed at facilitating exposure outcomes, i.e., promoting peer support (SUPPORT), self-efficacy (SELF-EFFIC), expectancy violation (EXPECT), or coping with bodily fear symptoms (COPE). METHODS: Three years after treatment, 308 treatment completers (64 % of all treatment completers) participated in the follow-up assessment including the same validated self-report measures of FoF, danger expectancy and anxiety expectancy as in the original trial. Moreover, behavioral outcomes (i.e., flights taken since treatment) were assessed. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVAs. RESULTS: Dropout analyses revealed no evidence of differential attrition between treatment conditions. Repeated measures ANOVAs of all fear-related measures showed highly significant effects of time (all p's < .001) indicating substantial and sustained improvement from baseline to 3-year follow-up. Neither significant main effects of treatment condition nor time × condition interactions were found for any outcome, irrespective of whether rmANOVAs or linear mixed models (LMMs) were used, with LMMs serving as a sensitivity analysis, indicating comparable long-term outcomes across all four exposure enhancement strategies. CONCLUSION: The standardized large-group one-session exposure intervention for fear of flying demonstrated robust and durable treatment effects over three years, irrespective of which exposure enhancement strategy was used. The findings suggest that the intervention was highly effective across different mechanistic approaches, with no evidence of differential long-term clinical outcomes.

titre: Bridge of imbalance: How does the brain-gut axis act as a catalyst for gastrointestinal tumors in aging
resume: Aging is a complex biological process regulated by multiple factors. Its characteristics include shortening of telomere length, DNA damage, abnormal secretion of cytokines, and cellular oxidative damage. These changes eventually lead to the formation of tumor cells and the remodeling of the intestinal microenvironment. The brain-gut axis is a complex bidirectional communication network connecting the intestine and the central nervous system, composed of the nervous system, immune system, microbiota and their metabolites. It allows for information exchange between the intestine and the brain, influencing the function of the digestive system and brain activity. The remodeling of the brain-gut axis function caused by aging is an important catalyst promoting the development of gastrointestinal tumors. In aging, the dysbiosis of the intestinal microbiota, abnormal release of neurotransmitters, and neuroendocrine disorders will directly affect tumor occurrence through the brain-gut axis. In addition, aging can put the gastrointestinal tract in an inflammaging state, causing dysregulation of cancer immune. At the same time, the disruption of the circadian rhythm can affect the homeostasis of the gastrointestinal tract and promote tumor development. This review will specifically explore the factors that induce gastrointestinal tumors in aging through the components of the brain-gut axis and propose new therapeutic perspectives targeting the intestinal microbiota, neurotransmitters, immune conditions, and clock rhythm.

titre: Interventions for Anxiety Following Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review
resume: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate interventions targeting anxiety symptoms in people with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI), identify gaps in knowledge, and propose avenues for research. METHODS: In this systematic review, a research librarian searched for articles published from 1994 to September 6, 2024, in MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Two independent reviewers selected studies based on the following inclusion criteria: adults with traumatic spinal cord injury; interventions including pharmacological, behavioral, and complementary and alternative medicine; presence of a comparator group; and a primary outcome of anxiety symptom reduction. Reviewers independently assigned a quality score using Hawker's guidelines and evaluated the risk of bias using Cochrane's risk-of-bias tools. Coauthors reconciled disagreements via unanimous consensus. RESULTS: Thirteen of the 7927 articles met inclusion criteria representing 12 studies. Investigators evaluated individual and group behavioral interventions including an online mindfulness course and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy. Six of the studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 3 were non-RCTs, 1 was quasi-experimental, and 2 were matched-control trials. Five studies reported a significant reduction in anxiety symptoms for the intervention versus control groups. Effective interventions included group coping effectiveness training, hyperbaric oxygen therapy combined with traditional Chinese medicine and psychotherapy, and supplemental physical rehabilitation techniques such as home automation training and vibration therapy. CONCLUSION: Clinicians may consider several interventions that show preliminary evidence of benefit in reducing symptoms of anxiety. Larger trials should compare effectiveness of available interventions and evaluate optimal delivery of interventions in practice.
revue: Topics in spinal cord injury rehabilitation

titre: Aortomesenteric Geometry and Abdominal Computed Tomography Findings in a Regional Cohort of Patients with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome: A Retrospective Hypothesis-Generating Clinical Imaging Study
resume: Background/Objectives: Gastrointestinal symptoms are common in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), but the potential contribution of abdominal anatomy and connective-tissue-related structural factors remains incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize abdominal computed tomography (CT) anatomy in patients with EDS, with particular focus on aortomesenteric geometry and its relationship with body habitus and abdominal anteroposterior (AP) depth. Exploratory analyses assessed associations with constipation and Irritable bowel syndrome/disorders of gut–brain interaction (IBS/DGBI). Methods: In this retrospective clinical imaging study, 113 patients with EDS and available abdominal CT were identified from regional administrative records. Superior mesenteric artery (SMA) angle, aortomesenteric distance, linea alba–aorta distance as a measure of internal abdominal AP depth, and subcutaneous fat thickness were assessed. Clinical characteristics and secondary abdominal CT findings were obtained from medical records and image review. Correlation, hierarchical regression, interaction, and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed. Results: Median age was 43 [34–58] years, and 105/113 (92.9%) patients were female. Median SMA angle was 41° [31–58°], and median aortomesenteric distance was 12 [9–19] mm. SMA angle and aortomesenteric distance were strongly associated (Spearman ρ = 0.840, p < 0.001). In complete-case hierarchical regression (n = 110), ln(SMA angle) explained 55.5% of the variance in aortomesenteric distance. Addition of body mass index (BMI) increased R2 to 0.659 (ΔR2 = 0.103, p < 0.001), while subsequent addition of linea alba–aorta distance further increased R2 to 0.726 (ΔR2 = 0.068, p < 0.001). Subcutaneous fat thickness provided no further improvement. A formal interaction between ln(SMA angle) and linea alba–aorta distance was not statistically significant (p = 0.165). Exploratory analyses did not identify significant differences in the principal quantitative CT measurements according to IBS/DGBI or constipation status. Conclusions: Within this EDS cohort, aortomesenteric distance was strongly related to SMA angle. BMI contributed additional explanatory information, while linea alba–aorta distance provided further information after accounting for BMI. No significant association between the principal quantitative CT measurements and IBS/DGBI or constipation was demonstrated. These findings describe anatomical relationships within the present cohort and should not be interpreted as EDS-specific in the absence of a comparison group.

titre: O split payment na reforma tributária brasileira: os limites da arrecadação automatizada diante da capacidade contributiva, da livre iniciativa e da neutralidade tributária
resume: The Brazilian tax reform, introduced by Constitutional Amendment No. 132/2023 and regulated, among other provisions, by Complementary Laws No. 214/2025 and No. 227/2026, has brought substantial changes to consumption taxation, particularly through the establishment of the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS), the Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS), and a tax collection mechanism operating at the financial settlement of transactions, known as split payment. This article aims to critically examine the constitutional compatibility of this mechanism with the principles of ability to pay, freedom of enterprise, proportionality, and tax neutrality, particularly in light of its potential effects on corporate cash flow and working capital. The research adopts a qualitative approach based on the legal-dogmatic method, using bibliographic and documentary research, as well as a comparative analysis of international experiences. It examines the legal framework of automated tax collection, its relationship with the non-cumulative taxation system, and the risks associated with accelerated collection, excessive withholding, and delays in making financial resources available to taxpayers. The study concludes that split payment is not inherently incompatible with the Brazilian Constitution, provided that its implementation is proportionate, transparent, and supported by effective safeguards for correcting errors, ensuring timely refunds, and preserving economic activity.
