titre: Decoding the microbiota–gut–brain axis in Parkinson’s disease: from microbial dysbiosis to systems-level regulation and acupuncture-based modulation
resume: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a multisystem disorder involving dysfunction of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA), encompassing gut microbial dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolism, intestinal barrier impairment, immune dysregulation, autonomic dysfunction, and α-synuclein pathology. Sequencing studies identify PD-associated differences in microbial functional potential, whereas chemical measurements reveal changes in fecal SCFAs, bile acids in plasma or intestinal tissue, and tryptophan-derived metabolites in plasma or cerebrospinal fluid. These changes interact with intestinal barrier dysfunction, TLR4/NF-κB and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling, microglial activation, and neural pathways including the enteric and vagal systems, forming interconnected microbiota–metabolic–immune–neural feedback networks. We propose a systems framework in which pathological attractors, network collapse, and system reset denote testable hypotheses about persistent MGBA configurations, impaired functional recovery, and sustained changes in responses after intervention, respectively. Their evaluation requires longitudinal measurements, controlled perturbations, and comparison with alternative explanations; these concepts are not presented as established mechanisms of PD. Within this framework, acupuncture is considered a candidate intervention affecting several MGBA-related processes. Studies in PD models report concurrent changes in microbial composition, intestinal barrier markers, inflammatory signaling, and neurological outcomes, while microbiota-depletion and transplantation experiments provide initial support for a microbial contribution to selected treatment effects. However, these findings do not establish a complete acupuncture–MGBA–PD causal pathway. Human evidence remains preliminary and concerns symptomatic outcomes rather than demonstrated neuroprotection or disease modification. Restoration of MGBA homeostasis is therefore a hypothesis to be evaluated through prespecified measures of sustained physiological function and recovery after perturbation. We therefore propose a causal and state-oriented framework integrating longitudinal multi-omics, mechanistic perturbation, interpretable artificial intelligence, and biologically informed patient stratification. This framework may facilitate the transition from descriptive MGBA associations toward testable causal models and ultimately support the development of state-informed precision acupuncture strategies for PD.

titre: Development of Type 2 Diabetes During Aging Shifts the Brain Metabolome and Gut Microbiome in a Sex-Dependent Manner
resume: Background/Objectives: The development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia. Both T2DM and aging are associated with alterations in brain metabolism and gut microbiome composition. However, the effects of age-related metabolic dysfunction during the development of T2DM on the brain metabolome and gut–brain axis (GBA), particularly with respect to sex-specific differences, remain poorly understood. Our objective was to elucidate the metabolic and GBA-driven mechanisms by which the development of T2DM, during aging, may contribute to cognitive impairment and dementia. Methods: We performed untargeted metabolomics on brain tissue, profiled the gut microbiome, assessed behavior by the open field test, and assessed cognitive function by the Y-maze in male and female nine-month-old db/db and age-matched wild-type (WT) mice. Results: Compared to WT mice, db/db mice exhibited increased brain fatty acids, altered glycerophospholipid metabolism, and elevated corticosterone; changes in gut microbiome composition; reduced locomotion; and altered behavior in the open field. Additionally, sex-specific increases in N-lactoyl-amino acids and reduced abundance of Turicibacter sp. LA61 and unclassified Anaerotruncus were observed in female db/db mice, whereas male db/db mice uniquely exhibited increased deoxycholic acid and decreased abundance of Kineothrix alysoides and Alistipes massiliensis. Additionally, only male db/db mice exhibited cognitive dysfunction as measured by the Y-maze. Conclusions: The development of T2DM during aging is associated with sex-specific changes in the brain metabolome, gut microbiome, and cognitive function, providing new insight into the potential contribution of the GBA to metabolic-disturbance-associated cognitive dysfunction.

titre: The self-compassion-informed cognitive behavioral psychoeducation program: its effects on social anxiety, cognitive distortions, and self-compassion
resume: This study aimed to examine the effects of a self-compassion-informed cognitive-behavioral psychoeducation program on social anxiety, cognitive distortions, and self-compassion among individuals exhibiting elevated social anxiety symptoms. A quasi-experimental design was employed. Data were collected using the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale, the Cognitive Distortions Scale, and the Self-Compassion Scale. Initially, 325 individuals were screened, and 45 participants who scored 48 or above on the LSAS anxiety subscale and met the eligibility criteria were invited to participate. Participants were allocated to an experimental group, a communication-focused active control group, or a waitlist group based on study eligibility and availability for participation. The experimental group received a nine-session self-compassion-informed cognitive-behavioral psychoeducation program, the communication-focused active control group received communication-focused psychoeducation, and the waitlist group received no intervention. Assessments were conducted at pre-test, post-test, one-month follow-up, and two-month follow-up. Significant Group × Measurement interactions were observed from pre-test to post-test for social anxiety, cognitive distortions, and self-compassion, indicating that changes over time differed across the three groups. The experimental group showed a significant reduction in social anxiety and cognitive distortions and a significant increase in self-compassion from pre-test to post-test. The communication-focused active control group showed a descriptive reduction in social anxiety scores, but this change did not reach statistical significance. In the follow-up analyses, Group × Measurement interactions were not statistically significant for social anxiety, cognitive distortions, or self-compassion, indicating that the groups did not show statistically different patterns of change from post-test through the one- and two-month follow-up assessments. The findings provide preliminary evidence that a self-compassion-informed cognitive-behavioral psychoeducation program may be associated with improvements in social anxiety, cognitive distortions, and self-compassion among undergraduate students exhibiting elevated social anxiety symptoms. However, the quasi-experimental design, small sample, and limited follow-up period warrant cautious interpretation. Randomized controlled studies with larger and more diverse samples and longer follow-up periods are needed to further evaluate the effectiveness and longer-term effects of the intervention.

titre: Data for: Effects of the isolated self-as-context component of acceptance and commitment therapy on anxiety in adult women: A randomized controlled trial
resume: This dataset contains the de-identified participant-level data from a two-arm randomized controlled trial of the isolated self-as-context component of acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) for anxiety in adult women. Participants were 676 Russian-speaking women aged 20–60 with self-reported, long-standing anxiety. They were randomized to a seven-day facilitator-led online program that delivered the self-as-context component of ACT in isolation (n = 338) or to a one-week wait list (n = 338). The intervention group was assessed before the program, immediately after it, and four weeks later, with all program materials and contact withdrawn during the follow-up month. The wait-list group was assessed at the first two points and then received the program. All 676 participants completed the post-test, and 325 of the 338 intervention participants completed the follow-up. Data were collected online in 2025. Measures: GAD-7; Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI); State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, state and trait scales (Spielberger–Khanin adaptation); Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II (AAQ-II); and the Level of Social Frustration scale (a 20-item Russian measure of satisfaction with life domains), which was collected but not analyzed in the related publication. The files contain a random participant code, group assignment, item-level responses and scale totals for each assessment, and coarsened screening variables. They contain no names, contact details or dates. Variable definitions, scoring rules (including reverse-keyed items) and missing-data codes are given in the accompanying codebook (README). All participants gave informed consent to participation and to the use of their de-identified data.The trial was conducted as the author’s doctoral dissertation research.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Enhanced management of home-based elders with depression (EMBED): protocol for a cluster randomised controlled trial
resume: Depression is common among older adults receiving in-home aged care, but access to evidence-based psychological treatment is limited. Enhanced Management of home-Based Elders with Depression (EMBED) is a brief, manualised, telehealth-delivered psychological intervention designed for this population. This trial aims to evaluate whether EMBED plus usual care is superior to usual care alone in reducing depressive symptoms. This pragmatic, assessor-blinded, cluster-randomised, parallel-group superiority trial will be conducted across 22 in-home aged care service areas in Western Australia and South Australia. Service areas are allocated 1:1 to EMBED plus usual care or usual care alone prior to an initial baseline usual care period for all areas. Eligible participants are aged 65 years or older, receive eligible in-home aged care services, have current depressive symptoms and are able to participate by telephone or video call. EMBED combines psychoeducation, lifestyle therapy and behavioural activation and is delivered remotely by mental health clinicians over 10 weeks. Treatment components and intensity are stratified according to baseline depressive symptom severity. For the primary endpoint, 660 participants are required to detect a standardised between-group effect size of 0.4 in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 change from baseline to 12 weeks. A recruitment target of 880 allows for 25% attrition. Secondary outcomes include changes in depression severity at 24 weeks and in the following outcomes at 12 and 24 weeks: anxiety, quality of life, self-rated health, loneliness, social interaction, perceived social support, depression stigma, and adverse events. Cost-effectiveness and implementation will also be evaluated. Explanatory variables include attitudes to ageing, apathy, and engagement in meaningful activity. Analyses will follow intention-to-treat principles using mixed-effects models that account for clustering and repeated measurements. This trial will provide evidence on the effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation of a low-intensity psychological intervention embedded within routine in-home aged care. If effective, EMBED could provide a scalable approach to improving access to mental health support for older adults receiving aged care at home. Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN 12623001345673. Registered prospectively 20 December 2023. First enrolment 11 January 2024.

titre: Effectiveness of a combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention for chronic migraine: A randomized controlled trial
resume: Background: Mindfulness has been proposed as a non-pharmacological strategy for chronic migraine management. Objective: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention in adults with chronic migraine. Methods: A randomized controlled trial was conducted in adults with chronic migraine. Forty participants were randomized, and 38 were included in the final analyses. The intervention group was assigned to a 12-week combined intervention consisting of paced breathing followed by a mobile app–based mindfulness intervention delivered through the Petit BamBou® app; the control group remained on a waitlist and continued usual care. The primary outcome was migraine days per month. Secondary outcomes included migraine episode pain intensity and duration, headache-related quality of life (Headache Impact Test-6), anxiety sensitivity (Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3), kinesiophobia (Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-11), and sleep quality (Athens Insomnia Scale). Between-group differences at post-intervention were evaluated using analysis of covariance, adjusting each outcome for its corresponding baseline value. Results: No statistically significant baseline-adjusted between-group differences were observed for migraine frequency or for any secondary outcome. For the primary outcome, the adjusted mean difference between the control and intervention groups was −3.07 migraine days per month (95% CI, −8.00 to 1.86; F(1, 35) = 1.599; p = 0.214; ηp2 = 0.044). Effect sizes were small for all outcomes. Conclusion: A 12-week combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention was not superior to waitlist usual care for reducing migraine frequency or improving the evaluated clinical and psychological outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, the marked baseline imbalance in migraine frequency, the use of a waitlist control group, and the absence of objective adherence monitoring. Future trials should include larger samples, active control conditions, objective measures of engagement, and longer follow-up periods. (Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN12624000611527 [prospectively registered on May 10, 2024]).

titre: Metabolic Syndrome and Health Outcomes Many Years After Education in a Low FODMAP Diet in Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study
resume: BACKGROUND: FODMAPs may alter the gut microbiota. We aimed to explore potential long-term health consequences of education in FODMAP restriction, with respect to metabolic syndrome risk and development of significant medical comorbidities. METHODS: Patients with IBS educated on a low FODMAP diet by a gastrointestinal dietitian were seen at a face-to-face interview mean 7.1 years later. Blood was collected along with dietary intake (Complete Nutritional Assessment Questionnaire) and physical assessment. Presence of metabolic syndrome and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) were calculated and compared across tertiles of the last 12 months of FODMAP intake. KEY RESULTS: Of 74 participants (84% women, median age 59 [IQR 47-67] years), 57% lived with overweight or obesity. Few reported medical comorbidities, but 39% (29/73) met the diagnostic criteria for metabolic syndrome. Central abdominal obesity was the most common risk factor for metabolic syndrome, followed by hypertension. Over the previous 12 months, 24 (40%) had metabolic syndrome, with no difference across tertiles of FODMAP intake (p = 0.67). In those with the highest FODMAP intake, 40% had a medical history of hypertension compared with 5% in the lowest tertile (p = 0.03). Other metabolic metrics did not differ across groups. There was no change in the CCI score from pre FODMAP diet to the time of study participation. Age-adjusted CCI scores were similar across tertiles (p = 0.38). CONCLUSIONS AND INFERENCES: Neither education in the FODMAP diet nor measured intake over 12 months prior to assessment were associated with significant health consequences with respect to metabolic syndrome or development of other medical comorbidities in this population.
revue: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology

titre: CONTRACTORS’ PERCEPTION IN INTEGRATING CIRCULAR ECONOMY IN INDUSTRIALISED BUILDING SYSTEM (IBS)
resume: Industrialised Building System (IBS) is well-recognised in improving sustainable deliverables for construction projects. However, the lack of integration of a circular economy (CE) in IBS construction hinders the continual use of resources and limiting waste elimination. This study investigated the IBS contractors’ perceptions of integrating CE in managing construction and demolition (C&D) waste. The STEEP (Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental and Political) matrix adopted in this study determined the drivers, enablers, challenges, and barriers to integrating CE into the IBS application. Twenty respondents from IBS construction companies participated in semi-structured interviews to provide insights into integrating CE in C&D waste management. The results highlighted that IBS contractors in Malaysia strongly associated CE with waste separation activities, reduction of waste generation, recycling and re-use materials of building components to extend its value. Although CE harbours greater potential in terms of the level of circularity (refuse, rethink, reduce, reuse, repair, refurbish, remanufacture, re-purpose, recycle and recover), the limited knowledge of CE among IBS contractors has hindered the optimisation of IBS from contributing to sustainability. Building on the STEEP matrix, the outcomes of the study initiate further study to determine strategies to improve efficient integration of CE in managing C&D waste for IBS projects.

titre: Mengoptimumkan Strategi Pemasaran Digital untuk Mempromosikan Teknologi IBS dalam Industri Pembinaan di Selangor
resume: Tahap penggunaan IBS dalam kalangan kontraktor di Malaysia, khususnya kontraktor kecil dan sederhana, masih berada pada tahap sederhana, sekali gus mencerminkan kekangan dalam pendekatan promosi sedia ada. Seiring dengan peningkatan pengaruh pemasaran digital terhadap proses pembuatan keputusan dalam industri pembinaan, kajian ini bertujuan untuk mengoptimumkan strategi pemasaran digital bagi meningkatkan penerimaan teknologi IBS oleh kontraktor di Selangor. Secara khusus, kajian ini mengenal pasti cabaran penggunaan teknologi IBS, menganalisis faktor-faktor yang mengehadkan keberkesanan pemasaran digital dalam mempengaruhi penggunaan IBS, serta meneliti impak pemasaran digital terhadap prestasi jualan IBS dalam industri pembinaan Malaysia. Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan melalui pengedaran soal selidik berstruktur kepada kontraktor pembinaan yang beroperasi di Selangor. Data daripada 170 responden telah dianalisis menggunakan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) melalui kaedah statistik deskriptif. Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa kontraktor mempunyai tahap penerimaan IBS yang berbeza-beza dan dipengaruhi oleh keberkesanan strategi pemasaran digital. Sebanyak 56.5% responden bersetuju bahawa proses pemasangan IBS memerlukan kursus latihan khusus yang sukar diakses, yang dikenal pasti sebagai cabaran utama kepada penerimaan IBS. Selain itu, usaha pemasaran digital IBS didapati kurang menekankan aspek penjimatan kos dan masa pembinaan, sekali gus mengehadkan daya tarikan teknologi IBS terhadap kontraktor. Kesimpulannya, kajian ini memberikan bukti empirikal yang kukuh bahawa pemasaran digital yang dirancang secara sistematik dan berkesan adalah penting untuk meningkatkan penerimaan serta prestasi jualan teknologi IBS, sejajar dengan matlamat pembangunan industri pembinaan yang lebih cekap dan moden di Malaysia.
revue: Research in Management of Technology and Business

titre: Compensating Transfer Pricing Adjustments and the Market-Value Standard in VAT: What Brazil’s IBS/CBS Reform Can Learn from International Experience
resume: Complementary Law 214/2025 introduces, for the first time in Brazilian consumption taxation, a market-value requirement for related-party transactions under Brazil’s new dual VAT, the IBS and CBS, alongside a broader question already debated under Brazil’s former indirect taxes: whether transfer pricing adjustments can themselves trigger a taxable event. Drawing on the European Unions’s case law, India’s and Australia’s models, and the Brazilian precedent on transfer pricing true-ups, the author develops recommendations for Brazil.

titre: PSYCHOEMOTIONAL STRESS AND GASTROINTESTINAL SYMPTOMS IN CHILDREN: PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL LINKS, CLINICAL ASSESSMENT, AND PREVENTIVE APPROACHES
resume: Background. Psychoemotional stress may influence the perception and regulation of gastrointestinal symptoms in children through bidirectional gut–brain interactions. Objective. To synthesize evidence on the relationships between stress, functional gastrointestinal symptoms, sleep, and dietary behavior in school-aged children and adolescents, and to outline a clinically appropriate assessment framework. Materials and Methods. A narrative review and structured conceptual analysis were conducted based on the Rome IV pediatric criteria, and selected peer-reviewed publications. No primary patient data were analyzed. Results. Evidence suggests that stress may exacerbate functional dyspepsia, functional abdominal pain, irritable bowel syndrome, and functional constipation through changes in visceral sensitivity, autonomic and neuroendocrine signaling, behavior, and attention to symptoms. Sleep disturbances, irregular meals, family circumstances, and school-related pressures may act as interacting modifiers rather than independent explanations for all symptoms. Rome IV provides a symptom-based diagnostic framework following appropriate clinical evaluation, while alarm features warrant further investigation. Conclusion. A biopsychosocial and age-sensitive approach to gastrointestinal assessment is justified; however, causality and intervention effectiveness cannot be inferred from this narrative synthesis. Prospective pediatric studies using validated stress assessment instruments and standardized outcomes are needed. RU Актуальность. Психоэмоциональный стресс может влиять на выраженность и регуляцию желудочно-кишечных симптомов у детей посредством двунаправленного взаимодействия между кишечником и головным мозгом. Цель — обобщить данные о взаимосвязях стресса, функциональных гастроинтестинальных симптомов, сна и пищевого поведения у детей школьного возраста и подростков, а также предложить подход к клинической оценке. Материалы и методы. Проведены нарративный обзор литературы и структурированный концептуальный анализ педиатрических критериев Rome IV и отобранных рецензируемых научных публикаций. Собственные клинические данные пациентов не анализировались. Результаты. Данные литературы свидетельствуют о том, что стресс может усиливать проявления функциональной диспепсии, функциональной абдоминальной боли, синдрома раздражённого кишечника и функционального запора посредством изменений висцеральной чувствительности, вегетативной и нейроэндокринной регуляции, поведения и внимания к симптомам. Нарушения сна, нерегулярное питание, семейные обстоятельства и школьные нагрузки могут выступать взаимосвязанными модифицирующими факторами, но не объясняют все случаи возникновения симптомов. Критерии Rome IV обеспечивают симптом-ориентированную основу клинической диагностики после надлежащего обследования, тогда как наличие тревожных признаков требует дополнительного исследования. titre: Patterns of daily-life walking in older adults – the HUNT4 Trondheim 70+ observational study
resume: Background Walking ability is crucial for independence, disease prevention, and healthy aging in older adults. Daily-life walking behavior is dominated by short walking bouts (WBs), yet little is known about how these are organized. This study aimed to describe patterns of daily-life walking in older adults in relation to sex and level of physical function, taking into account short interruptions between WBs in close temporal proximity. Methods Accelerometer data (Axivity AX3) from 1266 older adults (mean age 77.4, SD 6.1 years; age range 70–105 years; 54.6% women) were used to identify WBs and inter-bouts (IBs) of daily-life walking. WBs separated by IBs lasting < 60 s were clustered together, and older adults’ walking behavior was described across levels of physical function as assessed by the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) (Kruskal-Wallis tests) for both women and men (Mann-Whitney U). In addition, Spearman correlations between walking metrics and SPPB score were performed and compared using Steiger’s test for dependent correlations. Results The majority of IBs lasted < 60 s, indicating that most interruptions in walking activities are very brief. Temporal clustering of WBs showed that those with lower SPPB-scores had fewer clusters and shorter walking period duration compared to those with higher SPPB-scores (all p​ < 0.05). Median duration, inter-quartile range, and 95th percentile were more strongly correlated to SPPB scores when WBs were clustered than before clustering (all p​ < 0.001). Conclusions Our results show that most time periods between WBs are very short, indicating brief interruptions rather than actual termination of walking activity. In addition, clustering WBs into walking periods yields measures that are more closely related to physical function than individual WBs alone. Clustering WBs occurring close in time provides additional insights into patterns of daily-life walking in both women and men and represents a relevant extension of existing clinical and patient-reported measures. Further research is warranted to investigate how walking clusters may support early identification of functional decline or disease progression. Trial registration Not applicable.
revue: European Review of Aging and Physical Activity

titre: Zona Franca de Manaus e a Reforma Tributária: a nova competitividade, os incentivos e as decisões empresariais
resume: Livro publicado em e-book Kindle na Amazon. Este registro traz uma amostra (folha de rosto, ficha técnica, sumário, introdução e "Como ler este livro"); o livro completo está disponível apenas na Amazon. A reforma tributária acaba com a Zona Franca de Manaus? A resposta curta é não. A Constituição manteve a Zona Franca até 2073 e mandou que os novos tributos preservassem o seu diferencial competitivo. Mas os incentivos que durante décadas foram desenhados em torno do IPI, do ICMS, do PIS e da Cofins passam a ser desenhados em torno do IBS e da CBS: tributos cobrados por fora do preço, com crédito amplo e uma transição que vai de 2026 a 2033. A vantagem de produzir e vender a partir de Manaus continua, mas chega à empresa por outros caminhos, em outros momentos e com outro valor. O livro começa pela pergunta de fundo, o que é vantagem competitiva e por que incentivo fiscal não é a mesma coisa, e percorre as escolas da competitividade, da economia à estratégia empresarial: Porter e o cluster, a visão baseada em recursos, as capacidades dinâmicas, as cadeias globais de valor, Fajnzylber e a competitividade sistêmica. Em seguida lê a Lei Complementar nº 214/2025, o decreto da CBS, o regulamento do IBS e as normas da Suframa dispositivo por dispositivo, com atenção ao ano em que cada regra começa a valer, e transforma cada regra em reais, em empresas concretas. Está organizado em cinco partes: a vantagem que muda de mecanismo; a arquitetura tributária da Zona Franca na reforma (quem tem direito, as entradas, a indústria incentivada, o comércio, o Simples Nacional e as Áreas de Livre Comércio); os efeitos econômicos e financeiros (crédito, split payment e capital de giro, preço e margem, três cenários); aplicações e decisões empresariais (um ciclo industrial completo, três comerciantes e a mesma fábrica em Manaus e em São Paulo); e gestão e futuro (governança tributária e o desafio competitivo até 2073). As simulações usam alíquotas hipotéticas declaradas (IBS de 17,7% e CBS de 8,8%) e o regime pleno de 2033. Onde a lei, o regulamento e as orientações oficiais divergem ou não respondem, o texto mostra a regra expressa, a leitura adotada e a leitura contrária. 1ª edição, revisão 1, com a legislação e os atos publicados até 16 de novembro de 2026. Atualizações: https://www.zfmlab.com.br/zona-franca-de-manaus-e-a-reforma-tributaria
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Predicting Delivery Failures in Technical Courier Services: A Survival Learning Approach for Sustainable Last-Mile Logistics
resume: Purpose: This study develops a predictive monitoring framework based on statistical and machine learning survival analysis to anticipate delivery failures, operational disruptions, and associated fleet emissions in last-mile logistics. Because technical courier operations involve scheduled appointments, on-site technical tasks, strict SLAs, and right-censored delivery outcomes, time-to-event modeling provides a proactive alternative to reactive exception handling. Design/methodology/approach: Using a structured benchmark of 60,000 technical courier delivery orders engineered to capture operational, spatial, behavioral, and environmental dynamics, the study benchmarks semi-parametric Cox proportional hazards models and regularized extensions (Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net, and OSCAR) against non-parametric survival ensembles, including Random Survival Forests (RSF), Bagging Survival Trees, and Survival Boosting. Model discrimination, calibration, and prediction error are evaluated out-of-sample using Harrell's concordance index (C-index), time-dependent AUC, and the Integrated Brier Score (IBS), complemented by post-hoc interpretability (variable importance and partial dependence) and an online operational simulation. Findings: Survival learning models—and in particular the Enhanced Random Survival Forest incorporating dynamic operational and environmental covariates (including workload progression, routing/thermal/carbon indicators, and customer/service attributes)—outperform baseline statistical specifications, achieving strong out-of-sample discrimination (C-index≈0.84, AUC=0.8450) and low prediction error (IBS=0.0203). Post-hoc and sensitivity analyses show that cumulative workload, carbon/routing friction, thermal extremes, and urban/regulatory constraints (such as LTZ access) shape failure risk non-linearly, while proactive mid-route risk monitoring reduces preventable disruptions and associated CO2 emissions. Practical implications: The framework supports dispatchers and Transportation Management Systems (TMS) in shifting from post-facto disruption management to proactive, time-aware delivery monitoring—enabling earlier intervention on high-risk orders, better resource and route coordination, fewer failed attempts, and CO2 tracking aligned with ISO 14083:2023. Originality/value: Rather than treating delivery outcomes as static binary classifications or relying solely on reactive reporting, this work demonstrates how survival learning models can monitor time-dependent failure risk in technical courier logistics even when full physical IoT sensorization is not yet available, integrating operational reliability with environmental sustainability Keywords: Technical last-mile logistics, Supply chain resilience, Survival analysis, Delivery failure prediction, Green logistics. 🎯 Objective: This study proposes a dataset and proactive predictive framework based on survival analysis to evaluate and mitigate delivery failure risks in last-mile technical courier services, addressing operational inefficiency, elevated costs, and redundant emissions. • RQ1. Which factors exert the greatest influence on the occurrence of failed deliveries in technical courier services? • RQ2. Are advanced machine learning models capable of accurately predicting the time-dependent risk of delivery failure prior to service execution? • RQ3. What extent can predictive analytics enhance the sustainability of logistics operations by reducing failed deliveries and minimizing unnecessary vehicle movements?
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Acute stress is associated with rapid sex-dependent epigenetic changes in the human intestinal mucosa
resume: The intestinal barrier is essential for gut homeostasis, regulating immune responses, digestion, and nutrient absorption. Psychological and physical stress can rapidly alter barrier function, showing marked sexual dimorphism. Although epigenetic mechanisms are proposed to mediate these changes, it remains unclear whether acute stress is associated with changes in the human intestinal epigenome in vivo . We aimed to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation and microRNA (miRNA) changes in the human jejunal mucosa following acute stress and to assess sex-specific effects. DNA methylation and miRNA expression were analyzed in intestinal mucosa from healthy subjects at baseline and after 15 min of cold pain stress (CPS). DNA methylation (850,000 CpGs) was assessed using the Infinium MethylationEPIC array (Illumina), and 25 IBS-related miRNAs were quantified using an nCounter miR a-la-carte codeset. Comparison of biopsies obtained before and after CPS identified 4,116 differentially methylated CpGs. Sex-stratified analysis increased this number to 94,075, highlighting a marked sex-dependent epigenetic response. Enriched pathways included cell adhesion, cytoskeletal organization, neurodevelopment, cytokine signaling, and MAPK/Wnt pathways. CPS was also associated with reduced expression of miR-125b-5p and miR-145-5p. Acute stress is associated with rapid, sex-dependent epigenetic changes in the human intestinal mucosa, providing evidence for a potential role of epigenetic regulation in stress-associated intestinal barrier dysfunction, and disease vulnerability.

titre: A REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA NO BRASIL: IMPACTOS SOBRE A JUSTIÇA FISCAL, O SETOR PRODUTIVO E O DESENVOLVIMENTO SOCIOECONÔMICO
resume: A reforma tributária brasileira configura-se como uma das mais expressivas mudanças promovidas no sistema fiscal nacional nas últimas décadas, tendo como propósito tornar a estrutura tributária mais simples, eficiente e alinhada aos princípios da justiça fiscal. Ao longo dos anos, o sistema tributário brasileiro consolidou-se como um dos mais complexos do mundo, caracterizado pela multiplicidade de tributos, sobreposição de regras e excessiva burocracia, fatores que comprometem a competitividade econômica e dificultam o cumprimento das obrigações fiscais. Com a promulgação da Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023 e sua posterior regulamentação pelas Leis Complementares nº 214/2025 e nº 227/2026, foram instituídas alterações estruturais relevantes, incluindo o IBS, a CBS e o Imposto Seletivo. Nesse contexto, este estudo tem como objetivo analisar os desafios para a efetivação de um sistema tributário justo no Brasil, bem como os reflexos da Reforma Tributária sobre o setor produtivo e a competitividade das empresas. A pesquisa é orientada pelo seguinte problema: quais são os principais desafios para a efetivação de um sistema tributário mais justo no Brasil e quais os reflexos da Reforma Tributária sobre o setor produtivo e a competitividade das empresas? Parte-se da hipótese de que as mudanças representam avanço significativo na modernização da tributação nacional, embora persistam desafios relacionados à transição, à coordenação federativa e aos impactos distributivos da nova sistemática. Adotou-se pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo, fundamentada na análise da legislação, da doutrina especializada e de estudos econômicos. Os resultados indicam que a reforma possui potencial para reduzir distorções, ampliar a segurança jurídica e favorecer o desenvolvimento econômico, mas sua efetividade dependerá da aplicação coordenada das novas regras pelos diferentes níveis da Federação.

titre: Folinic Acid as a Precision Therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder: Interorgan Communication Through Folate Transport, Mitochondrial Metabolism, and the Gut–Brain Axis
resume: One‐carbon metabolism, which is dependent on folate, plays a critical role in central nervous system (CNS) development and neurogenesis by regulating nucleotide synthesis, epigenetic methylation, neurotransmission, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and redox balance. Disrupted cerebral folate transport due to folate receptor alpha (FRα) autoantibodies, genetic variants affecting folate metabolism, or impaired transport across the choroid plexus and blood–brain barrier can cause cerebral folate deficiency (CFD), increasingly associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Reduced CNS folate availability may impair methylation, alter monoamine and glutamate signaling, disrupt mitochondrial one‐carbon metabolism, and increase neuronal oxidative stress. Folinic acid (leucovorin), a reduced folate derivative, may bypass certain transport and metabolic limitations, replenishing cellular folate stores and supporting CNS function. It may also support mitochondrial redox homeostasis, glutathione‐dependent antioxidant defenses, and metabolic coupling between cytosolic and mitochondrial one‐carbon pathways. Clinical trials have reported improvements in language, communication, and adaptive behavior, particularly among FRα autoantibody‐positive ASD subgroups. This review integrates evidence on folate transport, genetic susceptibility, mitochondrial metabolism, and gut–brain interactions to explore cerebral folate dysregulation in ASD pathophysiology. From an interorgan communication perspective, cerebral folate homeostasis depends on coordinated intestinal absorption, systemic folate circulation, choroid plexus transport, and neuronal metabolism. Gut‐derived microbial metabolites may influence peripheral‐central metabolic signaling, although their direct contribution to cerebral folate availability remains uncertain. Understanding these interconnected pathways may support biomarker‐guided folinic acid interventions and advance precision therapeutic strategies for biologically defined ASD subgroups while identifying important mechanistic and clinical research priorities.

fiche.conclusion: Comprendre ces voies interconnectées pourrait soutenir des interventions à l'acide folinique guidées par biomarqueurs pour des sous-groupes d'autisme biologiquement définis.

titre: INTEGRATING PROBIOTICS, PREBIOTICS, SYNBIOTICS, AND DIETARY STRATEGIES FOR GUT MICROBIOTA MODULATION IN PARKINSON'S DISEASE: A NARRATIVE REVIEW
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. In 2021, approximately 11.8 million individuals were living with PD, and this number is projected to reach 25.2 million by 2050, representing a 112% increase. Pathologically, PD is characterized by the progressive degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, resulting in striatal dopamine depletion and accumulation of aggregated α-synuclein within Lewy bodies. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbial dysbiosis may contribute to disease mechanisms through the microbiota-gut-brain axis by impairing intestinal barrier integrity, promoting systemic and neuroinflammatory signaling, and potentially facilitating the propagation of misfolded α-synuclein. Nutritional and microbiota-directed strategies may therefore offer adjunctive support in PD management. Prebiotics can promote the growth and metabolic activity of beneficial bacteria, including short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, which may support intestinal barrier function and immune regulation. Probiotics have shown the most consistent clinical benefit for gastrointestinal symptoms, particularly constipation, although their effects on inflammatory and neurological outcomes remain uncertain. Synbiotics combine probiotic microorganisms with selectively utilized substrates and may simultaneously modify microbial composition and metabolic activity. Dietary strategies, including fiber-rich foods, fermented foods, and carefully timed protein intake, may also influence bowel function, nutritional status, and levodopa pharmacokinetics. Although these interventions are accessible and generally well tolerated, evidence for disease modification remains limited. Further randomized, strain-specific trials with standardized formulations, microbiome and metabolomic endpoints, and clinically meaningful outcomes are needed to define their safety, efficacy, and role alongside conventional PD treatment.

titre: Gut-Derived Metabolites Associated with Blood–Brain Barrier Alterations in Autistic Children: Preliminary Insights from a Sibling Pair Study
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently co-occurs with gastrointestinal symptoms, motivating the investigation of microbial and metabolic factors within the microbiota–gut–brain axis. However, the effects of participant-derived faecal preparations on brain endothelial barrier properties remain incompletely characterised. This exploratory study combined gut and oral microbiota profiling, faecal metabolomics, and an endothelial resistance assessment in four sibling pairs discordant for ASD. Microbiota were analysed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and untargeted HPLC-ESI/HRMS metabolomics was performed in two sibling pairs. Faecal cell-free supernatants were tested in human brain microvascular endothelial cells using electrical resistance measurements complemented by an ATP-based viability assay. Participant-level microbial profiles showed substantial heterogeneity, and several differences apparent in group averages were not consistently reproduced across sibling pairs. Putatively annotated metabolic features were assigned to tryptophan-related pathways and the superpathway of chorismate metabolism; chorismate itself was not detected. Supernatants from the ASD participants in two of four pairs produced lower normalised endothelial resistance than the corresponding sibling control specimens, whereas this pattern was not observed in the other two pairs. No apparent reduction in ATP-based viability was observed at the measured endpoint. These findings integrate microbial and metabolic profiling with a functional endothelial assessment relevant to blood–brain barrier (BBB) research but do not establish an ASD-specific signature, BBB dysfunction, or a causal microbiota–metabolite–barrier mechanism. Larger, prospectively characterised cohorts and the controlled validation of candidate bioactive components are required.

titre: Oral microbiome dysbiosis, neuroinflammation, and psychiatric disorders: A review of current progress
resume: The oral microbiome, as the largest and most diverse microbial community in the human body, has emerged as a potential contributor to brain health. However, the mechanistic pathways by which oral dysbiosis influences the pathogenesis of psychiatric disorders remain incompletely integrated, and its translational implications for clinical practice have yet to be fully elucidated. This minireview aims to systematically synthesize current evidence on the role of oral microbiome dysbiosis in psychiatric disorders, with a particular focus on neuroinflammation as the key mediating mechanism, and to discuss the clinical and translational implications of these findings. In contrast to prior reviews that have largely centered on the gut-brain axis or individual diagnostic categories, the current minireview synthesizes evidence on three neuroinflammatory pathways: Hematogenous, retrograde neural, and the oral-gut-brain axis by which oral dysbiosis may contribute to psychiatric outcomes. By consolidating findings across major psychiatric disorders and emphasizing neuroinflammation as a core mediating process, we propose an integrative framework that unites oral microbiology with psychiatric pathophysiology.

titre: Alzheimer's disease beyond the brain: the role of the enteric nervous system
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly understood as a systemic condition involving central and peripheral nervous and immune systems. This shift has directed attention to the gut, where the enteric nervous system (ENS) and its enteric glial cells sit at the interface of the gut-brain axis. Gastrointestinal disturbances, altered microbiota, and enteric deposits of amyloid-β and tau are all documented in AD, prompting closer investigation of the role enteric glia and the ENS play in disease progression. As the gut ages, it becomes a primed environment in which inflammation, dysbiosis, and protein deposition reinforce one another, raising an inflammatory tone that the gut-brain axis delivers to the brain. Enteric glial cells play a double-edged role in this process: in homeostatic states, they provide trophic and protective support, but in reactive states they amplify inflammatory signaling, weaken the epithelial barrier, and disturb neuronal circuits. On current evidence, the gut is best understood as an amplifier of AD pathology rather than its initiator, and enteric glia as double-edged modulators rather than primary drivers. Because this evidence remains convergent and partially indirect, this review outlines the priorities needed to test the proposed framework, identifying enteric glial reactivity as a target for future mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

fiche.conclusion: L'intestin est mieux compris comme amplificateur de la pathologie d'Alzheimer que comme initiateur, et les glias entériques comme modulateurs à double tranchant.

titre: Microbial dial: How the gut microbiome tunes the severity of autism spectrum disorder
resume: A recent study used a monozygotic (MZ) twin design to investigate how the gut microbiome influences the severity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) independent of genetic factors. By comparing genetically identical twins with discordant symptoms, the study identified the gut microbiome as a key non-shared environmental contributor. Beta-diversity analysis revealed distinct microbial community structures between high-severity and low-severity groups. Notably, the genus Porphyromonas , which is associated with inflammation and compromised gut barrier function, was enriched in high-severity twins. In contrast, these individuals exhibited reduced functional potential in pathways related to carbohydrate transport and amino acid metabolism. Collectively, these findings suggest that functional dysbiosis may exacerbate the symptoms of ASD via the gut-brain axis, potentially through systemic inflammation and altered metabolite production. While the MZ twin design effectively controls for genetic background, the study is limited by a small sample size and the absence of dietary data or mechanistic validation. Future research should employ multi-omics approaches and targeted interventions to confirm the regulatory chain of the gut microbiota metabolite-brain axis. Overall, the evidence suggests that while genetics provides the blueprint for ASD, the gut microbiome acts as a “dial” that modulates phenotypic severity.

titre: Digital CBT-based interventions for somatoform disorders and related conditions: a systematic review
resume: Protocol of a systematic review of randomised controlled trials on the efficacy of digital psychological interventions based on cognitive behavioural therapy (including ACT, mindfulness and psychoeducation) for adults with somatoform disorders (ICD-10 F45) or related diagnoses (e.g., somatic symptom disorder, illness anxiety, bodily distress, medically unexplained or persistent somatic symptoms). The primary outcome is the psychological burden associated with somatic symptoms (SSD-12, SSEQ); symptom severity (PHQ-15) is analysed additionally. Results will be synthesised narratively following SWiM; certainty of evidence will be assessed with GRADE. Full protocol details are provided in the registration form.

titre: A systematic review of self-compassion interventions for psychological well-being in children
resume: Children face increasing​ challenges that may threaten their psychological well-being. Self-criticism in response to failure is a key factor. Self-compassion interventions may help reduce self-criticism, thereby improving coping with failure and supporting psychological well-being. This systematic review synthesises current evidence on the effects of self-compassion interventions on psychological well-being in children and adolescents, with age-stratified analyses to clarify effects in children. Six databases (PubMed, CINAHL Ultimate, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science) were searched from inception to February 2026. Data extraction followed the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. Study quality was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) for randomised controlled trials and ROBINS-I V2 for quasi-experimental studies. Eight studies involving 324 participants met inclusion criteria. Among children, interventions were associated with significant reductions in anxiety and depressive symptoms from pre- to post-intervention, and one study reported a significant increase in positive affect relative to controls. Among adolescents, most studies reported significant reductions in anxiety, whereas findings for depression and perceived stress were mixed, and no significant changes were reported for positive affect or emotional well-being. Overall risk of bias was rated high, primarily due to lack of blinding and the absence of control groups. Self-compassion interventions may be beneficial for children and adolescents, however, with only eight studies (324 participants), including only two child-focused studies (44 participants), the evidence remains very limited and should be regarded as preliminary, particularly for children. Future research should employ adequately powered randomised controlled trials, qualified facilitators, and child-tailored strategies to strengthen intervention delivery and home practice and to generate more robust evidence on effectiveness.

titre: Randomized controlled trial of Group Interpersonal Therapy conducted by non-specialists versus waiting list for symptoms of depression and anxiety in community young adults: a research protocol
resume: Introduction Depression is a highly prevalent and potentially chronic mental disorder with significant impact on quality of life and social support, with a frequent onset in early adulthood. Despite the existence of effective treatments, many individuals do not have access to care, do not respond to, or do not tolerate medications. Additionally, access to mental health services remains limited, especially in low- and middle-income countries, where the World Health Organization estimates that 75% of individuals do not receive adequate care. Group Interpersonal Therapy (IPT-G) is an evidence-based, structured psychotherapy recommended by international guidelines for the treatment of depression and is adaptable for task-shifting approaches in primary care. Previous research has shown promising results for IPT-G delivered by non-specialists in low-resource settings in an open study, but randomized trials by non-specialists are still lacking. Objectives To evaluate the improvement in depressive and anxiety symptoms after eight sessions of IPT-G among young adults with depressive symptoms in a community setting, conducted by non-specialists in a randomized trial, representing a new step in demonstrating scientific evidence for novel clinical treatments. Methods This randomized controlled clinical trial is planned to include 76 participants randomized (1:1) between an interventional (IPT-G) and a control (waiting list) group. Our study will enroll young adults aged 18–24 years with depressive symptoms. The intervention will focus on interpersonal relationships within the IPT model and will be delivered by a university student and a medical doctor trained in IPT. The primary outcome is the HADS total score at 8 weeks, reflecting combined depressive and anxiety symptom severity; secondary outcomes include quality of life and social support. Discussion This study may provide evidence on the efficacy of IPT-G delivered by trained non-specialists among young adults with depressive symptoms. Positive findings could support the development of supervised task-sharing approaches to expand access to psychological care and address mental health treatment gaps. Further research could build on these findings to examine cost-effectiveness and implementation in different health care settings. Clinical trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06480019 , identifier NCT06480019.

titre: Stepwise psychological intervention: Mitigated psychological distress and suicide risk in patients with liver cancer chemoembolization
resume: BACKGROUND Patients with liver cancer undergoing targeted therapy combined with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) may experience substantial psychological distress, anxiety, depression, and suicide-related risk. Risk-stratified psychological care may help address these problems by matching the intensity of psychological support to patients’ assessed risk levels; however, evidence regarding structured stepped psychological interventions in this population remains limited. AIM To evaluate the short-term effects of a stepped psychological intervention on psychological distress and suicide risk in patients with liver cancer receiving targeted therapy combined with TACE. METHODS This single-center, unregistered randomized controlled trial included 98 patients with liver cancer who received targeted therapy combined with TACE between April 2024 and November 2025. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to a control group (n = 49), which received routine nursing care, or a stepped psychological intervention group (n = 49), which received risk-stratified psychological assessment and stepped psychological care in addition to routine care. Psychological distress, suicide risk, anxiety, and depression were assessed using the Distress Thermometer (DT), Nurses’ Global Assessment of Suicide Risk (NGASR), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), respectively. Treatment adherence, nursing satisfaction, and safety-related events were evaluated as secondary outcomes. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with significant psychological distress (DT ≥ 4) and high suicide risk (NGASR ≥ 5) at the 4-week follow-up. To minimize potential overadjustment and mediator bias, only baseline or prerandomization covariates were included in these models. RESULTS At the 4-week follow-up, DT, NGASR, SAS, and SDS scores decreased in both groups, with greater reductions observed in the stepped psychological intervention group. The intervention group had higher treatment adherence than the control group (95.92% vs 77.55%, P = 0.007) and higher nursing satisfaction (95.92% vs 75.51%, P = 0.004). Safety-related events were recorded in 2 of 49 patients (4.08%) in the intervention group and 9 of 49 patients (18.37%) in the control group (P = 0.025). In exploratory multivariable analyses, allocation to the stepped psychological intervention group was associated with lower odds of significant psychological distress at 4 weeks after adjustment for baseline DT score, tumor stage, and family support [adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 0.31, 95%CI: 0.12-0.78, P = 0.014]. Higher baseline DT scores and advanced tumor stage were associated with higher odds of psychological distress, whereas good family support was associated with lower odds. Similarly, intervention-group allocation was associated with lower odds of high suicide risk after adjustment for baseline NGASR score, tumor stage, and family support (adjusted OR = 0.27, 95%CI: 0.0-0.79, P = 0.018). Higher baseline NGASR scores and advanced tumor stage were associated with higher odds of suicide risk, whereas good family support was associated with lower odds. CONCLUSION In this single-center, unregistered randomized controlled trial, patients allocated to a stepped psychological intervention showed greater short-term improvements in psychological distress, suicide risk, anxiety, and depression than those receiving routine nursing care. Exploratory analyses also suggested associations with better treatment adherence and nursing satisfaction and fewer recorded safety-related events. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, short follow-up period, lack of prospective trial registration, and limitations in the assessment of secondary outcomes. Larger, prospectively registered multicenter trials using validated outcome measures, independent outcome assessment, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

titre: Peer Review Report For: OUTSIDE 2: Outdoor swimming as a nature-based intervention, offered in addition to usual care, compared to usual care alone, in people with depression: A study protocol for a randomised controlled trial and economic evaluation [version 1; peer review: 1 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
resume: Background Major depression affects at least 10% of adults, yet evidence-based treatments have modest clinical effectiveness and acceptability. In recent years, outdoor swimming has grown increasingly popular and emerging quantitative and qualitative evidence suggests potential as an intervention for depression, however, there is yet to be a full-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT). This is a protocol to assess the safety and test the clinical- and cost-effectiveness of an 8-session outdoor swimming course (in addition to usual care) on depression symptom severity in adults experiencing major depression, in comparison to usual care alone. Methods This study is a pragmatic, parallel group, superiority RCT with 1:1 allocation comparing the outdoor swimming intervention (in addition to treatment as usual) with treatment as usual, aiming to recruit 480 adult participants meeting diagnostic criteria for major depression. Recruitment will take place across 21 sites with blind post treatment and follow up assessments. The primary outcome is depression symptom severity at T1 post-intervention, 12 weeks post-randomisation (the primary end point) using the Patient Health Questionnaire 9 (PHQ-9). Secondary clinical outcomes are anxiety (Generalised Anxiety Disorder 7 at T1 and T2 [38 weeks post-randomisation] and PHQ-9 at T2), mindfulness is measured as a potential mechanism at all timepoints (Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire 15). Health economic measures at all time points are: EQ-5D-5L, Recovering Quality of Life (ReQoL), Client Service Receipt Inventory and the Productivity Cost Questionnaire. A qualitative study will examine the experience of participants during and after the swim course. Discussion If the 8-session outdoor swim course is safe, clinically- and cost-effective, findings will support national implementation, offering an evidence-based intervention to those affected by depression, while potentially reducing healthcare costs. Furthermore, this may pave the way for other outdoor activities to support people with poor mental health to be developed and evaluated as interventions. Trial registration Controlled trial registration number is ISRCTN registration number 24759023. Registered on 21 February 2024 (https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN24759023).

titre: Protocol for a Double-Blind Randomized Pilot Trial on the Augmentative Effect of Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Combined with Maintenance Medication in Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder
resume: Background: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with substantial functional impairment and represents a major public health concern. Although pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy are established treatments, a considerable proportion of adolescents experience inadequate treatment response, adverse effects, or poor adherence. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging non-invasive neuromodulation approach with potential therapeutic benefits; however, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical effects in adolescents with MDD remain insufficiently investigated. This study will evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of adjunctive tACS treatment in adolescents with MDD. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled pilot trial will enroll 30 adolescents aged 12–18 years with MDD, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active or sham stimulation. Participants will undergo a 4-week intervention phase consisting of 20 stimulation sessions, followed by a 12-week follow-up phase, resulting in a total study duration of 16 weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment performance, treatment completion, and participant retention throughout the study period. Safety will be evaluated through systematic monitoring and recording of adverse events and serious adverse events. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include CDRS-R-defined response and remission, as well as changes in depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicidality, sleep quality, Clinical Global Impression scores, rumination, and health-related quality of life. Exploratory assessments will examine cognitive, neurophysiological, and behavioral changes associated with tACS treatment. Discussion: This pilot trial will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of adjunctive tACS treatment for adolescents with MDD. The findings will help estimate potential clinical effects and inform the design of a future adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

titre: Bridging Treatment Gaps in Adolescent Depression With Neuromodulation Targeting Anhedonia
resume: Psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy remain the foundations of treatment for adolescent depression. Neuromodulation, such as electroconvulsive therapy or transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), is a relatively new approach to pediatric care and historically has not been used much within the field of child psychiatry. Electroconvulsive therapy is an important and highly effective treatment for selected adolescents with severe depression and catatonia.1 Its use, however, requires anesthesia and specialized clinical infrastructure and remains uncommon in pediatric practice. TMS offers a different form of neuromodulation with fewer procedural requirements that may help patients with significant depression. Anhedonia, or loss of interest and pleasure, deserves particular attention because greater anhedonia is associated with more severe illness and suicidality and may predict poorer treatment response.2,3In this issue of Pediatrics, Duan et al4 report a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of individualized functional connectivity-guided intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) in adolescents with major depressive disorder who had not responded adequately to at least one antidepressant trial. Compared with sham stimulation, active iTBS produced greater improvement in depressive symptoms. Improvement in anhedonia was particularly notable. The authors also found that change in anhedonia statistically mediated a substantial proportion of the later antidepressant effect. This finding does not establish anhedonia as the mechanism of treatment response, but it raises an intriguing possibility that reward-related symptoms may be an important target for neuromodulation.The individualized targeting strategy is another important feature of this study. The investigators selected a left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex region based on its functional connectivity with the nucleus accumbens, an important component of reward circuitry. Dysfunction in this network may contribute to impaired reward processing, reduced motivation, and difficulty engaging in goal-directed behavior. The study therefore provides an example of how treatment may eventually move beyond diagnosis alone and incorporate clinically important symptoms and their underlying circuitry.iTBS also has practical advantages for adolescents. It is a form of TMS that is noninvasive, does not require anesthesia, and can be delivered in an outpatient setting. Individual iTBS stimulation sessions are considerably shorter than conventional repetitive TMS sessions. This may make a repeated treatment course easier to incorporate into school and family schedules.In 2024, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) first cleared a TMS system as an adjunct for treatment of major depressive disorder in patients aged 15 to 21 years.5 Unlike the adult indication that specifies inadequate improvement with prior antidepressant medication, the adolescent indication does not require failed antidepressant trials. This regulatory language should not be interpreted as a recommendation to use TMS immediately after one unsuccessful selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) trial. It does, however, raise an important question about when consultation should occur.For pediatricians, the distinction between consultation and treatment may be more useful than defining a specific treatment threshold. The participants studied by Duan et al4 had greater treatment complexity than many adolescents with depression managed in primary care, including psychiatric comorbidity and substantial concomitant psychotropic medication use. Many were receiving other psychotropic medications, including antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, and mood stabilizers. These findings therefore should not be interpreted as establishing iTBS as the next treatment for an otherwise uncomplicated adolescent who has had an inadequate response to one SSRI.At the same time, referral does not need to wait until treatment has become highly complex. For an adolescent with persistent depression despite adequate initial treatment, particularly when anhedonia and functional impairment remain substantial, consultation with a child psychiatrist may be reasonable. TMS centers are increasingly available across the United States, and many practices can provide treatment to adolescents aged 15 years and older. However, child psychiatrists with specific expertise in neuromodulation remain relatively scarce, and consultation with a pediatric neuromodulation specialist may require referral to a regional specialty or academic center. This consultation model may be particularly relevant to pediatric practice. Pediatricians increasingly care for adolescents with depression because access to specialty mental health care remains limited. Referral for neuromodulation consultation does not require pediatricians to determine TMS candidacy themselves. Rather, it provides another option when initial treatment has not produced sufficient recovery.Several questions remain before this approach can be incorporated more broadly into care. The interaction between neuromodulation and other treatments deserves particular study. Medications may alter response to stimulation, and concurrent psychotherapy may enhance or modify treatment effects. These questions are especially relevant given the medication complexity of participants in this trial. Development also matters. The participants ranged from 10 to 17 years, a period of substantial brain maturation. Larger studies and longer follow-up are needed to better understand developmental differences, durability of response, and cognitive safety.Duan et al4 offer an important view of how treatment for adolescent depression may evolve. Their study combines a clinically meaningful symptom, individualized neural targeting, and a noninvasive intervention. For pediatricians, the immediate implication is not that iTBS should become the next step after an antidepressant fails. It is that neuromodulation can become part of the treatment discussion when depression persists despite appropriate initial treatment. Future research should help define which patients are most likely to benefit, how neuromodulation should be combined with psychotherapy and medication, and when consultation and treatment should occur.

titre: An Integrative Review on Sun Salutation for Health Outcomes Among Working Women: Implications for Corporate Women
resume: Introduction: In today's society, women are juggling multiple roles, including careers, leading to both empowerment and challenges in maintaining good health. Many working women, especially in the corporate world, seek time-efficient and affordable ways to stay healthy. Sun Salutation (SS), a sequence of 12 yoga postures combined with breathing and mindfulness, supports physical fitness, physiological and mental health, making it a valuable daily practice. This review synthesizes available evidence on the promising effect of SS practice on health outcomes among working adults and adult women, with particular attention to its potential implications for corporate women and their productivity. Methods: Considering predefined inclusion criteria and following the PRISMA guidelines, nine studies, including six on working adults where two specifically on women as direct evidence, while three were from mixed sex and one study not mentioned about sex as indirect evidence and other three supportive studies on age-matched healthy women, were identified through a comprehensive search of electronic databases, including Google Scholar, Web of Science, DOAJ, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and PubMed. Methodological quality of selected studies was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme, and risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBINS-I for randomized and non-randomized studies, respectively. Results: The study findings revealed that the regular practice of Sun Salutation (SS) is associated with promising impact in reducing stress, anxiety, blood pressure, and an increase in pulmonary function, forced vital capacity, cognitive function and quality of life. Additionally, supportive evidence demonstrated significant beneficial effects of SS on body mass index (BMI), body composition, cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular endurance, and flexibility among middle-aged women. However, considerable heterogeneity in study designs, participant characteristics, intervention protocols, and outcome measures influenced the overall consistency of the findings. Conclusion: Based on the evidence, this integrative review suggests potential benefits of the Sun Salutation practice for selected physical, physiological and psychological health outcomes, while limited studies were conducted on corporate women and workplace productivity. Therefore, well-designed and high-quality controlled studies need to be conducted to generalize the findings.

titre: What Survival Benchmarks Don't Tell You: Impact of Model Selection and Dataset Regimes
resume: Despite the proliferation of survival analysis methods, current benchmarks often operate under narrow conditions: they heavily rely on the concordance index (C-index) for evaluation and model selection, and frequently either exclude deep learning (DL) methods or underrepresent challenging dataset regimes. To address these limitations, we conduct a large-scale, neutral benchmark comparing 10 classical, tree-based, and DL methods across 49 diverse datasets. Crucially, we treat the model selection criterion (optimizing for C-index, Integrated Brier Score (IBS), or Mean Absolute Error (MAE-PO)) as an independent experimental variable. Using Bayesian mixed-effects modeling, we demonstrate that evaluation design heavily dictates conclusions. For complex DL and tree-based architectures, selecting hyperparameters to optimize for IBS instead of C-index yields substantial improvements in probabilistic accuracy and calibration at a negligible cost to discriminative ranking. Furthermore, method performance (C-index, IBS, MAE-PO, and X-CAL) is fundamentally governed by dataset characteristics. While DL models scale exceptionally well with larger sample sizes, they suffer notable performance drops in high-dimensional feature spaces. Additionally, we expose a structural vulnerability where heavy censoring artificially inflates absolute calibration metrics, creating overly conservative tests. Ultimately, our findings challenge the utility of global single-number performance summaries and advocate for survival analysis results that transparently report the evaluation setup. Our code is available at: https://github.com/sdening/surv-bench-study

titre: Alíquota zero da Cesta Básica Nacional e progressividade tributária: materiais de reprodutibilidade da análise da POF 2017–2018
resume: Este depósito reúne os materiais de reprodutibilidade de uma pesquisa sobre o potencial da alíquota zero do IBS e da CBS, previsto no art. 125 da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025 para os produtos da Cesta Básica Nacional, na promoção da progressividade tributária. Uma investigação utiliza os microdados da Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares (POF) 2017–2018, do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), para analisar a distribuição das despesas com os alimentos contemplados pela medida entre diferentes faixas de renda. O conjunto disponibiliza o roteiro de processamento em linguagem R, as planilhas de classificação dos produtos alimentados por códigos de cinco e sete dígitos, as tabelas finais, os resultados calculados em formato RDS e um relatório metodológico contendo os códigos utilizados e a explicação das etapas da análise. Os procedimentos compreendem a seleção e classificação dos alimentos, a identificação das auditorias financeiras, a anualização e mensalização das despesas, a formação de quartis de renda monetária bruta per capita com utilização de pesos amostrais e a cálculo dos indicadores apresentados nas quatro tabelas da pesquisa. Os scripts originais e revisados foram executados separadamente pelo pesquisador, em sessões limpas do RStudio, mediante execução sequencial dos comandos. Ambas as execuções produziram resultados coincidentes com os 58 valores numéricos apresentados nas quatro tabelas do estudo. Os microdados originais do IBGE não integram este depósito, devendo ser obtidos diretamente na fonte oficial indicada na documentação.

titre: Effects of the Self-Guided Web-Based Intervention vimida on Post–COVID-19 Fatigue: Randomized Controlled Trial (Preprint)
resume: BACKGROUND Persistent fatigue is one of the most debilitating symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), also referred to as Long COVID. However, evidence-based and scalable psychological interventions for managing this condition remain scarce. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of vimida, a self-guided, web-based intervention incorporating techniques from cognitive behavioral therapy, as an adjunct to treatment as usual (TAU) compared to TAU alone in alleviating fatigue among adults with PCC. METHODS We conducted a decentralized, pragmatic randomized controlled trial (RCT) in Germany. Adults (≥18 years) with confirmed PCC (ICD-10: U09.9), chronic fatigue syndrome (ICD-10: G93.3), and a Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFQ-11) score ≥16 were recruited online and randomized (1:1) to either vimida plus TAU (n=88) or TAU alone (n=88). The primary outcome was fatigue severity, measured by the CFQ-11 total score. Secondary outcomes included depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9; PHQ-9), somatic symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-15; PHQ-15), health-related quality of life (Assessment of Quality of Life-8D; AQoL-8D), psychosocial functioning (Work and Social Adjustment Scale; WSAS), and anxiety symptoms (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7; GAD-7). All outcomes were assessed at 3 months, the primary time point of assessment, and at 6 months. Intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses used multiple imputation and baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. RESULTS In the ITT analysis, vimida plus TAU significantly reduced CFQ-11 scores relative to TAU alone at 3 months (baseline-adjusted mean difference -2.04 points, 95% CI -4.07 to -0.01; P=.049; d=0.30) and 6 months (-2.6 points, 95% CI -4.6 to -0.6; P=.011; d=0.40). Following false discovery rate correction, somatic symptoms at 6 months represented the only statistically significant secondary outcome (PHQ-15: -1.8 points, 95% CI -2.8 to -0.7; P<.001; d=0.54). A prespecified response of a ≥5-point reduction on the CFQ-11 was achieved by 46.6% (41/88) of the intervention group versus 30.7% (27/88) of the control group (χ²₁=4.7; P=.03; odds ratio 1.97, 95% CI 1.06-3.65). All 88 participants in the intervention group registered and engaged with the platform on a mean of 32.4 days (SD 30.0). No adverse events were attributed to vimida. CONCLUSIONS vimida combined with TAU demonstrated small yet clinically meaningful reductions in PCC-related fatigue at 3 and 6 months, with an additional benefit for somatic symptoms at 6 months. As a fully remote intervention, vimida represents a scalable adjunctive treatment option for adults with PCC-related fatigue. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06251518; InvidiCO; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06251518
