titre: Comparison of Myo-Inositol and Metformin in the Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): A Systematic Review
resume: Background: Sleep disturbance is one of the most prevalent and clinically consequential features of depressive disorders. Insomnia, hypersomnia, altered rapid eye movement sleep, reduced slow-wave sleep, and circadian dysregulation may precede a depressive episode, intensify its severity, persist after mood improvement, and increase the risk of relapse and suicidal ideation. Sleep is therefore not only a symptom domain but also a potential mechanistic and therapeutic target.Aim: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms linking sleep and depression, the clinical and prognostic significance of sleep disturbances, and therapeutic approaches including cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, antidepressant and adjunctive sleep pharmacotherapy, wake therapy, and bright light therapy.Materials and Methods: A targeted narrative synthesis of 41 English-language publications was performed. The evidence set included mechanistic and polysomnographic studies, longitudinal cohorts, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses identified through PubMed and Europe PMC searches and citation screening. Publications were grouped into sleep phenotype and neurobiology, clinical significance, suicide and relapse risk, cognitive behavioral treatment, pharmacotherapy, and chronotherapy. No de novo meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.Results: Depression is consistently associated with impaired sleep continuity, reduced slowwave sleep, and disinhibited rapid eye movement sleep, although these findings are not sufficiently specific for diagnosis. Circadian, neuroendocrine, arousal, and neuroplasticity mechanisms provide a plausible bidirectional framework. Prospective evidence indicates that insomnia approximately doubles the risk of later depression, while residual insomnia is associated with earlier recurrence. Sleep disturbance also contributes clinically relevant information to suicide-risk assessment. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia improves sleep and can reduce depressive symptoms; recent randomized evidence supports a preventive effect in young people at elevated risk. Bright light therapy shows benefit in nonseasonal depression, particularly as an adjunct, whereas wake therapy may act rapidly but is limited by frequent relapse after recovery sleep. Pharmacological choices should be aligned with the patient's sleep phenotype and monitored for short- and long-term harms.Conclusions: Sleep disturbances should be assessed and treated in parallel with core depressive symptoms rather than assumed to resolve spontaneously. A phenotype-based, measurement-informed approach that combines depression treatment with evidence-based insomnia care, circadian stabilization, and ongoing risk monitoring is the most clinically defensible strategy.

titre: Mindfulness-based stress reduction and emotion-focused therapy for test-anxious students: Impacts on anxiety and academic self-handicapping
resume: Background: Test anxiety significantly impairs adolescents’ academic functioning and psychological well-being. The current study examined the relative effectiveness of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) and Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) in alleviating test anxiety and academic self-handicapping among ninth-grade male students. Methods: During the 2025–2026 academic year, we conducted a randomized, multi-group study utilizing pretest-posttest measures and a one-month follow-up evaluation. The target population comprised ninth-grade male students with test anxiety in Ahvaz, Iran. Following administration of the Ahvaz Test Anxiety Inventory (ATAI) and structured clinical interviews, students scoring more than one standard deviation above the mean (ATAI > M + 1 SD) were identified as having elevated test anxiety. Sixty eligible participants (mean age=14.52 years, SD=0.48) were selected and randomly assigned to three groups: MBSR (n=20), EFT (n=20), or a waitlist control group (n=20). Data were gathered using the ATAI and the Academic Self-Handicapping Scale. Results: Both MBSR and EFT significantly reduced test anxiety and academic self-handicapping relative to the control group (time × group interaction for test anxiety: F=83.52, P<0.001, η²ₚ=0.67; for academic self-handicapping: F=86.37, P<0.001, η²ₚ=0.62). MBSR produced significantly greater reductions in test anxiety than EFT (posttest MD=−5.11, P=0.012; follow-up MD=−5.14, P=0.018), whereas EFT yielded significantly larger reductions in academic self-handicapping (posttest MD=4.19, P=0.009; follow-up MD=4.87, P=0.007). Conclusion: Both interventions appear promising for reducing test-related distress and maladaptive academic behaviors in male adolescents. Pending longer-term follow-up data and replication in more diverse samples, cautious integration of these approaches into school counseling programs may be considered.

titre: Long-term implications of appendectomy in children: reappraising the appendix as a functional organ
resume: Appendectomy is among the most frequently performed operations in children, and acute appendicitis remains one of the most common pediatric surgical emergencies worldwide. For more than a century, the appendix was regarded as a vestigial structure whose removal carried no lasting consequence, an assumption that underlies the long-standing default of operative management of appendicitis. Two developments now invite reexamination of that assumption: the growing use of nonoperative management for uncomplicated appendicitis, and an expanding body of evidence arguing the appendix is immunologically active and serves as a reservoir for the gut microbiome. This review synthesizes current data on the long-term implications of appendectomy in the pediatric population. We first examine the appendix as a functional organ-its immunologic role, its function as a microbiome reservoir, and its participation in the gut-brain axis. We review its proposed associations with inflammatory bowel disease, systemic autoimmune disease, and Parkinson disease, followed by its oncologic relevance with respect to appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors and colorectal cancer. Much of the evidence is observational, derived from adults, and contradictory. Appendectomy for appropriate indications remains safe and effective, but increasing understanding of the appendix's biology and consequences of its removal may be helpful with shared decision-making.

titre: Associations between different dimensions of social cognition and apathy in early-to-moderate-stage Parkinson's disease
resume: INTRODUCTION: Apathy is a prevalent non-motor symptom in Parkinson's disease (PD), potentially linked to social cognition impairments. However, the relationship between distinct apathy dimensions and multiple domains of social cognition in early-stage PD remains unclear. This study investigated these associations. METHODS: Forty PD patients (Hoehn and Yahr ≤3) and their partners (informants and healthy controls) were included. Apathy was assessed using the Apathy Motivation Index (self- and informant-report). Social cognition covered emotion recognition (ERT), Theory of Mind (SET), alexithymia (TAS-20), and everyday social functioning (OSCARS). Group differences and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Moderate to severe apathy was reported in 15% of PD patients, while 32.5% of informants rated the patients as having moderate to severe apathy. Informant-rated apathy was significantly associated with both social cognition and everyday social functioning (R 2 = 0.555, p < .001), with the strongest contribution from everyday social functioning (β = 0.788, p < .001), followed by Theory of Mind (β = 0.282, p = .048, in an unexpected direction) and emotion recognition (β = -0.289, p = .042). Self-reported apathy was neither significantly associated with social cognition nor with everyday social functioning. Exploratory subscale analyses showed modest associations of self-reported apathy with alexithymia and everyday social functioning which require replication. Furthermore, PD patients reported higher levels of alexithymia than controls (d = 0.43, p = .030), while no significant group differences were found for emotion recognition (d = -0.34, p = .054) or Theory of Mind (d = -0.31, p = .061) after correction for multiple testing. CONCLUSION: In early-to-moderate-stage PD, informant-rated apathy was strongly associated with informant-rated everyday social functioning, partly reflecting shared informant ratings, and more weakly with emotion recognition. Associations of self-reported apathy with alexithymia and social functioning were limited to specific apathy dimensions and are exploratory. These findings support multi-informant assessment of apathy in clinical practice.

titre: Inpatient Faecal Disimpaction in Children: A Multicentre Audit of Management Practices and Short-Term Outcomes
resume: PURPOSE: Faecal impaction is a common complication of paediatric functional constipation and frequently necessitates inpatient disimpaction. Despite this, there is no universally accepted protocol for inpatient management, and endpoints defining successful disimpaction remain unclear. This study aimed to audit inpatient management strategies for paediatric faecal impaction and assess whether stool output characteristics at discharge are associated with short-term clinical improvement. METHODS: This multicentre retrospective audit included children aged 4-17 years admitted for inpatient faecal disimpaction across eight Queensland hospitals between January and December 2021. Data collected included demographics, disimpaction regimens, route of administration, adjunct enema use, length of stay (LOS), Bristol Stool Scale scores at admission and discharge, and Bowel Management Tool Scores (BMST) at admission and first follow-up. RESULTS: Seventy-five inpatient episodes were included. Median LOS was 4 days (interquartile range, 3-5). BMST improved by a median of 3.5 points, with 73% of patients demonstrating categorical improvement at follow-up. Adjunct enemas were used in 24% of admissions and were not associated with reduced LOS compared with admissions without enemas (median 5.2 vs. 4.3 days; p=0.60). Nasogastric/gastrostomy administration was used in 71% of cases and oral administration in 29%, with no significant difference in LOS (p=0.44). Approximately 84% of patients were discharged with Bristol Stool Types 7-7+. Achieving Type 7+ stool output (clear and watery) did not confer greater improvement in BMST compared with Type 7 output [3 (1.5-7) vs. 4 (2-6.2), p=0.7]. CONCLUSION: Inpatient faecal disimpaction is associated with meaningful short-term symptom improvement in children. Treating to clear outputs does not appear to confer additional clinical benefit. These findings support a pragmatic approach to inpatient disimpaction and highlight the need for standardised, evidence-based protocols.

titre: Goat milk infant formula and gut health: from traditional nutrition to scientific innovation
resume: When breastfeeding is not possible, goat milk-based infant formula (GMF) provides an alternative to cow's milk-based formula. This narrative review evaluates clinical, observational, and mechanistic evidence on the nutritional suitability of GMF and its potential relevance to infant gut health. Randomized trials and meta-analytic evidence support the safety and nutritional adequacy of GMF. Its distinct composition, including a higher β-casein-to-αs1-casein ratio and differences in the profile and concentrations of oligosaccharides and bioactive proteins compared with cow's milk, provides biological plausibility for differences in curd formation, protein digestion kinetics, and microbial fermentation. However, these mechanistic findings do not establish clinical benefit. Controlled evidence does not currently demonstrate that GMF prevents or treats feeding-related gastrointestinal symptoms, including infant colic and functional constipation, although observational studies suggest possible symptom differences in some infants. Well-designed randomized trials in symptomatic infants are needed to evaluate gastrointestinal outcomes, microbiota development, immune effects, and the potential value of emerging formula innovations. Future GMF development may combine the goat milk matrix with recombinant human milk proteins or microbiome-targeted ingredients to complement components that are absent, present at low concentrations, or altered during processing; however, their application and clinical benefits in GMF remain to be established.

titre: Carob (Ceratonia siliqua L.) as a functional synbiotic matrix: biochemical composition, probiotic compatibility, and gut microbiota modulation in food systems
resume: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are common worldwide, and their frequency has risen alongside the dietary shift that has stripped fermentable fibre out of everyday diets. Carob (Ceratonia siliqua L.) is a Mediterranean agro-industrial by-product that has mostly been put to low-value uses, although its composition is unusually varied for a fibre source. This review sets out what is known about that composition, covering galactomannans, polyphenols, dietary fibre and pinitol, and then examines how carob behaves during food processing. Three synbiotic roles are considered. Carob is a fermentable substrate that favours Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium and the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFA). It carries polyphenols that act on microbial niches alongside the fibre fraction. It is also technologically compatible with fermented matrices, where it helps probiotic cells stay viable. Mechanistic work and in vitro fermentation converge on the same picture: carob belongs among differentiated prebiotic ingredients, not among substitutes for inulin, galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS) or β-glucans. Four problems still block clinical validation. The materials tested differ widely between fractions and geographical origins; in vitro fermentation models remain distant from human physiology; almost no clinical trial has been designed around carob; and strain-substrate compatibility has never been demonstrated rigorously. The review closes with a research agenda covering targeted randomised controlled trials, CAZy-based genomic screening of candidate probiotic strains, stratified precision-nutrition designs and standardised formulations.

titre: Effects of Adjunctive Physiotherapy on Clinical Outcomes in Children with Functional Constipation: A Randomized Controlled Study
resume: PURPOSE: Functional constipation (FC) is a common pediatric gastrointestinal disorder that has a substantial impact on affected children and their families. This study aimed to evaluate whether the addition of physiotherapy (PT) to standard medical treatment improves clinical outcomes in children with FC. METHODS: In this randomized controlled study, 65 children aged 4-18 years diagnosed with FC according to the Rome IV criteria were allocated to receive standard medical treatment alone (n=35) or standard medical treatment plus PT (n=30). All patients received lactulose, toilet training, and dietary counseling. The PT program included abdominal isometric exercises, abdominal massage, pelvic floor exercises, and diaphragmatic breathing and was conducted for 3 months. The primary outcome was within-group improvement in constipation-related symptoms, and the secondary outcome was overall treatment success, defined as the absence of FC according to the Rome IV criteria at the end of follow-up. RESULTS: All constipation-related symptoms significantly improved over time in both groups. A significant between-group difference was observed only for stool-withholding behavior, which improved more frequently in the PT group (adjusted odds ratio, 3.680; 95% confidence interval, 1.410-9.610; p=0.008). No significant intergroup differences were found in other symptoms. The overall treatment success rate was higher in the PT group than in the standard medical treatment group (100.0% vs. 85.7%, p=0.031). CONCLUSION: Adjunctive PT may improve short-term overall treatment success in children with FC, particularly by reducing stool-withholding behavior. Larger studies with longer follow-up periods are required to confirm these findings.

titre: Expanding neurologic phenotypes in Ehlers-Danlos syndromes: a narrative review
resume: BACKGROUND: Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (EDS) are a heterogeneous group of heritable connective tissue disorders characterized by joint hypermobility, skin hyperextensibility, tissue fragility, and variable multisystem involvement. Although musculoskeletal and cardiovascular features are well recognized, neurologic manifestations are common, clinically significant, and frequently underrecognized. These manifestations range from dysautonomia and small fiber neuropathy (SFN) to cervical instability, epilepsy, and cerebrovascular complications. Emerging evidence further implicates autonomic dysfunction, altered connective tissue biomechanics, and neuroimmune interactions in gastrointestinal dysmotility and related gut-brain axis disturbances in EDS. This review highlights these emerging connections alongside the broader neurologic spectrum of EDS. OBJECTIVE: To summarize the major neurologic manifestations of EDS, with emphasis on nonvascular neurologic complications, diagnostic approaches, and management considerations relevant to clinical practice. METHODS: A literature search was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE. Studies published in English within the last 10 years were screened for eligibility. Eligible studies included human studies evaluating neurologic manifestations in patients with diagnosed EDS. Review articles, cohort studies, observational studies, and clinically relevant case series were included. RESULTS: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and other autonomic symptoms are frequently reported in hypermobile EDS (hEDS) and hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD). Autonomic dysfunction is also associated with gastrointestinal symptoms and dysmotility, although its causal contribution remains incompletely defined. SFN has been demonstrated in multiple hEDS/HSD cohorts and may contribute to neuropathic pain and autonomic symptoms. Structural neurologic complications including Chiari I malformation, cervical instability, atlantoaxial instability, and tethered cord syndrome are increasingly recognized. Migraine and orthostatic headache are common, while epilepsy and congenital structural brain abnormalities are associated with rarer subtypes. Vascular neurologic complications, especially in vascular EDS, include cervical artery dissection, aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, and stroke. CONCLUSION: Neurologic manifestations of EDS are diverse and often multisystemic. Earlier recognition improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary morbidity, and facilitates multidisciplinary management. Greater prospective data and subtype-specific neurologic characterization are needed.

titre: Short-term effectiveness, safety and treatment costs of vedolizumab versus infliximab in biologic-naïve patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis
resume: OBJECTIVES: To compare 14-week effectiveness, safety, and treatment costs of vedolizumab (VDZ) versus infliximab (IFX) in biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis (UC). METHODS: We retrospectively included 96 biologic-naïve patients with moderate-to-severe UC treated at Wuxi No. 2 People's Hospital (Jiangnan University Medical Center) between April 2021 and April 2026. Patients received IFX (n = 36) or VDZ (n = 60). Week-14 efficacy, biomarkers, symptom scores, World Health Organization Quality of Life Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) scores, adverse drug reactions (ADRs), and induction medication costs were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Baseline clinical characteristics were comparable between the groups (P > 0.05). At week 14, clinical response, clinical remission, and endoscopic remission rates were not significantly different between the groups (all P > 0.05). Both treatments significantly improved abdominal pain, diarrhoea, haematochezia, and WHOQOL-BREF scores from baseline (P < 0.05), with no significant between-group differences. Both treatments significantly reduced erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels at week 14 compared with baseline, with no significant between-group differences. The incidence of any adverse event was significantly lower in the VDZ group than that in the IFX group (1.7% vs. 13.9%, P = 0.027). Induction medication costs differed significantly according to the IFX product used. The mean 14-week induction medication cost per patient was significantly lower in the VDZ group than that in the overall IFX group (P = 0.038). In IFX-treated patients, baseline partial Mayo score and CRP levels were associated with remission status. CONCLUSIONS: IFX and VDZ showed comparable short-term efficacy, whereas VDZ demonstrated a more favorable short-term safety profile and a lower mean induction medication cost than the overall IFX group. Longer-term prospective studies are needed to assess maintenance efficacy, immunogenicity, and long-term safety.

titre: Subxiphoid versus right midclavicular T-tube exit route in laparoscopic common bile duct exploration: a retrospective comparative study
resume: OBJECTIVE: This study compared subxiphoid versus right midclavicular T-tube exit routes after laparoscopic common bile duct exploration (LCBDE) and assessed their impact on recovery, complications, comfort, and costs. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 280 patients who underwent LCBDE with T-tube drainage for choledocholithiasis (August 2023-February 2025). Patients were divided into subxiphoid (n = 137) and right midclavicular (n = 143) groups. General characteristics, intraoperative parameters, postoperative inflammatory markers (white blood cell count [WBC], neutrophil percentage [NEUT], C-reactive protein [CRP]) and liver function markers (total bilirubin [TBIL], alanine aminotransferase [ALT], aspartate aminotransferase [AST]), quality of life and psychological scores (Gastrointestinal Quality of Life Index [GIQLI], Self-rating Depression Scale [SDS], Self-rating Anxiety Scale [SAS]), recovery indicators (hospital stay, costs, Patient Scar Assessment Scale [PSAS]), and complication rates were compared. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, operative parameters, and postoperative inflammatory and liver function improvements were comparable between groups (all P > 0.05). The subxiphoid group showed significantly higher GIQLI scores and lower SDS and SAS scores (all P < 0.0001), with no significant differences in hospital stay, costs, PSAS, or complication/readmission rates. Rescue analgesic use was lower (13.1% vs 32.9%, P < 0.001), and more patients ambulated within 24 hours (79.6% vs 44.8%, P < 0.001) in the subxiphoid group. Skin irritation or maceration (8.0% vs 25.2%), tube fixation loosening (3.6% vs 14.7%), peritube bile leakage (4.4% vs 13.3%), and need for ≥ 4 dressing changes/week (8.8% vs 34.3%) were also significantly reduced (all P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: Both subxiphoid and right midclavicular T-tube exit routes are safe after LCBDE. The subxiphoid approach enhances postoperative comfort, patient-centered outcomes, and psychological recovery without compromising safety.

titre: How common is irritable bowel syndrome in the Mediterranean island of Malta? A cross-sectional study using Rome IV criteria
resume: BACKGROUND: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction that is diagnosed using symptom-based criteria. Prevalence estimates vary according to diagnostic definitions, and data from Southern Europe remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of IBS in a Maltese adult population using the Rome IV criteria, and to identify associated demographic and clinical factors. METHODS: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted in community settings. Adults aged ≥18 years were recruited using convenience sampling. The questionnaire incorporated Rome IV diagnostic items for IBS, symptom characteristics, dietary behavior, self-reported lactose intolerance, and food intolerance testing. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, t-tests, and binary logistic regression were used. RESULTS: A total of 1068 participants were included in the analysis (56.5% female; mean age 40.0+10.9 years). Among participants aged 18-50 years, 13.5% (95% confidence interval [CI] 11.3-15.9%) fulfilled the Rome IV criteria for IBS, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 11.0% (95%CI 9.2-13.0%) in the full cohort. The IBS group was predominantly female (77.8%), with diarrhea-predominant and mixed subtypes being the most frequent. Female sex, unemployment and current smoking were independently associated with meeting the Rome IV criteria for IBS. Participants meeting the Rome IV criteria also had higher odds of self-reported lactose intolerance and of having undergone food intolerance testing. BMI and education were not significantly associated with IBS. CONCLUSIONS: IBS is common among Maltese adults, particularly among women. The frequent use of food intolerance testing and high rates of dietary restriction among affected individuals highlight the need for better patient education and evidence-based dietary management strategies.

titre: C21 steroidal glycosides with anti-gastritis and functional constipation effects from Cynanchum wilfordii
resume: Plants of the genus Cynanchum (Apocynaceae) are recognized medicinal herbs widely used in traditional ethnomedicine for the treatment of gastrointestinal diseases. Cynanchum wilfordii (Maxim.) Hemsl., a typical medicinal species within this genus, has a longstanding traditional application for alleviating abdominal pain, dyspepsia, and various gastrointestinal disturbances, yet its definitive pharmacodynamic material basis remains elusive. In this study, eleven previously unreported C21 steroidal glycosides, namely wilfordiosides Z1-Z11, were isolated from the tuberous roots of C. wilfordii. Their chemical structures were elucidated by HRESIMS, IR, 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy analysis, in combination with acid hydrolysis. Wilfordioside Z6 (6), a relatively abundant compound, was selected for bioactivity evaluation. Results suggest that wilfordioside Z6 significantly regulated serum levels of TNF-α, EGF, MDA and SOD, increased intestinal propulsion rate and fecal moisture content, and alleviated pathological lesions in gastric and colonic tissues in mouse models of acute gastritis and functional constipation. These findings suggested that C21 steroidal glycosides in C. wilfordii should be the key bioactive constituents responsible for its gastrointestinal protective effects, providing a scientific basis for further research and development of this medicinal plant.

titre: Characterization of random media using diffusion constant: comparison of coherent and incoherent backscattering methods
resume: Within the broader field of quantitative ultrasound (QUS), multiple-scattering approaches provide a complementary framework for characterizing complex tissues or random media where conventional imaging and single-scattering assumptions become unreliable. Measuring the diffusion constant (D) in such media is highly relevant because D is directly related to scatterer density. This study evaluates two complementary techniques for measuring D: Incoherent Backscattering (IBS) and enhanced Coherent Backscattering (eCBS). Using Fullwave numerical simulations and experimental phantom validation, we compare their respective performance. Specifically, the interface between the ultrasound probe and the scattering medium is evaluated across three configurations: direct contact, a water layer, and an inhomogeneous aberrating layer. Our results demonstrate that while far-field measurements introduce significant errors due to diffraction for diverging waves, Gaussian beamforming effectively corrects this bias by refocusing the elements on the scattering medium surface. In contrast, the eCBS method (uses plane waves) is inherently independent of the distance between the probe and the scattering medium. The eCBS method proves more resilient to the phase distortions caused by an aberrating layer, but is limited by a shorter temporal window of phase coherence and is prone to instability in weakly scattering regimes where ballistic waves mask the backscattering cone. The simulations show that IBS provides more fitting samples and a longer usable temporal window than eCBS (40 μs vs. 22 μs), enabling meaningful diffusion measurements over a longer duration. In simulations, eCBS showed smaller deviations from the Direct baseline than IBS in the presence of an aberrating layer (RMSE_eCBS = 0.06, RMSE_IBS = 0.25). Experimentally, eCBS estimates were consistent with the baseline but had large uncertainties (N = 5), so this advantage should be considered preliminary. This work establishes a dual-method framework for selecting the optimal characterization tool based on acoustic environment, bridging the gap between idealized models and realistic configurations.

titre: Percutaneous Electrical Nerve Field Stimulation: Revitalizing the Management of Neurogastrointestinal Motility Disorders
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Neurogastrointestinal motility disorders and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are difficult to treat, particularly with pharmacotherapy alone. This review examines percutaneous electrical nerve field stimulation (PENFS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, addressing its potential mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, patient selection, practical implementation, and future directions of research. RECENT FINDINGS: PENFS appears to act through several pathways: limbic modulation via the central nucleus of the amygdala, altered vagal afferent signaling at the nucleus tractus solitarius, and effects on an enteric nervous system that continues to mature through adolescence. Randomized sham-controlled trials and a multicenter registry show improvement in pain, nausea, and disability alongside a favorable safety profile. Auricular allodynia and impaired cardiac vagal efficiency are emerging as markers of treatment response. PENFS is a safe, effective, non-pharmacologic option across the DGBI spectrum. Formal dose- and duration-response work, adult trials, and long-term durability data remain the principal gaps, though work is ongoing.

fiche.conclusion: La PENFS constitue une option neuromodulatrice non pharmacologique sûre et efficace pour les troubles de l'axe intestin-cerveau.

titre: Bergenin ameliorates anxiety- and depression-like behavior in antibiotic-treated mice: behavioral and in silico insights
resume: Broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure perturbs the gut microbiota and has been linked to anxiety- and depression-like behavior in rodents. Bergenin, an anti-inflammatory, antioxidant isocoumarin C-glycoside, has not previously been evaluated in this setting. Swiss albino mice received a 14-day oral-gavage antibiotic regimen (ampicillin, neomycin, metronidazole ≈10 mg/kg/day each; vancomycin ≈5 mg/kg/day), followed by 14 days of oral bergenin (25 or 50 mg/kg/day) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg/day, reference). Anxiety-like behavior was assessed by the elevated plus maze and open field test, and depression-like behavior by the forced swim and tail suspension tests. Docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics characterized bergenin's predicted binding to TLR4-MD-2 and the serotonin transporter (SERT), and ADMET/toxicity profiles were predicted. Antibiotic treatment produced weight loss and anxiety- and depression-like phenotypes across all four assays. Bergenin dose-dependently attenuated these deficits (high dose = ≈70-92% recovery) without altering behavior or body weight in antibiotic-free animals. Bergenin was predicted to occupy the SERT S1 site (ΔG = - 7.9 kcal/mol) with simulated stability resembling fluoxetine, whereas its TLR4-MD-2 interaction (ΔG = - 5.4 kcal/mol) was shallow and hydrogen bond poor relative to Eritoran. Its predicted ADMET profile was Lipinski-compliant, with some unverified toxicity alerts. Limitations include antibiotic doses lower than published protocols and no microbiome, biochemical, or molecular assays; dysbiosis, microbial recovery, and mechanism were not verified. Effects are interpreted in antibiotic-treated mice, and in silico findings are hypothesis-generating. Bergenin ameliorated anxiety- and depression-like behavior in antibiotic-treated mice; in silico data favored serotonergic over direct TLR4-MD-2 involvement, warranting experimental validation.

titre: Effectiveness of Precisely Graded Feeding Temperatures on Swallowing Function and Eating Comfort in Stroke Patients With Dysphagia: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke dysphagia (PSD) impairs recovery and quality of life, yet temperature-based feeding interventions remain insufficiently studied. This trial evaluated the effects of precisely graded food temperatures on swallowing outcomes in PSD. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 180 acute stroke patients with moderate dysphagia (Water Swallow Test grades 2-4) were assigned to cold (15°C-25°C), moderate-temperature (35°C-45°C), or hot (45°C-55°C) feeding groups. All received viscosity-adjusted diets and standardized feeding training. Outcomes included food intake volume, coughing frequency during swallowing, eating comfort score, gastric tube duration, WST grade, and gastrointestinal complications, assessed at five time points. Repeated measures ANOVA and chi-square tests were applied. RESULTS: Both cold and hot groups showed greater improvement than the moderate-temperature group in swallowing function (WST grade at 3 months: 1.15 ± 0.36 and 1.12 ± 0.32 vs. 1.83 ± 0.61; p < 0.05), gastric tube duration (9.75 ± 4.59 and 8.22 ± 6.14 days vs. 13.08 ± 9.09; p < 0.05), and fewer coughing episodes. The hot group had the highest eating comfort score (8.40 ± 1.08) and food intake volume (395.33 ± 20.46 mL). The incidence of gastric retention (p = 0.011) and diarrhoea (p = 0.043) differed significantly among groups, with the highest rates observed in the low-temperature group (6.60% and 8.30%, respectively) and the lowest gastric retention rate in the high-temperature group (3.30%). CONCLUSION: Feeding at cold or hot temperatures significantly improves swallowing recovery in PSD patients compared to moderate temperature. Hot food further enhances comfort and intake, supporting temperature-controlled feeding as a practical, individualized strategy in dysphagia rehabilitation.

titre: Patient Reported Outcome Measures of Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease Symptoms: A Systematic Review
resume: OBJECTIVE: To systematically document the validity and reliability of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) used for the assessment of symptoms associated with laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD). METHODS: Two independent investigators conducted a PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane database systematic review using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines for studies evaluating the psychometric properties (content validity, construct validity, reliability, responsiveness, and interpretability) of PROMs dedicated to LPRD symptom assessment. Risk of bias was assessed using the Clarity Group and Evidence Partners tool. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies evaluating six PROMs met the inclusion criteria, including the Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) (n = 16), Reflux Symptom Score (RSS) (n = 3), Singer Reflux Symptom Score (n = 1), Reflux Symptom Score-12 (RSS-12) (n = 4), COuGH RefluX Score (n = 2), and Laryngopharyngeal Reflux-Health-Related Quality of Life questionnaire (n = 2). PROMs evolved from predominantly laryngeal symptom questionnaires toward instruments integrating digestive, respiratory, and quality-of-life domains. RSI remained the most extensively translated and validated PROM, demonstrating generally high internal consistency (α = 0.715-0.99) and reproducibility (r/ICC = 0.70-0.988). RSS and RSS-12 demonstrated the most comprehensive psychometric profiles, including strong internal consistency (α = 0.739-0.969), reproducibility (r/ICC = 0.883-0.999), and convergent validity correlations with RSI, Voice Handicap Index, and quality-of-life instruments (r = 0.492-0.919). Only a minority of studies evaluated PROMs in patients with objectively confirmed LPRD using HEMII-pH monitoring, whereas most relied on populations with suspected LPRD. CONCLUSION: PROMs dedicated to LPRD symptom assessment generally demonstrated moderate-to-high psychometric performance. RSS showed the most complete psychometric profile for multidimensional symptom assessment, followed by RSS-12, whereas RSI remains the most widely translated instrument. Future validation studies should report content validity, ICC-based test-retest reliability, responsiveness, and thresholds established against objective reflux monitoring.
revue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation

titre: Effects of Exercise on Symptom Burden During Cancer Treatment: Real-World Evidence from a Statewide Exercise Oncology Program
resume: PURPOSE: Cancer treatment often exacerbates symptoms such as fatigue, insomnia, and gastrointestinal disturbances. This study aimed to provide real-world evidence of exercise on symptom control in patients undergoing cancer treatment. METHODS: The analysis included patients undergoing cancer treatment, who participated in the three-month Life Now Exercise oncology program across 13 community-based sites in Western Australia. Individually tailored resistance, aerobic, and flexibility exercises at a moderate-to-high intensity were delivered twice per week in a group format, supervised by accredited exercise physiologists. Symptom burden was assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and six months post-intervention using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality-of-Life Core module (EORTC QLQ-C30) and the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue scale (FACIT-F). RESULTS: Of 328 participants, 63% were aged under 65 years, 56% had breast cancer, 86% had localised disease, and 60% were undergoing hormonal therapy with/without additional radiotherapy and other systemic therapies. Improvements were observed at post-intervention in fatigue (EORTC: -3.3 [95% CI -5.5 to -1.1]; FACIT-F: 1.7 [95% CI 0.7 to 2.7]), insomnia (-3.6 [95% CI -6.9 to -0.3]), appetite loss (-3.2 [95% CI -5.9 to -0.5]), and financial difficulties (-2.8 [95% CI -5.5 to -0.1]), with most improvements sustained at six months post-intervention. Responses varied across breast, digestive, and genitourinary cancer subgroups and were associated with diverse demographic and clinical factors. However, meaningful improvements were consistently observed in patients with clinically relevant symptoms at baseline. CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal exercise at a moderate-to-high intensity is a promising non-pharmaceutical intervention for reducing symptom burden during cancer treatment. Similar exercise programs may be considered during cancer treatment for symptom control.
revue: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

titre: Effects of Different Exercise Modes on Prognostic Survival in Melanoma Patients and the Underlying Mechanisms
resume: Melanoma, a highly malignant tumor with a continuously increasing global incidence, has seen improvements in patient prognosis with the promotion of early screening and precision medicine. However, issues such as immune-related adverse reactions, drug resistance, and fatigue or functional decline during recovery still require urgent attention. Exercise, as a vital non-pharmacological adjunct intervention, demonstrates significant rehabilitative value through multiple synergistic mechanisms: aerobic exercise suppresses tumor growth, improves cachexia, and regulates ceramide metabolism to enhance chemotherapy sensitivity; resistance exercise effectively improves muscle strength and body composition; flexibility and balance exercises enhance physical stability and reduce the risk of falls. More importantly, combined exercise programs regulate immune cell function, remodel the tumor microenvironment, activate metabolic anti-tumor pathways, and optimize the gut microbiota-immune axis, thereby holistically inhibiting tumor progression and producing synergistic effects with immunotherapy. Based on clinical research, this narrative review comprehensively summarizes that scientifically designed individualized exercise programs (such as aerobic training combined with resistance and balance training) possess good feasibility and safety, which can significantly improve patients' physical function, relieve fatigue, and maintain quality of life. Therefore, comprehensively integrating exercise interventions into the comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation system for melanoma, and developing individualized, progressive exercise prescriptions, holds profound practical significance for optimizing patients' long-term survival and health outcomes.

titre: Grade 4 myelosuppression following the first chemotherapy in newly diagnosed lymphomas: results of a prospective study with a long-term follow-up
resume: BACKGROUND: Myelosuppression is a prevalent and potentially serious adverse effect of chemotherapy and patients with solid tumors develop chemotherapy-induced grade 4 myelosuppression and respond favorably to antibody immunotherapy. We hypothesize that newly diagnosed lymphoma patients with grade 4 myelosuppression following the first chemotherapy have different survival results and need other therapies. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Data from 28 patients (2013-2019) were analyzed using Cox proportional hazard models. EORTC QLQ-C30 scores were compared with reference values. RESULTS: The median follow-up was 91.3 months. The median PFS and OS of these patients were 17.8 and 50.5 months, respectively. Sex, age, lymphoma stage, and B symptoms were not significantly associated with survival in these patients. Patients with BM involvement had inferior PFS and OS than those without. Patients with GI involvement had a shorter OS than those without, but the difference in PFS was not significant. The PFS and OS of patients in the TCL group and ABCL group were 61.2 vs. 12.2 months and 113 vs. 12.2 months, respectively. The overall survival rates for 5 years in ABCL and TCL are 33.3% and 70.0%, separately. The GHS/QoL in the population, functioning scores and most symptom scores and symptoms were worse than those of the NHL reference values. CONCLUSION: In newly diagnosed lymphoma patients with grade 4 myelosuppression after first chemotherapy, bone marrow and gastrointestinal involvement were associated with inferior survival in exploratory analyses. ABCL patients had significantly shorter survival than reported, whereas TCL patients had better outcomes. Quality of life was substantially impaired. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, controlled cohorts.

titre: EXPRESS: Dry Eye Disease in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Associated Clinical and Systemic Factors
resume: BACKGROUND: Dry eye disease (DED) has been increasingly reported in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD); however, its frequency and associated clinical factors in this population remain incompletely characterized. PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the frequency of DED and identify factors associated with its presence in patients with IBD who underwent ophthalmological evaluation. STUDY TYPE: Retrospective cross-sectional study. POPULATION: A total of 501 adult patients with confirmed IBD, including 300 with ulcerative colitis and 201 with Crohn disease, were evaluated.Assessment Technique(s) or Outcome(s):DED was defined as a Schirmer test value of ≤5 mm/5 min. Demographic characteristics, disease duration, medical treatments, extraintestinal manifestations, and comorbidities were evaluated. STATISTICAL TESTS: Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test and Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with DED. RESULTS: DED was identified in 76 of 501 patients (15.2%). Multivariable analysis showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.06 per year, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04-1.08), extraintestinal manifestations (aOR 2.46, 95% CI 1.20-5.06), asthma (aOR 3.52, 95% CI 1.62-7.65), and anxiety/depression (aOR 3.09, 95% CI 1.25-7.65) were independently associated with DED. DATA CONCLUSION: DED was identified in approximately 15% of this clinically selected IBD cohort. Older age, extraintestinal manifestations, asthma, and anxiety/depression were independently associated with DED. These findings suggest that ocular surface involvement in IBD may be associated with patient-level factors beyond conventional measures of intestinal disease severity.
revue: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

titre: Defensive reactivity to interoceptive perturbation in panic disorder: Depressive symptom burden and panic severity dimensions
resume: Panic disorder (PD) is characterized by exaggerated defensive responding to panic-related somatic sensations. It remains poorly understood how greater PD and depressive symptom severity are linked to dysregulated defensive functioning and how this manifests during disorder-relevant interoceptive threat. Addressing this question is critical for elucidating pathomechanisms underlying disorder maintenance and the frequent PD-depression comorbidity. We therefore examined how depressive symptom severity and PD severity dimensions uniquely and jointly relate to defensive mobilization during interoceptive perturbation. Eighty-five treatment-seeking patients with a principal diagnosis of PD with/without agoraphobia completed a standardized 3-min hyperventilation (HV) task inducing panic-related body symptoms vs. a non-symptom-provocation control condition. Potentiation of the startle eyeblink response was assessed as a cross-species index of defensive mobilization during the 10-min post-HV phase. Defensive mobilization was modeled as a function of clinician-rated and self-reported PD severity and self-reported depressive symptom severity, complemented by exploratory network analyses of PD dimensions (e.g., avoidance), depressive symptoms, and defensive mobilization. HV reliably induced respiratory perturbation, autonomic activation, and increases in panic symptoms and anxiety. Startle responses remained persistently potentiated following HV vs. the control condition. Greater startle potentiation was associated with higher patient-reported and clinician-rated PD severity and, most strongly, with depressive symptom severity. Network models identified depressive symptoms as a robust correlate of defensive mobilization and interoceptive fear. Depressive symptom burden was uniquely associated with defensive mobilization to interoceptive perturbation beyond PD severity. These findings point to mechanisms linking panic-depression comorbidity to persistent interoceptive threat responding and may inform PD treatment optimization.

titre: Brief Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of effects on depression and anxiety across mental health, physical/medical, and non-clinical populations
resume: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of brief Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), operationalized using modality-specific thresholds (individual: ≤6 sessions/≤6 hours; group: ≤6 weeks/≤12 hours), on depression and anxiety across mental health, physical/medical, and non-clinical populations. Forty-nine RCTs were included in the review. Random-effects models (Hedges' g) were used, with subgroup analyses by control condition and population type. (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024531152). For depression (k = 41), brief ACT showed a moderate overall effect (g = 0.56; I2 = 90.61%), significant versus passive (g = 0.67) but not active controls (g = 0.14). For anxiety (k = 35), a small-to-moderate overall effect emerged (g = 0.42; I2 = 86.22%), significant versus passive (g = 0.53) but not active controls (g = 0.01). For depressive symptoms, significant effects were observed in mental health and physical/medical populations, but not non-clinical populations. For anxiety symptoms, the pooled effect reached significance in non-clinical populations but not mental health or physical/medical populations; tests of between-subgroup differences were non-significant. Brief ACT was associated with reduced depression and anxiety relative to passive controls, but not active interventions, and heterogeneity was substantial. Brief ACT may serve as a viable option in resource-constrained settings.

titre: Impact of Adding Fatigue-Focused Cognitive Behavior Therapy to Supervised Pilates-Based Core Stability Training on Balance and Walking in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: ObjectiveTo investigate the effectiveness of adding cognitive behavioral therapy to supervised Pilates-based core stability training on balance and walking parameters in patients with multiple sclerosis.DesignDouble-blinded randomized controlled trial.SettingOutpatient clinic, Faculty of Physical Therapy, Cairo University.ParticipantsNinety patients with multiple sclerosis aged ≥18 years.InterventionParticipants were randomly allocated to either a study group receiving supervised Pilates-based core stability training combined with cognitive behavioral therapy or a control group receiving supervised Pilates-based core stability training alone for 8 weeks.Main Outcome MeasuresPrimary outcomes were walking parameters and postural stability. Secondary outcomes included quality of life, fatigue, fear of falling, walking capacity, depression, and anxiety.ResultsNinety participants completed the study. Both groups improved significantly after treatment, with greater improvements in the study group. After 8 weeks, the overall stability index decreased from 2.45 ± 0.31 to 1.37 ± 0.24 in the study group and from 2.52 ± 0.24 to 1.95 ± 0.28 in the control group, with a between-group mean difference of -0.59 (95% CI: -0.70 to -0.48; p < .001). Cadence increased from 85.29 ± 8.39 to 96.76 ± 9.98 steps/min in the study group and from 82.22 ± 9.01 to 88.53 ± 8.16 steps/min in the control group, with a between-group mean difference of 8.22 steps/min (95% CI: 4.40 to 12.04; p < .001).ConclusionAdding cognitive behavioral therapy to supervised Pilates-based core stability training improved balance and gait performance more than supervised Pilates-based core stability training alone in patients with multiple sclerosis.

titre: Transdiagnostic effects of medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS): A systematic review and meta-analysis of sham-controlled trials
resume: BACKGROUND: There is a growing body of evidence to support the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) as having a central role in a variety of psychiatric disorders. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been investigated over the mPFC in multiple recent sham-controlled trials. However, no meta-analysis of transdiagnostic symptoms across psychiatric disorders has been undertaken. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD42022354346) examined the transdiagnostic symptoms of rTMS to the mPFC for a number of psychiatric diagnoses. METHODS: The analysis included randomised, sham-controlled trials of rTMS to the mPFC for psychiatric disorders. The key outcomes were change in clinical symptoms, quality of life, and cognition measures from pre- to post- treatment, in symptom domains including depression, anxiety, obsessive compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, craving, and consumption. FINDINGS: We retrieved 3,901 records, 176 were screened at full text, and 30 were included. Seventeen symptom domains and 1,083 participants were analysed. rTMS to the mPFC produced moderate to large effects for obsessive compulsive symptoms, moderate effects for negative symptoms and craving, and small effects for depressive symptoms. Effects for anxiety, cognition, consumption and impulsivity were non-significant. Interpretation was limited by the overall small number of studies, high heterogeneity in findings and some concerns of risk of bias. CONCLUSION: This systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that rTMS over the mPFC may have therapeutic potential for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, and craving, with modest effects for depressive symptoms. Further high-quality, adequately-powered trials are needed to confirm effects and clarify optimal stimulation protocols.

titre: Cognitive Emotion Regulation as a Pathway Between Childhood Adversity and OCD Symptoms
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms has widely been linked to childhood adverse experiences and emotion regulation difficulties. However, cognitive-emotional factors explaining how childhood adversity is associated with OCD symptoms remain underexplored, particularly among young adults in nonclinical settings. AIMS: The present cross-sectional study sought to test the mediating and moderating role of maladaptive and adaptive regulation strategies in the relationship between childhood adversity and obsessive-compulsive symptoms in Turkish college students. METHOD: Participants were 524 undergraduate students (70% female; M = 20.90 years) completed self-report measures assessing adverse childhood experiences, cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and obsessive-compulsive symptoms. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were conducted using the PROCESS macro for SPSS. RESULTS: Findings indicated that childhood adversity was significantly and positively related to maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation strategies and obsessive-compulsive symptoms and negatively associated with adaptive cognitive emotion regulation strategies. Maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation mediated the relationship between childhood adversity and obsessive-compulsive symptoms. In addition to mediating effect of adaptive strategies in this association, the results also showed that adaptive strategies moderated this indirect effect by attenuating the impact of maladaptive regulation. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, findings from the study underscore the importance of cognitive emotion regulation as a key mechanism in the link between childhood adversity and student symptoms. Particularly, strengthening adaptive strategies may reduce the negative effects of childhood adversity. Adaptive strategies may also serve as a protective factor in prevention and intervention efforts for at-risk young adults.
revue: The International journal of social psychiatry

titre: Stool consistency in IBS: a layer-wise multi-omics comparison
resume: Abstract Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is heterogeneous, and taxonomy-based subtyping has limited subject-level predictive value. In the Cell 2020 cohort (75 subjects; 441 Bristol-labelled samples) and an external LC-MS cohort, we compared multiple omics layers for Bristol stool consistency under subject-grouped cross-validation. In the primary measured-Bristol subset (n=235), the NMR metabolome had the highest point-estimate out-of-fold R² (0.247; 95% CI 0.097–0.327; ρ=0.510), but a paired comparison with genus on the measured common subset (n=127) did not establish superiority (ΔR² +0.186; 95% CI −0.010 to 0.404). A five-metabolite panel transferred externally (AUC 0.634), but added only +0.051 over age/sex/BMI (95% CI −0.029 to 0.132). Sample-wise centering increased NMR R² to 0.211–0.215, indicating a contribution from global solute concentration. Two-sample Mendelian randomization found no causal effects of 27 genera. Direct metabolic measurement captures stool consistency, but cross-layer superiority and incremental clinical value remain uncertain.

titre: Real-world adherence to guidelines in acute severe ulcerative colitis: automated assessment using large language models
resume: Background and Aims: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a medical emergency which requires close guideline adherence for optimal outcomes. However, measuring real-world adherence to guidelines and identifying guideline deviations are labor-intensive. We assessed how well a large language model (LLM) based framework can measure real-world adherence to ASUC guidelines and identify reasons for deviations. Methods: The retrospective study focused on clinician adherence to the 2025 American College of Gastroenterology guidelines on ASUC. A multi-agent GPT-5 framework first reviewed inpatient health records to confirm ASUC status. Then for each guideline, it assessed whether it was applicable, recommended by consultants, ordered, or executed. This system was benchmarked against manual chart review. The framework was then applied to all the first seven days of all ASUC hospitalizations in 2019-2024 at UCSF. An additional LLM assessed clinical justification of guideline deviations. Results: The system reliably recognized ASUC hospitalizations (sensitivity: 0.93) and annotated the guideline cascade (overall accuracy: 0.95, N=60). Across 121 hospitalizations (104 patients), adherence was >80%. Deviations concentrated in deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis (DVTp) and timely rescue therapy. Particularly, DVTp broke down at execution despite appropriate recommendation and ordering, whereas "avoidance" recommendations were followed in practice but seldom explicitly documented. Overall, 62% of non-adherence was unjustified, mostly process delays in DVTp. Conclusions: Real-world ASUC care at a tertiary center was largely guideline-concordant, with actionable gaps in DVT prophylaxis execution and rescue therapy timing. A guideline-constrained LLM system enables scalable monitoring of clinical quality and creates the potential in simultaneously improving clinical care and guidelines.

titre: Hierarchical Bayesian models of cardiac interoception in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders with the Heart Rate Discrimination task
resume: BackgroundPerception of external (exteroceptive) and internal (interoceptive) sensory information is critical for a coherent sense of self, others, and the world. Perception depends on the accuracy and precision of sensory beliefs. Predictive processing models propose that altered sensory beliefs contribute to schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (SZ). However, exteroception and interoception are commonly assessed with separate paradigmatic and analysis schemes. We use a Heart Rate Discrimination (HRD) paradigm and Bayesian modeling to assess perceptual accuracy and precision during exteroceptive and interoceptive processing in SZ, and test associations with clinical variables. Methods SZ (N=41) and healthy comparison (HC; N=44) participants completed the HRD and the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness; SZ additionally completed the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale. Hierarchical Bayesian models estimated threshold (bias) and slope (precision), with Bayes factors assessing group difference credibility. ResultsParticipants were less biased and more precise during exteroceptive trials, without evidence of credible group differences in bias. SZ participants had less precise perceptual beliefs overall (BF10=6.74) with no credible group-by-condition interaction. Across all participants, higher interoceptive bias was associated with greater Not-Distracting of internal bodily signals (r=.21, 95% CrI [0.005, 0.41]), and lower interoceptive precision was associated with greater self-reported Body Listening (r=.40, 95% CrI [.08, .67]). Among SZ, lower interoceptive bias was associated with greater positive symptom severity (r=−.29, 95% CrI [−.54, −.01]).Conclusions Sensory beliefs are less precise in SZ. Further, biased interoceptive beliefs relate to psychotic symptoms and subjective bodily awareness. Interventions increasing precision and reducing bias of sensory beliefs may improve psychosis.

titre: Motherly Plus: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Smartphone-Assisted Single-Session Psychotherapy Intervention for Postpartum Depression
resume: Introduction: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a public health problem, affecting approximately 17% of women worldwide. PPD is associated with significant costs to the healthcare system and impairments for the child. Although evidence shows that psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy are effective in reducing PPD symptoms, access to these treatments is limited, especially in low- and middle-income countries where there is a shortage of professionals and unequal distribution of mental health services. In this context, telehealth, smartphone apps, and brief psychotherapies emerge as viable, low-cost, and potentially scalable alternatives. However, gaps remain regarding the efficacy of single-session psychotherapies for PPD, especially when combined with digital support. Objectives: The primary objective is to test the efficacy of an intervention package combining single-session psychotherapy with subsequent self-guided use of a smartphone app for the treatment of PPD. Secondary objectives are to investigate moderators, mediators, and specific intervention processes. Method: A randomized clinical trial in which 104 women aged 18-40 years, up to 12 months postpartum, with a diagnosis of PPD will be randomized to the intervention (single-session psychotherapy supported by the Motherly app) or a waitlist. Participants in the intervention arm will retain access to the app throughout the study; waitlist participants will receive the intervention after post-treatment assessment. Assessments will occur at T1 (week 1, baseline), T2 (week 2, mid-treatment), T3 (week 4, post-treatment), and T4 (week 8, follow-up). The primary outcome will be depression assessed by the QIDS-C16 at T3. Secondary outcomes include anxiety, sleep, parental stress, and self-reported depression. Data will be analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE) models considering an intention-to-treat (ITT) perspective. Mediation models will be used to analyze mediators, while interaction models will be used to explore potential moderators. Regression models will be used to analyze the association between specific processes (therapeutic alliance and app engagement) and clinical outcomes. Perspectives: This study has potential public health relevance and innovation by testing an intervention package that combines single-session psychotherapy and technology, with high potential for scalability. Trial registration: clinicaltrials.gov NCT07925762 Key words: Postpartum depression; clinical trial; cognitive-behavior therapy; digital intervention; smartphone app; single session psychotherapy

titre: Effects of Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy on Obsessive- Compulsive Symptoms and Associated Metacognitive Processes in Contamination OCD: A Single-Case Experimental Study
resume: Abstract Thought–action fusion (TAF) and diminished memory confidence are core metacognitive mechanisms that maintain contamination-related obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and can impede inhibitory learning during exposure-based treatment. Although exposure and response prevention (ERP) remains the gold-standard intervention, practical, motivational, and logistical barriers frequently limit its delivery. Virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) offers a controllable, office-based, and potentially more acceptable alternative, yet its capacity to modify these specific cognitive processes has rarely been examined with experimental rigor. This concurrent multiple-baseline single-case experimental study evaluated a theory-driven, eight-session VRET protocol in three adult women with DSM-5 contamination OCD. Graded 360-degree real-world kitchen and bathroom environments were combined with active behavioral tasks, multisensory cues, in-session cognitive restructuring of TAF beliefs, and strict response prevention. Outcomes included the Thought–Action Fusion Scale, a computerized recognition-based memory-confidence task, washing frequency, reassurance-seeking, and clinician-rated OCD severity (Y-BOCS). Visual inspection, percentage of non-overlapping data, reliable-change indices, and percentage improvement demonstrated immediate, substantial, and clinically meaningful reductions in washing and reassurance-seeking that were maintained at one-month follow-up (post-treatment improvement 53–80%). Changes in TAF were heterogeneous yet clinically notable in one participant; memory-confidence gains were more limited. The protocol was highly acceptable, with full completion and no adverse events. Findings provide preliminary experimental evidence that a carefully designed VRET protocol can produce robust behavioral change and feasible targeting of TAF within an ERP framework. The results highlight both the promise of mechanism-focused virtual exposure for contamination OCD and the need for larger controlled trials to optimize metacognitive outcomes and establish generalizability.

titre: Health-related quality of life among patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Ethiopia: evidence from a tertiary hospital in sub-Saharan Africa
resume: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory condition affecting the gastrointestinal tract, primarily comprising Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC). IBD can significantly impair patients’ health related quality of life (HRQoL). Although health-related quality of life in IBD has been widely studied in developed countries, evidence from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly Ethiopia, remains scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to assess HRQoL and its associated factors among patients with IBD in Ethiopia. A cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2022 to August 2022 among 84 patients with IBD who were receiving follow-up care at St. Paul Hospital Millennium Medical College. Data were collected from medical records and through patient interviews using the Short Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire (SIBDQ). Descriptive statistics were presented as frequencies, medians, and means ± standard deviation (SD). Variables with a P-value < 0.20 in the bivariate analysis were included in the multivariable logistic regression analysis. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Of the 84 patients included in the final analysis, 69% were female. The mean age of the participants was 31.06 ± 10.7 years. Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis accounted for 62 (73.8%) and 22 (26.2%) patients, respectively. Impaired health-related quality of life (HRQoL) was observed in 68 patients (81%). Active disease (AOR: 9.8; 95% CI: 1.17-82; P = 0.03) and the presence of extra-intestinal manifestations (AOR:8.8; 95% CI:1.05-74; P = 0.04) were significantly associated with impaired HRQoL. The majority of patients with IBD in our Ethiopian study population had impaired health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Active disease and the presence of extraintestinal manifestations were significantly associated with impaired HRQoL. Because HRQoL extends beyond bowel symptoms, holistic care is particularly important for patients with active disease and extraintestinal manifestations.

titre: The effect of treatment by biological agents on quality of life and psychological outcomes in patients with Crohn's disease
resume: This prospective study aimed to evaluate changes in disease-specific and general health-related quality of life, fatigue, depression, and anxiety among adults with Crohn's disease before and after at least six months of treatment with biological agents. A total of 97 adult individuals with CD were prospectively recruited between May 2024 and August 2025. These participants underwent treatment with biological agents, which included infliximab, adalimumab, ustekinumab, or vedolizumab. Standardized measures for HRQoL and psychological outcomes were gathered. To evaluate these outcomes, a variety of tools were utilized, including the Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire (IBDQ), Crohn's Symptom Severity (CSS), the 36-item Short Form Survey (SF-36), EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L), Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). These assessments were conducted both before treatment and after at least six months of therapy. Statistical analyses employed paired sample t-tests and non-parametric methods, with statistical significance determined at P < 0.05. The cohort had a mean age of 26.34 years, predominantly male (81.44%), and mainly presented with mild disease (67.01%). Significant improvements were observed in disease-specific HRQoL, with the IBDQ total score increasing from 95.36 ± 13.81 pre-treatment to 122.80 ± 17.80 post-treatment (P < 0.001). Disease severity, as measured by the CSS, decreased significantly from 47.38 ± 5.84 to 38.21 ± 6.67 (P < 0.001). General HRQoL also showed substantial improvement, with SF-36 PCS and MCS scores increasing by 5.00 points (P < 0.001 for both), and the EQ-5D-5L VAS score improving by 11.33 points (P < 0.001). Fatigue, measured by FACIT-F, improved significantly by 9.18 points (P < 0.001). Psychological outcomes also showed notable improvement, with the PHQ-9 score decreasing from 14.28 ± 3.66 to 6.32 ± 4.39 (P < 0.001) and the GAD-7 score decreasing from 12.20 ± 3.15 to 7.22 ± 3.54 (P < 0.001). Biological therapy in individuals with CD was associated with improvements in disease-specific and general HRQoL and reductions in symptom severity, fatigue, depression, and anxiety. These findings support the value of incorporating patient-reported quality-of-life and psychological assessments into biologic-treatment follow-up and comprehensive CD care.

titre: Systems biology of gut microbiome dysbiosis in major depressive disorder: functional microbial modules associated with inflammation, illness severity, recurrence, and suicidal behavior
resume: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by disruptions in neuroimmune, metabolic, and oxidative stress (NIMETOX) pathways, potentially influenced by leaky gut. Most MDD microbiome studies have focused on taxonomic differences rather than systems-biology analyses. This cross-sectional study included 102 MDD inpatients and 38 healthy controls. Gut microbiome composition was assessed using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Taxonomic differences were examined using ANCOM-BC and machine-learning approaches. Functional potential was inferred using Tax4Fun and PICRUSt, and selected genera were grouped into biologically annotated modules. Beta diversity differed significantly between groups, with selective genus- and species-level differences. Feature selection identified nine modules that discriminated MDD from controls. MDD showed higher abundance-based scores for modules representing putative proinflammatory dysbiosis, LPS-related host–microbial interactions, oral pathobionts, and Actinobacteria-associated host–metabolite transformation, and lower lactobacilli and lactate cross-feeding scores. Selected genera explained substantial in-sample variance in overall depressive symptom severity (75.7%), physiosomatic symptoms (64.8%), suicidal ideation (27.2%), and recurrence of illness (36.7%). The acute-phase inflammatory response (based on measurements of monomeric C-reactive protein, albumin and transferrin) was associated with modules comprising genera previously linked to endotoxin exposure and mucosal immunity. Inferred MDD microbiome profiles showed greater predicted representation of microbial stress-response, host–microbial interaction, and biofilm-formation pathways. MDD is associated with selective taxonomic differences and altered inferred functional potential of the gut microbiome. Abundance-based modules enriched in genera previously associated with inflammatory signaling and barrier dysfunction collectively define systems-biology-informed individualized dysbiosis profiles.

titre: Depression, sleep disturbance, and negative life events as nonlinear risk factors for irritable bowel syndrome in Chinese adolescents: an interpretable machine-learning analysis
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder of gut–brain interaction that often begins in adolescence, yet tools to identify affected adolescents are lacking. We developed and internally validated an interpretable diagnostic machine-learning model for adolescent IBS and characterised nonlinear exposure–outcome relationships. In this school-based cross-sectional study, 2269 students aged 11–19 years in Yantai, China, were assessed with the Rome IV self-report questionnaire and validated instruments for anxiety, depression, negative life events, academic stress and sleep quality, plus diet and sociodemographic factors. Because predictors and outcome were concurrent, the model is diagnostic, not prognostic. Predictors were selected by penalised (LASSO) regression; seven algorithms were trained on 80% of the data with class weighting and evaluated on validation and test sets (10% each). The final model was interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and restricted cubic splines characterised nonlinearity. IBS prevalence was 21.7% (493/2269). Discrimination was similar across the seven algorithms (test area under the curve 0.791–0.816; no significant pairwise difference). XGBoost, pre-specified before the test set was examined, achieved an area under the curve of 0.808 (95% CI 0.730–0.879) in the test set (227 participants, 49 events), with positive predictive value 0.437 (0.337–0.542) and negative predictive value 0.921 (0.874–0.963); optimism-corrected bootstrap discrimination was 0.756. Depression and sleep quality were the largest SHAP contributors, then anxiety and life events. In the multivariable model, family history of gastrointestinal disease (adjusted odds ratio 3.06, 95% CI 2.09–4.47), poorer sleep (per SD 1.36) and depression (per SD 1.28) were associated with IBS. Associations with all five psychosocial exposures were nonlinear (all P for nonlinearity < 0.01), the curves flattening at higher exposure, although change points were imprecisely estimated and the plateau may partly reflect instrument ceiling effects. An interpretable diagnostic model based on routinely collectable psychosocial and behavioural information distinguished adolescents with and without Rome IV-defined IBS, and its associations with depression, sleep disturbance and negative life events were nonlinear rather than uniformly graded. The model has internal validation only, from a single district and survey wave; findings are hypothesis-generating and require external, preferably multicentre, validation before use.
