titre: Editorial: Precision medicine and targeted therapies in gastrointestinal and genitourinary solid tumors
resume: The management of gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) malignancies is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Advances in comprehensive genomic profiling, molecular diagnostics, immune characterization, and biomarker-guided drug development have shifted treatment from predominantly histology-and stage-based approaches toward increasingly individualized strategies (1). In GI cancers, contemporary practice incorporates actionable biomarkers such as HER2, PD-L1, mismatch-repair/microsatellite-instability status, and CLDN18.2, while broad next-generation sequencing is increasingly used to identify additional targetable alterations and pan-tumor biomarkers (2)(3)(4)(5)(6). Recent ASCO guidance further emphasizes obtaining predictive biomarker results early enough to inform treatment selection in advanced gastroesophageal cancers (4). In GU malignancies, genomic profiling is similarly becoming integral to treatment selection.Precision oncology is also becoming increasingly dynamic. Circulating tumor DNA and other liquid-biopsy approaches provide minimally invasive opportunities for genomic profiling and treatment selection, as well as response assessment, detection of emerging resistance, and longitudinal disease monitoring (7)(8). Repeat molecular testing may be particularly valuable when tumors evolve under therapeutic pressure or when initial tissue testing is negative or uninformative (9)(10). Integration of genomic, transcriptomic, immune, and other multi-omic data may further improve characterization of tumor heterogeneity and enable adaptive treatment strategies (11). Against this rapidly evolving background, the Research Topic "Precision Medicine and Targeted Therapies in Gastrointestinal and Genitourinary Solid Tumors" brings together 39 articles spanning molecular biomarkers, targeted therapies, immunotherapy, treatment optimization, real-world evidence, and translational technologies. Together, these contributions illustrate the shift from single-biomarker treatment matching to multidimensional, adaptive precision oncology.The articles can broadly be organized into six interconnected themes: molecular profiling and biomarker-driven patient stratification; actionable molecular targets and targeted therapies; immunotherapy and tumor immunity; treatment response, resistance and therapeutic optimization; rare clinical cases and real-world evidence; and emerging technologies and translational frontiers in precision oncology. Myosteatosis independently increased the risk of treatment-related adverse events (OR=7.64), whereas a higher cachexia index was protective. Low-attenuation muscle area relative to total skeletal muscle independently predicted dose-limiting toxicity. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were also associated with significantly worse disease-free survival, together with high-risk disease and KIT mutation status. These findings suggest that CTderived body-composition measures may complement molecular and clinicopathological factors to identify patients requiring closer monitoring, nutritional or exercise interventions, and more individualized imatinib management.The identification of actionable molecular vulnerabilities remains one of the foundations of precision oncology. The fourteen studies in this Research Topic highlight established and emerging targets, RNA-based strategies, antibody-drug conjugates, kinase inhibitors, and DNA-repair-directed therapies, underscoring both the expanding therapeutic landscape and the challenge of translating molecular discoveries into durable clinical benefit. El-Ghazzi et al. reviewed oligonucleotide-based gene-silencing strategies in GI and GU malignancies, focusing on antisense oligonucleotides, small siRNAs, and miRNAs. These approaches offer high sequence specificity and the potential to suppress previously 'undruggable' cancer drivers. The authors also highlighted major barriers to clinical translation, including nuclease degradation, poor cellular uptake, off-target effects, and delivery limitations. Advances in chemical modifications, lipid nanoparticles, and GalNAcbased delivery systems are beginning to address these challenges. Overall, the review underscores gene silencing as an emerging precision-oncology strategy capable of expanding the range of therapeutically actionable molecular targets. and CAR-T cell approaches. They also highlighted tumor heterogeneity and the complex microenvironment as major contributors to resistance and treatment failure. Overall, the review illustrates how HER2-targeted therapy is progressing from conventional receptor blockade toward increasingly diverse and multimodal precision strategies, while emphasizing the need to overcome spatial heterogeneity and acquired resistance to achieve durable benefit. Wang et al. reported a rare DCTN1-ALK fusion in gastric cancer and described a clinically meaningful response to ALK-targeted therapy. Although ALK rearrangements are uncommon in gastric malignancies, comprehensive genomic profiling identified an actionable fusion that enabled treatment with an ALK inhibitor beyond conventional histology-based options.The case illustrates the value of broad molecular testing in advanced tumors, particularly when standard therapies are limited, and supports a histology-agnostic approach to selected oncogenic drivers. More broadly, it highlights how rare genomic alterations can uncover therapeutic opportunities and generate evidence for precision treatment in uncommon molecular subsets. The emergence of immune-checkpoint blockade has reshaped treatment across multiple GI and GU malignancies. However, therapeutic benefit remains highly heterogeneous, and increasing attention is being directed toward understanding the immune microenvironment that determines sensitivity or resistance.Guo et al. evaluated neoadjuvant sintilimab combined with nab-paclitaxel and cisplatin in 29 patients with resectable stage II-III esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma. Twenty-one patients underwent surgery, with a pathological complete-response rate of 28.6% and a major pathological-response rate of 42.9%. Radiographic assessment showed the objective response rate and disease control rate were 70.8% and 100%, respectively. All surgical patients achieved R0 resection, with no treatment-related surgical delays. Although hematologic toxicities were common, the regimen was generally manageable, supporting further evaluation of chemoimmunotherapy as a neoadjuvant strategy in resectable ESCC. Higher infiltration of Pygo2+ CD8+ T cells also correlated with inferior response to immunecheckpoint therapy. These findings identify Pygo2+ T cells as potential prognostic and predictive biomarkers and suggest Pygo2 as a candidate therapeutic target in gastric cancer. Nonaka et al. reported a 64-year-old patient with microsatellite-stable, HER2-negative gastric cancer with a solitary liver metastasis and bulky regional lymph-node disease who received four cycles of SOX and nivolumab. Marked tumor regression enabled distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and partial hepatectomy, and pathological examination demonstrated complete response at the primary, nodal, and hepatic sites.Notably, the tumor was MSS and tumor mutational burden was low yet showed relatively high PD-L1 expression and CD8+ T-cell infiltration. This exceptional response highlights the limitations of relying on MSI status alone and suggests that broader immune-context biomarkers may better identify patients likely to benefit from checkpoint inhibition. Polito et al. described a 67-year-old woman with stage IV clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (RCC) and pulmonary, nodal, and peritoneal metastases who achieved durable disease control with first-line pembrolizumab plus axitinib. After ~32 months of systemic therapy, sustained tumor regression enabled robot-assisted nephrectomy, and histological examination showed a complete pathological response with no viable tumor.Pembrolizumab was continued postoperatively, and the patient remained in radiological near-complete response with a progression-free survival of ~41 months. This case highlights the potential of ICI-TKI combinations to induce deep responses and supports individualized consideration of consolidative nephrectomy after prolonged systemic control.response in 41 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. At 3 weeks after treatment, higher proportions of CD4+ T cells and NK cells independently predicted objective response. Their combined assessment further improved stratification: all patients with high levels of both cell populations achieved an objective response, whereas none in the low-low group did. Higher week-3 CD4+ T-cell and NK-cell proportions were also associated with longer progression-free and overall survival. These findings support peripheral immune-cell profiling as a minimally invasive approach for early assessment of immunotherapy efficacy and prognosis in advanced HCC.Zhang et al. evaluated HLA-G expression in 523 gastric cancer lesions and 283 matched peritumoral tissues. HLA-G positivity was significantly higher in peritumoral tissues than in tumor lesions (84.1% vs. 70.7%). Importantly, HLA-G expression in peritumoral tissues was associated with shorter overall survival (42.0 vs. 56.7 months), whereas HLA-G expression within the tumor itself was not prognostic. Multiplex analyses further identified fundic gland mucous neck cells as the HLA-G-expressing population. These findings highlight the prognostic importance of the peritumoral immune-regulatory environment and suggest that HLA-G expression outside the tumor may contribute to gastric cancer progression and immune escape.Identifying an active therapy represents only one component of precision oncology. Longterm benefit depends on how treatment is sequenced, continued, modified, and adapted in response to toxicity, resistance, recurrence, and evolving disease biology.GISTs following radical resection. Five-year relapse-free survival was higher in patients treated for more than 3 years than in those treated for 3 years or less (84% vs. 74%), although overall survival did not differ significantly. Importantly, treatment duration was not an independent predictor of outcome in multivariable analysis (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.15-1.83). The study therefore suggests that extending adjuvant imatinib beyond 3 years should not be routinely recommended without further prospective validation and highlights the need for individualized treatment-duration strategies. Bu et al. described the first reported case of hypouricemia associated with adjuvant imatinib in a 48-year-old woman with small intestinal GIST harboring a KIT exon 11 mutation. Serum uric acid progressively declined after initiation of imatinib, reaching 96 μmol/L, and subsequently normalized after treatment discontinuation, while liver and renal function remained preserved. A Naranjo score of 6 supported a probable drug-related association.Although based on a single case, this observation expands the recognized toxicity profile of imatinib and highlights the value of longitudinal laboratory monitoring and pharmacovigilance during prolonged targeted therapy. Hou et al. reported a 64-year-old man with jejunal GIST who developed bifocal hepatic metastases 15 years after primary tumor resection. The patient had received only 1 year of adjuvant imatinib and remained disease-free for the following 14 years. Two liver lesions were detected incidentally and successfully removed by partial hepatectomy with R0 resection; pathology confirmed metastatic GIST. At 6-month follow-up, no recurrence was observed. This unusual ultra-late relapse highlights the potential for prolonged tumor dormancy in GIST and supports extended surveillance, particularly in patients who received limited adjuvant tyrosine-kinase inhibitor therapy.Han et al. reviewed current evidence for maintenance therapy in advanced gastric cancer, where the goal is to prolong disease control while limiting cumulative toxicity and preserving quality of life. Across the available studies, maintenance approaches included fluoropyrimidines, targeted agents, immune-checkpoint inhibitors, and combination strategies, with capecitabine, S-1, bevacizumab, and avelumab among the most frequently evaluated agents. The review also highlighted emerging biomarkers, including hemoglobin levels, PD-L1 combined positive score, tumor-microenvironment features, angiogenesisrelated status, and CXCL12. Overall, the authors support biomarker-guided maintenance strategies as a promising approach that requires further prospective validation. Chen et al. performed a meta-analysis of 10 randomized controlled trials involving 7,927 patients with colorectal cancer to evaluate infection risk associated with anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies. High-grade infections occurred in 15.8% of patients receiving cetuximab or panitumumab compared with 10.2% in control groups, corresponding to a 49% increased risk (RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.23-1.82). In contrast, the increase in febrile neutropenia was not statistically significant. These findings highlight infection as an important safety consideration during EGFR-targeted therapy and support closer monitoring and preventive management in patients receiving these agents.Cisek et al. evaluated high-dose-rate interstitial brachytherapy in 270 patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases treated between 2015 and 2022. Median progressionfree survival was 10 months and median overall survival was 17 months, with a diseasecontrol rate of 85% and an objective-response rate of 35%. Prognosis was influenced by treatment intent, response, radiation dose, extrahepatic metastases, and tumor grade.Treatment-related toxicity was low, with injection-site pain being the most common adverse event. These findings support brachytherapy as a safe local-treatment option, particularly for patients with limited liver metastases who are not candidates for surgery or stereotactic radiotherapy.Tasaki et al. investigated baseline eosinophil levels as predictors of apalutamide-induced skin-related adverse events in Japanese patients with prostate cancer. Among 109 treated patients, those who developed skin toxicity had significantly higher baseline eosinophil proportions than those without toxicity (4.3% vs. 2.1%). An eosinophil proportion of ≥1.8% predicted skin-related adverse events with an AUC of 0.768 and was independently associated with approximately a 13-fold increased risk (OR 13.3, 95% CI 3.82-46.4). These findings suggest that pretreatment eosinophil proportion may provide a simple biomarker for identifying patients who require closer monitoring during apalutamide therapy.Finally, Diao et al. described a 65-year-old patient with metastatic alpha-fetoproteinproducing gastric cancer showing marked spatiotemporal HER2 heterogeneity. The primary tumor was initially HER2 1+ without ERBB2 amplification, but after 27 months of apatinib plus PD-1 inhibition, a progressing cervical lymph-node metastasis converted to HER2 3+ with ERBB2 amplification. Third-line treatment with the anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugate DP303c produced a rapid partial response and normalization of AFP, with overall survival reaching 79 months. This case highlights the importance of repeat biopsy at progression and demonstrates how dynamic biomarker reassessment can uncover new therapeutic opportunities during disease evolution. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of rare anal gland tumors and underscores the importance of comprehensive pathological evaluation when unusual immunophenotypic profiles could otherwise lead to misclassification. He et al. reported a 63-year-old patient with advanced rectal adenocarcinoma who developed both duodenal and cutaneous metastases, two uncommon sites of spread. After progression following CAPEOX plus bevacizumab, cutaneous biopsy confirmed metastatic rectal cancer with the same NRAS exon 2 mutation identified in the primary tumor. Because of poor performance status and limited tolerance for further chemotherapy, fruquintinib was initiated. Within seven days, the cutaneous lesions showed marked regression and CA 19-9 levels decreased, with no significant treatment-related toxicity observed. This case highlights the potential value of fruquintinib in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer with rare metastatic presentations.Li et al. reported a 58-year-old patient with high-risk GIST accompanied by marked secondary thrombocytosis, with a platelet count of 909 × 10^9/L. Pathology confirmed GIST, and molecular testing identified a rare KIT exon 13 mutation. Following tumor resection and adjuvant imatinib, platelet counts progressively normalized to 299 × 10^9/L within 3 months, while postoperative IL-6 levels also declined substantially. These findings support a tumorassociated mechanism for the thrombocytosis and suggest that platelet dynamics may reflect disease burden. The case also underscores the importance of molecular profiling in guiding therapy for uncommon GIST subtypes.The final group of contributions highlights the technological and experimental infrastructure required to advance precision oncology beyond current therapeutic paradigms. Tu et al. reviewed emerging strategies for preventing Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric cancer, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence-assisted vaccine development.Given the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and strain diversity, the authors highlighted the limitations of conventional eradication approaches and proposed AI-guided antigen selection and multiepitope vaccine design as potential precision-prevention strategies. They also discussed host immunity, immune evasion, and current vaccine- Several broader lessons emerge from this Research Topic. Precision oncology is becoming increasingly multidimensional, integrating molecular alterations with immune features, circulating biomarkers, host characteristics, and treatment tolerance. Biomarkers should also be viewed as dynamic, as illustrated by temporal changes in HER2 expression that may require repeated molecular assessment. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy are becoming increasingly interconnected, while treatment timing, sequencing, and combination strategies are gaining importance alongside drug selection. Finally, the collection highlights the complementary value of clinical trials, translational studies, realworld evidence, and case reports, particularly for rare molecular subsets.Despite rapid progress, tumor heterogeneity, acquired resistance, and limited biomarker validation continue to constrain precision oncology in GI and GU cancers. Dynamic HER2 expression in gastric cancer, TKI resistance in GIST, and evolving molecular profiles in renal-cell carcinoma illustrate the need for longitudinal monitoring. Future efforts should prioritize serial tissue and liquid biopsies, biomarker-guided adaptive therapy, rational treatment combinations, and earlier molecular profiling. Integration of multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and real-world data may further improve patient selection and resistance prediction, while scalable and cost-effective assays will be essential for broader clinical implementation.The studies in this Research Topic illustrate the transition from single-target approaches toward integrated and adaptive precision oncology. Effective personalization increasingly requires consideration of genomic alterations, tumor heterogeneity, immune state, host factors, treatment toxicity, and molecular changes arising during therapy. Future progress will depend on integrating these dynamic biological signals into clinically actionable strategies through multidisciplinary collaboration. Collectively, these contributions reinforce that optimal cancer treatment should be guided not only by tumor location or a single biomarker, but by the evolving biological context of each patient's disease.

titre: Baseline Physical Capacity and Psychosocial Changes During Structured Walking in Patients with Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Post Hoc Analysis of the Single-Arm StepFit-18K Trial
resume: Background/Objectives: It is unknown whether baseline physical capacity is associated with changes during a walking program in patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D). In this post hoc, exploratory analysis, we examined whether baseline Global Physical Capacity Score (GPCS) strata were associated with gastrointestinal and psychosocial changes. Methods: We analyzed 98 completers of the single-arm StepFit-18K trial, classified by baseline IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS) score (≥75, primary; <75, inactive comparison), and, post hoc, divided at the median GPCS into high-capacity (HC) and low-capacity (LC) strata. Mixed-design analysis of variance with false discovery rate (FDR) correction was used. Results: In the primary cohort (32 HC, 27 LC), IBS-SSS decreased in both strata (interaction p = 0.73). 36-Item Short Form Health Survey Social Functioning showed a nominal interaction (p = 0.016; FDR q = 0.16), with a baseline-adjusted difference between strata of 6.2 points (95% confidence interval −4.2 to 16.6). No other outcome had a significant interaction after FDR correction. Conclusions: Following the 12-week program, IBS-SSS decreased to comparable magnitudes irrespective of baseline GPCS stratum in this single-arm cohort. The nominal Social Functioning divergence was consistent with regression to the mean. The cutoff was post hoc, the GPCS is unvalidated, and subgroups were small; findings are hypothesis-generating.

titre: Comparative Effects of Mindful Yoga and Expressive Arts on Perceived Stress and Whole-Person Health in Individuals With Mild-to-Moderate Parkinson Disease: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: Background People with Parkinson disease (PD) experience substantial motor, nonmotor, and psychosocial burdens that are often inadequately addressed by pharmacological treatments alone. Mind-body interventions (MBIs), including mindful yoga and expressive arts therapy (EXAT), have shown promise in alleviating stress, increasing quality of life, and improving whole-person health. However, evidence of their comparative effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remains limited, leaving clinicians and patients with little guidance when selecting between these interventions. This study aims to fill this gap. Objective This trial aims to compare the effectiveness of mindful yoga and EXAT in reducing perceived stress, increasing quality of life, and improving whole-person health in people with PD. A secondary aim is to examine potential mechanisms of action, including functional, psychosocial, and gut microbiome–related pathways. Methods We are conducting a 2-arm, parallel-group, active-comparator randomized controlled trial. People with PD are randomly assigned to receive either mindful yoga or EXAT, delivered in six 90-minute sessions every 2 weeks. The primary outcomes are perceived stress and PD-related quality of life. Secondary outcomes include PD-related symptoms and broader quality of life. Potential mediators will cover biopsychosocial domains, including biological and physical factors (gut microbiota, constipation severity and bowel habits, and physical activity) and psychosocial factors (self-compassion, self-efficacy, and perceived social support). Motor assessments are conducted using Mon4t and BooGuu Aspire Fall Risk Management mobile apps. Fecal samples are collected to generate reproducible taxonomic and functional profiles of the gut microbiota. Outcomes are assessed at baseline and 3 months, 9 months, and 12 months after baseline assessment. Comparative effectiveness will be evaluated using linear mixed models, and potential mechanisms, including psychosocial and microbiome features, will be examined through path analysis. We hypothesize that both interventions will reduce stress, increase quality of life, and improve whole-person health, but they will demonstrate different pathways across biopsychosocial domains. Results This study was funded in April 2023, and ethics approval was granted in May 2024. Participant recruitment and data collection began in May 2024 and are ongoing. As of the submission of the manuscript, 144 participants had finished pre- and postintervention assessments (72 in each arm). Final follow-ups are still ongoing. Data analysis has not yet started, and primary findings are expected to be published in December 2026. Conclusions By directly comparing 2 active MBIs and integrating biopsychosocial-spiritual domains, this trial will provide comparative evidence on the effectiveness of MBIs. The findings are intended to guide the selection of mind-body approaches in PD, supporting preference-sensitive, whole-person care and informing integrative models that address the complex needs of this population.

titre: Constipation as an under-recognized symptom burden in peritoneal dialysis patients: a systematic review
resume: Background: Constipation and bowel dysfunction are clinically relevant concerns in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD), but reported prevalence varies because of differences in definitions, assessment methods, and study populations. Aim: To synthesize evidence on constipation and bowel dysfunction in adults receiving PD, including prevalence, assessment, symptom burden, quality of life, clinical outcomes, and management interventions. Methodology: A systematic review with narrative synthesis was conducted with PRISMA 2020 used as the reporting framework. Primary quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies providing directly extractable constipation- or bowel-function-specific PD data were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Results: Twenty-eight primary empirical studies published between 2002 and 2026 were included. All included studies used quantitative observational or interventional designs; no eligible qualitative or mixed-methods studies were identified. Reported constipation prevalence ranged from 13% to 77.4%. Observational studies associated constipation and gastrointestinal symptom burden with poorer quality of life, while prospective evidence identified associations with clinically relevant outcomes, including peritonitis. Interventional studies evaluated dietary, pharmacological, prebiotic, probiotic, synbiotic, and other approaches, with improvements in selected outcomes; however, heterogeneity precluded conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness. Conclusion: Constipation and bowel dysfunction are clinically relevant in PD. Standardized multidimensional assessment and individualized management are warranted, while adequately powered prospective and randomized studies using consistent outcomes and patient-reported measures are needed.
revue: Review of Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetics - International Edition

titre: The optimal time for removing the urinary catheter after laparoscopic surgery for patients with benign gynecological diseases
resume: This study aims to determine the optimal timing for urinary catheters removal in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery for benign gynecological diseases, to promote postoperative recovery. In this study, a total of 120 patients were randomly assigned to an experimental group ( n = 60) and a control group ( n = 60). Catheter removal occurred 4 h post-surgery in the experimental group, while the control group followed the traditional 24-hour removal protocol. Clinical symptoms, the incidence of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections (CAUTI), and average hospital stays were evaluated. The incidence of urethral irritation (8.33% vs. 16.67%) and UTI (5.00% vs. 13.33%) was numerically lower in the experimental group than in the control group, but neither difference was statistically significant ( P = 0.294 and P = 0.514, respectively).Nausea and vomiting also showed a downward trend, again without significant between-group differences ( P > 0.05). Additionally, the success rate of first urination was higher in the experimental group. Time to first postoperative urination was significantly shorter in the experimental group ( P 0.05). The experimental group also demonstrated shorter times for anal exhaust and first bowel movement ( P 0.05), but it accelerated urination and gastrointestinal recovery, promoted early ambulation, shortened hospitalization, and improved psychological status and quality of life; larger trials are needed to confirm the effect on UTI.

titre: Tetrapeptide selective μ1-opioid receptor agonists – the missing link in the treatment of chronic pain in oncology?
resume: Chronic pain syndrome remains one of the major unresolved problems in oncology: some patients continue to experience breakthrough pain, insufficient response to therapy, opioid-related adverse effects, reduced treatment adherence, tolerance, and opioid phobia. In this context, new analgesics with high efficacy and a more favorable safety profile are of particular interest. Taphalgin, a domestic tetrapeptide selective μ1-opioid receptor agonist, differs from classical opioids by lacking interaction with μ2-receptors, which may reduce the risk of adverse effects such as respiratory depression, impaired gastrointestinal motility, euphoria, and miosis. In phase II and III clinical trials, as well as in individual clinical observations, the drug demonstrated a pronounced analgesic effect in chronic cancer pain, comparable to that of morphine, with a lower incidence of adverse events and the possibility of long-term use without signs of significant tolerance or dependence. Selective peptide opioid receptor agonists may be regarded as a promising direction in the treatment of chronic pain in oncology, especially in cases of intolerance, insufficient efficacy, or limitations associated with the use of traditional opioid analgesics. Aim. To analyze the challenges in managing chronic pain syndrome in cancer patients and to evaluate the prospects of using selective tetrapeptide agonists of μ1-opioid receptors, using tafalgin as an example, taking into account its pharmacological features, clinical trial results, and real-world clinical practice experience.

titre: O papel do enfermeiro no aleitamento materno e prevenção do desmame precoce
resume: Breastfeeding is fundamental to the health of the child and the woman, as it provides nutrients and immunological substances, strengthens the emotional bond and reduces the risk of infections and respiratory and gastrointestinal diseases. Despite its proven benefits, early weaning is still a challenge in Brazil, especially because the prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding is below the target recommended by the World Health Organization. The study aimed to analyze the scientific evidence on the role of nursing in the face of the difficulties faced by mothers during breastfeeding and the factors associated with the early interruption of breastfeeding. This is a bibliographic study with a qualitative approach and a descriptive nature, carried out in the SciELO, LILACS, PubMed and Springer databases, by searching for scientific articles published between January 2020 and October 2026. Descriptors related to maternal breastfeeding, breastfeeding, early weaning, nursing, health education and lactation support were used, combined with the Boolean operators AND and OR. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, six articles made up the final sample. The results showed that early weaning results from biological, emotional, social, cultural and institutional factors, such as nipple pain and trauma, inadequate latch and positioning, myths about insufficient breast milk, maternal anxiety, low level of education, lower family income, use of pacifiers and bottles, and a fragile support network. It was concluded that nurses play a fundamental role in prenatal care, childbirth, the puerperium and child health care, through health education, user embracement, qualified listening, early identification of difficulties, guidance on breastfeeding techniques, home visits and family involvement. Continuous and humanized nursing care helps to strengthen maternal autonomy, prevent early weaning and increase exclusive breastfeeding rates up to six months of age.

titre: Interoceptive–Affective Calibration in Second-Language Classrooms: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Speaking Performance
resume: Students’ ability to demonstrate second-language knowledge in a classroom does not always match what they can retrieve during private study. Speaking tasks are especially sensitive to social evaluation, time pressure, uncertainty, and the learner’s interpretation of bodily arousal. Although research has separately examined stress and memory, foreign-language anxiety, working memory, and interoception, these strands are not yet routinely integrated into classroom-level models of moment-to-moment speaking performance. This conceptual article proposes an interoceptive–affective calibration framework: a model in which learners interpret internal bodily signals (such as changes in heart rate, breathing, muscle tension, and visceral sensation), appraise the situation, and allocate attention between communicative goals and self-monitoring. The framework does not assume that bodily arousal is inherently harmful. Instead, it proposes that performance depends partly on whether arousal is interpreted as manageable activation or as evidence of threat, and on whether learners can redirect attention toward meaning and retrieval. The article synthesises relevant work on stress and memory, second-language anxiety, cognitive load, emotion regulation, and interoceptive awareness. It identifies a research opportunity at the intersection of these fields and outlines testable hypotheses, feasible classroom measures, and ethical considerations. The proposed model is intended to guide empirical investigation rather than to present untested mechanisms as established facts.

titre: A Literature Review and an Introduction to Session Five: Social Connection
resume: Chapter Five positions social connection as a central pathway to psychological wellbeing and recovery. Drawing on social identity theory, the Social Cure framework, and contemporary models of autonomic regulation, this chapter conceptualises connection not simply as social contact but as a relational and regulatory process that supports emotional stability, belonging, and meaning. Evidence from population studies and applied interventions highlights how shared identity, relational safety, and sustained group participation promote wellbeing through interacting psychological and physiological pathways, while qualitative findings from the programme demonstrate how the experience of “being together” functions as an active mechanism of change alongside structured therapeutic content. The second part translates this theoretical framework into clinical practice, offering guidance for Session Five. Building progressively on earlier mindfulness practices, loving-kindness meditation extends attentional and interoceptive skills into the relational domain, intentionally cultivating warmth, compassion, and prosocial orientation towards self and others. Practices include acts of kindness, gratitude, and facilitated shared identity-building, supporting people to enhance individual regulation while strengthening collective connection.

titre: A Literature Review and an Introduction to Session Four: Connection Between Body and Mind
resume: Session Four explores the embodied foundations of wellbeing, focusing on how physiological regulation and everyday health behaviours support recovery following acquired brain injury (ABI). The chapter presents a body–mind framework in which the autonomic nervous system, particularly vagal function, indexed by heart rate variability (HRV), functions as a key psychophysiological resource supporting the regulation and integration of emotional, physiological, and social processes. Drawing on neurovisceral integration and polyvagal theories, it outlines how physical activity, nutrition, and sleep hygiene can strengthen autonomic regulation and adaptive flexibility. However, many techniques across the programme can be understood as supporting vagal function; here, the focus is placed specifically on everyday health behaviours as practical entry points for strengthening autonomic regulation. The chapter also addresses the autonomic dysregulation commonly observed after ABI and the role of behavioural strategies in promoting physiological stability. It then translates theory into practice through an accessible group-based psychoeducational approach. To continue building mindfulness skills, participants are introduced to a body scan meditation to deepen attention to bodily sensations and enhance interoceptive awareness. Participants have reported that the information provided in this session supports understanding of their condition and helps them to regulate difficult emotional responses that might otherwise become overwhelming.

titre: Effects of a hypnosis-based psychological skills training program on anxiety, self-confidence and stress-related psychological characteristics in young female athletes: a prospective, non-randomized field study
resume: Background Elite athletes devote considerable attention to psychological preparation and typically follow structured mental training routines before competition. However, many young athletes lack access to sport psychologists during the early stages of their athletic development. Therefore, early psychological preparation is essential because self-regulation skills require systematic practice. This study examined associations between participation in a systematic psychological preparation program and self-confidence, anxiety, and stress-related psychological characteristics in female athletes aged 15–19 years. Methods The study included 58 female athletes in the experimental group (EG) and 65 in the control group (CG). Participants represented four sports: basketball, handball, football/soccer, and gymnastics. All athletes trained at least five times per week, competed at the national level or higher, and had no previous experience working with a sport psychologist. The intervention consisted of a two-month introductory psychological skills training program comprising nine sessions, including pre- and post-intervention assessments. Participants completed the Self-Regulatory Skills Questionnaire (SRSQ) and the State–Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI Form X1 and X2). Group allocation was non-randomized. Independent-samples t-tests compared baseline scores between groups, and analyses of covariance compared post-intervention scores using baseline values as covariates. Results After adjustment for baseline scores, all measured variables favoured the experimental group, with effect sizes ranging from small to large. Compared with controls, athletes in the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher self-confidence, personal hardiness, self-regulated motivation, and more adaptive coping styles. They also reported significantly lower trait anxiety, state anxiety, and cognitive and somatic anxiety. These between-group findings do not establish within-group change or a causal intervention effect. Conclusion The findings indicate that systematic psychological preparation was associated with more favourable post-intervention scores on psychological characteristics relevant to competitive readiness and athletic performance. The results support the value of psychological skills training for optimizing pre-performance psychological states in young athletes. Future studies should examine whether similar effects can also be observed in male athletes.

titre: Surgical targeting in deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder and major depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis of target definition, rationale, postoperative electrode localization and relation to outcome
resume: Protocol of a systematic review and meta-analysis of how deep brain stimulation (DBS) targets for treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and major depressive disorder (MDD) are defined, justified, verified after surgery and related to clinical outcome. Main outcomes: reproducibility of the reported surgical target, and the proportion of implanted patients whose electrode position was verified with postoperative imaging (random-effects meta-analysis of proportions). The same protocol is registered in PROSPERO. Searches were run on 20/11/2026; screening had not started at registration.

titre: OCD en of neurodivergentie?
A Comprehensive Review of Analytical Methods for the Determination of Riluzole and Fluvoxamine Maleate in Pharmaceutical Dosage Forms
resume: Riluzole and Fluvoxamine Maleate are therapeutically important drugs widely used in the management of neurological and psychiatric disorders, respectively. Riluzole is a benzothiazole derivative approved for the treatment of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), where it exerts neuroprotective effects by inhibiting glutamatergic neurotransmission and reducing neuronal excitotoxicity. Fluvoxamine Maleate, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), is extensively prescribed for depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, anxiety disorders, and related psychiatric conditions. Owing to their significant clinical utility, the development of reliable analytical methods for their quantitative estimation is essential to ensure pharmaceutical quality, safety, efficacy, and regulatory compliance. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of the physicochemical properties, therapeutic significance, and reported analytical approaches for the determination of Riluzole and Fluvoxamine Maleate. Various analytical techniques reported in the literature, including Reverse Phase High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC), Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography (UPLC), High-Performance Thin Layer Chromatography (HPTLC), LC-MS/MS, and stability-indicating chromatographic methods, have been critically evaluated. These methods have demonstrated satisfactory linearity, precision, accuracy, specificity, robustness, and sensitivity for the estimation of individual drugs in bulk materials, pharmaceutical formulations, and biological matrices. The literature survey reveals that RP-HPLC remains the most preferred analytical technique owing to its simplicity, reproducibility, cost-effectiveness, and regulatory acceptance. Although numerous validated methods are available for the individual analysis of Riluzole and Fluvoxamine Maleate, studies reporting their simultaneous estimation are limited. This highlights the necessity for the development of a novel, rapid, precise, accurate, and stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for the simultaneous determination of both drugs in bulk and synthetic mixtures. Such a method would support routine quality control, formulation development, stability studies, and pharmaceutical research while improving analytical efficiency and reducing operational costs.

titre: Operating-condition-decoupled sparse order-domain gear fault monitoring for range-extended hybrid agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous areas
resume: Vibration signals from range-extended hybrid agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous areas are strongly nonstationary under variable conditions. Gear-fault components drift and broaden with rotational speed, causing normal fluctuations to overlap fault responses and increasing false alarms and missed detections. This study proposes a operating-condition-decoupled sparse order-domain monitoring (OCD-SOM) method. An operating-condition-powertrain-vibration simulation model and paired-sample strategy ensured that normal and fault samples shared identical slope, vehicle speed, load, battery state of charge (SOC), powertrain state, and speed trajectory, differing only in gear health. Variable-speed vibrations were transformed to the order domain; local amplitude, energy, and prominence features were sparsely selected before support vector machine classification. For 1000 normal and 1000 simulated fault samples, the method achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.9337 ± 0.0181 across five parent-cycle-grouped splits, exceeding frequency-domain and decomposition-based filtering methods by 2.60 and 5.74% points, respectively. Leave-one-level-out validation using mean speed, mean load, slope root mean square, and drive-shaft speed variability achieved 0.9364 across 12 unseen levels. Sensitivity analysis showed that the model maintained good classification performance under the specified limited fault-induced rotational-speed perturbations. The proposed method can mitigate the influence of operating-condition variations on gear fault identification, supporting its algorithmic feasibility for gear condition monitoring under variable-speed conditions and providing a methodological basis for subsequent real-machine validation.

titre: Exploring the Use of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Treating Diabetes-Related Constipation: A Single-Center, Retrospective, Self-Controlled Observational Study
resume: This study aims to retrospectively evaluate the clinical effectiveness and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in treating patients with functional constipation (FC) who also have type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). It analyzes changes in bowel function, glucose metabolism indicators, and gut microbiota structure before and after FMT, and further explores the relationship between donor-related microbiota remodeling, predicted microbial metabolic functions, and clinical outcomes.

titre: Pilot Study on the Effects of Snap Supplements Prostate Health Formula on Urinary Symptoms in Men Over 50
resume: This is a decentralized, observational pilot study evaluating the potential effects of Snap Supplements Prostate Health on urinary symptoms in men aged 50 years and older. Prostate enlargement and related urinary issues, such as daytime frequency, nighttime urination (nocturia), and urgency, are common with age and may negatively affect quality of life and sleep. In this study, approximately 50 participants will take three capsules of Snap Supplements Prostate Health nightly for 90 days while completing brief daily surveys using a secure online platform (Alethios). Surveys will track urinary frequency, nocturia, urgency, and sleep quality, with additional questions about product tolerability, satisfaction, and overall experience. The main goal is to explore whether taking the supplement for 90 days is associated with improvement in urinary symptoms compared with each participant's own baseline. This is a single-group, pre-post study without randomization or placebo. No in-person visits are required; all activities occur at home. The supplement contains a blend of natural ingredients (such as saw palmetto, beta-sitosterol, nettle root, turmeric, green tea extract, and mushroom extracts) that have been studied for their potential effects on prostate and urinary health. The study will help characterize user experiences in a real-world setting and generate preliminary data to inform future research. Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw at any time. Compensation is provided for completing surveys. Risks are expected to be minimal, with possible mild gastrointestinal or allergic-type reactions.

titre: Effectiveness of Pilates Exercises in the Treatment of Postpartum Constipation: A Randomized Controlled Study
resume: Postpartum constipation is a common problem that can affect women's comfort and quality of life after childbirth. This study aims to evaluate whether Pilates exercises can help improve constipation symptoms in women after vaginal delivery. A total of 40 women aged 22-35 years with postpartum constipation will participate in this study. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups, with 20 women in each group. The first group will receive a supervised Pilates exercise program in addition to standard postpartum care, while the second group will receive standard postpartum care alone. The Pilates program will last for 9 weeks, with three supervised sessions per week. Standard postpartum care will include advice about healthy eating, adequate fluid intake, dietary fiber, and physical activity. Constipation symptoms, bowel habits, stool consistency, and constipation-related quality of life will be assessed before and after the intervention. The results of both groups will be compared to evaluate whether adding Pilates exercises to standard postpartum care improves postpartum constipation.

titre: Effects of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation Combined With Rehabilitation on Clinical Outcomes Following Surgical Reconstruction of Grasp Function in Tetraplegia: A Randomized, Triple-Blind, Sham-Controlled Feasibility Study
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is feasible, safe and tolerable when combined with standard rehabilitation after surgery to restore grasp in adults with tetraplegia caused by spinal cord injury. taVNS delivers gentle electrical stimulation through an electrode placed on the outer ear. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Can participants follow the treatment schedule and complete the study assessments? * Is the treatment well tolerated, and what side effects or medical problems occur? * Are there preliminary differences in grasp function, tendon movement and daily activities between participants receiving active treatment and those receiving sham treatment? * Does active treatment affect blood markers of inflammation and scar tissue formation? Researchers will compare active taVNS with sham treatment delivered using an identical device and a specially designed electrode that provides subtle sensory feedback without electrical stimulation. Both groups will receive the same standard postoperative rehabilitation. Approximately 40 adults undergoing surgical grasp reconstruction at the Center for Advanced Reconstruction of Extremities (CARE), Sahlgrenska University Hospital/Mölndal, Sweden, will be randomly assigned to the two groups in equal numbers. Participants, treating therapists and outcome assessors will not know which treatment participants receive. Participants will: * Use the assigned device with an electrode on the left outer ear for 60 minutes daily, starting during the week of surgery and continuing for three months. * Receive training, together with a caregiver where needed, to use the device at home. * Return for a five-day inpatient rehabilitation stay three weeks after surgery, during which treatment will be supervised. * Complete assessments before surgery and at three weeks, 12 weeks, six months and 12 months after surgery. * Complete tests of grasp function, grip and pinch strength, hand opening and movement, together with questionnaires about daily activities, independence, bowel function, mood and quality of life. * Undergo ultrasound examinations to assess tendon movement and scar tissue around the tendons. * Provide blood samples before and at several time points after surgery to investigate inflammation and tissue healing. * Record each treatment session in a diary and report side effects or difficulties using the device. Approximately 10-15 participants will also be invited to an interview about their experiences of treatment and rehabilitation around three months after surgery. This feasibility study will help researchers plan a larger trial to determine whether adding taVNS to rehabilitation improves recovery after surgical grasp reconstruction.

titre: Comparison of Early and Late Outcomes of the Hybrid Ureteroenteric Anastomosis Technique Versus Wallace and Bricker Techniques in Patients Undergoing Radical Cystectomy: A Prospective Controlled Clinical Study
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the hybrid ureteroenteric anastomosis technique reduces strictures (narrowing) at the junction between the ureters and the bowel compared with the standard Wallace and Bricker techniques in adults undergoing radical cystectomy with ileal conduit urinary diversion for bladder cancer. titre: Vínculo: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Guided Digital Intervention for Anxiety, Depression, and Insomnia Symptoms
resume: Insomnia, anxiety, and depression are common mental health problems that frequently occur together. Psychological interventions that address shared processes underlying these symptoms may offer an accessible way to improve mental health and sleep. This study will evaluate the effectiveness of Vínculo, an eight-week, guided digital psychological intervention for adults experiencing clinically significant symptoms of insomnia, anxiety, and/or depression. Approximately 305 adults living in Brazil will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The experimental group will receive Vínculo, a psychological intervention delivered through a WhatsApp chatbot that combines acceptance and commitment therapy, behavioral activation, and behavioral strategies for sleep. The comparison group will receive an eight-week digital psychoeducation program covering mental health, emotions, sleep, and healthy lifestyle habits. Both groups will receive structured content through WhatsApp, three individual videoconference sessions with a psychologist, and access to asynchronous psychological support during the intervention. The main objective is to determine whether Vínculo is more effective than digital psychoeducation in reducing insomnia severity, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms after eight weeks. Participants will also be assessed three and six months after the intervention to examine whether improvements are maintained. Additional assessments will examine daily functioning and psychological processes related to treatment outcomes.

titre: Protocol for a Randomised Feasibility Study on Online Mindfulness-based Visualisation to Treat Visual Overload in Persistent Postural Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD)
resume: Persistent Postural Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is the leading cause of chronic dizziness, with symptoms frequently triggered during situations causing visual overload (e.g. supermarket aisles, crowded spaces, and riding an escalator). The current treatments include cognitive physical therapy and antidepressant medication to relieve anxiety and depression symptoms, but these do not directly target symptoms of visual overload. Whilst the benefits of mindfulness on other neurological disorders characterised by visual disturbances (e.g. visual snow syndrome) have been reported, the effects of mindfulness on visual symptoms associated with PPPD have not been explored. This paper will present the protocol of a two-arm parallel group randomised feasibility study, examining feasibility of recruitment, acceptability and potential benefits of a mindfulness-based visualisation intervention in PPPD. The primary objective of this study is to explore the feasibility of mindfulness-based visualisation as a treatment in visual subtypes across a cohort of PPPD patients.

titre: Chatbot-Delivered Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Program for Sports Active Adults: Intervention Development and Feasibility Trial
resume: Sport-active adults face persistent stressors such as performance and body-related expectations, injury risk, training load, scheduling demands, and the challenge of balancing sport with work, caregiving, and other life commitments, all of which can undermine psychological well-being. These stressors can undermine psychological well-being, elevate perceived stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, and reduce overall satisfaction with sport performance. Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) has shown efficacy for emotional regulation, focus and body awareness, but traditional in-person MBSR can be inaccessible because of time, scheduling, geographic and stigma-related barriers. Chatbot-delivered interventions offer 24/7 accessibility, anonymity and personalised support. This project will adapt an existing chatbot-delivered MBSR programme, built with Power Virtual Agents on Microsoft Teams, to the context of sport-active adults, and will evaluate its feasibility, acceptability and preliminary efficacy in an eight-week, parallel-group, non-randomised controlled trial. Participants will be allocated non-randomly to either the intervention group or an educational control group. The intervention group will receive the eight-session chatbot-delivered MBSR programme (one session per week for eight weeks); the educational control group will receive mental health education messages via WhatsApp once weekly for eight weeks. Primary outcomes will be subjective sport performance satisfaction and psychological well-being; secondary outcomes will be depression, anxiety, perceived stress and mindfulness. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and immediately post-intervention.

titre: Transcriptomic and Genomic Sequencing of South African Colorectal Cancer Patients Reveal Population-Specific Insights and Variants
resume: Colorectal cancer (CRC) genomic studies have largely underrepresented African populations, limiting understanding of disease biology in these groups. This study addressed this gap by generating integrated genomic and transcriptomic data from South African (SA) CRC patients, establishing a foundation for future cancer studies. Bulk RNA sequencing of 32 samples identified several differentially expressed genes between tumour and normal samples, with AGAP3, AMPD2, ANKRD10, and SALL4 showing strong diagnostic performance (average sensitivity 99.9%, specificity 94.22%, PPV 99.9%, NPV 89.5%). SALL4 performed best and was validated using TCGA data and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Consensus Molecular Subtype classification revealed a distinct distribution, with enrichment of metabolic (CMS3, 30%) and mesenchymal (CMS4, 30%) subtypes and under-representation of canonical CMS2 (21%). APC mutation rates were lower than in European patients (~55% vs ~75%). Functional analysis identified inflammatory pathways as primary drivers of carcinogenesis, with viral influences exacerbating the inflammatory tumour microenvironment. Altered neural pathways in tumour samples suggested a consequential gut-brain axis loop as cancer infiltrates enervated tissue, an increasingly relevant field to which these data contribute. Whole-genome sequencing of 12 samples revealed pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants with transcriptomic differential expression; SMPD1, PERM1, PRRT2, and RP1 emerged as potential multi-omics markers, while novel mutations (KDM6A, C2CD2, TAF2, SLC6A16, OR5M10, PITRM1, TRIM64B, CARD11) were identified as previously unrecognised contributors to CRC progression in African samples. These findings expand genomic resources for African cancer research and provide new insights into the molecular landscape and tumourigenesis mechanisms of CRC in SA patients, supporting the development of population-specific precision oncology approaches.

titre: Prevalence of Fatigue in Swedish Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease, and Factors Contributing to Fatigue—A Mixed-Methods Study
resume: Background/Objectives: Fatigue is defined as an overwhelming sense of tiredness, weakness, or exhaustion, which can be physical, psychological, or a combination of both. Evidence suggests that fatigue is more prevalent among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) than in the general population. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of fatigue among Swedish IBD patients. Another aim was to increase our knowledge about factors that may contribute to fatigue, and strategies for managing fatigue. Methods: Swedish IBD patients were asked to complete the IBD Fatigue Scale. Analyses involved both a quantitative and a qualitative approach. Results: A total of 675 patients participated in the study and 44% reported significant fatigue. Fatigue was significantly associated with continuous symptoms, extraintestinal manifestations, and impaired wellbeing. Four categories relating to fatigue were identified: (1) fatigue difficult to define and attribute, (2) fatigue arising from interacting bodily and psychosocial burdens, (3) managing a limited and fluctuating supply of energy, and (4) restoring energy through activity, support and recovery. Participants frequently described fatigue as arising from an interaction between disease activity, comorbid conditions, psychological distress, sleep problems, pain, and everyday life demands. Conclusions: Although fatigue was more severe among participants with continuous symptoms, extraintestinal manifestations and impaired wellbeing, the free-text responses demonstrated that patients frequently perceived comorbidities, disturbed sleep, pain, psychological distress and demanding life circumstances as additional contributors. Management involved balancing rest and activity, planning limited energy, and drawing on supportive relationships and restorative environments. These findings support a holistic and person-centred approach in which fatigue is assessed beyond intestinal disease activity.

titre: Linking global evidence to Brazilian needs in inflammatory bowel disease: translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and psychometric evaluation of the confide questionnaires for Brazilian Portuguese
resume: Aim Bowel urgency has a substantial impact on patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) but is not routinely captured by conventional disease activity measures. We aimed to translate and cross-culturally adapt the CONFIDE patient and health care professional (HCP) questionnaires into Brazilian Portuguese and examine selected measurement properties. Method Translation and cross-cultural adaptation followed Beaton’s framework, while the initial evaluation of selected measurement properties was informed by COSMIN guidance. The process included forward translation, reconciliation, back-translation, expert review, and cognitive pretesting. The adapted questionnaires were evaluated in 180 adults with UC and 20 HCPs; 179 patients provided valid urgency responses and 19 HCPs were included in the final analysis. Internal consistency, preliminary test–retest reproducibility, construct validity, and associations with functional activity avoidance were examined. Results Mean bowel urgency severity was 4.3 ± 1.8 on a seven-point scale, with 22.8% of patients reporting very severe urgency. Urgency intensity differed significantly across deferral-capacity categories (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001), with an overall pattern of greater intensity among patients reporting more limited ability to defer defecation. Five patients and five HCPs provided identical responses on retesting; this small sample offers only preliminary evidence of temporal stability. More than half of patients avoided at least one social, leisure, occupational, or educational activity because of urgency or fear of fecal incontinence. After adjustment, urgency frequency was independently associated with activity avoidance (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.31–2.14; p < 0.001), whereas urgency intensity was not. Conclusion The CONFIDE questionnaires were successfully translated and cross-culturally adapted into Brazilian Portuguese, preserving the conceptual content of the original instruments. The initial psychometric findings were encouraging, although further evaluation is needed to establish their measurement properties more fully.
auteurs: Pedro Luiz Toledo de Arruda Lourenção

titre: Bowel Function and Global Quality of Life by Rectal Status After Neoadjuvant Treatment for Rectal Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
resume: Background: Organ preservation is expected to spare bowel function, but whether that gain is reflected in how patients rate their own quality of life is unclear. Methods: A retrospective comparative cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary center in 2021–2024. Of 52 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer receiving neoadjuvant treatment, 31 entered the watch-and-wait arm and 21 formed a comparator arm. Bowel function (LARS, Wexner, Vaizey) and quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-CR29) were compared between TME-free (n = 13) and TME respondents (n = 20). Bowel function was the primary outcome family; the rest are exploratory and uncorrected for multiplicity. Results: Bowel function differed widely: median LARS 16.0 vs. 35.5, Wexner 2.0 vs. 11.5, Vaizey 2.0 vs. 15.0 (all p < 0.001), with major LARS in 15.4% vs. 90.0% (p < 0.001). No difference in global quality of life was detected (58.3 vs. 54.2; p = 0.615), or in physical or role functioning. Body image and six colorectal symptom scales favored the TME-free group, whereas blood or mucus, abdominal pain, buttock pain, and bloating showed none. Groups reflect rectal status at assessment, not randomized strategy. Eleven of 17 comparator patients had a coloanal anastomosis, nine of them at the anal verge itself, widening the functional contrast. Freedom from any rectal surgery was 74.2% (23 of 31) in the full arm and 68.4% (13 of 19) per protocol; median follow-up was 15 months. Conclusions: Bowel function was substantially better in TME-free respondents, while this small cross-sectional study did not detect a global quality-of-life difference. Its magnitude and generalizability await larger cohorts.

titre: Xiaoyao San ameliorates depressive-like behaviors and colonic inflammation in stress-colitis composite mice through the microbiota-gut-brain axis
resume: Introduction Chronic psychological stress and intestinal inflammation may interact through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Xiaoyao San (XYS), a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula, has long been used to alleviate gastrointestinal and emotional disorders, but the contribution of the gut microbiota to its effects remains unclear. Methods In this study, a chronic restraint stress combined with dextran sulfate sodium-induced stress-colitis composite mouse model was used to evaluate XYS with and without antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion. Behavioral tests, histopathology, ELISA, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, LC-MS, molecular docking, and 16S rRNA sequencing were performed. Results XYS alleviated depressive-like behaviors, reduced serum corticosterone levels, attenuated colonic injury and inflammation, improved intestinal barrier-associated features, and ameliorated hippocampal inflammation and microglial activation. XYS also reduced NLRP3-related protein expression in both the colon and hippocampus and altered gut microbiota composition, with specific bacterial taxa associated with intestinal, behavioral, neuroendocrine, and neuroinflammatory indices. Notably, compared with the Antibiotic group, Antibiotic-XYS treatment further reduced colonic inflammatory cytokines and colonic NLRP3-related protein expression, indicating that part of the local anti-inflammatory effect of XYS was retained under antibiotic treatment. In contrast, the effects of XYS on intestinal barrier-associated features, depressive-like behaviors, serum corticosterone, hippocampal inflammation, microglial activation, and hippocampal NLRP3-related protein expression were markedly attenuated following antibiotic treatment. Discussion These differential responses indicate that improvement of local colonic inflammation alone is insufficient to account for the full intestinal and neurobehavioral effects of XYS. Overall, these findings support an important contribution of the gut microbiota to the intestinal and neurobehavioral actions of XYS along the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

titre: Review on :Gut Microbiome and Mental Health Disorders
resume: The gut microbiome is a complex community of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other microbes, that play an important role in maintaining human health. Recent research has highlighted the relationship between the gut microbiome and the brain, known as the gut–brain axis. This bidirectional communication system connects the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system through neural, endocrine, and immune pathways. Gut microorganisms produce various biologically active substances, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), neurotransmitters, and other metabolites that may influence brain function, mood, behaviour, and emotional well-being. An imbalance in the composition of gut microorganisms, known as dysbiosis, has been associated with several mental health disorders, including anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and eating disorders. Factors such as diet, stress, physical activity, age, hormonal changes, and lifestyle can influence the composition of the gut microbiome. Studies have reported alterations in microbial diversity and the abundance of specific bacterial groups in individuals with different psychiatric conditions. The vagus nerve, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, immune system, and intestinal barrier are important components involved in gut–brain communication. This review discusses the role of the gut microbiome in mental health disorders, the mechanisms involved in gut–brain interactions, and the relationship between microbial changes and psychiatric conditions. It also highlights the potential use of probiotics, prebiotics, and dietary modifications as microbiome-based approaches to supporting mental health. However, the findings of existing studies are not always consistent, and further research is required to establish the underlying mechanisms, therapeutic effectiveness, and safety of these interventions. Understanding the gut microbiome may provide new perspectives for the future prevention and management of mental health disorders.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Recent advances in polyphenolic compounds: Mechanisms underlying anti-anxiety, antidepressant, and anti-PTSD effects
resume: Polyphenols are ubiquitous natural bioactive compounds with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, emerging as promising candidates for intervening in psychiatric diseases. Emotional disorders, including anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder, are highly prevalent, debilitating conditions that severely compromise patients’ quality of life and pose substantial challenges to clinical management due to their multifactorial pathogenesis. This review comprehensively summarizes the therapeutic efficacy and multi-mechanistic actions of polyphenols against emotional disorders, focusing on five core regulatory pathways: neurotransmitter and receptor modulation, regulation of neurotrophic factors and neuroplasticity, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, modulation of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis homeostasis, and gut–brain axis regulation. By integrating the latest findings from animal models and clinical studies, this article aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework and outline future research directions for the application of polyphenolic compounds in the prevention and treatment of psychiatric disorders.

titre: Chyme reinfusion in short bowel syndrome after mesenteric venous ischemia: a case report
resume: Introduction and importance: Short bowel syndrome (SBS) is a serious complication of extensive intestinal resection, often resulting in prolonged dependence on parenteral nutrition, and it may lead to electrolyte imbalances and vitamin malabsorption, potentially compromising the patient’s vital prognosis. Presentation of the case: We report the case of a 36-year-old woman with SBS secondary to mesenteric venous ischemia. Management involved chyme reinfusion (CR) into a functional distal intestinal segment with good postoperative results. Clinical discussion: SBS is defined as intestinal failure resulting from extensive resection of the small intestine, leading to insufficient absorptive capacity to meet the patient’s nutritional and fluid requirements. Intestinal adaptation is a key physiological process following resection. In this context, CR emerges as a simple yet physiologically sound therapeutic strategy that may significantly improve long-term nutritional outcomes and quality of life. Conclusion: This case illustrates the potential role of CR as part of the multidisciplinary management of SBS following extensive bowel resection for mesenteric venous ischemia. It also highlights the importance of individualized surgical decision-making. In the presence of extensive intestinal necrosis, bowel resection should be guided by intraoperative findings, even when the anticipated prognosis is poor. This patient’s favorable outcome suggests that meaningful recovery may be achievable in selected cases through comprehensive postoperative management, including nutritional support, anticoagulation when indicated, and in appropriate patients, CR. Further studies are needed to better define the role of CR in the management of SBS.
revue: International Journal of Surgery Case Reports

titre: Early Complications of Intestinal Stoma in Gastrointestinal Surgery: A Retrospective Study of 348 Cases at a Tertiary Military Hospital
resume: Intestinal stoma creation remains a common and important procedure in gastrointestinal surgery. Stoma-related complications represent a significant source of morbidity that affects patient outcomes, quality of life, and healthcare costs. Published complication rates vary widely, from 6 to 96%, depending on the study population and follow-up duration. To determine the incidence and types of early stoma complications, identify factors associated with these complications, and describe the management approaches used at a high-volume tertiary center. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 348 consecutive patients who underwent intestinal stoma creation at a tertiary military hospital, from August 2022 to August 2023. Patient demographics, surgical indications, stoma characteristics, and early complications occurring within 30 days were analyzed. Statistical analysis was performed using the Chi-squared and Fisher exact tests for categorical variables and the independent-samples t-test for continuous variables. Values of p < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The overall early complication rate was 6.9% (24 of 348 patients). Seven types of early complications were identified: peristomal dermatitis (2.6%), hemorrhage and hematoma (1.4%), peristomal infection (0.8%), ischemia and necrosis (0.6%), stoma prolapse (0.6%), peritonitis due to stoma retraction (0.6%), and parastomal hernia (0.3%). Significant associations were found between early complications and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status classification (p = 0.001), stoma configuration type (p = 0.007), and the surgical indication of peritonitis due to ruptured tumor (p = 0.025). The mortality rate was 0.3% and was unrelated to stoma complications. The early stoma complication rate of 6.9% in this large cohort is lower than many previously reported rates in the international literature. Higher ASA classification, stoma configuration type, and peritonitis due to ruptured bowel tumors were significantly associated with increased complication risk. These findings may assist surgeons in patient counseling, surgical planning, and postoperative surveillance to reduce stoma-related morbidity.

titre: Development and internal evaluation of models for screening kinesiophobia after hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in patients with gastrointestinal cancer
resume: Aims To examine characteristics associated with kinesiophobia and develop screening models for gastrointestinal cancer patients after surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). Design A single-center cross-sectional study with internal model evaluation. Methods From October 2025 to May 2026, 521 patients were recruited by convenience sampling at a tertiary hospital in Liaoning Province, China. Candidate predictors and kinesiophobia were assessed on postoperative day 3 after clinical stabilization. A Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia score ≥37 defined screening-positive status. LASSO and multivariable logistic regression were used for variable selection and association analysis. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and decision tree (DT) models were compared. A separate six-factor LR model was developed in 365 patients and evaluated in a same-center internal test set of 156 patients. Performance assessment included discrimination, classification, calibration, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis. Results Overall, 201 patients (38.6%) screened positive for kinesiophobia. Pain severity, anxiety, depression, general self-efficacy, postoperative catheter number, and comorbidities constituted the six-factor model. In the four-model comparison, test-set AUCs were 0.847 for RF, 0.842 for LR, 0.827 for SVM, and 0.730 for DT; corresponding Brier scores were 0.157, 0.153, 0.157, and 0.170. The separate six-factor model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.880 (95% CI, 0.825–0.934) and a Brier score of 0.144. At a probability threshold of 0.50, sensitivity was 76.92%, specificity was 78.85%, and the Youden index was 0.558. The calibration intercept-in-the-large and slope were −0.743 and 1.017, respectively; the Hosmer–Lemeshow test yielded χ 2 = 15.631 (df = 8; P = 0.048), indicating imperfect calibration. At a 20% assessment threshold, net benefit was 0.236, compared with 0.167 for assessing all patients. Conclusions The six-factor model demonstrated favorable discrimination for contemporaneous screening but overestimated screening-positive probability overall. Independent external validation, assessment of recalibration, and prospective clinical impact evaluation are required before routine implementation.
