titre: Raw data and original gel images for Gut microbiota depletion impairs meningeal lymphatic drainage and is associated with neuroimmune and behavioral alterations
resume: Meningeal lymphatic vasculature is essential for immune surveillance at the borders of the central nervous system, yet the factors regulating its function in vivo remain poorly understood. Here, we show that gut microbiota depletion is associated with alterations in meningeal lymphatic vasculature structure and drainage, accompanied by changes in immune-cell composition in meningeal-associated lymphatic tissues. These alterations are accompanied by altered expression of brain inflammatory markers and heightened anxiety-like behavior. Importantly, supplementation with the microbial metabolite propionate attenuated these alterations, consistent with a role for microbial metabolites in meningeal lymphatic and neuroimmune regulation. Together, our findings identify a gut microbiota-meningeal lymphatic axis that links intestinal microbial signals to neuroimmune regulation and behavior.

titre: Neonicotinoids and Mental Health: Mechanistic, Preclinical and Epidemiological Evidence for a Transdiagnostic Neurodevelopmental Risk
resume: Neonicotinoid insecticides (imidacloprid, clothianidin, thiacloprid, acetamiprid, thiamethoxam, nitenpyram, dinotefuran) were developed as insect-selective nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) agonists and have long been regarded as safe for vertebrates. However, parent compounds and, more potently, desnitro metabolites such as DN-imidacloprid act on mammalian α4β2 and α7 nAChRs with nicotine-like potency, implicating cholinergic circuits central to cognition, mood, and reward. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and epidemiological evidence linking neonicotinoid exposure to neuropsychiatric risk. Mechanistically, these compounds promote glial activation, oxidative stress, blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and gut microbiota alterations that converge on hippocampal and limbic dysfunction. Rodent and invertebrate studies show sex-, dose-, and exposure-window-dependent effects on anxiety-, depression-, and cognition-like behaviors, with developmental exposure mirroring prenatal nicotine effects. Human data, although limited, are convergent: poisoning case series document acute neuropsychiatric symptoms; biomonitoring studies in China, Japan, and Sri Lanka associate urinary metabolites with depression, anxiety, and a recognizable “neo-nicotinic” symptom cluster; in Mexico, studies of agricultural populations link pesticide mixtures to psychological distress, although neonicotinoid biomarkers have not yet been measured in that setting; and pediatric cohorts in China and Ecuador link prenatal and childhood exposure to impaired neurodevelopment, emotional symptoms, and hyperactivity. Collectively, this evidence is consistent with neonicotinoids being an underrecognized environmental risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, although the human data remain too fragmented to support causal inference and underscores the need for dedicated cohorts, expanded biomonitoring, and mechanistic research to inform regulatory assessment.

titre: Incidence and influencing factors of post-traumatic stress symptoms in patients after surgery for acute intestinal obstruction
resume: BACKGROUND Acute intestinal obstruction (AIO) is an urgent surgical emergency characterized by a high physiological and psychological burden. Post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) are now widely recognized as a common sequela of acute illness and emergency surgery in critically ill patients, with incidence rates of 20%-30% reported in intensive care unit populations; however, systematic studies of early postoperative PTSS following emergency abdominal surgery for AIO remain scarce. Risk factors for PTSS in this surgical population, including trauma severity, postoperative pain, complications, and social support, are not well characterized and warrant focused epidemiological investigation. AIM To explore the incidence and predictors of PTSS in patients with AIO after surgery. METHODS A total of 311 patients who underwent surgical treatment for AIO in the general surgery department of our hospital between January 2021 and July 2025 were enrolled. Clinical data were collected retrospectively from medical records; at three months postoperatively, psychological scales [Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist-Civilian Version (PCL-C), Self-rating Anxiety Scale, Self-rating Depression Scale, Social Support Rating Scale, and World Health Organization Quality of Life Brief Version] were administered via outpatient interview or telephone follow-up as part of the routine post-discharge follow-up program. Demographic, disease- and surgery-related, perioperative pain, and postoperative data were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors influencing PTSS. RESULTS Of the 311 patients, 89 (28.6%) were diagnosed with PTSS (PCL-C score ≥ 38) and 37 (11.9%) had a PCL-C score ≥ 50. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that strangulated intestinal obstruction [odds ratio (OR) = 2.348, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.287-4.285; P = 0.005], open surgery (OR = 2.612, 95%CI: 1.426-4.785; P = 0.002), stoma formation (OR = 2.184, 95%CI: 1.156-4.125; P = 0.016), postoperative complications (OR = 2.876, 95%CI: 1.582-5.231; P = 0.001), and the 24-hour postoperative pain score during activity (OR = 1.386, 95%CI: 1.132-1.697; P = 0.002) were independent risk factors associated with PTSS. The area under the curve of the prediction model was 0.782 (95%CI: 0.728-0.836), with a sensitivity and specificity of 74.2%, and 75.7%, respectively. CONCLUSION The prevalence of PTSS in patients after surgery for AIO is 28.6%. Strangulated bowel obstruction, open surgery, stoma creation, postoperative complications, and postoperative pain are independently associated with PTSS. Clinical practice should focus on postoperative mental health monitoring, with provision for early and targeted interventions in high-risk patients.

titre: A Critical Review of Mahiyat-i-Maraḍī, Asbāb wa ‘Alāmāt of Amrāḍ-i-Miʿda in Classical Unani Literature
resume: Diseases of Amrad-e-Mi‘da (stomach) affect a large number of people worldwide. factors contributing to decreased quality of life and adversely affecting overall health. Digestive diseases constitute a substantial component of the global disease burden, accounting for more than one-third of all prevalent cases and thereby representing a significant public health concern.(6) In 2019, these disorders were responsible for approximately 7.32 billion incident cases and 2.86 billion prevalent cases worldwide, contributing to nearly 8 million deaths and 277 million disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) lost. Collectively, these figures underscore the considerable impact of digestive diseases on global morbidity, mortality, and overall population health.(6) According to Unani medicine, the main organs involved in digestion are, the Mi‘da (stomach) , Jigar (liver) and A‘mā (intestines). Their proper functioning is essential for maintaining health. Any pathology affecting the Mizā (temperament) , Tarkib (structure) , or Afaal (functions) of these organs may lead to disease. Unani medicine provides a comprehensive description of the Asbāb (etiology), Mahiyat-iMaradi (pathogenesis), etiopathological factors and Alāmāt(clinical manifestations) of stomach diseases. However, the available literature on these concepts is scattered and not systematically compiled. Therefore, there is a need to collect, arrange, and compile the concepts related to Mahiyati-Maradi, Asbāb, and ‘Alāmāt of Amrad-i-Mi‘da from classical Unani literature in a systematic manner. This approach will facilitate a better understanding of Unani perspectives on the digestive system (Nizām-i-Hazm) and provide a valuable and effective reference for students, researchers, and Unani practitioners. Furthermore, it may contribute to the documentation of traditional Unani knowledge and help correlate classical concepts with contemporary medical concepts.

titre: PHYSIOTHERAPY IN PSYCHOGERIATRIC PATIENTS: POSSIBILITIES AND APPLICATION
resume: Introduction: multimorbid patients with psychiatric disorders are exposed to a number of risks, such as hypostatic pneumonia, decubitus and lethal outcome, which raises the question of the application of physiotherapy during their hospital stay. Purpose: to research the possibilities for physiotherapy application in psychogeriatric patients in a hospital environment. Material and methods: Material: 74 patients from the Third psychiatric clinic for the treatment of psychoses /mental disorders/ in the elderly, UMHAT “St. Marina” - Varna for the time period July 2024 - July 2025. An individual physiotherapeutic programme was applied, consistent with the somatic comorbidities and the rehabilitation potential. Methods: analytical, statistical. Results and discussion: Almost one fourth of the respondents suffer from recurrent depressive disorder, 18% from dementia, and 11% from schizophrenia and organic delusional schizophrenic-like disorder. The remaining 36% from the researched population suffer from diverse psychopathology: bipolar affective disorder (8%), mental behavioural disorders (9%), depressive episodes (5%), etc. More than half (59.45%) are multimorbid with three or more somatic comorbidities - neurological, cardiological, urological, gastrointestinal, etc., burdened with psychiatric disorders with symptoms of dementia, conditions after vascular accidents, organic disorders with psychotic symptoms, affective disorders (most often depressive), etc. The predominant physiotherapeutic methods and means were therapeutic gymnastics (93%), soft tissue mobilizations (4%) and passive exercises (3%). Therapeutic gymnastics were applied independently in more than half of the respondents (58%) and in combination with other methods and means in 35%. Conclusion: The research reveals the unlimited possibilities of application of active and/or passive physiotherapy in multimorbid psychogeriatric patients.
revue: Journal of IMAB - Annual Proceeding (Scientific Papers)

titre: Morbidity Pattern as Determinants of Functional Disability among Geriatric Patients attending the General Outpatient Clinic of Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Abeokuta
resume: Objective: This study aimed to examine the morbidity patterns as determinants of functional disability among geriatric patients attending the General Outpatient Clinic of Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Abeokuta. Methods: A descriptive, cross-sectional, hospital-based study was conducted with 385 elderly patients (aged 60 years and above). We utilized a systematic random sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire, Katz index of independence in activities of daily living (ADLs), and Lawton instrumental activities of daily living scale (IADLs). Logistic regression analysis was performed to assess the relationship between clinical characteristics and functional disability. Results: The majority of respondents (54.2%) had cardiovascular diseases. A significant association was found between cardiovascular diseases and functional disability in both BADL (P=0.032) and IADL (P=0.002). Musculoskeletal and endocrine/metabolic diseases also showed a significant relationship with functional disability in IADL. However, other conditions like digestive, eye, ear, and psychological disorders did not show a significant impact on functional disability. Additionally, the presence of multiple morbidities and non-communicable diseases significantly correlated with functional disability, particularly in IADL. Conclusion: The study highlights the significant impact of specific chronic diseases, particularly cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and endocrine/metabolic disorders, on the functional capabilities of elderly patients. Managing these conditions is crucial for maintaining the functional independence of the elderly. The findings underscore the need for integrated chronic disease management programs and a multidisciplinary approach to geriatric care. Recommendations: The study recommends the implementation of integrated chronic disease management programs, the establishment of multidisciplinary geriatric care teams, and the development of elderly-focused healthcare policies and infrastructure to improve the quality of life and functional independence of the elderly population.
revue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EVALUATION AND PHYSICAL REPORT

titre: Time-specific exploration of core symptoms in chemotherapy ovarian cancer: a network analysis
resume: Aim This study aims to investigate the dynamic changes in the symptom networks of ovarian cancer patients undergoing postoperative chemotherapy, thereby providing evidence-based support for precision symptom management. Methods A longitudinal study design was adopted. A total of 252 patients with ovarian cancer who were receiving postoperative chemotherapy were enrolled from August 2025 to August 2026. Assessments were performed after the first (T1), third (T3), and sixth (T6) chemotherapy cycles. Symptom severity was assessed using the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory (MDASI) and the tailored symptom module for ovarian cancer (TSM-OC). Contemporaneous networks and cross-lagged panel networks were constructed. Bootstrap-derived correlation-stability (CS) coefficients were calculated to evaluate network stability. Results Contemporaneous network analyses revealed prominent stage-specific shifts in core symptoms: somatic gastrointestinal symptoms predominated at T1, whereas psychological-emotional symptoms occupied the central position of the network at T6. For cross-lagged panel networks, In-strength of the T3→T6 window exhibited excellent stability (CS = 0.595). The top-four symptoms ranked by In-strength were irritability, distress, anxiety, and insomnia. Conclusion Symptom networks among ovarian cancer patients receiving postoperative chemotherapy exhibited distinct stage-specific evolution. Psychological-emotional symptoms in late-phase chemotherapy were temporally preceded by somatic symptoms. Clinically, stage-specific and individualized symptom-management strategies should be implemented.

titre: Bupleurum-based formulas and their modern preparations: from ancient usage to clinical application
resume: Ethnopharmacological relevance Bupleuri Radix (Bupleurum) has been used in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean herbal medicine for over two millennia. It was first recorded in Shennong Bencao Jing and was extensively used in Zhang Zhongjing’s Shanghan Lun. Traditionally, it is used for “harmonizing Shaoyang” and “soothing the liver and relieving depression.” Modern pharmacological studies support these traditional applications and have revealed anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and antidepressant activities, thereby bridging traditional efficacy and modern science. Aim of the review This review systematically summarizes the historical evolution, pharmacological mechanisms, and contemporary development of Bupleurum and its compound formulas. It traces their transition from traditional decoctions to modern dosage forms, discusses current challenges, and proposes a strategic framework to promote clinical application and the modernization of TCM. Materials and methods We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI from database inception to July 2026. The search was supplemented with official monographs, including the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (2025 edition). Studies on botany, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, and clinical application were screened using predefined criteria. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed original research on Bupleurum species. Data extraction and synthesis followed PRISMA guidelines. Duplicate publications, conference abstracts, and studies unrelated to Bupleurum were excluded. Results This review identified 109 modern Bupleurum-containing preparations in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (2025 edition). The major constituents—saikosaponins, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and volatile oils—exert diverse biological activities. These include anti-inflammatory effects via NF-κB/MAPK modulation, antitumor effects via PI3K/Akt/mTOR and STAT3 regulation, antidepressant effects via monoamine modulation, BDNF/TrkB signaling, and gut microbiota remodeling, and hepatoprotective effects via Nrf2/ARE and PPAR-α activation. Three classical formulas—Xiao Chaihu Tang, Buzhong Yiqi Tang, and Xiaoyao San—have been developed into modern dosage forms. This review integrates the legacy of Bupleurum into a “herb–component–target–disease” framework and identifies limitations in quality consistency, bioavailability, mechanistic elucidation, and clinical translation. Conclusion This review provides a comprehensive foundation for modernizing Bupleurum-containing formulas by integrating historical applications with contemporary pharmacology and pharmaceutical science. Future studies should adopt the “herb–component–target–disease” paradigm using network pharmacology, multi-omics, and high-throughput screening. Drug delivery systems, such as nanoformulations and sustained-release preparations, should be further developed. Comprehensive quality control should combine chemical fingerprinting with bioactivity assessments. Well-designed, large-scale randomized controlled trials are also needed to strengthen the evidence base and promote the international recognition.

titre: Interoception and Judgment: Evidence on Sex Differences and a Cue-Integration Hypothesis
resume: Studies of heartbeat perception and emotion recognition report sex differences that vary across tasks and measures. This review examines how task demands, peripheral physiology, and contextual cues may contribute to those differences. It distinguishes behavioral performance from self-reported bodily awareness, mean confidence, and metacognitive sensitivity. I then propose a cue-integration account: bodily signals may improve judgment when they add information beyond external cues and receive appropriate weight, with the benefit also depending on noise covariance. Attention, source attribution, and reporting strategies may affect how these signals are used; autonomic dynamics remain a further candidate moderator. A linear model illustrates these relations, and three proposed experiments address task format, physiological feedback, and decision costs. Current evidence does not establish a common mechanism underlying sex differences. The proposed studies distinguish whether a bodily signal carries information, whether it predicts choice, and whether using it improves judgment. Keywords: interoception; sex differences; cue integration; metacognition; heart rate variability; stress decision-making

titre: Interoceptive aberrations in major depressive disorder: Neural mechanisms, clinical correlates, and targeted interventions
resume: Interoception, the sensing and interpretation of internal bodily signals, supports homeostatic regulation and emotional experience. Findings in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain inconsistent across studies using non-equivalent measures, heterogeneous clinical samples, and predominantly cross-sectional designs. Accordingly, this narrative review compares methods for assessing interoceptive accuracy, sensibility, and awareness; synthesizes behavioral, neurobiological, and clinical findings; and evaluates emerging interventions relevant to interoceptive processing. Current evidence indicates that interoceptive dysfunction in MDD is multidimensional, encompassing task performance, subjective bodily appraisal, metacognitive calibration, and interoception-related neural processing. Variability across these domains appears to reflect not only differences in measurement but also variation in clinical state and illness stage. Consistent with this view, neuroimaging studies suggest stage-related differences in large-scale networks, including lower default mode network activity in early-stage samples and higher activity in chronic-stage samples. From an active-inference perspective, selected findings may be understood in terms of an altered balance between bodily predictions and incoming sensory evidence, whereby negatively biased predictions persist when sensory signals are insufficiently weighted. Emerging intervention studies indicate that selected interoceptive processes are modifiable in some clinical and nonclinical samples, providing a rationale for mechanism-based testing in MDD.

titre: Representational Profiles and Their Links to Interoceptive Sensibility and Well-Being: A Cluster Analysis of Young Adults
resume: In this cross-sectional survey, we examined whether distinct representational profiles were associated with subjective interoceptive sensibility and multidimensional well-being among young adults. Participants were 600 young adults from Japan (300 men and 300 women, aged 18–29 years) recruited from a registered online research panel. After excluding respondents who failed instructed-response checks, we analyzed data from 290 participants. Hierarchical cluster analysis using Ward’s method identified four representational profiles: high, moderate, low, and low spatial-visual. The first three profiles reflected overall levels across object-visual, spatial-visual, and verbal thinking. In contrast, the low spatial-visual profile showed relatively high object-visual and low spatial-visual thinking. Profiles were compared on interoceptive sensibility and well-being using the Japanese versions of the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness and Mental Health Continuum–Short Form, respectively. All six subscales differed significantly across profiles (ω² = .12–.31, ps < .001). Profile effects were significant for emotional, social, and psychological well-being (ps < .001), with the high profile showing the highest levels across all three domains. A significant sex × profile interaction was observed for emotional well-being, F(3, 282) = 3.26, p = .022, ω² = .023. These findings indicate that representational profiles are associated with subjective interoceptive sensibility and well-being, with the associations varying across dimensions and profiles.

titre: Disembodied cognition: How digital compulsion severs the neuropsychological pathways of human–nature association
resume: Humans are ecologically embedded organisms, yet increasingly large portions of everyday attention are organized by screen-mediated environments. This article, written for the research topic “Putting People in Their Place: Restoring the Human Animal in Ecological Systems,” develops the hypothesis that digital compulsion contributes to cosmological disassociation: the lived condition in which the person no longer experiences the self as materially and dynamically continuous with the ecosystems that sustain them. The central problem is not screen time, nor the mere substitution of screens for outdoor time, but the possibility that compulsive digital engagement repeatedly engages and modifies the neurocognitive processes that keep organisms situated in their environments: attention allocation, interoceptive regulation, reward prediction, circadian entrainment, and embodied spatial cognition. The argument is stronger than a nature-deficit account but more cautious than the claim that screen use has been shown to damage the brain. Existing research offers converging evidence for altered attention and reward processing in problematic digital use, circadian disruption from evening display exposure, and the constitutive role of body–environment coupling in cognition and selfhood, while evidence for lasting neuroadaptation remains weak. Reassociation is therefore unlikely to occur simply by encouraging people to spend time outdoors; it would require interventions that retrain attention, restore sensitivity to bodily and environmental rhythms, reintroduce embodied navigation, and weaken the reward architectures that make ecological presence difficult to sustain. These interventions are proposed as testable directions at the interface of neuropsychology and conservation, not as evidence-based recommendations.

titre: Informational Engineering and Nightly Cognitive Conditioning: A 30-Day Open-Access Observational Protocol for Autonomic Regulation and Epigenetic Resilience
resume: Chronic psychological stress and sustained sympathetic nervous system activation are associated with dysregulated hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis signaling and pro-inflammatory transcriptional activity, including nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kB) pathways. While mind-body interventions such as meditation, clinical hypnosis, and contemplative prayer have been studied for stress reduction and autonomic recovery, standardized, zero-cost nightly protocols designed for pre-sleep hypnagogic states remain under-documented in open observational cohorts. This protocol defines a 30-day open-access observational framework—the Fleetmikewood Protocol—utilizing structured pre-sleep visualization and linguistic anchoring ("Informational Engineering" / Designer Prayers) to promote parasympathetic dominance, subjective sleep quality, and perceived recovery. Built for universal AI interoperability, any generative AI model can be used to tailor these nightly scripts to fit any personal belief system, spiritual tradition, or secular self-hypnosis framing while maintaining consistent autonomic conditioning principles. Rather than altering underlying DNA nucleotide sequences, the framework examines non-sequence epigenetic regulation and behavioral conditioning as complementary wellness practices.

titre: Response of tic and obsessive-compulsive symptoms to striosomal dopaminergic modulation in tic-related OCD: an open-label pilot study
resume: Objectives This study investigated the therapeutic potential of striosomes in addressing ICSDs, focusing on the treatment response of tic and obsessive-compulsive (OC) symptoms in tic-related OCD (T-OCD) to a pharmacological intervention designed to enhance striosomal dopamine signaling through D1-type receptors (D1Rs). Methods Ten participants with T-OCD [30% male; mean age, 40.5 years (SD 20.1); mean age at onset, 9.2 years (SD 4.1)] received L-DOPA/carbidopa (50 mg) plus chlorpromazine-phenolphthalinate (5 mg), with doses increased stepwise to three times daily over 8 weeks, then maintained for 1 year. We used the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS) and the Yale-Brown Obsessive-Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) for clinical assessments. For statistical analyses, we used repeated-measures ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc tests and calculated partial eta squared (η 2 ) to report effect sizes. Results The study cohort showed significant, sustained improvements in both tics and OCD symptoms. At one-year follow-up, Total Tic Severity Scale scores on the YGTSS decreased by 73.3% ( n = 10; mean difference, −11.0; 95% CI, −13.99 to −8.04; p = 0.0025; η 2 = 0.715) compared with the baseline. In parallel, Y-BOCS scores decreased by 85.1% ( n = 10; mean difference, −13.10; 95% CI, −17.71 to −8.49; p = 0.0004; η 2 = 0.639). No adverse effects were reported during this one-year study. Conclusion Pharmacologic modulation of striosomal D 1 R signaling could provide significant, durable benefits for patients with T-OCD. Given its efficacy and safety in reducing both tic and OC symptoms in T-OCD, striosomes may serve as a promising therapeutic target for ICSDs. These findings warrant further investigation through larger, randomized, and placebo-controlled clinical trials.

titre: Efeito do uso de telas no desenvolvimento infantil
resume: Objective: To identify the main effects of screen use on child development, considering cognitive, socio-emotional, physical, and behavioral aspects. Methods: This is an integrative literature review of a qualitative and exploratory nature, conducted in the PubMed, Lilacs, Scielo, and CAPES Periodicals Portal databases, covering the period from 2015 to 2025. The final sample consisted of 15 scientific articles, analyzed using Bardin's Content Analysis. Results: The results reveal alarming data regarding the early access to screens, with 88% of children starting exposure before the age of two, with an exponential increase in average usage time as age advances. Furthermore, significant impairments were identified, including delays in language and working memory, risks of childhood obesity and sedentary lifestyle, worsening sleep quality, as well as psychosocial repercussions such as anxiety, aggressive behaviors, and a prospective association with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD). Final considerations: Excessive screen exposure acts as a multifactorial risk factor, involving important stages of development, by replacing human interactions and concrete experiences with impoverished digital stimuli.

titre: Quality of life in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease over the past decade: A repeated cross-sectional study
resume: OBJECTIVES: Children with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), experience a significantly lower health-related quality of life (HRQoL) compared to healthy children. Over the past decade, advancements in IBD care may have influenced HRQoL. The aim of this study was to compare HRQoL between two independent pediatric IBD cohorts from distinct time periods. METHODS: Two pediatric IBD cohorts, T1 cohort (2014-2015) and T2 cohort (2022-2024), completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 4.0 (PedsQL) and the IBD-specific IMPACT-III questionnaire. Total and scale scores of both questionnaires were compared between the two cohorts. Moreover, the HRQoL of T2 was compared to the general population (GP). RESULTS: In total, 117 (T1: 72, T2: 45) patients completed both questionnaires. The PedsQL total and scale scores did not differ between T1 and T2 for both patients with CD and UC. IMPACT-III total and subscale scores showed no differences for patients with CD and the total IBD-cohort. In UC, the IMPACT-III total score and its subdomain social functioning were higher in T2 (p = 0.049 and p = 0.013, respectively). Children with IBD in the T2 cohort scored lower in the physical (p = 0.001) and school (p = 0.001) functioning subscales when compared to the GP cohort. CONCLUSION: This study shows no overall difference in HRQoL for pediatric patients with IBD over the past decade but indicates an improvement in HRQoL for children with UC.

titre: Surgery Versus Medical Treatment for Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis: A Systematic Review of Pain, Quality of Life, Fertility, Recurrence, and Treatment-Related Complications
resume: Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) is associated with chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia, bowel and urinary symptoms, infertility, and impaired quality of life. Management includes hormonal treatment and surgery, but the comparative benefits and risks of these approaches remain uncertain. This review examines evidence concerning pain relief, quality of life, fertility, recurrence, and treatment-related complications in women with DIE. The available literature includes a limited number of direct comparisons between surgery and hormone-based treatment, together with observational surgical cohorts and studies comparing different surgical techniques. Both medical and surgical treatment have been associated with improvement in endometriosis-related pain. Surgical cohorts also report improvements in quality of life and bowel function, and pregnancies have been documented after excision of deep disease. However, most postoperative studies lack a nonsurgical control group, and comparisons between surgical techniques do not establish the relative effectiveness of surgery and medical treatment. Recurrence and clinically important bowel and urinary complications remain relevant considerations. The available evidence does not establish that surgery is universally superior to medical treatment. Management should therefore be individualized according to symptoms, lesion location and extent, reproductive plans, previous treatment, and the risks associated with the proposed intervention. The certainty of comparative conclusions is limited by the predominance of observational evidence and the inadequate recruitment of the available randomized trial.

titre: Globin digest ameliorates colitis-associated depression-like behavior in mice
resume: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with psychiatric disorders, including depression; however, the effects of globin digest (GD) on UC-like symptoms and the associated depression-like behavior remain unclear. We investigated the effects of GD in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-treated mice, an animal model of colitis. GD ameliorated DSS-induced diarrhea, bloody stools, and depression-like behavior, and attenuated reductions in hippocampal AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and CREB phosphorylation, NeuN expression, and neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus, while increasing BDNF expression. These findings suggest that the beneficial effects of GD on colitis-associated depression-like behavior involve the restoration of hippocampal AMPK/CREB/BDNF signaling and neurogenesis.

titre: Effectiveness of Nutritional Intervention in Reduction of Gastrointestinal Toxicity during External Beam Radiotherapy in Women with Gynecological Tumors
resume: Objective: To assess if nutritional intervention with a diet low in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) decreases acute gastrointestinal toxicity induced by pelvic external beam radiotherapy in patients with gynecologic tumors.Material and methods: Single-center, randomized, prospective clinical trial comparing patients on a low-FODMAP diet vs. standard Mexican diet, designed to detect an 80% decrease in Grade 1-2 acute gastrointestinal toxicity in the standard diet group to 25% of Grade 1-2 acute gastrointestinal toxicity in the low-FODMAP diet group.Results: Thirteen patients were recruited per group, with higher gastrointestinal toxicity grade 1-2 (85 vs. 77%) and 3 (23 vs. 0%) being reported in the standard diet group with regard to the low-FODMAP diet (p = 0.16).The low-FODMAP diet group had a lower end of treatment symptom score in the cervical cancer patient quality of life questionnaire (1.41 vs. 1.85; p = 0.01) and lower ECOG mean deterioration (0.61 [SD ± 0.5] vs. 0.23 [SD ± 0.43]; p = 0.049).Excellent adherence to the diet was shown by 85% of patients.No factors associated with the presence of grade 3 gastrointestinal toxicity were found.Conclusion: Implementation of a low-FODMAP diet during pelvic external beam radiation therapy is a low-cost and high-adherence measure that reduces end-of-treatment performance status and symptom deterioration in patients with cervical cancer.(creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).

titre: Dumping syndrome alleviated with semaglutide in a patient with hypoglycemia refractory to standard therapy
resume: Dumping syndrome after Nissen fundoplication is uncommon with therapeutic challenges. Accelerated gastric transit and dysregulated incretin-mediated insulin secretion are believed to drive postprandial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Treatment frequently fails to achieve sustained symptom control and is constrained by adverse effects. This case describes glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist therapy as a novel approach to address glycemic instability and gastrointestinal symptoms. A 55-year-old man presented with a 10-year history of persistent gastrointestinal distress and postprandial hypoglycemia, including irritability, fatigue, and cognitive impairment after Nissen fundoplication. After hospitalization to rule out insulinoma, outpatient follow-up led to a diagnosis of dumping syndrome with severe hypoglycemia. He was initiated on semaglutide. There was a decline in the frequency of hypoglycemia, with improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms, glycemic stabilization, and quality of life. This highlights the utility of off-label GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with dumping syndrome, resulting in a reduction in postprandial hypoglycemic episodes. Although emerging reports have described similar benefits, evidence remains limited. Further studies are needed to clarify efficacy, safety, and appropriate patient selection before GLP-1–based therapies can be recommended for dumping syndrome.

titre: Magnesium Deficiency in a Patient on Chemotherapy-Radiotherapy Treatment for Cervical Cancer: Case Report and Review
resume: Introduction: Magnesium deficiency is a common entity in cancer patients owing to cisplatin-containing chemotherapeutic schemes.Combination with radiotherapy in certain tumors where the gastrointestinal tract is part of the treatment field can elicit this entity.Clinical case: The case is presented of a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with uterine cervix cancer on treatment with concomitant chemotherapy plus radiotherapy.Owing to the tumor extension and lymph node involvement, the radiation treatment field was broad, with important doses at the level of the small intestine.During treatment, the patient had important diarrhea due to magnesium deficit.Results: Testing for hypomagnesemia is not common in clinical practice, but it should be contemplated in patients on treatment with cisplatin-containing chemotherapeutic schemes and extended-field pelvic radiotherapy.Discussion: Knowing this entity and providing adequate treatment can prevent quality of life deterioration in affected subjects and possible early treatment discontinuation due to poor tolerance.(creativecommons.

titre: Constipation Management in Hospitalized Patients: A Scoping Review of Nursing Strategies
resume: BACKGROUND: Constipation is a common yet frequently overlooked problem among hospitalized patients and is associated with reduced quality of life, prolonged hospital stays, and increased healthcare costs. Nurses play a central role in the prevention and management of constipation through both pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. However, evidence regarding nurse-led interventions is scattered across different clinical settings and study designs. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the available evidence on nursing interventions for the prevention and management of constipation in hospitalized patients. METHODS: This scoping review was conducted following a five-stage methodological framework. A comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was performed from January 2000 to November 2025. Grey literature sources were also searched. Studies conducted in hospital settings that examined nurse-led interventions for preventing or treating constipation were included, regardless of study design. Data were extracted and summarized descriptively, and methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria and were conducted across various countries and inpatient clinical settings, including orthopedic, cardiac, oncology, rehabilitation, and intensive care units, involving more than one thousand patients overall. Nurse-led interventions included non-pharmacological approaches such as abdominal massage, reflexology, acupressure, auricular therapy, dietary or fiber-based strategies, and structured bowel management protocols. Overall, most included studies reported improvements in constipation-related outcomes following nurse-led interventions, although findings varied across intervention types and study settings. Adverse effects were rarely reported and no serious harms were identified. CONCLUSION: The available evidence indicates that a range of nurse-led interventions have been implemented and have been associated with favorable outcomes in individual studies; however, further high-quality research is required before conclusions regarding effectiveness can be drawn.

titre: Chuzhen Therapy- A Non-Invasive External Therapy of Traditional Chinese Medicine for Non-specific Low Back Pain
resume: Low back pain (LBP) represents a prevalent and heterogeneous musculoskeletal disorder that severely impairs patients' daily functioning, with approximately 90%-95% of clinical cases categorized as non-specific low back pain (NSLBP). First-line conservative management for NSLBP predominantly relies on oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and opioid analgesics; however, these pharmacotherapies carry notable adverse risks, including peptic ulceration, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and long-term drug dependence. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a safe, nonpharmacological alternative intervention for NSLBP. Chuzhen therapy, a distinctive external therapeutic modality originating from the Nine Needles described in the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic), integrates core therapeutic principles of acupuncture and tuina without penetrating the skin. Unlike conventional tuina, which imposes heavy physical strain on practitioners and may result in inconsistent stimulation intensity among operators, Chuzhen therapy employs specialized, customized instruments to deliver stable, reproducible, and targeted acupoint stimulation with minimal physical exertion. Preclinical animal studies have validated its analgesic mechanisms, demonstrating that Chuzhen intervention elevates pain thresholds by modulating central monoamine neurotransmitter concentrations. This report establishes a fully standardized clinical protocol for Chuzhen therapy targeting NSLBP, covering standardized acupoint selection, pretreatment preparation, unified treatment duration, complete operational workflows, and standardized safety precautions. Three validated clinical outcome metrics-the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey-were adopted to preliminarily assess the feasibility and clinical applicability of the proposed protocol. Findings from this single-arm, self-controlled protocol-validation trial indicate that standardized Chuzhen therapy significantly alleviates pain intensity, restores lumbar physical function, and improves long-term health-related quality of life among patients with NSLBP. No serious adverse events were documented throughout the intervention period.

titre: Selective PDE4 inhibition enhances bone mass by stimulating bone formation and suppressing bone resorption
resume: Osteoporosis is a common skeletal disease that increases fracture risk and is a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and diminished quality of life in the elderly. Although bone anabolic therapies are available, inconvenient routes of administration and concerns regarding potential adverse effects substantially limit their use. Consequently, anti-resorptive drugs that slow further bone loss without rebuilding lost bone mass or restoring load-bearing strength remain the dominant therapies. Many patients nevertheless sustain fractures despite treatment, underscoring the weaknesses of this approach and the need for new anabolic strategies. The immune system plays an important role in regulating both bone formation and resorption, raising the possibility that immune pathways can be therapeutically harnessed to promote bone anabolism. Recent studies have further linked the gut microbiota to this osteoimmune network, demonstrating that microbiota-derived metabolites can promote T cell-dependent anabolic signaling in bone. It has previously been shown that broad-spectrum phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitors such as pentoxifylline (PTX) stimulate bone formation and promote bone accrual in animal models. We recently demonstrated that a major mechanism of PTX-induced bone anabolism is through an osteoimmunological pathway in which activated CD8 T cells trigger production of Wnt10b, a bone-anabolic Wnt ligand. However, PTX also directly promotes osteoclast bone resorption, limiting bone gain, while its adverse-effect profile further restricts its therapeutic utility. Here, we investigated the bone anabolic properties of apremilast, an FDA-approved PDE4-selective inhibitor targeting a major PDE regulating cAMP signaling in CD8 T cells. Micro-computed tomography demonstrated significant trabecular bone accrual and improved microarchitecture in femurs and vertebrae of apremilast-treated female C57BL/6J mice. Quantitative histomorphometry confirmed increased bone formation and reduced osteoclast indices. In vitro, apremilast did not directly stimulate osteoblast differentiation or mineralization but increased Wnt10b expression by CD8 T cells, supporting an indirect immune-mediated anabolic mechanism. Critically, unlike PTX, apremilast dose-dependently inhibited osteoclast differentiation from primary monocytes. These findings are consistent with an anabolic pathway, together with suppression of osteoclastogenesis, creating a remodeling environment favorable for net bone gain. These findings identify apremilast as an immunomodulatory regulator of bone remodeling and provide a rationale for further evaluation of PDE4 inhibition in preclinical models of osteoporosis.

titre: [Irritable bowel syndrome in clinical practice]
Successful Living Donor Liver Transplantation for Acute Intermittent Porphyria in an Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
resume: BACKGROUND: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is a rare metabolic disorder characterized by recurrent neurovisceral crises and significant morbidity. While liver transplantation (LT) offers definitive metabolic correction in refractory disease, pediatric experience has not been reported. METHOD: We report a 14-year-old male with recurrent neurovisceral attacks, seizures, autonomic instability, and psychiatric manifestations. Diagnosis of AIP was established by markedly elevated urinary porphobilinogen during an attack, an increased total urine porphyrins/creatinine ratio, and confirmation of a heterozygous HMBS mutation. Due to failure of medical therapy and persistent refractory symptoms, living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) was performed with meticulous perioperative planning, including avoidance of porphyrogenic drugs, continuous dextrose infusion, and anticoagulation strategies. RESULTS: The patient underwent LDLT using a modified right lobe graft with his mother as the donor and had an uneventful intraoperative course. Postoperatively, he was extubated on postoperative day (POD) 1 and showed gradual normalization of biochemical parameters including serum sodium and renal function. Serial Doppler studies confirmed satisfactory graft perfusion. There was no recurrence of porphyria attacks. Neurological and psychiatric symptoms improved progressively, and gastrointestinal issues resolved completely. He was discharged in stable condition on POD 14. CONCLUSION: Definitive metabolic correction of refractory pediatric AIP occurs with LDLT, with resolution of attacks and marked clinical improvement. Early consideration of LDLT in carefully selected patients can result in a good outcome.

titre: Hericium erinaceus polysaccharide ameliorates spatial working memory impairment and intestinal barrier dysfunction in high-fat high-sucrose diet-fed mice
resume: INTRODUCTION: Long-term consumption of high-fat and high-sucrose diets breaks intestinal balance and causes a series of physical disorders in animals. This study aimed to explore the regulatory effect of Hericium erinaceus polysaccharides on intestinal health and related internal physiological changes under such dietary conditions. METHODS: We established corresponding mouse models and carried out polysaccharide feeding intervention. Gut microbial community was detected by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and colon tissue morphology and barrier state were observed through tissue staining. Related inflammatory substances and functional indicators in hippocampal tissues were determined. RESULTS: The results showed that unreasonable dietary intake changed intestinal flora distribution, destroyed colon tissue structure and weakened intestinal barrier performance, and also raised inflammatory levels and disturbed normal substance levels in hippocampus. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that HEP may partially alleviate HFHSD-associated metabolic disturbances, intestinal barrier impairment, hippocampal inflammation, and spatial working memory deficits in mice. These effects were associated with alterations in gut microbial composition, intestinal barrier integrity, and hippocampal inflammatory and neurochemical markers.

titre: Gut microbiota‑driven indole‑3‑propionic acid protects against sepsis‑associated encephalopathy via inhibiting BNIP3L ubiquitination and restoring BNIP3L‑dependent mitophagy as a potential molecular mechanism
resume: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe refractory neurological complication occurring in up to 70% sepsis patients with no targeted therapies. Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a tryptophan metabolite, exerts neuroprotective effects, but its therapeutic mechanism against SAE remains unclear. BNIP3L-linked mitophagy and mitochondrial quality control are disrupted in septic neurons, while the potential correlative connection between IPA abundance and BNIP3L abundance remains undefined. This study aimed to explore the gut-brain axis mechanism and molecular target of IPA in treating SAE. METHODS: We established cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) SAE mouse models with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and exogenous IPA intervention; performed in vitro LPS-stimulated HT22 hippocampal neuronal experiments; enrolled a prospective clinical cohort of 111 ICU sepsis patients. 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted/targeted metabolomics, fiber photometry Ca2+ recording, transmission electron microscopy, Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation and linkage-specific ubiquitin ELISA were adopted. Statistical analyses included one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlation, multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analysis. RESULTS: Sepsis induced gut dysbiosis, reduced tryptophan-metabolizing bacteria and depleted endogenous IPA; FMT restored microbial homeostasis and IPA, improving mouse survival, cognitive function and reducing neuronal apoptosis. Clinically, plasma IPA was significantly lower in SAE patients, positively correlated with GCS scores, and exhibited excellent diagnostic value (AUC = 0.891). In CLP mice, IPA supplementation was accompanied by lower systemic inflammatory cytokine concentrations, partial normalization of aberrant EEG power spectra, attenuated excessive Ca2+ activity in hippocampal CA1 neurons, reduced neuronal loss, improved mitochondrial ultrastructural morphology, and parallel recovery of tissue ATP levels and antioxidant capacity. In HT22 cells, LPS exposure coincided with reduced BNIP3 levels, collapsed mitochondrial membrane potential, suppressed mitophagy and elevated neuronal apoptosis; IPA treatment correlated with parallel improvements in these cellular indicators. Mechanistically, global hippocampal total K48-linked polyubiquitin abundance exhibited an inverse correlation with circulating IPA concentrations, a trend that indirectly suggests potential shifts in BNIP3 ubiquitination profiles during sepsis, though protein-specific modification could not be confirmed herein. CONCLUSIONS: Circulating gut-microbiota-derived IPA concentrations showed inverse covariation with total hippocampal K48-linked polyubiquitin abundance, concurrent with parallel shifts in mitophagy-related molecular markers and less severe neuronal injury across clinical and preclinical SAE cohorts; direct evidence for BNIP3L-specific K48 ubiquitination modification was absent in this work in both clinical and preclinical SAE cohorts. IPA shows reliable diagnostic performance for SAE. Collectively, our multi-layer observational data collectively reveal a correlative gut metabolite-BNIP3L-mitochondrial homeostasis signature, which only provides preliminary associative evidence to guide future translational research targeting septic cerebral injury on sepsis-induced cerebral injury. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trials Registry, registration number ChiCTR2200067084, prospectively registered before participant enrollment.

titre: Posttraumatic growth in kidney and liver donors and recipients: a systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic growth (PTG) describes positive psychological changes following highly stressful events, including organ transplantation. Kidney and liver transplantation improve survival but pose significant psychosocial challenges for recipients and living donors. Understanding PTG and its correlates is important for strengthening psychosocial care. OBJECTIVE: To synthesise quantitative evidence on post-traumatic growth (PTG) among adult kidney and liver transplant recipients and living donors. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, five databases (CINAHL, PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Scopus) were searched between 18 March and 11 May 2025 for peer-reviewed, English-language quantitative observational studies (2015-2025) involving adult (≥ 18 years) kidney or liver transplant recipients or living donors assessed with validated PTG measures (e.g., PTGI). Data on study characteristics, PTG levels, and associated factors were narratively synthesized. Methodological quality was appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. RESULTS: Out of 276 records screened, 19 studies from eight countries were included (13 recipient-only studies, four donor-only studies, one study including both recipients and donors, and one study including recipients and family members/caregivers. PTG was generally reported at moderate-to-high levels, with higher scores commonly observed in domains related to relating to others, appreciation of life, and personal strength (as reported across studies). Study-reported positive associations with PTG included female sex, marital status, socioeconomic status, living donor graft type, time since transplantation, better perceived health, resilience, social support, adaptive coping, and spirituality. Negative associations were reported for depressive symptoms, alexithymia, and avoidant coping. Across the limited longitudinal evidence, PTG appeared higher in earlier post-transplant periods and tended to decrease over time. Methodological quality was appraised using JBI checklists; most studies had low-to-some concerns, with key limitations in confounding control and attrition reporting. CONCLUSION: PTG is commonly reported among transplant recipients and donors. The findings highlight potentially modifiable psychosocial correlates (e.g., resilience, coping, and social support) that may inform supportive care strategies across the transplant trajectory. PROSPERO REGISTRATION ID: CRD420251020904.

titre: Enhanced cognitive behavioural therapy for suicidality among people with comorbid mental and physical health conditions: study protocol of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Suicidal behaviours represent significant public health concerns. People who present with suicidal ideation and/or self-harm are at an increased risk of suicide. The presence of co-existing or comorbid mental and physical health conditions, coupled with neurobiological factors, exacerbates mental health conditions and increases the risk of suicidal behaviours. Psychotherapeutic interventions, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, have been considered first line of treatment for several standalone and comorbid populations. However, research into CBT tailored for people at risk of suicide and self-harm while living with mental and physical health comorbidities is lacking. Therefore, this pragmatic trial aims to examine the effectiveness of an enhanced CBT in addition to standard care in reducing suicidal ideation, compared to standard care only. METHODS: The study will follow a pragmatic randomised controlled trial design. The primary outcome is post-intervention severity of suicidal ideation and secondary outcomes include self-harm behaviours, depression and anxiety, coping, hopelessness, impact of comorbid conditions, and mental well-being. Additionally, blood and salivary samples will be collected to measure biomarkers of inflammation, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA)- axis, neural plasticity, and the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Participants will be randomised following stratification and blocking into the intervention and control arm, and the data will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and a 3-month follow-up. A participant safety plan specific to the project has been developed and will be implemented throughout the study duration. This protocol has been developed following the SPIRIT guidelines. DISCUSSION: People who live with long-term physical health conditions and co-existing depression, anxiety and distress are at increased risk of suicidal ideation and self-harm. Using a pragmatic randomised controlled trial methodology, the results of this study will contribute to improving our knowledge of implementing an evidence-based CBT intervention on suicidal ideation including self-harm behaviours, psychological state and biological factors. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered on ISRCTN, ISRCTN17751649. Registered on 21 August 2024, https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN17751649 .

titre: Distinct therapeutic roles of diet control and exercise in metabolic disorder-related depression: insights from metabolic and gut microbiota signatures
resume: Depression frequently co-occurs with metabolic disorders, yet the mechanisms linking metabolic dysfunction to depression remain incompletely understood. Using a chronic high-fat diet (HFD) feeding mouse model of metabolic disorder-related depression, we previously demonstrated that downregulation of astrocytic glutamate transporters in the ventral hippocampus drives depression-like behaviors through hyperactivation of ventral hippocampal glutamatergic projections to the nucleus accumbens. Although pharmacological restoration of these transporters rescued depression-like phenotypes, systemic glutamatergic modulation was associated with substantial mortality in chow-fed controls, highlighting the need for safer non-pharmacological strategies. Here, we showed that, compared with mice maintained on HFD for 12 weeks, switching from HFD to normal chow at week 9 ameliorated most metabolic abnormalities and anhedonia but failed to restore insulin sensitivity or alleviate behavioral despair. In contrast, initiation of mild-intensity treadmill running exercise at week 9 prevented further weight gain without improving metabolic dysfunction or depression-like behaviors. Neither intervention restored ventral hippocampal glutamate transporter expression, astrocytic structural integrity, nor hyperactivity within the ventral hippocampus-nucleus accumbens circuit. Notably, behavioral despair was strongly associated with systemic insulin resistance, but not overweight or corticosterone levels, implicating impaired insulin signaling as a key pathogenic factor and potential biomarker of this depression subtype. In parallel, we identified a distinct gut microbiota signature associated with HFD-induced depressive behaviors and astrocytic dysfunction. Together, these findings suggest that HFD-induced depression is driven by insulin resistance-linked astrocytic and circuit-level pathology and identify metabolic and microbial biomarkers with translational relevance for metabolic disorder-related depression.

titre: Frequency and Self-reported Outcomes of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder in the U.S. and Latin America
resume: INTRODUCTION: Obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) affects about 1-2% of the global population, with roughly 30% of patients not responding to first-line treatments. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has some support for treatment-resistant OCD but global use is unclear. METHODS: This study describes the frequency with which TMS was reported to be received among a large cohort of individuals who self-identified as Latino-Hispanic in Latin America and the United States. Among 3391 participants, 76 (2.2%) had completed TMS for OCD. RESULTS: Recipients who received TMS exhibited more severe current and lifetime OCD symptoms compared to non-recipients. On average, participants underwent 22.61 TMS sessions (SD=20.96), and self-reported experiencing minimal to some improvement from TMS. The majority of TMS recipients were from Brazil (n=26), Mexico (n=17) and USA (n=16). CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that TMS does not appear to be widely used in OCD treatment among the Latino-Hispanic population, particularly in Latin American countries. Further study of TMS efficacy and dissemination in underserved regions is warranted.

titre: Translation, Adaptation and Validation of an Instrument to Determine the Risk of Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder in Colombian
resume: OBJECTIVE: Few instruments are available for detecting avoidant restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID). The objective of this study was to translate, adapt and validate the Eating Disorders Youth Questionnaire (EDY-Q) in the Colombian pediatric population. METHODS: Culture adaptation and validation were carried out by judges. This version was applied to a sample of 104 children aged between eight and 11 years from public schools during the first semester of 2024. Reliability was analyzed, and a dimensional analysis of the construct was subsequently performed, carrying out an exploratory factor analysis and a confirmatory factor analysis. Structural equation modeling of the EDY-Q was performed with the items as units of analysis to interpret the variance in each construct. RESULTS: A Cronbach's alpha of 0.781 was found for the total, with two dimensions: selectivity (a=0.771) and avoidance/restriction (a=0.749), for a total variance of 69.775. In addition to the EDY-Q, the Child Behavior Checklist 4-18 was administered, which showed a statistically significant correlation with the EDY-Q in the domains of somatic symptoms and anxiety/depression. CONCLUSIONS: The present study presents a version of the EDY-Q for Colombian contexts with adequate validity and internal consistency.

titre: Field junction technique in MRI-guided ultra-hypofractionated radiotherapy for a long continuous target volume in prostate cancer: First clinical application, dosimetric and early toxicity outcomes
resume: BACKGROUND: MRI-guided radiotherapy (MRIgRT) on a 1.5 T MR-Linac is constrained by a 22 cm maximum field length, limiting long continuous planning target volumes (PTVs). A dual-isocenter field-junction technique has been previously validated in a phantom study. This work presents its first clinical application in hypofractionated prostate radiotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 79-year-old prostate cancer patient had six contiguous target volumes (PTV, CTV4000, PTVpubis, PGTVpubis, PTVp and PGTVnd), treated over 5 fractions with prescribed doses to the respective target volumes. PTVp was divided into PTVpup and PTVpdn, with a field overlap region between them. Two composite volumes were created: inferior volume (PTV, CTV4000, PTVpubis, PGTVpubis, PTVpdn) and superior volume (PTVpup, PGTVnd), each with its own isocenter. The inferior volume followed the adapt-to-shape (ATS) workflow. During its delivery, the superior volume was first optimized offline on daily MR images using dose feathering approach based on the inferior dose distribution. The optimized plan was then transferred for online adapt-to-position (ATP) adaptation. The inferior and superior volumes were combined offline for dose summation. The ArcCHECK phantom and ArcherQA Monte Carlo method were used for dose verification. Patient-reported outcomes, including FACT-P questionnaires, were collected during the 3-month follow-up. RESULTS: Treatment was delivered over 5 alternate-day fractions. ArcCHECK phantom gamma passing rates, using 3%/2 mm with a 10% threshold, were 96.7%, 97.1%, and 96.0% for the inferior, superior and composite reference plans, respectively. Daily ArcherQA showed consistently high passing rates across five fractions: 97.08%-98.43% for the inferior and 98.12%-98.74% for the superior volumes. CTV4000, PTV, PTVpubis and PGTVpub all met prescribed doses. PGTVnd and PTVp had intermittent underdose relative to initial prescriptions, but all fractions met second prescription limits. Organ at risks (OARs) constraints, especially for rectum and bladder, remained within tolerance across all fractions. Total treatment time decreased from 112 min in the first fraction to 80 min in the fifth fraction. FACT-P score declined from 69.17 at baseline to 55.5 at end-of-RT, partially recovering to 57.5 at 2.5 months. No urological or gastrointestinal toxicity was reported during follow-up. CONCLUSION: The proposed two-isocenter field junction technique is clinically feasible for MRIgRT of long continuous prostate cancer PTVs. It provides a practical solution for treating long PTVs on a 1.5 T MR-Linac.
revue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

titre: [Effect of electroacupuncture on mitochondrial unfolded protein response-associated proteins in the colon tissue of mice with functional constipation]
resume: OBJECTIVES: To observe the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) at "Tianshu" (ST25) and "Shangjuxu" (ST37) acupoints on the expressions of mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) - related proteins in the colon tissue of functional constipation (FC) model mice, so as to explore its potential mechanisms underlying improvement of FC. METHODS: Eighteen male C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into 3 groups:normal control (NC), FC model (M), and EA (n=6 per group). The FC model was established by gavage of loperamide suspension (1 mg/mL, 0.1 mL/10 g), twice daily for 14 d. The EA group received alternating unilateral EA stimulation of ST25 and ST37(3 Hz/15 Hz, an electric current intensity being able to induce slight tremor of the mouse's limbs) for 20 min, once daily, 5 d a week for 2 weeks. The mice in the NC and M groups underwent equivalent restraint. Gastrointestinal transit function was assessed by measuring the first blue stool discharge time, 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, and intestinal propulsion rate. Histopathological changes of the colon tissue were examined by H.E. staining, and the mitochondrial ultrastructure of colonic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) was observed by using a transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and the mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) levels were assayed using flow cytometry, and the mitochondrial ATP content in the colon tissue was measured using colorimetric assay. The immunohistochemistry stain was employed to detect the expressions of key UPRmt markers heat shock protein-60 (HSP60) and LON protease 1 (LONP1) in the colon tissue. RESULTS: Compared with the NC group, the M group exhibited a significant increase in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a considerable reduction in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP level, ATP content, and the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). Following EA intervention, compared to the M group, the EA group showed a marked decrease in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a notable increase in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP, ATP content, and the expression of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). The results of ultrastructure showed that the mitochondria of SMCs in the colon tissue was significantly swollen, with membrane damage and severe cristae rupture in the M group, while in the EA group, the mitochondrial swelling was mild, with significant improvement in the membrane and cristae integrity of the SMCs. CONCLUSIONS: EA at ST25 and ST37 can effectively ameliorate gastrointestinal dysfunction and restore mitochondrial integrity in colonic SMCs of FC mice, which may be associated with its functions in up-regulating the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins to activate UPRmt.

titre: The unresolved issue of OCD-bipolar disorder comorbidity: Evidence from a cross-sectional clinical study
resume: OBJECTIVE: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and bipolar disorder (BD) frequently co-occur, but it is unclear whether comorbid BD identifies a clinically distinct subgroup when the point of entry is OCD. Given unresolved controversies, the aim of this study was to investigate the prevalence of OCD-BD comorbidity in a large group of outpatients with OCD and compare those with and without BD. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 277 consecutive outpatients meeting DSM-5-TR criteria for OCD were recruited at a tertiary academic psychiatry unit (University of Pisa, Italy). Comorbid BD was diagnosed using the Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview. Patients were divided into OCD-only (n = 172) and OCD + BD (n = 105) groups and compared on sociodemographic, clinical, psychopathological, and pharmacological variables. RESULTS: Comorbid BD was identified in 37.9% of the sample. The OCD + BD group had later OCD onset (p = .042), higher premorbid obsessive-compulsive traits (p = .039), and fewer additional psychiatric comorbidities (1% versus 36%; p < .001). Y-BOCS total scores, symptom dimensions, suicidality, and substance use did not differ between groups. The negative correlation between age of onset and OCD severity in OCD-only patients was absent in the OCD + BD group. Treatment differed only for mood stabilizers and atypical antipsychotics. CONCLUSIONS: Comorbid BD delineates a phenotypically distinct but not more severe OCD variant when assessed from the OCD side. The attenuation of the onset-severity relationship in the comorbid group suggests that BD may modulate OCD expression through mechanisms independent of the neurodevelopmental gradient typical of pure OCD overall.

titre: Prevalence and factors associated with Rome IV-defined irritable bowel syndrome among Palestinian medical students: a multicentre cross-sectional study
resume: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the prevalence of Rome IV-defined irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and examine associated sociodemographic, academic, lifestyle, medical-history and psychological factors among medical students. DESIGN: Multicentre cross-sectional online survey. SETTING: Five medical schools across the West Bank, Palestine, from October 2025 to March 2026. PARTICIPANTS: Medical students in academic years 1–6 recruited by convenience sampling; those reporting physician-confirmed inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease or microscopic colitis were excluded. Of 1635 eligible complete respondents, 925 (56.6%) were female. The invitation denominator was unknown. PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was Rome IV-defined IBS prevalence. Secondary measures were survey-based bowel-habit patterns, IBS symptom severity, IBS-specific quality of life, generalised anxiety and adjusted associations with participant characteristics. RESULTS: Among 1635 participants, 342 met Rome IV criteria for IBS (20.9%, 95% CI 19.0% to 23.0%). Of affected participants, 57.6% had moderate and 27.2% had severe symptoms. Clinical-stage students had higher IBS prevalence than basic-science students (adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) 1.38, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.70). Compared with minimal anxiety, IBS prevalence was higher with mild (aPR 3.47, 95% CI 1.74 to 6.91), moderate (aPR 4.53, 95% CI 2.24 to 9.13) and severe anxiety (aPR 5.38, 95% CI 2.60 to 11.12). Each additional sibling was associated with modestly lower prevalence (aPR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88 to 0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in five surveyed Palestinian medical students met Rome IV criteria for IBS. Clinical-stage status and greater anxiety severity were associated with higher IBS prevalence. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporality and evaluate interventions addressing psychological distress and gastrointestinal health.

titre: Prevalence and psychological risk factors of irritable bowel syndrome among medical students in Nowshera Medical College: a Rome IV-based cross-sectional study
resume: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the prevalence of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) among medical students of Nowshera Medical College and to identify the psychological risk factors associated with it. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study using validated self-administered questionnaires. SETTING: Nowshera Medical College, Pakistan METHOD: 240 undergraduate medical students (120 men and 120 women) were recruited; all 240 completed the survey. Participants were selected via stratified random sampling across all five academic years. Inclusion required active enrolment; exclusion criteria included organic gastrointestinal conditions, lactose intolerance or ‘red flag’ symptoms (eg, haematochaezia, unexplained weight loss). Primary outcome: IBS prevalence assessed using Rome IV criteria. Secondary outcomes: stress, anxiety and depressive symptom severity, measured using Perceived Stress Scale-10, Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9, respectively. INTERVENTIONS: None. RESULTS: Of 240 students, 65 met Rome IV criteria, an absolute prevalence of 27.1% (65/240). A significant female predominance was noted (42/65 (64.6%) vs 23/65 (35.4%); p=0.006). While stress and anxiety levels were comparable between groups, students with IBS reported a significantly higher rate of depressive symptoms classified as severe (9/65 (13.8%) vs 6/175 (3.4%); p=0.013). Binary logistic regression identified depression as the only significant independent predictor of IBS (OR 1.08; 95% CI 1.01 to 1.16; p=0.034). Stress (OR 1.04; 95% CI 0.98 to 1.11; p=0.22) and anxiety (OR 0.95; 95% CI 0.87 to 1.04; p=0.29) were not independent predictors. CONCLUSION: IBS is prevalent among medical students, linked to female gender and depressive symptoms. Multivariate analysis suggests that depressive symptoms, rather than generalised stress, are the primary psychological driver of IBS in this population. Findings highlight a need for targeted mental health screening and integrated support within medical education. Longitudinal research is needed to establish causality between depressive symptoms and IBS onset.

titre: The probiotic dairy starter Propionibacterium freudenreichii CIRM-BIA129, isolated from Emmental cheese and cultivated in milk ultrafiltrate, mitigates post-colitis visceral hypersensitivity in vivo
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), with a worldwide prevalence, may include abdominal pain, gut microbiota dysbiosis, increased gut permeability and low-grade inflammation and leads to increased perception of colorectal distension. Modulatory probiotics may help treating IBS. Propionibacterium freudenreichii is a beneficial bacterium, present in raw milk and in Emmental cheese, consumed through various fermented dairy products and functional food supplements, with no noticeable side effects in vivo in healthy conditions. In the context of inflammation, including colitis and mucositis, the CIRM-BIA129 strain, which was isolated from Emmental cheese, reduces inflammation and protects the integrity of the intestinal barrier. We cultivated this strain in milk ultrafiltrate and we investigated the impact of its consumption on visceral sensitivity in rats. Rats consuming P. freudenreichii CIRM-BIA129 showed a decreased sensitivity towards colorectal distension, this being more pronounced in a post-inflammatory model of IBS and concomitant with an increase in intestinal population of Akkermansia muciniphila. This work opens new perspectives for the use of probiotic propionibacteria for the management of visceral pain and post-infectious IBS.

titre: Short and long-term mental and functional disorders in young adult Hodgkin lymphoma survivors

titre: Gut Holdemania filiformis raises brain isoallopregnanolone in progesterone-treated female mice
resume: Neuroactive 5α-steroids modulate γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor signaling and are of growing therapeutic interest: allopregnanolone (3α,5α) is a positive allosteric modulator, whereas its 3β-epimer isoallopregnanolone antagonizes this action and is itself in clinical development. Their formation has been attributed to host enzymes in the liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, whereas a contribution from any individual gut bacterium has not been demonstrated. Steroid 5α-reduction is an unusual microbial activity: among sequenced bacterial genomes, only 18 encode a recognizable steroid 5α-reductase. All available Holdemania genomes encode one of these (BaiJ-like, type 2), forming a clade distinct from the characterized Clostridium scindens BaiJ (type 1), together with a 3β-hydroxysteroid oxidoreductase. We therefore asked whether colonization with a single defined bacterium can measurably add to the host 5α-steroid pool. Consistent with this gene pair, anaerobic H. filiformis cultures converted progesterone principally to isoallopregnanolone, accumulating the intermediate 5α-dihydroprogesterone under sub-optimal conditions. In antibiotic-treated female C57BL/6 mice receiving oral progesterone, colonization with H. filiformis significantly increased isoallopregnanolone in cecal contents and brain, whereas hepatic allopregnanolone and isoallopregnanolone were unchanged. Brain isoallopregnanolone rose only in mice given both progesterone and H. filiformis, and [3,4-13C₂]progesterone tracing showed that the brain pool derived from the orally administered substrate rather than from endogenous progesterone. These findings identify Holdemania as a gut microbial source of isoallopregnanolone acting alongside host intestinal, hepatic, and cerebral steroidogenesis, and nominate H. filiformis as a candidate for microbiome-based modulation of host neuroactive 5α-steroid levels.
