titre: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization
resume: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development. After birth, rapid microbial colonization occurs in the intestine and lungs. Through signaling molecules including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs), coupled with vagal nerve and mucosal immune pathways, the microbiota maintains intestinal and pulmonary immune homeostasis, preserves blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and modulates microglial activation, thereby regulating neurogenesis, synaptic pruning, and brain functional programming. Early-life dysbiosis is commonly associated with preterm birth, cesarean delivery, infection, and antibiotic exposure. In human observational studies, it accompanies disrupted organ homeostasis and neuroinflammatory signatures, and is linked to an increased long-term risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability; in neonatal animal models, it aggravates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and encephalopathy of prematurity. Because dysbiosis frequently co-occurs with prematurity, infection, and other confounders, these associations do not by themselves establish causality. This review summarizes early-life colonization patterns of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota and their underlying neuroimmune mechanisms, analyzes the impacts of dysbiosis on neuroimmunity and related diseases, and proposes intervention strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for neonatal health protection and neurodevelopmental disorder prevention.

titre: Effects of a Prebiotic Functional Soda on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Adults Receiving GLP-1-Based Therapy for Weight Management: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial
resume: AIMS: Gastrointestinal (GI) adverse effects are common during glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapy and may negatively affect quality of life (QOL) and treatment persistence. This pilot evaluated the effects of daily consumption of a prebiotic functional soda on GI symptom burden in adults who recently initiated GLP-1-based therapy for weight management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled pilot, 80 adults receiving semaglutide or tirzepatide for weight management and experiencing at least one GI symptom were randomized 1:1 to consume a prebiotic functional soda (OLIPOP; 1 can/day, with the option of 2 cans/day) for 4 weeks or continue their usual free-living fluid intake. The primary outcome was change in Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) total score. Secondary outcomes included GSRS subscales, health-related QOL (SF-36), stool characteristics and frequency, appetite and cravings, dietary intake and GI rescue medication use. RESULTS: Sixty-eight participants completed the study (intervention, n = 36; control, n = 32). GSRS total score decreased significantly more with the prebiotic functional soda than control (adjusted least-squares [LS] mean change, -0.931 vs. -0.405; between-group difference, -0.526 [95% CI: -0.713 to -0.339]; p < 0.001). Greater reductions were observed for constipation, abdominal pain and indigestion relative to control. The group difference in overall SF-36 scores was also significant (p = 0.037). CONCLUSIONS: Four weeks of daily prebiotic functional soda consumption was associated with greater reductions in participant-reported GSRS scores compared with usual fluid intake among adults receiving GLP-1-based therapy for weight management. These preliminary findings warrant confirmation in larger, blinded trials using a matched beverage control. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07744360.

titre: When endoscopy is not required: reducing low value care for more sustainable endoscopy - European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Position Statement Update 2026 recycling ESGE published guidelines and position statements
resume: BACKGROUND: The European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) published its first Position Statement on digestive conditions that do not require endoscopy in 2020. Since then, multiple ESGE guidelines have expanded recommendations that promote appropriate indications, de-escalation of surveillance, and evidence-based avoidance of low value procedures. In parallel, avoiding unnecessary endoscopy has emerged as a major strategy for reducing the environmental burden of gastrointestinal endoscopy. This updated Position Statement consolidates such ESGE recommendations into a practical framework defining when endoscopy is not required. METHODS: This Position Statement is based exclusively on recommendations developed or endorsed by ESGE. Recommendations from ESGE Guidelines and Position Statements published in Endoscopy were systematically reviewed and synthesized. Positive recommendations advocating alternative management strategies were reformulated, where appropriate, into explicit "do not perform endoscopy" statements without modifying the underlying evidence or recommendation strength. The resulting document provides a clinically oriented synthesis rather than new guideline recommendations. RESULTS: Recommendations covering upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy, endoscopic ultrasound, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, capsule endoscopy, and therapeutic endoscopy were identified. Across these modalities, four overarching scenarios emerged in which endoscopy is not required: screening when endoscopy does not meaningfully prevent disease incidence or improve relevant outcomes; surveillance when repeat endoscopy provides no additional benefit beyond an adequate index examination or when expected benefit is limited by age, co-morbidity, or life expectancy; diagnostic endoscopy when validated noninvasive strategies provide sufficient information or when endoscopic findings are unlikely to change management; and therapeutic endoscopy when intervention does not improve clinically relevant outcomes compared with conservative or alternative management. Additional principles include avoiding redundant investigations and unnecessary repetition of adequately performed procedures. Together, these recommendations provide a framework for reducing low value endoscopy while limiting patient burden, healthcare resource use, and environmental impact. CONCLUSIONS: An appropriate indication is the cornerstone of high quality endoscopy and the primary driver of sustainable endoscopic practice. Endoscopy should be avoided when it does not provide meaningful additional benefit in screening, surveillance, diagnosis, or therapy. Applying these principles can improve patient safety, optimize healthcare resources, and reduce the environmental footprint of endoscopy. This updated ESGE Position Statement provides an evidence-based framework for high value, patient-centered, and sustainable endoscopic practice.

titre: "Patient Experiences During and Beyond Treatment with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Qualitative Research and Implications for Gastrointestinal Cancer"
resume: METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research (ENTREQ) guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Global Health, and Journals@Ovid for studies published between January 2014 and January 2025. Eligible studies were qualitative or mixed methods reports of patient experiences with ICIs; studies that did not report primary patient data were excluded. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for qualitative research, and the data were analyzed thematically. RESULTS: Thirty studies published between 2017 and 2025 were included, covering melanoma, lung cancer, and mixed solid tumor populations. Analysis identified six overarching themes: (1) prognostic uncertainty and expectations; (2) information needs and decision-making; (3) treatment burden and physical functioning; (4) psychosocial identity and social roles; (5) emotional and existential well-being; and (6) economic and practical impact. Patients generally perceived ICIs as more tolerable than chemotherapy but reported persistent toxicities, uncertainty regarding treatment durability, and psychosocial strain. The perspectives and experiences of caregivers regarding treatment discontinuation were underrepresented. No study specifically examined GI cancers. CONCLUSIONS: ICIs are experienced as both a lifeline and a burden. The absence of GI cancer perspectives represents a critical research gap in this field. Future studies should prioritize GI cancers, caregivers, long-term survivors, and patients with poor outcomes to inform patient-centered supportive care. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: This review highlights the need for personalised communication, routine assessment of psychosocial well-being, and proactive management of irAEs in patients receiving immunotherapy. Multidisciplinary supportive care should address the physical, psychological, practical, and financial impact of treatment. Given the limited representation of GI cancers in the current literature, further work is needed to ensure supportive care strategies adequately reflect the needs of this population. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024568112.

titre: Haze and health: a mixed method approach exploring physical and psychological challenges of smog faced by university employees in Pakistan
resume: The present study was designed to explore the role of smog on the physical and psychological health of university employees in Lahore, Pakistan, during November 2024. A mixed-methods approach was designed to assess the relationship between perceived air quality, psychological distress (depression, anxiety, stress), and physical symptoms (respiratory, digestive, sleep disturbances, headaches) in university employees. Study 1 was a cross-sectional survey of 350 university employees to assess the relationship between study variables. Results indicate a significant positive relationship between poor air quality, psychological and physical symptoms. In study 2, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 employees, exploring their exposure to smog and its impact on their physical and psychological health and the coping strategies they use to overcome these impacts. Thematic analysis highlighted greater vulnerability among older employees and those with preexisting conditions. Challenges included respiratory and cardiovascular issues, increased stress, cognitive impairments, and reduced productivity. Institutional shortcomings like inflexible policies worsened impacts. Recommended interventions include remote work, improved indoor air quality, and mental health support to alleviate these challenges and enhance well-being.

titre: Fear of cancer recurrence and coping experiences in gastrointestinal tract cancers: a phenomenological study
resume: BACKGROUND: Fear of cancer recurrence is common in gastrointestinal tract cancers and can adversely affect psychosocial well-being and coping. The aim of this study was to evaluate fear of cancer recurrence and coping experiences in gastrointestinal tract cancers with a phenomenological approach. METHODS: In this descriptive phenomenological study, semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with gastrointestinal tract cancer patients who were hospitalized in the general surgery service of a hospital in a province in the east of Turkey. The data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step descriptive phenomenological method. The study was conducted and reported according to the COREQ checklist. RESULTS: Three main themes emerged: psychosocial impacts, coping strategies, and coping with fear of cancer recurrence. Participants experienced fear of death, anxiety, sadness, uncertainty, depressed mood, and pessimism, alongside hope and a feeling of rebirth. They coped through religious beliefs and prayer, family and social support, hobbies, and healthy living habits. In response to fear of cancer recurrence, participants used denial or avoidance, acceptance and preparation, and taking control through regular check-ups and precautions. CONCLUSIONS: Patients with gastrointestinal tract cancers experience fear of cancer recurrence alongside considerable psychological distress, and they draw on spiritual, family-based, and health-oriented strategies to cope. Nursing care should assess fear of cancer recurrence and support adaptive coping strategies.
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

titre: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents
resume: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

fiche.verdict: Les questionnaires spécifiques détectent une altération de la qualité de vie liée aux troubles intestinaux chroniques post-chirurgie de Hirschsprung.

titre: Median arcuate ligament syndrome: Current evidence and controversies-A narrative review
resume: Median arcuate ligament syndrome is a rare and controversial cause of chronic abdominal pain, attributed to extrinsic compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament. The 2025 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider median arcuate ligament syndrome a diagnosis of exclusion and recommend management in specialized multidisciplinary centers. Anatomical compression of the celiac artery has been recognized for over a century, but a clear clinicopathological entity remains disputed. Median arcuate ligament syndrome is rare, with an estimated incidence of about 1.3 (0.5-3.6) per 100,000 inhabitants in a recent Dutch population study. Patients, predominantly women, typically present with long-standing postprandial epigastric pain and, in most cases, weight loss, often after years of extensive investigations for more common gastrointestinal disorders. Both ischemic and neurogenic mechanisms have been proposed, and data support elements of each. Diagnostic work-up relies on exclusion of differential diagnoses and imaging evidence of ⩾70% celiac artery stenosis, often with dynamic testing. Laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic decompression and video-assisted retroperitoneal decompression of the celiac artery are now the preferred approaches. Clinically significant symptom improvement is reported in up to 80% of operated patients, although treatment failure rates close to 50% have also been reported in large multicenter cohorts. Median arcuate ligament syndrome remains a challenging and controversial diagnosis with limited high-quality evidence. Careful patient selection, multidisciplinary evaluation, and realistic expectations regarding prognosis are essential. Ongoing randomized controlled trials and studies on objective ischemia biomarkers and quality of life may help refine indications and improve outcomes.
revue: Scandinavian journal of surgery : SJS : official organ for the Finnish Surgical Society and the Scandinavian Surgical Society

titre: Longitudinal analysis of email-based consultation support for gastrointestinal stromal tumor in Japan
resume: BACKGROUND: Supportive care reduces anxiety and improves quality of life for cancer patients, yet individuals with rare cancers often face unique challenges due to limited access to reliable disease-specific information and specialist expertise. Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is a rare cancer for which several molecular-targeted agents have been introduced over the past two decades. This study retrospectively analyzed email consultations submitted to a GIST expert platform to characterize temporal changes in consultation needs and email-specific challenges. METHODS: We reviewed 596 email consultations comprising 952 emails received between 2003 and 2025. Inquirers were medical professionals (n = 144), patients (n = 240), and family members (n = 196), companies (n = 4), or unknown/not applicable (n = 12). Background information, consultation topics, and challenges were extracted and categorized. RESULTS: During the first decade, the active drug-development period, many inquiries originated from healthcare professionals and focused on diagnosis and investigational treatment. In the second decade, inquiries increasingly came from patients and family members, and addressed treatment planning, adverse-event management, and access to disease-specific experts. Among patients and family members, 28% requested referral to specialists or specialized hospitals. Consultations for patients aged >70 years or < 20 years were mainly submitted by family members. Major challenges were insufficient medical information and unclear inquiry intent. CONCLUSIONS: GIST-related email consultations showed a shift from professional inquiries about diagnosis and drug development to patient- and family-centered needs regarding standard treatment and specialist access during the past two decades. Effective email consultation requires sufficiently precise clinical information.

fiche.population: 596 consultations par email (952 emails) reçues entre 2003 et 2025 (soignants, patients, familles)
fiche.intervention: Consultation et support d'information par email pour le GIST

titre: Phygital dining: A postmodern framework for food experience, agency, and well-being in blended physical-digital eating environments
resume: Recent developments across food service settings reflect a structural shift toward multisensory, artistic, and technology-driven dining formats. However, academic literature remains split: scholarship on digital food environments emphasizes operational efficiency and convenience, whereas multisensory research commonly evaluates environmental cues as static, top-down interventions that position diners as passive recipients. This perspective article introduces phygital dining as a novel postmodern framework that reconceptualizes eating as a liquid, agency-driven, and evolving meaning-making process unfolding within integrated physical-digital food ecosystems. Grounded in postmodern consumer theory and positioned at the intersection of phygital scholarship, gastrophysics, and experiential food research, this framework proposes that harmonizing digital augmentation with physical atmospherics and human mediation can support mindful savoring and may enhance interoceptive awareness and intrinsic self-regulation through greater diner agency, attentional focus, and sensory engagement. To articulate this conceptual shift, the article presents a five-pillar model comprising: (1) experiential drivers, (2) hybrid eating contexts, (3) liquid meaning-making, (4) triadic sensory-digital-human design, and (5) inclusivity and equity. These pillars explain how agency-centered phygital experiential design may shape food choice, attentional focus, emotional tone, and perceived well-being. Kitchen Theory is then examined as an illustrative case showing how the five pillars operate in practice. Finally, the article outlines managerial implications for food experience design, hospitality innovation, and health-oriented environments, alongside an empirical research agenda on agency-driven consumption in blended physical-digital food ecosystems.

resultats_cles: Proposition d'un modèle à cinq piliers intégrant design sensoriel, numérique et humain
Lien potentiel entre design phygital, attention, intéroception et bien-être
fiche.conclusion: Le design phygital centré sur l'agentivité peut façonner l'expérience alimentaire et le bien-être perçu.

titre: Integrative Approach to Cancer Pain Management in Pregnancy - A Narrative Review
resume: Background and objectiveCancer-related pain management in pregnancy presents significant challenges due to its complexity and the limitations that exist with conventional treatments. This review describes various forms of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) practices, highlighting their appropriate indications, adverse effects, and reasonable expectations for outcomes in treating cancer-related pain during pregnancy.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, SCOPUS, and Google scholar, to identify relevant studies published in English up to 2024. Narrative reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analysis, case reports, observational studies, and RCTs that mentioned CAM techniques for cancer pain management or pain management in pregnancy were included.Key content and findingsCAM is being increasingly used in the cancer population. It encompasses a range of practices such as acupuncture, yoga, hypnosis, guided imagery, aromatherapy, and herbal remedies, which have shown promise for pain control, reduce stress and anxiety, and lower the need for analgesic drugs in cancer and pregnancy populations studied separately. Integrating these practices with careful consideration of safety profile and efficacy addresses the immediate need for pain relief and supports holistic care.ConclusionCancer pain management in pregnancy presents unique challenges mainly because of the need to consider maternal-fetal health and the complex pathophysiology of cancer pain. A limitation of this study is that clinical efficacy and quality of the studies have not been evaluated for CAM techniques in management of cancer pain in pregnancy. In the future, the main focus should be on conducting prospective studies to evaluate the safety and efficacy of integrative treatment plans.

titre: Clinical Hypnosis for Chronic Pain: Review and Research
resume: This issue of the International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis (IJCEH) addresses the problem of chronic pain. Clinical hypnosis has a considerable research base attesting to its benefit in relieving chronic pain. However, there is much that is not yet known about its efficacy for specific chronic pain conditions and the feasibility of alternative delivery methods such as digital health delivery of clinical hypnosis. Among the questions addressed in this issue of the IJCEH are: "What is the efficacy of clinical hypnosis for osteoarthritis and arthritis-relatedpPain? How effective is clinical hypnosis for non-cancer pain? Does clinical hypnosis combined with exercise benefit individuals with fibromyalgia? What are the effects of clinical hypnosis on chronic pelvic pain and urogenital pain syndromes in women? Can clinical hypnosis for chronic low back pain be effectively delivered through digital health media? Is telemedicine a feasible strategy for delivery of clinical hypnosis for chronic neuropathic pain? The information and answers to these questions advances scientific knowledge and expands clinical applications of hypnosis in chronic pain management.
revue: The International journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis

titre: Effects of App-Based Mindfulness Training on Dental Patients' Anxiety Symptoms Prior to Undergoing Dental Surgery: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Dental anxiety is associated with treatment avoidance, poor oral health-related quality of life, increased procedural complications, and poor postoperative recovery. Negative appraisals may exacerbate anxiety and increase emotional and physiological arousal. Mindfulness may improve attentional and emotional regulation, and reduce dental anxiety through improved self-regulation. OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to investigate the effects of an app-based mindfulness intervention among patients experiencing dental anxiety prior to undergoing surgery. METHODS: Using a mixed methods design consisting of a randomized controlled trial and semistructured interviews, 100 participants will be randomized to an app-based mindfulness training or a control condition. Data will be collected prior to the start of the intervention (T0), postintervention, but presurgery (T1), and postsurgery (T2). Our primary outcome is dental anxiety; secondary outcomes include general anxiety, perceived stress, positive and negative affect, mindfulness, and postoperative pain. Analyses of covariance, mixed analyses of variance, and independent-samples 1-tailed t tests will be used to investigate within-group and between-group differences across 3 time points. Semistructured interviews will be conducted with 15 to 20 participants from the intervention group to explore patients' experiences; qualitative analyses will be conducted by 2 independent coders. RESULTS: Recruitment began in April 2026, and the first screening was completed on April 6, 2026. To date, 19 participants have completed the study, and 4 interviews have been completed. Study completion is projected for August 2027, with publication of the findings anticipated in December 2027. The study has not received any funding. Relative to T0, we expect significantly greater improvements across our primary and secondary outcomes among intervention group participants compared with control group participants at postbaseline time points. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings may inform future efforts to implement cost-effective interventions in dental care settings to manage dental anxiety in order to reduce both stress- and anxiety-related burdens for patients and dentists.

titre: Not All Fakes Are Equally Ugly: The Anti-AI Bias in Aesthetic Judgment and the Role of Affect, Self-Relevance, and Authenticity
resume: Art is devalued once it is attributed to artificial intelligence (AI). Whether this anti-AI bias is a generic penalty for non-original works or specific to the absence of a human author is unknown, as is how long it lasts. In a preregistered study, 324 participants rated 48 genuine human paintings, each presented as an Original, a human Forgery or AI-Generated, on beauty, valence, meaningfulness and monetary worth, then judged how synthetic (AI vs. human) and authentic (copy vs. original) each was. Forgeries were rated below Originals on every dimension, and AI-Generated works about twice as low, the AI-specific penalty falling most heavily on meaningfulness. The labels did not alter gaze, and their effects did not depend on the emotional content or personal relevance of the artworks. Artworks labelled AI-Generated were judged more synthetic and, less clearly, Forgeries less original, and the more beautiful an artwork, the more likely it was judged human-made, even when unlabelled. About six weeks later (n = 220), after learning that all artworks were human originals, participants no longer rated previously AI-labelled works as less beautiful. They had forgotten the labels but remembered what they had believed, and reconstructed the labels from these beliefs and their initial appraisal. The bias tracked attitudes toward AI, not interoceptive sensibility or visual imagery. The anti-AI bias thus combines a generic non-originality penalty with a penalty specific to the missing human author: it acts at the moment of judgment, yet leaves beliefs that outlast the memory of the label.

fiche.verdict: L'attribution à l'IA dévalorise l'art plus fortement que la contrefaçon humaine, indépendamment de la sensibilité intéroceptive.
fiche.population: 324 participants (220 au suivi à 6 semaines)
fiche.intervention: Évaluation de 48 tableaux étiquetés Original, Contrefaçon humaine ou Généré par IA
resultats_cles: Les œuvres étiquetées IA sont notées deux fois plus bas que les contrefaçons.
Le biais suit les attitudes envers l'IA, pas la sensibilité intéroceptive.
À 6 semaines, l'effet disparaît après révélation, mais les croyances persistent.
fiche.conclusion: Le biais anti-IA combine une pénalité de non-originalité et une pénalité liée à l'absence d'auteur humain.
limites: Prépublication non évaluée par les pairs
fiche.pertinence_raison: Hors champ clinique digestif et psychothérapeutique, simple mention de l'intéroception.
fiche.titre_court: Biais anti-IA dans le jugement esthétique
fiche.conclusion_simple: Le jugement esthétique pénalise fortement les œuvres attribuées à l'IA, un biais lié aux attitudes plutôt qu'à l'intéroception.

titre: Duodenal Responses to Food Challenges in Patients With Self-reported Food Intolerances: a Feasibility Study
resume: The goal of this study is to investigate the feasibility of using intravenous fluorescein during a standard endoscopy-along with a laser to activate it and an optical filter-to identify changes in the duodenal mucosa after a controlled food challenge in individuals with IBD and IBS who experience food intolerances. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Is this technique feasible approach to assess food intolerances in patients with IBD and IBS? * Does patients with IBD and IBS exhibit acute tissue changes upon exposure to specific food antigens? Researches will compare the food antigen to a placebo solution (saline solution without an antigen) to see if the reaction in the tissue is different. Participants will: * Answer questionnaires. * Provide a blood and stool sample. * Take an allergy test. * Undergo an upper endoscopy.

titre: Pilot Study for the Evaluation of a City-hospital Pathway for Early Management of Acute Pain in Oncology
resume: In France, the number of new cancer cases across all cancer types was estimated at 382,000 in 2018. The impact of pain on a patient's quality of life is profound, with physical consequences (insomnia, fatigue, loss of appetite), psychological effects (anxiety, depression, demoralization, attention deficit, memory disorders), and social repercussions. Acute pain induced by cancer, when poorly managed, can lead to the development of secondary chronic pain syndrome. The French National Authority for Health (Haute Autorité de Santé, HAS) deplores the late referral of patients with chronic pain, which complicates treatment and limits opportunities for improvement. Cancer-related pain has become a chronic condition in 50% of patients, leading to anxiety-depressive syndromes as well as social consequences such as social isolation or difficulty returning to professional activity. In France, the 2017 White Paper by the SFETD (French Society for the Study and Treatment of Pain) notes that, despite three successive Cancer Plans integrating supportive care into the comprehensive management of cancer patients, one in three patients does not receive analgesic treatment appropriate to the intensity of their pain. To prevent chronic pain, the HAS recently recommended early assessment of acute pain (within less than a week) with a high-quality city-hospital organization.

titre: Discoid/Double Discoid Excision Versus Segmental Resection for Rectal Deep Endometriosis Nodules <5 cm: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Bowel Complications and Functional Outcomes
resume: This clinical trial will compare two types of surgery for endometriosis affecting the rectum, the lower part of the bowel. It will include 200 women aged 18 to 45 years who have symptoms and a single area of rectal endometriosis smaller than 5 cm. All participants must need surgery and be suitable for either procedure. The main questions are: Do the two procedures differ in the risk of bowel complications within 90 days after surgery? How do the procedures affect bowel function, quality of life, and pain? Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups: Discoid or double discoid excision: The surgeon removes one or two overlapping discs of the affected bowel wall without removing an entire bowel segment. Segmental resection: The surgeon removes the affected bowel segment and joins the remaining bowel ends. Both procedures will be performed using keyhole surgery. Assignment will take place during surgery, after the surgeon confirms that either procedure is suitable. Researchers will compare bowel complications, including leakage from the bowel closure, narrowing of the rectum, and abnormal connections between the bowel and nearby organs or tissues. Participants will complete questionnaires about quality of life and bowel function before surgery and at 6 and 12 months afterward. Researchers will also assess pain, recovery, and the need for further surgery. Follow-up will continue for up to 24 months to assess later symptoms and further treatment.

titre: STEP - Stressor-focused Therapy for Emotional Processing in ICD-11 Adjustment Disorder: A Randomised Waitlist-Controlled Trial
resume: This randomized controlled trial evaluates the efficacy of STEP, a brief 12-session psychotherapy for adults with ICD-11 Adjustment Disorder (AjD). STEP is a manualized, CBT-based, event-focused intervention designed to reduce Adjustment Disorder symptoms and support adaptive emotional processing and coping. Participants in the waitlist control group will receive STEP after the 12-week waiting period. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and at a 3-month follow-up. The primary outcome is Adjustment Disorder symptom severity. Secondary outcomes include perceived stress, depression, anxiety, well-being, and experiential avoidance.

titre: Rare miRNA variants in complex neuropsychiatric pedigrees alter synaptic miRNA gene-targets
resume: Although rare non-coding variants are likely involved in psychiatric disorder susceptibility, their contribution is poorly understood. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression, and targets in the brain include genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic plasticity. Because single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) can alter miRNA processing and target specificity, this can have disproportionate downstream impact on multiple genes affecting pathways that regulate biological processes, making them compelling candidates for mediating psychiatric disorder risk. We investigated rare miRNA variants in whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 25 pedigrees with diagnoses including schizophrenia, psychosis, bipolar disorder, depression, OCD, and substance use disorder. Evidence of segregation with schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders was identified for five rare miRNA variants (two seed-region, one mature-region, and two precursor-region variants), including a SNV in the mature-region of miR-4794, segregating strongly in two unrelated pedigrees and identified in a parent-offspring pair with schizophrenia from a third pedigree. One of these two pedigrees also segregates a seed-region SNV in miR-4423-3p, predicted to significantly impact expression-regulation, causing the loss of synaptic gene-targets associated with psychiatric disorders. Collectively, targets of three of the miRNAs are enriched for schizophrenia rare variant risk genes (p-value: 0.00027): six SCHEMA genes were targeted by miR-96 and four genes by miR-4423-3p. While further understanding of miRNA function and validation is required, this study demonstrates the value of integrating structural modelling, target-shift prediction, and pathway enrichment to interpret non-coding variants. This highlights the utility of WGS for identifying and investigating rare non-coding variation in psychiatric disorder susceptibility, supplementing exome-based approaches.

titre: Structural characterisation of the effect of 5-chloroindole on orthosteric activation of murine 5-HT3A receptors
resume: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: 5-HT3 receptors play a central role in gut-brain signalling, and their hyperactivity is associated with pathologies ranging from chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting to irritable bowel syndrome. While the principles governing 5-HT3R orthosteric pharmacology are well established (spanning antagonists, partial agonists and full agonists), structural insights into allosteric mechanisms remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which a positive modulator of 5-HT3R, 5-chloroindole, potentiates agonist response by fine-tuning orthosteric activation of this receptor. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Here, we investigated the molecular basis of modulation by 5-chloroindole (5-CI), a selective positive allosteric modulator, using cryo-EM and electrophysiology. We present 5-HT3AR structures in the presence of 5-CI alone, as well as in combination with either submaximal concentrations of 5-HT or saturating concentrations of the partial agonist SMP-100. KEY RESULTS: Our results reveal that 5-CI potentiates 5-HT3R through a distinct mechanism involving co-occupancy of the orthosteric site and with additional modulation through an intersubunit site in the transmembrane domain. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This mode of action is reminiscent of benzodiazepine modulation in GABAARs, yet it notably occurs within homomeric binding sites. Together, these findings establish the structural basis for the previously reported ago-allosteric mechanism of 5-CI, which becomes functionally apparent only in the presence of agonistic ligands.

resultats_cles: Co-occupation du site orthostérique et modulation intersous-unité.

fiche.conclusion: Établit la base structurale du mécanisme ago-allostérique du 5-CI sur les récepteurs 5-HT3.

titre: Rome V biopsychosocial model and pediatric disorders of gut-brain interaction: recommendations for clinicians
Reversible Xerophthalmia in an Autistic Child With Selective Eating
resume: Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) is a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness. Increasingly, severe nutritional deficiencies are recognized in urban settings among children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) due to extreme dietary selectivity. A 9-year-old girl with ASD and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder presented with a 2-month history of bilateral ocular redness and photophobia refractory to topical therapies. Examination revealed a Bitot's spot, conjunctival keratinization and a corneal epithelial defect in the right eye and left inferior conjunctival xerosis. Diagnosed with xerophthalmia secondary to VAD, she also had multiple micronutrient deficiencies and nutritional rickets. Management included intravenous vitamins A and D, oral multivitamins, and electrolyte correction. Within 1 month, ocular changes fully resolved, leaving a superficial right corneal scar. Chronic, treatment-resistant ocular symptoms in children with ASD should prompt suspicion of VAD. Early multidisciplinary intervention and prompt supplementation are vital to prevent permanent blindness.

titre: Early Response and End-of-Treatment Outcomes in Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder
resume: OBJECTIVE: Early symptom change is among the most robust predictors of eating disorder treatment outcomes, but it has not been examined for the psychological features of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID). We tested whether early change in food neophobia, sensory sensitivity, and lack of interest in food/eating during cognitive-behavioral therapy for ARFID (CBT-AR) predicted end-of-treatment severity and subsequent improvement. METHOD: Participants were 25 non-underweight youth with ARFID (ages 10-18; 72% male; 92% white) in the 15-session CBT-AR arm of a randomized controlled trial; 23 treatment completers were analyzed. Hierarchical regressions tested whether early change (improvement from Sessions 1 to 5) predicted Session 15 severity and improvement from Sessions 5 to 15, controlling for baseline severity; additional models controlled for Session 5 severity. RESULTS: Greater early change predicted lower Session 15 severity in food neophobia (β = -0.85), sensory sensitivity (β = -0.72), and lack of interest (β = -0.67; all ps < 0.001), explaining 42%-44% of additional variance. Controlling for Session 5 severity, early change added little (ΔR2 = 0.001-0.09; ps = 0.090-0.847). Early change also did not predict improvement after Session 5 (ps = 0.085-0.369), and most improvement occurred later in treatment. DISCUSSION: In CBT-AR, early gains were maintained, but early responders did not improve faster thereafter. Session 5 severity, more than the magnitude of early change, indicated end-of-treatment severity. Session-by-session monitoring may help identify youth likely to remain symptomatic, but limited early change should not be taken to mean later improvement is unlikely.
revue: The International journal of eating disorders

titre: Not all plant-based diets are alike: intake of minimally processed plant foods is associated with gut microbial richness among vegetarians and vegans
resume: Plant-based diets are usually defined by what they exclude, overlooking which plant foods are eaten and how processed they are. Here we examine whether this overlooked dimension is related to the gut microbiome. In a cross-sectional study of 172 omnivorous, lacto-ovo-vegetarian and vegan adults profiled by shotgun metagenomics, vegetarians and vegans harboured fewer gut species than omnivores. Within this group, however, each standard deviation increase in minimally processed plant-food intake was associated with 27 additional species (p = 0.001), independently of fibre intake, and richness in participants with the highest intake approached that of omnivores. No such association was seen among omnivores. Higher intake was also linked to more species previously associated with favourable cardiometabolic health and to better health-related quality of life. Dietary labels alone may therefore conceal meaningful variation in the gut microbiome, and characterising how plant foods are processed may help in understanding how plant-based diets relate to health.

titre: Night shift work and abnormal defecation among physicians: The chain mediating effect of hindrance stress and anxiety
resume: Abstract Background Epidemiological evidence links night shift work to gastrointestinal dysfunction, yet research focused on clinical physicians is insufficient, with existing studies mostly targeting nurses and focusing on physiological mechanisms. Based on the Challenge-Hindrance Stressor Model, this study explored the relationships between night shift work, hindrance stress, anxiety and abnormal defecation among clinical physicians, as well as the chain mediating effects of hindrance stress and anxiety. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from April to May 2026. 447 clinical physicians from 17 hospitals across 9 Chinese provinces were recruited via convenience sampling. SPSS 29.0 and PROCESS macro 5.0 were used for statistical analysis including correlation analysis, serial mediation test and gender subgroup analysis. Results 74.3% of physicians worked regular night shifts, 39.1% had abnormal defecation, and 46.8% had anxiety. Night shift work had no direct effect on abnormal defecation, but exerted influence via three indirect pathways, among which only the chain mediation pathway (night shift work → hindrance stress → anxiety → abnormal defecation) was statistically significant, with an effect size of 0.050 and total indirect effect of 0.142. Gender differences were found in mediation effects. Conclusion Night shift work indirectly increases the risk of abnormal defecation in clinical physicians through the chain mediating pathway of hindrance stress and anxiety, which is the core mechanism. This study provides evidence for medical institutions to optimize shift schedules and protect physicians' health.

titre: Kluyveromyces marxianus CIDCA 8154 Attenuates Intestinal Damage in a Murine Model of Irinotecan Induced Mucositis Without Affecting Anti-Tumor Efficacy
resume: Intestinal mucositis is a common and severe side effect of cancer chemotherapy that continues to have a detrimental impact on patients' quality of life and treatment outcomes. Irinotecan is one of the chemotherapeutic drugs most frequently associated to this condition. Therefore, the development of new strategies to prevent or reduce mucositis remains a clinical need. Probiotics have been suggested as potential candidates for mucositis prevention and some bacterial strains have shown a protective effect.In this study, we evaluate the effect of the probiotic yeast Kluyveromyces marxianus CIDCA 8154 in a murine model of irinotecan induced intestinal mucositis. Administration of K. marxianus 8154 significantly improved clinical symptoms, reducing body weight loss and diarrhea development. In addition, it preserved gut mucosal integrity, attenuating villus shortening, crypt hyperplasia and decreasing the proportion of crypts containing proliferating cells. Mice receiving K. marxianus 8154 also showed decreased gut myeloperoxidase activity and eosinophilic infiltrate suggesting a reduced inflammatory injury. In vitro, K. marxianus 8154 reduced intestinal epithelial inflammatory response induced by irinotecan decreasing activation of Caco-2 ccl20-luciferase reporter cells and IL-8 secretion. Moreover, probiotic treatment mitigated irinotecan-induced oxidative stress, by reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in liver and gut, while preserving at basal levels irinotecan induced activation of the antioxidant master regulator Nrf2. Importantly, treatment with K. marxianus 8154 did not impair the ability of irinotecan to control CT-26 cell-derived tumor growth. These findings suggest that K. marxianus 8154 has a protective role on irinotecan induced intestinal mucositis without impairing its anti-tumoral activity.

titre: Continuous multimodal neuromonitoring of zolpidem-induced paradoxical awakening in chronic incomplete locked-in syndrome: ventral pontine deafferentation, cross-modal complementarity, and cardio-cortical dissociation
resume: OBJECTIVE: Zolpidem paradoxically restores responsiveness in select disorders of consciousness (DOC) cases, yet real-time electrophysiological and autonomic dynamics across the pharmacodynamic trajectory remain uncharacterized in incomplete locked-in syndrome (LIS). METHODS: A 52.18-min multimodal recording tracked baseline, enteral zolpidem administration (min 22.39), absorption, corticomotor peak, and plateau in a 42-year-old male with chronic LIS from pontine infarction. Analytics included continuous qEEG (0.5-70 Hz), microstates (Classes A-D), beta-band weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI) connectomics, heart rate variability (HRV), and heartbeat‑evoked responses (HER). RESULTS: Baseline deafferentation showed severe theta slowing (48.36 ± 4.14%) and phase hypersynchrony. Following enteral administration, the following changes were observed: 1. viscero-cortical dissociation: Infusion triggered an immediate HRV VHF surge (>80%) while the cortex remained quiescent for 14.1 min. 2. Corticomotor consolidation: Between min 36.5-46.0, relative beta surged (+266.89%) while theta dropped (-30.74%). Microstates accelerated into frontocentral Classes C/D, and connectomics demonstrated long-range edge pruning with selective frontocentral recruitment (wPLI > 0.40). 3. Interoceptive gating: During peak beta emergence, cardio-cortical communication collapsed; evoked global variance profile dropped > 60% (1.03 to 0.22 µV) alongside frontocentral dipole suppression. CONCLUSIONS: Paradoxical awakening is a coordinated multisystem process. Zolpidem disinhibits spared corticomotor networks while filtering ascending visceral baro-afferents, enabling an outward-facing behavioral state decoupled from internal interoception.

titre: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
resume: Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1-3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune-metabolic homeostasis4-9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

fiche.population: Rats (modèles de diabète de type 1 et 2)
fiche.intervention: Dispositif NeuroAxis (neurostimulation en boucle fermée)

Réduction de l'inflammation systémique chronique
fiche.conclusion: Ce dispositif représente une approche générale pour réguler la communication inter-organes et l'inflammation.

titre: Does Early-Life Participation in SNAP Improve Adult Mental Health? Evidence From a Regression Discontinuity Design
resume: We investigate the long-term impacts of participation in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) before age 18 on adult mental health outcomes. Utilizing data from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID) spanning 1968-2019, we link adult individuals to their parental households to source early-life experiences, parental information, and adulthood mental health outcomes. To identify the causal impacts of early-life SNAP participation on mental health, we employ a regression discontinuity design (RDD) that exploits state-level gross income eligibility thresholds for SNAP enrollment during early life as the cutoff. Results reveal that early-life SNAP participation reduces the probability of being diagnosed with mental illnesses in adulthood by nearly two percentage points (or 19.6% in relative terms), primarily driven by reductions in depression, mania, schizophrenia, drug or alcohol abuse, and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). This effect is most pronounced among individuals who participated in SNAP before the age of six and is greater for females than for males. Additionally, early-life SNAP participants are diagnosed with mental health conditions about 3.7 years earlier than non-participants.

titre: Electroacupuncture Alleviates Anxiety-like Behaviors and Modulates Gut Microbiota, Neurotransmitters, and Inflammatory Responses in Chronically Stressed Rats
resume: Abstract Objective: Based on the gut–brain axis theory, this study aimed to investigate the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) at Baihui (GV20) and Zusanli (ST36) on anxiety-like behaviors, neurotransmitters, inflammatory factors, intestinal neuropeptides, and gut microbiota in rats with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) induced by chronic restraint stress (CRS). The study sought to evaluate the therapeutic effects of EA on GAD, explore its potential underlying mechanisms, and provide a scientific basis and novel therapeutic insights for the use of EA in GAD treatment. Methods: Forty male specific pathogen-free (SPF) Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats were randomly assigned to four groups: a control group, a model group, an EA group, and a drug treatment group. A rat model of GAD was established using CRS. Rats in the EA group received EA at Baihui (GV20) and Zusanli (ST36) (1 mA, 2 Hz, 15 min) 1 h before daily CRS exposure for three consecutive weeks. Rats in the drug treatment group received paroxetine hydrochloride (20 mg/kg) by oral gavage 1 h before daily CRS exposure for three consecutive weeks. Anxiety-like behaviors were assessed using the elevated plus maze (EPM) and Open Field Test (OFT). Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure the levels of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) in intestinal tissues, as well as serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). Western blotting was performed to determine the protein expression levels of γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit α1 (GABRA1) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in the hippocampus. Gut microbiota composition was analyzed using 16S rDNA gene sequencing, followed by correlation analyses between microbial taxa and the measured biological parameters. Results: Compared with the control group, CRS-exposed rats exhibited pronounced anxiety-like behaviors, accompanied by decreased levels of 5-HT and GABA in intestinal tissues and reduced hippocampal expression of GABRA1 and BDNF, as well as increased serum levels of IL-6 and TNF-α and elevated intestinal VIP levels. Compared with the model group, EA significantly alleviated anxiety-like behaviors, increased 5-HT and GABA levels and GABRA1 and BDNF expression, and decreased IL-6, TNF-α, and VIP levels. 16S rDNA gene sequencing revealed that EA was associated with alterations in gut microbiota composition and richness. Correlation analyses identified associations between Duncaniella and members of the family Erysipelotrichaceae and selected neurotransmitter and inflammatory markers. Conclusions: 1. EA increased intestinal 5-HT and GABA levels, upregulated hippocampal GABRA1 and BDNF expression, reduced serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels, and modulated abnormal intestinal VIP levels in GAD model rats. These findings suggest that EA may exert anxiolytic effects by regulating neurotransmitter balance, promoting neuroplasticity, and suppressing inflammatory responses. 2. EA may exert its anxiolytic effects through the gut–brain axis by modulating gut microbial homeostasis and influencing neurotransmitter regulation and inflammatory responses.

titre: Voluntary Movement Initiation Is Associated with Cardiac Input in Libet's Task
resume: The relationship between motor intention and initiation of voluntary movement remains a fundamental topic in neuroscience, originating from the seminal framework of B. Libet, introduced in 1983. Libet's paradigm significantly influenced discussions on intentionality, motor control, and free will. However, methodological critiques continue to challenge its interpretations, specifically the accuracy and validity of the "urge to move" phenomenon. One understudied factor in this debate is the potential influence of interoceptive signals-such as cardiac activity-in shaping the experience of motor intention and movement initiation. In our study, we addressed this gap by examining whether cardiac signals modulate participants' experience of the "urge to move," using behavioral and electrophysiological measures in 39 healthy human participants (17 males and 22 females) performing Libet's task. Crucially, when participants were asked to follow the "urge to move," their button press timings were predominantly aligned with the diastolic phase of the cardiac cycle, indicating cardiac modulation of movement initiation. However, analyzing heart-evoked potential (HEP) amplitudes as a measure of cardiac input perception, we observed no differences in HEP amplitudes associated with changes in introspective demands during the task in both source and sensor spaces. Our results suggest that implicit perception of cardiac signals biases voluntary action initiation in Libet's task, independently of cortical interoceptive markers. These findings have implications for models of motor preparation, intentionality, and the bodily basis of voluntary action, challenging conventional interpretations of motor intention and informing debates on volition and interoception.
revue: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

titre: Cross-informant validation of the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview in adolescents: Agreement between child and parent reports
resume: Background Reliable assessment of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) in young people may require information from both children and caregivers, yet cross-informant agreement has not been examined for the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI). This study evaluated agreement between child and parent PARDI interviews for ARFID diagnosis, individual DSM-5 Criterion A, ARFID dimensions, and overall severity. Methods Twenty children aged 11–14 years screening positive for ARFID and one parent per child were recruited from the ARFID InitiativE Sweden (ARIES) cohort. Children and parents completed separate PARDI interviews with trained interviewers. Parent–child agreement was assessed using percentage agreement and Cohen’s kappa (κ) for categorical ratings of ARFID diagnosis and Criterion A consequences. For continuous ratings of ARFID dimensions and overall severity, agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and paired t-tests comparing mean parent and child scores. Results Parents gave higher mean scores than children across all continuous domains, although the difference was statistically significant only for overall severity (raw mean difference=0.42, p=.003). Parent–child agreement was poor for sensory sensitivity (ICC=0.42), moderate for lack of interest (ICC=0.63) and overall severity (ICC=0.71), and excellent for concern about aversive consequences (ICC=0.95). ARFID was identified in 17/20 parent interviews and 14/20 child interviews; diagnostic agreement was 75% (κ=0.31, p=.133). Agreement was perfect (100%) for Criterion A1, high for A2 and A3 (both 95%), and lowest for psychosocial impairment (A4; 65% agreement, κ=0.19). Item-level findings indicated a general tendency toward higher parental ratings, although children provided higher ratings on selected items involving food restriction, sensory experiences, hunger cues, and abdominal pain. Conclusions Child and parent PARDI interviews provided overlapping but non-interchangeable information. Agreement varied across different aspects of ARFID, with greater discrepancies for psychosocial impairment and sensory sensitivity. These differences may partly reflect what children and parents are able to observe or experience directly. Multi-informant assessment may therefore offer a more complete account of pediatric ARFID than either response alone. Plain English Summary Children may experience and describe avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) symptoms differently from how their parents observe and report them. We compared separate child and parent diagnostic interviews using the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI) in 20 pairs to understand how closely their assessments of ARFID agreed. Parents and children often provided similar information, but agreement differed depending on what was being assessed. They agreed more closely about effects on weight, growth, and nutrition, and about fears of aversive consequences of eating such as choking or vomiting. Agreement was lower for how eating difficulties affected daily and social life, for lack of interest in food or eating, and for sensitivity to the taste, texture, or smell of food. Parents generally rated the overall severity of eating difficulties higher than children, although children gave higher ratings for some experiences, such as difficulty recognizing hunger, discomfort with messy or sticky foods, and fear of abdominal pain. These findings suggest that children and parents provide overlapping but not identical information about ARFID. Child and parent accounts may each highlight different aspects of ARFID, making both perspectives valuable sources of information during assessment.

titre: Lactobacillusgasseri JM1 Alleviates Functional Constipation in Mice: Effects on Intestinal Motility, Aquaporin Expression, and Gut Microbiota
resume: Background: Functional constipation (FC) is a common digestive system disease that seriously affects the life of patients. Probiotics are potential strategies to alleviate FC, but the mechanism of action of lactobacilli, especially Lactobacillus gasseri (Lb. gasseri) is unclear. The purpose of this study was to screen and evaluate the efficacy and potential mechanisms of Lb. gasseri JM1 in alleviating FC. Methods: Five highly adherent strains were screened from 20 strains of lactobacilli through adhesion assays. The optimal strain was identified through in vivo experiments, and a preliminary safety assessment was performed using antibiotic susceptibility screening, hemolysis, and indole production assays. A mouse model of FC was established using loperamide hydrochloride, and the following parameters were evaluated: fecal parameters, intestinal transit rate, colonic tissue morphology, colonic mRNA expression of motility-related genes and aquaporins, serum levels of gastrointestinal regulatory factors, and gut microbiota composition. Results: Lb. gasseri JM1 was most effective at relieving constipation among the tested strains and exhibited no detectable hemolytic activity or indole production. This intervention significantly increased fecal water content (p < 0.0001), shortened the time to first black stool from 121.73 ± 5.74 to 85.67 ± 5.39 min (p < 0.0001), and improved intestinal propulsion rate from 27.42 ± 8.17% to 45.45 ± 4.76% (p < 0.05) in the medium-dose group compared with the Model group; increased colonic mRNA expression of stem cell factor (SCF), c-kit, and connexin 43 (Cx43); decreased aquaporin 3 (AQP3) and aquaporin 4 (AQP4) mRNA expression; increased aquaporin 9 (AQP9) mRNA expression; elevated serum motilin (MTL) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels while lowering peptide YY (PYY) and vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) levels; and increased the relative abundance of Firmicutes, Akkermansia, and Coprococcus in the gut microbiota. Conclusions: Lb. gasseri JM1 effectively alleviates constipation symptoms in FC mice. The observed effects may be associated with changes in SCF and c-kit mRNA expression accompanied by changes in Cx43 and aquaporin mRNA expression, as well as alterations in the levels of gastrointestinal regulatory factors and the composition of the gut microbiota. This study provides experimental evidence supporting Lb. gasseri JM1 as a candidate probiotic for alleviating functional constipation.

titre: Vagal Cholinergic Anti-Inflammatory Pathway and Gastrointestinal Microenvironment Remodeling Mediate Electroacupuncture Restoration of Gastric Motility in Functional Dyspepsia
resume: Functional dyspepsia (FD) is closely associated with gastric dysmotility and enteric nervous system (ENS) dysfunction. Here, we investigated the mechanisms by which electroacupuncture (EA) at ST36 modulates in vivo ENS dynamics and restores gastric motility in FD. Using iodoacetamide-induced FD and ChATGCaMP6s transgenic mice, gastrointestinal (GI) transit was tracked via in vivo X-ray imaging, while the real-time calcium activity of antral myenteric cholinergic neurons was recorded through a customized optical gastric window. Concurrently, gastroduodenal tissue cytokines, brain–gut peptides, and motility-related proteins were systematically quantified. Our results demonstrated that EA significantly accelerated delayed gastric emptying and whole-gut transit. In vivo imaging revealed that EA reversed the pathological functional inertia of antral choline acetyltransferase-positive (ChAT+) neurons, elevating their activation rate from 1.11% in FD to 27.78%. Rather than replenishing depleted prokinetic hormones, EA selectively suppressed elevated inhibitory peptides (SST, CCK, VIP) to release the pathological “motor brake”. Concurrently, EA intervention was associated with upregulated α7nAChR expression, attenuation of tissue proinflammatory cytokine levels, restored C-Kit protein expression, and downregulation of TRPV1 expression. These findings indicate that EA at ST36 rescues FD gastric dysmotility by awakening dormant cholinergic motor neurons and releasing the inhibitory neuroendocrine brake via coordinated neuro-immune regulation.

titre: Efficacy of Ayurveda Treatment Protocol Compared to Vonoprazan in Patients with Functional Dyspepsia (Amlapitta): Research Protocol for a Randomised Controlled Trial
resume: Introduction: Functional Dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterised by postprandial fullness, early satiety, and epigastric pain.Conventional management typically focuses on acid suppression and symptom control through pharmacotherapy. While this approach may provide temporary relief, concerns about recurrence and long-term safety highlight the need for alternative and complementary therapeutic strategies for effective long-term management of FD. Need of the study: This study evaluates a predefined, RAND/UCLA consensus-developed, standardised doshabased Ayurveda treatment protocol against standard pharmacotherapy. Vonoprazan is selected as the comparator, as current clinical guidelines recommend acid-suppressive therapy as the first-line pharmacological approach for FD, and vonoprazan, a potent potassium-competitive acid blocker, represents a contemporary option. Aim: To assess the efficacy and safety of a dosha-based Ayurveda protocol compared with vonoprazan in patients with FD. Materials and Methods: This open-label, randomised, parallel-group trial will be conducted at KAHER Shri BMK Ayurveda Mahavidyalaya and KLE Ayurveda Hospital, Belagavi, Karnataka, from January 2026 to May 2027. Sixty participants meeting ROME-IV diagnostic criteria for FD will be included. Participants will receive either the predefined dosha-based Ayurveda protocol or vonoprazan therapy for 28 days, with follow-up until day 56. Primary and secondary outcomes will evaluate dyspepsia severity, symptom burden, Quality of Life (QoL), and safety using validated tools. Depending on distribution, intergroup comparisons will be performed using the independent t-test or Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables, and Chi-square or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables. Intragroup comparisons will use the paired t-test or Wilcoxon signedrank test. A p-value <0.05 will be considered statistically significant.
revue: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

titre: The role of the kynurenine pathway in chronic muscle pain
resume: Chronic muscle pain, or chronic myalgia, is a common cause of disability among women worldwide. Muscle-related temporomandibular disorders, including local myalgia (MYA) and myofascial pain with referral (MFP), may represent its local and regional forms, respectively, whereas fibromyalgia (FM) represents its widespread form. These conditions frequently co-occur and are highly comorbid with depression, insomnia and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). However, their underlying mechanisms, and whether these mechanisms differ across local, regional and widespread chronic myalgia, remain unclear. The kynurenine pathway (KP), the primary pathway of tryptophan (TRP) metabolism, may play an important role through its effects on immune and glutamatergic processes. This thesis used a systematic review with meta-analysis and three clinical studies to investigate whether alterations in the KP contribute to the pathophysiology of chronic myalgia and its high comorbidity burden. The systematic review (Study II) searched five databases and synthesised blood levels of TRP, serotonin and kynurenine (KYN) in local or generalised chronic musculoskeletal pain. The clinical studies included a total of 566 women representing the pain spectrum, from pain-free controls (CTR) to patients diagnosed with MYA, MFP and FM. All participants completed validated questionnaires on pain and psychosocial burden. In Study I, we compared comorbid conditions between MYA (n = 80), MFP (n = 81) and FM (n = 81), using validated cut-off scores for these questionnaires. In Study III, microdialysis of the masseter muscle was performed in CTR (n = 13), MYA (n = 13) and MFP (n = 15) over 220 minutes to examine the effects of a 20-minute tooth-clenching exercise on the KP. In Study IV, a morning venous blood sample was collected from CTR, MYA, MFP and FM (n = 80 per group). Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry quantified TRP, KYN, kynurenic acid, 3- hydroxykynurenine (3-HK), quinolinic acid (QUIN), picolinic acid and nicotinamide (NAM). The systematic review indicated altered TRP metabolism in chronic musculoskeletal pain, but the evidence was limited and of very low certainty, and the studies of KYN were too few and inconsistent to pool or to establish a role for the KP. In Study I, MFP and FM more often reported IBS, depression, anxiety, somatic symptoms, stress and insomnia than MYA. FM also reported more IBS, depression and somatic symptoms than MFP (all P < 0.05). The number of comorbidities was higher in MFP and FM than in MYA (P < 0.001) and was associated with widespread pain. In the masseter muscle, NAM increased during tooth clenching in all groups, whereas TRP, KYN and QUIN increased only in MFP (q ≤ 0.02). In plasma, QUIN, 3-HK and the QUIN/KYN ratio increased in an ordered trend from CTR to MYA to MFP to FM (q ≤ 0.043). Together with psychosocial scores, the ratio could also separate patients from CTR (P < 0.001). In a cluster analysis, the same measures separated lower- and higher-burden biopsychosocial profiles, regardless of diagnosis. Overall, our findings suggest that the KP may play a role in chronic myalgia, particularly in those with widespread pain and a greater symptom burden. The results also suggest that patients with local, regional and widespread chronic myalgia overlap along a shared spectrum. Further studies are warranted to confirm our findings and should assess the potential of the KP to support mechanism-based management. List of scientific papers I. titre: Leakage-aware supervised machine-learning classification of normal and abnormal calf lung-sound recordings: a proof-of-concept study
resume: Digital auscultation with supervised machine learning (ML) may support objective calf lung-sound interpretation. This proof-of-concept study evaluated supervised ML using a curated multicenter dataset and leakage-aware validation. Digital lung-sound recordings were collected from pre-weaned dairy and dairy-crossbred calves in Canada, Italy, and Sweden, using a standardized digital auscultation protocol and were independently reviewed by two observers, with discrepant initial classifications resolved by consensus. Of 1,360 recordings, 424 met the predefined audio-quality criteria; 39 were subsequently excluded under the acoustic inclusion criteria and five duplicate copies were removed, yielding 380 unique recordings for analysis. The 380 retained recordings were each assigned one of five single-label consensus acoustic categories: Normal sounds, Crackles, Wheezes, Increased Breath Sounds (IBrS), and Increased Bronchial Sounds (IBS). Recordings were partitioned into 304 training and 76 held-out internal test recordings, with all recordings from the same calf (ear-tag identifier) kept in the same partition. Feature sets and tree-based ML algorithms were evaluated using five-fold stratified group-aware cross-validation. The primary task distinguished Normal from Abnormal recordings, with Abnormal comprising recordings assigned to Crackles, Wheezes, IBrS, or IBS. Two exploratory single-label multiclass tasks were evaluated secondarily: a three-class task comprising Normal sounds, Adventitious sounds (Crackles and Wheezes), and Increased sounds (IBrS and IBS), and a five-class task retaining the five individual consensus acoustic categories. On the held-out internal test set, a 94-feature non-amplitude Extra Trees classifier achieved accuracy of 0.816, balanced accuracy of 0.814, macro-F1 of 0.802, area under the ROC curve of 0.930, and average precision of 0.963; sensitivity and specificity for Abnormal recordings were 0.820 and 0.808. Exploratory three- and five-class macro-F1 values were 0.607 and 0.470, respectively. In this curated multicenter dataset, supervised ML showed promising discrimination between Normal and Abnormal calf lung-sound recordings under group-aware validation, whereas finer single-label acoustic-category classification remained less reliable. These findings warrant external validation of automated lung-sound analysis as an objective aid for respiratory screening and health monitoring in pre-weaned dairy calves.

titre: Orientation-Dependent Hydration Dynamics of FfIBP Adsorbed on a Gold Surface
resume: Abstract The interface between antifreeze proteins (AFPs) and inorganic nanoparticles is a nanobiointerface at which protein orientation and interfacial hydration may jointly influence protein function. Here, atomistic molecular dynamics simulations were used to examine the adsorption of the hyperactive Flavobacterium frigoris ice-binding protein (FfIBP) on a planar gold (Au) surface and to relate adsorption geometry to the structure and dynamics of layer-resolved hydration water. Starting from three orientations, FfIBP adopted two distinct adsorption configurations during the simulations while retaining its overall fold, and the ice-binding site (IBS) showed no concerted expansion or contraction. Adsorption through the A-face or B-face led to similar tilted geometries, whereas adsorption through the C-face produced a nearly flat, persistent contact with a narrow protein-Au gap. In the tilted geometries, water–water hydrogen bonding (HB) generally decreased in the first hydration layer, whereas water residence increased mainly beyond the first hydration layer. At the C-face of AuC, water–water HB increased slightly in the second hydration layer, while interfacial water showed longer-lived individual HBs, substantially longer residence times, and slower escape from the interfacial region, with outward exchange selectively reduced and the longest retention occurring near the Au surface. Tetrahedral order at this interface, however, was lower than in the Control. These results indicate that adsorption orientation is associated with differences in the location and magnitude of interfacial water reorganization, and that adsorption on gold may alter the accessibility and hydration environment of the ice-binding surface without major structural disruption of the IBS. Because each system was simulated using a single trajectory, these orientation-dependent differences should be interpreted in the context of the sampled trajectories.
revue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B

titre: Predicting under-five mortality in Bangladesh through comparative survival analysis using traditional, machine learning, and deep learning models
resume: Under-five mortality (U5M) remains a persistent public health challenge in Bangladesh, where 36.6 deaths per 1,000 live births separate the country from the SDG 3.2.1 target of 25. Standard survival models have shaped our understanding of this burden for decades, but their rigid structural assumptions limit how much of the underlying predicted risk architecture they can recover. Using data on 13,119 children from the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS), this study systematically compares eight survival models across three methodological paradigms: traditional Cox proportional hazards and its penalized variants (Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net), ensemble methods (Random Survival Forest (RSF) and Gradient Boosting Survival Analysis (GBSA)), and deep learning architectures (DeepSurv and DeepHit). A two-stage feature selection procedure: univariate Cox screening followed by Random Survival Forest permutation importance identified 15 predictors for model development. Performance was evaluated across discrimination, probabilistic accuracy, time-dependent AUC, and calibration, with stability confirmed across six k-fold configurations ( \(k = 5\) -30) via Friedman’s test ( \(p = 0.223\) ), while external validation was performed using an independent Nepal Demographic and Health Survey cohort processed with an identical analytical pipeline. DeepHit achieved the strongest joint performance: concordance index (C-index) of 0.977, Integrated Brier Score (IBS) of 0.016, mean time-dependent Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.987, and calibration slopes of 0.99–1.04 across three follow-up years, the only model in this comparison to approach ideal calibration. RSF led on C-index (0.978) but showed systematically inflated calibration slopes (1.42–1.45), while Cox-family models were competitive on discrimination but severely miscalibrated. Pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests further demonstrated that the performance differences between the best-performing models and conventional survival approaches were statistically significant ( \(p < 0.05\) ) with large effect size. In the Nepal cohort, DeepHit maintained its performance without retraining, with a C-index of 0.9663 and a mean AUC of 0.9811. The relative rankings of the other models also carried over. Number of living children, total children ever born, and antenatal care intensity consistently dominated feature importance, locating the strongest mortality signal in maternal reproductive history rather than socioeconomic status alone.
