titre: The Gut Microbiota/Gut Brain/BDNF Axis Mediates Ginsenoside Re’s Neuroprotection in Parkinson’s Disease
resume: Ginseng, as a traditional medicinal and edible resource, has shown potential in the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, particularly Parkinson’s disease (PD), through its active components, ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe). This study aimed to systematically investigate the neuroprotective effects and molecular underpinnings of total ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe) in a 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) induced PD mouse model, with a focus on gut-brain axis modulation. The results showed that GS and GsRe ameliorated motor deficits, reduced substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) dopaminergic neuron loss, restored intestinal barrier integrity, and reversed gut dysbiosis. Mechanistically, GsRe crossed the BBB (Blood brain Barrier), upregulated brainderived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and inhibited the TLR4 adaptor WDFY1, blocking excessive NFκB activation, M1 microglial polarization, and neuronal apoptosis. BDNF deficiency exacerbated TLR4 pathway hyperactivation, suggesting that BDNF modulates TLR4mediated neuroinflammation and contributes to the neuroprotective effects of GsRe. GS and GsRe target the gutbrain axis as an integrated hub: normalizing gut microecology to limit peripheral inflammatory signal translocation, while suppressing central neuroinflammation via the BDNF/TLR4 axis. These findings reveal a gut microbiota/gut brain axis whereby GsRe alleviates neuroinflammation by concurrently modulating gut microbiota composition and the BDNF/TLR4 pathway, providing a mechanistic basis for GS/GsRe based PD interventions.

titre: Intestinal ischemia–reperfusion injury and gut-brain axis alteration: a possible pathway to sex-specific neurodegeneration
Parkinson's Disease: Molecular mechanism, Biomarkers, and advances in therapeutic Development
resume: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder and a rising global health challenge, owing to population aging and increasing disease prevalence. Existing therapeutic strategies provide mainly symptomatic relief, but significant progress has been made in understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying PD that has accelerated the development of disease-modifying interventions. This review summarizes the recent progress in PD research, including advances in disease pathogenesis, biomarker discovery, therapeutic development, and precision medicine. We discuss the complex interplay between α-synuclein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, impaired autophagy-lysosomal and ubiquitin-proteasome systems, dysregulation of the gut-brain axis, and genetic susceptibility as the basis of disease progression. Recent advances in genetic profiling and multi-omics technologies have greatly improved our understanding of disease heterogeneity and identified novel therapeutic targets. The review also provides an overview of established and emerging biomarkers including cerebrospinal fluid α-synuclein seed amplification assays, neurofilament light chain, neuroimaging modalities, digital biomarkers, wearable technologies and artificial intelligenceassisted diagnostic approaches for facilitating early diagnosis and disease monitoring.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Beyond the Plate: New Frontiers in Nutrition and Dietetics
resume: From Planetary Sustainability to Cellular Metabolism: New Horizons in Nutrition The bond between human health and food extends far beyond the confines of the daily plate. In an era where global climate change threatens food systems, ultra-processed foods dominate modern diets, and digital platforms actively shape eating behaviors, adopting a holistic perspective on nutritional science is no longer optional—it is imperative. This volume provides a comprehensive exploration of the field, bridging planetary food security and microbial protein technologies with the gut-brain axis, chrononutrition, clinical dietary interventions, and eating disorders driven by digital food environments. Comprising seventeen specialized chapters, this authoritative work delivers evidence-based analyses, serving as an indispensable guide for healthcare professionals, scholars, and researchers. Key Topics Covered: • Climate crisis, sustainable food systems, and alternative protein sources • The impact of ultra-processed foods on the gut microbiota and metabolic health • Contemporary dietary approaches to Type 2 diabetes, cardiometabolic disease, and fatty liver • Nutritional management in special populations, including cystic fibrosis, ADHD, and the postmenopausal period • Digital misinformation, nutrition literacy, orthorexia nervosa, and athletic performance An essential reference for clinicians, registered dietitians, researchers, and students seeking a rigorous, evidence-based, and integrative view of contemporary developments in human nutrition and dietetics.

titre: Assessment of the efficacy and safety profile of correcting metabolic disorders and intestinal dysbiosis using “Bactizym Enzymbiotic” in patients with metabolic syndrome
resume: The prevalence of obesity and associated metabolic syndrome has reached global epidemic proportions. The intestinal microbiota is a key modulator of not only nutritional status but also systemic inflammation, lipid, and carbohydrate metabolism. Enzymbiotics, which combine enzymes, prebiotics, and metabiotics, represent a promising approach for the correction of metabolic syndrome. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Bactizym Enzymbiotic in the correction of metabolic disorders and the intestinal microbiome in patients with metabolic syndrome. Materials and Methods: A total of 138 patients with metabolic syndrome were examined (study group: n=92, treated with Bactizym Enzymbiotic for 1 month; comparison group: n=46, no treatment). The dynamics of body mass index, bioimpedance analysis (visceral fat), lipidograms, carbohydrate and hormonal profiles, Colonoflor 16 intestinal microbiota PCR, metabolomics parameters, anxiety, and appetite were studied. Results. Compared to the control group, 65% of patients in the study group reported an improvement in well-being, while 16% experienced a decrease in appetite. A decrease in waist circumference (Δ -3.8 cm, p < 0.05) and visceral fat (Δ -27.4%, p < 0.01) was noted, as were improved sleep quality and decreased anxiety (Δ -33,3%, p<0.01), as well as a decrease in triglyceride levels (Δ -29.5%, p < 0.05), and an increase in Bacteroides spp. and Akkermansia muciniphila (p=0.02 and p=0.05), a significant decrease in HOMA-IR (Δ -36.4%, p<0.01), LPS endotoxemia (Δ -54.9%, p<0.001), an increase in GLP-1 (Δ +61.9%, p<0.001) and adiponectin (Δ +57.4%, p<0.001). Conclusion. The use of Bactizym Enzymbiotic is associated with a multisystemic positive effect: correction of dysbiosis, reduction of metabolic endotoxemia, improvement of insulin resistance and atherogenic profile, modulation of the gut-brain axis. The drug can be considered an effective and safe component of MS therapy.

titre: Research Progress on Peripheral Physiological Responses and Central Neural Activity Characteristics of Competitive Anxiety
resume: Competitive anxiety is a core psychological factor constraining athletes’ competitive performance. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on its peripheral physiological responses and central neural activity characteristics. At the peripheral level, the autonomic nervous system has been associated with a dual imbalance of sympathetic dominance and parasympathetic suppression. Nonlinear heart rate variability indices have been proposed to be more sensitive than linear indices in one small BMX study, but this remains preliminary and requires replication. Anticipatory cortisol elevation in the HPA axis has been interpreted within the inverted-U hypothesis, with high-trait-anxiety individuals showing delayed recovery dynamics in preliminary studies. Temporal characteristics of catecholamines in the SAM system may be more predictive of performance than absolute concentrations. Oxytocin and progesterone have been proposed as protective neuropeptide mechanisms, whereas sustained elevation of β-endorphin may mask fatigue perception and suppress immunity; these mechanisms remain largely hypothetical. Gut–brain axis research suggests anxiety-associated microbiota restructuring, and probiotic interventions have been associated with improved EEG activity and cognitive function in preliminary trials. At the central level, the Neurovisceral Integration model has been proposed as a framework for peripheral–central interactions. Prefrontal–limbic circuit dysfunction has been proposed to contribute to cognitive interference and somatosensory amplification. Frontoparietal attentional network imbalance may contribute to shortened quiet eye periods and impaired executive function. Cortical neural oscillations have been characterized by enhanced β-band activity with suppressed α/θ activity in some studies. Dysregulation of 5-HT/NE/DA neurotransmitter systems has been proposed to contribute to functional reorganization of the triple brain network through BDNF-mediated synaptic plasticity alterations; this remains a hypothetical integrative pathway. It should be emphasized that many findings derive from heterogeneous designs, small samples, and non-athlete or non-competitive populations; conclusions should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Future research should integrate wearable monitoring, ecological momentary assessment, and machine learning to develop individualized interventions based on neurobiological phenotypes, pending validation of the proposed biomarkers.

titre: A rare case of Valentino syndrome presenting as acute right lower quadrant pain: a case report
resume: Abstract Background Valentino syndrome is a rare clinical entity in which a perforated peptic ulcer causes extravasation of gastrointestinal contents into the right lower quadrant, mimicking acute appendicitis. It is seldom reported in the literature but has significant diagnostic implications due to its deceptive presentation. Case Presentation A 33-year-old male presented with a 4-day history of worsening right lower quadrant abdominal pain accompanied by nausea. There was a long history of intermittent NSAID use. On physical examination, the right lower quadrant was tender with guarding and rebound tenderness. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis. Computed tomography demonstrated an 8-mm appendix suspicious for early acute appendicitis, together with mild prepyloric antral wall thickening and surrounding perigastric inflammatory changes, raising suspicion of a contained peptic ulcer perforation. Diagnostic laparoscopy was initially performed and was converted to open surgery after identification of the suspected gastric perforation. Intraoperatively, the appendix was mildly inflamed and hyperemic, and an appendectomy was performed. Further exploration revealed fibrinopurulent inflammatory changes over the anterior gastric region, with the suspected perforation contained by the omentum. No active leakage was observed, and the suspected perforation site was reinforced with omentopexy. The postoperative course was uneventful; the patient was discharged on postoperative day 5 with dietary, PPI and NSAID avoidance counseling. Conclusion Valentino syndrome should be included in the differential diagnosis of right lower quadrant pain, especially in patients with risk factors for peptic ulcer disease. Early imaging and thorough evaluation can prevent misdiagnosis and reduce morbidity.

titre: Sensory and Metabolic Changes Across the Menopausal Transition: Role of Estrogens and the Microbiome
resume: Menopause is a major life transition characterized by declining estrogen levels and increased risk of central adiposity, metabolic syndrome, and cardiovascular disease. Beyond these well-recognized metabolic consequences, menopause may also influence appetite regulation, food reward, sensory perception, and dietary behavior. This narrative review examines the interplay between estrogen decline, eating behavior, food perception, and the gut and oral microbiota during the menopausal transition. Evidence from human longitudinal studies indicates that menopause is associated with central fat redistribution and loss of lean mass, partly independently of chronological aging. Experimental studies in ovariectomized animals suggest that estradiol regulates homeostatic and hedonic feeding pathways and modulates sensitivity to gastrointestinal signals involved in appetite control. However, direct evidence on these mechanisms in menopausal women remains limited. Menopause-related changes in salivary secretion, taste perception, and olfactory function may also influence food preferences and eating patterns. In parallel, emerging but heterogeneous studies suggest that menopause may be associated with alterations in the gut microbiome which might indirectly participate in metabolism and dietary behavior, although causal relationships have not been demonstrated. Changes in the oral microbiome and salivary metabolome may further contribute to sensory alterations, although this area remains poorly characterized and hypothetical. Overall, menopause should be considered a multidimensional transition in which hormonal, metabolic, sensory, behavioral, and microbial factors interact. Better understanding these interactions may help us to identify targets for nutritional strategies that support healthy eating, metabolic health, and quality of life during midlife.

titre: Rational Use of Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs: Adverse Effects and Safe Prescribing
resume: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are among the most widely used medicines in the world. They are prescribed for pain, fever and inflammation and are freely available without a prescription, which leads to frequent self-medication. At the same time, NSAIDs cause serious adverse effects: gastrointestinal ulcers and bleeding, cardiovascular events, kidney damage and clinically important drug interactions. This review summarizes the mechanism of action of NSAIDs, their classification by cyclooxygenase selectivity, the main adverse effects and the evidence from large randomized trials and meta-analyses on their comparative safety. Based on this evidence, practical principles of rational NSAID use are formulated: the lowest effective dose for the shortest time, assessment of individual gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risk, gastroprotection in high-risk patients, avoidance of dangerous combinations and particular caution in elderly patients.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Research progress on short-chain fatty acids in Graves’ disease and thyroid eye disease
resume: Short-chain fatty acids are principal metabolites generated by gut microbiota during dietary fiber fermentation. They play essential roles in preserving intestinal barrier integrity and maintaining host immune homeostasis. Graves’ disease and its principal ocular complication, thyroid eye disease, are closely related autoimmune thyroid disorders. Together they impose a substantial burden on patient health and quality of life, presenting an important clinical challenge. Recent evidence indicates that reduced levels of these bacterial metabolites, particularly butyrate, are closely linked to the onset and progression of both conditions. This review summarizes current evidence on how changes in gut microbiota-derived metabolites contribute to these two disorders. In Graves’ disease, reduced production of short-chain fatty acids is associated with systemic immune dysregulation. These metabolites restore the balance between pro-inflammatory T helper 17 cells and regulatory T cells, suppress autoantibody generation by B lymphocytes, and preserve intestinal barrier integrity. In thyroid eye disease, beyond these systemic immune benefits, short-chain fatty acids—especially butyrate—can act directly on orbital fibroblasts to inhibit local inflammation, fibrosis, and fat accumulation, thereby slowing pathological tissue remodeling behind the eye. Therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating gut microbiota or directly supplementing short-chain fatty acids may offer novel promising approaches for managing Graves’ disease and its associated eye disease.

titre: Long-term Pouch Complications and Management in the 21st Century
resume: Abstract This article provides a comprehensive overview of long-term pouch complications following IPAA. Normal pouch function includes 7 to 8 bowel movements daily, no pain, no bleeding, minimal incontinence, and an excellent quality of life, akin to a healthy population. Complications can be classified into inflammatory, mechanical (fibrostenotic, penetrating, and technical), neoplastic, and functional categories, each presenting distinct challenges and management strategies. The prevention of complications is crucial, particularly through careful surgical technique and patient selection. Surgical volume significantly impacts outcomes, highlighting the need for procedures to be performed at experienced centers. Early complications often result from technical issues, with anastomotic leakage being the most common cause of pouch failure. Gender-specific concerns, such as infertility and long-term sexual dysfunction, may arise after pelvic surgery. Ultimately, a thorough understanding of these complications and their management is essential for optimizing patient outcomes and quality of life post-surgery, with salvage procedures, such as redo IPAA, providing viable options for many patients experiencing pouch failure. The management of complex long-term pouch complications requires a multidisciplinary team-based approach among healthcare providers at high-volume centers.

titre: Longitudinal trajectories of the 11 KOQUSS-40 domains after gastrectomy : a secondary analysis of the WECARE multicenter pilot randomized controlled trial
resume: Background: The KOQUSS-40 total score may mask divergent recovery across eight symptom domains; the primary report of the WECARE multicenter pilot randomized controlled trial quantified only two domains. We report estimates, confidence intervals (CIs), and effect sizes for all domains and examine clinical correlates of recovery. Materials and Methods: Eighty-eight patients undergoing curative gastrectomy at nine Korean hospitals were randomized to the WECARE digital platform or standard care; 77 completers were analyzed (WECARE, 39; control, 38). Linear mixed-effects models estimated between-group differences at 6 months and in change from baseline. Twenty characteristics and pathological stage were explored as correlates of the trajectory. Results: The total score fell from 88.1 to 80.3 (WECARE) and 81.5 (control) at 1 month and recovered to 85.3 and 83.6 at 6 months (difference, 1.7 points; 95% CI: −3.0 to 6.4; Cohen’s d: 0.14). Time had a clear effect (partial η 2 =0.140), unlike the group-by-time interaction ( P =0.590). No domain differed at 6 months; only general quality of life differed in change from baseline (−12.4 points; 95% CI: −24.1 to −0.7), reflecting a higher WECARE baseline. Indigestion fell by approximately 30 points at 1 month and remained 18–19 points below baseline at 6 months. No characteristic was robustly associated with the trajectory; sensitivity analyses were consistent. Conclusion: In this pilot trial, postgastrectomy quality of life changed primarily with time, with no detectable platform effect. Indigestion and bowel habit change remained below baseline at 6 months. Larger confirmatory trials are needed.

titre: Abnormal Angiogenesis in Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia: VEGF-, FGFR- and PI3K/AKT/mTOR-Targeted Therapies and IMiDs—A Narrative Review
resume: Background: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is an autosomal dominant vascular disorder characterised by abnormal angiogenesis caused by dysregulation of the BMP9/10–ALK1–ENG–SMAD signalling axis. The principal clinical manifestations are recurrent epistaxis, iron-deficiency anaemia, gastrointestinal bleeding and visceral arteriovenous malformations. Improved understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying endothelial dysfunction has enabled the development of targeted therapeutic approaches that modulate angiogenic pathways involved in disease progression. Methods: A narrative review was undertaken from clinical and translational perspectives. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for records published from January 2012 to May 2026. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms related to HHT, angiogenesis, VEGF, FGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, ANGPT2 and established or emerging therapies were used. Priority was accorded to randomised clinical trials, prospective studies, observational cohorts, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, international guidelines and consensus statements. Results: Bevacizumab remains the systemic anti-VEGF therapy with the strongest clinical evidence in severe bleeding, transfusion-dependent anaemia and symptomatic hepatic vascular involvement. Pomalidomide is supported by the most robust randomised evidence for reducing moderate-to-severe epistaxis and improving quality of life. Multikinase inhibitors, including nintedanib and pazopanib, together with tacrolimus, sirolimus and beta-blockers, have broadened the range of therapeutic options, although several approaches require further validation. Most recently, the AKT inhibitor engasertib achieved clinically meaningful reductions in epistaxis frequency and duration, thereby providing the first direct clinical validation of AKT as a therapeutic target in HHT. Emerging strategies directed at ANGPT2/Tie2 and other vascular-stabilisation pathways may further expand future treatment options. Conclusions: HHT management is progressively shifting towards a precision-medicine model that integrates genotype, haemorrhagic phenotype, visceral involvement, angiogenic biomarkers and treatment tolerability. Bevacizumab and pomalidomide are currently the best-established systemic therapies, whereas AKT inhibition is among the most promising recent developments. Further progress will require international collaboration, standardised outcome measures, biomarker-guided patient selection and prospectively validated and individualised treatment strategies.

titre: Beyond weight loss: selective myostatin inhibition as a muscle-preserving strategy in obesity pharmacotherapy
resume: Recently, Pratley et al. published the EMBRAZE trial, the first randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study to assess the weight-loss and muscle-preserving effects of apitegromab combined with tirzepatide in adults with overweight or obesity. This trial provided the first proof-of-concept evidence for the muscle-preserving value of an FDA-approved highly selective myostatin inhibitor in the setting of incretin-induced weight loss 14 . The EMBRAZE trial employed a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design with strictly defined eligibility criteria, intervention protocols, and efficacy endpoints. Conducted at seven clinical sites in the United States, the study enrolled 102 non-diabetic adults with overweight or obesity, who were randomized 1:1 to receive either tirzepatide (titrated to 15 mg weekly) plus apitegromab (10 mg/kg by intravenous infusion every 4 weeks), or tirzepatide plus placebo. The study comprised a 24-week double-blind treatment period followed by a 16-week safety follow-up; the primary endpoint was defined as the change from baseline in lean body mass assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) at week 24.Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) measures confirmed the drug's target-binding efficiency, and the muscle-preserving effect showed a degree of persistence after treatment discontinuation. Apitegromab plasma concentrations reached steady state at approximately week 16, accompanied by a synchronized rise and plateau in serum levels of latent myostatin, confirming that the 10 mg/kg dose achieves target saturation and effectively blocks the activation of endogenous myostatin. Exploratory follow-up at 8 weeks after discontinuation showed that the between-group difference in lean body mass remained statistically significant, indicating that the muscle-preserving effect was at least partially sustained and does not vanish immediately upon drug withdrawal.The short-term safety profile of this combination regimen is acceptable, yet important caveats complicate the interpretation of its body-composition and functional findings. The regimen was generally well tolerated over the short term: overall adverse event rates were balanced between groups, with gastrointestinal events typical of tirzepatide predominating. One serious adverse event occurred in each group, and both were adjudicated as unrelated to apitegromab. Approximately 6% of participants developed transient, low-titer anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) without hypersensitivity or other associated clinical reactions, and no hepatotoxicity or QT prolongation was identified as a safety signal. Two key considerations temper the interpretation of the body-composition data. First, lean body mass measured by DXA includes skeletal muscle alongside visceral organs, connective tissue and body water and is not a direct assay of skeletal muscle mass. The roughly 55% relative reduction in lean-mass loss reflects a favourable redistribution of lost weight between fat and lean compartments, rather than specific skeletal muscle protection, and should not be interpreted as definitive myoprotection. Notably, exploratory functional endpoints including handgrip strength and the sit-to-stand test showed no between-group differences. This dissociation between a promising DXA signal and absent functional benefit merits emphasis: preserved lean body mass did not translate into measurable improvements in strength, physical performance or patient-reported outcomes. Whether isolated gains in this DXA surrogate, unaccompanied by functional benefit, represent a clinically meaningful therapeutic advantage for people with obesity remains an open question that should shape expectations for this strategy (Figure 1).Beyond these interpretive challenges for trial endpoints, the EMBRAZE study has substantial methodological limitations that reduce the reliability and generalizability of its results. The most prominent methodological weakness is the choice of analysis set: primary efficacy relied on the completers population rather than the intention-to-treat (ITT) cohort. While investigators performed supportive sensitivity analyses yielding consistent directional findings, the completers set excludes participants who discontinued, and dropout often signals poor tolerability or inadequate response. The resulting selection bias is likely to overestimate treatment effects. Combined with a statistical plan that specified an 80% two-sided confidence level and omitted adjustment for multiple comparisons, these features restrict the findings to proof-of-concept status and are insufficient to support routine clinical use. Three additional constraints further weaken the evidence base. The trial enrolled only 102 randomized participants, limiting estimate precision and leaving subgroup comparisons underpowered. The study population was restricted to non-diabetic adults with overweight or obesity, excluding older adults at sarcopenia risk and patients with type 2 diabetes or cardiovascular disease -groups in whom lean-tissue loss carries the greatest clinical consequence. Treatment exposure lasted merely 24 weeks, too brief to assess the durability of the effect or detect delayed musculoskeletal harm, and several efficacy endpoints were exploratory and not formally powered. Collectively, these features compromise both internal validity and external applicability: the trial confirms that selective myostatin inhibition can alter the partitioning of weight loss during incretin therapy, but it cannot establish the magnitude, persistence or clinical value of that shift Future research should first advance larger confirmatory phase 3 trials to validate the true benefit of the muscle-preserving strategy against clinical hard endpoints. High-risk subgroups, including older adults prone to sarcopenia and patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes or cardiovascular disease, deserve priority enrolment. Meta-analyses have demonstrated that these populations suffer more severe lean-tissue loss during incretin-mediated weight reduction, with greater harms to glycemic control and physical function 5,7. Confirmatory trials should prioritize these high-risk subgroups and designate patient-important clinical outcomes (e.g., handgrip strength, gait speed, activities of daily living, and quality of life) as co-primary endpoints, rather than relying solely on DXA-derived lean body mass as a surrogate measure. Such a design would clarify whether preserved lean body mass translates into genuine functional and health benefits, thereby addressing the core scientific question that follows proof-of-concept validation. In parallel, trial designs should adopt intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis as the primary analysis set and prespecify correction for multiple comparisons, so as to strengthen the level of evidence and clinical persuasiveness.To define the clinical positioning of this intervention, its synergistic effects with lifestyle interventions must also be systematically evaluated. Resistance training combined with adequate dietary protein is currently the recognized first-line strategy for muscle preservation during weight loss, and has likewise been shown to effectively attenuate lean body mass loss in populations receiving incretin-based therapy 15,16 . However, existing studies have largely evaluated pharmacological or exercise interventions in isolation, and the synergistic effects of their combination remain unclear. Preclinical data in aged mice have demonstrated that combined myostatin blockade and exercise yields greater improvements in exercise endurance, habitual physical activity, and insulin sensitivity compared with either intervention alone 17 . Whether such additive benefits translate to humans with obesity undergoing incretin-mediated weight loss remains unknown. Subsequent research should establish standardized protocols for monitoring exercise and dietary intake, using objective wearable devices and dietary records to quantify resistance-training intensity, frequency, and dietary protein intake. Stratified analyses of the muscle-preserving effects of apitegromab across varying levels of exercise and nutrition would clarify the additive contribution of the drug relative to first-line muscle-preserving measures, and determine whether pharmacological intervention confers incremental benefit on top of lifestyle modification, thereby helping to avoid overtreatment. Likewise, baseline subgroup analyses could identify patient characteristics associated with a more favorable response, such as low muscle mass and a high catabolic state, providing a basis for more precise clinical application. Pharmacological muscle preservation is best understood as one component of a combined strategy rather than a substitute for the others: incretin-based therapy reduces fat mass, selective myostatin inhibition protects lean tissue, resistance exercise provides mechanical anabolic stimuli, and adequate protein intake supplies the substrates for muscle anabolism. These four interventions act via distinct pathways, and it is the combination, not any single element, that is likely to determine whether lean tissue is retained in a functional form (Figure 2).Achieving clinical translation of this therapeutic strategy will still require addressing multiple practical issues, including formulation optimization, long-term safety, and cost-effectiveness. Apitegromab is currently administered by intravenous infusion every 4 weeks, which, compared with the weekly subcutaneous injections commonly used in the management of chronic conditions such as obesity, represents a clear disadvantage in terms of dosing convenience and patient adherence. The subsequent development of a subcutaneous formulation, together with exploration of intermittent maintenance-dosing strategies after target achievement, could enhance the accessibility of long-term use. From a safety standpoint, myostatin exerts divergent effects across developmental stages. Germline myostatin-null mice exhibit congenital connective-tissue abnormalities of bone and tendon, a phenotype arising from lifelong genetic deficiency rather than adult-onset pharmacological Although the investigators supplemented this with sensitivity analyses pointing in the same direction, the completers set by definition excludes participants who withdrew-and dropout frequently reflects poor tolerability or insufficient response. The resulting selection bias would be 删除:(Figure 2).The current phase 2 proof-of-concept studies are limited by small sample sizes and a narrow study population, which restricts their generalizability, yet the very populations at highest risk of sarcopenia are precisely those in whom weight-loss-associated muscle loss is most detrimental. Existing meta-analyses have shown that obese patients with type 2 diabetes lose a greater proportion of lean mass during incretin-based therapy, and the adverse impact of muscle 删除: 上标 设置格式:; in older adults with obesity, weight-loss-related muscle loss is likewise an important contributor to frailty and increased fall risk blockade 18 . In contrast, preclinical studies demonstrate that therapeutic myostatin inhibition initiated in adulthood can ameliorate inflammatory and post-traumatic joint damage in murine models 19,20 . Even so, only 24-week clinical data are currently available; thus, unforeseen long-term musculoskeletal risks under sustained drug exposure in humans cannot be fully excluded, mandating multi-year safety surveillance to assess effects of prolonged multi-tissue drug exposure 8 . Sustained inhibition of myostatin also has consequences beyond muscle itself: because the ligand participates in tendon, bone and joint homeostasis, suppression sustained over years could in principle affect connective-tissue repair and bone quality in ways that a 24-week trial cannot detect. The available human safety experience is likewise indirect. Exposure to apitegromab has accrued almost entirely in patients with SMA, a population with a different baseline musculoskeletal phenotype, different metabolic and functional status, and no concomitant incretin-based therapy; these observations therefore cannot be extrapolated directly to adults with obesity receiving tirzepatide, in whom lean-tissue turnover, physical activity and comorbidity differ substantially. Long-term surveillance embedded in obesity development programmes, rather than inference from the SMA experience, will be required. In addition, pharmacoeconomic evaluation should be undertaken, integrating long-term health benefits and treatment costs to analyze the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio across different populations, thereby providing comprehensive evidence for subsequent reimbursement decisions and clinical decision-making.

titre: Alexithymia in ophthalmological and visual disorders: a scoping review
resume: Background Psychological factors are increasingly recognized as important components of ophthalmological and vision-related conditions. Alexithymia has been associated with emotional dysregulation, symptom perception, and psychosomatic processes across a range of medical and psychological disorders. However, the literature investigating alexithymia in the ophthalmological setting remains limited and has not previously been systematically mapped. Therefore, this scoping review aimed to synthesize the available evidence on alexithymia in ophthalmological and vision-related conditions. Methods This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to the final search date. Eligible studies included quantitative clinical investigations assessing alexithymia using validated instruments in individuals with ophthalmological or vision-related conditions, according to the Population–Concept–Context (PCC) framework. The review protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/TFHSE ). Results A total of 1,115 records were identified, of which 658 underwent title and abstract screening and seven were assessed for full-text eligibility. Four studies met the eligibility criteria. The included studies investigated central serous chorioretinopathy, dry eye disease, Sjögren's syndrome and sicca symptoms, and non-organic vision loss. Associations involving alexithymia were reported in studies of central serous chorioretinopathy and dry eye disease, whereas the remaining studies primarily investigated broader aspects of psychological functioning or implicit emotional processing without establishing direct associations between alexithymia and ocular outcomes. Conclusions The current literature on alexithymia in ophthalmological and vision-related conditions remains limited and heterogeneous. The available findings provide preliminary observations regarding alexithymia and related emotional processes in selected clinical conditions, without establishing consistent associations or causal relationships. Further longitudinal, methodologically rigorous, and interdisciplinary research is needed to clarify the potential relevance of alexithymia within ophthalmological settings and patient-centered models of care.

titre: Reframing Emotional Eating in Higher Education: Self-Regulation and Institutional Responsibility
resume: The transition to higher education is psychologically demanding, and emotional eating may emerge as a form of food-based coping with distress, academic pressure, loneliness, and uncertainty. This conceptual chapter reframes emotional eating in university students through an emotional self-regulation lens rather than as a nutritional knowledge problem. Drawing on emotion-regulation theory, alexithymia, interoceptive awareness, stress-related processes, and student well-being research, it examines how individual vulnerabilities may interact with academic, social, and institutional conditions. Attention is also given to gender, cultural variation, and intersectionality. The chapter identifies a potential institutional blind spot created by fragmented nutritional and psychological support and proposes a five-level framework encompassing curricular approaches, campus environments, integrated services, digital support, and institutional policy and culture. The framework is presented as a theory-informed model requiring context-specific implementation and empirical evaluation.

titre: Integrating hypnosis-based trauma-focused interventions into routine clinical care: a pilot feasibility case series conducted with the general population, high-risk pregnancy, and home-based palliative care patients
resume: Exposure therapy is a standard treatment for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Its clinical impact may be limited by insufficient memory reactivation and it may be difficult to implement in standard formats for patients with complex health pathways, such as high-risk pregnancy or home-based palliative care. To address these limitations, we enhanced exposure therapy with hypnosis and adapted it for medically vulnerable patients using Imagery Competing Task Interventions based on Tetris gameplay. This pilot feasibility case series describes the implementation and early clinical trajectories of three hypnosis-based trauma interventions embedded in routine care.

titre: Combined acupuncture and cognitive behavioral therapy for major depressive disorder: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
resume: Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a serious mental health condition. Although pharmacotherapy is the first-line treatment, its use is often limited by side effects and inadequate response. Acupuncture has demonstrated beneficial effects for MDD, and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is a guideline-recommended psychotherapy. Combining acupuncture with CBT may address both the physiological and psychological aspects of MDD, potentially enhancing therapeutic efficacy. We hypothesize that acupuncture plus CBT will yield superior clinical outcomes compared with antidepressant therapy alone in patients with mild-to-moderate MDD. Methods/design This trial is designed to compare combined acupuncture and CBT with sertraline for mild-to-moderate MDD, using an 8-week treatment period followed by a 16-week follow-up to evaluate clinical efficacy and safety. A total of 104 patients will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the acupuncture combined with CBT group or the control group. The primary outcome is the response rate as measured by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). Secondary outcomes include the remission rate, HAMD-17 scores, Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology–Self-Report (QIDS-SR) scores, Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15) scores, Sheehan Disability Scale (SDS) scores, and performance on the THINC-it tool. Safety will be assessed using Side Effect Rating Scale (SERS) scores. Adverse events (AEs) will be recorded whenever they occur during treatment. Discussion Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) views the mind and body as an integrated whole and therefore advocates for the concurrent regulation of psychological and somatic processes. Integrating acupuncture with CBT may offer comprehensive benefits for MDD, but high-quality comparative studies against antidepressants are lacking. As an exploratory trial, these findings will provide preliminary evidence to evaluate the role of the combined acupuncture and CBT approach in treating MDD. Clinical trial registration http://Itmctr.Ccebtcm.Org.Cn , identifier ITMCTR2024000653.

titre: Personalized nursing strategies to improve psychological adaptability in adults with cancer: a narrative review
resume: Psychological distress affects roughly one in three adults living with cancer, yet psychosocial support in oncology is still delivered largely in standardized formats that may not fit patients' clinical, cultural, or behavioral circumstances. This narrative review, restricted to adult oncology and reported against the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, synthesizes evidence on personalized nursing strategies for psychological adaptability, an umbrella process that includes coping, resilience, self-efficacy, and meaning-making. Personalization is examined along clinical, psychosocial and cultural, and digital and behavioral dimensions. The most consistent evidence supports structured, professionally facilitated care: mindfulness-based programs and nurse-led psychological and symptom-focused interventions reduced distress, anxiety, or depression in randomized trials and meta-analyses, although several syntheses were of low certainty. In the largest trial of cognitive behavioral skills for fear of recurrence, improvement was similar in the attention-control arm. Digital, peer, spiritual, and culturally adapted programs rest mainly on feasibility, pilot, heterogeneous, or associational data, and benefits were usually measured over weeks rather than months. No cited oncology study compared a tailored with a standardized version of the same intervention, so the added value of personalization is inferred from psychotherapy and nursing research outside cancer. Nurses' roles range from delivery to coordination and referral and depend on training and explicit pathways to specialist psycho-oncology care. Trials that randomize the tailoring decision, report provider training, and follow patients for six to twelve months are the next step.
revue: Journal of Cancer Research and Clinical Oncology

titre: Moving Minds: Physical Activity and Sport as Evidence-Based Resources for Mental Health
resume: Depression and anxiety disorders are among the leading causes of disability worldwide, yet accessto psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy remains limited. Physical activity and sport are low-cost,scalable and low-stigma options that can be delivered in clinical, educational, community andworkplace settings. The evidence base now ranges from large cohorts to network meta-analyses ofrandomised controlled trials (RCTs). Practitioners in psychology, social work and counselling,however, rarely receive a concise overview of what this evidence shows, how strong it is, and how itcan be translated into everyday practice. Following common usage, physical activity denotes anyenergy-expending bodily movement, exercise its planned and structured subset, and sport rule-based, often group-embedded exercise.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

fiche.verdict: Introduction méthodologique soulignant que l'activité physique et le sport constituent des interventions probantes, accessibles et peu stigmatisantes pour l'anxiété et la dépression.
fiche.population: Patients souffrant de troubles anxieux et dépressifs
fiche.intervention: Activité physique, exercice structuré et sport comme ressources thérapeutiques
resultats_cles: Dépression et anxiété parmi les premières causes de handicap mondial.
Niveau de preuve étayé par des méta-analyses de réseau d'essais contrôlés.
Nécessité de traduire ces données probantes dans la pratique clinique quotidienne.
fiche.conclusion: L'activité physique offre une ressource non pharmacologique scalable pour la santé mentale.

Pas de résultats d'études chiffrés originaux dans cet extrait

titre: Implementation and student outcomes of an implementation strategy for the sustainability of group evidence-based practices in schools
resume: Background: Limited research has examined the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of training strategies to sustain mental health evidence-based practices (EBPs) in urban elementary schools. Methods: We conducted a hybrid type 2 cluster-randomized trial comparing Prepare for Sustainment (PFS)-school district coach supervision of implementers supported by external consultants-to Sustainment as Usual (SAU), which relied on coach supervision alone. Two EBPs were implemented: the Coping Power Program (CPP) for externalizing problems and CBT for Anxiety Treatment in Schools (CATS) for anxiety. The study included three phases: full support (Phase 1), reduced support (Phase 2), and no support (Phase 3). Participants included 40 master's-level implementers, two district coaches, and 435 K-8 students. Outcomes included content and process fidelity, service penetration, mental health symptoms (parent and student report), and academic engagement with learning (teacher report). We also examined implementers' perceptions of training. Results: PFS implementers demonstrated stronger process fidelity: greater engagement with students in Phase 2 and warmer, clearer, and more organized treatment delivery in Phase 3. Content fidelity and service penetration did not differ between conditions in either phase. PFS showed medium and small effect-size improvement on student behavioral and emotional engagement with learning in Phase 2, and a large effect size in behavioral engagement and a medium effect-size improvement in behavioral disaffection with learning in Phase 3 compared to SAU. Students receiving CPP in Phase 2 in the PFS condition demonstrated a large improvement on self-reported externalizing behavior, and students receiving CATS in Phase 2 showed a medium-size reduction in internalizing symptoms relative to students in SAU. Qualitative data showed that implementers who did not receive support from coaches desired supervision on effective EBP delivery, and those experiencing reduced support wanted more frequent guidance. Administrators noted that ongoing collaboration with district coaches would have enhanced their ability to support implementers. Conclusion: A sustainment strategy consisting of an initial training for implementers and occasional consultation for school district coaches is effective for achieving high process fidelity and medium to large effects for engagement with learning activities and mental health outcomes compared to a sustainment as usual strategy. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04869657. Registered May 3, 2021.

fiche.verdict: Essai randomisé montrant qu'un soutien régulier des superviseurs améliore la fidélité des intervenants et l'efficacité des TCC pour enfants.
fiche.population: 40 intervenants, 2 coachs, 435 élèves de primaire/collège
fiche.intervention: Stratégie de pérennisation PFS (supervision par coach du district + consultants externes) vs SAU (supervision classique)

Réduction supérieure des symptômes d'extériorisation (CPP, grand effet) et d'anxiété (CATS, effet moyen) chez les élèves du groupe PFS.
fiche.conclusion: Une stratégie combinant formation initiale et consultation ponctuelle pour les coachs maintient une haute fidélité TCC et améliore la santé mentale des élèves.
limites: Pas d'application directe aux pathologies digestives

fiche.conclusion_simple: Un accompagnement continu des thérapeutes améliore la qualité de délivrance des TCC et augmente leur efficacité sur l'anxiété.

titre: Exploring caregiver burden among families of individuals with obsessive–compulsive disorder in Iran: a qualitative directed content analysis
Multi-Gaussian Model for Intrabeam Scattering
resume: Conventional analytical models of intrabeam scattering (IBS), such as the Piwinski model and Bjorken-Mtingwa model, generally rely on the assumption of a Gaussian beam distribution, limiting their applicability to non-Gaussian cases. In this work, we develop a multi-Gaussian model to extend analytical IBS calculations to a broader class of non-Gaussian phase-space distributions. The proposed approach represents a non-Gaussian distribution as a superposition of Gaussian components sharing a common covariance matrix but having different mean values. We derived a generalized model for evaluating the momentum second-moment evolution rate and the IBS growth rate. Furthermore, for equally spaced Gaussian components, we developed an infinite bunch train model and introduce a practical truncation rule to reduce computational costs. The model is applied to a representative steady-state microbunching (SSMB) storage ring, where longitudinal overlap between neighboring microbunches is shown to enhance IBS growth rates in all three directions. The proposed framework provides a practical approach to evaluating IBS in non-Gaussian beam distributions and offers a basis for further development toward a more general non-Gaussian IBS theory.

fiche.verdict: Développement théorique d'un modèle multi-gaussien pour étendre le calcul de la diffusion intragroupe (IBS) aux distributions non gaussiennes.
resultats_cles: Création d'un modèle multi-gaussien pour distributions non gaussiennes.
Application à un anneau de stockage démontrant l'impact du chevauchement longitudinal.
fiche.conclusion: Ce cadre fournit une approche pratique pour évaluer l'IBS dans les distributions non gaussiennes.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Domaine de la physique des faisceaux, sans rapport avec la psychologie ou la gastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Modèle multi-gaussien pour la diffusion intragroupe
fiche.conclusion_simple: Un nouveau modèle mathématique permet d'évaluer la diffusion intragroupe pour des distributions non gaussiennes.

titre: Before synchrony: the unresolved specificity of neural oscillations across brains
resume: Abstract EEG hyperscanning studies frequently report inter-brain synchrony across a wide range of frequencies, topographies, and social tasks. However, the interpretation of these findings usually relies on canonical frequency bands and builds on the assumption that oscillations are stable, sustained, and comparable across individuals. Yet, single-brain electrophysiology increasingly shows that neural oscillations are shaped by 1/f aperiodic activity, with important inter- and intra-individual differences in their properties, and with some frequency bands manifesting as short transient bursts rather than sustained rhythms. These properties are rarely addressed in hyperscanning research. They also interact with standard analytical pipelines, which implicitly assume sustained oscillations at a shared frequency across partners. Drawing on recent advances in neural oscillation research, the paper argues that IBS research should move beyond descriptive reports of synchrony and instead formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and brain regions, to build interpretable accounts of inter-brain dynamics.

fiche.verdict: Article théorique appelant à des hypothèses mécanistiques plus rigoureuses pour interpréter la synchronie inter-cérébrale en EEG.
resultats_cles: Les études d'hyperscanning ignorent souvent l'activité apériodique 1/f et les bouffées transitoires.
Les pipelines d'analyse supposent à tort des oscillations stables et comparables.
fiche.conclusion: La recherche sur la synchronie inter-cérébrale doit formuler des hypothèses mécanistiques précises.
limites: Article purement conceptuel sans nouvelles données
fiche.pertinence_raison: Méthodologie purement neurophysiologique (EEG), sans lien avec la pratique clinique.
fiche.titre_court: Limites de l'analyse de synchronie en EEG
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'interprétation de la synchronie cérébrale en EEG nécessite de mieux prendre en compte la variabilité des oscillations neuronales.

titre: Gut microbiota GABA regulation by intestinal pH osmolality and microbial consumption
resume: Abstract The production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by the gut microbiota has garnered attention due to its potential role as a driver of gut-brain axis signaling. However, mechanisms regulating microbiota-derived GABA under physiological conditions remain unclear. Here, we identified low pH and high osmolality as promoters of GABA production in the gut microbe Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by driving changes in the expression of the glutamate decarboxylase system. pH also emerged as a critical factor for enhancing GABA production in a broader set of gut microbes. However, in the cecal microbiota of specific pathogen-free mice and in an ex vivo model of the human colon microbiota, GABA levels did not increase under physiologically relevant acidic conditions. This can partly be explained by microbial GABA consumption. Consistently, reducing cecal pH increased GABA levels in Oligo-MM 12 mice, a gnotobiotic model lacking GABA-consuming gut microbes. Our findings highlight the intricate balance between gut microbial GABA production, consumption, and environmental factors such as pH and osmolality.

fiche.verdict: Un pH bas et une osmolalité élevée favorisent la production de GABA par le microbiote (ex. Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron), mais la consommation microbienne limite l'augmentation nette.
fiche.intervention: exposition à un pH acide et une osmolalité élevée, mesure de la production et consommation de GABA
resultats_cles: Un pH bas et une forte osmolalité augmentent la production de GABA par Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron.
La consommation active de GABA par certaines bactéries contrebalance la production dans le côlon.
fiche.conclusion: L'équilibre du GABA dans l'intestin dépend d'une balance complexe entre production microbienne (stimulée par le pH acide) et consommation.
limites: Modèles animaux et ex vivo, extrapolation à l'humain limitée
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien axe intestin-cerveau et GABA pertinent pour le syndrome de l'intestin irritable.
fiche.titre_court: Régulation du GABA par le microbiote intestinal
fiche.conclusion_simple: Le microbiote produit du GABA sous l'effet du pH acide, mais sa consommation par d'autres bactéries module les taux disponibles.

titre: Early Gastrointestinal Dysfunction Precedes Colonic Inflammation in a Rat Model of Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Sepsis
resume: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection, with gastrointestinal dysfunction contributing to morbidity and mortality, but its initial manifestations remain poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize the very early gastrointestinal effects of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced sepsis in rats, focusing on nausea-like behavior, visceral nociception, and colonic motility. Male Wistar rats received an intraperitoneal injection of LPS (5 mg/kg) or saline. Bedding intake, food and water consumption, and body temperature were recorded within 2 h post-injection (T2). Afterwards, visceral sensitivity was assessed using tonic colorectal distension. Four hours after treatment (T4), macroscopic gastrointestinal evaluation, enteropooling measurement, and assessment of whole-colon motor activity in an organ bath were performed. Different inflammatory markers were analyzed at T4 in both plasma and distal colon. LPS-treated rats exhibited increased bedding intake and drinking events, reduced body temperature, and unchanged visceral sensitivity during tonic stimulation, whereas phasic stimulation increased it. LPS also increased gastric and caecal weights and small intestinal fluid accumulation and induced more intense and organized colonic peristaltic activity. These functional changes occurred alongside elevated circulating TNF and IL-1β. In contrast, distal colonic TNF, IL-1β, and COX-2 expression, distal colonic histological damage, COX-2 immunoreactivity, and macrophage and mast cell abundance remained unchanged. Together, these findings identify acute systemic cytokine release as a rapid trigger of gastrointestinal dysfunction preceding detectable colonic inflammatory responses, thereby providing new insights into the early gastrointestinal manifestations of sepsis.

fiche.verdict: Un modèle animal montre que la septicémie induit rapidement des dysfonctions gastro-intestinales et des cytokines pro-inflammatoires systémiques avant toute inflammation colique visible.
fiche.population: Rats Wistar mâles (n = non spécifié)
fiche.intervention: Injection intrapéritonéale de lipopolysaccharide (LPS 5 mg/kg) versus solution saline
resultats_cles: Augmentation des prises de litière et de boisson, baisse de la température corporelle dès 2 h.
Péristaltisme colique accru et élévation du TNF et de l'IL-1β circulants à 4 h.
Absence d'inflammation ou de dommages histologiques dans le côlon distal à 4 h.
fiche.conclusion: La libération aiguë de cytokines systémiques déclenche rapidement un dysfonctionnement gastro-intestinal précédant la réponse inflammatoire colique.
limites: Étude animale (rats), non transposable directement à l'homme.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien axe intestin-cerveau et inflammation systémique, mais modèle animal (rat).
fiche.titre_court: Dysfonction gastro-intestinale précoce post-sepsis chez le rat
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'inflammation systémique aiguë perturbe rapidement la motilité digestive avant même les lésions coliques locales chez l'animal.

titre: EXPOSURE TO MICROPLASTICS, NANOPLASTICS, AND PLASTIC-ASSOCIATED CHEMICALS: MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES AND PSYCHONEUROIMMUNOENDOCRINE MECHANISMS — A SYSTEMATIZED LITERATURE REVIEW (2000–2025)
resume: Global plastic production exceeds 400 million metric tons annually, contributing to the widespread occurrence of microplastics and nanoplastics in the environment, as well as exposure to plastic-associated chemicals, including bisphenols, phthalates, and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). These contaminants have raised growing concerns regarding their potential effects on the nervous, endocrine, and immune systems. This study aimed to critically examine the available scientific evidence on the associations between exposure to plastic particles and associated chemicals, mental disorders, and psychoneuroimmunoendocrine mechanisms. A systematized literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, covering publications from 2000 to 2025. Twenty-five studies were included, comprising human epidemiological investigations and in vivo and in vitro experimental studies. The reviewed evidence suggests several potential mechanisms underlying the neurobiological effects of these contaminants, including alterations in hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis regulation, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, changes in gut microbiota composition and gut–brain axis communication, and disturbances in neurotransmission. Epidemiological studies reported positive associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and depressive symptoms, with odds ratios (ORs) ranging from 1.24 to 1.44. A cross-sectional study involving university students identified an association between higher estimated microplastic exposure and increased odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 1.38). Experimental studies also reported anxiety-like and depressive-like behaviors, as well as neurobehavioral alterations resembling features associated with neurodevelopmental disorders. Furthermore, investigations of human brain tissue have identified the presence of microplastic and nanoplastic particles. However, methodological heterogeneity, differences in exposure conditions, and limitations inherent to observational and experimental studies constrain the extrapolation of these findings and the establishment of causal relationships. Overall, the available evidence supports the biological plausibility of associations between exposure to plastic-related contaminants and neurobehavioral and psychoneuroimmunoendocrine alterations. Nevertheless, longitudinal studies and experimental investigations using environmentally relevant exposure conditions are needed to clarify the potential risks to human mental health.

fiche.verdict: La revue suggère un lien biologique plausible entre exposition aux microplastiques/produits chimiques et altérations neurocomportementales et psychoneuroimmunoendocrines.
fiche.population: Humains (études épidémiologiques) et modèles expérimentaux (animaux/cellules)
fiche.intervention: Exposition aux microplastiques, nanoplastiques et perturbateurs chimiques (bisphénols, phtalates, PFAS)
resultats_cles: Associations positives entre phtalates/microplastiques et symptômes dépressifs (OR entre 1.24 et 1.44).
Mécanismes impliqués : axe HPA, neuroinflammation, stress oxydatif et axe intestin-cerveau.
fiche.conclusion: L'évidence soutient la plausibilité biologique d'effets neurocomportementaux liés aux contaminants plastiques, nécessitant des études longitudinales.
limites: Limites inhérentes aux études observationnelles et expérimentales
fiche.pertinence_raison: Impacts sur l'axe intestin-cerveau, l'anxiété, la dépression et la neuroinflammation.
fiche.titre_court: Plastiques, santé mentale et microbiote
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'exposition aux plastiques et polluants associés est corrélée à des symptômes anxiodépressifs, possiblement via l'axe intestin-cerveau.

titre: Editorial: Chronic insomnia: treatment and management
resume: There were 11 articles in this category, comprising acupuncture-related articles (7 articles) and non-acupuncture-related articles (4 articles). The acupuncture-related articles consisted of 3 systematic reviews, while the other four articles were study protocols. The non-acupuncture-related articles focused on herbal medicines, aromatherapy, and mindfulness therapy.For the acupuncture-related articles, a systematic review of randomized controlled trials comparing acupuncture and sham acupuncture was conducted by searching eight databases for articles published up to March 17, 2025 (13). There were 10 eligible studies involving 757 patients with chronic insomnia. The study analysis found that acupuncture resulted in significantly better Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores than sham acupuncture, with a mean difference of -2.60 (p < 0.00001) and -2.04 (p = 0.0005), respectively.Another systematic review also reported similar findings (14).Acupuncture yielded significantly lower PSQI scores than sham acupuncture, with a mean difference of -3.55 (p < 0.00001) across 17 included randomized controlled trials. Additionally, this study showed that moderate-and high-session acupuncture yielded significantly greater improvements in PSQI scores than sham acupuncture, with mean differences of -3.02 (p < 0.00001, I 2 = 91%) and -2.14 (p < 0.00001, I 2 = 89%), respectively. Note that the I 2 values for both analyses were extremely high, indicating high heterogeneity. Conversely, the low-session group did not have significantly better PSQI scores than the sham acupuncture group, with a mean difference of -1.44 (p = 0.08, I2 = 90%). The I 2 was still high in this comparison; therefore, these results should be interpreted cautiously.The last systematic review was conducted to evaluate the effects of acupuncture on the brain in patients with primary insomnia based on a search of seven databases (15). The review included randomized controlled trials comparing patients with primary insomnia and healthy controls across 11 studies using functional magnetic resonance imaging. The main results showed that acupuncture significantly improved the function of eight brain areas, including the right superior frontal gyrus (1,404 voxels, p = 0.0123), left inferior frontal gyrus (1,068 voxels, p = 0.0088), left inferior temporal gyrus (903 voxels, p = 0.0074), left supramarginal gyrus (888 voxels, p = 0.0113), left precuneus (457 voxels, p = 0.0247), right precuneus (302 voxels, p = 0.0191), left supplementary motor area (82 voxels, p = 0.0354), and right parahippocampal gyrus (28 voxels, p = 0.0379).showing that: 1) acupuncture exerts a regulatory influence on the functional activity of brain regions implicated in cognitive and emotional processes, and 2) acupuncture affects metabolite levels and circadian clock gene expression, and enhances both inflammatory responses and energy metabolism (16). However, there is limited data on this aspect. Further clinical trials and basic research are needed to confirm the mechanisms of acupuncture on the brain in human subjects with insomnia.Finally, the three study protocols for upcoming randomized controlled trials were: 1) Brain function assessment of acupuncture for chronic insomnia disorder with mild cognitive dysfunction based on functional near-infrared spectroscopy; 2) Efficacy of electroacupuncture treatment for generalized anxiety disorder-related insomnia; and 3) Dose-effect relationship of different acupuncture courses on chronic insomnia disorder (17)(18)(19). These three study protocols present notable approaches, and their findings could significantly contribute to the comprehension of the brain mechanisms underlying acupuncture.The four non-acupuncture-related articles focused on Suanzaoren decoction (1 article), a systematic review of aromatherapy (1 article), a randomized controlled trial of mindfulnessbased cognitive therapy (1 article), and a study protocol for long-snake moxibustion (1 article).The first study compared Suanzaoren decoction with estazolam in the treatment of chronic insomnia in adults (20). A total of 80 patients were included, with 51 patients receiving Suanzaoren decoction and 29 patients receiving estazolam. The efficacy of both medications was comparable, with effective rates of 78.40% and 72.40%, respectively (p = 0.543).The second study was a systematic review of five databases that included randomized controlled trials comparing aromatherapy to a control for the treatment of comorbid insomnia (21). The review included 27 articles comprising 2,072 patients in total. The authors found that inhalation aromatherapy improved symptoms of insomnia, anxiety, and depression more effectively than the control, with mean differences of -2.90 (p < 0.00001), -3.97 (p < 0.0001), and -9.58 (p = 0.0007), respectively. The authors concluded that inhalation aromatherapy significantly improved sleep quality compared to the control in patients with comorbid insomnia. Notably, there were no serious adverse reactions reported in the study.The third study was conducted in Norway and explored insomnia symptoms in patients with recurrent depression (22). The authors enrolled 68 patients with at least three episodes of depression and divided them into two groups; ultimately, 55 patients completed the study: 25 in the mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) group and 30 in the control group. After 8 weeks of treatment, the MBCT group had less severe insomnia symptoms (p = 0.017), shorter sleep onset (p = 0.047), and fewer nocturnal awakenings (p = 0.023) than the control group. However, there were no significant differences regarding early morning awakening, daytime impairment, or dissatisfaction with sleep. In other words, MBCT may improve specific insomnia symptoms in patients with recurrent depression. Finally, the study protocol in this category is entitled "Efficacy and Mechanism of Long-Snake Moxibustion for Treating Insomnia in Breast Cancer Survivors" (23).These articles show the potential benefits of alternative medicine and cognitive therapy for insomnia. However, due to the limited number of studies and small sample sizes, further clinical studies are needed to confirm these findings.There were three articles in this category. The first is a review of gut microbiota and insomnia after COVID-19 infection (24). This review by Fang et al. showed that COVID-19 infection caused widespread and long-lasting changes to the gut microbiota by reducing beneficial flora and increasing harmful pathogens. These changes may be related to insomnia in patients who have recovered from a COVID-19 infection. Additionally, the authors discussed potential treatments for insomnia after COVID-19 infection through gut microbiota regulation, such as probiotics, prebiotics, or synbiotics.The second study was conducted by Yang et al. from China (25). The authors used a twosample Mendelian randomization analysis based on genome-wide association data to evaluate the association between gut microbiota and insomnia. They identified four gut microbial taxa related to insomnia, acting as either risk factors or protective factors. The family Ruminococcaceae and the genus Lachnospiraceae were two risk factors for insomnia, with odds ratios of 1.497 (p = 0.047) and 1.726 (p = 0.004), respectively. The genus Flavonifractor and the genus Olsenella were significant protective factors against insomnia, with odds ratios of 0.596 (p = 0.030) and 0.808 (p = 0.031), respectively. The authors proposed two major implications for their findings: 1) the potential to use gut microbiota as an objective diagnostic tool and potential treatment target for insomnia; and 2) unlike observational studies, the Mendelian randomization method can control for confounding factors.However, further clinical studies are needed to confirm the results of this study and explore gut microbiota-based treatments for insomnia.The third article analyzed whether any key genes could serve as biomarkers in patients with sleep deprivation compared with healthy human controls (26). The authors found a total of 50 differentially expressed genes, which were divided into two groups: six upregulated genes and 44 downregulated genes. Based on machine learning, five genes were identified as key genes for sleep deprivation: C2CD2L, SPINT2, APOL3, PKNOX1, and A2M. However, only the C2CD2L gene was confirmed by both the qRT-PCR method and machine learning.In summary, there is emerging data regarding the role of gut microbiota and specific genes in chronic insomnia, as demonstrated by Mendelian randomization analysis, machine learning, and PCR methods. However, further studies in this area are still needed.This category includes two subcategories: clinical assessment articles (comprising two studies) and research on three specific populations-patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), adolescents, and adults diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity d isorder (ADHD).The first study, by Ayabe et al. from Japan, developed a self-reported quality of life scale for patients with insomnia, known as the QOL-I ( 27). The QOL-I consisted of 11 items, which were tested in 93 adult patients with chronic insomnia and 228 healthy participants. The QOL-I demonstrated high reliability with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.92 and significant criterion-related validity (p < 0.001).The second study from Korea evaluated insomnia treatment practices using data from the Korea National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (NHIS-NSC) from 2002 to 2019 (28). Interestingly, the authors found that pharmacological treatment was the most common intervention (89.9%), rather than Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), which should be the first-line treatment. Zolpidem and benzodiazepines were the two most commonly prescribed hypnotics, accounting for 60% and up to 40% of prescriptions, respectively The third article was conducted by Gabryelska et al. from Poland (29). The 127 patients with OSA were categorized into four groups as follows: insomnia with sleepiness (20 patients; 15.75%), sleepiness (22 patients; 17.32%), insomnia (30 patients; 23.62%), and asymptomatic (55 patients; 43.31%). In patients with OSA, the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) was positively associated with the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (r = 0.205; p = 0.021), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) (r = 0.578; p < 0.001), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) item 2 (subjective sleep latency) (r = 0.199; p = 0.025), and the subjective-to-objective sleep latency ratio (r = 0.208; p = 0.019). Additionally, the BDI was negatively associated with PSQI item 4 (total sleep time) (r = -0.203; p = 0.022). The authors found that the ISI was significantly associated with both mild and moderate depression in patients with OSA. The adjusted odds ratio of the ISI for mild depression was 1.23 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.09, 1.38; p < 0.001), while the adjusted odds ratio of the ISI for moderate depression was 1.39 (95% CI: 1.13, 1.72; p = 0.002). Patients with OSA who have a high ISI score may represent a specific phenotype of depression in this setting.The fourth article by Gao et al. from China demonstrated an increasing trend in research on adolescent insomnia using a bibliometric analysis of the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database between 2002 and 2022 (30). The authors found that there were 2,468 publications on adolescent insomnia. These publications originated from 3,102 institutions across 87 countries, primarily from China and the USA. This study emphasized the growing importance of adolescent insomnia research.The final article evaluated physical activity and sleep in adult patients with ADHD using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) database between 2013 and 2020 (pre-COVID pandemic) (31). The authors found that there were 162 eligible adult patients with ADHD who reported using stimulant medicines. Those who engaged in moderate to vigorous physical activity for 150 minutes per week had a lower risk of trouble sleeping, with an odds ratio of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.10, 0.67; p = 0.006). These findings were observed in men, but not in women. This study highlights the importance of physical activity in adult patients with ADHD who use stimulants. However, further research on the treatment and management of chronic insomnia is required to fully understand the underlying mechanisms and clinical outcomes of these various approaches.

fiche.verdict: Cet éditorial résume 11 articles sur l'insomnie chronique, rapportant des effets positifs mais très hétérogènes de l'acupuncture et quelques approches complémentaires.
fiche.population: Patients souffrant d'insomnie chronique ou primaire (selon les études résumées)
