titre: Tracking Neurophysiological Trajectories in Adolescent Non-Suicidal Self-Injury During Mindfulness-Based Intervention: A Longitudinal Single-Channel EEG Study
resume: OBJECTIVE: Adolescent non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) remains a major clinical challenge, and objective neurophysiological monitoring during early intervention is lacking. This prospective longitudinal observational study characterized longitudinal EEG trajectories during an individualized home-based EEG biofeedback editation (H-EBM) intervention in hospitalized adolescents with NSSI and explored whether neurophysiological trajectory features were associated with emotional improvement. METHODS: Fifty-two hospitalized adolescents with NSSI (DSM-5 criteria) who received routine inpatient psychiatric care together with daily H-EBM sessions over approximately 10 days were included in the per-protocol analysis. H-EBM integrated metaphor-guided therapeutic narratives with real-time EEG biofeedback via a single-lead device (Fp1, 512 Hz). Emotional states were assessed at admission and discharge using the profile of mood states (POMS). Participants were exploratorily classified into exploratory responder ( n = 36 ) and non-responder ( n = 16 ) subgroups based on total mood disturbance (TMD) improvement. Longitudinal alpha/beta power ratio trajectories were compared between subgroups, and associations between EEG trajectory slopes and TMD improvement were examined. RESULTS: The exploratory responder subgroup showed significant reductions in TMD scores and core symptom subscales (depression and tension; all p < 0.001 ), whereas the exploratory non-responder subgroup showed no improvement. The alpha/beta ratio in the exploratory responder subgroup exhibited a progressive upward trajectory across training sessions, while this ratio remained stable or fluctuated in the exploratory non-responder subgroup. The alpha/beta ratio slope was positively associated with TMD improvement scores (Pearson r = 0.43 , 95% CI [0.18, 0.63], p = 0.002 ). Exploratory logistic regression suggested that the alpha/beta ratio slope was associated with exploratory responder status after adjusting for age and gender (OR = 9.49, 95% CI [1.01, 89.44], p = 0.049 ). Exploratory ROC analysis showed moderate apparent (in-sample) discriminative performance (AUC = 0.774, 95% CI [0.638, 0.899]). CONCLUSION: Longitudinal neurophysiological trajectories during individualized H-EBM were associated with emotional improvement in hospitalized adolescents with NSSI. These preliminary findings suggest that EEG trajectory analysis may represent a promising objective monitoring approach during individualized mindfulness-based interventions. Given the observational design without a control group, future randomized controlled studies are warranted to examine potential therapeutic effects.

titre: Mapping the interplay among somatic symptoms, alexithymia, and emotion regulation difficulties in community-dwelling older adults with multiple chronic conditions: a network analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Somatic symptoms are highly prevalent among older adults with multiple chronic conditions and are associated with functional impairment and reduced quality of life. Emerging evidence suggests that psychological factors, particularly alexithymia and emotion regulation difficulties, are closely associated with somatic symptom burden. However, the conditional associations among the dimensions of these constructs remain unclear. Network analysis provides a complementary approach to examining these relationships. This study aimed to examine these associations and identify central and bridge nodes among older adults with multiple chronic conditions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used convenience sampling to recruit 1,497 participants from 13 prefecture-level cities in Jiangsu Province between February 2024 and February 2026. Data were collected using the Somatic Symptom Scale-China (SSS-CN), the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), and the short form of the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS-16). R version 4.2.0 was used to construct a network of symptom dimensions and identify central and bridge nodes, and SPSS 26.0 was used for descriptive analyses. RESULTS: A total of 1,497 participants were included, with a mean age of 71.02 ± 4.69 years. Centrality analysis identified "Limited access to emotion regulation strategies perceived as effective" (strength z-score = 1.61), "Difficulty Identifying Feelings" (strength z-score = 1.38), and "Physical disorder" (strength z-score = 0.98) as central nodes in the network. Bridge centrality analysis identified "Difficulty Identifying Feelings" (bridge strength = 0.40), "Limited access to emotion regulation strategies perceived as effective" (bridge strength = 0.32), and "Depression disorder" (bridge strength = 0.25) as the nodes with the highest bridge strength within the predefined alexithymia, emotion regulation difficulties, and somatic symptom communities, respectively. The network showed good stability (CS = 0.75). Network comparison analysis revealed significant differences between participants with SSS-CN scores below 30 and those with scores of 30 or above in overall network structure (M = 0.438, P < 0.001) and global strength (S = 1.358, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Somatic symptoms, alexithymia, and emotion regulation difficulties showed close conditional associations among community-dwelling older adults with multiple chronic conditions. "Difficulty Identifying Feelings" and "Limited access to emotion regulation strategies perceived as effective" exhibited relatively high strength and bridge strength, while "Physical disorder" also occupied a central position in the network. Significant differences in network structure and global strength were observed between groups with different levels of somatic symptom burden. These findings highlight potentially relevant dimensions for future longitudinal and intervention studies.

titre: Cultural and Familial Context of Contamination-Related Obsessive-Compulsive Symptoms in an Adolescent: A Case Report
resume: Contamination-related obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) can cause substantial distress and functional impairment, particularly when compulsive behaviors become intertwined with familial and culturally shaped beliefs about purity and cleanliness. Understanding the distinction between culturally normative practices and clinically impairing compulsions is important for culturally sensitive assessment and treatment. This case report describes an 18-year-old woman with adolescent-onset, contamination-related obsessive-compulsive symptoms that developed at approximately 14-15 years of age during a period of academic and family stress. Her symptoms included persistent feelings of being unclean after toileting, prolonged bathing and toileting, repeated checking of undergarments after urination, counting rituals, avoidance of food and water to reduce elimination-related urges, and avoidance of physical contact in crowded or public settings. A distinctive feature of the presentation was its development within a familial environment in which purity and cleanliness were associated with bodily practices and social boundaries. The patient reported routine post-defecation bathing by family members, restrictions on physical contact with individuals from Scheduled Caste backgrounds, cleansing of the household after such contact, and repeated scrutiny of the adequacy of her own washing. These experiences were considered contextual influences that may have shaped the meaning and reinforcement of contamination concerns rather than direct causes of OCD. Her behaviors were distinguished from the family practices she described by their excessive duration, associated distress, impaired control, and functional interference. The baseline Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) score was 24, indicating severe symptoms. Treatment focused on psychoeducation, reduction of ritualized behaviors, distraction and urge-management strategies, toilet retraining, relaxation, and supportive psychotherapy, alongside concurrent pharmacological treatment. By sessions six to seven, checking and counting had ceased, bathing and toileting duration had markedly decreased, food and water avoidance had resolved, and previously avoided bus travel and crowded settings were tolerated. At session nine, approximately two months after baseline, the Y-BOCS score had decreased to 4, indicating symptoms in the subclinical range. The remaining sessions focused primarily on maintaining improvement and adjustment to college, with no recurrence of the principal rituals documented through the final session. This case highlights how familial and culturally transmitted concepts of purity may shape the content of contamination-related OCD symptoms. Substantial improvement occurred during a symptom-focused behavioral intervention without directly challenging the family's broader cultural framework. However, concurrent pharmacological treatment and the availability of only one follow-up Y-BOCS assessment limit conclusions about the independent effect of psychotherapy and the durability of improvement.

titre: A pectin-type acidic polysaccharides from Coix lachryma-jobi L. seeds alleviated depression-like behavior by modulating microbiota-gut-brain axis in CRS-induced rats
resume: Coix lachryma-jobi L. is a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible resource with multiple nutritional values. However, the effect of Coix polysaccharide on depression and its underlying mechanism were still unclear. In this study, a polysaccharide (CSP-A) was isolated from Coix lachryma-jobi L. seeds with molecular weight of 15.625 kDa. The backbone of CSP-A was composed of →4)-α-D-Glcp-(1→,→4)-GlcAp-(1→, and→3)-Galp-(1 → with side chains containing Rhap-(1→, Manp-(1→, and Galp-(1 → which was further identified as a pectin-type acidic heteropolysaccharide with homogalacturonan (HG) and rhamnogalacturonan-I (RG-I) domains. Animal experiments demonstrated that CSP-A significantly ameliorated CRS-induced depressive-like behaviors by remodeling the imbalance of gut microbiota, recovered SCFA levels, and mitigated colonic pathological damage and inflammation induced by CRS treated rats. Moreover, CSP-A notably restored the disturbed metabolic profiles associated with nervous diseases. Based on its structural characteristics, it was supposed that CSP-A may act as prebiotics increasing the activities of beneficial bacteria, enhancing SCFAs production, activating AhR/CYP1A1/BDNF signaling pathway, and ultimately alleviating depressive-like behaviors. This work reported a new type of polysaccharide from Coix lachryma-jobi L. seeds and its antidepressant mechanism, highlighting its potential candidate as a new psychiatric drug.

fiche.conclusion: Le CSP-A agit comme un prébiotique modulant l'axe microbiote-intestin-cerveau, représentant un candidat potentiel pour le traitement de la dépression.

titre: An Examination of Psychological Pain, Alexithymia, and Chronotype in Depressive Disorder within the Framework of the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide
resume: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is strongly associated with increased suicide risk, with psychological pain considered an important experiential dimension related to suicide vulnerability. Within the framework of the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide (IPTS), perceived burdensomeness, thwarted belongingness, and acquired capability for suicide are key interpersonal constructs associated with suicidal ideation and behavior. In addition, alexithymia and chronotype have also been linked to depression and suicidality. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 121 patients with MDD and 141 healthy controls. Participants completed the Beck Depression Inventory, Psychache Scale, Toronto Alexithymia Scale, Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire, Interpersonal Needs Questionnaire, and Acquired Capability for Suicide Scale. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed. Results: Compared with controls, individuals with MDD showed higher levels of psychological pain, depressive symptoms, alexithymia, interpersonal unmet needs, and acquired capability for suicide, and were more likely to exhibit an evening chronotype. Psychological pain was positively associated with depressive symptoms, perceived burdensomeness, thwarted belongingness, alexithymia, and acquired capability for suicide. In the multivariable model, perceived burdensomeness showed the strongest association with psychological pain, followed by depressive symptom severity and thwarted belongingness. Conclusion: Psychological pain in MDD appears to be closely associated with interpersonal unmet needs, particularly perceived burdensomeness. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating psychological pain together with IPTS-related interpersonal constructs in comprehensive clinical assessments of individuals with depression.

titre: [Pharmacokinetics of Baizhu San in normal and diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome model rats]
resume: An ultra-performance liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole tandem mass spectrometry(UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS) method was established for the simultaneous quantification of seven absorbed components(pogostone, puerarin, daidzin, 3'-methoxypuerarin, glycyrrhizic acid, glycyrrhetinic acid, and ginsenoside Rb_1) in Baizhu San(BZS). This method was subsequently employed to investigate the pharmacokinetics of these components in normal rats and in a rat model of diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome(IBS-D), on the basis of which the impact of disease status on the pharmacokinetics of the active components in this classic formula was evaluated. The IBS-D rat model was established via acetic acid enema combined with gavage of senna leaf extract and restraint stress. Following gavage of BZS, blood samples were collected at various time points from the orbital sinus of rats in each group. Plasma concentrations of the components were determined through the established UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS method, and pharmacokinetic parameters were calculated in Phoenix WinNonlin 8.1 software. The results showed that compared with the control group, the model group showed decreased AUC of puerarin, daidzin, and 3'-methoxypuerarin(P<0.05). For pogostone, T_(max), AUC, and MRT were significantly decreased in the model group. The AUC, t_(1/2), C_(max), and MRT of ginsenoside Rb_1 and glycyrrhizic acid were all increased, while the AUC of glycyrrhetinic acid showed a decreasing trend in the model group. Collectively, these results indicate that the pharmacokinetic profile of BZS differs between normal and model animals, which may be attributed to intestinal microbiota dysbiosis, abnormal intestinal motility, and intestinal barrier damage under IBS-D conditions, thereby influencing the absorption and elimination of the active components. This study provides a scientific basis for the rational clinical application of BZS.
revue: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica

titre: Cause of death in a contemporary cohort of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension
resume: BACKGROUND: In pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), contemporary risk tools primarily estimate all-cause mortality, offering limited insight into what patients die from. AIMS: We aimed to characterize cause of death across baseline mortality risk strata and to examine baseline factors associated with PAH-related versus non-PAH-related death in a national PAH cohort. METHODS AND RESULTS: Adult patients with Group 1 PAH registered in the Hellenic Pulmonary Hypertension Registry (2015-2024) were classified according to ESC/ERS three-strata risk score at baseline. Cause of death was adjudicated as PAH-related or non-PAH-related and further categorized. We modelled cause-specific mortality using competing-risk models with prespecified predictors. Model performance was summarized by discrimination and calibration. Among 462 patients followed for a median (IQR) of 2.2 (5.7) years, 163 deaths occurred; cause was adjudicated in 149 cases (55% PAH-related, 45% non-PAH-related). PAH-related deaths increased across risk strata, whereas the pattern of non-PAH causes did not differ significantly. Sepsis was the leading non-PAH cause. In multivariable competing-risk analyses, higher baseline risk for mortality and male sex independently aligned with PAH-related death, while older age aligned with non-PAH death. Discrimination was acceptable: AUC 0.77 (95% CI 0.70-0.83) for non-PAH death and 0.75 (95% CI 0.68-0.80) for PAH-related death. Integrated Brier score (IBS) improved versus null models, and calibration was good across the central predicted-risk distribution. CONCLUSION: In contemporary PAH, what patients die from differs by baseline risk. PAH progression dominates in high-risk patients, whereas competing causes, especially sepsis, remain influential across strata. Cause-specific modelling may refine counselling, prevention, and resource allocation beyond all-cause risk alone.
revue: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease

titre: Adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen for patients labelled as having refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Persistent reflux-like symptoms during proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy may reflect ongoing reflux, reflux hypersensitivity, functional heartburn, or overlapping disorders of gut-brain interaction. We assessed adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen in Chinese patients labelled as having refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease (rGERD). METHODS: We reviewed controlled trials explicitly described as randomized. Quasi-randomized and non-randomized allocation were ineligible. Eight databases were searched from inception to 28 July 2026. Post-treatment arm-level data were used consistently for continuous outcomes. Random-effects models, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), exploratory subgroup and sensitivity analyses, small-study-effect tests, and GRADE assessments were performed. RESULTS: Twenty-nine trials (3242 participants), all conducted in China, were retained after source re-audit. Adjunctive therapy was associated with higher total clinical effectiveness (26 trials; RR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20 to 1.29; I²=0%), but this was a non-standard composite assessed largely without blinding. Anxiety (23 trials; SMD - 2.38, 95% CI - 2.93 to - 1.84; I²=97.0%; 95% PI - 5.01 to 0.24), depression (24 trials; SMD - 2.36, 95% CI - 2.86 to - 1.85; I²=96.5%; 95% PI - 4.82 to 0.11), and RDQ scores (8 trials; MD - 4.01, 95% CI - 5.27 to - 2.74; I²=98.6%; 95% PI - 7.67 to - 0.35) favored adjunctive therapy on average, but effect magnitude was highly uncertain. Eight trials sparsely reported adverse events (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.84); this cannot establish a protective effect or comparative safety. Small-study effects were detected for total effectiveness and the principal psychological outcomes. Certainty was very low. CONCLUSIONS: In Chinese trials of patients labelled as having rGERD, adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen was associated with short-term improvements in composite response and symptom scores. Extreme heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing no effect for the psychological domains, limited objective reflux confirmation, unclear allocation concealment and blinding, small-study effects, and sparse harms reporting preclude confident estimates of benefit or safety and do not support routine use.

titre: Study protocol: efficacy and safety of Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32 as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder-a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Although antidepressant medications are widely used as first-line treatments, a substantial proportion of patients experience insufficient therapeutic response or limited tolerability, highlighting the need for additional safe and effective adjunctive treatment strategies. In recent years, growing evidence has suggested that the microbiota-gut-brain axis may play an important modulatory role in the onset, maintenance, and treatment response of depression. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32, a human breast milk-derived probiotic strain, as an adjunctive intervention to stable antidepressant therapy in patients with MDD, and to further explore its potential effects on selected biological markers. METHODS: This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. A total of 86 patients with MDD diagnosed according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5), are required to complete the study. Allowing for an anticipated dropout rate, 108 participants will be recruited. All participants will continue stable antidepressant treatment and will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32 or a matched placebo for 8 weeks. The primary outcome is the change in the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) score from baseline to week 8. TRIAL STATUS: This manuscript describes protocol version 1.0, dated 8 April 2025. The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100388) on 8 April 2025, a WHO ICTRP Primary Registry, which collects and publicly displays the WHO Trial Registration Data Set (TRDS). Participant recruitment began on 10 June 2025 and is ongoing at the time of submission. Recruitment is expected to be completed by December 2026.

titre: The functional connectivity of the frontoparietal control network mediates the relationship between alexithymia and non-suicidal self-injury in depressive adolescents
resume: BACKGROUND: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is common among adolescents with depression, posing a significant public health concern. Although NSSI has been linked to heightened alexithymia-characterized by difficulties in identifying and describing emotions-the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this association remain insufficiently understood in adolescents. METHODS: This study included 233 adolescents diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD), for whom resting-state functional magnetic resonance images were acquired. All participants completed the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS) and the Functional Assessment of Self-Mutilation (FASM). We estimated intra-network functional connectivity (FC) within 17 large-scale brain sub-networks and examined associations between intra-network FC, TAS scores, and NSSI. Mediation models were then fitted to examine indirect pathways among alexithymia, intra-network FC, and NSSI. RESULTS: Adolescents with MDD who engaged in NSSI showed higher alexithymia than those without NSSI, and NSSI frequency was positively correlated with the difficulty of identifying feelings in the NSSI group. Lower intra-network FC within the frontoparietal control network was associated with the presence of NSSI, and higher TAS total scores were linked to reduced intra-network FC in this network. Mediation analyses further indicated that intra-network FC in the frontoparietal control network partially mediated the association between TAS total scores and NSSI. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that alexithymia and aberrant connectivity within the frontoparietal control networks are jointly associated with NSSI in adolescent MDD. The identified neural markers and pathways offer insights into potential therapeutic targets, emphasizing the importance of addressing emotion regulation deficits and alexithymia in the treatment of NSSI.
revue: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

titre: Mindfulness-based intervention for adults with spinal cord injury: study protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is associated with high rates of depression and anxiety, yet evidence-based psychological interventions tailored to this population are lacking. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) hold promise but have not been evaluated in large-scale trials. METHODS: This is a multi-center, assessor-blind, parallel, two-arm randomized controlled trial with an initial 6-month internal pilot phase. Following a successful pilot, 216 adults with chronic SCI will be randomized to an 8-week videoconferencing-delivered, tailored MBI plus usual care, or usual care alone. The primary outcome is quality of life measured by the SF-36 at 8 weeks post-intervention. Secondary outcomes include anxiety, depression, pain, post-traumatic growth and functional independence. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle using mixed-effects regression models. RESULTS: In the feasibility study, the MBI was highly acceptable (100% willing to recommend). Significant large improvements were observed in mental health (Cohen's d = 0.83), maintained at 3-month follow-up. Attrition was 38.5%, with dropouts having significantly poorer baseline mental health. These findings informed key trial adaptations: enhanced retention strategies, a 6-month primary endpoint, and refined statistical handling of non-random missing data. CONCLUSIONS: This trial will provide robust evidence on the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a tailored MBI for improving psychological health in people with SCI, potentially guiding integration of mindfulness-based approaches into standard SCI rehabilitation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111437.

titre: Efficacy and mechanisms of device-monitored aerobic exercise for depression treatment and cognitive function improvement (DAECD trail): protocol for a randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Depression is a major public health concern, yet many patients fail to achieve remission with standard pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy, and often experience relapse and persistent cognitive impairments. Enhancing treatment outcome is therefore an urgent clinical need and aerobic exercise may have great potential. However, its efficacy in depression treatment and improving cognition, as well as the underlying mechanisms remains unclear. METHODS: This device-monitored aerobic exercise for depression and cognition improvement (DAECD) trail will enroll 80 patients with depression, randomly assigned (1:1) to an aerobic exercise group or a waiting control group. The intervention group will receive a device-measured aerobic exercise prescription for eight weeks, consisting of moderate-intensity sessions lasting 30 to 50 min, three times per week, alongside their routine treatment. The control group will continue with routine treatment and will initiate the same exercise intervention after the 8-week follow-up period. No additional pharmacological treatment will be initiated or adjusted during the intervention period as part of the study protocol. For those not currently on medication, the intervention will consist of aerobic exercise only. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, mid-intervention (week 4), and post-intervention (week 8) to evaluate the efficacy of aerobic exercise. The primary outcome is the change in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score from baseline. Secondary outcomes include cognitive function, depressive and anxiety symptoms, rumination, sleep quality, psychological resilience, safety, physical fitness, exercise capacity, and biological markers. All analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. A mixed-effects model will be used for continuous outcomes, and modified Poisson regression will be applied for binary outcomes. Neuroimaging, laboratory and multi-omics tests will be conducted at both baseline and post-intervention, to explore the potential mechanisms through which aerobic exercise exerts its antidepressant effects. DISCUSSION: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of aerobic exercise in improving depression and cognition, elucidate its underlying mechanisms, and identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit. The findings may contribute to improved treatment outcomes for depression and inform the development of individualized clinical exercise prescriptions. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClincalTrials.gov NCT06594588, registered 5 Sep 2024.

titre: Pre-treatment NUDT15 testing to inform thiopurine prescribing in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: an economic evaluation
resume: BACKGROUND: Pre-treatment NUDT15 genotype is effective at identifying individuals likely to have severe thiopurine-induced myelosuppression (TIM). We evaluate the cost-effectiveness of pre-treatment NUDT15 pharmacogenetic testing to inform thiopurine prescribing for people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). METHODS: Three strategies were compared to current practice (TPMT enzyme activity testing, not TPMT genotyping) using a decision tree model with a one-year time-horizon: • TPMT enzyme activity and NUDT15 genotyping. • Genotyping of both TPMT and NUDT15. • No testing, thiopurines are avoided, alternative treatments prescribed. Patients with IBD considered for thiopurine treatment were modelled from the UK National Health Service perspective. Primary health outcome is avoidance of severe TIM. Costs include testing, treatment for IBD and TIM. Analyses were conducted for the general population and sub-groups depending upon genetic ancestry. Parameter uncertainty is explored via deterministic sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Compared to current practice, all strategies were associated with fewer severe TIM events. Avoidance of thiopurines was the most expensive strategy. In the general population, avoidance of thiopurines had a cost per event avoided of £227,610 compared to current practice. Adding NUDT15 genotyping to TPMT testing was associated with a cost per event avoided of £6,447 compared to current practice. Genotyping of NUDT15 and TPMT dominated current practice. Differences in cost-effectiveness estimates were seen between the two sub-populations. Depending on assumptions, NUDT15 testing could be considered less costly than current practice in both groups. Genotyping costs and specific clinical management decisions had the greatest impact on results. CONCLUSIONS: Notwithstanding limitations in the model, NUDT15 genotyping could be cost-effective to inform thiopurine use in patients with IBD in the UK.
revue: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E

titre: Signal mining and safety profile analysis of prucalopride: a pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS) database
resume: BACKGROUND: Prucalopride is a highly selective 5-HT4 agonist used for chronic idiopathic constipation and gastroparesis. Although clinical trials suggest a favorable safety profile, real-world data on rare adverse events (AEs) remain scarce. This study mined the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) to detect safety signals warranting clinical attention. METHODS: FAERS data from December 14, 2018 to September 30, 2025 were collected via OpenVigil 2.1. AEs were categorised using the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities. Signal detection was performed using four specific algorithms: the Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR), the Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR), the Multi-item Gamma Poisson Shrinker (MGPS), and the Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network (BCPNN). Kappa consistency and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: We collected 1101 prucalopride-related reports and identified 35 positive adverse drug event (ADE) signals across 10 system organ classes. Gastrointestinal disorders dominated (12 signals, 373 cases), followed by psychiatric disorders (9 signals, 107 cases) and nervous system disorders (5 signals, 181 cases). Frequent reactions included headache, diarrhoea, nausea, dizziness and abdominal pain. Signal intensity varied across algorithms; gastrointestinal bacterial overgrowth emerged as a strong signal in all four. We found 19 ADEs that were not listed in the prescribing information of China, the United States, or Europe; serious unlabeled signals included intestinal obstruction and serotonin syndrome. Notably, depression, suicidal ideation, depressed mood, and nightmares appear only in the United States prescribing information. CONCLUSIONS: Prucalopride-related ADEs involve multiple organ systems, predominantly presenting as gastrointestinal disorders, psychiatric disorders and nervous system disorders. Some ADEs not included in the instructions may be serious adverse events, require great attention from clinicians. For patients with underlying comorbidities or those undergoing combination therapy, close monitoring for potential severe adverse events is essential to ensure clinical medication safety.

titre: Gastrointestinal functional disturbances in patients with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease (MAFLD): a cross-sectional study
resume: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, spectrum, and clinical significance of gastrointestinal functional disturbances in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), and their associations with disease severity, fibrosis stage, and health-related quality of life. METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study included 268 adults with MAFLD between October 2024 and October 2025. Fatty liver severity was assessed by ultrasound, and fibrosis stage was evaluated using liver stiffness measurement. Gastrointestinal functional disturbances were defined using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with disease severity and fibrosis, and linear regression evaluated relationships with quality of life. RESULTS: Gastrointestinal functional disturbances were present in 46.6% of patients with MAFLD (125/268, 95% CI 40.6%-52.6%). Compared with mild disease, moderate MAFLD was associated with higher odds of gastrointestinal functional disturbances (OR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.01-2.79), while severe MAFLD showed a stronger association (OR = 2.54, 95% CI 1.36-4.73; P for trend = 0.002). Advanced fibrosis (LSM ≥ 12.4 kPa) was also independently associated with gastrointestinal functional disturbances (OR = 2.21, 95% CI 1.02-4.78). Patients with gastrointestinal functional disturbances had significantly lower SF-36 General Health scores (β = -9.15, 95% CI - 12.84 to - 5.46, P < 0.001). These associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses and after multivariable adjustment for metabolic factors, medication use, and psychological status. CONCLUSIONS: Gastrointestinal functional disturbances are common in MAFLD and are associated with more severe disease and impaired quality of life, highlighting the need for integrated clinical management.

titre: When alpha-gal hides: a case series of atypical presentations of alpha-gal syndrome in children
resume: BACKGROUND: Alpha-gal syndrome is an IgE-mediated allergy resulting from sensitisation to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose (alpha-gal). Although classically associated with delayed urticaria or anaphylaxis following red meat ingestion, it can present with diverse and atypical manifestations. We report four paediatric patients with rare and atypical manifestations of alpha-gal syndrome. CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1: An 18-month-old boy with recurrent respiratory symptoms was on treatment for allergic rhinitis and poorly controlled asthma for 6 months. His symptoms showed an inconsistent association with dairy consumption; however, there were no cutaneous manifestations. Case 2: An 11-year-old boy with recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits for 1 year was managed as irritable bowel syndrome. His symptoms frequently followed ingestion of dairy products. Case 3: An 8-year-old boy had been experiencing brief episodes of urticaria for 4 months. He was treated as having chronic spontaneous urticaria with poor response to standard treatment. Case 4: An 18-year-old girl had 19 episodes of idiopathic anaphylaxis since the age of 6 years, with symptoms that were not consistently associated with an identifiable food trigger. All patients recalled a history of tick bites. Detailed history revealed delayed symptom onset and inconsistent reactions to alpha-gal-containing foods. The diagnosis of alpha-gal syndrome was confirmed in all four patients by skin prick testing and elevated specific IgE for alpha-gal. Elimination of the implicated food allergens led to complete resolution in all cases. CONCLUSIONS: This case series illustrates the diverse and atypical clinical presentations of alpha-gal syndrome in children which can lead to delayed recognition and misdiagnosis. Increased clinician awareness is the key to early diagnosis, thus preventing recurrent episodes of symptoms and anaphylaxis and improving overall outcomes.

titre: Captive parrot interspecific and intraspecific variation in gastrointestinal microbiota composition revealed by large-scale profiling
resume: BACKGROUND: Parrots (Psittaciformes) are the most popular pet birds kept throughout the world. It is estimated that presently about half of the global parrot population lives in captivity. However, domestic parrots are susceptible to numerous health issues, with digestive and behavioural disorders being the most commonly reported. Such disorders can be linked to gastrointestinal tract (GIT) microbiota either directly or via gut-brain axis. Yet, the parrot GIT microbiota is largely unexplored, which limits the potential for therapeutic use of probiotics in veterinary practice. Here, we addressed the interspecific and intraspecific variation in parrot-associated bacterial diversity by assessing healthy captive parrots' GIT bacterial microbiota composition through 16 S rRNA profiling. RESULTS: We analysed faecal and oral microbiota of 286 individuals from 66 parrot species. Faecal and oral microbiota differed in composition, with oral microbiota having significantly higher alpha diversity and lower interindividual variation. We did not find any core OTU or bacterial genus present in faecal or oral samples of all individuals or species studied. Yet, the genera Corynebacterium and Streptococcus were represented in over 90% of the oral samples. Lactobacillus was predominant in faeces (75% of the samples). Our results reveal high interspecific and intraspecific variation in both faecal and oral microbiota, with host species and owner identity being the most important factors influencing microbial composition and diversity. Individuals representing the same parrot species or genus shared similar microbiotas, but deeper phylogenetic lineages showed only low levels of phylosymbiosis. Similarities in the composition of the parrot oral microbiota were more strongly aligned with phylogeny than similarities observed in the faecal microbiota. Sampling date exerted minor yet significant effects on microbial composition, and sex had an additional effect in the oral microbiota. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides presently the most comprehensive characterisation of the GIT microbiota composition and its variation in parrots. Comparing a wide range of healthy captive parrots, we uncover the main factors contributing to microbiome diversity. Our results offer a reference for further research aimed at investigation of the physiological effects of GIT bacteria and the development of novel veterinary therapeutics.

titre: Effect of probiotic, prebiotic, and synbiotic supplementation on anemia in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
resume: BACKGROUND: Anemia is common in hemodialysis patients and reduces quality of life. Gut dysbiosis may contribute. Biotic supplements (probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics) could help, but evidence is uncertain. This review evaluated their effects on hemoglobin, hematocrit, ferritin, and TIBC. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, and Google Scholar up to May 2026 (PRISMA 2020). We included randomized controlled trials that compared probiotics, prebiotics, or synbiotics with a placebo in hemodialysis patients. PRIMARY OUTCOME: hemoglobin. Secondary: hematocrit, ferritin, TIBC. Two reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed bias risk independently using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. We performed meta-analyses with a random-effects model. We evaluated the certainty of evidence using the GRADE framework. PROSPERO: CRD420261404639. RESULTS: Nine randomized controlled trials with 878 patients were included. Biotic supplementation did not significantly improve hemoglobin (MD = 0.56 g/dL, 95% CI = -0.21 to 1.32, P = 0.15; I² = 89%). It also did not significantly affect hematocrit (MD = -0.09%, 95% CI = -2.43 to 2.26, P = 0.94; I² = 51%), ferritin (MD = 11.65 ng/mL, 95% CI = -12.70 to 35.99, P = 0.35; I² = 26%), or TIBC (MD = -68.35 mg/dL, 95% CI = -139.18 to 2.48, P = 0.06; I² = 56%). Subgroup analysis showed that probiotic supplementation (3 studies, 148 patients) significantly increased hemoglobin (MD = 0.51 g/dL, 95% CI = 0.01 to 1.01, P = 0.04; I² = 0%). In contrast, synbiotic supplementation (4 studies, 168 patients) did not have a significant effect (MD = 0.14 g/dL, 95% CI = -0.46 to 0.74, P = 0.65; I² = 62%). Prebiotic supplementation (1 study, 162 patients) showed a significant increase, but this finding should be interpreted with caution. Sensitivity analysis that excluded the prebiotic study led to an overall null effect with lower variability (I² = 32%). The certainty of evidence was low for hemoglobin, hematocrit, and TIBC, and moderate for ferritin. CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests probiotics may slightly improve hemoglobin in hemodialysis patients. Synbiotics do not appear effective. Prebiotics require further study. Larger, well-designed trials are needed to confirm these findings. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

titre: Predicting response to electroconvulsive therapy combined with antipsychotics in patients with schizophrenia using insula-related functional connectivity: an interoceptive theory-driven analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Variability in electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) response among patients with schizophrenia and the risks of ineffective treatment limit its clinical use. Identifying reliable predictors to accurately forecast patient response to ECT continues to be a major challenge. This study aimed to investigate whether insula-related functional connectivity features (FCs), grounded in interoceptive dysfunction theory, can accurately predict ECT-antipsychotics (APs) combination outcomes in schizophrenia and identify reliable predictors and potential neural mechanisms of ECT-APs. METHODS: Forty-five patients with schizophrenia, either treatment-resistant or in an acute exacerbation, underwent MRI and clinical assessments at baseline and after 4-weeks of ECT-APs treatment in this single-center proof-of-concept study. Based on interoceptive dysfunction theory, baseline insula-related FCs were extracted to train a machine learning model for predicting the change in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale scores (PANSS%) within a nested cross-validation framework. We also identified the functional connectivity patterns of responders and explored potential neural targets of ECT-APs. RESULTS: Cross-validation of the optimal model revealed that 16 baseline insula-related FCs significantly predicted post-ECT-APs changes in PANSS(%) scores (r[predicted vs. observed] = 0.93, p < 0.001). These features involved FCs between the insula (ventral anterior and posterior) and large-scale networks encompassing frontal, temporal, limbic, thalamic, and cerebellar regions. Among them, three FCs showed significant post-ECT-APs changes that were associated with symptom improvement, suggesting dual roles as predictors and potential therapeutic targets involving salience-auditory-interoceptive circuits. Others, such as insula-cerebellar Crus II and insula-precuneus connections, distinguished responders and non-responders but less modifiable by ECT-APs. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preliminary evidence for the predictive value of insula-related functional connectivity in ECT-APs response; future multi-center studies are needed to confirm generalizability. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

titre: Brief guided written exposure therapy for PTSD and complex PTSD in adolescents: a pilot randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is prevalent among adolescents, yet evidence-based treatments remain inaccessible to most. Complex PTSD (CPTSD), recently recognized in ICD-11, lacks empirical evidence to guide intervention in this population. Guided Written Exposure (GWE) is a brief, non-phased trauma-focused treatment with established efficacy in adults. This pilot trial evaluated the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of group-delivered GWE for adolescent PTSD and CPTSD. METHODS: Fifty-three adolescents (aged 13-17) with PTSD symptoms following diverse trauma exposures were randomized to five-session group GWE (n = 27) or waitlist (n = 26). Primary outcomes were PTSD and CPTSD symptoms. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, and affective and behavioral problems. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, 1-month, and 3-month (GWE only) follow-up. Treatment effects were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: GWE produced significantly greater reductions than waitlist in PTSD (d = - 1.15, 95% CI [- 1.89, - 0.41]) and CPTSD symptoms (d = - 0.97, 95% CI [- 1.70, - 0.23]) at post-treatment, with gains maintained through 3-month follow-up. Depression and affective and behavioral problems also improved significantly. Retention was high (92.6%) with no adverse events. Anxiety did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Group-delivered GWE demonstrates promise as a brief, scalable intervention for posttraumatic stress symptoms, particularly in low-resource settings, and provides preliminary support that non-phased trauma-focused approaches may be feasible for adolescents with CPTSD. Replication in larger trials is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06403449). Registered on 3 May 2024.

titre: Rapunzel syndrome in a 16-year-old girl without noticeable hair loss or bald patches: a case report
resume: BACKGROUND: Trichotillomania is a disorder consisting of repetitive hair pulling due to a strong urge to do so with a sense of relief after. Trichophagia is closely related to trichotillomania and involves the eating of hair that has been pulled out. It is estimated that only 1% of patients with trichophagia go on to develop a trichobezoar, a bezoar made of hair. Trichobezoars are formed when the hair strands get stuck within the folds of the gastric wall and eventually form a ball as the hair accumulates. CASE PRESENTATION: A 16-year-old Caucasian girl was transferred to our hospital with vomiting and a suspected gastrointestinal (GI) obstruction. Upon an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan, it was discovered that she had a large bezoar spanning her stomach and duodenum which was surgically removed due to inability to reach it with a scope. It was found to contain hair and after interviewing the patient a diagnosis of trichotillomania was made. There was no noticeable hair loss on the patient. The psychiatry team started her on sertraline 25 mg with a referral for CBT once discharged from the hospital. CONCLUSIONS: This patient represents a unique case in that her condition began 2 years ago and has been stable in severity ever since it began. This case demonstrates the importance of having this disease on the differential diagnosis even for those who do not have another clear mental illness and who do not meet the usual criteria of psychiatric causes. Given that trichobezoars have the potential to be very dangerous, and sometimes even deadly, it is important to not overlook this diagnosis in an adolescent female with nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain even in the absence of noticeable hair loss or a coexisting psychiatric disorder.

titre: Appetitive trait profiles in late life: links to eating disorder psychopathology and psychosocial well-being
resume: OBJECTIVE: Appetitive traits shape eating behaviors across the lifespan, yet their patterns and health correlates in later life remain poorly understood. This study used latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify potential distinct profiles of appetitive traits among older adults and to examine their sociodemographic and oral health correlates, as well as their associations with eating disorder symptoms and psychosocial outcomes. METHOD: A sample of 579 Chinese older adults (aged 60-93 years) was included. LPA was conducted to derive appetitive trait profiles, followed by multinomial logistic regression and Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars (BCH) analyses to examine correlates of profile membership and psychosocial and physical health outcomes. RESULTS: Older adults were reflected across four profiles: Low Appetitive Traits (16.1%), Moderate Appetitive Traits with Emotional Under-Eating (29.0%), Moderate Appetitive Traits (44.9%), and High Conflicted Appetitive Traits (10.0%). Oral health emerged as a consistent correlate of profile membership, alongside age, marital status, residence, and education, whereas sex and number of natural teeth were not associated with membership. Profiles differed significantly in psychological distress, disordered eating, ARFID symptoms, and health-related quality of life. The High Conflicted Appetitive Traits profile was characterized by the highest levels of eating-related symptoms and the poorest psychosocial outcomes, whereas the Low Appetitive Traits profile showed relatively more favorable psychological and quality-of-life indicators in this sample. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in appetitive traits in later life and highlight their close links with oral health, sociodemographic factors, and psychological well-being. Identifying high-risk appetitive profiles may inform targeted interventions integrating nutritional guidance, oral health promotion, and psychosocial support to promote healthy aging.

titre: Navigating the diagnostic challenges of maladaptive daydreaming: a case report of ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic obsessive fantasies with functional impairment in a 17-year-old
resume: INTRODUCTION: Maladaptive daydreaming (MD) is an emerging and insufficiently recognized clinical phenomenon characterized by immersive fantasy activity associated with functional impairment. Its overlap with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and schizophrenia spectrum conditions creates significant diagnostic uncertainty, particularly in adolescents. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 17-year-old female presenting with intrusive celebrity-focused fantasies, sleep disturbance, behavioral regression, social withdrawal, and reduced self-care. She described co-existing ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic obsessive imagery with auditory-like pseudo-hallucinatory experiences. The Maladaptive Daydreaming Scale (MDS-16) score was 76%, consistent with probable MD. Extensive medical and neuroimaging investigations were unremarkable. Differential diagnoses included OCD, schizotypal traits, ASD, and schizophrenia prodrome. INTERVENTION AND OUTCOME: Initial treatment with fluoxetine was changed to quetiapine, alongside cognitive behavioral therapy, occupational therapy, structured behavioral strategies, and family psychoeducation. The patient demonstrated gradual improvement in distress, insight, sleep, and engagement, although intrusive fantasies persisted. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the complexity of distinguishing MD from other psychiatric conditions in adolescents and supports the value of a multidisciplinary, function-focused management approach. Early recognition may prevent misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. NUMBER OF CLINICAL TRIALS: Not applicable.

titre: Efficacy of community interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms: a Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
resume: BACKGROUND: Communities play a crucial role in addressing trauma-related stress. Broadly, community interventions include both evidence-based psychotherapies delivered in community-relevant settings, such as cognitive processing therapy (CPT), prolonged exposure (PE), and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and community-tailored approaches adapted to local resources and service needs, such as Common Elements Treatment Approaches (CETA), community psychoeducation, and care management. Although an increasing number of studies have examined community interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms, debates persist, and systematic evidence remains limited. This study conducted a network meta-analysis (NMA) to assess and compare the effectiveness of community interventions for PTSD symptoms. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included if they examined community interventions for PTSD symptoms among trauma-exposed community populations. Studies were identified through Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, Wanfang, and CINAHL. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool, and data were synthesized using Bayesian NMA with random-effects models. RESULTS: Thirty-six RCTs involving 5,350 participants and 16 intervention types were included. The primary outcomes were immediate post-treatment and follow-up PTSD symptoms within 6 months; secondary outcomes included immediate depression and anxiety symptoms, and treatment attrition. PE (SMD = 1.69, 95% CrI [1.14, 2.24]) and CPT (SMD = 1.23, 95% CrI [0.81, 1.67]) showed relatively strong immediate effects on PTSD symptoms in community settings. When combined into a single node, community-tailored interventions showed a significant moderate immediate effect (SMD = 0.52, 95% CrI [0.34, 0.71]). When modeled separately, community-tailored psychological interventions, care management, psychoeducation, and CETA also showed significant moderate effects, with SMDs ranging from 0.48 to 0.59. CONCLUSIONS: Trauma-focused interventions, particularly PE and CPT, appeared to show relatively strong effects in reducing PTSD symptoms in community settings, suggesting the potential value of approaches that incorporate cognitive restructuring and structured engagement with trauma-related cues. Community-tailored approaches showed some evidence of immediate benefit and may provide feasible, accessible support for trauma-affected populations, especially where specialist resources are limited. This NMA provides comparative evidence to guide the selection, adaptation, and delivery of PTSD interventions in community settings. PROSPERO registration number: CRD42023396053.

titre: CalliSpheres® drug-eluting beads transarterial chemoembolization versus conventional transarterial chemoembolization in patients with refractory liver metastases: a propensity score-matched multi-center study
resume: BACKGROUND: CalliSpheres® is the first domestically developed drug-eluting bead product in China. Although its therapeutic efficacy has been reported in primary liver cancer, clinical data remain limited for patients with refractory liver metastases failing standard systemic therapy, and head-to-head comparisons between CalliSpheres® drug-eluting beads transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) and conventional TACE (cTACE) are scarce. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of the two interventional modalities for refractory liver metastases. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective multi-center study enrolled patients with refractory liver metastases who received DEB-TACE or cTACE across four clinical centers between January 2018 and December 2021. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance confounding bias. Tumor response was assessed at 1, 3 and 6 months post-procedure per RECIST version 1.1 criteria. Primary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints consisted of disease control rate (DCR), quality of life (assessed via QLQ-C30), liver function parameters and adverse events. RESULTS: A total of 102 patients received DEB-TACE and 118 received cTACE. After PSM, 58 patients remained in each group with balanced baseline characteristics. The DEB-TACE group had significantly higher ORR at 1, 3 and 6 months than the cTACE group (58.6% vs. 34.5%, P = 0.001; 48.3% vs. 27.6%, P = 0.009; 44.8% vs. 25.9%, P = 0.038). Median PFS (10.5 vs. 6.7 months, P = 0.003) and median OS (25.2 vs. 15.7 months, P = 0.006) were significantly prolonged in the DEB-TACE group. Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that cTACE was an independent adverse risk factor for PFS (HR = 1.72, P = 0.009) and OS (HR = 1.65, P = 0.026). The degrees of postoperative day-4 elevations in ALT and AST as well as the incidence of abdominal pain were significantly lower in the DEB-TACE group (all P < 0.05). There were no grade ≥ 3 serious adverse events in either group. CONCLUSIONS: CalliSpheres® DEB-TACE achieves superior ORR, PFS and OS and better safety compared with cTACE for patients with refractory liver metastases. Prospective randomized controlled trials are warranted to validate these findings.

titre: Systematic review and meta analysis of self guided virtual reality exposure therapy for social anxiety
resume: Self-guided virtual reality exposure therapy (SGVRET) may offer a scalable approach for social anxiety, but its independent effects remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA and Cochrane methodological guidance. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus, and 13 randomized controlled trials were included. Results indicate that SGVRET was associated with a significant reduction in public speaking anxiety (PSAS; SMD = -1.47, 95% CI [-2.56, -0.37]). For overall social anxiety severity (LSAS/LSAS-SR), the pooled estimate favored SGVRET but did not reach statistical significance and showed substantial heterogeneity (SMD = -0.69, 95% CI [-1.50, 0.13]). No statistically significant improvements were detected for social phobia symptoms (SPS/SPS-6; SMD = -0.17, 95% CI [-0.67, 0.32]) or social interaction anxiety (SIAS/SIAS-6; SMD = -0.35, 95% CI [-1.07, 0.37]). However, most included trials had a high risk of bias, limiting the robustness of the evidence. Overall, the findings suggest that SGVRET may hold potential for performance-related social anxiety, particularly public speaking anxiety, but the current evidence remains preliminary and requires confirmation in larger, rigorous trials.

titre: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia alleviates Alzheimer's disease model phenotype by inhibiting Aβ aggregation via autophagy
resume: Probiotics exert neuroprotective effects against Alzheimer's disease (AD) through modulation of gut-brain axis signaling pathways, yet disease-modifying therapies remain elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (S. maltophilia) ameliorates AD-associated pathological and behavioral phenotypes in Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) models, including learning deficits and paralysis. Mechanistically, S. maltophilia suppresses β-amyloid (Aβ) peptide aggregation by orchestrating the activation of conserved cellular pathways: autophagy, innate immune signaling, and unfolded protein responses in the mitochondria (UPRmt) and endoplasmic reticulum (UPRer). Specifically, S. maltophilia induces UPRmt in an atfs-1-dependent manner and activates UPRer via the PERK kinase PEK-1. Further mechanistic analysis suggests that S. maltophilia initiates a signaling cascade: activation of ATF-7 immune pathways enhanced autophagy and subsequent clearance of Aβ aggregates. Metabolomic screening further pinpointed pizotifen as a bioactive metabolite that might inhibit Aβ aggregation through immune modulation.

titre: [Research progress on the mechanism of acupuncture in protecting the intestinal barrier to intervene in Parkinson's disease]
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence from recent years indicates a strong association between PD pathogenesis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, with impairment of the intestinal barrier being recognized as a critical initiating factor. This review summarizes current research on the multi-target mechanisms through which acupuncture protects the intestinal barrier and thereby intervenes in PD progression. Evidence suggests that acupuncture can restore gut microbiota homeostasis by increasing short-chain fatty acids and reducing lipopolysaccharide levels; upregulate the expression of tight junction proteins (zonula occludens-1, occludin) and mucin (Muc 2), thereby directly reinforcing the intestinal physical barrier; effectively clear aberrant α-Syn aggregates in the colon and suppress the NOD-like receptor 3 and nuclear factor κB pathway to alleviate intestinal inflammation. These mechanisms act synergistically to maintain intestinal barrier integrity and block the transmission of pathological signals from the gut to the brain.
revue: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research

titre: The role of the gut microbiome in stress responses of dogs: gut-brain axis and microbiome-targeted interventions
resume: Stress poses a significant threat to canine welfare and adoptability, particularly in animal shelters where dogs are exposed to multiple environmental and social stressors. Growing evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis (GBA), a bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system, plays a critical role in regulating stress responses. This review summarizes the mechanisms through which the gut microbiome influences canine behavior and physiology via neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways. We further examine current evidence showing that acute and chronic stress can disrupt the canine gut microbiome, leading to reduced microbial diversity and shifts toward pro-inflammatory bacterial communities. In addition, we discuss microbiome-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modulation, and fecal microbiota transplantation, as potential strategies for improving stress resilience and gastrointestinal health. Collectively, the available evidence suggests modulation of the gut microbiome may provide a practical, non-invasive approach to supporting stress management and psychological well-being in dogs. A better understanding of host-microbiome interactions may contribute to the development of evidence-based nutritional and microbial interventions to improve canine stress management and welfare.
revue: The Journal of veterinary medical science

titre: Efficacy and Predictors of Response to a Low‐FODMAP Diet in Patients With Overlap of Functional Dyspepsia and Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Prospective Multicentre Randomized Clinical Trial
resume: In patients with functional dyspepsia–IBS overlap, a low-FODMAP diet provided better symptom relief and quality-of-life improvement than traditional dietary advice. Most patients who initially improved experienced symptom recurrence when FODMAPs were reintroduced, suggesting dietary responsiveness. Postprandial distress and greater baseline symptom burden were independently associated with true response. ABSTRACT Background and Aims Functional dyspepsia (FD) frequently coexists with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), resulting in a complex clinical phenotype characterized by prominent postprandial symptoms and limited treatment options. We compared the efficacy of a low–fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) diet with traditional dietary advice (TDA) in this population. Methods In this multicentre randomized, assessor-blinded trial, adults fulfilling Rome IV criteria for both FD and IBS were assigned to a low-FODMAP diet (LFD) or TDA for 6 weeks, with structured dietitian support. The primary endpoint was a combined response, defined by both a ≥ 50-point reduction in IBS Symptom Severity Scale and a ≥ 30% reduction in Short-Form Nepean Dyspepsia Index (SFNDI) symptom scores at 6 weeks. Among patients who responded to LFD, FODMAPS were systematically reintroduced from 7 to 12 weeks, and patients who had symptom recurrence were defined as ‘true responders’. Baseline predictors of true LFD response were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression (CTRI/2025/04/084483). Results A total of, 112 participants were randomized (LFD, n = 59; TDA, n = 53; mean age 40.9 ± 15.2 years, 42.8% males). After 6 weeks, the combined IBS-FD response rates were 59.3% versus 32.1% ( p = 0.005) in the LFD and TDA arms respectively. After FODMAP reintroduction, 32/35 patients (91.4%) had symptom recurrence (true responders). Improvements in symptom and disease-specific quality-of-life scores favoured LFD. Exploratory multivariable predictors of response to LFD were postprandial distress sub-type and a higher (worse) baseline SF-NDI quality-of-life score. Conclusion A low-FODMAP diet was superior to traditional dietary advice in improving global symptoms and HRQoL in patients with FD–IBS overlap, supporting targeted fermentable carbohydrate restriction as an effective, personalized therapeutic strategy.

titre: Machine learning-integrated full-length 16S rRNA gene profiling reveals early-life gut microbial signatures associated with subsequent infantile colic in Thai infants
resume: Infantile colic develops after the neonatal period, but neonatal gut microbial patterns preceding symptom onset remain unclear. We examined early-life gut microbiome associations with subsequent infantile colic and internally evaluated microbiome-only prediction alongside retrospective metadata-containing comparisons. Stool samples collected 0-4 days after birth from 209 Thai infants (119 healthy and 90 who later met Rome IV diagnostic criteria for infantile colic) were profiled by Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing. Analyses included diversity and composition assessments, covariate-adjusted MaAsLin3 models, repeated nested cross-validation, and exploratory conditional association networks. Infants who subsequently developed infantile colic had lower Chao1 richness than healthy infants (q = 8.7 × 10-5), although delivery mode and collection day explained more community variation than outcome status. After covariate adjustment, Enterococcus faecium presence was associated with subsequent colic (odds ratio, 4.23; q = 0.021). The fully nested model-development procedure yielded participant-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) values of 0.773 and 0.740. In a secondary fixed-model comparison including feeding summarized through one month, a species-presence radial basis function support vector machine outperformed metadata alone (mean outer-fold AUROC/AUPRC, 0.780/0.764 vs. 0.539/0.484), while adding metadata produced only a small, uncertain improvement. Exploratory network analysis contextualized candidate taxa within group-specific conditional association modules. These findings support a focused early-life species-level pattern associated with subsequent infantile colic and prioritize candidate microbial features for external validation.

titre: Butyrate and the brain-gut axis in Parkinson's disease: From microbial metabolite to potential therapeutic target
resume: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with substantial unmet therapeutic needs. This narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the role of the gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acid butyrate in the brain-gut axis in Parkinson's disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies suggest that butyrate reinforces intestinal barrier integrity and modulates intestinal immune responses, with enteric glial and vagal pathways providing possible links to central neuroinflammation. Its effects on microglial inflammatory phenotypes and autophagic clearance of α-synuclein, including possible cholinergic mediation, require further validation. We critically evaluated the strengths and limitations of this evidence, discussed inconsistent findings across cohorts, and summarized clinical studies on butyrate-related interventions, including butyrate supplementation, dietary fiber, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Although preclinical evidence is substantial and context dependent, clinical translation is constrained by small and heterogeneous human cohorts, unresolved butyrate bioavailability, optimal dose and route of administration, long-term safety concerns, variability of the gut microbiota, and the absence of randomized evidence establishing butyrate-specific disease modification. Microglial heterogeneity revealed by single-cell transcriptomic studies also challenges the classical M1/M2 framework. We conclude by proposing priorities for future research, including well-powered randomized trials, standardized butyrate and microbiome measurements, patient stratification, and single-cell investigations.
revue: The Journal of international medical research

titre: The catalpol-gut-brain-neurogenesis axis: a testable framework for the pharmacokinetic paradox of catalpol in the aged hippocampal niche
resume: Adult hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG) neurogenesis declines with brain ageing, contributing to cognitive impairment. Catalpol, an iridoid glycoside from Rehmannia glutinosa, exerts robust neuroprotective effects, yet its poor brain penetration (XLogP3-AA ≈ -3.2; TPSA = 162Å²) poses a pharmacokinetic paradox. We propose the Catalpol-Gut-Brain-Neurogenesis Axis (CGBNA) as a falsifiable framework generating four predictions: (i) germ-free or microbiota-depleted animals will not exhibit catalpol-induced DG neurogenesis or cognitive improvement; (ii) hippocampal tissue will contain gut-derived phenolic metabolites, not intact catalpol, at functionally relevant concentrations after oral catalpol; (iii) re-colonisation with catalpol-metabolising bacteria will restore these effects; (iv) direct administration of candidate metabolites will recapitulate catalpol's neurogenic and cognitive effects. Direct in vivo evidence that orally administered isolated catalpol is converted by gut microbiota into scopoletin, protocatechuic acid, or vanillic acid at functionally relevant concentrations remains lacking. These predictions define the experimental agenda for validating or refuting the CGBNA.

titre: Combined prognostic association between GLIM-diagnosed malnutrition and quality of life with survival in digestive cancer patients
resume: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between malnutrition, diagnosed using GLIM criteria, and SF-36 General Health score among patients with colorectal (CRC) and other digestive cancers and to evaluate the combined prognostic association of malnutrition and QoL with survival at 90 days and 1 year after discharge. METHODS: In a prospective cohort of 519 cancer patients, nutritional status was assessed using MUST and GLIM criteria. QoL was measured with the SF-36 and EuroQol questionnaires, and functional status with the Barthel Index. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox regression identified prognostic factors. RESULTS: Patients were 62% male with a mean age of 67.9 years; 23.51% were moderately and 21.97% severely malnourished. The most prevalent diagnosis was CRC (65.5%). Patients had moderate functional status and QoL scores at admission. Mortality was 12.5% at 90 days and 27% at 1 year. Combined low SF-36 General Health score and malnutrition was associated with 90-day mortality (HR = 6.03, p 0.80). CONCLUSIONS: Combined assessment of GLIM-defined malnutrition and self-reported general health may help identify hospitalised patients with digestive cancer who are at increased risk of post-discharge mortality. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Whether interventions based on this risk stratification improve outcomes requires prospective interventional evaluation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov as ID NCT04188990. Registration date: 2 December 2019.
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

titre: Gut Microbiota, Red Wine and Atherosclerosis
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review the relationships among gut microbiota, dietary patterns, red wine (RW) consumption, and atherosclerosis, with emphasis on microbiome-related metabolic pathways and their potential relevance to cardiovascular prevention. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence has expanded our understanding of the microbiome-metabolome interface in cardiometabolic disease. Dietary patterns can modify microbial diversity and metabolites involved in inflammation, glucose homeostasis, and cardiovascular risk. Recent studies also support associations between wine-related dietary exposures, gut microbiota composition, and circulating metabolites. In the Wine Flora Study, moderate RW consumption was associated with broad shifts in gut microbiota and plasma metabolomic profiles without modifying plasma trimethylamine N-oxide. The gut microbiota participates in multiple metabolic pathways relevant to cardiovascular health and atherosclerosis. Diet is an important determinant of microbiome composition, and RW polyphenols may influence microbial and metabolic profiles. Nevertheless, a healthy diet, regular physical activity, smoking avoidance, and weight control remain cornerstones of cardiovascular prevention.

titre: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Study Comparing Effects of Metronome-Cued Versus Yoga Breathing on HRV in Patients with Chronic Pain
resume: Background In a previous study, patients with chronic pain showed increased vagally mediated heart rate variability (VmHRV; the variation in the time between heartbeats driven by the vagus nerve) and positive mood states after 10 minutes of metronome-cued low-inspiration-to-expiration (MC low i/e) breathing. Low i/e can also be achieved with yoga breathing which may be less anxiety producing while improving interoception, than metronome regulated breathing. Bumblebee yoga breathing (BBYB) involves a low i/e ratio with a reduced breathing rate. The present explorative study aimed to determine how BBYB and MC low i/e influence VmHRV in patients with chronic pain. Methods In this, exploratory randomized controlled trial, three hundred and four patients with chronic pain, aged between 20 and 70 years, were randomized into four groups. These were: (i) MC low i/e (with a ratio of 28:72 and 12 breaths/minute), (ii) metronome cued equal i/e breathing (MC equal i/e; with a ratio of 50:50 and 12 breaths/minute), (iii) BBYB, and (iv) spontaneous breathing (SB) act as control. The VmHRV, respiration, blood pressure and global vigor (self-reported energy) and mood states (using the Global Vigor and affect Scale (GVA)) were assessed. The data were analyzed using repeated measures analyses of variance (RM-ANOVA). Results The BBYB group alone achieved a low i/e ratio (attained i/e of 0.34). The MC low i/e group and MC equal i/e group had breath rates of 13.72 and 12.29 BPM, respectively but neither achieved the intended i/e ratio. Natural log of LF power in the HRV series for the low frequency band (0.04-0.15 Hz) (LnLF) was significantly greater during BBYB than during spontaneous breathing as control (SB). Natural log of HF power in the HRV series for the high frequency band (0.15-0.40 Hz)) (LnHF) was significantly higher during the MC low i/e and MC equal i/e breathing compared to SB. Natural log of the root mean square of successive time differences between normal, consecutive heartbeats (LnRMSSD) was significantly higher during the MC low i/e, MC equal i/e, and BBYB compared to SB. Self-reported pain intensity was significantly lower after the MC low i/e and BBYB compared to SB (p < 0.05; in all cases based on RM-ANOVA). Conclusion The results suggest that decreased breath rate in both BBYB and MC low i/e appears to increase VmHRV. Pain was significantly lower after MC low i/e and BBYB compared to SB. Also, BBYB alone demonstrated a low inspiration/exhalation ratio, suggesting that modifying breathing in line with yoga practices may facilitate the transition more easily than MC breathing.

titre: Scoping review on dosing of anaesthetic and perioperative drugs in patients with obesity: which body weight for which molecule
resume: BACKGROUND: The prevalence of obesity is rising. Patients with obesity are increasingly exposed to anaesthesia, critical care, and perioperative pharmacotherapy. Obesity alters drug pharmacokinetics in a non-linear, drug-specific manner, so that simply scaling doses to total body weight (TBW) exposes patients to overdose or underdose. A recurring clinical question is therefore: which body weight descriptor should be used for which molecule? METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. We synthesized pharmacokinetic evidence, recent meta-analyses, and French and European guidelines on dose adjustment in adults with obesity for five drug classes of anaesthesia and critical care: hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA), perioperative antibiotics, and non-opioid analgesics. We summarised the recommended dosing weight for each molecule in a table and a figure. RESULTS: No single weight descriptor applies. Lipophilic induction agents (propofol), most opioids (alfentanil, fentanyl, sufentanil), and non-depolarising NMBA are best dosed on lean or ideal body weight, whereas succinylcholine, neuromuscular reversal, and aminoglycosides use total or adjusted body weight. Maintenance of hypnosis and pain management in the post-anaesthesia care unit are titrated to monitored effect. Cephalosporin-based antibiotic prophylaxis relies on fixed doses (e.g., cefazolin 2 g) up to high body mass index values due to their hydrophilic properties. Paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are given at standard doses and never scaled to TBW. Findings are consolidated in a single bedside reference table. CONCLUSION: Dosing in obesity must be molecule-specific, guided by the relevant weight descriptor and by intraoperative monitoring rather than by TBW alone.
