titre: Bach flower remedies and the discrepancy between randomized controlled trials and patient-perspectives A critical review
resume: Bach flower remedies are widely used complementary interventions for emotional well-being. Despite their popularity and frequent reports of perceived benefit, previous reviews concluded that placebo-controlled trials provide little evidence for effects beyond placebo. This discrepancy between trial findings and patient experiences remains insufficiently explored. This non-systematic critical narrative review examined clinical literature on Bach flower remedies, including trials, observational studies, case reports, and theoretical literature, focusing on methodological quality, placebo-controlled evidence, and potential psychological mechanisms. Uncontrolled studies and case reports frequently reported positive outcomes, particularly for emotional distress, anxiety, stress, and subjective well-being. In contrast, most randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials showed no clinically meaningful effects beyond placebo, despite improvements in both groups. The evidence does not support a specific pharmacological or energy-based mechanism of action. We suggest a hypothesis that several psychological and contextual factors may contribute to perceived benefits, including the provision of a coherent explanatory model, positive treatment expectancy, hope, therapeutic alliance, emotional self-awareness, self-reflection, therapeutic rituals, conditioning processes, spirituality, and motivational congruence. The discrepancy between predominantly negative placebo-controlled trials and frequently positive patient-reported experiences suggests that Bach flower therapy may be more appropriately conceptualized as a psychologically mediated intervention rather than an energy-based treatment. Experimental studies in this field are lacking. Future research should aim to clarify these mechanisms, evaluate effectiveness under informed consent, assess its role as adjunct to conventional care, and reduce publication bias through reporting both positive and negative findings.

titre: Ayurvedic management of mixed-type obsessive-compulsive disorder along with comorbid depression (Atatvabhinivesha): A case report
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a chronic and debilitating neuropsychiatric condition characterised by persistent intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours performed to alleviate anxiety or distress. Ayurveda describes a similar entity, Atatvabhinivesha, a Manovikara characterised by delusional adherence to false beliefs due to Rajo-tamo vitiation. A 34-year-old male, pre-diagnosed with mixed type OCD with comorbid depression, presented to Ayurvedic hospital with obsessive cleaning rituals, intrusive thoughts, disturbed sleep with hypnic jerks, and sustained anxiety for two years. Despite two months of conventional treatment, symptom control remained inadequate. The patient was managed through Panchakarma [Virechana Karma (∼purgation therapy), Basti Karma (∼enema therapy), Nasya Karma (∼nasal drops therapy)] followed by oral Medhya Rasayana for 45 days of IPD. Oral Medhya Rasayana was prescribed with Pathya-apathya for the next 5 months in OPD. Daivavyapashraya chikitsa [Gayatri Mantra chanting, Havan, meditation, Moti Dharana, etc.] was also performed throughout the treatment. Marked reduction in HAM-D (26 to 5), Y-BOCS (28 to 6) scores, and almost complete relief in symptoms were observed. The quality of life of the patient was also improved. The conventional medicine dosage was reduced in a tapering dose up to 3 months and was completely stopped by the patient after 3 months of Ayurvedic treatment without any symptomatic aggravation. Even after 1 year from the date of admission, no relapse was observed, despite discontinuation of all oral medications for the past six months. This case highlights the efficacy of Ayurvedic treatment in OCD comorbid with depression management without any clinically apparent or patient-reported adverse effects during the treatment period.
revue: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

titre: Gut microbiota in non-hospitalised SARS-CoV-2 infection is compositionally distinct from IBS despite comparable dysbiosis prevalence: a prospective cohort study from acute infection to six months
resume: Abstract Background Gut dysbiosis has been documented after COVID-19, but whether it occurs and persists after mild to moderate non-hospitalised infection, and how it compares with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), remains unclear. Methods We prospectively followed 31 non-hospitalised patients with mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection at acute infection, four weeks and six months using the GA-map® Dysbiosis Test, with healthy controls (n = 36) and patients with moderate-to-severe IBS (n = 58) as cross-sectional reference groups. Composition was compared by PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, individual taxa by Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and within-patient change by linear mixed-effects models. Gastrointestinal symptoms, fatigue and cognitive symptoms were related to the microbiota by Spearman correlation. Results Overall composition differed across groups (p = 0.001). SARS-CoV-2 patients differed from healthy controls (adjusted p = 0.048, 0.005 and 0.007) and from IBS (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.004 and 0.004) at all three time points, whereas composition within the SARS-CoV-2 cohort did not change over follow-up and IBS did not differ from healthy controls. Alpha diversity did not differ across groups. Five taxa were altered at every time point against both reference groups, with Eubacterium rectale , Bacteroides stercoris , Ruminococcus gnavus and Proteobacteria depleted and Shigella spp. & Escherichia spp. elevated. Actinobacteria and Bifidobacterium spp. increased within patients by four weeks (both FDR = 0.002) and exceeded IBS levels at six months (both FDR < 0.001). Dysbiosis was as prevalent as in IBS (8/28, 3/29 and 7/26 versus 15/58) and more prevalent than in healthy controls (2/36) at baseline and six months, but individual trajectories were bidirectional and no patient was dysbiotic throughout. Gastrointestinal symptoms largely resolved, whereas mental fatigue remained at the IBS level and cognitive symptoms were present in 13/26 patients at six months versus 6/35 healthy controls. Neither individual taxa nor the Dysbiosis Index was associated with symptom severity in the SARS-CoV-2 cohort. Conclusions Gut microbiota alterations after mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection persisted through six months without resembling the microbiota seen in IBS, and were not associated with persistent fatigue or cognitive symptoms. Corresponding author : birgitte.berentsen.jacobsen@helse-bergen.no

fiche.verdict: Le microbiote post-COVID non hospitalisé est distinct des contrôles sains et de l'IBS à 6 mois.
fiche.population: n = 31 patients non hospitalisés, COVID léger-modéré ; contrôles sains n = 36 ; IBS n = 58
fiche.intervention: Exposition : infection SARS-CoV-2 non hospitalisée (comparateurs : contrôles sains et IBS)
resultats_cles: Composition microbiote distincte des contrôles et de l'IBS aux 3 temps (p ajustés < 0,05)
Aucune évolution de la composition au cours du suivi chez les patients COVID
Cinq taxons altérés à chaque temps (ex. : Eubacterium rectale et Proteobacteria diminués, Shigella/Escherichia augmentés)

titre: Patient-Reported Quality of Life and Comfort Following Endoscopic Pancreatic Duct Stent Placement in Acute Pancreatitis: A Single-Center Exploratory Study
resume: Abstract Background: Although endoscopic pancreatic duct stent placement is not currently recommended as a routine treatment in clinical guidelines for acute pancreatitis (AP), our institution has accumulated extensive clinical experience with this procedure, having treated over 2,000 patients to date. While previous clinical practice and studies by our team have established the efficacy and safety of this intervention, its impact on patient-reported outcomes (PROs) remains largely uncharacterized. To further establish a comprehensive evidence chain for this practice from multidimensional perspectives, this study aimed to describe the characteristics of PROs in patients with AP receiving pancreatic duct stents during their recovery, thereby evaluating its influence on patients' subjective rehabilitation. Methods: We conducted a single-center, longitudinal observational study of 146 patients with AP who underwent endoscopic pancreatic duct stent placement between October 2025 and April 2026. The clinical decision for stenting was individualized, based on the presence of prominent abdominal pain/distension, marked peripancreatic fluid exudation on contrast-enhanced CT, and significant elevation of inflammatory markers. All procedures were performed by a single senior endoscopist. PROs were assessed using the adapted Pancreatitis Quality of Life Instrument (PANQOLI) and the General Comfort Questionnaire (GCQ) at admission, before discharge, and 2 weeks post-discharge. Results: Among the 146 patients (biliary AP: 42.5%; hypertriglyceridemic AP: 38.4%), no procedure-related adverse events (e.g., bleeding, perforation, or exacerbation of pancreatitis) were observed. Mean PANQOLI total scores increased from 19.84 ± 3.92 at admission to 68.04 ± 2.93 before discharge, and 82.23 ± 2.35 at 2 weeks post-discharge. Similarly, mean GCQ scores improved significantly from 57.82 ± 3.35 to 93.51 ± 3.31 and 103.55 ± 2.42, respectively (P<0.001 for time effects). Notably, changes in objective laboratory inflammatory markers showed weak correlations with the trajectory of these subjective PRO scores. Conclusion: In this cohort study, patients with AP who underwent pancreatic duct stent placement demonstrated significant short-term improvements in quality of life and comfort, with no procedure-related adverse events observed. The divergence between subjective improvement and objective inflammatory markers highlights the value of incorporating patient-reported outcomes (PROs) into efficacy assessment frameworks. These exploratory findings provide a supplementary dimension of evidence for this off-guideline practice; however, further confirmation through future controlled studies is warranted.

fiche.verdict: La pose de stent pancréatique en pancréatite aiguë améliore la qualité de vie et le confort à court terme sans événement indésirable.
fiche.population: n = 146 patients avec pancréatite aiguë, pose de stent endoscopique du canal pancréatique
fiche.intervention: Pose d'endoprothèse pancréatique endoscopique (pas de comparateur)
resultats_cles: PANQOLI : 19,84 → 68,04 → 82,23 (admission, sortie, 2 semaines)
Aucun événement indésirable lié à la procédure
fiche.conclusion: Les auteurs rapportent une amélioration courte durée de la qualité de vie et du confort, et préconisent des études contrôlées.

titre: Development and feasibility of a novel online individual Mindfulness-integrated Trial-Based Cognitive Therapy (M-TBCT) intervention: a phase 1 single-arm pilot and feasibility study in judiciary workers
resume: Abstract Background: Work-related mental health problems are highly prevalent, yet scalable and context-sensitive integrative interventions remain underexplored in high-demand occupational settings. Objective: To examine the feasibility and acceptability of a novel online individual mindfulness-integrated Trial-Based Cognitive Therapy (M-TBCT) intervention in a real-world occupational context, describe its development, and, as an exploratory secondary aim, examine preliminary signals of change in psychological outcomes. This study was not designed to evaluate efficacy. Methods: This Phase 1 mixed-methods pilot study was conducted with judges and court employees from a Brazilian regional labor court. Participants were screened with the Self-Report Questionnaire (SRQ-20), and 30 eligible participants were offered an eight-session weekly online intervention. The intervention integrated mindfulness and self-compassion practices derived from the Mindfulness-Based Health Promotion (MBHP) protocol with Trial-Based Cognitive Therapy (TBCT). Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, retention, and attendance; acceptability was assessed through satisfaction ratings and qualitative feedback. Pre- and post-intervention outcomes included well-being (WHO-5), depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), anxiety symptoms (GAD-7), and self-care agency (ASAS-R). Results: Recruitment reached 100.0% of the target sample, and retention was 96.7%. Acceptability was high (M = 4.71, SD = 0.45; α = .95), with qualitative reports indicating perceived gains in self-awareness, emotional balance, tranquility, and assertiveness. Among participants with complete pre–post data (n = 28), changes coinciding with the intervention period were observed in well-being (MD = 19.00, 95% CI [12.24, 25.76]; d = 1.09), self-care agency (MD = 8.57, 95% CI [4.84, 12.30]; d = 0.89), anxiety (MD = −5.60, 95% CI [−7.91, −3.29]; d = 0.94), and depressive symptoms (MD = −3.22, 95% CI [−5.72, −0.72]; d = 0.50). These changes cannot be causally attributed to the intervention in the absence of a control group. Depressive symptom changes were more modest compared to other outcomes (d = 0.50), and the proportion of participants above the PHQ-9 clinical cutoff did not change appreciably between pre- and post-intervention. This suggests that clinical improvement in depression was less consistent across participants. Conclusions: This pilot study supports the feasibility and acceptability of M-TBCT and provides preliminary signals that justify progression to a controlled trial. Rather than providing evidence of efficacy, these findings support the implementation viability and conceptual plausibility of M-TBCT, thereby justifying progression to adequately powered randomized trials.

fiche.verdict: Un programme en ligne de TCC intégrant pleine conscience et autocompassion est faisable et acceptable, avec des signaux préliminaires sur l'anxiété et le bien-être.
fiche.population: n = 30 juges et employés de tribunal (Brésil), n = 28 avec données pré-post complètes

Dépression (PHQ-9) : MD −3,22, IC 95 % [−5,72 ; −0,72], d = 0,50, seuil clinique inchangé

titre: Effectiveness of a Digital Therapeutic on Chronic Pain: A Real-World Proof-of-Concept Study
resume: Background: Chronic pain affects about 42% of French adults. Multidisciplinary care is recommended but often hard to access. QoLibri is a CE-marked digital therapeutic that combines a psychological programme (ACT, therapeutic education, mindfulness) with a physical programme (gradual return to movement).Methods: We conducted a single-arm, one-stage Fleming design on data routinely collected by the app between February and December 2025. The non-efficacy bound was 25% and the efficacy bound 50% (α = 5%, power = 90%), which required 33 patients. The primary outcome was the proportion of responders, defined as a decrease of at least 5 points in the PROMIS-29 Pain Impact Score (PIS) between Day 0 and Month 3. Secondary outcomes were exploratory: the Mental Health Score (MHS), the Physical Health Score (PHS) and the PROMIS-29 domains.Results: Thirteen of 33 patients were responders (39.4%; 95% CI 25.1–52.1%), which met the pre-specified decision threshold. Mean age was 51 years and 97% of patients were women. The PIS (d = 0.57), MHS (d = 0.54) and pain interference (SRM = 0.67) improved significantly. Smaller improvements were observed for anxiety, fatigue and pain intensity. No adverse events were reported.Conclusion: QoLibri shows a promising signal of benefit on the impact of chronic pain at 3 months. Given the absence of a control group and possible selection bias, these findings need confirmation in the ongoing cluster-randomised trial QoLiDoc.

fiche.verdict: Le numérique QoLibri (ACT, mindfulness) réduit significativement l'impact de la douleur chronique à 3 mois (39,4 % de répondeurs).
fiche.population: 33 patients avec douleur chronique (âge moyen 51 ans, 97 % femmes).
fiche.intervention: QoLibri (programme psychologique ACT, éducation, mindfulness + physique graduel) vs pas de groupe contrôle (monocentrique, vie réelle).
resultats_cles: Taux de répondeurs : 39,4 % (IC 95 % 25,1–52,1 %) sur l'impact de la douleur (PIS).
Amélioration significative de l'interférence douloureuse (SRM = 0,67) et de la santé mentale (d = 0,54).
Pas d'événements indésirables signalés.
fiche.conclusion: QoLibri présente un signal d'efficacité prometteur sur l'impact de la douleur chronique, à confirmer dans un essai randomisé contrôlé par grappe (QoLiDoc).
limites: Biais de sélection possible (vie réelle, monocentrique).
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour la douleur chronique comorbide et l'approche ACT digitale.

titre: A Whole-Blood Four-Gene Panel Distinguishes Pediatric Crohn's Disease from Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction
resume: Background and Aims: Crohn's disease and disorders of gut-brain interaction present with overlapping symptoms, and distinguishing them often requires endoscopy. We assessed whether the whole-blood transcriptome at presentation distinguishes these conditions and reflects disease activity. Methods: In a prospective two-center cohort, whole-blood RNA sequencing was performed in 425 treatment-naive participants aged 5 to 25 years (112 Crohn's disease, 313 disorders of gut-brain interaction). Differential expression was modeled for diagnosis and, within Crohn's disease, for the Pediatric Crohn's Disease Activity Index. Co-expression modules were integrated with protein-protein interaction networks, and machine learning distilled network genes into a diagnostic panel, evaluated internally and in an independent pediatric cohort. Results: Of 1,095 diagnosis-associated genes, 377 were also associated with disease activity, all with concordant direction. Five co-expression networks were perturbed, spanning neutrophil degranulation, hemostasis, interferon signaling, and T-cell and cytotoxic lymphocyte programs. A 4-gene panel (PSTPIP2, CLIC4, CACNB4, GZMK) drawn from 4 networks achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.96 in held-out samples and up to 0.93 externally, with external specificity and positive predictive value of up to 0.95 and 0.93, respectively. The panel matched or exceeded every single-network panel with fewer genes, and minimally active Crohn's disease overlapped transcriptionally with disorders of gut-brain interaction. Conclusions: At diagnosis, Crohn's disease is distinguished from disorders of gut-brain interaction by a systemic signature of neutrophil and platelet activation and lymphocyte depletion that scales with disease activity. A 4-gene whole-blood panel may help prioritize symptomatic children for endoscopy and warrants prospective validation.

fiche.verdict: Un panel de 4 gènes sanguins distingue Crohn pédiatrique des troubles gut-brain (AUC 0,96).
fiche.population: 425 participants naïfs de traitement âgés de 5 à 25 ans (112 Crohn, 313 troubles gut-brain).
fiche.intervention: Transcriptomique sanguine (RNA sequencing) et apprentissage machine pour un panel diagnostique de 4 gènes.
resultats_cles: Le panel de 4 gènes (PSTPIP2, CLIC4, CACNB4, GZMK) atteint une AUC de 0,96 en interne et 0,93 en externe.
Signature systémique d'activation des neutrophiles et plaquettes, déplétion lymphocytaire.
Spécificité externe jusqu'à 0,95, valeur prédictive positive jusqu'à 0,93.
fiche.conclusion: Ce panneau biologique pourrait prioriser les enfants symptomatiques pour une endoscopie, méritant une validation prospective.
limites: Chevauchement transcriptionnel pour les formes minimalement actives de Crohn.
Utilité clinique réelle non encore évaluée prospectivement.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Crucial pour distinguer DGBI de Crohn dans la pratique clinique.

titre: Incretin-Based Therapies and the Gut-Brain Axis in Neurodegenerative Diseases
resume: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), originally developed for metabolic disorders, remain under active investigation as potential therapeutic candidates for neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, with clinical trials to date reporting both positive and negative findings. This scoping review critically synthesizes evidence from preclinical and clinical studies (n = 99), with a focus on the molecular pharmacodynamics of semaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide, dulaglutide, and lixisenatide, together with tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (GLP-1/GIP RA) discussed separately given its distinct receptor pharmacology. In preclinical models, GLP-1 receptor activation has been associated with engagement of intracellular signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt/GSK-3β, cAMP/PKA/CREB, and AMPK/SIRT1, and several studies report reduced neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and amyloid-β or α-synuclein accumulation. These findings are not uniform: recent studies in preventive and established Alzheimer's disease mouse models found no benefit of semaglutide or tirzepatide, and the phase 3 EVOKE/EVOKE+ trials of oral semaglutide in early Alzheimer's disease did not slow clinical progression. GLP-1 RAs are also frequently associated with shifts in gut microbiota composition, including enrichment of short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, which supports a biologically plausible gut-brain axis interaction. However, microbiota responses are heterogeneous and context-dependent, and no included study used causal designs such as germ-free models or fecal microbiota transplantation. Whether neuroprotective effects arise from direct central receptor engagement, from peripheral metabolic effects, or from microbiota remodeling therefore remains unresolved, and microbiota changes may be a secondary consequence of metabolic improvement rather than a mediator of therapeutic effect.

fiche.verdict: Les agonistes GLP-1 (semaglutide) présentent un intérêt neuroprotecteur incertain, freiné par les échecs cliniques dans l'Alzheimer.
fiche.population: Études précliniques et cliniques (n=99) sur l'Alzheimer et la maladie de Parkinson.
fiche.intervention: Agonistes GLP-1 (semaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide, dulaglutide, lixisenatide, tirzepatide).
resultats_cles: Réduction préclinique du neuro-inflammation et de l'amyloid-β, mais pas de bénéfice clinique pour semaglutide dans l'Alzheimer précoce (EVOKE/EVOKE+).
Modulation hétérogène du microbiota intestinal (augmentation des acides gras à chaîne courte).
Aucune étude n'a utilisé de designs causaux pour le microbiota.
fiche.conclusion: L'effet neuroprotecteur des GLP-1 RAs reste résolu, pouvant dépendre des effets métaboliques périphériques plutôt que de l'axe gut-brain.
limites: Résultats cliniques hétérogènes et négatifs dans les essais de phase 3.
Pas de conception causale pour le microbiota.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Théoriquement passionnant pour l'axe gut-brain, mais cliniquement lointain.

titre: Recuperación del deterioro neuromotor y gastrointestinal posterior al manejo erradicador del Helicobacter Pylori con medicina integrativa. Reporte de caso clinico
resume: Introducción: La terapia de erradicación para Helicobacter Pylori es altamente efectiva, pero puede inducir disbiosis gastrointestinal severa ya que modifica la microbiota intestinal por reducción de LACTOBACILLUS, disminución de BIFIDOBACTERIUM, aumento de enterobacterias y disminución de la diversidad bacteriana, lo que puede favorecer la inflamación de bajo grado, alteración de la permeabilidad intestinal, fatiga y síntomas neuropsiquiátricos y síndrome de astenia crónica debido a la disfunción mitocondrial y al estrés metabólico secundario.Presentación del caso: Se presenta el caso de una paciente femenina de 75 años, con antecedentes de diabetes mellitus tipo 2, hipotiroidismo, diverticulosis y síndrome de intestino irritable con estreñimiento, quien consultó por episodios recurrentes de dolor abdominal intenso, distensión, vómitos ocasionales y estreñimiento. Los estudios complementarios evidenciaron gastritis crónica activa asociada a Helicobacter Pylori, duodenitis erosiva y enfermedad diverticular del colon. Tras recibir una triple terapia antimicrobiana de 14 días para gastritis por H. Pylori, desarrolló un deterioro clínico agudo caracterizado por fatiga severa, postración por pérdida de fuerza muscular periférica, síntomas depresivos, dependencia funcional grave y exacerbación del dolor abdominal. Debido a dichos síntomas se instauró un protocolo Medicina Integrativa de Sistemas con Traumeel, Ubichinon Compositum, Coenzyme Compositum, Cerebrum Compositum y Nuxeel Homaccord, orientada a la optimización mitocondrial, detoxificación gastrointestinal y modulación del sistema nervioso, administrados por vía endovenosa durante cinco semanas. Se complementó el tratamiento con un simbiótico intestinal Lactobacillus Rhamnosus GG y Zinc durante 30 días y posteriormente con terapia de mantenimiento mediante Centreel.Resultados: Se observó mejoría clínica progresiva desde el tercer ciclo de tratamiento, con recuperación funcional completa al finalizar la intervención. La escala de fatiga FSS disminuyó de 58 a 9 puntos; la escala IBS-SSS pasó de 380 a 0 puntos; el índice de Barthel aumentó de 55 a 100 puntos y la escala de depresión geriátrica GDS-15 disminuyó de 11 a 1 punto. Adicionalmente, la prueba de aliento para H. pylori fue negativa.Conclusión: Este caso documenta una evolución clínica favorable posterior a un abordaje integral que incluyó tratamiento convencional para H. Pylori y Medicina Integrativa. La intervención sistémica permitió la restauración completa de la fuerza muscular, la resolución de los síntomas neuropsiquiátricos y gastrointestinales, y la erradicación exitosa de la bacteria. La medicina integrativa representa una alternativa coadyuvante viable en el agotamiento post-antibiótico. Por tratarse de un reporte de caso, no es posible establecer una relación causal entre la intervención biorreguladora y los resultados observados.

fiche.verdict: La médecine integrative (probiotique, mitochondriale) permet la récupération complète après dégradation gut-brain post-antibiotique.
fiche.population: Une patiente de 75 ans avec diabète, hypothyroïdie, SII-C et H. pylori.
fiche.intervention: Protocole de médecine intégrative de systèmes (Traumeel, Ubichinon, Coenzyme, Cerebrum, Nuxeel) + symbiotique (Lactobacillus GG + Zinc) après erradication de H. pylori.
resultats_cles: Récupération fonctionnelle complète (Barthel de 55 à 100).
Disparition des symptômes SII (IBS-SSS de 380 à 0) et de la fatigue (FSS de 58 à 9).
Régression de la dépression (GDS-15 de 11 à 1) et erradication de H. pylori.
fiche.conclusion: La médecine intégrative apparaît une alternative co-adjuvante viable pour le syndrome de fatigue post-antibiotique, sans pouvoir établir de causalité.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Cas clinique très illustratif de dégradation gut-brain post-antibiotique.

titre: Enzymatic and Microbial Modification of Carbohydrates for Improved Bread Quality and Nutritional Functionality
resume: Bread production is increasingly based on clean-label strategies that reduce ingredients and additives while maintaining quality, convenience and affordability. Sourdough fermentation and enzymes are promising clean-label approaches to modifying carbohydrates. The research presented in this thesis aimed to investigate microbial and enzymatic strategies for modifying wheat carbohydrates and to determine how these modifications influence bread quality and nutritional functionality. The comparison of the ingredient lists of commercial wheat breads in different countries demonstrated substantial differences in additive use and suggested a link between the use of sourdough and shorter ingredient lists. Sourdough contributes to several technological and nutritional functions through either general microbial metabolism or strain-specific activities. However, current evidence indicates that sourdough alone cannot yet replace all additives. It nevertheless provides a strong basis for translating sourdough fermentation into reliable clean-label applications in industrial bread production. The reduction of FODMAPs in grain-based food products is of interest for alleviating IBS symptoms. The contribution of sourdough fermentation and baker’s yeast to FODMAP degradation was explored in bread and pasta. The results indicated that yeast invertase together with a long proofing time suffices to reduce FODMAP levels in bread. Starch-modifying enzymes can improve bread quality by modifying starch functionality that can act as hydrocolloids. Biochemical characterisation of the glucan-branching enzyme GlgB from intestinal bacteria showed a higher preference on amylose while current commercial branching enzymes are preferentially active on amylopectin. A reduced in vitro starch digestibility was observed after enzyme reaction, suggesting the potential of GlgB to modify starch in bread applications. The translation of starch modification into bread functionality was further assessed. The effects of the 4,6-α-glucanotransferase GtfB, the reuteransucrase GtfA, and two glucan-branching enzymes, GlgB and Branchzyme, on bread quality were investigated individually and in combination. Bread quality showed a non-linear response to enzyme activity, with an optimum dosage required for each enzyme. GtfB and Branchzyme also reduced crumb hardness and in vitro starch digestibility, whereas GlgB showed the opposite effect. GtfA and GtfB acted synergistically. Although increased donor substrate availability enhanced GtfB activity in a simplified bread model, it did not further improve bread quality. Optimised bread quality thus requires a balance among enzyme dosage, substrate availability, and the extent of starch modification in the dough. Taken together, the successful application of sourdough fermentation and carbohydrate-active enzymes requires strain selection and process optimisation within the intended food matrix rather than maximisation of microbial or enzymatic activity alone. These findings contribute to the development of function-driven and industrially relevant clean-label strategies for improving bread quality and nutritional functionality.
revue: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)

fiche.verdict: La fermentation sanitaire et les enzymes réduisent les FODMAPs et la digestibilité de l'amidon dans le pain.
fiche.population: null

titre: Sleep-related threat processing in chronic insomnia: A psychosomatic framework for hyperarousal, learning, and treatment
resume: Chronic insomnia is maintained by interacting cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and physiological processes that may persist after precipitating factors resolve. Hyperarousal models emphasize persistent activation, whereas cognitive and behavioral models identify worry, selective attention, monitoring, conditioned arousal, sleep effort, dysfunctional beliefs, and safety behaviors as maintaining processes. This review examines whether sleep-related threat processing may provide an integrative psychosomatic framework connecting these mechanisms. For this review, sleep-related threat processing is conceptualized as the appraisal of sleep-related states, cues, uncertainty, or anticipated consequences as potentially harmful or requiring a defensive response, together with the attentional, cognitive, behavioral, emotional, and physiological processes recruited by that appraisal. The framework is not proposed as a replacement for Harvey’s cognitive model or other established theories. Its proposed contribution is to organize conditioned learning, interoceptive interpretation, multidimensional hyperarousal, sleep effort, safety behavior, and cognitive processes within an explicitly reciprocal and testable system. Conditioning and predictive processing may contribute to persistence, while inhibitory learning provides a framework for understanding corrective experiences during cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia. Trauma-related insomnia provides a particularly salient example because sleep itself may become associated with vulnerability and reduced vigilance. The model generates testable predictions concerning temporal ordering, threat content, physiological coupling, treatment mediation, and incremental validity beyond established insomnia and anxiety constructs. Sleep-related threat is not proposed as a universal cause of insomnia, an established etiological mechanism, or a validated treatment-matching system. Rather, it is presented as a hypothesis-generating psychosomatic framework whose value depends on prospective, experimental, and treatment-mechanism testing.
revue: Journal of Clinical and Basic Psychosomatics

fiche.verdict: Cadre conceptuel sur le traitement de la menace liée au sommeil, sans données empiriques.
resultats_cles: Aucun résultat empirique rapporté.
Cadre hypothèse-génératrice intégrant conditionnement et interoception.
Prédictions testables pour la TCC-I et les mécanismes de traitement.
fiche.conclusion: Le traitement de la menace liée au sommeil est un cadre à tester, non un mécanisme étiologique établi.

titre: Endogenous Satisficing: A Distributed Theory of Viability Regulation for Autonomous Survival Agents
resume: Abstract An agent that maximizes a specified reward can exhibit sophisticated adaptation while remaining dependent on an externally defined criterion of success. Living systems present a different organizational problem: action must continually regulate the changing conditions of the acting system’s own persistence. We develop endogenous satisficing as a computational framework for this problem. The framework brings together three ingredients: viability-constrained bodily dynamics, aspiration conditions generated from interoceptive state and individually acquired evidence, and distributed competition among partially autonomous behavioral processes. Satisficing is defined operationally as the selection of an action meeting a context-dependent set of locally generated acceptance conditions within bounded sensing and computation, rather than as the global maximizer of a permanently fixed external score. We specify an executable transition system, bodily need variables, local aspiration and risk conditions, a recurrent motor-competition field, event-grounded memory with delayed credit assignment, and a minimal causal self-model criterion based on prediction intervention. Four theoretical consequences follow: internally conditioned action preferences, a distinction between resource transfer and acquisition, the causal importance of model readout, and the risk of changing a previously accurate belief under noisy evidence. Existing SISE-N artificial-survival experiments provide initial mechanistic evidence. In a common-frozen-policy, four-controller comparison over 12 paired maps, distributed controllers achieved longer observed survival than their central-acceptance counterparts, while the additional dynamic-threshold effect within the distributed architecture was small. Subsequent interventions showed that individually learned bodily-outcome predictions altered action selection, whereas injury-probability calibration and survival improvement remained separate empirical questions. The resulting theory provides an experimentally decidable account of functional autonomy grounded in an agent’s own conditions of persistence, without equating distributed control with consciousness or digital simulation with biological life. Keywords: artificial life; endogenous satisficing; viability; distributed control; homeostasis; causal self-model
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

fiche.verdict: Théorie computationnelle de l'autonomie pour agents artificiels, sans application clinique.
resultats_cles: Modèle de régulation de la viabilité par satisfaction endogène.

titre: Recreating the situated action cycle: a conceptual framework for how culturally fit, hands-on engagement may support meaning-making in Alzheimer’s disease through a reverse sensory-motor pathway
resume: Most dementia care asks people to remember through words. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), this generative, executively mediated retrieval of one’s life story fails earlier than the perceptual and motor knowledge on which direct, cue-driven retrieval draws. This paper proposes a conceptual framework, the reverse sensory-motor pathway, to explain how culturally fit, hands-on engagement may still give access to that knowledge. “Sensory” refers to recreating the visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory, and interoceptive-spatial inputs of the situations in which the knowledge was formed. “Motor” refers to the act of making, which draws on body memory and procedural skill. “Reverse” refers to the direction of access: the recreated situation reaches stored knowledge from the bottom up, rather than through top-down verbal search. Drawing on Barsalou’s perceptual symbol systems and situated action cycle, Conway’s self-memory system, cultural psychology, neuroaesthetics, and Default Mode Network (DMN) research, the framework proposes that such cues reinstate perceptual and motor simulators, whose content may engage residual capacity in the posterior DMN, a network implicated in self-referential processing. The pathway incorporates factors identified in earlier work—familiarity, reminiscence, social contact, procedural memory, and the persistence of affect—most of which were studied in receptive modes such as listening or viewing. What it adds is making: the motor act sustains engagement and regenerates the cues, so that spontaneous narrative, positive affect, and agency can emerge. The pathway is graded by cultural fit, which, following Baltes’s life-span account, has three components: lived-experience, shared-experience, and dispositional fit. A second contribution distinguishes narrative-enticing environments, which invite a person to share a story through making, from narrative-demanding ones, which test for the capacity the disease impairs. The framework yields predictions that separate the contribution of making from familiarity, arousal, and procedural memory considered alone, and it aims to provide a mechanistic foundation for culturally fit, hands-on, non-pharmacological interventions in dementia care.

titre: Editorial: Human behavior in extreme conditions: novel approaches and technologies
resume: Lu et al. (2025) used virtual simulation to investigate indoor earthquake early-warning information, finding that protective guidance improved the accuracy and speed of participants' selection of appropriate avoidance areas. Faiz et al. (2025) compared contextual virtual reality (VR) fire-safety simulations with noncontextual VR materials. Realistic home and apartment scenarios produced greater improvements in fire-hazard identification, alongside higher engagement and perceived usefulness. Mehta et al. (2025) examined firefighter training under simulated stress. Participants trained under stress demonstrated poorer learning performance and longer operation times than controls, although subsequent retrieval was similar. Gaze and pupillary responses also differed, illustrating VR's potential for investigating performance under pressure. Together, these studies demonstrate how immersive simulations can investigate hazard recognition, learning, and performance under controlled conditions. Whether these results transfer to real-world emergencies, persist over time, and improve safety remains to be established. McKeever et al. (2024) found increased nature-relatedness following a VR simulation of the Overview Effect, but not in the control condition. These preliminary findings suggest that immersive experiences may influence perceptions of our relationship with nature, although the durability and practical significance of such changes require further investigation. Bodner et al. (2026) report a formative evaluation of VR tools for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) treatment and place-attachment-based therapy following the October 7 attacks in Israel, emphasizing cultural, geographical, and operational adaptations. Shalaby et al. (2026) present the conceptual foundation of The Canaries' Experience, integrating VR, avatars, immersive storytelling, and AI for suicide prevention and early intervention. These contributions illustrate potential technological approaches to psychological support in highrisk settings, but their effectiveness, safety, and acceptability require further evaluation.Richard (2026) examines ecological momentary assessment in ICE environments, including its integration with wearable sensors and digital biomarkers. Farsadaki and Griffy-Brown (2026) consider AI-based affective computing for behavioral health, addressing validity, privacy, ethics, and human-centered design. Both contributions highlight opportunities for continuous, context-sensitive monitoring while underscoring the need to validate digital indicators across populations and operational settings. Osei et al. ( 2026) examine psychological, ethical, and design dimensions of human-AI interaction in ICE environments, including trust, autonomy, transparency, and reliance on AI. Complementing this focus on human-technology interaction, Osei and Carie (2026) explore Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for investigating relationships among psychological, experiential, and technological factors. Using secondary mobile-health data as an illustrative analogue, they demonstrate the method's potential while emphasizing the need for validation in operational ICE settings. Together, these papers suggest that technological outcomes depend not only on technical performance but also on how people understand, trust, and use systems under pressure. How these relationships evolve during prolonged operations, and how technology can support human judgment without undermining autonomy, remain important research questions.Nezami (2025) examines how stress, altered perceptual experiences, arousal regulation, and interoception may shape astronaut adaptation and inform countermeasures. The paper adopts a multilevel perspective connecting psychological, physiological, sensory, and environmental processes. Thomas (2023) reviews the potential of VR for behavioral health assessment, monitoring, and countermeasures during long-duration space exploration. These contributions suggest opportunities for integrating psychological science and immersive technologies into astronaut support systems, while underscoring the importance of evaluating their operational effectiveness under spaceflight conditions. Nezami et al. ( 2026) extend the discussion to the systemic challenges of sustained human expansion beyond Earth. Their exploratory system-dynamics architecture integrates infrastructure, governance, and psychological and social processes within a framework for examining sustainability and resilience across coupled Earth-space systems. The infrastructure layer provides an initial prototype, while the remaining layers are conceptual extensions. The framework offers a basis for further development, but its predictive value requires empirical testing. Nielsen ( 2025) introduces an epistemological perspective by examining what may be lost when technology substitutes for direct human presence in extreme environments. The paper argues that technological mediation may not fully capture the embodied and experiential dimensions of direct observation. This perspective challenges the assumption that greater technological capability necessarily produces equivalent scientific understanding and highlights the complementary roles of direct experience and remote or simulated observation.In a study of personnel during a Latin American Antarctic expedition, Melo Vargas and Barriga Medina (2025) identify habitability, preparation, leadership, interpersonal relationships, workload, role clarity, institutional support, and conflict management as factors relevant to well-being and performance. Thompson (2025), uses interpretative phenomenological analysis with seven NASA leaders to identify connections between awe narratives and resilience practices, including cognitive reappraisal, meaning, gratitude, hope, and social connectedness. These studies suggest that adaptation depends not only on individual capacities but also on social relationships and organizational conditions. Their context-specific findings, however, do not establish universal determinants of resilience. Further research should examine how these factors interact across different populations and environments and how they can inform effective organizational practices.Across the collection, three conclusions emerge. First, immersive simulations and emerging monitoring technologies offer valuable methods for investigating human functioning and developing potential interventions. Second, adaptation is shaped by interactions among individuals, environments, social relationships, and technological systems. Third, technological innovation introduces new questions concerning validity, trust, privacy, autonomy, and the preservation of human judgment. These conclusions must be interpreted in light of the diverse evidence represented. Experimental studies demonstrate specific effects under particular conditions; preliminary evaluations suggest potential applications; and conceptual frameworks identify relationships and mechanisms for future investigation. Together, these contributions advance our understanding of human functioning in extreme conditions while identifying important questions about real-world effectiveness, durability, and generalisability. Future research should prioritize real-world validation, longitudinal evaluation, and the transfer of learning from simulations to operational settings. Digital biomarkers and AI-based assessments require validation across contexts, while technology-assisted interventions need evidence of sustained effectiveness and safety. Human-AI relationships warrant investigation under prolonged stress, and systems-level models require further development and empirical testing. Integrating experimental, qualitative, longitudinal, and computational approaches may help establish not only whether an intervention works, but for whom, under what conditions, and with what consequences.

titre: Adding self-administered music listening to sleep hygiene education for insomnia in young men during subacute high-altitude acclimatization (4100 m): a preliminary comparative study with retrospective data
resume: Insomnia is highly prevalent at high altitude, primarily driven by hypoxia-induced psychophysiological hyperarousal. Although cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the first-line treatment, its implementation is often restricted in resource-limited high-altitude settings. Music listening has shown promise for sleep improvement in lowland populations, but its additive value in mitigating hypoxia-related sleep disturbances remains unexplored. To evaluate the feasibility and preliminary associations of adding self-administered music listening intervention (SMLI)—a scalable intervention requiring only a personal audio device and headphones, no specialist supervision—to sleep hygiene education (SHE) compared with SHE alone for insomnia and co-occurring anxiety in young men residing at 4100 m, using robust statistical adjustments for non-randomized data. This retrospective comparative study analyzed de-identified data from 35 males (aged 20–45 years) diagnosed with insomnia disorder. The sample size was determined by the availability of eligible participants from the original wellness program, consistent with the hypothesis-generating objective of this exploratory study to generate effect size estimates for future randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Key inclusion criteria included high-altitude residence duration of 1–3 months and no use of hypnotic medications. Participants were categorized into SMLI + SHE ( n = 18) or SHE-only ( n = 17) groups based on actual program participation. The intervention consisted of daily SMLI sessions lasting 30 min over 4 weeks (requiring only a personal audio device and headphones, with no specialist guidance). Adherence was monitored, with ≥ 80% compliance considered adequate; a per-protocol (PP) analysis was conducted, including only participants who met this adherence threshold. To mitigate selection bias and baseline imbalances, the primary analysis employed analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) adjusted for baseline scores, supplemented by sensitivity analyses. Given the exploratory nature and small sample size, we prioritized effect sizes (Cohen’s d, ηp 2 ) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) alongside p -values. Primary outcomes were changes in the modified Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI, excluding the medication component, maximum score = 18) and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI); the secondary outcome was the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS). Of 87 screened individuals, 35 males met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Baseline demographic characteristics (age, BMI, and education level) were comparable between groups (all p > 0.05); however, the SHE-only group had slightly higher baseline PSQI scores (mean ± SD: SMLI + SHE 10.33 ± 1.98 vs. SHE-only 11.24 ± 2.15; SMD = 0.44). ANCOVA revealed that the SMLI + SHE group was associated with significantly better post-intervention sleep quality than the SHE group (adjusted mean modified PSQI: 5.91 [95% CI: 5.32–6.50] vs. 6.98 [95% CI: 6.37–7.59]; F (1, 32) = 6.84, p = 0.013; Cohen’s d = 0.82 [95% CI: 0.27–1.35]; ηp 2 = 0.176). Similarly, insomnia severity (ISI) was associated with greater reduction in the SMLI + SHE group (adjusted mean: 4.85 [95% CI: 3.98–5.72] vs. 7.04 [95% CI: 6.15–7.93]; F (1, 32) = 5.38, p = 0.027; Cohen’s d = 0.76 [95% CI: 0.21–1.29]; ηp 2 = 0.144). For anxiety, the reduction in SAS scores did not differ significantly between groups (SMLI + SHE: from 53.28 to 47.39, mean reduction = 5.89; SHE-only: from 52.76 to 48.06, mean reduction = 4.70; adjusted between-group difference: p = 0.186). The SMLI + SHE group showed a moderate effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.45 [95% CI: -0.09 to 0.98]). All 18 participants in the SMLI + SHE group met the ≥ 80% adherence threshold (mean adherence rate: 94.2% ± 4.1%), suggesting the feasibility of the self-administered protocol in this resource-limited setting; however, this high adherence may reflect selection bias, as participants who opted for SMLI may have been more motivated. No adverse events (e.g., auditory discomfort or exacerbated anxiety) were reported throughout the 4-week intervention period. In this resource-limited, high-altitude setting, adjunctive SMLI combined with SHE was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in sleep quality and insomnia severity compared with SHE alone. No statistically significant benefit was observed for anxiety symptoms in this preliminary sample. Given the retrospective non-randomized design, small sample size, reliance on subjective outcomes, and absence of objective sleep measures—particularly polysomnography to distinguish subjective sleep perception from underlying high-altitude periodic breathing and nocturnal hypoxemia—these findings are hypothesis-generating and associative, precluding definitive causal inference. However, the favorable safety profile, promising feasibility, and moderate-to-large effect sizes (Cohen’s d = 0.76–0.82) provide foundational data to inform the design of future adequately powered RCTs specifically targeting SMLI in this high-altitude population.

titre: Analysis code for "Local and circulating cytotoxic CD4 T cells are early markers of disease activity in pediatric Crohn's disease"
resume: This repository contains the analysis scripts, computational notebooks, and supporting data files associated with the study "Local and circulating cytotoxic CD4 T cells are early markers of disease activity in pediatric Crohn’s disease." The study investigates cytotoxic CD4 T cells (CD4 CTLs) in intestinal tissues and peripheral blood from pediatric patients with Crohn’s disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), and disorders of gut–brain interaction (DGBI), as well as healthy donors. The analyses focus on the identification and characterization of CD4 CTLs, their association with disease activity and response to anti-TNF treatment, and potential mechanisms regulating their differentiation. Contents of the archive The ZIP archive contains R scripts, Python scripts, Jupyter notebooks, R Markdown files, and supporting analysis files organized into the following directories: 01_Cohort_characteristics: Clinical cohort characteristics, disease distribution, and laboratory parameters. 02_Gut_all_cells: Processing, annotation, and differential gene expression analyses of intestinal single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets. 03_Gut_CD4: Characterization of intestinal CD4 T-cell populations, including CD4 CTL frequencies, compositional analysis, trajectory analysis, transcription factor analysis, and T-cell receptor (TCR) analyses. 04_Other_datasets: Analysis of independent published datasets for external validation and comparison. 05_Integrated_ILE_LP_atlas: Integration and annotation of ileal lamina propria single-cell datasets, analysis of cellular associations, and inference of ligand–receptor interactions using NicheNet. 06_Bulk_deconvolution_RISK: Deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq data from the RISK cohort using single-cell reference profiles and BayesPrism. 07_Blood_all_cells: Analysis of peripheral blood scRNA-seq datasets, blood–gut CD4 T-cell integration, and TCR comparisons. 08_Sorted_CD4_CTL: Analysis of sorted CD4 CTL populations. 09_Flow_cytometry_data: Analysis of flow cytometry experiments. The Files directory contains supporting data tables, including differential gene expression results, cell population frequencies, clinical laboratory measurements, TCR analysis outputs, flow cytometry results, and sample metadata. The archive preserves the relative directory structure used in the analysis workflows. GitHub repository The analysis code is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/vercanie/predict_cd4_ctl/ The Zenodo archive provides a fixed, citable snapshot of the analysis code associated with the publication, whereas the GitHub repository is maintained and may contain more recent updates or corrections. Users are encouraged to consult the GitHub repository for the most up-to-date version of the code. Single-cell data availability The scRNA-seq data generated in this study have been deposited in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GSE352630: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE352630 The processed datasets can also be explored interactively through the Broad Institute Single Cell Portal (SCP): SCP3737 – Peripheral blood: https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP3737 SCP3739 – Total CD3 and NK cells from gut: https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP3739 SCP3741 – CD4 T cells from gut: https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP3741 SCP3898 – Integrated atlas of all cell types from ileal lamina propria: https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP3898/local-and-circulating-cytotoxic-cd4-t-cells-are-early-markers-of-disease-activity-in-pediatric-crohns-disease-all-cells These resources provide access to the single-cell transcriptomic datasets associated with the study and facilitate independent exploration and reanalysis of the results. Reproducibility The scripts and notebooks document the computational analyses underlying the manuscript. The associated GitHub repository specifies R version 4.2.1 or higher and provides package version information in the notebooks. Some analyses require additional software dependencies and publicly available external datasets. The code and supporting files are provided to facilitate transparency, reproducibility, and reuse of the analytical workflows described in the manuscript.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: STARLI · MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE FAMILY 01 | CHINESE QIGONG AND MIND–BODY REGULATION Research Working Edition v1.1 · Scientific & Technical Notebook · 16 November 2026 Five formal flagship titles and Zenodo-ready scientific introductions F001 | Respiratory Rhythms and Autonomic Regulation in Chinese Qigong at the Limit A breathing rhythm can feel as intimate as a whispered question; the scientific test starts where the poetry leaves off. F001 follows respiratory phase and cardiac interbeat intervals as two clocks that must be independently calibrated. The primary prospective endpoint is respiratory–RMSSD phase coupling (0–1), witnessed by synchronous belt and raw ECG signals. Plain paced breathing with matched posture, attention and duration is permitted to explain the same result. CO2 context, effort and drift remain live rival explanations. This is a nonclinical measurement program, not a claim about a hidden energy source or direct vagal-tone activation. F002 | Postural Stability and Control During Qigong Standing Practice at the Limit In quiet standing, the body draws a small map under the feet. F002 studies that map through center-of-pressure path speed (mm/s), not through an assumed spiritual or clinical outcome. Foot placement, visual reliability, surface compliance and fatigue may all bend the trace. A calibrated force plate, motion timing and a matched ordinary standing comparison keep the inference grounded. A calmer-looking sway is not automatically greater balance reserve, and an unfamiliar task must be studied separately before any transfer is suggested. F003 | Neural–Motor Coordination Across Dynamic and Static Qigong at the Limit The brief border between motion and stillness offers both artistic grace and a difficult timing problem. F003 examines transition smoothness (0–1) alongside EMG-to-kinematics lag (ms), preserving raw inertial data and synchronized muscle onset rather than trusting beautified trajectories. A matched slow-movement sequence can reveal whether familiarity, cue timing or filtering accounts for the difference. We invite an independent analyst to challenge the proposed neuromotor account; no single fluid gesture establishes neural plasticity. F004 | Attention Regulation and Interoceptive Precision in Qigong at the Limit F004 begins with a respectful paradox: a sensation may be vivid even when an objective discrimination task remains uncertain. Attention regulation and interoceptive precision must therefore be separated into narrative report, task accuracy, response bias and confidence calibration. Blinded heartbeat or respiratory tasks, concealed cue validity and an attention-matched external discrimination baseline provide the witnesses. Language and expectation may explain part of the apparent effect. This program honors reported qi sensations without treating their vividness as proof of a newly isolated physical field. F005 | Longitudinal Mind–Body Adaptation Dynamics in Qigong at the Limit F005 looks beyond the lesson, toward what remains when a practiced sequence, familiar instructor and research room are gone. Prospective untrained-task retention (%) is assessed against time-stamped adherence, delayed follow-up, washout and an active control matched for attention and teaching contact. Learning on the trained task cannot substitute for durable transfer; missingness, selection, seasonal routines and withdrawal must be visible in the analysis. The long view makes room for human growth while remaining ready to report a null or reversed result. Editorial note: these five topics retain the exact bilingual flagship titles and scientific boundaries inherited from the user-provided 40-family Eastern-culture master outline. The manuscript offers prospective methods, not clinical findings or evidence of exotic physical mechanisms. A physical sensor with quantum components may assist measurement, but the word quantum does not establish nonlocal intention or a new field. titre: Robotic Embodiment in Contemplative Practice: Individual Differences and Design Implications for Somatic AI
resume: In the era of AI, technology is increasingly used to facilitate contemplative practices like mindfulness. While traditional digital interventions primarily rely on disembodied audio guides, the physical presence of a robotic agent may offer unique benefits for somatic learning. This paper presents a qualitative investigation of how practitioners experience a robotic agent during contemplative practice, compared to a conventional human-recorded audio guide. We conducted a within-subjects study with 15 participants; data from surveys and semi-structured interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis. Quantitative analyses revealed no significant difference in Toronto Mindfulness Scale (TMS) scores between the robot and audio conditions, though scores were numerically higher in the robot condition. Notably, state anxiety was negatively correlated with mindfulness outcomes in both conditions, and male participants rated the robot significantly higher in anthropomorphism and animacy than female participants. Qualitative findings revealed substantial variation in how the robot’s embodiment was experienced. While many participants perceived the robot as a non-judgmental co-practitioner that reduced social evaluation anxiety, others found its physical presence distracting, with motor sounds and movement drawing attention outward and disrupting interoceptive focus. These findings highlight the ambivalent nature of robotic embodiment in contemplative settings and provide deployment-oriented design implications, including dynamic bio-synchronization, adaptive social presence calibration, and state-responsive engagement.

titre: Association of mindfulness-based stress reduction added to dexmedetomidine with patient-reported outcomes in permanent enterostomy: A retrospective cohort study
resume: BACKGROUND Permanent enterostomy, including colostomy and ileostomy, is common in colorectal cancer and causes body image changes, abnormal defecation, and stigma.Patients often develop clinically significant anxiety and/or depressive symptoms.Dexmedetomidine provides short-term relief but does not address long-term psychosocial adaptation.Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) may complement dexmedetomidine, but evidence in this population is limited.AIM To investigate the association between MBSR added to dexmedetomidine and outcomes in permanent enterostomy with anxiety and/or depressive symptoms.METHODS This single-center, nonrandomized, retrospective comparative cohort study included 120 patients with permanent enterostomy (including colostomy and ileostomy) and clinically significant anxiety and/or depressive symptoms [Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)-A ≥ 8 and/or HADS-D ≥ 8] from January 2016 to December 2025.Patients selfselected MBSR: Observation group (n = 63) received dexmedetomidine plus MBSR; control group (n = 57) received dexmedetomidine plus routine care.Outcomes were assessed using the HADS, Stoma Quality of Life Scale, General Self-Efficacy Scale, and Ostomy Adjustment Inventory-20. RESULTSRepeated-measures showed significant group main effect and time × group interaction for HADS (both P < 0.05).At discharge and post-treatment, HADS-A and HADS-D scores were lower in the observation group than in the control group (both P < 0.01).Post-4 / 37 treatment Stoma Quality of Life Scale total score was higher in the observation group (62.63 ± 5.60 vs 54.30 ± 6.78, P < 0.001).General Self-Efficacy Scale score was higher in the observation group (29.14 ± 4.65 vs 26.68 ± 4.64, P = 0.005).Ostomy Adaptation Scale score was higher in the observation group (69.16 ± 7.65 vs 63.42 ± 7.85, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONAdding MBSR to dexmedetomidine was positively associated with improved anxiety, depression, quality of life, self-efficacy, and psychosocial adaptation in permanent enterostomy patients.These exploratory findings require randomized confirmation.

titre: Feasibility and preliminary outcomes of a brief prison-based mindfulness intervention: a mixed-methods study in a central prison in India
resume: Purpose Although mindfulness programmers have shown potential in correctional settings, controlled evidence from Indian prisons remains limited. This study aims to examine the preliminary effects of an eight-week group-based mindfulness programme on perceived stress, anxiety, anger, self-control and exploratory psychopathy-related outcomes among incarcerated men in an Indian central prison. Design/methodology/approach This study involved 40 incarcerated men in an Indian central prison who were randomly allocated to a mindfulness programme or routine prison activities (control) condition; 37 completed the post-intervention assessment. A pilot randomized controlled trial with a convergent mixed-methods design was used. Quantitative outcomes were analysed using analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline scores, while written accounts from mindfulness participants were thematically analysed and integrated with quantitative findings. Findings The mindfulness group reported lower perceived stress and significantly higher self-control than the control group. Qualitative findings indicated greater calm, earlier recognition of emotional escalation and more deliberate responses during interpersonal tension. Participants identified noise, limited privacy, institutional routines and concerns about appearing vulnerable as barriers to independent practice. Research limitations/implications As a small pilot study conducted in a single prison, the findings of this study are preliminary and may have limited generalisability. Larger, adequately powered trials with longer follow-up are needed to examine the durability and broader effects of mindfulness in correctional settings. Practical implications Mindfulness may be incorporated as an adjunct to existing correctional rehabilitation, with protected opportunities for regular practice integrated into prison routines. Social implications Accessible mindfulness programmes may support psychological well-being and self-regulation among incarcerated people, particularly within restrictive custodial environments. Originality/value This study extends limited controlled research on mindfulness in Indian prisons by integrating trial outcomes with participants’ accounts of how custodial conditions shape programme use. The findings indicate that a brief prison-based mindfulness programme requires protected opportunities for safe, routine practice beyond facilitated sessions.

titre: Indigenous Pedagogies for Burned-Out Students on a Burned-Out Planet
resume: Abstract Students in the author’s environmental philosophy courses are committed to pursuing ecological revitalization and climate justice. They see these pursuits as their generation’s greatest responsibility, if in an attenuated sense circumscribed by the demand to assume their prescribed place in a racial capitalist socioeconomic order. Given their subjection to structural deformities associated with kinlessness, they’re acculturated to shoulder undue blame both for ongoing ecological/climatological degradation and for the debilitating conditions—including generalized anxiety, clinical depression, ADHD, and OCD—from which they nearly all suffer partially as a result. This dynamic is self-reinforcing. Challenging it, if modestly, requires an overtly anticolonial pedagogical stance. Thanks to guidance from Indigenous scholars who generously share their experiences with pedagogies aimed at sustaining their communities within a settler state bent on their destruction, this chapter explores how to help counteract the worst of students’ suffering. Unsurprisingly, this requires taking steps to subvert kinlessness.

titre: Methodological Framework and Reproducible R Code for the Five-Layer Comorbidity-Aware Endometriosis AI Pipeline
resume: This repository contains the detailed Supplementary Methods (Methodological Framework and Simulation Architecture for the Comorbidity-Aware Endometriosis AI Pipeline) and the fully annotated, reproducible R script accompanying the manuscript: "Epidemiological spectrum bias in endometriosis AI: a simulation-based perspective and a comorbidity-aware validation framework". Methodological Summary: To address epidemiological spectrum bias and phenotypic overlap between endometriosis (ENDO), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we provide a five-layer, regulatory-aligned (FDA SaMD & TRIPOD+AI) validation framework: Layer 1 (Generative):Conditional Gaussian copula simulation calibrated to literature-derived age and ethnicity marginals (Bougie et al., BJOG 2019) and multi-organ biomarker profiles (pelvic pain, GI dysfunction, hs-CRP). Layer 2 (Predictive):Random forest classifiers trained on referral-centre cohorts. Layer 3 (Calibration): Multivariate Vector Platt Scaling adjusting ENDO logits for concurrent IBS/IBD confounding. Layer 4 (Safety): Dual-tier deferral mechanism combining Mahalanobis distance out-of-distribution (OOD) rejection and ambiguity deferral. Layer 5 (Evaluation):30-iteration Monte Carlo external validation auditing discrimination (ROC/DeLong), calibration (ECE, Brier score), clinical utility (Decision Curve Analysis), and race-stratified fairness. Software Requirements: Before running the script, users must install the following required CRAN packages: tidyverse (data manipulation and piping, MASS (multivariate normal generation via mvrnorm for the Gaussian copula), ranger (fast random forest modelling), scales (graphical scaling and formatting), ggplot2(publication-grade data visualisation), and patchwork (multi-panel figure composition).
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Chemical Recycling of Acrylonitrile–Butadiene–Styrene (ABS) via Nitrile Reduction and Imine Vitrimer Formation
resume: Abstract As plastic consumption accelerates, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) remains a major waste contributor because of its widespread use and limited recyclability. Here, we report a closed-loop chemical recycling strategy in which a boron catalyst selectively reduces ABS nitrile groups to generate amine-functional ABS (AFABS), followed by dynamic imine cross-linking with glutaraldehyde to form an imine-based vitrimer (v-IBS). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirms efficient nitrile-to-amine conversion and subsequent imine formation. Thermal and mechanical analyses reveal enhanced network rigidity (differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) Tg = 115 °C; dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) tan δ peak = 145 °C), while stress relaxation experiments (120–150 °C) show Arrhenius behavior with an activation energy of Ea = 146 kJ·mol–1, consistent with associative imine exchange. In contrast to pristine ABS, which fully dissolves in tetrahydrofuran (THF), v-IBS retains up to 93% of its mass after 24 h, indicating robust cross-linking and solvent resistance. Tensile testing shows reduced strength but substantial stiffness retention, with reprocessed samples maintaining ∼45% of the original modulus, demonstrating partial mechanical recovery enabled by dynamic bond exchange. Notably, acid-catalyzed hydrolysis in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) regenerates AFABS, establishing a reversible pathway for functionalization, vitrimerization, and chemical decross-linking of ABS.
