Drawing on examples from ancient healing traditions, the Cartesian divide, and emerging sciences such as psychoneuroimmunology, it illustrates how reductionism separated mind, body, spirit, and environment, obscuring the unity of human experience. The chapter positions hypnosis as a natural extension of nursing’s relational, presence-based foundations, demonstrating how focused attention, imagery, and meaning-making support physiological and emotional healing. Hypnosis is presented as a core expression of holistic nursing and a pathway to restoring wholeness in modern healthcare.

Evidence-based hypnotic techniques are presented as tools for reducing sympathetic arousal, enhancing vagal tone, and supporting immune balance. Together, PNI and hypnosis offer nurses a biologically grounded, patient-centered approach to healing.

titre: Acute Pain, Procedures, and Surgery

Pain may also be iatrogenic, caused by medical or surgical intervention. Nurses trained in hypnotic strategies can play an important role in reducing sympathetic arousal and activating endogenous pain-modulating systems, bringing a sense of safety and enhanced comfort to their patients. For procedures and surgeries, hypnosis has been shown to decrease both postoperative pain and opioid use, decrease anxiety, nausea, and vomiting, and enhance healing. Clinical hypnosis is a transformative tool for improving comfort, outcomes, and empowerment for patients with acute and iatrogenic pain.

titre: Care of the Nurse
resume: Vicarious trauma arises when healthcare professionals, caregivers, and helpers internalize elements of the traumatic experiences shared by those they serve. The neurobiological and interpersonal processes of empathy, mirror-neuron activation, and emotional contagion contribute to the gradual reshaping of one’s beliefs about safety, trust, and the world. Common symptoms include emotional exhaustion, anxiety, depersonalization, reduced empathy, cognitive impairment, and burnout. Protective strategies such as grounding, reflective supervision, and clear boundaries are essential. Emerging evidence highlights hypnosis as a promising tool for building resilience and regulating stress in trauma-informed nursing. Further research is needed to establish the clinical impact of hypnosis and guide system-level integration.

titre: The Quantum World and the Mind's Potential
resume: Both quantum theory and hypnosis reveal a reality far more dynamic and interconnected than classical frameworks allow. Quantum theory overturned Newtonian determinism by revealing a world shaped by probability, superposition, and the active role of the observer. Similarly, hypnosis demonstrates that consciousness is fluid, context dependent, and capable of rapid shifts in awareness. Drawing on developments in quantum biology, quantum cognition, and theories of consciousness, this chapter examines how quantum principles, such as entanglement, coherence, and state collapse, offer useful metaphors and possible mechanisms for understanding altered states, suggestibility, and subconscious processing. While acknowledging scientific debate and avoiding reductionistic claims, the discussion highlights how quantum-informed perspectives can enrich psychological and therapeutic models, particularly within holistic disciplines such as nursing. By integrating insights from physics, psychology, and emerging holistic research, this chapter invites a re-examination of free will, perception, connections between humans, and the malleability of subjective experience.

titre: Effect of Supportive Psychotherapy on Quality of Life and Psychological Distress Among Maternal Near-Miss Survivors in Kilimanjaro, Tanzania: A Randomised Controlled Trial
resume: Background/Objectives: Maternal near miss (MNM) may have lasting effects on women’s quality of life (QoL) and psychological well-being. Evidence on interventions to support recovery after MNM remains limited, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated the effect of supportive psychotherapy (SPT) on QoL and symptoms of anxiety and depression among MNM survivors in Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. Methods: In this parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial, 160 women with MNM were allocated 1:1 to four weekly sessions of SPT plus standard postnatal care (SPNC) or SPNC alone. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and at three-month follow-up using the WHOQOL-BREF and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Linear mixed-effects models estimated between-group differences in change following the intention-to-treat principle. The trial was prospectively registered (PACTR202304525632216). Results: Of 160 randomised participants, 157 (98.1%) completed the three-month follow-up. Group-by-time interactions were significant for all outcomes (p ≤ 0.002). At three months, SPT produced greater improvements than SPNC alone in physical health (mean difference in change [ΔΔ] = 8.48; 95% CI 3.36–13.60), psychological health (ΔΔ = 16.28; 95% CI 10.97–21.59), social relationships (ΔΔ = 13.80; 95% CI 8.25–19.35), environmental health (ΔΔ = 9.38; 95% CI 5.88–12.88), overall QoL (ΔΔ = 17.39; 95% CI 10.87–23.90), and satisfaction with health (ΔΔ = 13.64; 95% CI 7.26–20.01). Anxiety and depression scores also decreased more with SPT (ΔΔ = −1.83; 95% CI −2.59 to −1.07 and ΔΔ = −1.87; 95% CI −2.56 to −1.18, respectively). Conclusions: Four sessions of SPT improved QoL and reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms following MNM, with the largest between-group differences observed at three months. Brief psychosocial support may strengthen postnatal recovery among MNM survivors, although its longer-term effectiveness and its generalisability to other settings remain to be established.

titre: Effects of a cognitive-behavioral therapy–based program on substance use, well-being, and psychological symptoms
resume: This study examined associations between a seven-session cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)-based group intervention and substance-use frequency, well-being, and psychological symptoms among university students. In a non-randomized, three-group quasi-experimental design, 90 students were allocated by session availability to CBT ( n = 34), inactive control ( n = 33), or active placebo ( n = 23) groups. CBT comprised seven weekly sessions of approximately 90 min. Assessments occurred at pretest, posttest, and 12-week follow-up. The Substance Use Frequency Scale assessed tobacco/nicotine use, heavy episodic alcohol consumption, and nonmedical prescription medication use; the Holistic Wellbeing Measure assessed hedonic and eudaimonic well-being; and the Brief Symptom Inventory-18 assessed somatization, depression, and anxiety. Six mixed-design ANOVAs showed significant Group × Time interactions for all outcomes (ηp 2 = 0.081–0.184). Baseline-adjusted comparisons using HC3-robust standard errors and Benjamini–Hochberg correction showed statistically significant differences favoring CBT in all 12 posttest and 10 of 12 follow-up contrasts. Follow-up comparisons with the active placebo group were not significant for eudaimonic well-being or somatization. CBT participation was associated with reduced substance-use frequency and psychological symptoms and increased well-being, although non-random allocation and low reliability of the substance-use composite limit interpretation. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov , NCT07884422.

titre: Clinical Significance of Pharmacogenetic Profiling in Akathisia Associated With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) involves involuntary, distressing thoughts and compulsive behaviors. While selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are widely used in the treatment of OCD, when administered concomitantly with antipsychotics, they can contribute to akathisia. Drug metabolism and side-effect profiles can be influenced by genetic variations in genes encoding cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes. In this case report, the pharmacogenetic findings and clinical features of a 29-year-old male patient diagnosed with OCD and experiencing akathisia were evaluated. The patient received standard pharmacotherapy prior to the genetic test. However, pharmacogenetic analysis revealed that the patient was an intermediate metabolizer (IM) for CYP2D6, a normal (extensive) metabolizer for other CYP enzymes, and showed increased induction for CYP1A2. Despite beta-blocker therapy, akathisia persisted and subsided following the readjustment of the quetiapine dose. However, the simultaneous use of multiple psychotropic drugs, dose changes, and potential drug-drug interactions limited the interpretation of the pharmacogenetic findings. This case report highlights the potential role of pharmacogenetic tests in clinical practice, but demonstrates that they do not definitively predict treatment response or adverse effects. Larger studies are needed to determine the clinical utility of pharmacogenetic testing in the management of OCD.

titre: Oculomotor and stimulus-locked ERP responses during an emotional antisaccade task in obsessive-compulsive disorder
resume: Introduction Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is clinically heterogeneous, and responses to OCD-relevant images remain incompletely understood. We compared oculomotor activity, stimulus-locked event-related potentials (ERPs), and presaccadic measures. Methods Thirty-eight volunteers with OCD and 38 healthy controls (HC) completed an emotional pro−/antisaccade task with neutral and OCD-relevant images (aggression, contamination, checking, symmetry) during simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking. Subjective valence and arousal ratings were collected. Clinical subgroup, image-category, and symptom-severity analyses were exploratory. Results Volunteers with OCD rated symmetry images as less pleasant and both symmetry and contamination images as more arousing than HC. Antisaccade correction rates were higher in volunteers with OCD. Mean and peak saccade velocities were higher during prosaccade trials when correct and erroneous saccades were analyzed together. These group differences were no longer statistically significant when only correct saccades were analyzed. Volunteers with OCD showed reduced P2 and N2 amplitudes and prolonged N2 latencies. Significant main effects of the image category were observed for P3 amplitude revealed a significant difference between aggression and symmetry stimuli, with symmetry images eliciting lower amplitudes. Stimulus-locked ERPs showed no statistically significant Group × Image Category interactions. Presaccadic measures showed no statistically significant group differences. Exploratory analyses within the OCD group suggested an association between higher Y-BOCS (Yale–Brown Obsessive-Compulsive Scale) scores and shorter P2 peak latency for symmetry images. No statistically significant differences were detected among clinical subgroup. Discussion Responses to individually symptom-matched and unmatched images were not directly compared. Affective symptoms, treatment exposure, and psychiatric comorbidity limit attribution to OCD alone. Exploratory findings require replication in larger samples with adequate subgroup representation. Non-significant results do not establish equivalence between groups or clinical subgroups.

Novel Dietary Interventions in Functional Dyspepsia
resume: This pilot study will test whether people with functional dyspepsia can follow two new dietary approaches and whether these diets may improve symptoms. Thirty adults will be randomly assigned to follow a low-histidine diet, a low-tryptophan diet, or a comparison diet for six weeks. The study aims to reduce-not eliminate- intake. The comparison diet provides dietary instructions that are not intended to reduce either nutrient. The main goal is to determine whether participants intake of these nutrients can change through diet approaches. Participants will receive nutrition counseling, follow the diet assigned, describe food consumption during dietary-recall interviews, complete questionnaires, provide blood and urine samples, and swallow a capsule that measures movement and gases in the digestive tract before and after the intervention.

titre: Rôle de l'Axe Intestin-cerveau Dans le TDAH : Exploration Des Liens Entre le Microbiote Intestinal, la Cognition et la Symptomatologie
resume: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder in child and adolescent psychiatry, affecting approximately 8% of the population worldwide. Beyond the inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity that define it in DSM-5, ADHD is consistently associated with attentional and executive deficits considered central to its symptomatology. Its aetiopathogenesis is multifactorial and remains poorly understood: decades of research have identified no specific genetic or environmental factor. The gut microbiota modulates the bidirectional gut-brain axis, notably through the intestinal mucosa, which secretes neuromediators such as serotonin and precursors of dopamine implicated in concentration and in ADHD. Roughly ten case-control studies have reported differences in gut microbiota diversity, richness and composition between individuals with ADHD and typically developing individuals, and several have associated specific bacterial taxa with symptom severity. Methodological heterogeneity across these studies has so far precluded consensus on a specific bacterial signature. Critically, they relied almost exclusively on clinical questionnaires, which are subjective and vulnerable to respondent and observation bias, and did not assess the cognitive deficits that characterise the disorder. To date, no study has investigated the relationship between gut microbiota composition and cognitive performance measured with standardised neuropsychological tests in children with ADHD compared with typically developing children. This is the specific gap addressed here. This monocentric, prospective, case-control observational study will enrol 140 French-speaking children aged 6 to 12 years: 70 children with ADHD, combined presentation, diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria and recruited from the paediatric psychiatry clinics of the Hôpital Universitaire de Bruxelles (Erasme and HUDERF sites), and 70 typically developing children recruited through advertisements. Children are excluded for prematurity, IQ below 75, psychiatric or serious chronic disease, gastrointestinal or inflammatory bowel conditions, coeliac disease, food intolerances, eating disorders, dietary supplements within 4 weeks, and antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors or any psychotropic medication within 3 months, yielding a medication-free ADHD sample and removing major confounders of microbiota composition. Each participant attends a single assessment visit. A stool sample is self-collected at home the day before or the day of the visit using a stabilising collection kit, then stored at -80 °C. Metagenomic DNA is extracted, the V1-V3 region of the 16S rRNA gene is amplified with universal eubacterial primers, amplicons are sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform, and reads are processed with the QIIME2 pipeline, in academic collaboration with the Louvain Drug Research Institute (UCLouvain). At the same visit, participants complete a cognitive assessment comprising the WISC-V (estimated IQ), selected subtests of the Test of Attentional Performance (visual and auditory selective attention, divided attention, vigilance, flexibility, Go/NoGo inhibition, working memory) and the Maudsley Index of Delay Aversion. ADHD symptom frequency and severity are rated by the physician using the ADHD Rating Scale IV, and dietary habits are documented with a Food Frequency Questionnaire completed before the visit. The study has three objectives: to determine whether gut microbiota composition and diversity differ between children with ADHD and typically developing children, and to identify a possible imbalance or bacterial signature; to compare attentional and executive performance between the two groups and examine its association with microbiota composition; and to explore correlations between the severity of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms and microbiota composition. The hypotheses are that children with ADHD differ from typically developing children in microbiota diversity and composition, that they show poorer attentional and executive performance associated with their microbiota composition, and that their microbiota is associated with clinically rated symptom severity.

titre: Visceral Hypersensitivity, Urgency and Persistent Symptoms After Mucosal Healing in Ulcerative Colitis Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study in Switzerland
resume: This is a prospective, single-arm, observational, multicentre study conducted at four centres in Switzerland. A total of 280 adult patients with moderately active UC (Mayo score 6-12) initiating or receiving standard-of-care treatment will be enrolled. Patients will undergo standard disease monitoring according to STRIDE II recommendations, including clinical assessment, endoscopy, histology and faecal calprotectin. In addition, anorectal manometry and rectal barostat measurements will be performed at baseline and after 12 weeks of treatment. The primary endpoint is the presence of visceral hypersensitivity, defined as a discomfort/pain threshold below 90% of maximal rectal capacity during rectal distension, in patients achieving endoscopic mucosal healing (Mayo endoscopic score 0) compared with those without mucosal healing. Secondary endpoints include anorectal motor function, histological remission (Geboes score), predictors of mucosal healing and urgency resolution, and correlations between rectal hypersensitivity and faecal calprotectin.

titre: A Prospective Observational Study on Patients' Assessment of the Quality of Care During Their Treatment for Cholecystectomies at Limoges University Hospital
resume: SATISCHOL is a prospective, monocentric observational study designed to assess pain management and quality of care in patients undergoing elective cholecystectomy at Limoges University Hospital, France. The primary objective is to assess the proportion of patients reporting a visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score below 4 two hours after surgery, in association with the occurrence of no postoperative complication or a grade I early postoperative complication according to the Clavien-Dindo classification, within four weeks after surgery. Secondary objectives include assessing early postoperative pain, describing postoperative complications and intraoperative pain management techniques, and evaluating changes in patients' quality of life using the Gastrointestinal Quality of Life Index (GIQLI) and EQ-5D-5L questionnaires. Patient-reported experience will also be assessed using a study-specific questionnaire (PREMS). A total of 70 participants are expected to be enrolled. Patients will be followed for approximately 3 to 6 weeks after surgery.

titre: Simple Nut Supplementation Induces Positive Gut Metabolic Signals in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
resume: People with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, often continue to experience disruptions in the gut microbiome and metabolism even when their disease is in clinical remission on biologic therapy. These persistent gut-level changes may contribute to disease flares over time. Nuts are nutrient-dense foods rich in unsaturated fats, fiber, minerals, and polyphenols, and have been shown to support gut health in general and cardiometabolic populations. However, their specific effects on the gut microbiome and metabolome in people with IBD in remission have not been examined. This proof-of-concept study investigated whether short-term, daily consumption of a standardized mixed nut blend (almonds, walnuts, and pecans) shifts the gut microbiome and metabolic signals of people with IBD toward a healthier, control-like profile. Sixty participants: 21 healthy controls, 19 participants with Crohn's disease in remission, and 20 participants with ulcerative colitis in remission, underwent a 3-day nut-avoidance washout, followed by 10 days of consuming 30 g/day of a mixed nut blend. Fecal samples were collected on days -3, 0, 5, and 10 and analyzed for microbiome composition (16S rRNA sequencing) and metabolite profiles (untargeted LC-MS metabolomics). Participants also completed a food frequency questionnaire and a daily adherence survey. The study aimed to characterize how a defined, single food item influences gut health signals in IBD remission, providing a foundation for larger, longer-term dietary interventions.

titre: The Effect of Hypnotherapy on the Production of Transcription Factor NF-kB, IL-6, IL-10, and Anxiety in Patients Undergoing Cesarean Section: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: This randomized controlled trial tests whether listening to an audio hypnotherapy recording before a planned cesarean section reduces preoperative anxiety and changes blood markers of inflammation. Sixty pregnant women scheduled for elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at Prof. Dr. I.G.N.G. Ngoerah General Hospital, Denpasar, Indonesia, will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either two 30-minute audio hypnotherapy sessions (the evening before surgery and the morning of surgery) or standard care without hypnotherapy. Anxiety will be measured with the Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale (APAIS). NF-kB, IL-6 and IL-10 will be measured in blood before the intervention and 24 hours after surgery.

titre: Healing and Improving Postnatal Nights Through Sleep (HIPNoS): A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness for Sleep (PUMAS) in Postpartum Women With Insomnia and Depression
resume: Insomnia and depression are highly prevalent during postpartum, but effective treatment options are severely limited. Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness (PUMAS) combines behavioral sleep strategies and mindfulness-based exercises to improve sleep and mood during pregnancy. Indeed, PUMAS has been shown to effectively treatment comorbid insomnia and depression in pregnancy in controlled and uncontrolled trials. The present randomized controlled trial (RCT) will evaluate the effectiveness of PUMAS in a sample of postpartum women with comorbid insomnia and depression who will be randomized to to telemedicine PUMAS or online sleep hygiene education (SHE; enhanced usual care). Patients will be treated for six weeks followed by assessment after treatment then follow-up assessment 3-months later. The investigators hypothesize that PUMAS patients, relative to SHE patients, will report superior acute treatment effects on insomnia and depression as well as more durable effects at 3-month follow-up.

titre: Stratified Stepped Care Telehealth Care Pathways for Child and Adolescent Mental Health
resume: This study will evaluate a telehealth-delivered stepped-care model to improve access to mental health support for children and adolescents in Brazil and South Africa. The study will include children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years who have concerns related to anxiety, depression, irritability, or disruptive behavior. Participants will first complete an online mental health assessment. Depending on their symptom level, they may receive psychoeducational materials, a brief single-session intervention, or additional mental health support. Participants whose symptoms remain elevated after the single-session intervention may be randomly assigned to one of three groups: four-session cognitive behavioral therapy, twelve-session cognitive behavioral therapy, or more intensive psychoeducational materials. The study will compare changes in mental health symptoms across the three groups. It will also evaluate whether the interventions are acceptable, feasible, safe, and suitable for delivery through telehealth. Participants will complete assessments at baseline, during treatment, after treatment, and approximately six months later.

titre: Large-scale shotgun metagenomic analysis of gut bacteria-phage interactions in IBS
Predictors of Fecal Elastase Testing Completion in Outpatient and Inpatient Settings: A Single Center Retrospective Analysis
resume: OBJECTIVES: To characterize completion of fecal elastase-1 (FE-1) testing, identify clinical contexts associated with abnormal results, evaluate downstream diagnostic and treatment events, and determine the clinical significance of non-completion. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with FE-1 orders from 2017 through 2022 in a large integrated health system. Orders placed within 30 days were consolidated into diagnostic episodes. Completion required a linked specimen with a reported result. We evaluated pre-order clinical contexts and one-year outcomes and performed a weighted manual chart review of 200 unique patients with non-completed episodes sampled from four downstream pathway strata. RESULTS: Among 23,422 diagnostic episodes, 11,834 (50.5%) were completed. FE-1 ≤200 µg/g occurred in 20.4% of interpretable results and varied by clinical context: 13.7% with irritable bowel syndrome, 21.2% with chronic diarrhea, 38.3% with chronic pancreatitis, 60.1% with pancreatic cancer, and 79.5% after pancreatic surgery. Initial completion was associated with higher odds of new exocrine pancreatic insufficiency diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio, 2.27; 95% confidence interval, 1.91-2.70) and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy initiation (adjusted odds ratio, 2.20; 95% confidence interval, 1.89-2.55), whereas non-completion was associated with more repeat FE-1 testing. Among eligible unique non-completers, weighted chart review classified 66.9% as probable missed diagnostic follow-through based on available documentation; failure to submit or return the specimen (60.1%) and specimen-processing problems (20.4%) predominated. CONCLUSIONS: FE-1 completion was modestly associated with measured pre-order factors, while abnormal results varied substantially by clinical context. Specimen return, processing, and closed-loop follow-up represent potential targets for improving evaluation of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

titre: Bacteroides Fragilis-Derived Ceramide-1-phosphate Contributes to Depression Comorbidity in Irritable Bowel Syndrome Through Hippocampal SMPD4 and Myelin Disruption
resume: Depression affects more than one-third of patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D), yet the gut-brain mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified enrichment of Bacteroides fragilis in IBS-D patients with comorbid depression, with relative abundance positively correlating with Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. B. fragilis exposure induced depressive-like behaviors in antibiotic-treated and germ-free mice and was accompanied by reduced hippocampal sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 4 (SMPD4), altered myelin-associated gene programs, and myelin loss. A combined hippocampal rescue strategy using Syn- and MBP-promoter AAV vectors restored SMPD4 expression and improved behavioral and myelin-related outcomes. B. fragilis cultures and a C1P-producing engineered bacterial strain supported an association between bacterial sphingolipid production and the phenotype, whereas peripheral C1P administration increased hippocampal C1P and reduced SMPD4 and myelin markers. Dietary branched-chain amino acid restriction reduced systemic C1P-associated signals, restored SMPD4 expression, and partially improved depressive-like phenotypes. Collectively, the findings support a B. fragilis-associated C1P-SMPD4 pathway linking intestinal dysbiosis to hippocampal sphingolipid imbalance and myelin disruption, while leaving the route and molecular form by which peripheral lipid signals influence the brain unresolved.

titre: Human milk oligosaccharides as immunomodulators of the gut-immune-brain axis: a potential route to suppressing neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease
resume: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common cause of dementia, is characterized by interacting pathological processes in which chronic neuroinflammation plays a central role. The gut-brain axis connects intestinal and central nervous system function through immune, neural, and metabolic pathways, yet how immune signaling integrates these pathways in AD remains unclear. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are structurally diverse bioactive glycans whose immunomodulatory properties extend beyond their prebiotic effects. This narrative review examines HMOs within a gut-immune-brain framework, proposing that neuroinflammation amplifies the interplay between gut-derived immune signals, amyloid-β and tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. METHODS: Relevant literature was retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through January 2026. The review focused on English-language publications from 2010 onward, supplemented by earlier foundational studies that provided essential mechanistic or historical context. RESULTS: We synthesize evidence on immune communication along the gut-brain axis and examine how HMOs may influence this communication through microbiota-dependent effects and direct interactions with immune receptors. Particular attention is given to the relationships between HMO structure, receptor engagement, immune cell responses, and inflammatory signaling. These mechanisms provide a rationale for investigating whether HMOs can modify peripheral immune signals that contribute to neuroinflammation in AD. Throughout the review, findings from infant and other experimental settings are distinguished from evidence directly relevant to aging and AD. CONCLUSION: Research on HMOs in aging and AD remains insufficient: direct evidence from aged or AD models is scarce, human trials are lacking, infant physiology differs substantially from that of older adults, and the bioavailability of HMOs to the aged brain is still uncertain. We therefore delineate this translational gap and outline research strategies to address it. Collectively, this review provides a conceptual framework for understanding the potential immunoregulatory roles of HMOs in neuroinflammation and identifies them as a hypothesis-generating class of candidate immunomodulators for AD.

titre: Association of a Yoga and Naturopathy-Based Lifestyle Program with Gut Microbiome Changes in People Living with Obesity: An Observational Study
resume: BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with gut microbiota alterations and impaired metabolic health. Lifestyle-based complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) interventions, including yoga, dietary modification, and naturopathy, may modulate gut microbiota and improve metabolic health. However, evidence from integrated residential programs remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine changes in the gut microbiota composition, anthropometric and inflammatory parameters, and quality of life associated with participation in a 21-day residential yoga and naturopathy-based lifestyle (YNBL) program among adults with obesity. METHODS: This prospective observational pilot study included 20 adults (10 males, 10 females; aged 25-45 years) with obesity (BMI 30-45) who participated in a 21-day inpatient YNBL intervention at a CAM facility. The multicomponent yoga and naturopathy-based lifestyle program comprised daily yoga sessions, a vegetarian diet, weekly fasting (≤500kcal), sun exposure, hydrotherapy, mud therapy, and health-education modules. Gut microbiota profiling, anthropometric measurements, body weight, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and quality-of-life indices were assessed before and following the intervention. Changes over time were evaluated using appropriate statistical methods, with correction for multiple comparisons where applicable. RESULTS: Post-intervention, gut microbial species showed significant alterations, including Megasphaera (p = 0.003), Veillonella (p = 0.046), and Klebsiella (p = 0.041). Participants demonstrated significant reductions in BMI at the first follow-up (33.80 ± 2.97) compared to baseline (36.10 ± 3.06) [Mean Difference (MD) = -2.30, p < 0.001] and waist-to-hip ratio at second fellow-up (0.77 ± 0.20) compared to baseline (0.83 ± 0.21) [MD = 0.05, p = 0.008] Quality-of-life scores improved significantly across physical [MD = 1.70, p<0.001], psychological [MD = 1.75, p = 0.003], social [MD = 0.60, p = 0.001], and environmental [MD = 1.40, p < 0.001] domains. Given the small sample size, absence of a separate control group, and multifactorial nature of the program, these findings represent exploratory temporal associations. They cannot establish causality or attribute the observed changes to any specific component of the intervention. CONCLUSION: Participation in the 21-day therapy multicomponent YNBL program was associated with short-term changes in selected gut microbial taxa, anthropometric and inflammatory measures, and quality of life in adults with obesity. These preliminary findings highlight the potential benefits of YNBL interventions as supportive strategies for improving metabolic and overall health in obese populations.

titre: Deep Brain Stimulation for Intractable Hiccups due to Diaphragmatic Dystonia: A First Reported Case
resume: INTRODUCTION: Chronic hiccups (singultus) are involuntary diaphragmatic contractions that, when persistent, can cause severe physical and psychological distress. While most cases are benign and self-limited, intractable hiccups may rarely indicate underlying neurological dysfunction. One exceptionally rare cause is diaphragmatic dystonia - a condition for which no established diagnostic criteria or treatment guidelines exist, and which has been described only in isolated case reports. CASE PRESENTATION: We present the first known case of deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the internal and external globus pallidus (GPi and GPe) used to treat chronic, treatment-resistant hiccups. A 70-year-old woman experienced 2 years of continuous hiccups unresponsive to multiple pharmacologic and surgical interventions. Extensive diagnostics excluded metabolic, neurological, gastrointestinal, and psychiatric causes. Diaphragmatic dystonia was suspected. Bilateral octa-contact DBS electrodes were implanted targeting the GPi and GPe. Intraoperative monopolar stimulation (1.5 mA, 90 µs, 130 Hz) was initiated on day of surgery. Electrodes were accurately placed without complications. RESULTS: Near-complete resolution of hiccups occurred immediately postoperatively. Quality of life significantly improved: Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) from 8 to 0, EQ-5D-3L from 0.530 to 1.0, Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale from 13 to 0, and PHQ-9 from 16 to 4. At the 14-month follow-up, the improvement was fully maintained. CONCLUSION: DBS targeting the globus pallidus may represent a novel and effective intervention for refractory chronic hiccups, particularly in cases suspected to involve diaphragmatic dystonia.

titre: Quality-of-life outcomes of MR-guided ultrahypofractionated SBRT versus CBCT-guided moderately hypofractionated IMRT for localized prostate cancer: an EPIC-based real-world comparative study
resume: BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance-guided stereotactic body radiation therapy (MR-linac SBRT) is increasingly used for localized prostate cancer; however, its impact on patient-reported quality of life compared with cone beam computed tomography-guided conventional intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) remains unclear. We compared quality-of-life outcomes between MR-linac SBRT and IMRT using the Expanded Prostate Cancer Index Composite (EPIC-50). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 82 patients with localized prostate cancer treated with MR-linac SBRT (n = 51) or IMRT (n = 31) between 2022 and 2025. Clinically meaningful declines in EPIC-50 domain scores were assessed at 1-3 and 9-12 months. Predictors of urinary quality-of-life deterioration were evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: The proportions of patients with clinically meaningful declines in urinary, bowel, sexual, and hormonal domains did not differ significantly between the treatment groups at either 1-3 or 9-12 months. Symptom-directed pharmacotherapy was initiated more frequently after IMRT, including medications for lower urinary tract symptoms (P = .028), gastrointestinal symptoms (P = .0044), and vasomotor symptoms (P = .0014). Among patients receiving MR-linac SBRT, a higher baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) was associated with urinary quality-of-life deterioration. An IPSS cutoff of ≥9 was significantly associated with urinary deterioration (odds ratio, 27.0, 95% CI 4.11-541.49; P = .0002). CONCLUSIONS: MR-linac SBRT showed no significant differences in patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes compared with IMRT and was associated with less frequent use of symptom-directed pharmacotherapy. Baseline IPSS may help identify patients at increased risk of urinary quality-of-life deterioration after MR-linac SBRT.

titre: Genetic Evidence Linking Gut-Brain Peptide Signaling to Anorexia Nervosa: Implications for Early Risk Detection
resume: BACKGROUND: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe psychiatric disorder with high mortality, yet its biological underpinnings remain unclear. Gut-brain peptides, which influence brain function through circulatory and vagal routes, have emerged as potential contributors to AN, though causal relationships remain unexplored. Given the unclear biological mechanisms and lack of biomarkers for AN, this study aims to explore the causal role of gut-brain peptides in AN development, in order to identify potential diagnostic or therapeutic targets. METHODS: We applied Mendelian randomization (MR) to assess the causal effects of 12 gut-brain peptides on AN risk, using genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from populations of European ancestry. The inverse variance weighted (IVW) method was the primary analytic tool, supplemented with sensitivity analyses. Peptides showing associations with AN were also tested across five other psychiatric disorders: schizophrenia (SCZ), major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)-were also explored. RESULTS: Elevated peptide YY (PYY) levels were causally linked to increased AN risk (OR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.01-1.15, p = .035). No significant associations were found for the other peptides. Reverse MR showed that genetic liability to AN was associated with reduced levels of leptin and chromogranin A (CgA). These associations were not observed in the five other psychiatric disorders. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies PYY as a potential causal factor in AN and highlights leptin and CgA as downstream biomarkers. These findings suggest gut-brain peptides may be uniquely involved in AN pathogenesis, offering targets for early detection and therapeutic intervention.

titre: Gastric Bypass Reversal: Indications, Surgical Management, and Outcomes in a Single-center Series
resume: BACKGROUND: Gastric bypass reversal is an uncommon salvage procedure for severe refractory complications. Surgical strategies are heterogeneous, and perioperative and long-term outcomes remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 30 patients undergoing RYGB or OAGB reversal between 2020 and 2025. Indications, surgical management, perioperative morbidity, and one-year weight and functional outcomes were assessed. Exploratory analyses evaluated outcomes according to reconstructive extent and concomitant procedures. RESULTS: Thirty patients (23 women; median age 48 years) underwent reversal. Indications were multifactorial in 66.7%, most commonly protein-energy malnutrition (46.7%), refractory diarrhea (43.3%), and post-bariatric hypoglycemia (36.7%). Major complications occurred in 23.3%, 16.7% required reoperation, and no mortality occurred. Standard reversal was performed in 24 patients (80%), whereas 6 (20%) required additional reconstruction. In exploratory analyses, additional reconstruction was associated with longer operative time (225 vs. 120 min, p = 0.005), hospital stay (10 vs. 5 days, p = 0.046), and higher reoperation rates (50.0% vs. 8.3%, p = 0.041). At one year, two-thirds experienced weight regain (median + 6 kg). Malnutrition and refractory diarrhea improved or resolved in 92.9% and 92.3%, respectively, compared with 45.5% for post-bariatric hypoglycemia and 33.3% for chronic abdominal pain. Perceived quality of life improved in 63.3%. CONCLUSION: Gastric bypass reversal may provide substantial functional benefit in selected patients, particularly for malnutrition and refractory diarrhea, despite significant postoperative morbidity and variable weight outcomes. Reconstructive extent was associated with perioperative outcomes, highlighting the importance of both clinical indication and reconstructive requirements when considering reversal.

titre: Teletherapy for Adolescent Mental Health: A Scoping Review of Comparative Effectiveness
resume: BACKGROUND: Teletherapy has become an increasingly common delivery format for adolescent mental healthcare, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Given adolescents' distinct developmental characteristics, its effectiveness requires evaluation against in-person treatment and alternative remote formats. The objective was to map the randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence on teletherapy for adolescent mental health and to conduct a quantitative synthesis where the evidence permits. METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidance, six databases were searched for RCTs published from 2014 onward that evaluated therapist-delivered remote psychotherapy for adolescents (13-18 years) with diagnosed mental health conditions, compared with face-to-face treatment, an alternative teletherapy format, or a waitlist or minimal-contact control. Quantitative synthesis was stratified by comparator type. RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs across eight diagnostic categories were included. Six compared teletherapy with face-to-face treatment, six compared two remote formats, and six used only waitlist or minimal-contact controls. Among face-to-face comparisons, two obsessive-compulsive disorder trials met noninferiority margins, two anxiety trials nonsignificantly favored face-to-face treatment (g = -0.54 and -0.45), and single tic-disorder and insomnia trials found no clear difference. Teletherapy was superior to waitlist or minimal-contact control for anxiety (k = 6, g = 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.75-2.38) and depression (k = 5, g = 1.14, 95% CI: 0.64-1.64). Risk of bias was low in 3 of 18 trials. CONCLUSIONS: Teletherapy improves adolescent anxiety and depression relative to waitlist or minimal-contact controls, although the size of the benefit is uncertain. Face-to-face comparisons are few, and their findings differ by condition, so equivalence to in-person care cannot yet be established. Condition-specific trials with face-to-face comparators are needed.

titre: Sustainability of Treatment Success 5 Years after Exposure-Based Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for Anxiety Disorders
resume: INTRODUCTION: Achieving sustainable success in the treatment of anxiety disorders remains a central objective in mental health care. Although research has demonstrated the short-term efficacy of psychotherapy, evidence regarding long-term sustainability is limited. This study examined treatment outcomes 5 years after prediction-error-based exposure therapy. METHODS: For 355 patients (616 eligible; 58% follow-up rate), newly collected follow-up data on anxiety symptoms and psychosocial functioning were compared to pretreatment, posttreatment, and 6-month follow-up data from a multicenter clinical trial characterized by high treatment fidelity. RESULTS: Improvements in anxiety symptoms and psychosocial functioning that were evident at posttreatment and 6-month follow-up were largely preserved after 5 years. No significant differences emerged between randomized groups of temporally intensified and non-intensified exposure. From 6 months to 5 years, overall remission rates remained stable, with the majority of patients exhibiting no reliable change in symptom severity. Reliable relapse occurred in 4.9% and reliable new remission in 6.5%. Most patients (63.4%) did not seek additional treatment. Among those who did, depression (64.2%) and anxiety (60.5%) were the most frequently cited reasons, although only a minority (6.0%) sought further treatment exclusively for anxiety. Additional treatment during the follow-up period was associated with higher symptom severity throughout assessments. CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the sustainability and long-term public health benefits of exposure-based CBT for anxiety disorders. Most patients do not need additional treatments for mental disorders even 5 years after treatment. Nevertheless, further efforts are needed to optimize interventions for those patients who do not achieve remission or experience relapse.

titre: Therapeutic Change May Begin before the Therapist and Patient Ever Meet: Pretreatment Alliance Changes Predict Clinical Outcomes
resume: INTRODUCTION: Mechanisms of change are widely assumed to be activated by the onset of treatment. This foundational premise underlies decades of psychotherapy research and guides the timing of measurement and intervention in clinical science. The present study challenges this assumption by demonstrating that one of the most well-established predictors of treatment outcome - the therapeutic alliance - not only changes before therapy begins, but that these early, pretreatment changes predict both alliance development and symptom reduction throughout treatment. METHODS: In a randomized controlled trial for depression (N = 100), the therapeutic alliance was assessed twice before patients met their therapist and weekly thereafter. RESULTS: The pretreatment change in alliance significantly predicted subsequent alliance dynamics and clinical improvement, above and beyond baseline levels. The findings remained robust even after controlling for pretreatment outcome expectations and previous treatment experience. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that mechanisms traditionally viewed as the result of treatment targeting may, in fact, be antecedents. By revealing pre-treatment shifts in a mechanism once thought to be non-existent prior to patient-therapist contact, this work may challenge fundamental assumptions in clinical psychology and highlights the need to reconceptualize mechanisms of change as person-specific dynamic signatures that characterize individuals even before psychotherapy begins. Such a shift has implications for how we define, measure, and intervene on core mechanisms of human change.

titre: Non-pharmacological interventions for anxiety and pain in thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) is the diagnostic standard for evaluating thyroid nodules but commonly provokes procedural anxiety and pain, which may contribute to non-diagnostic cytology, repeat procedures, and increased healthcare utilization. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions for reducing anxiety and pain during thyroid FNAB. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing non-pharmacological interventions with usual care or no intervention in patients undergoing thyroid FNAB. Primary outcomes were post-procedural anxiety and anxiety change scores; pain was evaluated as a secondary outcome. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using standardized mean differences (SMDs). The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261411294). RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1,439 patients were included, with six contributing to the meta-analysis. Non-pharmacological interventions significantly reduced post-procedural anxiety (SMD = - 0.26; 95% CI, - 0.51 to - 0.01; p = 0.044; I² = 70.3%) and produced a greater pre- to post-procedure reduction in anxiety (change-score SMD = 0.57; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.75; p < 0.0001; I² = 0%), where positive change-score values denote a larger reduction in anxiety in the intervention group. Video-based interventions showed a consistent moderate benefit, whereas music-based interventions did not significantly reduce post-procedural anxiety (test for subgroup differences, p = 0.005). Pain reduction was not statistically significant (SMD = - 0.49; 95% CI, - 1.23 to 0.25; p = 0.19; I² = 94.4%). One non-pooled trial found mindfulness reduced procedural adverse events and emotional stress. CONCLUSIONS: Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly video-based preparation, reduce anxiety during thyroid FNAB. Evidence for pain reduction remains inconclusive because of substantial heterogeneity. These findings support incorporating simple, low-cost interventions into routine thyroid FNAB while encouraging standardized protocols and further high-quality randomized trials.
revue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

titre: Electroconvulsive Therapy Ameliorates Obsessive-Compulsive Symptoms in Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: A Case Series
resume: Obsessive-compulsive (OC) symptoms are prevalent in patients with schizophrenia and may be exacerbated by clozapine, the cornerstone pharmacotherapy for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an established augmentation strategy in TRS; however, its impact on comorbid OC symptoms in this population has not been systematically described. We report a case series of 5 patients with TRS maintained on clozapine who exhibited prominent OC symptoms. All patients underwent a course of ECT. Psychopathology was assessed with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) and the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) at baseline (week 0) and at weeks 2 and 6. All 5 patients demonstrated substantial improvement in both psychotic symptoms (PANSS) and OC symptoms (Y-BOCS) over 6 weeks of follow-up. The median reduction was 78.3% for Y-BOCS (range: 50.0% to 80.0%) compared with 24.3% for PANSS (range: 22.5% to 65.4%; n = 3), suggesting marked remission of OC symptoms. ECT may selectively ameliorate OC symptoms arising in the context of TRS or clozapine use, possibly through distinct neurobiological mechanisms not operative in primary OCD. Further controlled studies are warranted, as this contrasts with the known lack of efficacy of ECT in primary OCD.

fiche.population: 5 patients avec schizophrénie résistante et clozapine, présentant des TOC comorbides
fiche.intervention: Cure d'électroconvulsivothérapie (ECT)

Amélioration conjointe des symptômes psychotiques (PANSS)

titre: Regional Differences in Publication Volume on Pediatric Sports Knee Conditions Between North America and the Asia-Pacific Regions
resume: PURPOSE: To characterize and compare publication patterns for 5 major pediatric sports knee conditions-anterior cruciate ligament tears, discoid meniscus pathology, osteochondritis dissecans (OCD), patellar instability, and tibial eminence fractures-across North America and the Asia-Pacific regions, examining regional research volume, condition-specific publication patterns, and changes in research output over time. METHODS: EMBASE, PubMed, and Medline were searched from inception to January 2025. Studies focusing on pediatric populations (≤18 years) addressing the 5 specified knee conditions were included. Publications were classified by geographic region based on recruiting institution country, with North America including the United States, Canada, and Mexico and Asia-Pacific defined according to the World Health Organization regional classifications. RESULTS: Of 1100 included publications, North American institutions contributed 907 studies (82.5%) compared with 193 from Asia-Pacific institutions (17.5%). Anterior cruciate ligament injuries dominated research focus globally, comprising 613 publications (56%). Regional differences emerged in condition-specific priorities: discoid meniscus research represented 18% of Asia-Pacific output versus 6.5% in North America, whereas OCD accounted for 26% versus 19%, respectively. Patellar instability and tibial eminence fractures together represented the smallest share of publications (16% combined). Asia-Pacific research showed rapid growth, with 75% of regional publications occurring within the last decade. CONCLUSIONS: Research output rose across both regions, with North America as the dominant contributor. Anterior cruciate ligament injury was the most studied condition, comprising over half of all publications, followed by OCD, patellar instability, discoid meniscus, and tibial eminence fractures. Marked regional variation in condition-specific focus was observed, with Asia-Pacific institutions contributing proportionally greater output on discoid meniscus and OCD. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: North America's dominant research output means that guidelines are largely derived from Western populations, which may limit their applicability in the Asia-Pacific context. These findings highlight the need for internationally collaborative studies to improve generalizability of clinical evidence across diverse populations.

titre: Signatures of Performance Monitoring in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and At-risk Groups: Midfrontal Theta Predicts Divergent Behavioral Adaptation
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been robustly linked to increased performance monitoring, most consistently indexed by an increased error-related negativity (ERN). However, the role of response-related midfrontal theta oscillations, a key neural mechanism supporting cognitive control and behavioral adaptation, remains incompletely understood in OCD and at-risk populations. METHODS: EEG was recorded from 180 adults (46 OCD, 39 unaffected first-degree relatives, 39 with adverse childhood experiences, and 56 controls) during an arrowhead flanker task. Response-related midfrontal theta power (4-7 Hz) was investigated alongside behavioral indices, including error rates and post-error slowing. Group differences in neural and behavioral data, trial-wise theta-behavior relationship, and associations with clinical symptoms were investigated. RESULTS: Error-related increases in midfrontal theta were robust across participants. Relative to the combined non-OCD sample, individuals with OCD exhibited enhanced error-related theta power, while unaffected first-degree relatives and individuals with adverse childhood experiences did not differ from controls. Single-trial analyses revealed altered neural-behavioral coupling: greater theta predicted slower and less accurate performance on subsequent trials in OCD, and, contrarily, improved subsequent performance in controls. Consistent with these findings, individuals with OCD showed prolonged post-error slowing. Across participants, error rate and PES were associated with worry and depressive symptoms, whereas theta power was associated with age and depressive symptoms. CONCLUSIONS: OCD is characterized by enhanced error-related midfrontal theta together with an altered association between neural error signals and adaptive behavioral adjustment. These findings suggest that abnormal performance monitoring in OCD reflects not only exaggerated error processing but also disrupted implementation of cognitive control.
revue: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

titre: Selective Gut-Related Biomarker Profiles Define Parkinson Disease Trait and State
resume: Objective: Gut-brain-axis abnormalities are increasingly implicated in Parkinson disease (PD), but most studies examine individual biological compartments of this axis. We asked whether readily accessible stool and plasma-based biomarker profiles show broad or selective gut abnormalities in PD and whether the profiles associated with PD diagnosis (Trait) are the same as those associated with clinical severity (State). Methods: : This cross-sectional study included 211 participants with PD and 204 healthy controls. Twenty-four stool and plasma biomarkers were organized into an overall profile, three parent domains (microbiome/dysbiosis, gut barrier/inflammation, systemic inflammation/immune activation), and eight more focused mechanistic profiles. Rank-based Global Statistical Tests (GSTs) compared PD Trait and State. Results: : The overall profile showed no evidence of a PD vs. control difference (GST P=0.607; permutation P=0.521), whereas the domain of microbiome/dysbiosis differed (GST P=0.017; permutation P=0.013). Four of eight focused profiles differed nominally: microbial functional-groups, microbial functional-ratios, epithelial injury/bacterial translocation, and myeloid activation. Across PD clinical severity, overall-profile results differed (GST P=0.053; permutation P=0.037); both categories of microbiome/dysbiosis (GST P=0.023; permutation P=0.016) and microbial alpha-diversity (GST P=0.027; permutation P=0.031) differed. Interpretation: The analyses detected differences associated with PD Trait and State in selected gut-related profiles rather than a detectable overall PD-control difference. Microbiome-related profiles showed the most consistent domain findings across PD Trait and State, but they are sufficiently different to suggest that causation and progression of PD follow distinctly different gut processes. These findings refine the concept of the Parkinson gut and prioritize the microbiome for mechanistic and interventional studies.

titre: Interoceptive sensibility tracks confidence, not detection, even without breathing along: five samples with a respiratory change-detection task
resume: The Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) measures adaptive interoceptive sensibility (attention to the body and how one appraises it) and predicts mental health; how that disposition shows up during a bodily task has rarely been tested. We asked whether MAIA scores predict accuracy, confidence or their coupling in the Breath Change Awareness Task, in which participants breathe along with a visual pacer, report whether its pace changed and rate confidence on every trial. Across five samples (N = 687; in Study 5, a respiratory belt confirmed breathing along in 145 of 170 recorded participants), MAIA scores predicted mean confidence (metacognitive bias) in every sample (pooled r = .27, 95% CI [.17, .37]), including Study 5’s preregistered test (r = .26 [.13, .38]; Breath blocks only, r = .26). They were not positively related to perceptual sensitivity (how well changes were detected) or to metacognitive sensitivity, how well confidence tracked accuracy: pooled, positive relations of r = .10 or more were ruled out for both. Study 5’s preregistered detection-threshold null, a stricter criterion, was not established (BF₀₁ = 2.2, below the required 3). In Study 5, the association held with self-esteem, self-doubt, alexithymia and affect controlled. It was also present with vision alone (following the pacer by eye without breathing along), which should weaken a body-based link: r = .22 [.01, .41], with no detectable difference from breathing along (.20). During sensory discrimination, adaptive sensibility showed up as confidence, independent of accuracy and present even without breathing along.

fiche.verdict: Étude sur 5 échantillons montrant que la sensibilité intéroceptive mesurée par le MAIA prédit la confiance (biais métacognitif) mais pas la sensibilité perceptive.
fiche.population: 687 participants au total à travers 5 échantillons
fiche.intervention: Tâche de détection de changement respiratoire et questionnaires (MAIA)

fiche.conclusion: La sensibilité intéroceptive adaptative se manifeste par la confiance dans la tâche, indépendamment de la précision objective.

fiche.titre_court: Intéroception, MAIA et biais de confiance

titre: "The self" as shifting coalitions of brain systems in a continuous configuration space
resume: Philosophers and psychologists distinguish many forms of self, yet neuroimaging results often implicate a shared core in the cortical midline or insula. We propose self-related processing arises from shifting coalitions of distributed brain systems, without a core. In a meta-analysis of 912 neuroimaging publications, titles and abstracts clustered into ten forms, including autobiographical memory, body ownership and interoception. No single location was significant in all ten associated brain maps, although each occupied different parts and amounts of midline and insular territory. Their differences were distributed across the brain. Regional patterns varied with study context, corresponded selectively with aspects of consciousness and resembled maps of general functions. Brain patterns combined at continuously varying strengths predicted regions reported in held-out publications better than single patterns or on/off combinations. Self-related processing therefore has no core and arises from shifting coalitions of distributed brain systems whose graded contributions define a continuous configuration space.

titre: Hunger and Concentration in Daily Life: Inter-Individual Differences and Eating-Related Variation but No Robust Average Association
resume: Momentary reductions in concentration may affect daily functioning. In addition to external distractors, bodily signals might divert attention from ongoing tasks. Hunger might not only signal short dips in energy supply but also trigger distracting interoceptive sensations. We focus on hunger as a frequent sensation that is regularly regulated through food intake and therefore may display a complex relation to concentration. To test the relation between hunger and concentration, 64 participants in an experience sampling study reported their momentary concentration, hunger, and food intake six times daily for four weeks. Using Bayesian multilevel within between models, we assessed the hunger concentration association and, in exploratory analyses, whether this relation differed depending on prior food intake. We found no robust average hunger concentration association, with a Bayes Factor supporting the absence of a systematic population level within participant association. At the same time, the association varied considerably between individuals. Prior food intake did not clearly change the association overall. In exploratory meal-specific-analyses, more negative hunger concentration associations were estimated after breakfast and lunch compared with assessments without the respective meal. Thus, the momentary hunger concentration relation in daily life was characterised by considerable inter-individual differences and possible dependence on specific meal contexts. These findings suggest that everyday concentration may be shaped less by hunger per se than by individual differences and the context in which hunger occurs.

fiche.verdict: Il n'y a pas d'association globale robuste entre faim et concentration au quotidien, malgré de fortes variations interindividuelles.
fiche.population: 64 participants
fiche.intervention: Évaluation écologique momentanée (6 fois par jour pendant 4 semaines)
resultats_cles: Absence d'association globale moyenne entre faim et concentration (facteur de Bayes favorable à l'absence)

Associations faim-concentration plus négatives après le petit-déjeuner et le déjeuner

titre: Prevalence, Symptom Severity and Risk Factors Associated With Irritable Bowel Syndrome in MBBS Students of Nishtar Medical University, Multan
resume: Background: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits without structural abnormalities. Globally, its prevalence ranges from 10–15%, and in Asia from 6.8–33.3%. Medical students are at higher risk due to academic stress, poor sleep, and psychological factors. Studies report associations of IBS with anxiety, depression, physical and academic stress, sleep disturbances, and early life trauma. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence, subtypes, symptom severity, and associated factors of IBS among MBBS students at Nishtar Medical University, Multan.Methodology: This cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2024 in the Department of Community Medicine, Nishtar University Multan. Sample size (n = 78) was calculated using Epi Info sample size calculator with 95% confidence limits. MBBS students from first to final year were included; those with red flag symptoms or known organic gastrointestinal diseases were excluded. Ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Ethical Review Board. Data were collected via validated self-administered questionnaires, including socio-demographics, Rome IV criteria for IBS, IBS Symptom Severity Scale (SSS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), and Student Stress Inventory (SSI). Associations were analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression (p<0.05).Results: IBS prevalence was 39.7%, with mixed subtype (48.4%) and mild severity (51.6%) most common. Significant associations were observed with past history of IBS (p = 0.001), effect on grades (p = 0.010), physical stress (p = 0.0004), academic stress (p = 0.005), anxiety (p = 0.003), depression (p = 0.002), poor sleep (p = 0.014), physical abuse (p = 0.016), and emotional neglect (p = 0.019). Strongest associations were with past IBS history, poor sleep, and academic impact.Conclusion: IBS is common among medical students, with psychological and lifestyle factors significantly associated. Early identification of these factors may help reduce symptom burden in high-risk populations.
revue: Journal of Fatima Jinnah Medical University

titre: Sex-stratified immune signatures in irritable bowel syndrome suggest reduced neutrophil-associated transcriptional activity in males and altered interferon signalling in females
resume: Abstract Background Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastrointestinal disorder with a higher prevalence in females. While most transcriptomic studies have focused on gut mucosal biopsies, systemic transcriptional differences remain poorly understood. We investigated sex-stratified whole-blood transcriptome profiles in IBS using a cross-sectional observational design. Methods Whole-blood bulk RNA sequencing was performed on the DNBSEQ-G400 platform. Differential expression analysis was performed separately for males and females using DESeq2 (FDR < 0.05). Functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction analyses were performed using STRING database. Cell-type enrichment scores were estimated with xCell2. Transcription factor (TF) coordination network analysis was conducted using NetREm. In silico validation was performed using three independent publicly available RNA-seq datasets from small intestine, colon, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Results We identified sex-stratified transcriptional signatures, comprising 43 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in males (17 upregulated and 26 downregulated) and 289 DEGs in females (139 upregulated and 150 downregulated). In males, genes involved in neutrophil-mediated antibacterial responses were downregulated. In females, genes involved in antiviral defence and interferon signalling pathways were downregulated, whereas neutrophil-associated pathways showed increased activity. Transcription factor coordination analysis revealed widespread alterations in regulatory relationships, including both shared and sex-stratified TF–TF interactions. Cross-cohort comparisons revealed partial concordance across datasets, with both sexes overlapping primarily with small intestine data; males showed gene- and pathway-level overlap, whereas females showed gene-level overlap. Conclusions Whole-blood transcriptome profiling revealed distinct immune-related signatures in IBS, suggesting sex-stratified immune modulation in IBS pathophysiology.

titre: Disorders of gut-brain interaction as a risk factor for low adherence to pharmacotherapy for obesity. A review
resume: This review addresses the relationship between obesity and disorders of gut-brain interaction, as well as gastrointestinal adverse events arising during pharmacotherapy of obesity with incretin mimetics (semaglutide, tirzepatide). According to population-based studies, obesity is associated with an increased prevalence of disorders of gut-brain interaction, and the risk rises as body mass index increases. The high incidence of gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation) during therapy with incretin receptor agonists frequently leads to dose reduction or treatment discontinuation. The review discusses the concept of „motility support“ for incretin-based pharmacotherapy of obesity using trimebutine, a motility regulator with a modulating mode of action. The rationale draws on the results of randomized clinical trials and meta-analyses. Thus, personalized correction of gastrointestinal motility disorders may improve treatment tolerability and adherence; further investigation of this strategy will help define its place in clinical practice more precisely.

titre: THE GUT-BRAIN AXIS: MICROBIAL METABOLITES AND NEUROINFLAMMATION
resume: The gut–brain axis represents a complex network of bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system (CNS), in which metabolites and other bioactive compounds generated by intestinal microorganisms play essential signaling roles. This communication system involves several interconnected components, including the autonomic nervous system, vagal pathways, neuroendocrine signaling mechanisms, immune responses, and the intestinal mucosal barrier. Under physiological conditions, beneficial gut microorganisms convert dietary substrates into biologically active metabolites that contribute to immune regulation, metabolic balance, and cellular homeostasis. However, alterations in the composition and function of the intestinal microbiota, commonly referred to as dysbiosis, together with impaired intestinal barrier integrity, may facilitate the passage of bacterial endotoxins and pro-inflammatory mediators into systemic circulation.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Probiotics in neurodegenerative disorders
resume: Background:Neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), multiple sclerosis (MS), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), are associated with chronic neuroinflammation and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Increasing evidence suggests that modulation of the microbiota–gut–brain axis with probiotics may represent a novel therapeutic strategy. Aim:To summarize current evidence on the effects of probiotic supplementation in AD, PD, MS, and ALS, focusing on potential mechanisms of action and therapeutic outcomes. Material and methods: A review of scientific literature concerning the influence of gut microbiota on the nervous system through the microbiota-gut-brain axis was conducted. Clinical and preclinical studies evaluating the effectiveness of probiotic therapy in selected neurodegenerative diseases were analyzed. Results: Probiotic supplementation demonstrated beneficial effects across several neurodegenerative disorders. In AD, probiotics improved cognitive performance, reduced inflammatory markers, and attenuated oxidative stress. In PD, they alleviated gastrointestinal symptoms, improved bowel function, enhanced motor performance, and reduced systemic inflammation. In MS, probiotics decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, promoted anti-inflammatory immune responses, and increased brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels. Experimental ALS studies indicated restoration of gut microbiota, improved intestinal barrier integrity, delayed disease progression, and prolonged survival in animal models. Conclusion: Probiotics demonstrate promising therapeutic potential in treating neurodegenerative diseases through modulation of gut microbiota and influence on the gut-brain axis. However, further clinical studies are necessary to confirm their clinical significance and biological effects.
revue: Journal of Education Health and Sport

titre: The nicotine–Parkinson paradox and molecular hydrogen from the gut microbiome
resume: The inverse association between tobacco smoking and Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, known as the smoking paradox, is one of the most consistent yet unexplained findings in neuroepidemiology. We propose that it may originate from the gut microbiome, specifically from the modulation of endogenous molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) production and its downstream signaling along the gut-brain axis, which could explain why transdermal nicotine fails where smoking protects. Despite robust evidence showing 32%–60% risk reduction in smokers, clinical trials with nicotine replacement therapy have failed to demonstrate disease-modifying effects. While preclinical studies have identified direct neuroprotective mechanisms of nicotine via nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) suppression, and anti-inflammatory pathways, these mechanisms alone cannot explain the differences between transdermal nicotine and smoking, including passive exposure. A key distinction is that smoking delivers nicotine and smoke condensates via the oropharyngeal and gastrointestinal route, directly contacting the intestinal mucosa and its resident microbiota, whereas transdermal patches bypass the gut entirely. PD patients consistently exhibit depletion of butyrate-producing and H 2 -generating bacteria alongside enrichment of hydrogen sulfide-producing Desulfovibrio species. Smokers, conversely, harbor increased abundance of Prevotella and Bacteroides , taxa equipped with group B [FeFe]-hydrogenases capable of substantial H 2 production. Endogenous H 2 is thought to promote butyrate synthesis, stabilize intestinal barrier function, and reduce systemic inflammation via the gut-brain axis. Molecular hydrogen has anti-inflammatory and mitochondria-protective effects, although the selective antioxidant mechanism originally proposed for it remains debated. We suggest that the application of exogenous molecular hydrogen, deliverable via hydrogen-enriched water, inhalation, or oral formulations designed for colonic release, may offer a novel preventive strategy without tobacco's toxicity. Such a strategy could simultaneously engage direct neuroprotective pathways and microbiome-mediated gut-brain signaling during the critical presymptomatic window of neurodegeneration.

titre: LGALS1-Associated Candidate Myeloid Signature and In Silico Regulatory Analysis in Ulcerative Colitis: A Bioinformatics Study
resume: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) substantially impairs patients’ quality of life and increases the risk of colorectal carcinogenesis. However, its precise molecular pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. Methods: Bioinformatic tools and methods were used to achieve the objectives of this study. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data to comprehensively identify key molecular determinants underlying UC. scPagwas and Scissor analyses were performed to identify the critical cell subpopulations. Subsequently, single-cell Mendelian randomization (scMR) analysis was applied to prioritize the cell-type-specific putative causal genes. The candidate genes were further refined using univariate and multivariate regression analyses. The resulting gene set was incorporated into a machine-learning-based feature gene model, with model interpretability rigorously assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAPs). Mechanistically, virtual knockout perturbation analysis (scTenifoldKnk) was complemented by CellOracle, CellChat, and pseudotime trajectory analyses. Drug2cell analysis was employed to evaluate the cell-type-specific drug activity of multiple compounds. Results: Myeloid cells emerged as the predominant pathogenic cell subgroup in UC, as identified by scPagwas and Scissor analyses. scMR analysis prioritized 69 myeloid cell-specific putative causal genes associated with UC. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses narrowed this list to four candidate genes. Among them, a three-gene signature comprising galectin 1 (LGALS1), ribosomal protein S25 (RPS25), and N-acylethanolamine acid amidase (NAAA) reached an apparent cross-validated AUC of 0.992 in the training cohort. SHAP interpretation confirmed LGALS1 as the most influential feature in the model. Mechanistic investigations predicted that LGALS1 plays a potential role in modulating myeloid cell differentiation and immune homeostasis in UC. Furthermore, Drug2cell gave higher target-expression-based scores for alpidem, bosutinib and gefitinib in LGALS1-positive monocytes (LGALS1+mono). Conclusions: Collectively, this computational study identifies a candidate three-gene signature (LGALS1, RPS25 and NAAA) and generates hypotheses about LGALS1 in monocyte differentiation in UC.
