titre: Gut microbiome alterations and depression in patients with diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and narrative synthesis of the gut-metabolic-brain axis
resume: Background Diabetes mellitus and depression frequently coexist and may share inflammatory, metabolic, neuroendocrine, and behavioral pathways. The intestinal microbiome may represent a biological interface linking metabolic dysfunction with depressive symptoms, but direct human evidence in populations with diabetes remains limited. Objective To systematically synthesize direct human evidence on intestinal microbiome alterations associated with depression or depressive symptoms among people with diabetes and interpret the findings within a gut-metabolic-brain axis framework. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020, with search reporting informed by PRISMA-S. Eight databases were searched through August 27, 2026, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, Google Scholar, Research4Life/HINARI, reference lists, and citation tracking. Eligible studies assessed diabetes, depression or depressive symptoms, and intestinal/fecal microbiome data within the same participant sample. Contextual studies not meeting these criteria were considered separately. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively rather than by meta-analysis. Results Database searches identified 1,293 records, with 61 additional unique records from ClinicalTrials.gov. After removing 497 duplicates, 857 records were screened, 94 full-text reports were assessed, and five eligible reports met the eligibility criteria. Three involved type 1 diabetes populations, while two were randomized dietary intervention studies in type 2 diabetes. Across studies, depression or depressive symptoms were associated with differences in intestinal microbial composition and microbiome-related metabolic or neurobiological measures; however, findings varied considerably according to study design, population, depression assessment, and microbiome methodology. Conclusion Direct human evidence suggests that depression or depressive symptoms in people with diabetes may be associated with alterations in the intestinal microbiome and related metabolic and neurobiological measures. However, the direct evidence base remains small and heterogeneous, and the available findings are better regarded as hypothesis-generating biological signals than evidence of a consistent microbial signature or causal microbiome-mediated pathway. Larger longitudinal, multi-omics, and intervention studies using standardized microbiome methods, validated depression measures, rigorous confounder adjustment, and mediation analyses are needed.

titre: The interoceptive-metabolic fear loop: linking stress physiology, metabolic health, aging, exercise, and fear memory
resume: Fear memory is usually modelled in terms of neural circuits centred on the amygdala, hippocampus, and prefrontal cortex, yet fear is acquired, retrieved, and extinguished in a body whose autonomic, endocrine, metabolic, and inflammatory state changes during threat. This Perspective proposes the Interoceptive-Metabolic Fear Loop, in which the physiological configuration present during threat becomes part of the context of fear learning, so that later states resembling it facilitate retrieval of threat associations and renew the state that sustains them. Learning theory already treats internal states as contexts; the loop specifies the physiological state itself as a context whose availability at retrieval may be shaped by systemic health, aging, and fitness. Two mechanisms conflated in current designs are distinguished. Under state congruence, fear returns because the internal state at test matches the acquisition state; under state modulation, arousal at test nonspecifically impairs extinction retrieval. A design that separates them is proposed, manipulating state at extinction and test while quantifying similarity to the measured acquisition state. Physiological state flexibility, the capacity to enter mobilization and return efficiently toward baseline, is introduced as an integrative construct hypothesized to be reduced by metabolic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and aging, and enhanced by exercise. Exercise is reframed as physiological relearning: repeated safe exposure to the bodily signature of anxiety combined with metabolic and autonomic adaptation. Five falsifiable predictions link internal-state congruence, physiological flexibility, metabolic health, biological age, and exercise to extinction retention and return of fear.

titre: STARLI · MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜; 讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. FAMILY 06 | BREATHING, DANTIAN AND INTEROCEPTION Research Working Edition v1.0 · Scientific & Technical Notebook · 17 November 2026 Five formal flagship titles and Zenodo-ready scientific introductions F026 | Dantian-Focused Attention and Abdominal Interoception at the Limit This prospective, nonclinical research flagship investigates dantian-focused attention, abdominal localization and independently coded interoceptive discrimination with a preregistered primary outcome of abdominal interoceptive localization error after concealed somatic reference mapping (cm). Its three-part candidate mechanism is controlled practice exposure × independent physical or behavioral witness × uncertainty-aware causal comparison. A rigorous study would use masked somatic cue location, anatomical photo registration, belt waveform and raw response-coordinate trace while giving time-matched neutral abdominal attention and concealed non-dantian body regions an equal chance to explain the result. Competing accounts include expectation, somatosensory cue leakage, visceral signal strength, attention allocation and drawing anchor bias. The decisive boundary is that dantian names are inherited concepts; a location judgment alone cannot establish an invisible anatomical energy centre. No observed efficacy, uniquely physical dantian organ or external qi field is claimed in this working edition. F027 | Diaphragmatic Breathing and Heart Rate Variability Regulation at the Limit This prospective, nonclinical research flagship investigates diaphragmatic motion, respiration-driven heart-rate oscillation and paced-breathing comparison with a preregistered primary outcome of within-person respiration-associated RMSSD change under matched ECG segment length (ms). Its three-part candidate mechanism is controlled practice exposure × independent physical or behavioral witness × uncertainty-aware causal comparison. A rigorous study would use ECG R-peak intervals, simultaneous respiratory belt or flow, posture log and RR artifact ledger while giving matched-pace breathing at equal volume without dantian language and a spontaneous-breath reference an equal chance to explain the result. Competing accounts include respiratory rate and tidal volume, posture, ECG artifact, mean heart rate, expectancy and recording duration. The decisive boundary is that an immediate HRV rise does not establish durable benefit, new qi physics or a specific practice effect. No observed efficacy, uniquely physical dantian organ or external qi field is claimed in this working edition. F028 | Breath Pauses and Carbon Dioxide Physiology at the Limit This prospective, nonclinical research flagship investigates voluntary respiratory pause reports versus measured end-tidal carbon dioxide recovery dynamics with a preregistered primary outcome of modeled post-event return time of end-tidal carbon dioxide to a preregistered reference window (s). Its three-part candidate mechanism is controlled practice exposure × independent physical or behavioral witness × uncertainty-aware causal comparison. A rigorous study would use time-aligned capnography waveform, reference-gas calibration, respiratory flow, exhalation validity and safety ledger while giving resting spontaneous-respiration controls and externally supplied synthetic CO2 transients; avoid unsupervised provocation an equal chance to explain the result. Competing accounts include pre-event ventilation, sample-line delay, nasal cannula leaks, lung volume, motion artifacts and individual variability. The decisive boundary is that the synthetic pause axis is not a human protocol; no forced breath holding or respiratory challenge is advised. No observed efficacy, uniquely physical dantian organ or external qi field is claimed in this working edition. F029 | Separating Respiratory Imagery from Respiratory Mechanics at the Limit This prospective, nonclinical research flagship investigates respiratory imagery, covert muscular excursion and actual gas-flow discrimination with a preregistered primary outcome of held-out AUC of blinded imagery-versus-actual-respiration task labels under equal cue and movement budgets (0-1). Its three-part candidate mechanism is controlled practice exposure × independent physical or behavioral witness × uncertainty-aware causal comparison. titre: De la alexitimia a la terapia de la ternura: Fenomenología del dolor somático, interocepción atípica y autorregulación en el trauma complejo y la triple excepcionalidad (3e)
resume: Español:"Cuando al cuerpo se le prohíbe llorar hacia afuera, aprende a hablar en un lenguaje invisible de memoria, calambres y ternura silenciosa." — Reflexión introspectiva de la autora. El presente estudio autoetnográfico y neurofenomenológico analiza la relación entre la alexitimia, la interocepción atípica y la somatización del dolor en perfiles con triple excepcionalidad (altas capacidades, autismo y TDAH) e historial de trauma complejo (TEPT-C). Se examina cómo la desconexión forzosa de las señales corporales —producto del enmascaramiento social y la invalidación temprana— deriva en manifestaciones físicas agudas, incluyendo dolor somático difuso ("miembro fantasma"), bloqueos motores y crisis de desregulación autonómica. Finalmente, se propone un modelo de autorregulación basado en la integración entre la Terapia Cognitivo-Conductual (TCC), el movimiento somático y la "Terapia de la Ternura" como puente entre la mente adulta que investiga y la memoria emocional infantil. Incluye versión en español e inglés. English:"When the body is forbidden from crying outward, it learns to speak in an invisible language of memory, cramps, and silent tenderness." — Introspective reflection by the author. This autoethnographic and neurophenomenological study analyzes the relationship between alexithymia, atypical interoception, and pain somatization in thrice-exceptional profiles (giftedness, autism, and ADHD) with a history of complex trauma (C-PTSD). It examines how the forced disconnection from bodily signals—resulting from social masking and early invalidation—leads to acute physical manifestations, including diffuse somatic pain ("phantom limb"), motor blocks, and autonomic dysregulation crises. Finally, it proposes a self-regulation model based on the integration of Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT), somatic movement, and "Tenderness Therapy" as a bridge between the researching adult mind and childhood emotional memory. Includes both Spanish and English versions.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Effects of mindfulness-based interventions on sport performance and psychological outcomes in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
resume: Background and objective Athletes use mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) as part of psychological preparation, but their effects on sport performance and related psychological outcomes remain uncertain. This review synthesised controlled trial evidence and explored potential sources of variation across programmes and sporting contexts. Methods Six databases were searched in August 2025: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, PsycINFO via EBSCOhost, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus. The prespecified design criterion was a randomised controlled trial. Between-group standardised mean differences (SMDs) were pooled using random-effects models; exploratory subgroups considered intervention category, sport type, competitive level, and session duration. Results The review included 21 studies reported to meet the trial criteria, with 920 participants in the study-characteristics table. Between-group estimates favoured MBIs for mindfulness (SMD 0.77, 95% CI 0.43–1.12), flow (0.87, 0.25–1.48), and sport performance (0.94, 0.56–1.32), and for lower anxiety (−1.13, −1.99 to −0.27). The stress estimate included no effect (−1.11, −2.32–0.10), as did the exploratory emotion-related estimate (1.05, −0.51–2.62). Mental toughness was inconclusive, with a rounded lower confidence limit at zero (1.18, 0.00–2.35; p = 0.05). Heterogeneity was substantial ( I 2 67%–89%). No subgroup interaction provided clear evidence that the effects on performance differed between categories. Conclusion MBIs may support athletes’ psychological preparation and sport performance, but the evidence does not establish an optimal programme or session duration. Benefits for stress, emotion-related outcomes, and mental toughness remain uncertain. Practical use should be tailored to the athlete and evaluated against clearly defined sporting goals. Systematic review registration PROSPERO under CRD420251004127. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251004127 .

titre: Stress, Anxiety and Depression among Nursing Students: A Systematic Review of Prevalence, Associated Factors and Academic Consequences
resume: Background: Nursing students face demanding coursework and supervised clinical practice at the same time, which exposes them to stress, anxiety and depression. Published prevalence estimates vary widely, and the academic consequences of distress are seldom examined together with prevalence, particularly in India. Objective: To synthesize published evidence on (1) the prevalence of stress, anxiety and depression among nursing students, (2) the factors associated with these conditions, and (3) their academic and professional consequences. Methods: This systematic review was reported according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, PsycINFO, Web of Science and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2010 and October 2026, without geographic restriction. Review-level evidence (systematic reviews, meta-analyses and umbrella reviews) and primary studies that used validated screening tools were included. Because primary studies overlap across reviews, prevalence estimates from reviews were tabulated as reported and not re-pooled; comparable Indian primary studies were pooled with a random-effects model. Results: Thirty sources were included (18 review-level and 12 primary studies, seven of them Indian). Pooled estimates in meta-analyses were about 29% to 38% for depression, 29% to 34% for anxiety and 27% to 52% for stress, with very high heterogeneity, and they were highest during the COVID-19 pandemic and varied with instrument and cut-off. In three comparable Indian studies using the DASS (n = 642), pooled prevalence was 43.2% (95% CI 31.9-54.9) for depression, 55.2% (95% CI 47.0-63.2) for anxiety and 35.1% (95% CI 27.9-42.7) for stress. Academic workload, clinical placement demands, financial difficulty and poor sleep were the main risk factors, and resilience, social support and effective coping were protective. Consequences included lower perceived academic achievement, burnout and intention to leave, whereas associations with grade point average were inconsistent. Mindfulness-based interventions showed benefit, but the evidence is of limited quality. Conclusions: Stress, anxiety and depression are common among nursing students in the included evidence and are linked to reduced engagement and burnout. Nursing colleges should provide routine validated screening, accessible counselling and supportive clinical placements, and future research, especially in India, should use standardised instruments, longitudinal designs and well-designed trials.
revue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

titre: RELAX-ECT: Reducing Emotional Load and Anxiety before ECT - a randomized controlled feasibility trial
resume: RELAX-ECT (Reducing Emotional Load and Anxiety before ECT; DRKS00038579) is a single-center, randomized controlled feasibility trial with a delayed-start design, conducted at the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin (Campus Benjamin Franklin). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an effective and safe treatment for severe depression, yet many patients experience considerable anticipatory anxiety, particularly while waiting for the procedure. This anxiety may reduce treatment acceptance and complicate anesthesia induction and treatment delivery. The trial investigates whether a brief (10-minute) guided breath-focused mindfulness meditation reduces pre-treatment anxiety in patients with unipolar or bipolar depression scheduled for ECT. Participants are randomized 1:1 (paRANDies tool). The experimental group is first guided through the meditation on the ward and then listens to the audio recording via headphones in the preparation room immediately before the first ECT session. The control group receives treatment as usual before the first session and receives the intervention from the second session onward (delayed start). Treating psychiatrists and anesthesiologists are blinded to group allocation. The trial is a feasibility study, and its principal aim is effect-size estimation rather than confirmatory hypothesis testing. Subjective anxiety (visual analogue scale, VAS) immediately before the first ECT session is assessed alongside physiological candidate endpoints: propofol dose required for anesthesia induction, seizure duration, heart rate and blood pressure. These are examined in parallel to identify the most informative and sensitive endpoint for a future, adequately powered confirmatory multicenter trial. Feasibility endpoints include time spent in the treatment room (compared with non-study ECT patients), a staff survey on disruption and workload, and a patient survey on perceived burden. Exploratory analyses address depression severity (QIDS), state/trait anxiety, childhood trauma (CTQ), daily stressors, diagnosis (unipolar vs. bipolar) and medication effects. The primary analysis uses linear mixed models (Group × Time interaction, random intercept per participant, QIDS as covariate) on the intention-to-treat set, with a repeated-measures ANOVA and a per-protocol analysis as sensitivity checks. Because of the exploratory nature of the trial, no correction for multiple testing is applied, and all p-values are interpreted descriptively. The original target sample size was N = 52 (G*Power, d = 0.4, α = .05, power = .80); recruitment has been revised to n = 40. Expected outcomes: We expect the meditation to reduce pre-ECT anxiety relative to treatment as usual, and possibly to lower sympathetic arousal (heart rate, blood pressure) and propofol requirements. These expectations are exploratory. The main deliverables are effect-size estimates with 95% confidence intervals across all candidate endpoints, and an assessment of acceptability and feasibility (e.g., consent rate, dropout, procedural burden). Together these will inform the design and primary endpoint of a confirmatory trial.

titre: From antidepressants to psychedelics: revisiting the pharmacology of so-called serotoninergic treatments
resume: Recent years have seen a resurgence of interest in serotoninergic psychedelics as potential treatment for diverse psychiatric disorders. Here, we will delve into the molecular mechanisms of drugs used to treat depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), with implications on the mechanism of action of so-called ''serotoninergic'' psychedelics as well as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). In particular, we argue that the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of SSRIs suggest that the inhibition of the serotonin transporter (SERT) alone does not provide a comprehensive account of their clinical effects. On the contrary, the SSRI posology required to treat depression and OCD is consistent with their major molecular target(s) displaying an SSRI affinity much lower than SERT. Such is the case for the tyrosine receptor kinase B (TrkB), recently described as a putative target for drugs with antidepressant effects. TrkB might thus provide a unifying framework for understanding the therapeutic effects of antidepressant drugs. We finally discuss the pharmacological implications of this hypothesis on the therapeutical potential of psychedelics.

fiche.verdict: L'inhibition du SERT seule n'explique pas l'effet clinique des ISRS, suggérant l'implication d'autres cibles comme TrkB.
resultats_cles: L'affinité des ISRS pour SERT ne suffit pas à rendre compte de leur posologie clinique.
Implication possible du récepteur TrkB dans les effets antidépresseurs.

fiche.conclusion: La réévaluation pharmacologique des traitements sérotoninergiques suggère des mécanismes d'action élargis au-delà du SERT.

titre: Role of a Probiotic Mixture on Gut Microbiota Repopulation and Abdominal Symptoms Relief After Colonscopy in Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) Patients
resume: The goal of this open-label, pilot study, was to evaluate the impact of bowel preparation on IBS patients' gut microbiota, their recovery within thirty days, and whether the probiotic mixture administration contained in Lactichoc® altered their recovery from spontaneous resilience, while simultaneously monitoring the course of gastrointestinal symptoms. The primary objective of our study is to evaluate whether the administration of this probiotics modifies the recovery of the intestinal microbiota after colonoscopy preparation in patients with IBS in terms of speed (kinetics) and extent of recovery, compared to the spontaneous recovery observed in the control group. The secondary objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of probiotics in improving gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life (GIQLI questionnaire) and stool consistency (Bristol scale), in patients with IBS undergoing colonoscopy, compared to an untreated control group.

titre: Effects of Individualized Resting-State fMRI-Guided Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation on Depressive and Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Sham-Controlled Trial
resume: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of individualized intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) on depressive and gastrointestinal symptoms in patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and depressive symptoms. A total of 60 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to active or sham stimulation. Individualized stimulation targets within the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) will be identified using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Participants will receive 10 stimulation sessions over two weeks. Clinical assessments and multimodal brain MRI will be performed at baseline and at the end of Week 2. The primary outcome will be the change in depressive symptom severity measured by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). An optional ancillary study involving paired stool sample collection at baseline and Week 2 is planned to support future exploratory investigations of gut microbiota and its associations with clinical symptoms and brain network characteristics. This ancillary component will be implemented only after the relevant ethics approval and additional informed consent have been obtained.
auteurs: The Affiliated Hospital of Hangzhou Normal University

titre: Effect of Bifidobacterium Longum Subsp. Longum Combination Intervention on Stress Status and Related Health Outcomes: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Study
resume: This study is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial designed to evaluate the effects of a combination of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. longum strains on stress-related health outcomes in adults. The study plans to enroll 126 adults experiencing stress-related problems, who will be randomly assigned in equal proportions to either the probiotic group or the placebo group and will receive the assigned intervention for 8 weeks. Participants will complete the scheduled study visits and assessments. The study will systematically evaluate the principal health concerns of young adults experiencing high levels of stress through multiple approaches, including subjective questionnaire assessments, biological sample testing, and gut microbiome analysis. The main assessments will include a comparison of changes in stress status before and after the intervention between the probiotic and placebo groups using validated psychological assessment instruments. The effects of the intervention on sleep quality, quality of life, and related emotional states will also be evaluated. Sleep quality and quality of life will be assessed using validated assessment instruments. To further investigate the potential biological mechanisms, stool samples will be collected from participants for gut microbiome metagenomic analysis to characterize changes in microbial composition and functional features. Laboratory-based assays will also be used to measure stress-, immune-, and inflammation-related biomarkers. This study is expected to provide preliminary evidence supporting the clinical application of microbiota-targeted interventions based on modulation of the gut-brain axis in populations experiencing high levels of stress.

titre: Revolutionary Concept of X-biotics for Correcting Disease-associated Microbiota Compositions: Focus on Atopic, Gastrointestinal, Neurological, and Metabolic Disease: Study the Mechanism and Effectiveness of Probiotics on Atopic Dermatitis
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether probiotics isolated from breast milk and healthy infant feces can reduce the severity of atopic dermatitis (eczema) in children aged 3 to 18 years with moderate-to-severe disease. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Does taking the probiotic capsule twice daily for 12 weeks reduce eczema severity, measured by the EASI SCORAD? * Does the probiotic improve quality of life, blood markers of allergic inflammation (IgE, histamine, IL-31, T-cell subsets), and gut microbiota composition? Researchers will compare the probiotic to a placebo capsule that looks the same but contains no probiotic bacteria. Participants will: * Take one capsule twice daily for 12 weeks, in addition to their usual atopic dermatitis treatment * Complete the PO-SCORAD and a quality-of-life questionnaire at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8 and 12 * Provide stool samples at baseline and weeks 4 and 12, and a 10 mL blood sample at baseline and week 12.

titre: Effects of Increasing the Dose of Rumination-Targeted Intervention on Mindfulness-Based Intervention for Emotional Distress: A Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: This study tests whether adding a rumination-focused training module to an 8-week online mindfulness program helps reduce emotional distress and repetitive negative thinking (rumination) more than the mindfulness program on its own. When people feel distressed, many get caught in cycles of repeatedly going over worries or upsetting experiences-a habit called rumination. This study aims to find out whether teaching specific skills to notice and respond helpfully to rumination, in addition to a standard mindfulness program, leads to better outcomes. About 150 Chinese adults aged 18 to 65 who report elevated emotional distress and elevated rumination will take part. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) a standard online mindfulness program (Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress, MIED); (2) the same mindfulness program with an added rumination-targeted module; or (3) a wait-list control group that is offered the standard mindfulness program free of charge after the study period. The programs run for 8 weeks. All participants complete the same set of questionnaires at four time points: before starting, around weeks 3 and 5, and within 7 days after the program ends. The main outcome is emotional distress, measured with the K10 scale. Rumination, depression, anxiety, and mindfulness are also measured. The results will help clarify whether adding rumination-focused training is feasible and beneficial, and whether earlier reductions in rumination help explain later improvements in emotional distress. The study does not promise a cure or guaranteed individual improvement.

titre: Study of Traditional Chinese Medicine Augmentation Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder With Nonresponse to Initial Treatment
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a psychiatric disorder characterized by recurrent intrusive obsessive thoughts, urges, and ritualized compulsive behaviors. OCD often follows a chronic and protracted course with a high risk of relapse and is frequently accompanied by comorbid anxiety, depression, and other negative emotional symptoms, resulting in substantial impairment in occupational functioning, interpersonal relationships, and family and social functioning.Integrative treatment combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Western medicine may help address several limitations of conventional monotherapy, including suboptimal treatment response rates, medication-related adverse effects, the limited diversity of available therapeutic approaches, and insufficiently individualized treatment strategies, thereby offering potential clinical benefits.Chaixia Dingzhi Powder, the investigational Chinese herbal formula used in this study, was developed based on the formulation principles of two classical TCM prescriptions, Xiaoyao San (Free and Easy Wanderer Powder), documented in the Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang (Formulary of the Pharmacy Service for Benefiting the People in the Taiping Era), and Banxia Houpo Tang (Pinellia and Magnolia Bark Decoction), recorded in the Jingui Yaolue (Essentials from the Golden Cabinet). The formula was further modified according to the TCM pathophysiological characteristics of the target population, particularly liver qi stagnation with spleen deficiency, impaired qi movement, and the interaction of phlegm and qi stagnation.Therefore, this study aims to further investigate the efficacy and safety of Chaixia Dingzhi Powder as an adjunctive traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) who have demonstrated nonresponse to initial SSRI treatment, while maintaining their existing SSRI therapy at an adequate therapeutic dose or the maximum tolerated dose.

titre: The gut microbiome is associated with structural and functional brain alterations in adolescents with social anxiety disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Social anxiety disorder (SAD) commonly emerges in childhood or early adolescence and is associated with persistent impairments in social and emotional functioning. Although structural and functional brain abnormalities have been reported in SAD, the potential involvement of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in adolescent SAD remains poorly understood. AIMS: To investigate gut microbiota composition, predicted microbial functional pathways and multimodal brain alterations in adolescents with SAD, and to examine microbiome-brain associations and their exploratory discriminative value. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 48 adolescents (31 with SAD and 17 healthy controls [HCs]) with complete clinical, faecal and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. Diagnoses were established using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview for Children and Adolescents interviews and Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition-based clinical review. Participants underwent psychological assessment, faecal 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with linear discriminant analysis effect size and Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States, version 2 analyses and multimodal MRI including structural measures and resting-state functional indices. Partial correlations were used to assess microbiome-brain associations within the SAD group, and exploratory logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed for internal validation. RESULTS: Adolescents with SAD had significantly higher scores for social anxiety, general anxiety, depressive symptoms and fear of negative evaluation. The SAD group showed enrichment of Roseburia, Parasutterella and Clostridium sensu stricto 1, whereas Prevotella, Collinsella and Saccharimonadales were enriched in HCs; predicted microbial pathways also differed between groups. Neuroimaging analyses identified nominal differences in multiple structural and functional measures involving the anterior cingulate, caudal middle frontal, entorhinal and posterior cingulate regions, among others. Within the SAD group, several differential microbial genera were associated with MRI-derived measures. In exploratory internal validation, Clostridium sensu stricto 1 showed the highest discriminative performance among microbial markers (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.852), whereas right parahippocampal regional homogeneity showed the highest performance among MRI markers (AUC = 0.871). CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents with SAD showed altered gut microbial composition, predicted microbial functional changes and widespread multimodal brain abnormalities, together with microbiome-brain associations in regions relevant to emotion regulation, fear-related memory and self-referential processing. These findings support a role for microbiota-gut-brain dysregulation in adolescent SAD and suggest that integrated microbiome and neuroimaging features may represent preliminary candidate markers that require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies.

titre: Latent Profiles and Network Characteristics of Alexithymia Among Undergraduate Nursing Students
resume: BACKGROUND: Alexithymia is prevalent among nursing students and significantly impairs their psychological well-being. While the overall burden of this condition is well-documented, prior studies have predominantly focused on variable-centered prevalence rates, overlooking the latent heterogeneity of alexithymic traits in this population. This study employed latent profile analysis (LPA) to examine the heterogeneity of alexithymia among undergraduate nursing students by identifying subgroups with distinct symptom patterns. Subsequently, factors associated with subgroup membership were explored, and symptom network characteristics were analyzed within each latent profile. METHODS: This cross-sectional study recruited 1434 undergraduate nursing students from 10 Chinese universities using an online convenience sampling strategy. Participants completed an electronic survey assessing sociodemographic characteristics, alexithymia, childhood trauma (CT), and physical activity. Data were analyzed using LPA to identify subgroups, multinomial logistic regression to determine predictors, and network analysis to map symptom interconnections. RESULTS: LPA identified three distinct subgroups: low alexithymia group (42.259%), moderate alexithymia group (26.569%), and hyperalexithymia group (31.172%). According to the multinomial logistic regression analysis, female gender, CT, and low professional interest were identified as the primary predictors of higher alexithymia risk. Crucially, network analysis revealed different central nodes across the profiles. Specifically, difficulty identifying feelings (Toronto Alexithymia Scale [TAS]-II) was the central hub in the moderate alexithymia group, while lack of fantasy (TAS-III) was the core node in the hyperalexithymia group. CONCLUSION: Alexithymia in undergraduate nursing students exhibits substantial heterogeneity, manifesting as three distinct profiles. By identifying the predictors and central symptoms of each subgroup, this study provides an empirical foundation for targeted psychological support. These findings can help nursing educators implement tailored interventions to address the specific vulnerabilities of each profile.

titre: Differential neural mechanisms of hypnosis and progressive muscle relaxation in reducing social anxiety symptoms
resume: BACKGROUND: Hypnosis (HYP) and progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) are effective for social anxiety disorder (SAD), but their neural mechanisms remain unclear. This study compared their effects on brain activity and connectivity during emotional face processing. METHODS: Forty-five participants with high social anxiety symptoms were randomized to HYP (n = 24) or PMR (n = 21) and assessed before and after 6 sessions using the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale and fMRI. 23 matched healthy controls (HC) served as baseline controls. Brain activation and generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analyses were conducted. RESULTS: At baseline, SAD group versus HC showed higher LSAS scores, slower emotional face RTs, and reduced activation in occipital, postcentral, prefrontal/temporal regions, caudate, putamen, and thalamus. After intervention, both groups had lower LSAS scores. PMR increased RTs while HYP did not. HYP selectively decreased activation in the left superior frontal gyrus (lSFG) for negative stimuli and in the right superior temporal gyrus for neutral stimuli, whereas PMR showed no such effects. Both interventions reduced activation in the caudate, putamen, and thalamus. gPPI revealed that HYP increased lSFG-posterior cingulate cortex connectivity under negative stimuli, while PMR decreased this connectivity. CONCLUSIONS: Both interventions alleviated SAD symptoms via limbic modulation; however, HYP more strongly targeted fronto-temporal regions and cognitive-attentional networks, suggesting partially distinct neural mechanisms from PMR. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1900022651).

titre: Feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of blended modality online parent training in exposure and response-prevention (ERP) for children with OCD
resume: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the co-design, feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a brief, intensive, parent-led cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention (CBT-ERP) intervention delivered via a blended digital modality. METHOD: An open pilot case series (N = 4) involved families of children aged 7-14 years diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The intervention comprised four self-guided web-based modules, four therapist-led videoconference group sessions, and a three-week maintenance phase with brief therapist check-ins. Feasibility was assessed through adherence, acceptability through usability, satisfaction, and recommendation ratings, and preliminary outcomes through clinician-, parent-, and child-reported OCD severity. . RESULTS: Findings indicated high feasibility and acceptability, with strong intervention adherence and usability ratings within the "best imaginable" range. Parents reported high satisfaction, particularly with therapist-led sessions. OCD symptom severity decreased across measures, with 50% of participants no longer meeting diagnostic criteria at post-treatment, although changes were not statistically significant. Family accommodation remained relatively stable. CONCLUSIONS: Findings provide preliminary support for the feasibility and acceptability of blended, parent-led CBT-ERP as a potentially scalable intervention for paediatric OCD. However, the small sample and uncontrolled design warrant cautious interpretation and further evaluation in larger controlled trials.

titre: Variant Foramina of the Orbital Apex: Osteological Evaluation and Systematic Review
resume: The orbital apex contains several anatomical variations that can significantly impact surgical procedures involving the orbit and skull base. Among these anatomical variants, the metoptic canal (MC), Warwick's foramen (WF), and optic canal duplication (OCD) may serve as important conduits for neurovascular elements. Despite their clinical relevance, these variant structures are inconsistently described in the literature, and data on their incidence and morphology remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, morphology, and anatomical relationships of these accessory orbital foramina. A total of 110 adult dry skulls and 15 isolated sphenoid bones from the department of human anatomy were examined. The size, shape, and position of any MCs, WF, or OCDs present were recorded. Morphometric assessments were performed on these foramina as well as the optic canal, optic strut, and superior orbital fissure. A systematic review of relevant studies was also conducted for comparative analysis. Accessory orbital foramina were identified in 20 of the 125 specimens (17.6%). OCD was present in five cases (4%), MC in eleven cases (8.8%), and WF in eight cases (6.4%). Statistical analysis revealed that the optic strut and superior orbital fissure were significantly wider in skulls displaying OCD. In addition, orbits with WF were associated with shorter superior orbital fissures compared to non-variant orbits. The systematic review identified 35 relevant studies for analysis. This study highlights the considerable anatomical variability of accessory orbital foramina and the need for awareness during surgical dissection. Features such as increased size of the optic strut and reduced size of the superior orbital fissure can raise the suspicion of a variant foramen in the orbital apex.

titre: The Mint Scale: A Fresh Validation of the Multimodal Interoception Questionnaire and Comparison to the MAIA, BPQ and IAS
resume: Interoception, the sensing of the body's internal state, is an important component of homeostatic and allostatic regulation with wide-ranging implications for mental and physical health, yet its measurement is hindered by tools with conceptual and psychometric issues. To address these limitations, we developed and validated the Multimodal Interoception Questionnaire (Mint). In Study 1 (N=559), a comprehensive item pool using a novel "modality-by-context" framework was generated and then reduced using psychometric network analysis. In Study 2 (N=737), we validated the Mint in an independent sample, establishing its structure, comparing its predictive power against established interoception questionnaires (MAIA-2, BPQ, IAS), and across a wide range of clinical and cognitive outcomes. This rigorous process yielded a 33-item scale with a stable hierarchical structure comprising three metaclusters (Interoceptive Deficit, Interoceptive Awareness, Visceroception) and 11 distinct facets. The Mint demonstrated superior criterion validity, consistently outperforming existing scales in predicting outcomes tied to altered bodily perception, including alexithymia, ADHD, autism, and somatic symptom clusters. The Mint offers a psychometrically robust and nuanced measure of self-reported interoception that integrates and extends existing scales, providing researchers and clinicians with a practical and readily usable tool to investigate the role of bodily sensations in health and disease.

titre: Efficacy and Safety of Ondansetron for Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome: an Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
resume: Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ondansetron for diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) and update the randomized evidence following the 2023 TRITON meta-analysis. Methods: An updated systematic review of randomized controlled trials in adults with Rome III-or IV-defined IBS-D was conducted. Full-text placebo-controlled trials of ≥4 w were eligible. The primary quantitative outcome was study-defined stool-consistency response. Three parallel-group trials were pooled in Review Manager 5.4.1 using a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratio (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI). The crossover trial by Garsed et al. was included qualitatively but excluded from the primary independent-arm meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2. Results: Four randomized controlled trials were included, of which three parallel-group trials involving 304 participants contributed to the meta-analysis. Stool-consistency response occurred in 91/161 participants receiving ondansetron and 53/143 receiving placebo/control. Ondansetron significantly improved stool-consistency response (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.18–1.93; Z=3.25; P=0.001), with no observed statistical heterogeneity (Tau²=0.00; Chi²=1.13, df=2, P=0.57; I²=0%). Constipation was reported more frequently with ondansetron, although safety outcomes were not pooled because of heterogeneous reporting and study designs. Conclusion: Ondansetron significantly improved study-defined stool-consistency response in adults with IBS-D. Larger trials using standardized contemporary endpoints are warranted.
revue: International Journal of Current Pharmaceutical Research

titre: Sleep Quality and Its Relationship with Functional Dyspepsia Among University Students
resume: Pendahuluan: Dispepsia fungsional ialah gangguan saluran cerna yang sering dijumpai di kalangan mahasiswa dan berkaitan dengan berbagai faktor, salah satunya adalah kualitas tidur. Gangguan tidur diduga memengaruhi fungsi gastrointestinal melalui sumbu otak–usus (brain-gut axis), namun hasil penelitian mengenai hubungan antara kedua variabel tersebut masih memperlihatkan inkonsistensi. Tujuan: Studi ini dilakukan untuk menganalisis keterkaitan antara kualitas tidur dan kejadian dispepsia fungsional pada kalangan mahasiswa. Metode: Pendekatan cross-sectional dengan desain analitik observasional digunakan pada penelitian ini, melibatkan 101 mahasiswa yang diperoleh melalui teknik total sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner daring terstruktur yang mencakup karakteristik responden, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) guna mengukur kualitas tidur, serta kriteria Roma III untuk mengevaluasi dispepsia fungsional. titre: AN AYURVEDIC APPROACH TO THE MANAGEMENT OF GRAHANI ROGA (IBS) USING AYUGMA TAKRABASTI AND BHUNIMBADI CHURNA: A CASE REPORT
resume: Introduction: Grahani Roga is one of the common disorders of the Annavaha Srotas described in Ayurveda, primarily resulting from Agnimandya, which leads to impaired digestion, Ama formation, and derangement of Grahani Avayava. Clinically, its manifestations closely resemble Irritable Bowel Syndrome(IBS), a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain associated with altered bowel habits, mainly the appearance of loose stools in the absence of structural abnormalities. Contemporary management provides symptomatic relief; however, recurrence is common. Ayurveda emphasises correction of Agni by eliminating Ama as the principal line of treatment. Ayugma Takrabasti, owing to its Deepana, Pachana, Grahi and Vatanulomana properties, along with Bhunimbadi churna, is expected to restore the normal function of Grahani and provide sustained relief. The present case describes a 38-year-old male patient presenting with frequent loose stools, associated with Udarashoola, Urodaha, Aruchi and Adhmana for a duration of 2-3 years. Based on the clinical presentation, the case was diagnosed as Grahani Roga, while the clinical features fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for IBS. The patient was treated with Deepana-Pachana following Ayugma Takrabasti and orally with Bhunimbadi churna for over 40 days. The patient was assessed before and after treatment using relevant clinical parameters, including bowel frequency, stool consistency, abdominal pain, Adhmana, Agnimandya and associated symptoms. Following the intervention, after one week the patient had symptomatic relief with a reduction in the frequency of loose stools, abdominal pain and improvement in bowel pattern. This case highlights the potential of an Ayurvedic therapeutic approach in the management of a chronic functional gastrointestinal disorder.
revue: International journal of applied ayurved research.

titre: Structural Biology at EMBL Grenoble, IBS-CIBB, IAB and ILL
resume: This proposal clusters crystallography and bioSAXS projects at the EMBL Grenoble, IBS-CIBB, ILL and IAB. A wide range of projects are included in this BAG application. These range from studying the molecular mechanisms of infection by parasites (eg. T. gondii and Cryptosporidium hominis), bacteria (eg Wolbachia), and various viruses (rabies, Orthopoxviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus etc) and the development of therapeutics targeting these pathways. We also study many different cell signalling processes, from abscisic acid receptors in plants to mammalian cellular receptors and downstream signalling pathway, including kinase signalling and the role of other post-translation modifications, such as ubiquitination. The BAG is also actively involved in methods development from the automation of high throughput fragment screening to the integration of microfluidic devices for time resolved bioSAXS experiments.

titre: Ganodermanontriol attenuates DSS-induced colitis and visceral hypersensitivity involving gut microbiota remodeling and TRPV1-expressing sensory neurons
POLYPHENOLS AND GUT MICROBIOTA METABOLITES IN AUTISM: PERSPECTIVES FOR NUTRITIONAL MODULATION
resume: Alterations in the microbiota, redox balance, and inflammatory signaling have been investigated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), increasing interest in nutritional strategies targeting the gut-brain axis. Oxidative stress and neuroinflammation act synergistically in ASD, favoring the activation of inflammatory pathways. Therefore, experimental studies suggest that polyphenols and their metabolites may influence processes related to brain function, including mechanisms involved in memory, cognition, mood, and behavior, constituting a possible avenue of investigation to understand the relationship between diet and manifestations associated with ASD. Polyphenols and microbial metabolites represent a promising area of nutritional research in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their potential still requires clinical validation. Controlled clinical trials with standardized protocols and integrated assessment of clinical, metabolic, and microbial outcomes are needed to clarify their mechanisms of action and establish the consistency of potential benefits. Furthermore, the heterogeneity of ASD is a relevant factor in the interpretation of results and the development of individualized nutritional interventions, which may influence the response to polyphenols and microbial metabolites.

titre: Is the Gut Microbiome Linked to Depression? A Covariate-Adjusted Analysis of the American Gut Project
resume: A preregistered, cross-sectional analysis of publicly available 16S rRNA gene (V4) sequencing data from the American Gut Project will be conducted. Participants with self-reported depression will be compared with participants reporting no mental illness, using one stool sample per person. Alpha diversity (Shannon index) will be analyzed with linear regression and community composition (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity) with PERMANOVA. Both models will be adjusted for covariates known to influence the microbiome (sex, age, BMI, antibiotic and probiotic use, exercise, sleep duration, smoking, and alcohol consumption). Community composition will be visualized with principal coordinates analysis, and a propensity-score-matched sensitivity analysis will be conducted.

titre: Neurophysiological correlates of interoceptive compassion training for depression
resume: Abstract Depression is often linked to interoceptive dysfunction and self-critical thinking. The Heart-Smile Training-Intensive Introduction Program (HST-IIP) integrates interoceptive attention training with compassion-based practices to support emotional well-being. This pilot study randomized 23 individuals with depression to either HST-IIP or a waitlist control group. Participants completed EEG recordings and clinical assessments before and after a 4-week intervention. The primary outcome was heartbeat-evoked potentials (HEPs), while depression severity was our main clinical outcome, assessed using the Computerized Adaptive Test-Mental Health (CAT-MH). Exploratory outcomes included Delta power spectral density (PSD) during guided meditation, as well as psychological measures of interoceptive awareness (MAIA-2) and self-compassion (SCS). Compared to the control group, participants assigned to HST-IIP showed greater improvements in depression scores (Hedges’ g = –1.422, p = 0.028) and increases in interoceptive awareness. EEG analyses revealed attenuated (less negative) HEP amplitude in right frontal electrodes during attention-focused meditation and reduced Delta power during compassion-focused meditation. Changes in these neural markers were associated with improvements in depression outcomes. This exploratory pilot study provides preliminary evidence that HST-IIP is associated with improvements in depressive symptoms together with changes in HEP and Delta activity. These findings suggest that interoceptive compassion training may influence neurophysiological processes relevant to depression and support further research into interoceptive compassion training as a treatment for depression.

titre: Emotional Freedom Techniques Under Hypnosis: Suggestion, Emotional Regulation, and the Limits of Combined Treatment Evidence
resume: This critical narrative review examines the proposed combination of Emotional Freedom Techniques (EFT) and clinical hypnosis, emphasizing hypnotic suggestion, emotional regulation, and induction pacing. EFT combines emotionally focused statements with repetitive tapping, whereas hypnosis uses suggestion within a structured interpersonal and attentional context. Both approaches have been evaluated separately for selected symptom outcomes; however, improvement after a combined procedure cannot establish synergy or reveal which component produced the change. The review examines controlled clinical syntheses, research on hypnotizability and imagery, direct versus indirect suggestion, and the mechanisms and functions of induction. Evidence for anxiety and trauma-related symptoms supports continued investigation of EFT, while hypnosis studies demonstrate context-dependent changes in symptoms, perception, and response to suggestion. Yet the reviewed literature does not establish that EFT administered under hypnosis has a reliably superior effect compared with credible active controls. Nor does it demonstrate a general rule that rapid induction selectively enhances direct suggestions while gradual induction preferentially facilitates narrative imagery. Three original conceptual figures separate proposed treatment components, clarify the induction-by-suggestion factorial hypothesis, and map the requirements for testing incremental efficacy and mediation. We propose preregistered randomized comparisons, standardized scripts, hypnotizability and expectancy assessment, adverse-event monitoring, objective and patient-centered outcomes, and longitudinal follow-up. The proposed combined protocol is scientifically testable, but claims of additive efficacy, special induction matching, or neural repair remain provisional until supported by independent controlled evidence.

titre: Rapid Versus Gradual Hypnotic Induction: Suggestibility, Imagery, and the Evidence for Procedure-Specific Responses
resume: This critical narrative review evaluates whether rapid hypnotic induction preferentially facilitates direct suggestions whereas a ten-to-fifteen-minute gradual induction favors narrative or imaginal suggestions. Although the distinction is clinically appealing, induction duration is typically confounded with language, expectancy, relaxation, attention, and practitioner behavior. The review synthesizes methodological analyses of induction, controlled comparisons of direct and indirect suggestions, standardized hypnotizability research, and studies of imagery and subjective responding. Results do not establish a general induction-duration by suggestion-style matching rule. Behavioral responses and self-reported responding to clinical outcomes can diverge, and the clinical transferability of brief laboratory demonstrations is limited. A proposed factorial experiment independently randomizes brief versus gradual induction and direct versus imaginal suggestions, assesses baseline hypnotizability and expectancy, and balances script content and contact time. Three conceptual figures describe the procedural contrast, the four-cell interaction test, and the staged evidentiary pathway from immediate responding to clinical outcomes. Additional research should differentiate motor response, image vividness, subjective absorption, and patient-important symptoms while monitoring tolerability and individual preference. The hypothesis remains scientifically testable but should not be treated as established therapeutic guidance. Both rapid and gradual approaches may be appropriate in specific consent-based contexts; their comparative effectiveness should be judged by transparent measurement, controlled replication, and clinical relevance rather than by assumptions about hypnotic depth.

titre: An Umbrella Review on Psychological Stress and Infertility
resume: This umbrella review reports on biological mechanisms and synthesizes evidence from 88 systematic reviews and meta-analyses on stress, infertility, medically assisted reproduction (MAR) outcomes and management. Stress-induced activation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis predominantly suppresses reproductive function in animal models; nonetheless, human data remain heterogeneous. Infertility was consistently associated with substantial psychological burden, with pooled prevalence of depression and anxiety in infertile women ranging between 31.6 and 48.8% and 36.2 and 41%, respectively, with higher levels in women than men. Psychological burden increases during MAR as well as after unsuccessful treatment. Psychological stress adversely affects semen parameters and menstrual regularity, while evidence on MAR outcomes was inconsistent. Despite reducing depression and anxiety, stress cognitive–behavioral therapy and mindfulness’s impact on pregnancy rates remains uncertain. Overall confidence was critically low, with substantial heterogeneity and overlap. This analysis highlights a biologically plausible but methodologically not validated bidirectional association, underlining the need for standardized stress assessment, longitudinal designs, and a multidisciplinary approach to elucidate causality. This leaves both the MAR specialist and the infertile patient in unchartered territory. Future studies should focus on how to navigate this zone by addressing the anticipated impact of psychological stress on infertility or, ideally, alleviating it as part of preconception care.

titre: The rs1030757 in GRID2 and Its Sex-Specific Associations with Checking, Hoarding and Neutralization Symptoms in Obsessive–Compulsive Disorder
resume: Background: Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) is a complex psychiatric disorder with a lifetime prevalence of about 3%. Because glutamate is thought to play a role in OCD, we investigated its relationship with DLGAP1 and GRID2, genes encoding a scaffold protein involved in glutamatergic signaling and a glutamate receptor predominantly expressed in the cerebellum, respectively. The present study aims to investigate the association of polymorphisms in the GRID2 (rs1030757) and DLGAP1 (rs9952159 and rs11081062) genes with OCD and its phenotypical characteristics. Methods: Case–control study including 200 OCD individuals and 203 healthy controls from the Brazilian population. The samples were genotyped using pre-designed TaqMan® assays through real-time polymerase chain reaction. Results: No association was observed between the studied polymorphisms and OCD status. However, in a dominant model for the rs1030757 C allele in men with OCD, positive and statistically significant associations were observed with dimensions of hoarding (p = 0.015, odds ratio (OR) = 3.059, 95% confidence interval (CI = 1.217–7.685) and neutralization (p = 0.044, OR = 2.429, 95% CI = 1.014–5.815). An effect against checking symptoms in women was observed in both the dominant (p = 0.029, OR = 0.252, 95% CI 0.068–0.932) and overdominant (p = 0.006, OR = 0.239, 95% CI 0.082–0.697) models. Conclusions: Our findings reveal preliminary, nominal associations between GRID2 variation and specific symptom dimensions of OCD. Given the exploratory, hypothesis-generating nature of this initial mapping, future confirmatory studies with larger independent sample sizes are essential to validate these trends under strict multiple-testing corrections.
auteurs: Glenda da Silva Rodrigues de Oliveira

titre: Probiotics and Prebiotics in Restoring Gastrointestinal Microbiota Dysbiosis: Emerging Alternatives to Antibiotic Therapy
resume: The human gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota is a complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem that plays a fundamental role in maintaining host metabolism, immune homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and protection against pathogenic microorganisms. Disruption of this microbial community, known as gut dysbiosis, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous GI and systemic diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infection, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, colorectal cancer, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Although antibiotics remain indispensable for the treatment of bacterial infections, their indiscriminate use frequently disrupts gut microbial composition, reduces microbial diversity, promotes opportunistic pathogen overgrowth, and accelerates the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. These limitations have stimulated increasing interest in microbiota-targeted interventions as safer and more sustainable therapeutic strategies. Probiotics and prebiotics have emerged as promising approaches for restoring gut microbial homeostasis through complementary mechanisms. Probiotics inhibit pathogen colonization, enhance intestinal barrier function, produce antimicrobial metabolites, and modulate host immune responses. Prebiotics selectively stimulate the growth and metabolic activity of beneficial microorganisms, promoting the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that support intestinal and systemic health. Increasing evidence from experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, and meta-analyses demonstrates that these microbiota-directed interventions can reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea, improve symptoms of IBD and IBS, enhance Helicobacter pylori eradication, decrease recurrence of C. difficile infection, and contribute to the management of several metabolic disorders. Despite these promising findings, important challenges remain regarding strain specificity, optimal dosage, treatment duration, product standardization, regulatory oversight, and interindividual variability in treatment response. Emerging advances in metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine are facilitating the development of personalized microbiome-based therapies that may further enhance clinical outcomes. This review critically summarizes the current understanding of GI microbiota dysbiosis, discusses the mechanisms through which probiotics and prebiotics restore microbial balance, evaluates their clinical applications as alternatives or adjuncts to antibiotic therapy, and highlights existing challenges and future research directions for microbiome-based therapeutics.

titre: The Effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum 299v on Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
resume: Lactiplantibacillus (L.) plantarum 299​v DSM 9843 is a probiotic strain that showed safety and properties potentially beneficial in managing irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). To systematically review and meta-analyze the effects of L. plantarum 299​v in participants of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with IBS. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials. A meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model, pooling the outcomes of abdominal pain, bloating/flatulence, constipation, global symptoms. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (registration number CRD420261322875). Six RCTs enrolling 527 adult patients with IBS were included. L. plantarum 299​v significantly reduced abdominal pain scores (SMD = - 2.16; 95% CI - 3.59 to - 0.72; p = 0.003), abdominal pain severity (SMD = - 0.39; 95% CI​ - 0.67 to - 0.12; p = 0.005), daily abdominal pain frequency (SMD = - 0.66; 95% CI​ - 1.02 to - 0.30; p = 0.0004) compared with placebo. The improvement rates of abdominal pain (RR = 4.83; 95% CI​ 1.94-11.99; p = 0.0007), bloating/flatulence (RR = 1.96; 95% CI​ 1.06-3.61; p = 0.03) and global symptoms (RR = 4.69; 95% CI​ 1.52-14.45; p = 0.007) were significantly higher in the probiotic group. No significant effect was observed for constipation (RR = 1.39; 95% CI 0.32-6.11; p = 0.66). Meta-analytic evidence supports the capacity of L. plantarum 299​v to relieve abdominal pain, bloating, flatulence, and general symptoms. The observed diet-dependent response underscores the need for future research to investigate combined probiotic dietary interventions.

titre: Enduring neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex following chronic colitis: A role for C1q?
resume: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Fatigue profoundly affects patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), even during periods of remission. This study investigates molecular changes along the gut-brain axis in mice that had recovered from chronic colitis. METHODS: Chronic colitis was induced in C57BL/6J mice by repeated administration of 2% dextran sodium sulfate for one week, alternating with two weeks of normal drinking water and with an extra two-week recovery period after the third cycle (rcDSS). Mouse behavior was assessed, and transcriptomics of distal colon and choroid plexus were analyzed using consensus weighted correlation network analysis. Specific gene expression was validated by qRT-PCR. Neuroinflammation was evaluated through qRT-PCR of inflammatory markers in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, alongside microglial and astrocytic 3D morphology. Complement component 1q (C1q) serum levels were measured in mice and patients with quiescent IBD using ELISA. RESULTS: Spontaneous wheel-running activity was decreased in rcDSS mice compared to healthy controls. A consensus module comprising 123 genes was up-regulated in distal colon and choroid plexus of rcDSS mice and was enriched in genes involved in the immune response, with C1q as a hub gene. Persistent neuroinflammation was confirmed by the up-regulation of inflammatory markers Lcn2, S100a8, and S100a9, and the presence of activated microglia and astrocytes in prefrontal cortex. While neuroinflammation markers decreased over a recovery period of eight weeks, they did not fully return to baseline levels. Colonic C1q expression and serum levels correlated with inflammatory changes in prefrontal cortex. Notably, an exploratory study in quiescent IBD patients revealed a correlation between serum C1q levels and fatigue scores. CONCLUSIONS: Asymptomatic chronic colitis leads to enduring neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex of mice, with a potential central role for C1q, including in quiescent IBD patients.

titre: Dietary Clostridium butyricum NCU-02 and Its Postbiotic Butyrate Ameliorate Autism Spectrum Disorder-like Symptoms: Involvement of Hippocampal Oxidative Stress Modulation
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition closely linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, yet effective dietary interventions remain limited. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum NCU-02, a probiotic candidate, and its sterile supernatant in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced mouse model of ASD, with emphasis on their postbiotic properties. Both treatments significantly ameliorated core ASD-like behaviors, attenuating repetitive marble-burying by over 35% and restoring social novelty preference to near-control levels (p < 0.05 for both). These interventions were associated with improved intestinal barrier integrity, upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and occludin), and suppressed colonic and hippocampal pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Metabolomics profiling identified butyrate as a key differential metabolite, with butyrate levels elevated by approximately 1.3- to 2.5-fold following interventions (all p < 0.05 vs. M group). Correlation analyses further linked butyrate elevation to activation of the hippocampal GPR109A/AMPK/Nrf2 pathway and reduction of oxidative stress markers. Collectively, these findings suggest that C. butyricum NCU-02 and its sterile supernatant are associated with protective effects against ASD-like symptoms, and that the postbiotic metabolite butyrate may contribute to these benefits through dual modulation of gut homeostasis and neuroprotective signaling. A sodium-butyrate comparison group reproduced several of these effects, indicating that exogenous butyrate is sufficient to reproduce several of these effects, although the present design does not establish butyrate as a necessary mediator for the live-strain effects. These findings position butyrate, and butyrate-producing probiotics, as promising candidates for dietary intervention in neurodevelopmental disorders.

titre: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder
resume: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. Environmental stressors converge on this genetic susceptibility through DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, particularly among neurotransmitter-producing taxa, further extends the pathophysiological map beyond the brain itself. Together, these findings support a shift from a unidimensional monoaminergic model to an integrated, multi-systems molecular framework of MDD. Realising the clinical potential of this framework will require validated precision biomarker panels, dedicated South Asian GWAS cohorts, and longitudinal multi-omics studies.

titre: Microbiome-sparing antimicrobial stewardship in food animals: a conceptual farm-level decision framework
resume: Antimicrobial stewardship in food animals must reduce unnecessary antimicrobial exposure while preserving therapeutic success, animal welfare, and productivity; when animals or animal products enter the food chain, applicable withdrawal periods and residue limits must be observed under the rules in the relevant jurisdiction. However, stewardship often remains framed as a reduction target rather than a decision-quality problem. Under field conditions, variable delivery during group medication and diagnostic uncertainty can result in ineffective or unnecessary exposure; antimicrobial-associated microbiome changes are an additional ecological concern, but their contribution to relapse, retreatment, or productivity loss remains incompletely established. This review proposes a microbiome-sparing antimicrobial stewardship framework for food-animal systems. The framework integrates four practical decision layers: exposure integrity, diagnostic confidence, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) adequacy, and microbiome-risk assessment. It emphasizes reliable route and dose delivery, avoidance of prolonged suboptimal exposure, decision-changing diagnostics, severity-based treat-versus-observe thresholds, and explicit de-escalation and stop criteria. These principles are illustrated through syndrome-specific decision pathways for poultry enteric syndromes, calf diarrhea complexes, bovine respiratory disease, and mastitis, with emphasis on supportive care, preventive management, treatment permitted under applicable local rules, and withdrawal compliance. The review also advances a proposed six-domain reporting framework for stewardship studies, including clinical cure and relapse, productivity, exposure reliability, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) endpoints, microbiome disruption and recovery, and residue compliance. Overall, microbiome-sparing stewardship shifts food-animal antimicrobial use from quantity-focused reduction toward therapeutically reliable, ecologically informed, and farm-implementable decision pathways; its clinical and ecological effects require prospective evaluation across production systems.

titre: Amitriptyline alters gut microbial composition and compromises host resistance to enteropathogenic infection
resume: Amitriptyline, a tricyclic antidepressant commonly prescribed for depression and various other disorders, has been reported to possess both anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Paradoxically, clinical evidence suggests that patients with depressive disorders receiving pharmacological treatment exhibit an increased susceptibility to infections, though the mechanisms behind this increased susceptibility remain unclear. This study investigates the impact of amitriptyline on intestinal homeostasis and vulnerability to enteropathogenic infection in a murine model. Oral administration of amitriptyline was found to significantly reduce gut microbial diversity and alter microbiota composition under both homeostatic and infectious conditions, as determined by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Importantly, there was a marked depletion of butyrate-producing bacteria, accompanied by decreased fecal butyrate levels. Additionally, amitriptyline treatment led to a reduction in colonic regulatory T cells and cytokine production in specific pathogen-free mice, but not in germ-free animals. These results indicate that amitriptyline directly modulates host-microbiota interactions, and suggest that disruption of the gut microbiota may underlie the increased susceptibility to infection. Overall, this study underscores the critical role of the gut microbiome in shaping host responses to pharmacological interventions and identifies it as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate infection risks associated with amitriptyline use.

titre: Practicing Focused Attention or Open Monitoring During Interoceptive Challenges: Seed-Based Functional Connectivity Changes Following Video-Based Online MBSR
resume: BACKGROUND: Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) has been shown to improve well-being, but its neural mechanisms during interoceptive challenges remain unclear, particularly when delivered online. Previous neuroimaging research has primarily focused on the salience network, with limited attention to the dorsal attention network. This study investigated changes in functional connectivity within these networks following an eight-week video-based online MBSR program. METHODS: Thirty-nine healthy adults were included in the analysis (18 in the MBSR group and 21 in the control group). Participants underwent functional MRI before and after the intervention, while experiencing intermittent inspiratory occlusions under baseline, focused attention (FA), and open monitoring (OM) conditions. Seed-based connectivity analyses used bilateral frontal eye fields and anterior cingulate cortices as seeds for the dorsal attention and salience networks, respectively. RESULTS: Exploratory analysis revealed a significant Group × Time interaction in anterior cingulate seed connectivity during OM. This finding survived correction within the seed-by-condition map but not across all six interaction analyses. Connectivity with the right frontal pole showed a greater negative change in the MBSR group than in the control group. Within the MBSR group, frontal eye field connectivity changed with frontal and occipital regions during FA. Anterior cingulate connectivity also changed in frontal, sensorimotor, parietal, and occipital regions during FA and with the left frontal pole during OM. In the control group, the only significant change was increased frontal eye field connectivity with the right temporal fusiform cortex during OM. CONCLUSIONS: Functional connectivity between the network seeds and specific cortical regions changed following video-based online MBSR. Exploratory analysis also identified a group difference in connectivity changes between the anterior cingulate cortex and the right frontal pole during OM, although this finding requires replication. The functional significance of these neural changes for behavioral outcomes, including interoceptive awareness and attentional regulation, warrants further investigation.
