titre: Altered degree centrality and functional connectivity in adolescents with obsessive-compulsive disorder: A resting-state fMRI study
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in adolescence is associated with substantial burden, but whole-brain network alterations remain poorly understood. Previous research has emphasized adults and cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry. METHODS: Resting-state functional MRI data were acquired from 40 adolescents with OCD and 40 healthy controls. Following global signal regression preprocessing, degree centrality (DC) identified regions with altered whole-brain connectedness for seed-based functional connectivity (FC) analysis. Associations between FC and clinical symptoms were examined. RESULTS: Adolescents with OCD showed increased DC in the right ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) and left angular gyrus. The angular gyrus finding was less robust across DC thresholds. The vmPFC showed increased FC with the supplementary motor area, bilateral inferior temporal gyri, right posterior cerebellum, and other regions. Nominal inverse associations were observed between vmPFC-supplementary motor area FC and OCD severity, and between vmPFC-temporal/cerebellar FC and depressive/anxiety symptoms. None survived false discovery rate (FDR) correction. CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents with OCD exhibited increased DC in the right vmPFC and left angular gyrus, together with altered vmPFC-seeded FC. These group-level brain-network findings provide candidate neural correlates for future longitudinal and interventional research in adolescent OCD.

titre: Gut Dysbiosis at the Intersection of Depression and Addiction: A Microbiota–Gut–Brain–Reward Framework and Digital Precision Behavioural Health Agenda for the United Arab Emirates
resume: Background: The microbiota–gut–brain axis provides an emerging framework for understanding neuropsychiatric disorders. Depression and addiction, despite substantial comorbidity, are frequently investigated separately. This review examines whether gut dysbiosis contributes to vulnerability, symptom persistence and recovery through shared inflammatory, endocrine, metabolic and reward-related mechanisms. Methods A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and PsycINFO, supplemented by citation searching. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, human cohorts, randomised trials and mechanistic studies. Evidence was evaluated for methodological quality, confounding, replication, biological plausibility and clinical relevance. Results Convergent evidence implicates altered short-chain fatty acid production, intestinal barrier dysfunction, dysregulated tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism, systemic inflammation, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal-axis disturbance and altered affective and reward signalling. Human evidence is strongest for major depressive disorder and alcohol use disorder, whereas evidence involving opioids, psychostimulants, cannabis and polysubstance use remains comparatively limited. Dietary interventions, probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and faecal microbiota transplantation demonstrate preliminary therapeutic potential. However, methodological heterogeneity, uncertain causality, limited replication and insufficient evidence of sustained benefit prevent routine clinical recommendation. Digital phenotyping, wearable technologies and artificial intelligence may facilitate integration of microbial, metabolic, behavioural and longitudinal clinical information, although prospective validation and demonstrated clinical utility remain limited. Conclusions The proposed Microbiota–Gut–Brain–Reward framework conceptualises dysbiosis as a potentially modifiable contributor rather than an independent cause of depression or addiction. Clinical translation requires longitudinal multi-omic research, harmonised methodologies, mechanistically informed trials and integration with established pharmacological, psychological and social interventions. Digitally enabled precision approaches may support personalised recovery monitoring, provided interpretability, privacy, equity and clinical governance are prioritised. The United Arab Emirates offers opportunities for culturally responsive translational research, although implementation must remain evidence-driven, ethically governed and subject to rigorous prospective evaluation before clinical adoption.

titre: Gut Microbiota, Microbial Metabolites, and Mucosal Immune-Barrier Dysfunction in Human Post-Infectious Irritable Bowel Syndrome (2019–2026): A Scoping Review Protocol
resume: Post-infectious irritable bowel syndrome (PI-IBS) develops in approximately 10% of individuals after acute infectious enteritis and involves gut microbiota perturbations, altered microbial metabolites, impaired intestinal barrier integrity, and low-grade mucosal immune activation. Although the Rome Foundation Working Team published an integrative consensus on PI-IBS in 2019, subsequent human cohorts have examined post-COVID-19 PI-IBS alongside multi-omic datasets spanning bacterial, parasitic, and viral etiologies. Exploratory searches of PubMed, OSF Registries, INPLASY, and PROSPERO on 14 November 2026 identified no registered scoping review mapping this integrated microbiota-metabolite-barrier-immune axis from 2019 to 2026. Objective: To map and compare primary human evidence published between 2019 and 2026 on gut microbiota composition, microbial metabolites, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and mucosal immune responses in PI-IBS across bacterial, parasitic, and viral triggers. Methods: Guided by Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, PRISMA-ScR, and PRISMA-S, eligible primary human studies (English, Spanish, or Portuguese; January 2019 onward) with PI-IBS and at least one biological domain will be retrieved from seven databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane CENTRAL, LILACS, and SciELO). Following Zotero deduplication, six reviewers in three pairs will pass a 50-record pre-screening sensitivity and inter-rater agreement calibration (Fleiss' kappa >=0.75, pairwise Cohen's kappa, PABAK >=0.80, >=85% agreement) before blinded screening in Rayyan, and a 5-to-10-study calibration (Cohen's kappa/PABAK >=0.80, >=85% agreement) before duplicate data charting. Conflicts undergo within-pair consensus and expert adjudication. Findings will be synthesized descriptively without meta-analysis.

titre: IBS BAG
resume: The IBS BAG includes teams from IBS (Grenoble) and external groups from CEA-Cadarache (St Paul lez Durance), CEA-Grenoble, CERMAV (Grenoble) et IRBA (Brétigny-sur-Orge). We study the structure-function relationships of proteins and biological macromolecular complexes with a focus on human health, biotechnology and methodology. Most of the projects are a continuation of the MX-2686 proposal and can be grouped under the following themes: host-pathogen interaction, new therapeutic targets, fundamental cellular mechanisms, membrane proteins, biotechnological applications and methodology. Some of these projects use integrative approaches (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, SAXS and NMR) together with other biophysical and biochemical studies and, more recently, the use of AI (e.g. AlphaFold, Chai-1) to fully understand the complexity of the biological systems under study.

titre: ibs-11
Efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation in children with refractory functional abdominal pain disorders: an open-label pilot trial with exploratory microbiome analyses
resume: Abstract Background Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) rebuilds the gut microbiota, yet its efficacy in pediatric refractory functional abdominal pain disorders (FAPDs) is insufficiently described. The purpose of this study is to identify gut microbiota dysbiosis in pediatric FAPDs and to examine the effectiveness, safety, and microbial biomarkers of FMT in these patients. Methods In a two-phase study, gut microbiota (16 S rRNA sequencing) were compared between 47 children with FAPDs and 39 healthy controls. Thereafter, a non-randomized, open-label prospective pilot trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05753774) allocated the 47 refractory patients, according to guardian and/or patient preference, to receive FMT plus conventional therapy ( n = 26) or conventional therapy only ( n = 21). The trial was terminated early because of slow recruitment (47 of 50 planned participants). The primary endpoint was the composite response rate at weeks 4 and 8. Results At baseline, patients had significant gut microbiota dysbiosis: 3.5-fold Proteobacteria enrichment (20.6% vs. 5.8%; P < 0.001), 4.1-fold Escherichia–Shigella expansion (12.7% vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), and reduced α-diversity (Shannon index 4.7 ± 1.1 vs. 5.4 ± 1.1; P = 0.002). FMT plus conventional therapy was associated with a higher composite response rate at week 4 (69.2% vs. 14.3%; RR 4.85, 95% CI 1.65–14.24; Fisher’s exact P < 0.001) and week 8 (80.8% vs. 47.6%; RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.04–2.76; P = 0.029), with significantly better adjusted symptom scores in the FMT group at both time points. Post-FMT, Faecalibacterium and Blautia increased (+ 44.5% and + 99.1%), while Escherichia–Shigella declined (− 19.2%). Exploratory random forest models (seven genera for diagnosis; four genera characterizing the post-FMT, response-associated microbial signature) yielded internally validated AUCs of 0.896 (95% CI 0.821–0.952) and 0.890 (95% CI 0.699–1.000), respectively. FMT showed favorable short-term tolerability, with transient constipation in 50.0% of patients and no severe adverse events. Conclusions In this open-label pilot trial, FMT plus conventional therapy was associated with higher short-term response rates that were maintained through week 8 in children with refractory FAPDs. Exploratory microbial signatures further demonstrated potential for both diagnosis and characterization of the post-treatment, response-associated microbial state, and pending external validation. Trial registration: This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 11 February 2023 (registration number: NCT05753774), before the enrollment of the first participant. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05753774

titre: A IMUNIDADE DAS INSTITUIÇÕES DE EDUCAÇÃO SEM FINS LUCRATIVOS NA REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA DO CONSUMO: O IBS, A CBS E O ALCANCE DO ART. 9º DA LEI COMPLEMENTAR Nº 214/2025
resume: O artigo examina o alcance da imunidade das instituições de educação sem fins lucrativos em relação ao Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e à Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), instituídos pela Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023 e regulamentados pela Lei Complementar nº 214/2025. Parte-se da delimitação constitucional das imunidades tributárias e da distinção, construída pela doutrina e pela jurisprudência do Supremo Tribunal Federal, entre a imunidade de impostos das instituições de educação e de assistência social sem fins lucrativos (art. 150, VI, “c”, da Constituição Federal) e a imunidade de contribuições das entidades beneficentes de assistência social (art. 195, § 7º). Em seguida, analisam-se o parágrafo único do art. 149-B da Constituição, que submete o IBS e a CBS às imunidades do art. 150, VI, e afasta a aplicação do art. 195, § 7º, e o art. 9º, III, §§ 3º e 4º, da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025, que condiciona a imunidade apenas aos requisitos do art. 14 do Código Tributário Nacional. Sustenta-se que a nova disciplina alargou a imunidade das instituições de educação quanto à contribuição federal sobre o consumo, que deixa de depender da certificação prevista na Lei Complementar nº 187/2021, mas restringiu seu alcance econômico ao excluir as aquisições. Conclui-se que a proteção constitucional foi preservada, embora sua fruição passe a exigir das mantenedoras governança e prova consistentes.

titre: Decoding the gut-brain axis with C. elegans: a translational model for bioactive food discovery
Effects of probiotics on selected regulatory mechanisms and thyroid function in patients with hypothyroidism and bowel dysfunction
resume: Background. Hypothyroidism-related bowel dysfunction may persist despite levothyroxine therapy. Gut-thyroid interactions involving alterations in the intestinal microbiota, visceral hypersensitivity, and neurohumoral regulation may contribute to these manifestations. This study evaluated the effects of 30-day probiotic supplementation on the thyroid hormone profile, bowel function, intestinal microbiota, visceral sensitivity, cortisol, and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) levels in patients with hypothyroidism and constipation or diarrhea. Materials and methods. Eighty-one patients were studied. Of 53 patients with constipation, 28 received Bifidobacterium longum 35624® plus levothyroxine and 25 received levothyroxine alone. Of 28 patients with diarrhea, 14 received a probiotic formulation containing Saccharomyces boulardii plus levothyroxine and 14 received levothyroxine alone. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), VIP, cortisol, visceral sensitivity index (VSI), and intestinal microbiota were assessed. Results. In patients with constipation, B.longum 35624® reduced TSH from 5.79 ± 0.16 to 4.84 ± 0.10 μIU/mL and increased T3 from 1.57 ± 0.08 to 1.96 ± 0.06 nmol/L (p < 0.05). Bowel movement frequency increased from 2.2 ± 0.2 to 3.9 ± 0.2/week, and 71.4 % of patients no longer required regular laxatives. Colonic Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus counts increased significantly, whereas Bacteroides, Klebsiella, S.aureus, Candida spp., and lactose-negative E.coli decreased. VSI decreased from 59.9 ± 1.6 to 54.1 ± 1.6, cortisol from 328.1 ± 5.9 to 287.3 ± 7.2 nmol/L, while VIP increased from 46.28 ± 1.47 to 53.32 ± 1.40 pg/mL (p < 0.05). In patients with diarrhea, the probiotic formulation reduced TSH from 4.94 ± 0.18 to 4.46 ± 0.13 μIU/mL and increased T4 from 1.38 ± 0.09 to 1.73 ± 0.11 ng/dL (p < 0.05). Loose stool frequency decreased from 3.6 ± 0.3 to 1.5 ± 0.2/day; bloating resolved in 92.9 % and excessive gas in 71.4 % of patients. Small-intestinal Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Bacteroides, and Enterococcus counts decreased significantly. VSI decreased from 62.9 ± 1.9 to 55.0 ± 1.7 and VIP from 151.3 ± 32.2 to 87.6 ± 4.1 pg/mL, whereas cortisol showed a nonsignificant downward trend. Conclusions. Adding probiotics to levothyroxine therapy was associated with favorable changes in thyroid parameters and bowel symptoms, modulation of the intestinal microbiota, and reduced visceral hypersensitivity. VIP responses differed according to the predominant type of bowel dysfunction.

titre: A Multi-Pathway Natural Botanical Candidate Formula for Alleviating Opioid Withdrawal and Reducing Craving
resume: This technical note presents a preclinical hypothesis of a multi-cluster botanical formulation targeting autonomic stabilization, neuroinflammation suppression, HPA stress regulation, gut–brain axis modulation, electrolyte homeostasis, and reduction of opioid withdrawal symptoms and craving. No confidential ratios or proprietary manufacturing parameters are included. Contains pathway diagram SVG, raw material specification, risk assessment, extraction strategy, and experimental roadmap. This is not an approved therapeutic product and is for scientific archiving only.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Sleep Disturbance and Psychological Burden in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
resume: Background and aims: Sleep disturbances and psychological symptoms are common in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We compared sleep outcomes in IBD and non-IBD outpatients and explored associations with disease activity. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 155 patients with IBD and 149 non-IBD controls (March–May 2026). Sleep quality, insomnia severity, and psychological symptoms were assessed using the PSQI, ISI, and HADS. Multivariable and sensitivity analyses assessed associations with IBD. Results: Poor sleep quality (PSQI > 5) and moderate-to-severe insomnia (ISI ≥ 15) were more frequent in IBD than controls (50.3% vs. 36.2%, p = 0.015; and 20.0% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.003). However, median PSQI (6 vs. 4; p = 0.056) and ISI (8 vs. 7; p = 0.097) scores did not differ significantly, nor did ISI ≥ 8 prevalence (52.3% vs. 45.6%; p = 0.248). Anxiety (HADS-A ≥ 8: 39.4% vs. 27.5%; p = 0.029) and depressive symptoms (HADS-D ≥ 8: 42.6% vs. 17.4%; p < 0.001) were more frequent in IBD. In primary adjusted models, IBD was associated with poor sleep (aOR 2.00, 95% CI 1.23–3.24) and ISI ≥ 15 (aOR 3.40, 95% CI 1.61–7.18). Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusting for diabetes, hypertension, alcohol use, and BMI supported these associations; continuous-score models identified higher PSQI (β = 1.13; p = 0.008) and ISI (β = 1.52; p = 0.021) scores. Further HADS adjustment yielded nonsignificant, imprecise IBD associations. Continuous disease activity indices were not significantly correlated with sleep outcomes. Conclusions: IBD was associated with more frequent poor sleep and moderate-to-severe insomnia despite nonsignificant median and ISI ≥ 8 comparisons. Disease-activity findings were exploratory; causality cannot be inferred.

titre: Bipolar Depression with Secondary Psychosis Triggered by Polysubstance and Hyperhomocysteinemia: A Case ReportBipolar Depression with Secondary Psychosis Triggered by Polysubstance and Hyperhomocysteinemia: A Case Report
resume: The intersection between early-onset mood disorders, substance use, and the development of psychotic conditions in adolescence represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in psychiatric practice. This article presents a case report of a 17-year-old male with a history of persistent depressive disorder, hyperactivity, and multiple suicide attempts, who progressed to severe psychic disorganization ("schizophrenization") associated with cocaine use and severe nicotine dependence. The clinical evolution illustrates the complexity of differentiating between substance-induced psychosis and the prodrome of a primary psychotic disorder, as well as the impact of delirium secondary to nicotine withdrawal on mental disorganization. Therapeutic management required multiple pharmacological approaches, culminating in the consideration of atypical strategies due to refractoriness. We discuss the hypothesis of schizophrenization as an interpretative matrix, expanded by the concepts of self-medication of distress, alexithymia, limbic hypersignification in patients with Bipolar Affective Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) traits, offering a model to understand progressive destructuring in adolescents with multiple vulnerabilities.
revue: International Journal of Medical Science and Clinical Research Studies

titre: When Anxiety and Depression Overlap: Understanding Worry, Withdrawal, and the Path Back to Engagement
resume: Abstract Anxiety and depression frequently occur together, creating overlapping patterns of persistent worry, negative thinking, emotional exhaustion, behavioural avoidance, and social withdrawal. This evidence-informed narrative review examines the psychological processes that may contribute to the development and maintenance of anxiety and depressive symptoms. Particular attention is given to repetitive negative thinking, including rumination and worry, avoidance behaviours, reduced engagement in meaningful activities, and their implications for counselling practice. Drawing on selected peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical treatment guidelines, the discussion explores cognitive behavioural therapy, behavioural activation, transdiagnostic interventions, and individualized clinical assessment. The review also considers how evidence-informed approaches can guide anxiety counselling for individuals experiencing persistent worry, fear, and avoidance, alongside depression counselling for those experiencing low mood, reduced motivation, and emotional withdrawal. Effective mental health support requires understanding the relationship between symptoms, personal experiences, cultural circumstances, relationships, and everyday functioning. Recognizing these interconnected factors can help mental health professionals develop more individualized and responsive approaches to care. Publication type: Evidence-informed narrative practitioner review. Scope: Non-systematic synthesis of selected published literature. No original participant research or clinical trial findings are reported. This work has not undergone independent peer review. Affiliation: C.S. Counselling & Consulting Services, 2250 Bovaird Dr E #408, Brampton, ON L6R 0W3, Canada AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI ChatGPT was used substantially for literature discovery, synthesis, organization, and manuscript drafting. The cited research and clinical guidance are identified in the document.

titre: Trait absorption association with ketamine’s benefits and drug-context interactions in treatment-resistant depression: exploratory results from the MUSIK randomized clinical trial
resume: Ketamine exerts rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD) but therapeutic predictors remain elusive. The personality trait absorption – tendencies for immersive sensory, imaginative, and emotional experiences – influences responses to serotonergic psychedelics, like psilocybin, but has not been studied for ketamine. This study explores trait absorption’s influences on ketamine-therapy for TRD, including interactions with music- versus mindfulness-based support. This exploratory analysis draws on the MUSIK trial (NCT04701866), a multi-site, parallel, single-blind RCT at two Montreal hospitals, whose primary outcome examined hemodynamic effects of pairing ketamine with music. Thirty-two adults (aged 18-75 years) with severe TRD, receiving a structured psychedelic ketamine-therapy intervention, were randomized 1:1 to receive either music (n = 15) or matched non-music support (n = 17) during their six infusions (0.5 mg/kg over 40 min) over four weeks. Outcome assessors but not participants were blinded. Across 181 infusions, this exploratory outcome examined associations between baseline absorption and (1) changes in depression, anxiety, and suicidality; and (2) mystical/emotional experiences using linear correlations and multilevel models. Baseline trait absorption is associated (p ≤ .002) with pre-post improvements in depression (r = .721), anxiety (r = .546), and mean/peak Mystical Experience Questionnaire scores (r = .528-.637). In multilevel models, higher absorption is associated with steeper declines in depression and suicidality. Three-way interactions with timepoint and group suggest that music, versus matched non-music support, is associated with greater depression improvements in higher-absorption individuals (p <.001). Although confirmation in larger studies is required, this exploratory study suggests that trait absorption relates to ketamine’s benefits for TRD. Observed drug-context interactions highlight possible strategies for individuallytailoring ketamine-therapy. Low-dose ketamine can be very beneficial for severe depression even when other treatments have not helped. However, much remains unknown about how ketamine works and who might most benefit. This study explored how a personality trait called absorption may influence the benefits of a series of ketamine doses, paired with either music- or mindfulness-based support, for adults with severe depression. Trait absorption reflects an individual’s tendencies to become deeply immersed in sensory, imaginative, and emotional experiences. The results suggest that higher trait absorption is associated with greater benefits from ketamine, especially when administered with music. This may be because high-absorption individuals tend to have more significant ketamine experiences – indeed, the study found that higher trait absorption was associated with more mystical-like ketamine experiences. If confirmed, these results may help guide patient selection and the personalized use of mindfulness or music in ketamine therapy for depression. Garel et al. explore the influence of the personality trait absorption in the MUSIK trial which administered 181 doses of ketamine, with either music or mindfulness, for treatment-resistant depression. Higher absorption is associated with larger antidepressant effects, reduced suicidality, and more mystical experiences, especially with music-based support.

titre: Prevalence and risk factors for perinatal obsessive-compulsive disorder: an umbrella review protocol
resume: This project registers the protocol for an umbrella review aiming to identify, critically appraise, and synthesise the available systematic review evidence on the prevalence of perinatal obsessive-compulsive disorder (P-OCD) during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Secondary objectives include examining associated risk factors, incidence, and the clinical features of obsessions and compulsions, as well as exploring differences in prevalence between pregnancy and the postpartum period. The review will follow JBI methodology and PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines. Searches will be conducted in five electronic databases, with methodological quality assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist and certainty of evidence evaluated using the GRADE approach. Findings will be synthesised narratively.

titre: The psychiatric burden of lichen sclerosus: a cross-sectional study in a US registry
resume: Abstract Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition with known impacts on quality of life, yet its psychiatric burden remains under characterized. LS predominantly affects postmenopausal women, though it can occur in individuals of any age or sex. In this cross-sectional matched study using the NIH All of Us database, we examined associations between LS and various psychiatric conditions among a diverse national cohort of U.S. adults. SNOMED codes were used to identify LS cases ( n = 2,946) that were matched to controls ( n = 11,781) by age, sex, race, ethnicity, and smoking status. Logistic regression analyses revealed significant associations between LS and several psychiatric disorders, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), dissociative disorder (DD), adjustment disorder (AD), and insomnia, even after adjusting for autoimmune comorbidities. These findings suggest that LS patients experience a substantial psychiatric burden, emphasizing the need for integrated dermatologic and psychiatric care.

titre: Neuropathic Pain in Women With Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Prospective Observational Study
resume: PURPOSE: To estimate the prevalence of neuropathic pain among women with chronic pelvic pain and explore associated clinical characteristics. DESIGN: Prospective observational study. METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a pelvic pain and endometriosis outpatient clinic between August 2022 and July 2025. Women underwent anamnesis, physical and complementary examinations, and questionnaire assessment. Neuropathic pain was classified using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment was applied to comparisons as a single family. RESULTS: The prevalence of neuropathic pain was 34.3%. A higher Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire total score was the only association retained after adjustment (p < .001; q = 0.004). Parity (p = .010), miscarriage history (p = .049), fibromyalgia (p = .016), infertility (p = .019), irritable bowel syndrome (p = .046), urinary symptoms (p = .005), myofascial pain (p = .004), and anxiety (p = .024) showed nominal associations only. CONCLUSION: Neuropathic pain was common in this specialized clinic population, and greater sensory and affective pain severity was the only association retained after multiplicity adjustment. The other eight nominal findings are exploratory and require confirmation; multidimensional assessment remains relevant to individualized care. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Neuropathic pain screening may complement comprehensive nursing assessment of women with chronic pelvic pain. Integrating pain characteristics, associated symptoms, and patient priorities may support individualized multidisciplinary evaluation and care.
revue: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

titre: Sex differences in the effect of viable cell-containing and heat-killed Roseburia faecis on repeated water avoidance stress-induced irritable bowel syndrome Wistar rat model
resume: BACKGROUND: Roseburia faecis has been reported to mitigate irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), which is characterized by altered intestinal motility, mucosal immune activation, and gut microbial dysbiosis. This study aimed to evaluate the sex-dependent effects of heat-killed R. faecis (HK-BBH024) and a viable cell-containing R. faecis preparation (L-BBH024) in a repeated water avoidance stress (rWAS)-induced IBS Wistar rat model. METHODS: Fecal pellet output (FPO) and colonic mast cell infiltration were measured in the rWAS IBS model induced in 7-week Wistar rats (males and females). Gut microbial composition and function were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway prediction, with or without BBH024 treatment. RESULTS: The marked rWAS-induced increase in FPO in both sexes was reduced by HK-BBH024 and L-BBH024. rWAS also increased colonic mast cell infiltration in the proximal colon and the mRNA expression of protease-related genes, whereas L-BBH024 attenuated these sex differences. Specifically, L-BBH024 was associated with a borderline decrease in mast cell infiltration and suppressed Prss1 and Prss2 mRNA expression in females, whereas Prss3 expression was reduced in males. Microbiota profiling showed that rWAS-associated alterations in beta diversity, selected bacterial taxa, linear discriminant analysis-derived microbial biomarkers, and predicted KEGG functional pathways were more evident in females. CONCLUSIONS: Both preparations reduced rWAS-induced FPO in both sexes. In the L-BBH024 experiment, additional changes in mast cell infiltration, protease-related gene expression, and microbial features were more evident in females.

titre: Editorial overview: The microbiota-gut-brain axis in neuroimmunology: From molecular dialogue to therapeutic evidence
The interplay between gut microbiota and inflammatory markers in bipolar disorder: A systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis may play a role in the pathophysiology of bipolar disorder (BD), with the gut microbiota influencing immune and inflammatory pathways. OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the evidence on the association between gut microbiota composition and inflammatory markers in individuals with BD. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251011554). Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, BVS, Lilacs, SciELO, PsycINFO, and EMBASE up to March 20, 2025. Observational studies in humans evaluating gut microbiota and inflammatory markers in BD were included. RESULTS: Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall, the results suggest that TB is associated with alterations in specific microbial taxa rather than consistent changes in overall microbial diversity. Differences in beta-diversity and taxonomic composition were noted, including increased abundance of bacteria previously linked to inflammatory processes such as Enterobacteriaceae and changes in short-chain fatty acid-producing genera, such as Roseburia. Regarding inflammation, some studies identified elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha, whereas others found no significant associations. Notably, correlations between bacterial taxa and inflammatory markers were observed, and Mendelian randomization studies suggested potential causal relationships involving both microbial taxa and inflammatory mediators. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence indicates that interactions between gut microbiota and inflammatory pathways may contribute to the pathophysiology of BD through mechanisms involving microbial metabolites, intestinal barrier function, and immune activation. However, heterogeneity across studies and methodological limitations highlight the need for longitudinal and multi-omics research to clarify these associations and their clinical relevance.

titre: Dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain axis induced by intermittent access to palatable food is associated with binge-like eating regardless of obesity development
resume: Recurrent consumption of energy dense palatable foods contributes to the rising prevalence of obesity and can also promote loss-of-control eating in a subset of individuals. Obesity is commonly associated with peripheral inflammation, impaired sensitivity to appetite-regulating hormones, and alterations in gut microbiota composition, all of which may exacerbate binge-eating behaviors. However, emerging evidence suggests that repeated exposure to palatable foods alone can induce maladaptive eating patterns even prior to the development of obesity. In this study, intermittent access to palatable food (e.g., cheesecake) induced binge-like eating behavior in non-obese female rats, accompanied by hypothalamic microglial reactivity and altered leptin signaling pathway. Additionally, even sporadic exposure to palatable food was sufficient to alter gut microbiota composition, increasing microbial diversity and promoting taxa adapted to high fat and sugar availability, including potential pathobionts (e.g., Escherichia, Streptococcus, and Clostridium spp.) as well as carbohydrate-fermenting bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Roseburia. Notably, increased microbial diversity was associated with both hyperphagic behavior and reduced hypothalamic leptin pathway responsiveness. Overall, these findings suggest that gut microbiota imbalance and central neuroimmune adaptations occurred in the absence of significant weight gain. This highlights the potential value of early interventions which may represent promising candidate strategies for future investigation.

titre: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum postbiotics attenuate Salmonella LPS-triggered neuroinflammation by modulating the microbiota-gut-brain axis in a pig model
resume: This study explored the effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (LP) postbiotics on Salmonella LPS-induced neuroinflammation, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms. Sixty pigs were randomly divided into control, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), cell-free supernatant of LP (CFS) and CFS + LPS groups. The pigs were fed with 0.8% CFS or MRS medium for 28 days, and then exposed to 30 μg kg-1 LPS. The results showed that CFS alleviated damage of the liver, colon and brain, and improved brain tight junctions. LPS significantly upregulated the levels of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α (P < 0.05) and downregulated IL-4 and IL-10 (P < 0.05), while CFS pretreatment markedly reversed this trend. LPS activated the brain inflammasome by increasing NLRP3, IL-1β, IL-18 and GSDMD (P < 0.05), and CFS pretreatment significantly decreased NLRP3 and IL-1β (P < 0.05). CFS modulated the levels of neurotransmitters, particularly the tryptophan metabolism. Moreover, CFS markedly increased the contents of microbial metabolites (P < 0.05) and optimized the gut microbiota through improving Lactobacillus amylovorus and Lactobacillus reuteri (P < 0.05). To further clarify the role of the microbiota on alleviating neuroinflammation, the fecal microbial transplantation (FMT) model in mice was established. The mice were administered with fecal suspension from CFS-treated pigs for 14 days and challenged with 3 × 108 CFU Salmonella Typhimurium (ST) for three days. The results showed that the weight loss caused by ST was significantly alleviated by CFS and FMT-CFS pretreatment (P < 0.05). FMT-CFS markedly inhibited ST translocation in the spleen and brain (P < 0.05), and attenuated tissue damage. FMT-CFS dramatically suppressed neuroinflammation and NLRP3 activation. In summary, LP postbiotics attenuated Salmonella LPS-induced neuroinflammation via modulating the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Our findings provide the potential of postbiotics as a nutritional supplement to alleviate neuroinflammation.

titre: Metabolic syndrome and Alzheimer's disease: Mechanistic links and precision prevention (Review)
resume: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with increased risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), however, the majority of previous studies regard MetS as an isolated risk factor and focus on single pathways, lacking systematic understanding of combined effects among multiple metabolic components. The present review systematically summarizes the multifaceted mechanisms by which MetS promotes AD pathology, including insulin resistance and cerebral energy dysregulation, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation and glial cell activation, vascular dysfunction and dysregulation of the renin‑angiotensin system, as well as the central convergent signaling pathway involving glycogen synthase kinase‑3β. The present review further highlights emerging regulatory mechanisms involving the gut‑brain axis, epigenetic reprogramming, sex differences and hormonal effects and senescent microenvironment. By emphasizing the peripheral‑central crosstalk and interactive amplification of MetS components, the present review aimed to position AD as a central manifestation of systemic metabolic disorders in the brain and propose a multi‑domain precision strategy integrating lifestyle intervention, metabolic drug repurposing, gut microbiota regulation, anti‑aging therapy and biomarker‑guided subtype classification for intervention against MetS‑associated AD.

titre: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG
resume: Background: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support. Objective: To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of PLWNT in sleep-onset chronic insomnia and to investigate, via multimodal techniques, its modulatory effects on cerebral cortical networks. Methods: This prospective, single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3-diagnosed sleep-onset chronic insomnia, randomized 1:1 to a 12-week PLWNT or CBT-I intervention in a superiority design. The primary endpoint is the baseline-to-week-12 change in PSQI total score. Secondary measures include validated scales (ISI, PSAS, HADS, PSS, HAS, MEQ, MFI-20, GSRS, SF-36), sleep diary, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI. Exploratory mechanistic endpoints include (1) EEG-derived spectral power and wPLI within the DMN, SN, and CEN during wakefulness, sleep-onset latency, and sleep stages (N1–N3, REM), and (2) resting-state fMRI connectivity of the same networks. Clinical assessments occur at baseline (week 0), week 6, week 12 (end of intervention), and weeks 16, 20, 24, and 36 after randomization (7 time points); laboratory and imaging measures are obtained at baseline and week 12 only. Primary analysis will use generalized estimating equations on LOCF-imputed data, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. Discussion: This randomized controlled trial directly compares PLWNT with CBT-I for sleep-onset chronic insomnia, integrating clinical outcome measures with neuroimaging-based mechanistic insights. The findings could position PLWNT as a non-drug therapeutic option backed by objective imaging data. Keywords: sleep-onset chronic insomnia, prolong life with nine turn-method, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, randomized controlled trial, cortical networks

titre: Living in an Altered Body: An Integrative Review of Body Image Dissatisfaction in Adults With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
resume: Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic gastrointestinal condition that affects physical health, psychosocial functioning, and quality of life. Body image dissatisfaction is a prevalent yet underrecognized concern among adults living with inflammatory bowel disease and has important implications for nursing care. The purpose of this integrative literature review was to synthesize existing evidence on body image dissatisfaction in adults with inflammatory bowel disease and examine its relevance for nursing practice. A systematic search of four electronic databases was conducted in December 2025, and 20 studies met the inclusion criteria. Both qualitative and quantitative studies were critically appraised and analyzed. Four key themes emerged: altered body perception, psychosocial effects, gender and societal influences, and symptom burden with associated treatments. Findings demonstrate that body image dissatisfaction extends beyond physical appearance and is closely linked to emotional distress, social withdrawal, stigma, and reduced health-related quality of life. Symptoms, medical treatments, and surgical interventions further contribute to negative body perception. Nurses are uniquely positioned to identify and address body image concerns through holistic assessment, patient education, emotional support, and advocacy for multidisciplinary care. Integrating body image assessment into routine nursing practice may improve patient engagement, psychosocial well-being, treatment adherence, and overall quality of life for individuals living with inflammatory bowel disease.
revue: Gastroenterology nursing : the official journal of the Society of Gastroenterology Nurses and Associates

titre: Has a consensus on alexithymia been reached? Letter to the Editor regarding Preece and Gross (2026)
A periodontal Piezo1-dependent brain-bone interoceptive circuit couples occlusal force to craniofacial bone homeostasis
resume: The skeleton continuously monitors mechanical state to maintain tissue homeostasis, but whether such interoceptive control operates in the craniofacial skeleton remains unclear. Here, we identify a brain-bone axis in which Piezo1 in Gli1-lineage periodontal mesenchymal stromal cells (Gli1-lineage MSCs) senses occlusal force and initiates prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)-dependent interoceptive signaling. Mechanistically, mechanical loading activates a transcriptional complex comprising YAP and Gli1 that directly promotes COX-2 expression and PGE2 production. This signal engages trigeminal sensory pathways and is associated with sustained ventromedial hypothalamic (VMH) activity and reduced paraventricular nucleus (PVN)-related sympathetic output. Disruption of this circuit under occlusal hypofunction elevates sympathetic tone, increasing osteoclast activity and impairing type H vessel formation. Importantly, conditional deletion of Piezo1 in Gli1-lineage MSCs largely abolished occlusal force-dependent regulation of VMH activity, sympathetic tone, and mandibular bone homeostasis, establishing its required role in this pathway. Our findings define a Piezo1-PGE2-mediated skeletal interoceptive circuit that links occlusal force to central sympathetic control of craniofacial bone mass, revealing a potential neuromechanical strategy for preventing disuse-induced bone loss.

titre: Cluster analysis based on alexithymia in young women: exploring addictions, psychological symptoms and relational vulnerability factors
resume: BACKGROUND: Alexithymia has been identified as a transdiagnostic risk factor for addictive behaviours. It has also been widely linked to various psychological risk factors related to addictions. OBJECTIVES: (I) to explore clusters of young women based on alexithymia and; (II) to examine differences between clusters in terms of addictive behaviours (gambling, alcohol, drugs and compulsive buying) and associated psychological symptoms. METHODS: The sample consisted of 239 women aged between 18 and 35 years. RESULTS: Three clusters were found based on the three subscales of alexithymia (TAS-20). Cluster 1 was characterised by lower scores on alexithymia and low scores on all variables. Cluster 2 was characterised by intermediate levels of identifying and describing emotions and high scores on hopelessness. Cluster 3 showed the highest levels of alexithymia, addictive behaviours and all other study variables except for hopelessness. CONCLUSIONS: Young women with addiction risk or problems may benefit from different preventive and therapeutic approaches depending on the alexithymia subscales.

titre: Psychological interventions for functional/dissociative seizures: A systematic review
resume: OBJECTIVE: Functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) have limited treatment options despite the major societal and personal impact of this condition. The efficacy of psychological interventions varies considerably and is influenced by social, economic, and personal factors. To guide future research on the condition, a systematic review of the published literature on the psychological treatments available for FDS was conducted. Current psychological interventions including diagnosis communication, psychoeducation, psychotherapy, hypnosis, and behavioural therapies have yet to show sufficient evidence of long-lasting successful treatment for FDS. The frequency and impact of FDS requires continued treatment development beyond the limited options currently available. Such treatments have been systematically reviewed for this purpose. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was carried out using the keywords: dissociative seizures, functional seizures, NEA, non-epileptic, pseudoseizures, psychogenic seizures, psychological treatment, hysterical seizures, and pseudoepileptic. Studies evaluating psychological treatments for FDS were included. Studies including patients with comorbid seizure disorders were also included. RESULTS: A total of 55 studies (58 publications) met the inclusion criteria. A wide variety of psychological interventions for FDS have been investigated. Existing evidence suggests that several psychological interventions may be effective, with cognitive behavioural therapy demonstrating the strongest evidence base. Promising findings were also reported for diagnosis communication, psychoeducation, psychodynamic therapy, mindfulness-based therapy, behavioural therapy, and combined treatment approaches. CONCLUSION: While a range of psychological treatments may be beneficial, cognitive behavioural therapy currently possesses the strongest evidence supporting its efficacy. However, no clear evidence suggests whether a particular intervention is most appropriate for specific patient subgroups. Structured diagnosis communication and psychoeducation appear to be valuable early interventions but may require additional psychological therapy to maintain treatment gains. Large studies of high methodological quality with longer follow-up periods are required to establish the most effective forms of treatment.

titre: Self-guided web-based mindfulness and skills-based distress reduction training versus treatment as usual optimised in patients with cancer (Reduct): a multicentre, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Electronic mental health (EMH) interventions in oncology offer low-threshold psychosocial support but efficacy research remains heterogeneous and lacking multicentre trials. OBJECTIVE: This trial assessed the efficacy of an EMH intervention compared with optimised treatment as usual (TAU-O) in reducing distress. METHODS: In this multicentre, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial, patients (18–65 years) with recent cancer diagnosis or progression (≤12 months) and elevated distress were recruited at eight university hospitals in Germany. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to the intervention or control condition. Randomisation was stratified by study centre using a computer-generated algorithm. The 16-week self-guided intervention provided structured psychosocial modules. TAU-O comprised psychosocial standard care and text-based digital information. The primary outcome was Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) total score at post-intervention (T1). Analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population using analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline and study centre, with multiple imputation for missing data. FINDINGS: Between 12 November 2021 and 22 April 2025, 1932 patients were assessed for eligibility, of whom 561 were randomly assigned (intervention n=281; control n=280) and included in the intention-to-treat population. The recruitment period was extended due to a 7-month recruitment pause following a cyberattack on the university’s information technology infrastructure. From baseline to T1, HADS scores decreased from 18.59 (SD 4.97) to 13.34 (6.67) in the intervention group and from 19.60 (5.43) to 15.13 (7.06) in the control group. The adjusted between-group difference in HADS score at T1 was −1.00 (95% CI −2.09 to 0.09; p=0.073) and not significant. Significant between-group differences were observed for the secondary outcomes anxiety symptoms and self-efficacy. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Both groups improved over time, with no significant between-group difference in distress. Significant improvements in anxiety symptoms and self-efficacy in the intervention group compared with the control group suggest potential benefits for selected secondary outcomes, although these findings require further confirmation. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Although the self-guided EMH intervention did not demonstrate superiority over optimised psychosocial cancer care in reducing distress, it may offer complementary benefits for selected mental health outcomes. EMH interventions may therefore be considered as adjuncts within stepped-care approaches. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: DRKS00025213.

titre: Smartphone-Delivered Cognitive Behavioral Digital Therapeutic for Children and Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder: Protocol for a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Depression is a leading contributor to morbidity and disability in children and adolescents. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a guideline-recommended first-line treatment, but access is constrained by therapist supply, distance, and stigma. Internet-based CBT is a scalable adjunct in adults, yet regulatory-grade evidence in Chinese pediatric samples remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This trial will determine whether a smartphone-delivered CBT-based digital therapeutic is superior to a matched health-education placebo in reducing depressive symptoms in Chinese children and adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD), and characterize its safety. METHODS: This is a prospective, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial at 4 tertiary-A hospitals in mainland China. Children and adolescents aged 8-17 years meeting DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders [Fifth Edition]) criteria for current MDD without psychotic features and scoring above 30 on the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R) at screening will be randomized 1:1 to the investigational digital therapeutic (Model WL-PD) or a visually matched health-education placebo. Both arms receive 8 weeks of structured content on an identical schedule; participants with CDRS-R ≥57 additionally receive open-label fluoxetine under weight-banded dosing. The primary end point is CDRS-R total-score reduction from baseline to week 8. Secondary end points include CDRS-R change at weeks 1 to 6; response and remission rates; Clinical Global Impression scores; the Children's Depression Inventory; the Conners' Parent Symptom Questionnaire; and a week-8 device-performance evaluation. Safety end points include adverse-event, serious adverse-event, and device-defect incidence. The planned sample of 214 participants (107 per arm) is powered at 80% to detect a between-arm difference of 4.6 CDRS-R points (assumed control SD 10.7) with a 1-sided α of .025 and 20% inflation for attrition. The primary analysis is an analysis of covariance on the full analysis set adjusting for baseline CDRS-R, severity category, fluoxetine exposure, and site; superiority is declared if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI excludes zero, with a mixed model for repeated measures as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: The trial opened to enrollment in March 2026; recruitment is ongoing, with a planned close in December 2026. The last week-8 visit is expected in the first quarter of 2027, and the primary analysis the following year. CONCLUSIONS: The trial addresses 3 recognized gaps in the pediatric digital therapeutics literature: a rigorous, structurally matched blinded control condition, recruitment beyond a single site, and integration of guideline-concordant pharmacotherapy. Because recruitment is confined to tertiary hospitals and excludes participants with prominent suicidality or comorbidity, findings will apply to supervised use in specialist services rather than unselected community care. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2600120453; https://tinyurl.com/3xzaajhp. INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/103430.

titre: Online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for people with multiple sclerosis with mild-to-moderate depression- protocol for a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study
resume: BACKGROUND: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is an effective treatment for recurrent depression in the general population and is recommended in clinical guidelines for those with mild-moderate depression. However, the effectiveness of MBCT in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) with mild to moderate depression is unknown. Further, how best to tailor and implement MBCT for PwMS is largely unstudied. This manuscript describes the study protocol for a hybrid-effectiveness study to evaluate online MBCT tailored for PwMS. METHODS: This type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study will employ an embedded mixed methods experimental design. Quantitative findings will be collected through a powered waitlist randomized controlled trial examining online MBCT in a minimum of 152 PwMS with case-ness of mild-moderate depression (Clinical Trials Gov #NCT07742579). The intervention will consist of an online 8-week MBCT course with weekly sessions conducted by qualified mindfulness instructors experienced int the care of PwMS. Questionnaires will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and 3 months later. The primary outcome will be depression, measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Score - Depression (HADS-D). An intention-to-treat analysis will be conducted. Qualitative findings will be collected through semi-structured interviews with 30-40 MBCT participants, HCPs, MBCT instructors, and MS decision makers. Thematic analyses will be used to analyze interview data. The RE-AIM PRISM tool will be used to evaluate implementation and mixed data assessed in a joint display. CONCLUSION: The results from this study will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of online MBCT in PwMS with mild to moderate depression, recommendations for intervention tailoring and implementation. Findings will be disseminated through traditional and novel, creative knowledge mobilization methods.

titre: Internet-delivered self-help acceptance and commitment therapy for family carers of people with dementia (iACT4CARERS): a mixed-methods process evaluation of reach and recruitment
resume: OBJECTIVES: A mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial of iACT4CARERS, an eight-session, online, self-help Acceptance and Commitment Therapy intervention with minimal therapist support for family carers of people with dementia. The study examined the reach of the intervention and factors influencing recruitment to inform equitable implementation. METHODS: Demographic data from 565 screened carers and interviews with 30 referrers across UK health services were analysed. RESULTS: The screened sample was predominantly aged 50-79 years (82.5%), female (77%), and White (91.7%). Five themes were identified: referrers' coordinated referrals, mutual motivation, and community outreach supported engagement; referrers' trust-building, tailored communication, and timely approaches facilitated participation; carers' time constraints and referrers' assumptions about older carers' digital skills influenced recruitment; proactive outreach was important for engaging ethnic minority carers; and cultural perceptions of mental health created barriers to participation. CONCLUSIONS: The sample was broadly comparable with previous estimates of the UK dementia carer population. For the equitable implementation of interventions such as iACT4CARERS, coordinated recruitment across health, social care, and voluntary organisations, alongside centralised intervention delivery, may be critical. Outreach can be further strengthened by enhancing referrers' communication and empowerment skills, including challenging assumptions about older carers' digital abilities.

titre: Accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation integrated with intensive exposure and response prevention therapy for refractory obsessive-compulsive disorder
resume: Exposure and response prevention (ERP) is a gold-standard treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and there is increasing interest in intensive approaches that provide treatment over a shortened timeframe. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an FDA-approved treatment for OCD that has similarly attracted interest in accelerated protocols. Yet there have been no reports on the combined use of intensive ERP ('iERP') and accelerated TMS ('aTMS'). Here, we demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating iERP and aTMS. We provided a 5-day course of aTMS-iERP for refractory OCD, with each day consisting of 8 ERP sessions in between 10 TMS sessions. In patients with severe and refractory OCD this novel approach was well tolerated, with positive clinical effects observed in each patient (N = 5). These early feasibility data suggest that innovative approaches to brain stimulation and psychotherapy should be explored not just in isolation but in combination with each other.

titre: Digital Tools for the Detection of Dermatitis: A Systematic Review
resume: Contact dermatitis (CD) plays a significant role in occupational health due to its frequent occurrence and environmental triggers and is among the most common occupational diseases in Western countries. Despite its prevalence, occupational contact dermatitis (OCD) is often overlooked by occupational physicians, largely due to limited knowledge and a lack of validated detection tools. Advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising opportunities for improving early detection, yet an overview of available digital tools and their effectiveness in dermatitis detection is lacking. A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cinahl, and Scopus. The search focused on original studies published in peer-reviewed journals between 2014 and 2024. Forty-three studies evaluating digital tools for dermatitis detection were included, categorized as models (n = 31) or devices (n = 12). Models represent AI algorithms not yet in practical use, while devices are tools already implemented. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) were the most commonly used computational technique. Median sensitivity and specificity were 0.84 and 0.97 for all tools, 0.85 and 0.97 for models, and 0.78 and 0.97 for devices. The results provided in this review will serve as valuable input for the development of new tools to enhance early OCD detection.

fiche.conclusion: Les technologies numériques et l'IA offrent des performances prometteuses pour le dépistage précoce de la dermatite de contact.

titre: What is the most efficacious target in deep brain stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder? A systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Introduction Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a therapeutic option for treatment-resistant obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD). Relative efficacy of regions that are currently being targeted for the treatment of OCD has not previously been investigated. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess and compare the efficacy of DBS treatment across conventional targets for OCD. Methods We performed a search of clinical studies investigating the efficacy of DBS for OCD. Relevant articles were retrieved from OVID, PubMed and Web of Science from database inception to 26 January 2026. For all studies, response rate to DBS treatment by region and changes in Yale-Brown Obsessive–Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) score over time were assessed. Results In total, 33 studies were included in the systematic review. Of which data of 447 unique patients across 30 studies were used to assess response rates by regions. Changes in Y-BOCS score were assessed using data from 363 patients from 27 studies. No significant difference in response rate was observed across targets. Of all stimulation targets, the ventral capsule/ventral striatum demonstrated highest pooled efficacy (SMCR=−7.92 (SMCR, standardised mean change using raw score standardisation); 95% CI (−12.16 to −3.68)). Conclusion Clinical studies underscore the efficacy of DBS for OCD, highlighting the effectiveness of stimulating the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis separately. Assessing the efficacy of all DBS targets better informs target selection for the treatment of OCD.
revue: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry

titre: Focused shock wave therapy improves histological scores for acute osteochondral defects in a skeletally immature porcine knee model
resume: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the capitellum presents a clinical challenge in preadolescent and adolescent athletes. Although debridement is effective, residual defects remain a persistent concern, typically resulting in inferior fibrocartilage rather than hyaline cartilage, despite the high intrinsic repair potential of cartilage in skeletally immature patients. Focused shock wave therapy (FSWT) shows promise in small animal models of osteochondral defects, but its efficacy in a clinically relevant, skeletally immature large animal model remains unknown. This study evaluated the effect of a single FSWT application on acute osteochondral defects intended to represent postdebridement tissue loss in a skeletally immature porcine knee model. METHODS: Bilateral medial femoral condyle osteochondral defects (5-mm diameter, 7-mm depth) were created in seven 6-week-old pigs. Right knees received a single FSWT application (2500 impulses, 0.20 mJ/mm2) directly to the defect immediately after its creation, and left knees served as untreated controls. At 6 weeks, evaluations included Goebel macroscopic and Niederauer histological scores, immunofluorescence analysis (SOX9, aggrecan, and COL2A1), and computed tomography to assess premature physeal closure. RESULTS: There was no statistically significant difference in the median Goebel macroscopic score between the FSWT and control groups (5.5 [interquartile range {IQR}, 3.5, 7.8] vs. 8.5 [IQR, 4.0, 9.0], lower is better; P = 0.397). The median Niederauer histological score was statistically significantly higher in the FSWT group (14.0 [13.3, 14.7] vs. 13.0 [11.3, 13.5]; P = 0.042). Immunofluorescence showed that the median percentage of SOX9-positive cells was statistically significantly greater in the FSWT group (20.1% [12.4, 22.3] vs. 11.6% [7.4, 18.4]; P = 0.018), as was the median aggrecan-positive immunoreactive fraction (15.2% [7.1, 18.5] vs. 7.1% [6.9, 10.7]; P = 0.028). The median COL2A1-positive immunoreactive fraction showed no statistically significant difference (4.0% [3.1, 7.8] vs. 2.8% [2.4, 4.9]; P = 0.499). No premature epiphyseal closure was observed at 6 weeks. CONCLUSION: A single FSWT application improved the 6-week histological repair of an acute osteochondral defect in a skeletally immature porcine model. This improvement was accompanied by statistically significant increases in the percentage of SOX9-positive cells and the aggrecan-positive immunoreactive fraction. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of FSWT. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Not Applicable, controlled laboratory study.
revue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine

titre: Lindera aggregata -derived Extracellular Vesicles Target Inflammation for Alleviating IBD associated psychiatric disorders via Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis
resume: Abstract Background The imbalance in the gut-brain is strongly associated with psychiatric conditions related to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and an effective treatment approach has not been established. Current oral treatments are limited due to the spatial and functional divide between gut inflammation and central nervous system (CNS) issues. Purpose The purpose of this research was to investigate the therapeutic impact of extracellular vesicles derived from Lindera aggregate leaf (LALEVs) and root (LAREVs) in alleviating DSS-induced intestinal damage and behavioral disorders in mice. Methods Dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) was used to establish an acute ulcerative colitis (UC) mouse model, and the mice were administered LALEVs and LAREVs orally. After the oral intervention, comprehensive assessments were performed utilizing pathological, biochemical, and molecular biological approaches, alongside 16S rRNA sequencing and behavioral evaluations, to examine intestinal barrier integrity, gut microbiome composition, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. Behavioral assessments were conducted to assess anxiety-, depressive-like behaviors, and cognitive impairment, while neuroinflammatory responses were evaluated by monitoring microglial and astrocytic activation, neuronal injury, and neuroinflammation. Potential targets were explored by serum proteomics, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), and network pharmacology, and verified by western blot. Results Oral administration of LALEVs or LAREVs targeted inflamed colon, effectively restoring the compromised barrier. Colon length normalized, weight loss ceased, and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were quieted. Behavioral tests indicated marked improvements in spontaneous activity and a substantial reduction in anxiety, depression-like behaviors, and cognitive impairment. Through by microbiota-gut-brain axis, LALEVs and LAREVs prevent LPS and inflammatory factors from entering the blood and suppress microglial and astrocyte activation in brain through modulating of TLR4/p38 MAPK axis, thereby reducing neuroinflammation and protecting against neural damage. Our work suggested that Lindera aggregate -derived extracellular vesicles could serve as a dual-target therapy for addressing IBD and psychiatric disorders.

titre: Perinatal high-fat diet induces systemic inflammation via altered tight junction complex organization during development and decreases expression of intestinal satiety peptides in male offspring
resume: ABSTRACT Objective Epidemiological evidence suggests that maternal obesity increases risk for offspring obesity and comorbidities, pointing to the significance of critical periods of development. Adverse metabolic effects of high fat (HF) diet consumption on the gut microbiome and inflammation have been well documented in obesity models. Emerging evidence demonstrates that the gut microbiome may play a role in transgenerational obesity, however, underlying mechanisms still need to be elucidated to identify intervention targets. Methods A rat model was used to demonstrate whether maternal HF diet during gestation and lactation results in gut-brain axis deficits in rat offspring. Gene expression of small intestinal satiety hormones and C-fiber innervation in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS) were measured in adult offspring. At weaning, circulating inflammatory mediators and colonic microbial metabolites were measured in offspring. Results In adulthood, HF males had reduced vagal innervation in the NTS and reduced small intestinal expression of CCK, GLP-1, and PYY. At weaning, HF offspring had elevated levels of CRP and IL-1β and depleted levels of microbially produced colonic short chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which are critical for maintaining intestinal barrier function. HF males had reduced colocalization between tight junction proteins, Claudin-1 and ZO-1 at weaning, while HF females did not. Conclusion Disorganization of tight junction complexes in HF male offspring during development may play a role in the gut-brain axis deficits seen in HF males in adulthood. Together, these data demonstrate that inflammation-induced by HF diet can negatively impact gut-brain axis development and function.

titre: Dietary Lipids Shape Neuroimmune Microenvironment in Alzheimer’s Disease: A Stage-Specific Framework for Precision Nutrition
resume: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is no longer viewed simply as a proteinopathy driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau. It also involves neuroimmune dysregulation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction, gut-brain axis perturbation, and peripheral metabolic imbalance. Dietary lipids are biologically distinct molecules that can influence these systems through membrane remodeling, lipid-mediator generation, receptor signaling, metabolic support, and central-peripheral crosstalk. Clinical studies of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and related lipid interventions have nevertheless produced inconsistent or negative results, which may reflect both genuinely limited efficacy in some settings and heterogeneity in lipid species, disease stage, formulation, exposure, and host background. We therefore place the proposed 4D framework within a broader systems-physiology concept of allostatic integrity: the capacity of interacting neural, glial, vascular, immune, and metabolic systems to adapt to repeated perturbations and return toward functional stability. We further use “biological memory” as an operational concept for persistent molecular and cellular state changes—such as epigenetic, metabolic, lipidomic, and glial-state remodeling—that can alter responses to subsequent challenges. The 4D framework comprises Disease stage, Dominant driver pathway, Delivery and formulation, and Data-guided stratification. It is intended as a hypothesis-generating research framework for trial design and stratification, not as a validated clinical algorithm. The 4D framework has not yet been prospectively validated, and its prospective utility remains to be tested.

titre: Nutritional Strategies for Managing Gastrointestinal Adverse Effects Associated with GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: A Narrative Review with Practical Recommendations
resume: Incretin-based therapies have marked a turning point in the treatment of obesity, because of their demonstrated effects on body weight and beyond, including numerous cardi-ometabolic outcomes. Within obesity management, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1 RAs) are, to date, the most effective pharma-cological strategies. A growing body of evidence, however, points to limited tolerability caused by gastrointestinal adverse effects, which may impair treatment adherence and reduce both quality of life and the nutritional adequacy of patients’ diets. These effects, which include nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, constipation, diarrhea, and abdominal bloating, are often observed in the early phases of treatment and during dose escalation. Yet the dietary recommendations available for their management remain fragmentary and inaccurate. This narrative review sets out to analyze the main pathophysiological mechanisms un-derlying the gastrointestinal manifestations of incretin-based therapies and to gather the available evidence on nutritional strategies for their prevention and management. We address the contribution of the GLP-1 and GIP systems to the modulation of gastroin-testinal motility, appetite, and clinical tolerability, with attention to the differences cur-rently recognized between selective GLP-1 RAs and dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs. We then present practical, symptom-specific recommendations covering meal distribution, mod-ulation of fat and fiber intake, hydration, food choices, and the overall quality of diet and lifestyle. Finally, we discuss the key role of nutrition in preservation adequate energy and protein intake, preventing micronutrient deficiencies, and conserving muscle mass throughout treatment with incretin-based therapies. A structured, personalized, symptom-oriented nutritional approach could improve the tolerability of these therapies, optimize clinical outcomes, and support their efficacy over the long term.

titre: Investigating reliability and internal consistency of the Spider, a multisystemic symptom screening tool for people with hypermobility related disorders
resume: Abstract Background: Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders (HSD) and hypermobile Ehlers Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) are often associated with symptoms affecting many bodily systems. The Spider questionnaire assesses eight common symptoms: pain, fatigue, neuromusculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, urogenital, cardiac dysautonomia, anxiety, and depression. This study evaluated the Spider’s reliability and internal consistency. Methodology: Ethical approval was obtained. Hypermobility support organisations aided recruitment through social media advertisements. Participants self-selected based on inclusion criteria and completed two online surveys, one-to-two weeks apart. Data collection included demographics, the Spider questionnaire and the SF-36/PEDS-QL. Relative reliability was assessed using Intraclass Correlation Coefficients (ICC). Absolute reliability was evaluated using the Standard Error of Measurement (SEM), Minimal Detectable Change (MDC), and Bland-Altman analysis. Pearson correlations with SF-36/PedsQL scores were compared across timepoints to monitor stability. Internal consistency was analysed using Cronbach’s alpha (α). Results: 617 participants aged 13-65 with HSD/hEDS or symptomatic hypermobility completed both surveys. Test-retest reliability was good to excellent in individual domains and total score (ICC: 0.79 to 0.92). SEM ranged from 4.0 to 11.60 and MDC from 11.08 to 32.13. Seven domains and the total score demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (α=0.70 to 0.91). The pain domain had marginally lower internal consistency (α=0.69). Conclusions: The Spider questionnaire demonstrated good to excellent test-retest reliability. Seven of the eight domains and the total score demonstrated acceptable internal consistency. These findings support the reliability of Spider scores for repeated measurement over time.

titre: A brief breathing challenge reveals a cardiac correlate of generalized anxiety beyond resting physiology and interoceptive measures
resume: Physiological markers measured at rest, such as heart rate variability, have proved relatively weak predictors of mental health symptoms. One potential reason is that resting measures are influenced by uncontrolled state factors, such as spontaneous breathing, whereas a standardized challenge holds these constant and may reveal regulatory differences not evident at rest. Here we asked whether respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) during slow paced breathing, a challenge that strongly increases RSA, carries information about symptoms beyond resting RSA and interoceptive measures. In 207 young adults (mean age 23.6 years, SD = 3.1), electrocardiogram (ECG) was recorded at rest and during slow (6 breaths/min) and fast (20 breaths/min) paced breathing. Lower RSA during slow breathing, relative to that predicted by resting RSA, was associated with more severe generalized anxiety symptoms (β = −0.21, BF₁₀ = 13), also when depressive symptoms were controlled, whereas resting RSA was not. The association was concentrated among participants with at least moderate anxiety symptoms, whose resting RSA was typical but whose rest-adjusted slow-breathing RSA was 0.62 SD lower, and who in exploratory analyses also showed weaker phase coupling between heart period and respiration. Interoceptive accuracy, measured with heartbeat counting or heart rate discrimination, was unrelated to symptoms, self-report and slow-breathing RSA, and interoceptive questionnaires tracked distress shared across anxiety and depressive symptoms rather than generalized anxiety symptoms. At the group level, slow-breathing RSA thus carries information about generalized anxiety symptoms beyond resting RSA and self-reported interoception. Brief paced-breathing challenges may therefore increase the sensitivity of autonomic markers in anxiety research and merit testing in clinical samples.

titre: Neural and Experiential Dynamics of High-Ventilation Breathwork Mirror Psychedelic States
resume: High-ventilation breathwork (HVB) is a simple breathing technique that nevertheless frequently triggers experiences resembling psychedelic states. While recent studies have begun to pinpoint physiological and neural changes involved in altered states of consciousness (ASCs) evoked by HVB, the interplay between neural and experiential dynamics throughout an HVB session remains unclear. Here we tracked neural activity (via 64-channel EEG recordings) as well as subjective experience depth and content in 25 experienced HVB practitioners across resting-state recordings interleaved throughout a naturalistic HVB session. We find that neural dynamics evoked by HVB emulate the most robust neural signatures of classical psychedelic states, specifically (1) loosening of temporal structure, including broadband cortical desynchronization, increased signal complexity, and decreased oscillatory power in the Alpha (8 - 13 Hz) range, and (2) reorganization of spatial structure, including a flattening of cortical processing hierarchy. These neural effects directly correlated with participants’ subjective depth with minute resolution, but were not explained by isolated features of HVB such as music listening or active interoception. Together, these results identify unifying neural features of psychedelic-like ASCs regardless of induction method, demonstrating that cortical states triggered by psychedelics can also be accessed by non-pharmacological routes, and breathwork is a powerful way to do so.
