titre: Bacterial Preconditioning Differentially Reshapes Neuronal Responses to Intermittent and Continuous Hypoxia-Like Stress
resume: Abstract The microbiota–gut–brain axis exposes the nervous system to microbial information, but whether such exposure becomes part of the biological history that shapes later neuronal stress responses remains unknown. Here, we tested whether transient direct exposure to live Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ( L. plantarum ) alters how differentiated B35 neuronal cells subsequently respond to hypoxia-like metabolic stress. We compared two trajectories combining chemical HIF stabilization with nutrient restriction: an intermittent, sublethal condition with recovery periods (MHX), relevant to recurrent vascular insufficiency, and a continuous severe condition (SHX). These trajectories generated distinct structural, metabolic and transcriptional states. Prior L. plantarum exposure was associated with higher MTT-derived metabolic viability after MHX but not SHX, and induced broader transcriptional reorganization under MHX (167 versus 64 differentially expressed genes), engaging signaling and cytoskeletal programs together with pathways linked to negative regulation of apoptosis and oxidative-stress-induced cell death. Only one bacterially responsive gene was shared between the two stress trajectories. Thus, L. plantarum did not impose a fixed neuroprotective program. Instead, prior microbial exposure acted as a biological input whose consequences depended on the subsequent stress trajectory. These findings establish neuron–bacteria communication as history-dependent and define an adaptive range in which microbial signals can influence neuronal responses before metabolic stress becomes overwhelming—a principle relevant to preventive intervention during recurrent vascular stress.

fiche.verdict: L'exposition préalable à des bactéries (L. plantarum) modifie de façon dépendante du stress les réponses neuronales au stress métabolique in vitro.
fiche.population: Cellules neuronales B35
fiche.intervention: Exposition à Lactiplantibacillus plantarum suivie de stress hypoxique intermittent (MHX) ou continu (SHX)
resultats_cles: Viabilité métabolique améliorée après MHX (mais pas SHX) suite à l'exposition bactérienne.
Réorganisation transcriptionnelle spécifique (167 gènes différentiels en MHX).
fiche.conclusion: La communication neurone-bactérie est dépendante de l'historique d'exposition et influence l'adaptation au stress vasculaire récurrent.
limites: Étude in vitro sur lignée cellulaire
Modèle animal/cellulaire non transposable directement en clinique
fiche.pertinence_raison: Axe intestin-cerveau et mécanismes cellulaires du stress, pertinent en psychogastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Préconditionnement bactérien et stress neuronal
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'exposition bactérienne préalable module la résistance neuronale au stress hypoxique intermittent de façon spécifique.

titre: The role of Sacral TENS in Improving Continence and Quality of Life in Children with Anorectal Malformations: A six-year Follow-up
resume: Abstract PURPOSE Anorectal malformations are congenital defects of the posterior intestinal development, leading to structural and functional abnormalities of the rectum and/or anal canal. Typically, these patients develop long-term constipation or fecal incontinence, which can be challenging to manage. Sacral transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) is a non-invasive technical alternative initially studied for bladder elimination disorders and has been increasingly established as a tool for treating intestinal dysfunctions. This study aims to observe outcomes in patients who underwent surgery for anorectal malformations and received TENS therapy. METHODS: A longitudinal and retrospective observational study (2018 to 2024). Included children with corrected anorectal malformation, aged 4 to 15 years who underwent TENS therapy. The analysis considered medication use, quality of life through the Paulista Continence Score, and anorectal manometry at three time points: before TENS application, four weeks and six years post TENS. RESULTS: Eleven children were included, 6 had low anorectal malformations and 5 had high anorectal malformations. Among these patients, 81.81% used some type of laxative or bowel management before application, and six years after the treatment, the immediate post-results remained, only 27.27% of patients used some type of laxative or bowel management. Applying São Paulo Continence Score 36.36% were classified as a continent before TENS, increasing to 75% continence six years after TENS. The number of Paulista score had shown improvement through time (χ² (2) = 29.7, p < 0.001). Post-TENS and late follow-up scores were significantly lower than pre-TENS scores (post vs. pre: p = 0.005; late vs. pre: p < 0.001), and late follow-up scores were also significantly lower than post-TENS scores (late vs. post: p = 0.012). Manometric evaluation did not show statistical significance when analyzing resting pressure and average contraction pressure, neither intra-rectal volumes across the three time points. CONCLUSION: patients with anorectal malformation improved clinical outcomes with TENS therapy and can be used for treating elimination disorders.

fiche.verdict: La neurostimulation électrique transcutanée sacrée (TENS) améliore durablement la continence fécale et réduit l'usage de laxatifs chez l'enfant opéré d'une malformation anorectale.
fiche.population: 11 enfants (4-15 ans) avec malformation anorectale opérée
fiche.intervention: TENS sacrée vs état pré-intervention
resultats_cles: Baisse de l'usage des laxatifs de 81,8% à 27,3% à 6 ans.
Hausse de la continence (Score de Paulista) de 36,4% à 75% à 6 ans (p<0,001).
Pas d'effet significatif sur la manométrie ano-rectale.
fiche.conclusion: La TENS sacrée améliore les symptômes cliniques d'élimination chez ces patients sur le long terme.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Hors champ direct (pédiatrie chirurgicale), mais illustre l'effet de la neuromodulation sur les troubles sphinctériens.
fiche.titre_court: TENS sacrée et continence fécale pédiatrique
fiche.conclusion_simple: La TENS sacrée semble réduire l'incontinence et l'usage de laxatifs à long terme chez l'enfant, malgré un effectif très limité.

titre: Factors Associated with Anastomotic Leak After Colostomy Reversal in Northwest Ethiopia: A Retrospective Case–Control Study
resume: Abstract Anastomotic leak is a feared complication after gastrointestinal surgery; however, the risk factors following colostomy reversal in low-resource settings remain poorly defined. We conducted an institution-based case–control study at Debre Markos Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, northwest Ethiopia, using data from all patients who underwent colostomy reversal between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2024. Cases were patients with a documented anastomotic leak during the index hospitalization or within 30 days postoperatively, while controls had no anastomotic leak. Data were extracted using a pretested checklist and analyzed using binary logistic regression. Of 225 eligible patients, 56 (24.9%) developed an anastomotic leak. Factors independently associated with anastomotic leak were residence more than 60 km from the hospital (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 8.45, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.43–20.83), colostomy duration of less than 3 months (AOR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.10–5.82), comorbid illness (AOR = 5.15, 95% CI: 1.97–13.49), significant intraoperative adhesions (AOR = 2.73, 95% CI: 1.15–6.49), a short distal stump (AOR = 2.82, 95% CI: 1.18–6.74), iatrogenic bowel injury (AOR = 3.20, 95% CI: 1.09–9.46), failure to pass flatus within 72 hours (AOR = 5.84, 95% CI: 1.63–20.91), and other postoperative complications (AOR = 3.48, 95% CI: 1.03–11.73). Anastomotic leak after colostomy reversal is influenced by patient-related, geographic, intraoperative, and postoperative factors, several of which are modifiable. Preoperative optimization, appropriate timing of reversal, meticulous adhesiolysis, avoidance of bowel injury, careful assessment of the distal stump, and vigilant postoperative monitoring may reduce leak-related morbidity and mortality in similar resource-constrained settings.

fiche.verdict: Une étude rétrospective éthiopienne identifie les facteurs de risque de fuite anastomotique après stomie, soulignant l'impact des comorbidités et de l'éloignement.
fiche.population: 225 patients (56 avec fuite, 169 contrôles) ayant eu une fermeture de colostomie
fiche.intervention: facteurs associés à la fuite anastomotique vs absence de fuite
resultats_cles: Taux de fuite anastomotique de 24,9%.
Facteurs de risque incluant l'éloignement géographique (>60 km), les comorbidités et des adhérences per-opératoires.
Délai de reprise du transit >72h fortement prédictif (AOR=5,84).
fiche.conclusion: Plusieurs facteurs modifiables et non modifiables influencent le risque de fuite, nécessitant une optimisation pré et post-opératoire.
limites: Contexte de pays à ressources limitées
fiche.pertinence_raison: Chirurgie digestive lourde, sans lien direct avec la psychogastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Facteurs de fuite après fermeture de colostomie
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les complications post-opératoires de stomie dépendent de facteurs cliniques et logistiques ciblables.

titre: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Non-Inferiority Trial Comparing Microbial and Porcine Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Chronic Pancreatitis (Np-Pert Trial) - Protocol
resume: Abstract Background Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a progressive inflammatory disorder causing irreversible pancreatic damage, eventually resulting in pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (PEI). This may lead to malabsorption, malnutrition, weight loss, and impaired quality of life. Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) is the standard treatment for PEI and is predominantly derived from porcine sources. However, religious, ethical, dietary, and supply-related concerns highlight the need for effective non-porcine alternatives. Microbial based pancreatic enzymes have shown promising safety and efficacy in preliminary studies, but evidence in CP remains limited. Objective To compare the efficacy and safety of non-porcine microbial -based pancreatin with standard porcine-based pancreatin in patients with PEI secondary to CP. Methods This investigator-initiated, randomized, double-blind, single-center, non-inferiority trial will enroll 134 adults with CP-associated PEI (defined as having a faecal elastase 1.4. After a two-week washout period, participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive either microbial-based or porcine-based pancreatin for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change from baseline in the PEI-Q score at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes include nutritional status, anthropometric measures, gastrointestinal symptoms, pain scores, stool consistency, glycemic parameters, laboratory markers, and quality of life. Discussion This study aims to evaluate whether microbial-based pancreatin is non-inferior to porcine-based therapy and may provide a culturally acceptable and sustainable alternative for managing CP-related PEI.

fiche.verdict: Protocole d'essai clinique randomisé comparant l'efficacité d'enzymes pancréatiques microbiennes versus porcines dans l'insuffisance pancréatique exocrine liée à la pancréatite chronique.
fiche.population: 134 adultes souffrant de pancréatite chronique avec insuffisance pancréatique exocrine
fiche.intervention: Enzymes microbiennes vs enzymes porcines (PERT) pendant 12 semaines
resultats_cles: Objectif principal : variation du score PEI-Q à 12 semaines.
Évaluation de la non-infériorité des enzymes d'origine non porcine.
fiche.conclusion: L'étude vise à évaluer une alternative culturelle et éthique aux extraits porcins habituels.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Concerne la digestion et les enzymes, mais cible la pancréatite chronique organique.
fiche.titre_court: Protocole essai enzymes microbiennes pancréatite
fiche.conclusion_simple: Ce protocole teste une alternative aux enzymes porcines pour l'insuffisance pancréatique.

titre: Capturing continuous spectrotemporal pupil–brain coupling with simultaneous wearable EEG/Eye tracking
resume: Spontaneous fluctuations in pupil diameter are closely linked to neural dynamics, yet most evidence for pupil–brain coupling has been obtained in conventional laboratory settings. We therefore asked whether the spectrotemporal and directional organization of such coupling can be captured with wearable systems to test their use in naturalistic settings. Using combined lightweight mobile EEG (MUSE) and eye tracking (Tobii Pro Glasses 3) devices, we investigated resting-state pupil–brain coupling and explored interoceptive attention to determine whether the core organizational principles observed with stationary equipment are detectable within and preserved across continuous recording states. Cross-correlation, mutual information, and Granger causality analyses revealed that pupil–brain coupling displayed clear frequency-dependent organization. Lower EEG frequencies (2-12Hz) preceded pupil dynamics by roughly 764ms, while higher frequencies showed a distinct coupling range. Granger-causality analysis further indicated predominantly EEG-to-pupil directional coupling. Similar observations were made during interoception. Overall, these findings align well and extend previous evidence on spontaneous pupil–brain coupling, demonstrating that lightweight and movable wearable devices are suitable to characterize spectrotemporal and directional pupil– brain interactions. In turn, these results encourage future fundamental and translational research in naturalistic environments.

fiche.verdict: Une étude démontre que des dispositifs portables légers (EEG et eye-tracking) captent fidèlement le couplage pupille-cerveau au repos et en intéroception.
fiche.intervention: Enregistrement simultané EEG mobile et eye-tracking en conditions naturelles et d'intéroception.
resultats_cles: Couplage pupille-cerveau dépendant de la fréquence (ondes basses 2-12Hz précédant la dynamique pupillaire).
Directionnalité principalement de l'EEG vers la pupille.
fiche.conclusion: Les appareils portables légers conviennent pour caractériser les interactions pupille-cerveau en environnement naturel.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour l'intéroception mais méthodologique et préclinique.
fiche.titre_court: Couplage pupille-cerveau par EEG portable et eye-tracking
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les outils portables permettent d'étudier l'intéroception et les dynamiques neuro-végétatives en vie réelle.

titre: Somatic symptom burden is associated with anger internalization measured as reduced reactive aggression
resume: Objectives Difficulties in emotion regulation, including anger suppression, have been linked to more severe somatic symptoms in patients with chronic pain. Because this evidence comes mainly from clinical samples, it remains unclear whether such difficulties precede or follow symptom chronification. We examined whether somatic symptom burden is associated with reduced reactive aggression, as a behavioral marker of anger internalization. Method Forty-four healthy adults (25 females) completed the Taylor Aggression Paradigm, a competitive reaction-time task in which they selected noise intensity delivered to a fictitious opponent across three provocation conditions (low, moderate, and high). somatic symptom burden was evaluated using the Somatic Symptom Scale-8 (SSS-8) and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15). Alexithymia was evaluated using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20). Results Participants with higher somatic symptom burden selected lower noise intensities overall, with significant differences at low and moderate provocation levels. Difficulty identifying feelings tended to be positively associated with somatic symptom burden, whereas alexithymia was not associated with reactive aggression. Discussion These findings suggest that inhibited retaliation, previously reported in chronic pain patients, may already be present in healthy individuals with higher somatic symptom burden, potentially aiding early identification of chronic pain risk. Difficulty distinguishing emotions from bodily sensations may also contribute to somatic symptom expression.

fiche.verdict: Une étude transversale montre qu'un fardeau de symptômes somatiques élevé est associé à une réduction de l'agression réactive chez des adultes sains.
fiche.population: 44 adultes sains (25 femmes)
fiche.intervention: Tâche de paradigme d'agression de Taylor, questionnaires SSS-8, PHQ-15 et TAS-20.
resultats_cles: Les participants avec plus de symptômes somatiques choisissent des intensités de bruit plus faibles (agression récurrente inhibée).
Difficulté à identifier les sentiments positivement liée au fardeau somatique.
fiche.conclusion: L'inhibition de la colère est présente chez les sujets sains ayant des symptômes somatiques, ce qui rapproche l'alexithymie de la somatisation.
limites: Étude transversale ne prouvant pas la causalité
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien direct entre alexithymie, symptômes somatiques et inhibition de la colère (proche SII).
fiche.titre_court: Symptômes somatiques et internalisation de la colère
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'inhibition de la colère et la difficulté à identifier ses émotions caractérisent les sujets à forte charge somatique.

titre: Anxiety and Depressive Symptom Trajectories During Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Incorporating Gratitude Touch: Implications for Multimodal Mental Health Care
resume: Background: /Objectives: Brief nonpharmacological exercises may complement psychotherapy within multimodal mental health care, although their specific contribution to symptom change requires controlled evaluation. We described 12-month psychological symptom trajectories in women receiving cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) that included the Gratitude Touch exercise. Methods: This single-group, non-randomized study included 50 women aged 25–45 years. Weekly individual CBT sessions incorporated tactile contact with each finger, verbalized gratitude, and brief bodily observation. DASS-21, Endler Multidimensional Anxiety Scales (EMAS), and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores were assessed at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months. Longitudinal differences were examined using Friedman tests and Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon comparisons. Results: Mean DASS-21 Anxiety scores decreased from 13.30 at baseline to 8.72 at 3 months, then increased to 11.44 at 6 months and 11.94 at 12 months. The reported omnibus difference was significant (χ²(3) = 127.40, adjusted p < 0.001; Kendall’s W = 0.8493). Depression and stress subscales showed a similar early decrease followed by partial rebound. EMAS-S and BDI-II means decreased at intermediate assessments but matched baseline values at 12 months; conflicting paired-test summaries limit interpretation of these endpoints. Conclusions: The cohort showed temporal symptom variation during combined nonpharmacological therapy, rather than consistent improvement across all measures. Without a CBT-only comparison, the added contribution of Gratitude Touch and its clinical significance remain undetermined.

fiche.verdict: Une thérapie cognitivo-comportementale combinée à un exercice de toucher de gratitude montre des variations temporelles des symptômes anxieux et dépressifs chez les femmes.
fiche.population: 50 femmes âgées de 25 à 45 ans
fiche.intervention: Séances de TCC hebdomadaires intégrant l'exercice 'Gratitude Touch' sur 12 mois
resultats_cles: Baisse initiale des scores d'anxiété (DASS-21) à 3 mois, suivie d'une remontée à 6 et 12 mois.
Absence de groupe de comparaison TCC seule.
fiche.conclusion: Variations temporelles des symptômes observées, mais l'absence de groupe contrôle empêche de déterminer l'effet propre de l'exercice.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour l'évaluation d'outils somatiques et psycho-corporels en TCC.
fiche.titre_court: TCC et toucher de gratitude : trajectoires
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'ajout d'un exercice tactile à la TCC montre des fluctuations symptomatiques, mais l'efficacité spécifique reste à prouver sans groupe contrôle.

titre: Altered pre-supplementary motor area recruitment during semantic inhibition in individuals with elevated obsessive–compulsive traits
resume: Background: Inhibitory control dysfunction has been implicated in obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD), but neuroimaging research has focused predominantly on motor response inhibition. Whether obsessive–compulsive traits are associated with altered neural recruitment during semantic inhibition remains unclear. Methods: Forty right-handed participants with lower or elevated obsessive–compulsive traits performed an fMRI adaptation of the Hayling Sentence Completion Task. Participants either selected an expected sentence completion (initiation) or suppressed this strongly prepotent response to select an unrelated word (inhibition). Whole-brain and anatomically defined region-of-interest (ROI) analyses examined task-related activation and Group × Condition interactions, with particular interest in the pre-supplementary motor area (preSMA) and SMA proper. Results: Semantic inhibition produced a robust behavioural cost in reaction times and error rates, with no significant differences between groups. Whole-brain analysis identified the strongest inhibition-related activation in the left preSMA. The exploratory Group × Condition analysis also yielded its peak interaction in this region. Anatomically defined ROI analysis showed a significant Group × Condition interaction in the preSMA after family-wise error correction (t = 2.56, pFWE = .012), reflecting a larger inhibition-related increase in controls compared to individuals with elevated obsessive–compulsive traits. The corresponding interaction in SMA proper did not reach statistical significance (t = 1.74, pFWE = .084). Conclusions: Elevated obsessive–compulsive traits were associated with altered preSMA recruitment during semantic inhibition in absence of behavioural impairment. This extends neural markers of obsessive–compulsive alterations from the domain of motor inhibition to that of semantic inhibition.

titre: Association between serum ghrelin concentrations and depression severity in patients with irritable bowel syndrome: a clinic-based case–control study
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastrointestinal disease commonly associated with psychological comorbidities. Ghrelin, a gut-derived peptide hormone participated in gut-brain axis regulation, may play a role in both gastrointestinal and emotional symptoms. This study aimed to investigate the association between ghrelin levels in serum and depression severity in a Northwestern Iranian patients with IBS. In this case–control study, 140 IBS patients (diagnosed based on Rome III criteria) and 115 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. Depression severity was assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Also, serum ghrelin concentrations were measured via an enzyme-linked immune-sorbent assay (ELISA). Statistical analyses included independent t-test, ANOVA, linear regression, and Pearson’s correlation analysis. Our results showed that IBS patients had significantly lower ghrelin levels compared to healthy controls ( P = 0.001). IBS patients with minimal, mild, moderate, or severe depressive symptoms (≥ 29) exhibited lower ghrelin levels than controls with mild depression (All, P = 0.00). Serum ghrelin levels were inversely correlated with IBS severity ( r = − 0.18, P = 0.001). Also, serum ghrelin remained a significant predictor of BDI-II score (standardized β = −0.442, P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, serum ghrelin remained independently associated with depression severity after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI ( P < 0.001). Decreased ghrelin levels in IBS patients are linked to higher depression severity and this issue is the major driver of disease severity. These findings suggest a potential role of the gut–brain axis in the IBS and psychological symptoms interactions. However, further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms since causal relationships cannot be inferred based on the cross-sectional study.

fiche.verdict: Une ghrelin sérique basse est liée à une dépression plus sévère chez les patients SII.
fiche.population: 255 participants : 140 patients SII (Rome III) et 115 témoins sains
fiche.intervention: ghrelin sérique (exposition) chez patients SII vs témoins sains
resultats_cles: Ghrelin plus bas chez les patients SII (P = 0,001)
Corrélation inverse avec la sévérité du SII (r = −0,18, P = 0,001)
Ghrelin prédit la sévérité dépressive (β = −0,442, P < 0,001)
fiche.conclusion: Une ghrelin diminuée est associée à une sévérité dépressive et à la sévérité du SII.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien biologique ghrelin-dépression-sévérité SII
fiche.titre_court: Ghrelin, dépression et sévérité du SII
fiche.conclusion_simple: Une ghrelin basse pourrait refléter une dépression plus sévère chez les patients SII, sans preuve de causalité.

titre: Diet and synbiotics in the gut–immune–brain axis: implications for gastrointestinal and psychological health
resume: The gut microbiota participates in gut–immune–brain communication through metabolic, immune, neural and endocrine pathways. Dietary patterns and microbiota-directed interventions, including prebiotics, probiotics and synbiotics, may affect these pathways, but biological responses do not necessarily translate into clinical benefit. We examine mechanistic and human evidence, focusing on disorders of gut–brain interaction, particularly irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and on psychological outcomes. Selected synbiotic trials report improvements in gastrointestinal symptoms, although formulations, populations, comparators and endpoints differ substantially. Evidence for psychological benefit is less consistent and remains limited by small or uncontrolled studies. Human milk oligosaccharides illustrate the potential for selective substrate use, but their clinical value in adults requires further testing. Future trials should specify the intended clinical effect, select appropriate comparators and measure microbial, metabolic and host responses alongside validated symptoms.

fiche.verdict: Les synbiotiques améliorent les symptômes gastro-intestinaux du SIB/TMF, mais les bénéfices psychologiques restent incohérents et limités.
fiche.population: Patients souffrant de troubles de l'interaction intestin-cerveau (notamment syndrome de l'intestin irritable - SII)
fiche.intervention: Interventions ciblant le microbiote (prébiotiques, probiotiques, synbiotiques) et régimes vs comparateurs variés
resultats_cles: Amélioration des symptômes gastro-intestinaux dans certains essais de synbiotiques.
Preuves de bénéfices psychologiques moins cohérentes, limitées par de petits effectifs ou l'absence de contrôle.
Nécessité d'études futures standardisées mesurant les réponses microbiennes et les symptômes validés.
fiche.conclusion: Les interventions sur le microbiote montrent un potentiel gastro-intestinal mais nécessitent des essais rigoureux pour confirmer les effets psychologiques.
limites: Hétérogénéité des formulations, populations et critères d'évaluation.
Études souvent de petite taille ou non contrôlées.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Cible directement le SII et les liens psychologiques en psychogastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Synbiotiques et axe intestin-cerveau dans le SII
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les synbiotiques soulagent les symptômes digestifs du SII, mais leurs effets psychologiques restent à consolider par des essais rigoureux.

titre: Sattvic Diet and Gut-Brain Axis Scoping Review
resume: Scoping review to compare the impact of a Sattvic diet on the Gut-Brain axis and other secondary markers of health.

titre: Gut-brain axis and neuroinflammation: mechanisms, interactions, and recent advances
resume: In recent years, the gut-brain axis (GBA), an essential bidirectional communication network linking the gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) functions, has attracted increasing research interest at the intersection of microbiology and neuroscience. This pathway is involved in multiple physiological and pathological conditions including emotion regulation, cognitive function and neuroinflammation through neural, immune, endocrine and metabolic mechanisms. Based on human observational studies, animal models and in-vitro experiments, there is evidence that gut dysbiosis is also related to intestinal barrier dysfunction, altered microbial metabolites and neuroinflammatory response. Evidence is largely preclinical or mechanistic, whereas human data are currently more limited for causal relationships. Signal transfer involves three components: the vagus nerve, immune mediators and the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Microbiota-targeted interventions have been shown to yield proportionally consistent mechanistic benefits in preclinical models, whereas human intervention studies remain heterogeneous and show mixed positive and null outcomes—among these microbiota-targeted interventions there are probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and dietary modulation. Hence, their clinical utility for neuroinflammatory disorders is only preliminary and needs to be validated in bigger, placebo-controlled trials. Although the present studies are confronted with difficulties, which include unclear causality and great individual variations among subjects, GBA research has been gradually moving into a novel stage from the perspective of mechanistic explanation and precision intervention along with advancements in multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence, generating new theoretical hypotheses and translational significance for the prevention or treatment of neuroinflammatory diseases.

fiche.verdict: Montre mécanismes de l'axe gut-brain et neuroinflammation, mais preuves humaines limitées.
resultats_cles: Communication gut-cerveau bidirectionnelle.
Neuroinflammation via mécanismes neuronaux, immunitaires, endocriniens, métaboliques.
Données humaines causales limitées ; interventions ciblées préliminaires.
fiche.conclusion: Les preuves restent largement précliniques et l'usage clinique des interventions ciblées est préliminaire.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intérêt GBA, mais données humaines limitées.
fiche.titre_court: Microbiote et neuroinflammation
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les preuves sur l'axe intestin-cerveau et l'inflammation cérébrale sont encore limitées chez l'homme.

titre: Research Progress on Using Non-drug Traditional Chinese Medicine Interventions to Treat Parkinson's Disease by Regulating the Gut-Brain Axis
resume: Conventional Western medical treatments for Parkinson's disease (PD) still have limitations in terms of maintaining efficacy and managing adverse reactions; the "microbiota-gut-brain" axis offers a new perspective in this regard. The Braak hypothesis suggests that α-synuclein can enter the brain via the vagus nerve, and damage to the intestinal barrier and TLR4-mediated intestinal inflammation are key links in neurodegeneration along the gut-brain axis. This article reviewed the mechanisms and clinical evidence supporting the prevention and treatment of PD through therapies such as acupuncture (body, electroacupuncture, scalp, ocular, and abdominal), moxibustion, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) exercises, and auricular acupuncture. In terms of mechanism, the evidence is fairly clear for electroacupuncture. It upregulated colonic GPR40/43, elevated GLP-1, and activated neuroprotective pathways such as PI3K-AKT-GSK3β through the gut microbiota–brain axis. By comparison, animal studies on other therapies mostly described broader effects, including modulation of the microbiota, repair of intestinal permeability, and inhibition of enteric inflammation. Clinical observations also suggested some symptom improvement. These therapies appear to improve motor symptoms and, to varying degrees,non-motor symptoms such as constipation, insomnia, and depression. One study reported an overall efficacy rate of 93.3% for ocular acupuncture, which was higher than the 75.6% observed for body acupuncture (single study). Still, this comparison should be treated cautiously. Most of the available evidence came from animal experiments and small-sample observational studies, with few direct cross-comparisons between therapies. For that reason, the gut-brain axis mechanisms involved in ocular acupuncture and scalp acupuncture still need closer examination and confirmation in large-sample multicenter studies.

fiche.verdict: Les thérapies non médicamenteuses en MTC améliorent les symptômes moteurs et non moteurs de Parkinson en agissant sur l'axe intestin-cerveau.
fiche.population: Patients atteints de la maladie de Parkinson
fiche.intervention: Interventions de médecine traditionnelle chinoise sans médicaments (acupuncture, moxibustion, exercices MTC) vs comparateurs divers

titre: Gut Microbiota and Emotional Eating Behavior: Neuropsychological Pathways Involving Stress, Anxiety and Depression
resume: Emotional eating is described as eating without feeling physically hungry to cope with stress, anxiety and negative emotions. Hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis activity associated with stress, anxiety and depression, along with changes in cortisol levels and neurobiological processes that regulate appetite and reward mechanisms, can trigger emotional eating behavior. The gut microbiota may influence emotional eating through modulation of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis activity, as hypothesized from a neuropsychological perspective. The aim of this review is to evaluate the neurobiological and neuropsychological mechanisms associated with stress, anxiety and depression that may play a role in the potential relationship between the gut microbiota and emotional eating; to provide a comprehensive perspective on the current evidence regarding these mechanisms. The gut microbiota is a dynamic ecosystem that regulates metabolic, immune and neuroendocrine homeostasis through host-microbiota interactions. The gut microbiota may influence the gut–brain axis through the metabolism of short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan and GABA, along with BDNF and FXR/TGR5 signaling pathways, thereby regulating emotional eating behaviors associated with stress, anxiety and depression. As a result, alterations in the gut microbiota can affect emotional eating associated with stress, anxiety and depression through various pathways. Current evidence is largely based on in vitro and animal studies, while human studies are mostly observational, limiting causal inferences regarding the relationships between gut microbiota, depression, anxiety, and stress. Future studies should address the impact of the gut microbiota on emotional eating through individualized intervention studies that evaluate stress, anxiety and depression.

titre: Editorial: Impact of gut probiotic metabolites on human metabolic diseases
resume: irritable bowel syndrome, a multifactorial disorder with abdominal pain, altered bowel habits and multifaceted interactions among the gut microbiome. The importance of evaluating probiotic efficiency at the strain level rather than at the species level, with particular emphasis on their metabolites, notably short-chain fatty acids, is highlighted. Inadequate dietary control and incomplete strain, dose, and biomarker assessments limit the application of probiotics for IBD (Mora Guzmán et al., 2026) .The effects of probiotics, Lactobacillus plantarum strain LP-115 and Bifidobacterium bifidum strain BB-06, on gut microbiota functions were investigated among liver failure cases. Rats supplemented with probiotics showed increased levels of SCFAs and decreased levels of toxic metabolites, such as ammonia. Shotgun metagenomic reconstruction of faecal DNA provided comprehensive insights into the metabolic potential of the microbiome (Luo et al., 2026).The effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, Lactobacillus plantarum, and Bifidobacterium longum on intestinal barrier function and hepatic injury in an animal model of fulminant liver failure (FLF) has been reported in this study. Probiotic treatment reduced intestinal hyperpermeability and restored tight junction integrity. In addition, probiotics reduced serum levels of alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, bilirubin, ammonia, oxidative stress markers and pro-inflammatory cytokines.Histopathological examination of liver tissue showed reduced hepatocellular injury and apoptosis.Probiotics may represent an effective therapeutic approach for protecting against FLF (C. Wu et al., 2026).Random forest models classified disease stages with 89.3% accuracy and identified key microbial markers, providing microbiome signatures as potential diagnostic, severity, and personalized therapeutic tools for H. pylori-related diseases. H. pylori eradication therapy along with probiotics might enhance eradication rates, reduce the side effects associated with antibiotics, help to preserve gut and oral microbiota and support their use as adjunctive therapy (X. Wu et al., 2025). Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 reduces IL-6 and TNF-α levels, increases intestinal occludin expression, and improves gut microbial composition and diversity in a rat model of sepsis. It stimulated the growth of beneficial bacteria and inhibited the growth of harmful bacteria, suggesting a potential to block disruption of the intestinal barrier and inflammation (Liu et al., 2025).In a double-blind randomized controlled trial, probiotics improved irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms by modulating increased fecal acetate, propionate, and butyrate levels; enhancing intestinal barrier integrity and tight-junction protein expression; and decreasing inflammation. Higher SCFA levels were associated with symptom improvement, highlighting the possible role of SCFAs in probiotic benefits. Overall, probiotics seem safe and effective for treating IBS through SCFA production, barrier strengthening, and anti-inflammatory effects (E. Li et al., 2025). A network metaanalysis of 29 randomized controlled trials with 4,389 patients showed that fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) had the best improvement in bowel movements and stool consistency and acupuncture had a good clinical response. Probiotics had the lowest risk of adverse events. This study supports FMT, with or without acupuncture, as a promising treatment for functional constipation, but further high-quality studies are needed (Tan et al., 2025).The gut microbiome is a key factor influencing host energy metabolism. The review highlights the role of probiotic-fermented herbal residues in managing obesity by revealing the biological processes that improve bioactive compounds and their bioavailability by modulating the gut-liver axis. The combined herbal medicine and modern biotechnology will be a promising approach for managing metabolic disorders (Tian et al., 2026). The multi-omics approach assessed the impact of probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition and metabolomic profiles in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).Administration of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium significantly changed the gut microbiota and increased the levels of SCFAs, particularly butyrate and acetate. Gene expression analysis using RT-PCR showed a 2.5-to 1.9-fold increase in insulin receptor and AKT expression, suggesting greater insulin sensitivity; however, gut barrier genes (ZO-1 and CLDN1) also increased. Probiotic supplementation may be a non-invasive, safer therapeutic approach for GDM by improving insulin sensitivity and gut health (Su et al., 2026).The meta-analysis covers 46 randomized controlled trials with 3,580 participants with either type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Probiotic/synbiotic administration significantly decreased CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α, along with increased IL-10 and SCFA levels. Probiotic/synbiotic and SCFA supplementation may be a better diabetes care strategy (Xie et al., 2025).Another meta-analysis showed that microbial metabolites from probiotics interact with host proteins and tissue-specific pathways affecting gastrointestinal and metabolic health. Network and transcriptomic analyzes revealed important metabolite-gene relationships involving 10-hydroxy-cis-12-octadecenoic acid, glycodeoxycholic acid and N-(1-carbamoyl-2-phenyl-ethyl) butyramide. These findings identify molecular connections between microbial metabolites and host function that can inform microbiome-directed therapies and precision nutrition approaches to improve metabolic health (Yao et al., 2025).Potential host targets and biological functions of probiotic-based metabolites were identified using an integrative network-based approach based on metabolite-protein interactions and tissue-specific transcriptomics. High-degree genes including SLC27A4, LCN12 and APOD were highly expressed in gastrointestinal tract tissues, suggesting their involvement in host-microbe interactions. Metabolitespecific analysis showed different expression patterns. 10-hydroxy-cis-12-octadecenoic acid demonstrated a relationship to sialyltransferases and neuraminidase, glycodeoxycholic acid was related to bile acid metabolism and lipid transport and N-(1-carbamoyl-2-phenyl-ethyl) butyramide was related to detoxification pathways (Ma & Zhang, 2025).The systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of probiotic-derived metabolitetargeted interventions on hormonal and metabolic outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Experimental treatments included synbiotics, probiotics, sodium butyrate, Akkermansia muciniphila, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) compositions, and all interventions lasted at least 8 weeks. Pooled data analysis showed a significant decrease in total testosterone, LH/FSH, fasting insulin, and HOMA-IR, with a slight increase in HDL cholesterol (Maddirevula et al., 2025).A total of 46 randomized controlled trials involving more than 12,500 pregnant women suggest that probiotic supplementation may reduce gestational weight gain and postpartum weight retention and improve fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, total cholesterol, and LDL. This study reveals that probiotics are a promising non-pharmacological strategy for improving maternal metabolic health and reducing adverse pregnancy outcomes in obese women through multiple pathways (Jia et al., 2025).A randomized double-blind and placebo-controlled trial assessed multistrain probiotics (Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and Bifidobacterium longum) administered to 84 subjects who had closed tibial shaft fractures, through 3-dimensional microcomputed tomography (CT) measurements of BV/TV. Exploratory analyses showed that probiotics were associated with earlier weight-bearing, reduced pain at week 2, and higher RUST scores at 12 weeks. These results suggest that perioperative probiotic administration could not only promote fracture healing but also accelerate functional recovery, likely mediated by gut-bone axis-based immunomodulatory effects. Thus, probiotics can positively impact fracture care as an adjunct to standard treatment (Huang et al., 2026).Another study explored the role of probiotics in sarcopenia using data from NHANES and the UK Biobank, integrated with in vitro C2C12 myotube experiments, molecular docking, and machinelearning models. Individuals who regularly consume probiotics have higher handgrip strength and fatfree mass, and lower signs of inflammation, than those who do not. Probiotic-conditioned media greatly promoted muscle cell fusion, increased cell diameter, and increased expression of the muscle regulatory genes MyoD, Myogenin, and MyHC; it also reduced NF-κB and TNF-α while boosting PGC-1 levels. Butyrate showed strong interactions with AMPK, mTOR and NF-B. Thus, probiotics could help preserve muscle via immune responses and microbiota-controlled metabolic and muscleanabolism pathways (Wang et al., 2026).The study evaluated the impact of gut microbiome changes on postoperative recovery in postmenopausal women by examining stool samples using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and QIIME2.Analysis of alpha and beta diversity exhibited major changes in microbial composition, with a predominance of Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, associated with improved functional outcomes and faster recovery. Conversely, Proteobacteria and Escherichia were linked to delayed healing and worse clinical outcomes. Based on microbial abundance, a random forest machine learning model achieved 85% accuracy in predicting clinical recovery, suggesting that gut microbiome signatures may serve as key biomarkers and provide a basis for microbiome-based personalized strategies to accelerate postoperative recovery and enhance long-term musculoskeletal health. Furthermore, microbiome composition correlates with various important surgical parameters such as bone healing and infection rate (Pan et al., 2026).A meta-analysis evaluated the effects of different doses and intervention durations of different probiotic strains on bone metabolism. The review states that probiotic supplementation boosts bone formation and decreases bone resorption in patients with osteoporosis. Formulations with probiotic consortia and higher doses showed significant improvements, especially in postmenopausal women, suggesting that probiotics may be a promising adjunctive approach to improve bone health. Psychobiotics are promising microbiomebased interventions for supporting mental health. These benefits may arise from modulation of neurotransmitter production, SCFA signaling, immune responses, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity. Thirty-eight ASD children who underwent a full course of WMT from a single donor were evaluated before and 4 weeks after treatment by clinical rating scales and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. WMT significantly improved core ASD symptoms, sleep, and GI symptoms. In addition, the therapeutic effect was related to the gut microbiota of both the donor and recipient before therapy, suggesting that donor-recipient microbiota compatibility may influence the effect of WMT in ASD (Quan et al., 2026).The multi-omics study provides mechanistic evidence supporting the neuromodulatory effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and Bifidobacterium longum 1714. L. rhamnosus GG mainly boosts GABAergic and SCFA-based synaptic pathways, whereas B. longum 1714 influences the tryptophanserotonin-immune axis. Additionally, in vitro validation demonstrated increased GABA and serotonin release, reduced ROS levels, and enrichment of anti-inflammatory transcripts in EVs. These findings reveal the therapeutic potential of L. rhamnosus GG and B. longum 1714 for neurological health (Jin et al., 2026).The effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG was evaluated in sepsis-induced lung injury by assessing the gut-lung axis. Probiotic supplementation in Wistar rats endangered by caecal ligation and puncture improved pulmonary function, lung histology, and respiratory parameters. Probiotic culture also restored the gut microbiota and reduced hypoxemia and inflammation. Thus, efficient therapeutic probiotics will greatly increase the success of treatment and improve the patient's quality of life and survival (Wang et al., 2026).A single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the effects of probiotic lozenges in children with adenoid hypertrophy and otitis media with effusion receiving standard nonsurgical management. Probiotic treatment significantly improved tympanogram classification compared with placebo, with favorable changes in tympanometric and audiological parameters, including DPOAE conversion. Lactis BB12 led to higher recovery rates in energy and protein intake in the early postoperative phase through the gastrointestinal tract. Inflammatory markers CRP, IL-6, and leukocyte count had increased, and albumin and prealbumin levels had declined. The probability of complications, including pneumonia, wound infection and pharyngocutaneous fistula, was much reduced. Hospital stay and antibiotic use were reduced (Wei et al., 2025).In this meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials with 1,246 women with endometrial cancer (EC), probiotics increased gut microbiota diversity, increased beneficial bacteria, and reduced gastrointestinal complications. Probiotics also improved well-being and reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Multi-strain formulations, higher doses (≥10¹⁰ CFU/day) and longer interventions had greater benefits, supporting probiotics as a potential adjunctive therapy (Chen et al., 2025).This review explores the significant role of Akkermansia muciniphila, an important gut commensal, in maintaining gut immune homeostasis and metabolic balance. The molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of A. muciniphila involve intestinal barrier enhancement, immune modulation, metabolite-mediated signaling and reshaping the gut microbiota. This review also notes that pasteurized preparations and bioactive metabolites can have therapeutic effects alongside live bacterial cultures (Xie et al., 2026). Pre-and probiotic-based approaches could benefit phenylketonuria treatment by increasing microbial diversity and making the microbiome more resilient, enabling the intestine to resist disturbances and prevent losses in functional diversity (Kalla Veedu et al., 2025).Though gut microbiome and their metabolites ae gaining more attention and popularity, the interpretation and therapeutic strategy of the available data are limited due to less availability of clinical translations. Molecular docking, computational projections, and in vitro investigations provide mechanistic insights, but they do not adequately replicate physiological circumstances or prove clinical relevance. Such in silico studies require experimental validation for identified biomarkers and predicted metabolite-protein interactions. Clinical consequences are not always causally linked to changes in microbial abundance or metabolite concentrations. It is yet unclear how microbial metabolites, live probiotics, microbial consortia, and host responses relate to one another. Furthermore, conclusions drawn from certain strains, formulations and disease models cannot be applied to all probiotic treatments. titre: The effect of a one-session slow breathing exercise on emotional reactivity, heart rate, and blood pressure in alexithymic vs. non-alexithymic individuals
resume: Alexithymic individuals experience difficulties in emotion regulation at both emotional and somatic levels. Some studies suggest that breathing interventions might compensate for these impairments. The main aim of the present study was to test whether a one-session breathing exercise affects emotional reactivity, blood pressure, and heart rate in alexithymic vs. non-alexithymic individuals. Based on their TAS-20 scores from the screening part of the study ( n = 210), participants were allocated to an alexithymic ( n = 27) or non-alexithymic group ( n = 29). They underwent negative mood induction and they were randomly allocated to one of the breathing training conditions (faster – 12 breaths/minute vs. slower – 6 breaths/minute). Their mood, heart rate, and blood pressure were measured 3 times throughout the study. The results revealed a marginally significant interaction between alexithymia and breathing exercise for the arousal dimension of emotional reactivity. Alexithymic participants who underwent slower breathing reported lower arousal, akin to non-alexithymic participants but contrary to participants after faster breathing, who reported higher arousal. Additionally, alexithymic participants, after the slower-breathing exercise, experienced a significant drop in HR. We did not observe any significant effects on blood pressure. The present findings suggest that breathing-based strategies may warrant further investigation as a simple approach to supporting emotional and physiological recovery in individuals with alexithymic traits. Given the preliminary nature of the evidence, these findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

titre: Dissociation, Trauma, Interoception, and Sleep: A Network Analysis
resume: Dissociation, as a multidimensional psychological construct, encompasses a broad spectrum of experiences, ranging from everyday detachment and lapses in attention to severe clinical symptoms observed in dissociative disorders and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD; ​Danböck et al., 2025)​. Current evidence indicates the transdiagnostic nature of dissociative symptoms ​(Ellickson-Larew et al., 2020; Lyssenko et al., 2018)​, which may co-occur across various forms of psychopathology. Competing models of dissociation etiology—the posttraumatic model (PTM) and the sociocognitive model (SCM)—have been proposed, yet consensus between them remains unresolved ​(Lynn et al., 2024)​. The present study investigates relationships between dissociative symptoms and variables derived from both theoretical frameworks (PTM and SCM) within a single sample, aiming to elucidate multidirectional associations among dissociation, trauma exposure, posttraumatic symptomatology, interoception, and sleep quality. Existing evidence suggests that these variables are highly interconnected. Of particular interest is the link between dissociation and atypical interoception ​(Fani et al., 2023; Kaldewaij et al., 2024; Maqueda et al., 2015; Michal et al., 2014; Millman et al., 2023; Pick et al., 2020; Schäflein et al., 2018; Woelk & Garfinkel, 2024)​, which has been conceptualized as a potential “P factor”​(Smith et al., 2024)​ contributing to broad vulnerability in mental disorders ​(Brewer et al., 2021)​. Interoceptive dysfunctions have also been observed in individuals with PTSD ​(Leech et al., 2024)​. Furthermore, accumulating evidence suggests that sleep disturbances represent an important mechanism contributing to dissociative experiences ​(Arora et al., 2020; Eiser, 2024; Giesbrecht et al., 2007; Lopez et al., 2023; Quaedackers et al., 2022; Selvi et al., 2017; van der Kloet et al., 2012; Van Der Kloet et al., 2012)​. Several studies have documented significant associations between sleep quality and interoceptive processing ​(Alfì et al., 2025; Arora et al., 2021; Asaoka et al., 2025; Bynum & Brindle, 2025; Julie et al., 2025; Seo et al., 2025; Wei et al., 2016; Wei & Van Someren, 2020)​. Sleep disturbances are particularly prevalent among individuals with PTSD ​(Miller et al., 2020; Palagini et al., 2022)​. Taken together, substantial evidence points to complex, multidirectional relationships among dissociative symptoms, interoceptive functioning, sleep quality, and posttraumatic symptomatology. These variables may share a common underlying mechanism—namely, stress-related dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system and its communication with the central nervous system ​(Beutler et al., 2022; Siciliano et al., 2022)​.

titre: Relationship between Alexithymia and Chronic Stress by Compassionate Goals
No Words for Intergroup Feelings: Intergroup Empathy Mediates the Relationship Between Alexithymia and Intergroup Relations
resume: ABSTRACT Alexithymia is linked to poor interpersonal relations; less is known about its role in intergroup relations. We examined which of its facets predict negative intergroup relations, and whether dispositional and intergroup empathy mediate these associations. We also tested whether alexithymia is associated with general social impairment or disproportionately poorer intergroup relations relative to interpersonal relations. White British heterosexual men ( N = 302) participated in a preregistered cross‐sectional online survey on experiences with gay men. Alexithymia was measured with the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS‐20) and the Perth Alexithymia Questionnaire (PAQ), and dispositional and intergroup empathic concern (EC) and perspective‐taking (PT) were assessed using the Interpersonal Reactivity Index. Results first showed an intergroup bias: Individuals reported lower PT, greater affective prejudice, lower behavioral intentions, and lower self‐disclosure toward outgroup than ingroup members. Individuals higher on the alexithymia externally oriented thinking (EOT) facet rated both ingroup and outgroup members more negatively on affective prejudice, stereotypes, and behavioral intentions than individuals with lower alexithymia‐EOT. They also reported lower self‐disclosure in both interpersonal and intergroup relations. Finally, lower intergroup (but not trait) EC and PT mediated the negative relationship between alexithymia‐EOT and outgroup attitudes (affective, cognitive, behavioral), across both the TAS‐20 and PAQ. These findings suggest that alexithymia is linked to broader social difficulties, and highlight the importance of targeting intergroup empathy in efforts to reduce negative outgroup attitudes among individuals high in alexithymia‐EOT.

titre: The Effectiveness of Group-Based Positive Youth Development Training on Attachment to Parents and Alexithymia in Male Adolescents with a Tendency Toward Addiction in Isfahan
resume: Objective: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of group-based Positive Youth Development training on attachment to parents and alexithymia among male adolescents with a tendency toward addiction in Isfahan. Methods and Materials: This quasi-experimental study used a pretest–posttest–follow-up design with a control group. The statistical population included male lower-secondary students with a tendency toward addiction in Isfahan during the 2023–2024 academic year. Thirty eligible adolescents were selected through purposive sampling and randomly assigned to experimental and control groups. The experimental group received twelve 90-minute weekly sessions of Positive Youth Development training, while the control group remained on a waiting list. Data were collected using the Inventory of Parent and Peer Attachment and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and Bonferroni post-hoc tests. Findings: Repeated-measures ANOVA indicated a significant time effect for attachment to mother, attachment to father, and alexithymia. The results showed that the intervention produced a significant improvement in attachment to mother and a significant reduction in alexithymia from pretest to posttest and follow-up. However, the between-group effect for attachment to father was not significant, and Bonferroni comparisons confirmed that changes in attachment to father were not statistically meaningful. The intervention effects for attachment to mother and alexithymia remained stable at follow-up. Conclusion: Group-based Positive Youth Development training can be considered an effective preventive and corrective intervention for improving attachment to mothers and reducing alexithymia in male adolescents with a tendency toward addiction. However, improving attachment to fathers may require longer, family-based, or father-inclusive interventions.
revue: Journal of Adolescent and Youth Psychological Studies (JAYPS)

titre: Restoring embodied safety through martial arts: Japanese ju-jitsu [JJJ] for embodied reappraisal & psychosocial function in a woman with trauma
resume: Background: Martial Arts halls are important community-mental health hubs. Japanese Ju Jitsu (JJJ) delivered with clear consent rules, breath/voice work, & positional-control may cultivate Interoceptive Awareness (IA), embodied reappraisal, & thus emotion regulation in trauma & survivors of violence. Case: A 51-year-old woman with mental-health trauma from adolescent-sexual violence completed a brief JJJ-informed program. Outcomes included the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) and a hermeneutic-phenomenological interview. Intervention: Six 60 - 75-minute sessions over six weeks emphasizing diaphragmatic-pressure-control, boundary-setting voice cues, kata-based drills, & self-regulated positional scenarios, integrated with therapist-guided self-awareness & embodied reappraisal. Outcomes: MAIA showed notable gains in Emotional Awareness, Body Listening, & Self-Regulation; qualitative data indicated resolution of nightmares, improved sleep, & greater agency. Discussion: The current case study provides a framework to guide Martial Arts instructors in supporting students with trauma histories. Mind-Body & Nervous-system clinicians (e.g., Exercise Physiologists & Physiotherapists) are important for participant support.

titre: Hipnose terapêutica como tratamento para o estresse acadêmico: uma revisão bibliográfica
resume: Introduction: Academic stress is a prevalent issue in the university setting, affecting student performance, mental health, and retention. Therapeutic hypnosis has emerged as a complementary intervention with a growing body of evidence. This research aims to synthesize the scientific literature on the effectiveness of hypnosis in managing academic stress, with a focus on findings from Cuba and the rest of the world. Materials and Methods: A narrative review was conducted by searching databases such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SciELO, as well as institutional repositories. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and experimental studies published between 2000 and 2026 were selected. Results: International findings consistently show significant reductions in test anxiety and perceived stress, alongside improvements in executive function and emotional regulation. In Cuba, a quasi-experimental study demonstrated that hypnotherapy modified personality traits and reduced vulnerability to stress among law students. Discussion: Hypnosis acts through cognitive-behavioral and psychophysiological mechanisms, making it a viable, cost-effective, and low-risk alternative. Conclusions: The evidence supports the inclusion of hypnosis in university wellness programs; however, further randomized controlled trials—with long-term follow-up and tailored to the Cuban context—are required.

fiche.intervention: Hypnose thérapeutique comparée aux prises en charge habituelles ou absence d'intervention

Amélioration des fonctions exécutives et de la régulation émotionnelle.

fiche.conclusion: Les données soutiennent l'intégration de l'hypnose dans les programmes de bien-être universitaires, mais des essais randomisés supplémentaires restent nécessaires.

fiche.conclusion_simple: L'hypnose semble réduire l'anxiété et améliorer la régulation émotionnelle, mais des essais contrôlés randomisés doivent confirmer ces effets.

titre: Pharmacokinetic--pharmacodynamic blueprints for the anaesthetized adult digital twin: a coupled five-layer specification with an open reference implementation
resume: General anaesthesia is a multi-drug intervention, yet the pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models that guide it are applied one drug at a time. As precision anaesthesia and closed-loop control move toward clinical reality, this fragmentation becomes a central obstacle: no reference maps validated PK/PD models across drug classes onto the clinical signals they drive, specifies the interactions that couple them, and states the result precisely enough to be implemented. This review addresses that gap in three steps. First, the validated single-agent models for hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blockers, vasoactive drugs and volatile agents are consolidated into a covariate-aware selection guide that includes the organ-function covariates omitted by anthropometric models. Second, the resulting architecture is converted into a complete mathematical specification: an enumerated state vector with units and initial conditions, an input vector that includes surgical stimulus, the equations of five pharmacodynamic layers (hypnosis, nociception, respiratory safety, haemodynamics, neuromuscular blockade), the mechanistic couplings that link them, and an observation model that treats the bispectral index as a confounded measurement of a latent hypnotic state rather than as that state itself. Third, an open reference implementation supports three in-silico demonstrations: a coupled clinical case, a quantification of what monitor feedback adds to an open-loop population prediction, and a Fisher-information analysis of which parameters are identifiable from which signals. Individualising the twin on twenty minutes of monitoring reduced the median error of a subsequent fifteen-minute-ahead bispectral index prediction from 18.4% to 5.8%, while leaving the underlying effect-site concentration no better estimated, which delimits both the value and the limits of model-based prediction. A prioritised research agenda follows. The framework is a pharmacological substrate and an in-silico test-bench, not a clinically validated device.

fiche.verdict: Une revue propose un modèle pharmacocinétique-pharmacodynamique global et couplé pour l'anesthésie générale, testé in silico.
resultats_cles: Consolidation de modèles à agent unique en une spécification mathématique à cinq couches.
La personnalisation du jumeau numérique réduit l'erreur de prédiction de l'indice bispectral.
fiche.conclusion: Le cadre fournit un substrat pharmacologique et un banc d'essai in silico pour l'anesthésie de precision.

fiche.titre_court: Modèle pharmacodynamique pour jumeau numérique en anesthésie
fiche.conclusion_simple: Un nouveau modèle mathématique couplé améliore la prédiction de la profondeur de l'anesthésie in silico.

titre: Does self-esteem act as a mechanism of change within Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for young people with Social Anxiety? A systematic review and meta-analysis
Psychological distress during the first 12 months post-upper limb fracture: systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Abstract Background and purpose Upper limb fractures cause substantial disability and loss of independence, creating a growing burden in an ageing population. The purpose was to systematically review the evidence to determine how psychological distress may change during the initial 12 months following post-upper limb fracture. Methods A systematic review of published and unpublished literature databases was performed to 25th August 2026. Studies presenting data on psychological distress were eligible. Data were appraised using the Downs and Black Appraisal tool, with analysis through meta-analysis comparing scores from fracture to early- (two to six weeks) and longer-term (six to 12 months) follow-up. Results 28 studies ( n = 5,638 people) were eligible and included. There was a significant decrease in depression from early recovery to up to 12 months (Standardised Mean Difference (SMD): 0.65; 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.43–0.86; N = 2,230), and anxiety (SMD: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.43–0.59; N = 1229). Overall, methodological quality was moderate, with inadequate adjustment for confounding (24 studies) and limited accounting for loss to follow-up (26 studies) identified as common limitations. Kinesiophobia scores were lower at six- to 12-month follow-up compared with the initial fracture assessment (MD: 8.32; 95% CI: 7.26–9.38; N = 1,072). Pain catastrophising scores were lower at six- to 12-month follow-up compared with the initial fracture assessment (MD: 2.05; 95% CI: 1.66–2.43; N = 1,803), although the difference in effect estimates between shorter- and longer-term follow-up was not statistically significant ( p = 0.26). Conclusion Psychological distress was reported following upper-limb fracture, at a population level, anxiety, depression, kinesiophobia and pain catastrophising generally decreased during the first 12 months following fracture. However, kinesiophobia and pain-catastrophising scores did not reach clinically important levels. Further research is required to determine the prevalence and trajectories of clinically important distress and to identify individuals at greatest risk. Clinicians should remain alert to symptoms of anxiety, depression, fear of movement and fear of falling, particularly where recovery is delayed. They should consider further assessment or referral where clinically indicated. Evidence is currently insufficient to recommend universal screening or a specific psychological intervention. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

titre: Virtual reality exposure therapy for anxiety and trauma-related disorders: clinical evidence, behavioral sensing, and implementation priorities
resume: Virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) provides a controlled environment for delivering exposure to feared cues. Evidence supports benefit over inactive controls for selected specific phobias and social-anxiety presentations, but nonsignificant differences from active treatment do not establish equivalence. This critical narrative review integrates systematic reviews, representative randomized trials, mechanistic studies, and measurement and implementation frameworks. We distinguish diagnosed social anxiety disorder from performance-focused and symptom-selected samples, and exposure-based treatment from VR distraction or relaxation. PTSD findings require particular caution because military cohorts, trauma cues, and treatment histories may not represent civilian clinical populations. Behavioral and physiological signals are examined at four levels: technical capture, experimental association, clinical validity, and incremental clinical utility. Feasible recording and associations with arousal or attention do not establish that a signal measures therapeutic learning or improves treatment decisions. We propose a clinician-governed precision VRET loop as a conceptual framework requiring prospective evaluation, rather than a clinically validated adaptive intervention. Research priorities include appropriately designed comparative trials, explicit diagnostic characterization, standardized intervention and hardware reporting, purpose-specific measurement validation, systematic harms assessment, longer follow-up, and implementation and economic evaluation. VRET should be evaluated as a defined exposure intervention for a specified population and care setting, with patient choice and accountable clinical oversight.

fiche.population: Patients souffrant de troubles anxieux et liés au trauma
fiche.intervention: Thérapie par exposition en réalité virtuelle (VRET) comparée à des contrôles

fiche.conclusion: La VRET doit être évaluée comme une intervention d'exposition définie pour une population et un cadre de soins précis.

titre: Beyond AI Chatbots: A Human-AI Collaboration Framework for Anxiety Support in University Counseling Services- a Systematic Review (Preprint)
resume: BACKGROUND Anxiety is among the most common mental health problems experienced by university students, while university counseling services face demand that human staff alone cannot meet. Chatbots based on artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly offered as a solution, but evidence on how AI works alongside counselors remains scattered. OBJECTIVE This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on the functions of AI in anxiety support, human-AI collaboration models, and safety and ethical requirements, and then derive a framework for university counseling services. METHODS Searches were conducted in Scopus, PubMed, ERIC, and Lens.org on October 28, 2026, for English-language journal articles published 2021-2026 examining AI systems for mental health support and involving university students, young adults, counselors, or counseling services. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI checklist according to design, the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and PROBAST. Findings were synthesized thematically and narratively using Whittemore and Knafl's integrative approach. RESULTS Of 368 records, 75 studies reported in 76 articles met the inclusion criteria: 8 qualitative studies, 11 cross-sectional and survey studies, 8 comparative experimental and observational studies, 18 system development, mixed methods, and prediction model studies, and 30 reviews and conceptual papers. Only 14 studies measured anxiety directly. Qualitative and survey studies consistently position AI as a complement and expect human judgment in crises. Experimental studies show short-term anxiety reduction; a systematic review of 31 trials reported an SMD of -0.37 (95% CI -0.58 to -0.17), with the greatest improvements in clinician-supported AI-assisted CBT. System development and prediction model studies report high performance, but mostly on simulated or public data and at high risk of bias. Risk of bias was low in 24 studies, moderate in 30, and high in 21. CONCLUSIONS Evidence supports AI as a risk-tiered complement within counselor-controlled services, rather than as a standalone chatbot. We propose a Human-AI Collaborative Anxiety Support (HACAS) framework with four tiers of service, counselor decision-making at every escalation point, and a governance foundation. This framework needs prospective testing.

fiche.conclusion: L'IA doit servir de complément à risque gradué dans les services contrôlés par des conseillers, et non de chatbot autonome.

titre: The Neural Basis of Emotion Regulation: A Review of Prefrontal-Limbic Mechanisms and Their Implications for Psychotherapy
resume: Emotion regulation involves the strategies by which people adjust the strength, time course, or display of emotional responses. This review integrates psychological theory, functional neuroimaging, meta-analytic evidence, and intervention studies to characterize the neurocognitive basis for emotion regulation,which emerges from dynamic interactions among distributed brain networks. Regulation depends on context-sensitive activity in the amygdala, insula, and cingulate cortex during emotion generation, whereas intentional control engages lateral and medial prefrontal regions that maintain goals, interpret events, and shift attention or meaning. Effective regulation therefore relies on information integration rather than the inhibition of one brain region by another. Depression and anxiety involve maladaptive regulation patterns and ineffective prefrontal-limbic interaction, although these alterations are heterogeneous and non-specific to particular diagnoses. Cognitive behavioral therapy, exposure therapy, and mindfulness-based interventions may alter appraisals, salience, self-referential processing, and neural connectivity. However, small samples, heterogeneous tasks, and the correlational nature of functional imaging constrain causal and clinical inference. Future work should adopt integrated, longitudinal, multimodal, and ecologically valid designs to identify individual-level predictors of treatment outcomel.
revue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

titre: Connectopic Mapping of Striatal and Hippocampus-Amygdala Gradients in OCD
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a chronic psychiatric condition characterized by intrusive, unwanted thoughts or images, and repetitive or ritualistic behaviors (American Psychiatric, 2022). Functional alterations in OCD are well documented, particularly within corticostriatal-thalamocortical (CSTC) and frontolimbic circuitry and associate with symptom severity and clinical features (Bruin et al., 2023; Li & Mody, 2016; Thorsen, Hagland, et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019). Neurotransmitters such as dopamine and serotonin are considered key modulators of this circuitry, but evidence for neurotransmitter alterations in OCD is inconsistent (Dougherty et al., 2018; Mota et al., 2026). Specifically, alterations in striatal dopaminergic markers are repeatedly reported in OCD, though with varying directionality of effects (Mota et al., 2026). Further, reduced serotonin transporters across CSTC and limbic regions have been observed in OCD, and serotonin appears closely linked to anxiety and symptom severity, although null findings are also noted (Dougherty et al., 2018). Serotonergic and dopaminergic alterations in OCD are particularly relevant considering that serotonin reuptake inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy, whereas dopamine antagonist augmentation benefits a subset of patients.(de Oliveira et al., 2023). However, directly characterizing these neurotransmitter alterations using PET imaging with radioligands is resource-intensive and difficult to implement in large cohorts. Connectopic mapping utilizes standard resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) to map dominant and non-dominant voxel-wise fingerprints of connectivity within a region of interest. Where standard resting-state fMRI analysis is typically constrained by the assumptions of homogenous regions, predefined single seed or network se connectopic mapping can provide insight into fine-grained patterns for both the dominant and non-dominant functional connectivity gradients of the region of interest to the rest of the brain. Connectopic gradients reflect how each voxel within a region is functionally connected to the rest of the brain. By capturing both dominant and secondary patterns of connectivity variation, connectopic provides a complementary framework for investigating subtle alterations in the functional organization of brain regions. Dominant striatal connectopic gradients have recently been linked to OCD symptom severity in a smaller cohort (Webb et al., 2025), while striatal and amygdala-hippocampus connectopic projection maps can provide insight into topographical patterns of connectivity across networks, i.e., reward processing, sensorimotor or limbic networks (Marquand et al., 2017; Mulders et al., 2022; Nordin et al., 2025). Importantly, the non-dominant modes have been shown to spatial corresponds to dopamine transporter (DAT) density in the striatum, and to 5-HT1A receptor density in the hippocampus-amygdala complex in human neuroimaging samples, including healthy adults and individuals from a range of psychiatric cohorts (Haak et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2026; Oldehinkel et al., 2022). The current study will utilize datasets from the global OCD study, a worldwide initiative with harmonized data collection and analysis pipelines of ethno-culturally diverse samples of medication-free (6-week wash-out) individuals with OCD, unaffected siblings of individuals with OCD and healthy controls from five international sites (Simpson et al., 2020), to gain insight into connectopic gradients of the striatum and amygdala-hippocampus in OCD. Including unaffected siblings may help elucidate whether alterations in functional gradients reflect familial vulnerability to OCD or are more specifically associated with clinical symptoms. The objectives of the current investigation are to characterize dominant and non-dominant functional gradients (spatially corresponding to DAT and 5-HT1A) of the striatum and hippocampus-amygdala complex in individuals with OCD compared to unaffected siblings of individuals with OCD and healthy controls (HCs), and to examine whether these gradients are associated with clinical measures (i.e., depression, anxiety, OC symptom severity).
