titre: Harmful or Helpful? Beliefs About Emotions and Bipolar and Depressive Mood Dimensions in Emerging Adults
resume: Emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are a transdiagnostic challenge in psychopathology, and in mood disorders in particular (e.g., Kring & Sloan, 2009; Gruber, 2011; Joormann & Siemer, 2014). Mood disorders include depressive and bipolar disorders, which are characterized by periods of depressive, manic, and mixed mood symptoms associated with marked functional impairment and distress. Difficulties with ER are well documented in both bipolar (BD) and depressive mood disorders. With respect to BD, the positive emotion persistence model posits that individuals with BD exhibit increased positive emotional reactivity in a context-insensitive manner, have greater trouble regulating positive and negative emotions, and expend greater effort to regulate their emotions although these efforts are ultimately less successful (Gruber, 2011; Gruber et al., 2012; Villanueva et al., 2024). With respect to depressive disorders, individuals with depression also struggle to regulate their emotions, experiencing attenuated (or decreased) emotions, less reward responsiveness, and difficulty sustaining positive emotions over time (e.g., Tomarken & Keener, 1998; Rottenberg, 2005; Vanderlind et al., 2020). Improving our understanding of the psychological factors contributing to these ER difficulties in mood disorders may advance knowledge of their etiology and maintenance. One construct highly relevant to understanding ER difficulties in mood disorders is beliefs about emotion (e.g., Ford & Gross, 2019; Tamir, 2016). Emerging work has begun to explore the role of emotion beliefs in emotional disorders (e.g., Ford et al., 2017; Karnaze & Levine, 2017). For example, research has demonstrated links between beliefs about emotional malleability and depression and anxiety (Kneeland et al., 2016), and links between beliefs about the emotions people prefer or want to feel and depression and bipolar disorders (Millgram & Tamir, 2019; Millgram et al., 2021). This work underscores the importance of examining additional domains of emotion beliefs that are theoretically and clinically relevant to mood disorders. Beliefs about the helpfulness versus harmfulness of emotions is one such domain. Previous work suggests that emotion-harmful beliefs are associated with clinical symptoms of depression and anxiety and worse life satisfaction in MTurk and undergraduate samples (Willroth et al., 2023). Beliefs about emotions’ helpfulness or harmfulness (i.e., emotion-helpful beliefs [EHB]) in the context of decision making may be especially relevant to mood dimensions. An example of a belief that emotions are helpful in decision making is, “Emotions help people make better decisions,” whereas an example of a belief that emotions are harmful in decision making is, “People make the wrong decisions when they listen to their emotions” (Mazumder et al., in prep). Initial research on EHB suggests its potential importance in impulsive decision making (Mazumder et al., in prep), though little is known about EHB in association with bipolar-relevant mood dimensions (i.e., depression and mania mood dimensions concurrently), particularly among emerging adults at risk for mood onset and recurrence. EHB may be particularly important when considering bipolar-relevant mood symptoms, given documented challenges in emotion-relevant decision-making in bipolar disorders (e.g., Johnson, 2005) and depression (e.g., Bishop & Gagne, 2018; Paulus & Yu, 2012). Such work examining EHB could contribute to the understanding of malleable factors in the etiology and maintenance of bipolar spectrum disorders. The current two-study investigation seeks to examine associations between EHB and self-reported mood and anxiety dimensions in emerging adults. This is especially critical during a sensitive period of mood development in emerging adulthood (ages 18-25), which represents a peak period of initial mood onset difficulties and emotion regulation challenges more generally. Study 1 examines cross-sectional relationships between EHB and mood dimensions, including bipolar risk and current manic and depressive symptoms, and commonly comorbid anxiety symptoms, in emerging adults (approximate N = 750). Study 2 provides a multi-site replication of these findings in a larger sample (approximate N = 1,177 at baseline [or T1]; approximately N = 796 at a follow-up time point [or T2]) of emerging adults recruited from universities in the U.S., Canada and the U.K., and extends these findings by examining whether EHB predicts increases in mood and anxiety symptoms at a follow-up time point (T2). titre: A Practical Guide to Understanding Interoception and Translating Knowledge into Practice
resume: Growing recognition of the relationship between interoception, self-regulation, and occupational participation has increased clinical interest in interoception within pediatric occupational therapy. However, translating interoception science into practice remains challenging because interoception is multidimensional, current assessments cannot precisely identify the processes contributing to a child’s occupational difficulties, and evidence supporting available interventions remains limited. In this paper, we present an overview of the neuroscience of interoception and offer the Interoception Ladder Framework, a conceptual clinical reasoning tool for planning and evaluating interoception-informed occupational therapy. We position comprehensive assessment and collaborative, participation-focused goal setting as guides for intervention planning, with co-regulation and caregiver coaching embedded throughout. We propose three inter-related intervention rungs addressing mind–body awareness, arousal regulation, and explicit interoceptive awareness training. Intervention selection and sequencing are individualized and iterative. We suggest a planned review point at which therapists can examine whether occupational performance has improved. When participation is not improving, we encourage therapists to review their clinical reasoning, reconsider the intervention target, and assess whether activities, environments or contextual demands need to be modified. We position occupational participation as the primary outcome of interoception-informed occupational therapy, placing change in interoceptive awareness as secondary. Empirical evaluation is required to establish the framework’s validity, feasibility, and clinical utility.

titre: Interoceptive self-report profiles in patients with endometriosis
resume: Abstract Purpose Interoception is central in pain perception and processing and has been associated with individual differences in psychological wellbeing. Interoceptive self-report (SR) refers to the subjective evaluation of one’s tendency to sense and interpret internal sensations. Endometriosis is a systemic disease characterised by persistent visceral pain, highlighting the importance of interoceptive processes in patients who suffer from this condition. Methods We studied interoceptive SR profiles in endometriosis patients, focusing on assessing their relations with psychological and pain-related outcome factors. In total, 122 endometriosis patients filled out the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) for interoceptive SR, along with other questionnaires, including health-related quality of life of women with endometriosis (EHP-30), symptoms of anxiety/depression (HADS), pain catastrophising (PCS), childhood adversities, and resilience (RS14). We conducted a hierarchical cluster analysis, using the subscale scores from the MAIA-questionnaire. Results Four interoceptive SR profiles were identified and named according to the appearance of interoceptive SR dimensions as Attentive ( n = 16), Hypo-responsive ( n = 26), Balanced ( n = 50), and Hypervigilant–distrustful ( n = 30). Patients in the Balanced group showed stable patterns across different interoceptive SR dimensions and reported better psychological wellbeing than patients in the other groups. Patients in the Hypervigilant-distrustful group were characterised by worry about uncomfortable bodily sensations and low trust in their bodily sensations. They also reported poorer psychological wellbeing than patients in the other groups. Conclusions Our findings shed light on the importance of taking interoceptive tendencies into account when tailoring more individualised interventions for patients with endometriosis. Trial registration clinicaltrials.gov, ID: NCT03834922, registration date: 2019-02-07.

titre: Interoception and Autism Heterogeneity: A Systematic Review Protocol
Pain Interoception Assessment: Discriminating Thermal and Mechanical Pain Intensity
resume: Interoceptive processing is increasingly recognized as modality-specific, challenging the validity of applying cardiac-based paradigms to all bodily signals. Considering nociception as an interoceptive signal, we have developed a task to evaluate the ability to discriminate variations of pain intensity and its implications for metacognitive treatment. This study aimed to investigate if pain interoception is altered in chronic pain (CP) patients. Fifty-seven participants (28 healthy controls, 29 CP patients) performed both thermal and mechanical pain-intensity discrimination tasks. In a trial-by-trial paradigm, participants judged whether consecutive stimulus intensities differed and rated their confidence. We quantified pain interoceptive accuracy with a newly-devised “accuracy of pain-intensity discrimination” (APID) score, pain interoception sensibility with confidence ratings and pain interoception awareness with the MAIA clinical scale. While patients with CP had a significantly lower thermal pain threshold, their thermal and mechanical APID scores were comparable to controls (Thermal: H – 0.82 (0.18); CP – 0.80 (0.16), Mechanical: H – 0.78 (0.12); CP – 0.74 (0.13)). Interestingly, differences between groups emerged at the metacognitive level. Confidence ratings significantly correlated with objective performance in high-APID healthy subjects, but this accuracy-confidence coupling disappeared for CP patients. These findings point to an altered pain interoceptive process characterized by intact sensory discrimination alongside impaired central metacognitive processing. Relationships between APID scores and items from MAIA scores suggest that the proposed tasks constitute a valid framework for assessing pain interoception. These pain-intensity discrimination tasks provided 5 pain parameters for CP patient phenotyping: pain and pain intensity discrimination thresholds, APID, sensibility and pain interoceptive awareness scores.

titre: Trait–state integration of interoception in preschool children: associations with cardiac recovery and regulation
resume: Interoception plays an important role in self-regulation and embodied development, yet how relatively stable interoceptive capacities relate to momentary physiological responses in early childhood remains unclear. Recent perspectives distinguish between trait-level interoceptive capacity and state-level interoceptive processing. This study aimed to examine the relationships between trait-level interoceptive capacity, state-level responses, and post-activity physiological change in preschool children. Interoceptive functioning was examined in 38 typically developing preschool children aged 3–5 years. Trait-level capacity was assessed using the Dynamic Metacognitive Interoception Measure (DMIM). State-level responses were elicited using a brief Jumping Jack Paradigm, with heart rate recorded via smartphone-based photoplethysmography at baseline, post-activity, and recovery. Perceptual–physiological alignment was indexed as the discrepancy between perceived and physiological cardiac change, and post-activity physiological change was indexed by the recovery-to-baseline difference (T2 − T0). Repeated-measures analysis of variance, correlation analyses, and hierarchical regression analyses were used. Heart rate increased after activity and then partly returned toward baseline, F (2, 74) = 72.18, p < .001. DMIM total scores were not associated with heart rate reactivity (ΔHR), but were associated with lower recovery-to-baseline difference values (β = −0.32, p = .031) and lower perceptual–physiological discrepancy. Exploratory analyses indicated that Interoceptive Attention was associated with both the recovery-to-baseline difference and perceptual–physiological discrepancy, whereas Interoceptive Discrimination was associated with the recovery-to-baseline difference. Higher perceptual–physiological discrepancy was associated with higher recovery-to-baseline difference values. These findings suggest that interoceptive functioning in early childhood can be examined within a trait–state framework, with post-activity heart-rate differences providing an exploratory indicator of physiological change following activation.

titre: The Role of Stimulants like Caffeine in Triggering or Amplifying Intuitive Gut Feelings and Premonitory Experiences: A Salience-Gain and Interoceptive Threshold Hypothesis
resume: This paper proposes, rather than claims to demonstrate, that intuitive gut feelings and premonitory experiences are a universal human baseline: everyone has them, though people differ in how often they notice them [1–4]. Stimulants such as caffeine are treated as visibility amplifiers, not as creators of a special faculty. The primary hypothesis is that an acute moderate-to-high dose of caffeine—acting via central adenosine $A_1$ and $A_{2A}$ receptor antagonism [7, 8]—increases subjective gain in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) and the anterior insula (AIC) [5, 6], raising the likelihood that suppressed or low-intensity intuitive threat signals—already present in ordinary human cognition—will cross the perceptual threshold into conscious awareness. The proposal is motivated by a longitudinal case observation: unexplained warnings to stay away from certain people were later followed by those people encountering danger, including a colleague who died in an accident; the feelings faded for years and returned, after a high caffeine dose, in connection with an elderly neighbor. An evolutionary reading treats these signals as conserved survival tools, once relied on in prehistoric hunting and social threat detection, and now dulled by chronic stress, poor sleep [11, 12], social media, and cognitive offloading to artificial intelligence (AI) [14, 15]. A further, speculative concern is that unused neural pathways can weaken with disuse through experience-dependent synaptic plasticity and, over generations, could fade from skilled cultural use or relaxed selection. A parallel is drawn with the apparent outsourcing of human creativity and critical judgment to social media templates and AI [14, 15]. A prospective, counterbalanced, 14-day within-person self-logging study ($N = 80$ across two baseline-noticing strata) is outlined to test the amplifier claim using Signal Detection Theory ($d'$ sensitivity versus criterion $c$). Cognitive biases and the ethical risk of acting on false alarms are discussed. The conclusion is a call to notice and preserve these interoceptive capacities before people become permanently dependent on external pharmacological or algorithmic triggers to feel them at all.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: 内感受解离、突显网络切换与内脏自主神经修复:从默认模式网络精度加权下调、迷走神经张力重分配到无评判视觉表象流的神经现象学及《黄帝内经》「内观」考辨 | Interoceptive Decoupling, Salience-Network Switching and Autonomic Visceral Restoration: From Precision-Weighting in the Default Mode Network and the Redistribution of Vagal Tone to the Neurophenomenology of a Non-Judgmental Imagery Stream, with a Textual Examination of neiguan in the Huangdi Neijing
resume: Can attending to the inside of the body without interpreting it release sympathetic defence and let visceral and pelvic microcirculation restore itself? This book presents mathematical models and methodological discussion for teaching and research and is not medical advice. It breaks the claim into six testable links and falsifies before it sets bounds. The first result is negative: in a precision-weighted Bayesian framework, lowering the precision of the interoceptive channel lowers the posterior estimate only when the prior is itself benign; with an alarmed prior (set here at 3.0 units) the same move pushes the posterior up — lowering sensory precision from 2.0 to 0.25 raises it from 2.333 to 2.800, so the practice makes things worse the better it works — the dark-room problem of the free-energy framework. Bringing the posterior down requires moving the prior, which is not the same operation as declining to interpret. Second, written as a gain term in a signal-detection model, "not interpreting the inner picture" leaves d′ untouched: with the criterion re-tuned, the expected cost is identical at every gain (0.3857); without re-tuning, a gain of 0.5 cuts the hit rate from 0.622 to 0.281 and raises the cost to 0.4634. Non-judgmental attention changes which errors are made, not how much information there is. Third, a triple-network Markov chain shows that lowering the probability that inner events recruit salience raises default-mode occupancy (0.362 to 0.596) and dwell time (2.06 to 5.54 s) while necessarily lowering the entropy rate and lengthening first passage to the executive state (4.92 to 6.66 s): a cost, not a side effect. Fourth, and most important: the vagus does not innervate the pelvic organs. The pelvic spinal outflow is sacral, and the "sacral parasympathetic" is itself contested (Espinosa-Medina et al. 2016, 2018 and Sivori et al. 2024 argue it is sympathetic; Jänig et al. 2017 and Neuhuber et al. 2017 reply). Heart-rate variability therefore indexes cardiac vagal control and cannot be read as a measure of pelvic blood flow. The book states this as a structural identifiability result: four parameter sets reproduce the same cardiac trace to within floating-point error while implying mean visceral conductances from 0.506 to 0.884 and minima from 0.000 to 0.426, so "HRV rose, therefore visceral perfusion was restored" is not an inference but an assumption written as if it had been measured. Fifth, RMSSD and high-frequency power move with the breathing pattern: in synthetic records whose mean interbeat interval is held exactly constant, RMSSD ranges from 18.4 to 31.4 ms, and at six breaths a minute the high-frequency index collapses because the respiratory peak has left the band. Sixth, flow is constrained by the fourth-power law and by autoregulation: doubling flow needs a 18.9 % radius increase, flow-sensing autoregulation absorbs 34 % to 60 % of the steady-state response, and at fixed cardiac output dilating one bed steals flow from the others. Chapter 7 reads these beside the Suwen's "tranquil emptiness", the Lingshu chapter "Root of the Spirit" and the Zhuangzi's "fasting of the heart", set against the Stoic inner citadel; one finding of textual examination: the compound neiguan could not be verified in the Huangdi Neijing in this round, its securely datable early use being the Tang-attributed Scripture on Inner Observation, while modern Chinese also uses it to render vipassanā, and it is not the acupoint name neiguan. Chapter 8 gives a four-step checklist and a pre-registered two-arm trial: single primary comparison non-judgmental interoceptive attention against a structurally matched external-focus control, single primary outcome the week-6 body-vigilance score by analysis of covariance, smallest effect of interest 0.35 SD, 165 analysable and 195 randomised per arm, 390 in all, with a pre-specified negative-control outcome to detect a generic expectancy effect. Marked boxes separate published evidence, runnable Python calculations (16 programs), classical sources and the author's models and hypotheses; apart from cited literature data, all data in the book are synthetic. 把注意力放到身体内部而不去解释它,能不能解除交感防御、让内脏与盆腔的微循环自行恢复?本书是教学与研究用的数学模型与方法学讨论,不是医疗建议。它把这一链条拆成六个可检验的环节,并先证伪、再立边界。第一个结果是否定的:在精度加权的贝叶斯框架里,「下调内感受通道的精度」只有在先验本身温和时才使后验估计下降;先验是警觉的(本书设为 3.0 个单位)时,同样的操作把后验推高——感觉精度从 2.0 降到 0.25 时后验从 2.333 升到 2.800,越练越糟,这正是自由能框架的「暗室」问题。要让后验下降,必须移动先验本身,而这与「不作解释」不是同一件事。第二,把「不解释内视觉画面」写成信号检测模型中的增益项后,判别力 d′ 与增益无关:重新调定判准时各增益的期望代价完全相同(0.3857),不重调时增益 0.5 使命中率从 0.622 降到 0.281、代价从 0.3857 升到 0.4634。所以「无评判」改变的是哪一类错误,不是信息量。第三,三网络马尔可夫链表明,降低「内部事件招募突显网络」的概率在提高默认模式占位(0.362 → 0.596)与驻留时间(2.06 → 5.54 秒)的同时,必然降低熵率并延长到执行状态的首达时间(4.92 → 6.66 秒),这是代价而非副作用。 第四,也是最重要的一处修正:迷走神经不支配盆腔器官。盆腔的脊髓出路是骶部,而「骶部副交感」本身正受到质疑(Espinosa-Medina 等 2016、2018 与 Sivori 等 2024 主张其为交感,Jänig 等 2017 与 Neuhuber 等 2017 反驳)。因此心率变异度衡量的是心脏迷走控制,不能当作盆腔血流的指标。本书用结构可识别性把这一点写成定理:四组参数完全重现同一条心脏观测曲线(残差为浮点误差量级),而它们蕴含的平均内脏传导度从 0.506 到 0.884、最低值从 0.000 到 0.426,所以「心率变异度上升,故内脏灌注恢复」不是推论,而是把假设写成了测量。第五,RMSSD 与高频功率随呼吸方式大幅改变:在平均心搏间期完全不变的合成记录中,RMSSD 从 18.4 变到 31.4 毫秒,而 6 次/分时高频指标反而塌陷,因为呼吸峰已移出频带。第六,血流本身受 r⁴ 律与自动调节约束:流量翻倍需半径增加 18.9%,而流量敏感的自动调节吸收了 34% 到 60% 的稳态反应;在固定心输出量下,扩张一个床区同时从其他床区夺走血流。 第七章与《素问·上古天真论》「恬淡虚无」、《灵枢·本神》及《庄子》「心斋」并读,并与斯多亚学派的「内在堡垒」对勘;一处重要考辨:本轮未能在《黄帝内经》中核到「内观」这一复合词,该词可确定的早期用例是传为唐代的《太上老君内观经》,现代汉语又以之译 vipassanā,与经络穴名「内关」亦非一事。第八章给出四步核查表与一项预注册两臂试验:唯一主要比较为无评判内感受注意对结构匹配的外部注意对照,唯一主要结局为第 6 周身体警觉量表的协方差分析,最小关注效应 0.35 个标准差,每臂 165 例可分析、195 例随机,共 390 例,并预先指定一个阴性对照结局,用以识别泛化的预期效应。书中以标注框区分已发表的证据、可运行的 Python 计算(16 段程序)、原典与作者的模型和假说;除注明的文献数据外,书中数据都是合成的。 Disclosure. The author uses the works of 5D Library, including this book, as the methodological basis of his community courses, the 5D Ascension Cards (Dimensional Shift Card Decks) and the Yafu AI knowledge base, and therefore has a commercial interest in the subject of this book. titre: Developmental Trajectories and Sex-Related Differences in Inner and Outer Body Representations from Childhood to Older Adulthood
resume: Background: Our representation of the body is multidimensional, involving both the processing of internal bodily signals and representations of the body’s external features. Although interoception (inner) and outer body representations show age-related differences, their trajectories have rarely been examined together across different stages of life. Methods: The present study investigated age- and sex-related differences in three dimensions of interoception—interoceptive accuracy (IAcc), interoceptive awareness (IAw), and interoceptive sensibility (ISe)—and in action-oriented (aBR) and non-action-oriented (NaBR) body representations in a large sample of 561 healthy participants distributed across seven age groups, from childhood to older adulthood. Age- and sex-related differences were examined through comparisons across the seven age groups and linear and quadratic regression analyses. Results: Age-related differences emerged across all bodily dimensions, but with distinct patterns. IAcc, as operationalized by heartbeat-counting performance, showed a positive linear association with age, with generally higher scores in middle-aged and older adults, whereas IAw was higher in emerging and young adults than in younger children. ISe showed a negative linear association with age, with greater self-reported focus on bodily sensations in younger age groups and lower levels in later adulthood. Both aBR and NaBR showed inverted U-shaped age-related performance patterns, with generally poorer performance in childhood and better performance in adulthood, although their patterns did not fully overlap. Sex effects were dimension-specific: males showed higher heartbeat-counting scores (IAcc), although this finding was not consistent across analyses, whereas females reported higher ISe levels and performed better on NaBR. Age-by-sex interactions were not significant. Conclusions: Overall, these findings indicate that different dimensions of inner and outer bodily representations show partially distinct age-related patterns and support a multidimensional account of bodily representations across the lifespan, although the cross-sectional design and measurement limitations warrant caution in interpretation.

titre: Emotions Body and Mind: The Holistic Nexus of Well-Being and Performance
resume: Traditional Cartesian dualism separated the mind and body, limiting understanding of the complex interactions between emotions and physiological functioning. Contemporary psychophysiology adopts a biopsychosocial perspective, emphasizing the dynamic interplay among neural, autonomic, endocrine, and social systems in shaping emotional experiences and human behavior. This chapter explores key concepts including interoception, allostasis, autonomic regulation, and polyvagal theory, and examines the effects of chronic emotional dysregulation on cognition, inflammation, and overall well-being. The influence of emotional processes on performance across educational, occupational, athletic, and healthcare settings is discussed. Evidence-based interventions such as cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness, breathing techniques, yoga, and heart rate variability biofeedback are reviewed, along with future directions focusing on digital health, inclusivity, and ethical considerations.

titre: Movement, action, and the case for naturalistic neuroimaging: why OPMs matter
resume: Abstract Contemporary neuroimaging has been optimised for experimental control rather than for the conditions under which neural systems evolved to operate. Accumulating theoretical and empirical work suggests that cognition, perception, and regulation emerge from ongoing sensorimotor coupling between brain, body, and environment. As a result, movement-restricted paradigms may systematically limit the questions we can ask and the phenomena we can observe. Recent advances in movement-tolerant neuroimaging now make it possible to study these processes directly, motivating a shift toward more naturalistic experimental designs. We focus on optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) as they are uniquely placed to record neural and bodily signals within a single measurement framework. We synthesise evidence from computational neuroscience, interoception research, and embodied cognition to demonstrate why naturalistic neuroimaging is not merely complementary to static methods but necessary for understanding brain function as it evolved to operate. We detail how this relaxation of compliance constraints might accelerate clinical advances. This review makes the case that conceptualising the brain as a body-regulator engaged in active inference offers a broader perspective on the importance of movement-tolerant neuroimaging.

titre: Digital Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for insomnia in older adults: a secondary analysis from a population-based randomized controlled trial (Preprint)
resume: BACKGROUND Digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (dCBT-I) has demonstrated robust effects in large population-based studies. However, older adults are underrepresented in trials of fully automated dCBT-I, and evidence on treatment effects and engagement in this age group remains limited. Exploring whether the benefits of fully automated dCBT-I extend to adults aged ≥65 years, and whether older adults engage with unguided digital treatment, is important for informing the use of dCBT-I in this population. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to examine the effects of fully automated dCBT-I on insomnia severity, fatigue, anxiety and depression and sleep-diary outcomes among adults aged ≥65 years, and to assess their engagement with the intervention. METHODS We conducted post hoc secondary age-stratified analyses of data from a large population-based randomized controlled trial of dCBT-I including 1721 adults aged ≥18 years. We focused on participants aged ≥65 years who had been randomized to either a fully automated dCBT-I program (intervention group) or a patient education program (control group). Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 9 weeks, and 6 months and included the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI; primary outcome), anxiety and depression (HADS), fatigue (CFQ), and sleep-diary parameters. Treatment effects were estimated using mixed-effects models examining change over time by group. Engagement was assessed based on completion status of the six intervention modules. RESULTS A total of 139 participants were included, with a mean age of 70 years. Participants who received dCBT-I showed significantly greater reductions in insomnia severity at both 9 weeks (between-group difference -4.4, 95% CI -6.3 to -2.5; Cohen d = -1.2) and 6 months (-2.4, 95% CI -3.6 to -1.2; Cohen d = -0.7) compared to the control group. dCBT-I also led to improvements in fatigue at 9 weeks and in wake after sleep onset, early-morning awakenings, and sleep efficiency, with effects maintained at 6 months. Among participants randomized to dCBT-I, 88% completed the first module and 61% completed all six modules. CONCLUSIONS Even though the program was not specifically adapted for this age group older adults aged ≥65 years benefited from fully automated dCBT-I, with clinically substantial improvements in insomnia severity and sustained improvements in several sleep-continuity outcomes. These findings support the acceptability and therapeutic potential of digital interventions in ageing populations. titre: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Remission from Childhood Anxiety Disorders Across CBT and Control Conditions: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis
resume: This preregistered individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) will use harmonised data from the PADDY repository to develop and validate machine learning models that predict remission from childhood anxiety disorders following cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and control conditions. The study will examine post-treatment and follow-up remission outcomes using pre-treatment child and parent characteristics, and will explore treatment characteristics within CBT-treated participants. The study will compare multiple machine learning algorithms, including logistic regression, random forests, gradient-boosted trees, and deep learning approaches, and evaluate model performance through internal and external validation across independent trials. Beyond prediction accuracy, the study will identify the characteristics that contribute most strongly to remission predictions and assess how well findings generalise across diverse studies and treatment settings.

titre: The epistemic and zetetic irrationality of incessant checking in OCD
resume: Incessant checking is one of the most common compulsive behaviors used to relieve the anxiety caused by obsessions in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). It is agreed that this behavior can be practically irrational, since it only reduces anxiety temporarily and may interfere with one’s daily goals. But what about their irrationality as inquirers? Is there something irrational in what OCD checkers believe about their own inquiries, or in the way they carry them out? In this paper, I take a closer look at these questions. I argue that we must distinguish between those who keep inquiring despite holding incorrect beliefs about their prospects for success in inquiry, and those who do so despite holding correct beliefs about those prospects. In the first case, the failure occurs at the level of belief (i.e. the failure is epistemic), while in the latter case it occurs at the level of inquiry (i.e. the failure is zetetic). Distinguishing between these two scenarios allows for a finer-grained understanding of incessant checking in OCD than existing accounts provide. It also brings into view a dimension of insight that is not captured by standard clinical assessments, namely, whether the agent correctly evaluates her prospects for success in inquiry.

titre: ColoREctal Cancer Surgery and Multimodal pREhabilitation Assessing Tailored Nutrition vs. Exercise - An Open Label Superiority Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: This study will test whether tailored nutritional support before surgery, alone or combined with a structured exercise program, can help adult patients recover better after surgery for colorectal (bowel) cancer. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: usual care, tailored nutritional support alone, or nutritional support combined with a structured exercise program (multimodal prehabilitation). The main goal is to find out whether either approach improves physical function 30 days after surgery, measured by how far participants can walk in 6 minutes (the 6-minute walk test). The study will also look at nutritional intake, physical function, quality of life, complications, hospital readmissions, and length of hospital stay. A total of 140 adult patients scheduled for surgery for colorectal cancer at hospitals in Northern Norway will be enrolled.

titre: Effects of a Prebiotic-Probiotic Combination on Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Quality of Life in Individuals With Constipation: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Controlled Trial
resume: This study aims to evaluate whether a combination of a prebiotic (1-kestose) and a probiotic (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus BBH112) improves gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life in adults with constipation-related symptoms. A total of 40 adults aged 19 to 80 years will be enrolled in this randomized, double-blind, controlled trial. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the probiotic combined with the prebiotic or the probiotic combined with a placebo for 8 weeks. The primary objective is to compare overall satisfaction with gastrointestinal symptom improvement between the two groups after 8 weeks. The study will also assess changes in abdominal pain, bloating, bowel habits, stool consistency, quality of life, and psychological well-being. In addition, changes in the gut microbiome will be evaluated using stool samples collected before and after the intervention. The findings may help determine whether adding a prebiotic to probiotic supplementation provides additional benefits for adults experiencing constipation-related gastrointestinal symptoms.

titre: Immediate effect of hot and cold lumbar douche on gastric myoelectrical activity in healthy individuals: A randomized trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Gastric slow-wave dysrhythmias are associated with functional dyspepsia, gastroparesis and constipation. Lumbar douche, a traditional hydrotherapy thought to act on abdominal and pelvic organs by reflex, has not been tested using electrogastrography. OBJECTIVE: To assess the immediate effect of cold and hot lumbar douche on cutaneous electrogastrographic (EGG) measures in healthy adults. METHODS: In this randomized, parallel-group trial, 78 healthy young adults (n = 39 per group) received hot (HLD; 40-52°C) or cold (CLD; 13-21°C) lumbar douche for 30 s. EGG was recorded before and after the intervention, and fifteen spectral parameters were derived from a visually selected 15-min segment per recording. Post hoc analyses tested whether power changes reflected uniform changes in recording gain. RESULTS: Mean bradygastric frequency fell in both arms (HLD 0.0411 to 0.0371 Hz, p < 0.001; CLD 0.0371 to 0.0341 Hz, p = 0.010), without between-arm difference (p = 0.37). After hot douche, power rose in all three bands (1.73- to 2.39-fold), but uniformly: the distribution across bands was unchanged (all p ≥ 0.45) and a gain-independent power ratio did not change (p = 0.070). This cannot be separated from altered electrode-skin contact. CONCLUSION: A brief thermal stimulus over the thoracolumbar region was followed by a small, consistent fall in bradygastric-band frequency with both hot and cold water, independent of signal amplitude. The rise in EGG power after hot application is confounded by possible electrode-skin contact changes. Neither intervention displaced the normogastric rhythm. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a therapeutic effect. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2025/04/084250.

titre: Latent Class Analysis May Predict Patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome Who Respond to Amitriptyline: Post Hoc Analyses from ATLANTIS
resume: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Low-dose amitriptyline was superior to placebo for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) in the ATLANTIS trial. We performed post hoc analyses of ATLANTIS to assess whether combinations of gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms influenced response to amitriptyline. METHODS: We used latent class analysis (LCA) to subtype participants in ATLANTIS into clusters using both gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms. We assessed differences in response rates with amitriptyline, compared with placebo, by cluster, using mean difference in IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS) and multivariate odds ratios (ORs), along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusted for age, sex, baseline symptom severity score, and IBS subtype. RESULTS: Among 401 participants followed up at 6 months, a four-cluster solution yielded clusters with mild gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms (cluster 1), predominant gastrointestinal symptoms with milder psychological symptoms (cluster 2), predominant psychological symptoms with milder gastrointestinal symptoms (cluster 3), and more severe gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms (cluster 4). Mean change in IBS-SSS by cluster according to treatment allocation was not significant overall (treatment-by-cluster interaction, p=0.76). However, for cluster 3, mean difference in IBS-SSS from baseline to 6 months was significantly greater with amitriptyline than placebo (-103.44 (SD 117.81) versus -61.89 (SD 101.49) p=0.045). Participants in cluster 4, with more severe gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms, were significantly more likely to discontinue trial medication before 6 months (p=0.0023). Mean Antidepressant Side Effect Checklist scores at 6 months were highest in cluster 4, irrespective of treatment allocation, although they were generally higher with amitriptyline than placebo in this cluster. CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory analyses demonstrate clusters of people with IBS based on gastrointestinal and psychological symptoms, which may predict response to, and tolerability of, amitriptyline. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN48075063.
revue: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

titre: Parental self-efficacy and functional constipation in preschool children: a cross-sectional study
resume: PURPOSE: To evaluate parental self-efficacy, parenting attitudes, and maternal anxiety and depression in mothers of preschool children with and without functional constipation (FC) and to examine their associations with FC. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 145 preschool children (72 with FC and 73 controls) and their mothers. FC was diagnosed according to Rome IV criteria. Parental self-efficacy, parenting attitudes, and maternal anxiety and depression were assessed using the BPSE-R, Parenting Attitude Scale, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with FC. RESULTS: Mothers of children with FC had lower child-development teaching and total BPSE-R scores than controls (p = 0.002 and p = 0.019, respectively). Parenting attitudes and mean anxiety and depression scores did not differ between groups. Higher BPSE-R total scores were independently associated with lower odds of FC (aOR = 0.952, 95% CI 0.919-0.986; p = 0.006). Maternal employment was associated with lower odds of FC (aOR = 0.285, 95% CI 0.118-0.690; p = 0.005), whereas a processed-food dietary pattern was associated with higher odds (aOR = 3.261, 95% CI 1.378-7.717; p = 0.007). CONCLUSION: Lower parental self-efficacy was independently associated with FC in preschool children. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the direction of this association.

titre: A Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15-Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 consortium alleviates loperamide-induced constipation by coordinating gut microbiota remodeling, mucosal barrier repair, and aquaporin-mediated water transport
resume: Functional constipation is increasingly recognized as a microbiota-associated disorder involving impaired motility, low-grade inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and abnormal intestinal water transport. This study evaluated whether a defined probiotic consortium composed of Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 (AB consortium; 1:1) could alleviate loperamide-induced constipation and clarified its microbiota-metabolite-barrier mechanism. Male KM mice were allocated to a normal control group, loperamide model group, positive-control group, and low- and high-dose AB consortium groups for 21 days. Gastrointestinal transit, defecation parameters, inflammatory cytokines, gastrointestinal hormones and neurotransmitters, colonic histopathology, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), barrier- and aquaporin-related gene expression, and 16 S rRNA microbial profiles were systematically assessed. The AB consortium markedly shortened the time to first black stool, increased small intestinal transit, and improved weight gain in constipated mice. Mechanistically, the consortium suppressed colonic interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) while restoring interleukin-10 (IL-10), rebalanced gastrin (GAS), motilin (MTL), vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) levels, improved mucosal architecture and goblet-cell-associated mucus secretion, upregulated zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), Claudin-3, and Mucin-2, and normalized the constipation-induced overexpression of aquaporin 3 (AQP3), aquaporin 4 (AQP4), and aquaporin 8 (AQP8). These effects were accompanied by increased acetic, propionic, butyric, and valeric acids and by a shift of the gut microbiota toward a healthier configuration, characterized by higher microbial richness, enrichment of beneficial genera, and suppression of opportunistic pathogens. Correlation analysis further linked beneficial taxa with SCFA production, anti-inflammatory signaling, barrier repair, and reduced aquaporin-associated water absorption. Collectively, these findings indicate that the AB consortium mitigates constipation through an integrated microbiota-SCFA-barrier-water transport axis, supporting its development as a next-generation functional food candidate for constipation management.

titre: Normative Measures of Colon Length in Children With Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Aged 11-17 Years, Based on MRI
resume: To better understand (abnormal) colonic anatomy on imaging, data on normal colonic anatomy in the unaffected population are crucial. We assessed colon lengths in children without constipation on MRI. This retrospective study included patients (< 18 years), who underwent MRI-enterography between 2016 and 2020 for suspected inflammatory bowel disease, and did not meet Rome-IV criteria for functional constipation. Patients with colonic inflammation were excluded. Primary outcome was the mean total colon length/BSA (cm/m2) (95% CI; ±2SD), and the secondary outcomes were total colon length (cm), rectosigmoid length/BSA (cm/m2), and rectosigmoid length (cm). Colon segments were independently measured on coronal T2-weighted MRI using 3D multiple-point measurements. Linear regression was used to evaluate associations between total colon length and sex, age, height, weight, body surface area (BSA). Eighty-one patients (median age 15 years; range 11-17; 53% male) were included. The mean total colon length/BSA was 72.9 ± 21.0 cm/m2. Mean total colon length was 115.8 ± 13.8 cm, mean rectosigmoid length/BSA was 24.2 ± 12.3 cm/m2, and mean rectosigmoid length was 38.2 ± 7.9 cm. Additionally, we assessed colonic segments per age group. Colon length significantly correlated with age (p = 0.03), height (p < 0.001), weight (p < 0.001), and BSA (p < 0.001). In a multivariable linear regression analysis, BSA was significantly correlated with total colon length (95% CI 21.4-49.4; p < 0.0001). This study provides data on colon and rectosigmoid lengths in children, aged 11-17 years, without constipation measured on MRI-enterography. This knowledge can be used for the identification of abnormal colonic anatomy in children with therapy-resistant constipation on imaging.

titre: Xiaoyaosan ameliorates depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction: insights into gut-brain fluid metabolism and aldosterone/MR-related signaling
resume: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The co-occurrence of depression and gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction presents a clinical challenge, as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like sertraline frequently exacerbate gastrointestinal adverse symptoms. Xiaoyaosan, a classic Chinese prescription, simultaneously alleviates both domains, yet its underlying its dual-target efficacy remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the effects of Xiaoyaosan on depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction, with particular emphasis on their associations with fluid metabolism-related alterations and aldosterone/MR signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) -induced depressed rat model was employed. We evaluated depression-like behaviors, fluid metabolism phenotypes, colonic transcriptomics, and performed targeted molecular analyses on colonic and hippocampal tissues. RESULTS: At the tested dose, Xiaoyaosan improved depression-like behaviors and several gastrointestinal and fluid metabolism-related parameters in CUMS-exposed rats. Although both XYS and sertraline alleviated depression-like behaviors, distinct effects on gastrointestinal functional indicators were observed under the volume-matched administration conditions. Colonic transcriptomic analysis revealed gene expression changes associated with aldosterone-related signaling. XYS treatment reduced circulating aldosterone and corticosterone levels, improved serum electrolyte profiles and colonic barrier-associated indicators, and decreased MR expression in the colon and hippocampus. These changes were accompanied by increased hippocampal AQP4 mRNA expression, improved ATPase activities, and attenuated neuroinflammatory responses. Correlation analyses further revealed associations among these molecular alterations and behavioral parameters. CONCLUSION: Using integrated behavioral, gastrointestinal, transcriptomic, and molecular analyses, this study provides novel experimental evidence linking the beneficial effects of XYS on depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction to coordinated alterations in fluid metabolism-related indicators and aldosterone/MR signaling, offering a fresh mechanistic perspective on gut-brain regulatory effects of XYS.

titre: A human gut-BBB-brain microphysiological model for studying Alzheimer's disease
resume: The gut-brain axis (GBA) has emerged as a crucial contributor to neurodegenerative diseases, with growing evidence implicating gut-derived metabolic and signaling alterations in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the lack of human-relevant in vitro models limits our ability to explore the mechanisms of this axis effectively. To address this limitation, we developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived gut-blood-brain barrier (BBB)-brain microphysiological system that enables systematic investigation of gut-brain interactions in AD under controlled conditions. Using this platform, we showed that communication between gut and brain compartments was associated with increased expression of neuronal and glial markers, as well as phenotypes indicative of enhanced maturation-associated molecular features. Integrating gut and brain compartments also revealed disease-associated molecular and cellular alterations not observed in brain organoids alone. Importantly, exposure of healthy brain organoids to signals from AD patient-derived gut organoids induced changes in neuronal and glial phenotypes, indicating that gut-derived factors may contribute to brain dysfunction in AD. Collectively, our findings establish a human iPSC-derived gut-BBB-brain platform for studying brain organoid responses under combined intestinal and BBB co-culture conditions and provide an experimental framework for exploratory studies of AD-associated inter-organ influences.

titre: Does obesity pharmacotherapy change eating behaviour in humans? Evaluation of the literature using learnings from bariatric surgery
resume: Obesity is characterised by the dysregulation of the neurobiological systems governing hunger, satiety and food reward. Dysfunction in signalling across the gut-brain axis impairs both homeostatic and hedonic control of eating, ultimately resulting in excessive energy intake. The weight loss achieved through pharmacological and surgical interventions is not primarily the result of cognitive behavioural restraint; it instead reflects the direct biological modification of the neuroendocrine circuits involved in regulation of eating behaviour. This review applies a conceptual framework structured around two axes; homeostatic versus hedonic eating and the appetitive versus consummatory phases of feeding to interpret how these interventions change eating behaviour. Bariatric surgery has a substantially more mature evidence base. The Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in particular, produces sustained modification in consummatory homeostatic behaviour - with earlier satiation and meal termination, in conjunction with short-term changes in food preferences. Evidence for GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists demonstrates a parallel profile of reduced hunger, increased satiety, attenuated food-cue reactivity and subduing of the hedonic drive. Whether the effects of pharmacotherapy and surgery engage in the same biological processes and whether their effects follow a similar time course remains an unresolved question. We consider the implications of this framework for nutrition and dietetic practice.
revue: The Proceedings of the Nutrition Society

titre: Ketamine, an interoceptive associative agent? Evidence from ketamine-assisted Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement for opioid use disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Relapse in opioid use disorder (OUD) remains common despite pharmacotherapy. Altered interoceptive processing may contribute to addiction, and ketamine-induced changes in salience and insula-related networks may facilitate mindfulness-based interoceptive learning. AIMS: This secondary analysis examined whether ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) added to Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) improved interoceptive awareness and whether these changes mediated reductions in opioid craving. METHODS: Sixty-eight adults with OUD receiving buprenorphine were randomized to 8 weeks of MORE with or without KAP. Assignment was unblinded, and outcomes were self-reported. Interoception was assessed using ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of body awareness and Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) subscales. Posttreatment EMA data were available for 18 MORE + KAP and 15 MORE participants. Mixed-effects models and path analysis were conducted. RESULTS: Piecewise modeling showed a greater increase in EMA-assessed body awareness salience in MORE + KAP during days 1-35, spanning the pre-dosing and first-ketamine-dose period (B = 0.039, standard error (SE) = 0.005, p < 0.001). Slopes attenuated during days 36-90 (group × slope-change: B = -0.035, SE = 0.008, p < 0.001), although body awareness remained higher for MORE+KAP through follow-up. MORE + KAP increased MAIA Self-Regulation and Body Listening. A composite of these facets mediated reduced opioid craving at 3 months (indirect effect: B = -11.27, 95% bootstrap confidence interval (CI) [-25.50, -0.25], p = 0.044; κ2 = 0.378). CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive ketamine was associated with rapid, sustained increases in body awareness salience. Improvements in interoceptive regulatory capacity mediated reduced opioid craving, supporting interoception as a potential mechanism and treatment target in ketamine-augmented mindfulness interventions for OUD. CLINICALTRIALS: gov:NCT04892251.

titre: Developing content validity of a questionnaire exploring various relationships with one's body in obesity: A Delphi expert consensus
resume: BACKGROUND: Factors contributing to weight variation, and specifically the perception of one's own body, are major elements to take into account in the obesity clinical pathway. The aim of the study was to develop and test the content validity of a multidimensional self-administered questionnaire exploring body-relatedness. METHODS: A review guided the development of the questionnaire. Fifty-two dimensions and 261 items were extracted. A Delphi method was then performed with 23 experts and 7 patients suffering from obesity. In the 4-Round Delphi, the group rated their agreement on the utility and the relevance of dimensions and items, respectively. The consensus was reached when 75% of members were in agreement. RESULTS: Consensus was reached for a 38-dimension and 65-item questionnaire covering 11 domains: (1) body image satisfaction, (2) anxiety about the whole or parts of the body, (3) deviation of logical thinking from reality, (4) socio-cultural influence on appearance, (5) behaviour related to body image, (6) perception of interoceptive signals, (7) perception of health related to body relationships, (8) gap between silhouette perception and reality, (9) reaction to hunger, (10) satisfaction with the sensation generated by touch, and (11) social distances. CONCLUSIONS: The new clinical tool is multidimensional, the items are specific, easy to understand and to interpret in the clinical care pathway. Through this new tool, we hope to raise professionals' awareness of complex body-related disorders.

titre: Brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression: Desynchronization between salience network neuropsychological connectivity and heart rate variability
resume: Somatic depression is a distinct subtype of major depressive disorder, with a poorer response to treatment, an elevated risk of suicidal behaviour, and a worse prognosis. Interoception, the sense of internal bodily signals, is related to somatic symptoms. However, the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms of body brain communication remain unclear. 293 depressed patients (145 with somatic symptoms and 148 without), and 160 healthy controls underwent magnetoencephalography during a resting state. Both the intra- and inter-network neural oscillation patterns of the salience network, were computed, alongside and heart rate variability (HRV) as a measure of autonomic function. Individuals with somatic depression exhibited lower HRV, accompanied by theta hyper-connectivity within the salience network. Although higher theta connectivity was linked to increased HRV in controls, this correlation was attenuated or even reversed in patients with somatic depression. Our findings identify a specific pattern of brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression, characterized by disrupted communication between salience network theta oscillations and autonomic cardiac regulation. This provides novel neuroimaging evidence for body-brain communication deficits in a clinically important depression subtype.

titre: Choosing now Over Later: What Temporal Discounting Reveals About Italian University Students and Addiction Risk
resume: Delay, or temporal discounting - the tendency to prefer smaller immediate rewards over larger delayed ones - is a cognitive phenomenon closely linked to impulsivity, executive functioning, and addiction. It is also regarded as a transdiagnostic marker across various psychiatric conditions. Following its significance, research on addiction risk has examined this phenomenon within university students, as a vulnerable group due to the transition from adolescence to early adulthood, along with the academic stress and pressure they commonly experience. In the present study, we examined the relationship between temporal discounting and psychological risk factors associated with the development and maintenance of addictive behaviors in a sample of Italian university students. Participants (N = 175) completed an intertemporal choice task involving decisions between hypothetical monetary rewards available either immediately or after a specified delay. In addition, they completed self-report questionnaires assessing emotional dysregulation, psychological distress, alexithymia, body awareness, autonomic reactivity, and potentially addictive behaviors. The results indicated that steeper discounting rates were significantly associated with higher levels of addiction-related factors and specific psychological profiles, including emotional dysregulation, obsessive thinking, and difficulties in emotional stability and reactivity. These findings underlie the importance of reward-related decision-making and emotional regulation/processing as individual vulnerability factors for addiction among university students. They also suggest potential targets for prevention and early intervention strategies in this population.

titre: Symptom burden mediates the link between self-reported interoceptive accuracy and self-care in chronic heart failure: a CSM-based cross-sectional study
resume: Effective chronic heart failure (CHF) management critically depends on patients’ self-care (maintenance, symptom perception and management).1 Successful self-care begins with the perceived ability to accurately perceive internal bodily signals; when assessed by self-report, this construct is referred to as self-reported interoceptive accuracy (i.e. perceived interoceptive accuracy).2 Guided by the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation (CSM),3 self-reported interoceptive accuracy helps transform raw somatic signals into symptom representations, while cumulative distress constitutes symptom burden that guides self-care actions. Although impaired interoception may amplify negative symptom appraisals, direct mediation testing of symptom burden in the self-reported interoceptive accuracy-self-care link remains lacking in CHF. Therefore, this study used the Interoceptive Accuracy Scale (IAS), a self-report instrument measuring perceived interoceptive accuracy, and tested whether symptom burden mediates the relationship between self-reported interoceptive accuracy and self-care dimensions. This cross-sectional study enrolled 353 CHF patients from the Department of Cardiology, First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University (February–October 2025; Ethics Approval No. 2025-592). Inclusion: age ≥ 18 years, CHF diagnosis per guidelines,4 NYHA class II-IV, and informed consent. The investigation conforms with the principles outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki. Sample size was estimated via Monte Carlo simulation for SEM (power = 0.80, α = 0.05), indicating a minimum required sample of 262; our final sample exceeded this.

titre: Emergent Roles of RVLMC1 Neurons in Cardiovascular Homeostasis and Systemic Physiological Regulation
resume: PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: Adrenergic C1 neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLMC1) have long been recognized for their role in regulating sympathetic activity and arterial blood pressure (BP). However, novel approaches such as genetic targeting, optogenetics, fiber photometry, among others, allowed us to study the biology of these neurons in deeper detail and in non-anesthetized preparations, unraveling previously underappreciated or unrecognized functions. Here we will discuss recent studies that explored the function of RVLMC1 neurons for the sympathetic regulation of BP and also the emergent roles of these cells for other processes involved in systemic physiological regulation. RECENT FINDINGS: Using selective methods of manipulation and recording of neuronal activity in conscious animals, it was demonstrated that RVLMC1 neurons play a critical role in BP stability across multiple behaviors, including sleep-wake state and postural changes. Besides cardiovascular control, recent evidence shows that these neurons play a critical role in different homeostatic functions such as thermoregulation, immune response, glycemia and in complex behaviors such as anxiety. RVLMC1 neurons are a key hub that integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral systems to regulate BP and other basic physiological functions. Along with their role in cardiovascular regulation, these emergent roles of RVLMC1 neurons may also need to be considered when explaining the complex and multifactorial pathophysiology of cardiometabolic diseases associated with hypertension.

titre: Acting Out Traumatic Hysteria at the Salpêtrière Hospital: Performance and Practice in Jean-Martin Charcot's Clinic
resume: This article reexamines neurologist Jean-Martin Charcot's (1825-1893) clinical work at the Salpêtrière Hospital in Paris and reassesses how he diagnosed and treated patients with traumatic hysteria. Departing from scholarship that views Charcot as a positivist nosologist or a clinical performer, this study demonstrates that his clinical practice cannot be reduced to either nosological classification or theatrical spectacle alone. Drawing on photographic documentation, clinical lessons, recorded physician-patient interactions, and a first-person testimony, the study advances three main arguments. Charcot's clinical practice was defined by embryonic versions of psychological concepts (autosuggestion, transference, acting out, dissociation, idées fixes, abreaction, and motor reeducation) that foreshadowed Janet's and Freud's psychoanalytic theories. Moreover, the performative nature of Charcot's clinical theater also created, perhaps inadvertently, a setting in which patients could explore their unconscious and act out their trauma. Finally, rather than viewing patients' somatic expressions as exclusively symptoms of suffering (or worse still, as malingering or forms of clinical manipulation), they are interpreted as posttraumatic protests directed, consciously or unconsciously, at the traumatic event(s) and the social, institutional, and medical conditions that pathologized and silenced their expressions.
revue: Journal of the American Psychoanalytic Association

titre: Exposure-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Increases Connectivity Between the Central Executive and Salience Networks in Pediatric Anxiety
resume: OBJECTIVE: Exposure is considered the most active element of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for pediatric anxiety. Yet many youth do not respond to CBT, and exposure is the component patients most often find difficult to tolerate. Cognitive control and its supporting neural substrates may enhance exposure efficacy by helping youth remain engaged with feared stimuli despite urges to avoid. However, little work has identified how exposure-based CBT modulates intrinsic connectivity of tripartite networks that support cognitive control (e.g., central executive [CEN], salience [SN], and default mode networks [DMN]), limiting efforts to develop strategies to improve and personalize treatment. Progress may be limited by individual variability in network connectivity in anxiety, which may obscure treatment-related effects in group-averaged analyses. This randomized clinical trial (RCT) leverages person-specific network modeling to test how exposure versus relaxation components of CBT influence resting-state connectivity of cognitive control networks in pediatric anxiety. METHOD: Youth aged 7-18 years with an anxiety disorder (N = 100) or low/no anxiety (L/NA; N = 35) completed resting-state fMRI scans at baseline. Patients were randomized to exposure-focused CBT (EF-CBT) or relaxation mentorship training (RMT). Resting-state connectivity was reassessed following treatment (or after a commensurate interval in L/NA youth) in 112 participants. Changes in within-CEN, CEN-SN, and CEN-DMN density were examined using Group Iterative Multiple Model Estimation, which yields sparse, person-specific networks capturing both shared and individual connectivity structure. RESULTS: At baseline, anxious youth exhibited lower density within-CEN and between CEN-DMN than L/NA youth. Treatment effects differed by intervention: EF-CBT selectively increased CEN-SN density, whereas RMT increased within-CEN density. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate dissociable effects of exposure and relaxation on cognitive control network organization in pediatric anxiety. These results indicate that exposure-focused CBT is uniquely associated with increased connectivity between control and salience systems, consistent with a mechanism supporting top-down control of threat-related signals during exposure. Person-specific measures of tripartite network connectivity may inform future efforts to identify candidate neural targets for optimizing and personalizing treatment.
revue: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

titre: Enhancing relationship quality in couples affected by ADHD: a randomized controlled study of a couple's intervention
resume: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is highly prevalent among adults, making it one of the most common psychiatric diagnoses in this population associated with negative functional impact across multiple life areas, including romantic relationships. Despite this, scientifically evaluated interventions specifically targeting relationship quality in couples where one or both partners have ADHD remain limited. This study presents a randomized controlled evaluation of a couple-based intervention for ADHD, assessing its impact on relationship quality and participants' experiences. Eighty couples (n = 160 participants) were randomized to either an intervention group or a waitlist control group, with assessments conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Intention-to-treat analyses using Linear Mixed Models indicated no significant between-group difference for the primary outcome of relationship quality (QDR-36), nor for secondary outcomes of stress, depression, anxiety, or ADHD-related quality of life. A significant between-group interaction effect was found for ADHD symptoms (ASRS), however, this effect unexpectedly favored the waitlist control group, which showed a greater reduction in symptoms compared to the intervention group. The participants' evaluation of the course indicated an overall high rating of satisfaction with the content. Suggestions for improving access to the course as well as improving the course's effect on relationship quality are discussed.

titre: Efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depression symptoms in Parkinson's disease patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depression are highly prevalent non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease (PD), severely compromising health-related quality of life. Conventional pharmacological management is frequently constrained by adverse effects, polypharmacy, and pharmacokinetic interactions. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) represents a promising structured non-pharmacological strategy, but an updated, comprehensive synthesis of clinical trial evidence is warranted. OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and clinical safety profile of CBT for alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with PD. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to October 2025. RCTs evaluating CBT (≥ 4 sessions over ≥ 4 weeks) versus control conditions (e.g., treatment as usual, waitlist, active controls) in adults with PD reporting anxiety and/or depression outcomes were included. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled via random-effects models. Subgroup, sensitivity, and publication bias analyses were performed. RESULTS: Twenty-one RCTs comprising 892 patients with PD (CBT: n = 465; control: n = 427) were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that CBT was associated with statistically significant reductions in anxiety symptoms (16 studies; SMD = -0.66, 95% CI -0.83 to -0.50; P < 0.001; I2 = 79.1%) and depressive symptoms (14 studies; SMD = -0.61, 95% CI -0.78 to -0.44; P < 0.001; I2 = 86.6%). Subgroup analyses indicated enhanced therapeutic effects in interventions with durations exceeding 10 weeks and when evaluated using population-adapted instruments (e.g., GAI, GDS). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of pooled estimates, and Egger's tests revealed no significant publication bias. CONCLUSION: CBT produces significant, clinically meaningful reductions in anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with Parkinson's disease. Despite substantial between-study heterogeneity and variations in intervention delivery, structured CBT should be recommended as an integral component of multidisciplinary PD care. Larger multicenter RCTs with standardized disease-specific core outcome sets and longer follow-up are warranted.
revue: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

titre: Efficacy of remote cognitive-behavior therapy for obsessive-compulsive disorder: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common psychiatric condition. Several factors limit individuals from receiving evidence-based treatment, and remote treatments have been developed to improve access. The aim of this study was to synthesize the existing literature on remote treatment for OCD using a meta-analytic approach. Twenty-three studies (n = 1897; Mage range = 11.00 - 41.10 years; % female range = 38.00 - 93.30%) were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled within-group effect size was large across all remote treatments from pre-treatment to post-treatment (k = 29; g = 1.13; 95% CI [0.95, 1.30]) and from pre-treatment to follow-up (k = 17; g = 1.19; 95% CI [0.99, 1.38]). The pooled between-group effect size was small at post-treatment (k = 27; g = 0.43; 95% CI [0.17, 0.69]), favoring the remote treatment group. While the pooled between-group effect size was also small at follow-up (k = 8; g = -0.21; 95% CI [-0.41, -0.01]), it favored the control condition. Moderator analyses indicated that remote treatments were more efficacious than passive control groups (k = 12; g = 1.05; 95% CI [0.76, 1.34]) and active control groups (k = 6; g = 0.45; 95% CI [0.12, 0.79]) at post-treatment. However, face-to-face treatment was more efficacious than remote treatment at post-treatment (k = 9; g = -0.32; 95% CI [-0.63, -0.02]). However, moderator analyses were not significant at follow-up. These findings add to the growing body of literature examining the efficacy of remote treatment for OCD and demonstrate potential for remote stepped care treatment.

titre: Network-based virtual perturbation for modeling DBS-related network effects in obsessive-compulsive and major depressive disorders
resume: BACKGROUND: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) efficacy for psychiatric disorders remains heterogeneous due to incomplete mechanistic insights and insufficient individualized treatment planning. A biologically grounded computational framework is urgently needed to simulate DBS-related differences for treatment-resistant patients. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data from 11 patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and 11 with major depressive disorder (MDD), scanned in DBS-ON and DBS-OFF states, were used to derive functional connectivity (FC) via network deconvolution. Whole-brain dynamic modeling incorporated stimulation targets, amplitudes, and frequencies to simulate DBS effects in silico. RESULTS: The model recapitulated syndrome-specific DBS-related network patterns in exploratory analyses. OCD stimulation primarily altered frontal-subcortical connectivity, whereas MDD stimulation predominantly affected default mode network hubs (p < 0.05). Under leave-one-out cross-validation, correlations between predicted and observed clinical outcomes were r = 0.625 in OCD (p = 0.040) and r = 0.659 in MDD (p = 0.028). Applying the same FC signatures to simulated FC yielded r = 0.465 in OCD (p = 0.149) and r = 0.627 in MDD (p = 0.039). In a proof-of-concept application to a separate OCD cohort (N = 92), three individuals showed high model-predicted NAc-response profiles and predicted improvement exceeding 35%. CONCLUSIONS: This hypothesis-generating framework retrospectively models DBS-related network effects using individualized resting-state FC and virtual perturbations. Linking simulated FC states with empirical DBS-ON/OFF patterns may help characterize how baseline functional architecture shapes DBS-related network responses and inform future individualized DBS modeling.

titre: Proctalgia Fugax: An Emerging Anorectal Disorder in Children and Adolescents
resume: Introduction: Proctalgia fugax (PF) is an anorectal disorder characterized by sudden, transient episodes of rectal pain. Although it has traditionally been described in adults, its recognition in pediatrics has gained relevance with its inclusion in the Rome V Criteria. Objective: To determine the prevalence of PF according to the Rome IV Criteria for adults modified for pediatrics, in schoolchildren and adolescents attending a Public School in Cali, Colombia. Methods: An observational, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted in schoolchildren and adolescents aged 10–18 years. Demographic, clinical, and socioaffective variables were collected. Questionnaires were administered to identify disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs) (QPGS-IV), quality of life (PedsQL), and anx-iety/depression (PROMIS-Anxiety/PROMIS-Depression). PF was defined using the Rome IV Criteria for adults modified for pediatrics. Statistical analysis included measures of central tendency and the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, with p Results: A total of 199 schoolchildren and adolescents were included (mean age 14.3 ± 2.0 years; 75.4% adolescents; 53.8% male; 39.7% mixed race). Regarding socioaffective variables, 65.8% had separated or divorced parents; school and social ab-senteeism were present in 43.2% and 34.2%, respectively; impaired quality of life in 53.8%; anxiety in 35.2%; and depression in 37.2%. The prevalence of any DGBI was 28.1%, defecation-related DGBIs 16.6%, and PF 3.0%. None of the variables analyzed showed significant differences for PF, except anxiety (p=0.002). Conclusions: PF was identified in 3.0% of the participants, showing that it can occur in schoolchildren and adolescents, with anxiety being an important factor to consider.

titre: The rise of ileal bypass surgery in the United States: A cautionary tale for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: From jejuno-ileal bypass to duodeno-ileal bypass
resume: Abstract The landscape of metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) has become increasingly complex with the proliferation of intestinal bypass procedures and the rise in ileal bypass (IBS) procedures (SADI-S and DS) in the United States, alongside a confusing array of procedure names that fail to reflect underlying physiology. We propose an anatomy-based classification distinguishing jejunal bypass (JBS), including RYGB, OAGB, and SASJ, from ileal bypass (IBS), including SADI-S, BPD/DS, SASI, and type I distalization, based on the site of intestinal anastomosis. This classification enables better patient selection, facilitates benefit-risk assessment of new procedures like SASJ and SASI, highlights the importance of standardized measurement of biliopancreatic limb (BPL) length, common channel (CC), and total alimentary limb length (TALL) to prevent malnutrition, and promises to improve comparative research, individualized procedure selection, and future surgical innovation.

titre: ACTIVATION OF THE ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR REDUCES VISCERAL HYPERSENSITIVITY IN A MOUSE MODEL OF COLITIS IN REMISSION
resume: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is expressed on gut-projecting transient receptor potential vanilloid-1 (TRPV1) + nociceptors, but whether it has a role in regulating abdominal pain remains to be determined. Approximately 50% of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients experience chronic abdominal pain, even when their inflammatory disease is in remission. Previous work has shown that tryptophan metabolism to indole derivatives is reduced in IBD patients. Since microbial tryptophan metabolites (indole derivatives) serve as ligands for AhR, we hypothesized that reduced AhR activation contributes to enhanced pain sensitivity. We used a post-colitis mouse model of visceral hypersensitivity to examine the role of AhR as a mediator of nociception. AhR activation using both natural and synthetic agonists reduced visceral hypersensitivity in both male and female post-colitis mice. Conversely, pharmacological inhibition of AhR blocked the antinociceptive effects of indoles. Mechanistically, AhR activation by indole-3-pyruvic acid (IPyA) increased the transcription of the inward rectifying potassium channel Kir2.2, in TRPV1 + neurons and markedly reduced neuronal activation within the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. Metagenomic analysis revealed sex differences in indole-producing bacteria, with control males exhibiting enriched abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and Alistipes compared to post-colitis males and female controls. These findings demonstrate that oral IPyA supplementation in post-colitis mice attenuates visceral hypersensitivity in part through activation of nociceptor AhR, providing insights that support the therapeutic targeting of AhR to treat abdominal pain in IBD patients in remission.
