titre: The application of an artificial intelligence-enhanced virtual reality cognitive behavioral therapy tool is feasible and acceptable in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: A multicenter mixed methods pilot study
resume: Background Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently experience anxiety, pain, and reduced quality of life. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective for anxiety, but access may be limited. We evaluated the feasibility and explored the potential clinical impact of an artificial intelligence-powered virtual reality CBT-based application (XAIA [eXtended Reality Artificially Intelligent Ally]) in patients with IBD. Methods This was a multicenter, mixed-methods pilot study recruiting adults with IBD from the University of Chicago and Cedars-Sinai medical centers. Participants completed a single 30-minute session with the XAIA conversational avatar. Pain and anxiety were measured before and after the session using a visual analog pain scale and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, respectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted after the session to assess acceptability. Quantitative analysis was completed using paired t tests, and interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis. Results Thirty-four participants (median age 34 years, 71% women, 59% with Crohn's disease) participated in this study. Qualitative analysis revealed high acceptability, with participants reporting feelings of safety, validation, and improved coping. Participants valued the immersive environment, conversational avatar, and ability to discuss sensitive topics without judgment. As an exploratory outcome, participants reported a statistically significant improvement in pain (-0.46; P = .011) and anxiety (-10.65; P Conclusions A single artificial intelligence-driven virtual reality CBT-based session in patients with IBD was feasible and well accepted and demonstrated preliminary evidence for acute reductions in pain and anxiety scores. Immersive digital behavioral health interventions may represent a scalable adjunct to traditional mental health support among adults with IBD.

titre: Transanal irrigation: a valid option for patients with major low anterior resection syndrome or those who are refractory to medical treatment
resume: Introduction Sphincter-preserving rectal surgery may be associated with functional disorders. Low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) is a complication that presents as faecal incontinence, urgency and fragmented stools. Its treatment is stepwise, with transanal irrigation (TAI) being a second-line treatment in refractory cases and a first-line treatment in major LARS. The aim is to analyse the usefulness of TAI in improving symptoms and quality of life in patients with major LARS or LARS refractory to treatment. Methods A retrospective descriptive study of patients with LARS treated with TAI at our hospital. Demographic and clinical variables, details of previous treatments, factors related to rectal cancer and TAI, and scores on the LARS and EuroQol-5D scales were recorded before and 6 months after treatment. Results A sample of 25 patients with a mean age of 63.8 years, most of whom had undergone surgery for rectal cancer with end-to-end colorectal anastomosis. The LARS score improved from 33.5 to 24.6 following treatment. The EuroQol-5D score increased from 36 to 62.8, with both changes showing a statistically significant difference (p Conclusions In patients with major LARS or LARS refractory to medical treatment, TAI may be a useful and effective treatment, improving their symptoms and quality of life. It is a simple therapeutic strategy with few serious complications, although a considerable proportion of patients discontinue treatment. More extensive and structured programmes of education, training and follow-up should be implemented for patients eligible for this treatment.

titre: The Lived Experiences of Long-Term Users of Copper-T Intrauterine Devices: A phenomenological Qualitative Study among women at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Uganda
resume: Background The Copper-T intrauterine device (Cu-T IUD) is a highly effective, non- hormonal, long-acting reversible contraceptive that can protect against pregnancy for up to 12 years, with a failure rate under 1%. Despite its clinical efficacy, early discontinuation remains a substantial challenge in Uganda, where discontinuation is approximated at 29% within the first year of use. Understanding the experiences of women using the Cu-T IUD is important to predict factors associated with discontinuation and to inform practice. Methods Between September and November 2025, we conducted twenty in-depth interviews with women of reproductive age (15-49 years) who had used a Cu-T IUD for at least two years, recruited from the family planning clinic of Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Kampala, Uganda. Data were analysed thematically, guided by the Social-Ecological Model and Lazarus and Folkman’s Transactional Model of Stress and Coping. Results Long-term Cu-T IUD users reported both positive and negative experiences shaped by individual, interpersonal, and community factors. Two themes were identified at the individual-level domain: experiences during insertion and post-insertion experiences. Negative experiences, particularly heavy menstrual bleeding, anxiety, and abdominal pain, were common and distressing. Participants employed coping strategies, including taking painkillers, using home remedies, and resting, to manage these challenges with Cu-T IUD use. Conclusions Negative experiences of Cu-T IUD are common among long-term users; women’s coping strategies such as taking painkillers lead to continued use. Client-centred pre- insertion counselling addressing both anticipated side effects and common misconceptions, alongside accessible follow-up services, may facilitate long-term Cu-T IUD use.

titre: Effectiveness and safety of pharmacological treatments for Cushing's disease: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Objective To provide an updated assessment of the efficacy, safety, and clinical outcomes of pharmacological treatments for Cushing's disease, focusing on cabergoline, ketoconazole, pasireotide, and osilodrostat. Materials and methods This systematic review update was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. Outcomes included disease control rates, adverse events, and improvements in comorbidities and quality of life. Results Eleven new studies were included. In the updated analysis, disease control rates were 35.5% for cabergoline (95% confidence interval [CI]: 28-43%; 7 studies, 155 patients), 42% for ketoconazole (95% CI: 38-47%; 7 studies, 488 patients), 42% for pasireotide (95% CI: 28-58%; 10 studies, 580 patients), and 67% for osilodrostat (95% CI: 61-73%; 4 studies, 263 participants). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was very low for pasireotide and low for the other agents. Osilodrostat increased cortisol normalization 4.56-fold versus placebo (95% CI: 1.53-13.56; 2 studies, 144 patients; moderate certainty). Osilodrostat and pasireotide improved CushingQoL scores by 13.23 points (95% CI: 10.78-15.68) and 8.96 points (95% CI: 4.37-13.55), respectively. Pasireotide was predominantly associated with dysglycemia. Cabergoline most often caused mild adverse events, with treatment escape in 11%. Ketoconazole was linked to mildly elevated transaminases and gastrointestinal symptoms. Osilodrostat most commonly resulted in fatigue and adrenal insufficiency, often reflecting therapeutic response. Conclusion Pharmacological disease control rates in Cushing's disease range from 35.5% to 67%, with osilodrostat achieving the highest rates and being the only agent supported by placebo-controlled evidence demonstrating a statistically significant effect. In the absence of head-to-head comparisons, treatment decisions remain individualized.

titre: Pharmacology Update: Pruritus in Palliative Care With Focus on Naltrexone
resume: BackgroundPruritus is a common and often distressing symptom in palliative care, affecting a significant fraction of patients and significantly impairing sleep, mood, and quality of life. Common etiologies include chronic kidney disease, cholestatic liver disease, hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, medication-related syndromes, and paraneoplastic processes. Conventional treatments, including antihistamines, antidepressants, gabapentinoids, ondansetron, and ultraviolet-B phototherapy, are frequently limited by adverse effects, cost, or practicality in seriously ill patients.ObjectiveTo review the pathophysiology of pruritus relevant to palliative care and evaluate the emerging role of naltrexone as a therapeutic option for refractory pruritus.MethodsNarrative review of the literature addressing the mechanisms of pruritus, current treatment approaches, and clinical evidence supporting the use of naltrexone across various pruritic conditions encountered in palliative medicine.ResultsIncreasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the endogenous opioid system in the pathogenesis of several forms of chronic pruritus. As a competitive opioid receptor antagonist, naltrexone may mitigate "itch" through μ-opioid receptor blockade and restoration of opioid signaling balance. The strongest evidence supports its use in cholestatic pruritus, where randomized placebo-controlled trials demonstrated significant reductions in symptom severity with 50 mg daily dosing. Evidence in uremic pruritus is mixed, with some studies showing benefit and others finding no superiority over placebo. Case reports and small series suggest potential efficacy in malignancy-associated pruritus, polycythemia vera, and selected dermatologic disorders. Limitations include contraindication in patients receiving opioid therapy, potential precipitation of withdrawal, and adverse effects such as nausea, gastrointestinal distress, dizziness, fatigue, and sleep disturbance.ConclusionsNaltrexone represents a mechanistically rational and potentially effective option for selected patients with refractory pruritus in palliative care. Current evidence is most compelling for cholestatic pruritus, while data for other etiologies remain limited and heterogeneous. Larger prospective studies are needed to define optimal dosing strategies, identify patients most likely to benefit, and better characterize its role in opioid-exposed palliative care populations.
revue: The American journal of hospice & palliative care

titre: Feeling Too Much or Too Little: Alexithymia Moderates How Self-Reported Physiological Hyperarousal Shapes Risky Decisions
resume: Background Embodied cognition frameworks propose that physiological states shape decision-making, yet the contribution of sustained threat-related hyperarousal and individual differences in interoceptive integration remains poorly understood. This study examined whether self-reported physiological hyperarousal predicted Prospect Theory decision parameters: loss aversion (λ), value sensitivity (ρ), and choice consistency (τ); and whether alexithymia moderated these associations. Methods Sixty-eight healthy young adults ( M age = 18.94, SD = 1.46; 85% women) completed the DASS-21 anxiety subscale as a measure of hyperarousal, the TAS-20 as a measure of alexithymia, and a 64-trial Mixed Gambles Task; individual Prospect Theory parameters were estimated via hierarchical Bayesian analysis. Moderation analyses were conducted using Hayes’ PROCESS macro with Johnson-Neyman probing. Results Self-reported hyperarousal negatively predicted choice consistency and value sensitivity, but not loss aversion. Alexithymia moderated both effects through distinct conditional patterns: the self-reported hyperarousal–choice consistency association was significant only below a TAS-20 threshold of 51.05 (67.65% of the sample), reflecting monotonic buffering; the self-reported hyperarousal–value sensitivity association was significant within a bounded TAS-20 range (45.31–66.08), suggesting that intermediate alexithymia constitutes a zone of maximal vulnerability, though this model only reached trend significance and should be treated as exploratory. No effects emerged for loss aversion. Conclusion These findings indicate that sustained hyperarousal could selectively degrade evaluative precision and decision consistency, while leaving loss aversion intact. Alexithymia may operate as a stage-specific, conditional moderator of the body–decision relationship.

titre: Organizing Benzodiazepine Withdrawal-Related Symptoms: A Provisional Ontology and Severity-Allocation Analysis
resume: Abstract Background. Benzodiazepine withdrawal can involve many symptoms across different body systems. Existing symptom lists and rating scales help identify and measure these symptoms, but they do not show how the full symptom vocabulary fits together. We organized a community-compiled withdrawal-symptom list into a provisional, phenomenology-first ontology and then examined where patient-reported severity concentrated within that framework. Methods. We analyzed cross-sectional intake data from 39 adults presenting to a specialty benzodiazepine taper practice (37 presenting for taper care; 2 symptomatic after completing a taper). In Analysis A, 243 original symptom phrases from a publicly available benzodiazepine withdrawal-symptom list were decomposed into 278 analyzable rows and organized into 171 provisional symptom nodes. Each node was mapped by the author to one or more of 17 regulatory systems using a written codebook. In Analysis B, this frozen map was applied to patients’ 0–10 ratings on a 233-item questionnaire using severity-conserving fractional attribution, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Robustness was examined using alternative analytic choices and a separate blinded AI coding pass. Results. The highest-rated individual symptoms were anxiety (mean 7.3/10), insomnia (6.5), hypersensitivity to stress (5.5), nervousness (5.4), loss of confidence (5.4), and depression (5.2). Under the author’s coding, 157 of 171 symptom nodes (91.8%) mapped to two or more regulatory systems. The largest allocated severity shares mapped to interoceptive regulation (14.3%), state-level regulation (13.5%), cognitive control (10.2%), and threat-arousal regulation (10.0%). When severity was summarized as the mean rating of questionnaire items contributing to each system, cognitive control ranked highest (3.23/10), followed by affective/reward regulation (3.09/10) and threat-arousal regulation (2.79/10). Across robustness checks, interoceptive regulation, cognitive control, and threat-arousal regulation consistently ranked in the top five, and affective/reward regulation ranked in the top six. Two features were coding-dependent: under the blinded AI coding pass, 70 of 171 nodes (40.9%) were multi-system, and state-level regulation fell from second to twelfth, while affective/reward regulation rose to first. Conclusions. This study organized a broad vocabulary of benzodiazepine withdrawal-related symptoms into 171 provisional symptom nodes mapped to 17 regulatory systems, providing a structured approach to understanding complex symptom experiences. Applying this framework to patient-reported severity ratings identified interoceptive regulation, cognitive control, and threat-arousal regulation as consistently prominent across alternative analyses, with affective/reward regulation also prominent. Although some findings varied with coding decisions, the framework provides a transparent, auditable approach to organizing symptoms and examining their severity across overlapping regulatory systems. Further research may help refine the framework and assess its applicability to other clinical populations.

titre: Can Digital Mental Health Support Meet the Needs of Autistic People? A Systematic Review
resume: Autistic people experience high rates of mental health conditions and barriers to accessing supports. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) may be one way to improve access, but their applicability is unclear. We reviewed DMHIs that focus on mental health outcomes in autistic people, examining their scope, adaptation, community involvement and evidence of effectiveness.Five databases were searched in 08/2024 and 04/2026. Eligible studies evaluated a DMHI and reported pre-post mental health outcomes in autistic people. Findings were synthesised narratively using SWiM guidelines. Thirty-three studies reported on 1,258 autistic participants across fifteen studies were randomised controlled trials and 17 uncontrolled designs. Although anxiety was the primary focus of DMHIs, effects of DMHIs on depression, specific phobia, obsessive-compulsive disorder and trauma were also explored. Comparative findings for anxiety were mixed, and the predominantly small and uncontrolled evidence base could not establish efficacy. Most interventions were CBT-based, community involvement in study or DMHI design was very limited. DMHIs could be a promising option to support the mental health of autistic people, but research is in preliminary stages. Future studies should focus on co-producing DMHIs and embedding these into adequately powered controlled studies that are inclusive for a broader range of participants.

titre: Adjunctive delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol during prolonged exposure therapy for PTSD: A randomized, double-blind feasibility pilot trial with mechanistic assessment of extinction recall
resume: Abstract Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a chronic and debilitating condition. Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) has been shown to influence fear extinction learning and recall, providing a mechanistic rationale for its use as an adjunct to exposure-based therapy. We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot feasibility trial evaluating low-dose oral THC administered during Prolonged Exposure (PE) therapy for PTSD. Twenty-three adults with PTSD completed massed PE delivered via telehealth and were randomized to receive either 7.5 mg oral dronabinol (THC) or placebo prior to PE sessions 3–6. Primary outcomes included clinician-rated PTSD severity assessed with the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and self-reported symptoms assessed with the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Mechanistic assessments examined extinction recall using behavioral, psychophysiological, and neuroimaging measures. Across both drug conditions, clinician-rated and self-reported PTSD symptoms decreased substantially, and improvements were maintained through 3-month follow-up, at which point 91% of participants no longer met diagnostic criteria for PTSD. Significant improvements were also observed for anxiety, depression, sleep quality, and dissociative symptoms. The study was not powered to detect between-group differences; however, descriptive contrasts yielded numerically lower PTSD severity and reduced persistence of dissociative symptoms among THC-treated participants. THC was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. During extinction recall, THC was associated with greater hippocampal differentiation between extinguished and unextinguished threat cues, whereas behavioral and psychophysiological measures did not differ between groups. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and tolerability of pairing low-dose THC with PE therapy and support evaluation in adequately powered randomized trials.

titre: Tannins' Role in Elevating Symptoms of Irritable Bowel Syndrome through Gut Health Improvement
resume: Tannins are a class of polyphenol compounds that have been studied to modulate symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and gut health regulation. This chapter defines the molecular processes underlying tannins' influence on the pathophysiology of IBS and on gut health. Tannins modulate gut microbiota composition by selectively promoting the proliferation of pathobionts, including Escherichia and Clostridium species, while concomitantly suppressing the growth of beneficial microorganisms, such as bifidobacteria and Lactobacillus. This tannininduced dysbiosis disrupts the homeostatic production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, which are essential for maintaining the integrity and function of the intestinal epithelial barrier. The resulting impairment of gut epithelial barrier function triggers a pro-inflammatory response, characterized by the upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and activation of immune cells, ultimately leading to gut inflammation and potentially contributing to the development of gastrointestinal disorders. Tannins modulate the expression of genes governing inflammation, secretion, and gut motility, inducing pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β) and downregulating the serotonin transporter (SERT). Activation of NF-κB, MAPK, and PI3K/Akt signalling pathways exacerbates IBS symptoms and gut inflammation. Elucidating these molecular mechanisms may inform novel therapeutic strategies for IBS management, targeting specific pathways, modulating gut microbiota, and tailoring personalized medications.

titre: Predictors of response to a multidisciplinary internet-delivered intervention for irritable bowel syndrome: an explorative secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
resume: Abstract Background Internet-delivered interventions for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) have proven effective, but predictors of treatment response remain unclear. Aim To explore baseline patient characteristics and treatment-related variables associated with clinically meaningful improvement in IBS symptoms and quality of life following a multidisciplinary internet-delivered intervention. Methods This exploratory secondary analysis used data from a RCT ( n = 350) comparing internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), FODMAP diet or their combination to patient education. Predictors were selected pragmatically based on clinical relevance and included demographic, clinical, psychological, dietary, and treatment-related variables related to outcomes. The primary outcome was defined as ≥ 50-point reduction on the IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS). In addition, two secondary outcomes were defined: 1) ≥ 30% reduction on the IBS-SSS and 2) ≥ 14-point increase on the Irritable Bowel Syndrome Quality of Life (IBS-QoL). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to explore the associations. Results More severe baseline IBS symptoms and higher baseline IBS-QoL were associated with increased odds of achieving ≥ 50-point reduction in IBS-SSS, whereas longer symptom duration and previous poor treatment effect of the FODMAP diet were associated with reduced odds of reduction. When treatment-related factors were added, adherence to patient education was associated with increased odds of reduction. For the secondary outcomes, the multivariable models including treatment‑related factors indicated that previous poor treatment effect of the FODMAP diet was associated with reduced odds of achieving a ≥ 30% reduction in IBS-SSS, whereas higher baseline IBS-QoL was associated with reduced odds of increased IBS-QoL. Across all outcomes, the explained variance of the models was low to modest. Conclusions No robust or consistent predictors of clinically meaningful improvement in IBS symptoms or quality of life were identified. Prior poor response to the FODMAP diet was associated with reduced odds of improvement across both responder definitions for IBS symptoms, suggesting that previous treatment experiences may be relevant to consider. Overall, these results highlight the limited utility of the assessed variables for forecasting individual treatment response and underscore the need for future research to identify more robust predictors and explore mechanisms of change in internet-delivered interventions for patients with IBS. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06117865. Registered 31.10.2023.

titre: A REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA E A TRIBUTAÇÃO DOS SERVIÇOS DE ADVOCACIA: IMPACTOS DA SUBSTITUIÇÃO DO ISS PELO IBS E DA INSTITUIÇÃO DA CBS
resume: A Reforma Tributária do consumo, inaugurada pela Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023 e regulamentada, em seus aspectos centrais, pelas Leis Complementares nº 214/2025 e nº 227/2026, altera profundamente a tributação de bens e serviços no Brasil. O presente artigo analisa os efeitos dessa transformação sobre os serviços de advocacia, com especial atenção à substituição gradual do Imposto Sobre Serviços de Qualquer Natureza (ISS) pelo Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e à instituição da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS). A pesquisa adota método dedutivo, abordagem qualitativa e procedimentos bibliográfico e documental. Parte-se do regime constitucional do ISS e das características econômicas da atividade advocatícia para examinar a estrutura do IVA dual brasileiro, a não cumulatividade, o princípio do destino, o período de transição e o tratamento diferenciado conferido aos serviços profissionais regulamentados. A Lei Complementar nº 214/2025 prevê redução de 30% das alíquotas do IBS e da CBS para serviços prestados por advogados, observadas as condições legais. A análise demonstra que a simples comparação entre a alíquota nominal do ISS e as futuras alíquotas do IBS/CBS é insuficiente para medir o impacto efetivo da reforma, pois devem ser considerados o regime tributário do prestador, o perfil dos tomadores, a possibilidade de apropriação de créditos, a estrutura de custos e as regras de transição. Conclui-se que a reforma tende a ampliar a neutralidade e a padronização da tributação do consumo, mas impõe desafios específicos à advocacia, especialmente para estruturas intensivas em mão de obra e com reduzida geração de créditos, exigindo planejamento, adaptação tecnológica e acompanhamento da regulamentação.

titre: Investigating factors causing defects in Industrialised Building System (IBS) implementation for the People's Housing Programme (PPR) in Parit Buntar, Perak
resume: Industrialised Building Systems (IBS), or prefabrication, involves off-site manufacturing of components for easy installation. However, IBS faces challenges in Malaysia due to inadequate risk management, resulting in common failures. This paper objectives are to identify the types of defects and to analyse the causes of defects in the IBS project at PPR Parit Buntar, Perak housing. Questionnaires from 80 residents were analysed, revealing roof leaks as the primary defect. Interestingly, residents expressed high satisfaction with the quality of the house space. The findings also indicated that natural phenomena were the main contributors to defects in PPR housing. To enhance long-term satisfaction, it is recommended for housing developers and contractors to prioritize higher-quality materials in IBS projects.
revue: Journal of Islamic Social Economics and Development

titre: A REGRA-MATRIZ DE INCIDÊNCIA DO IMPOSTO SOBRE BENS E SERVIÇOS (IBS) NA REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA DO CONSUMO: OS EFEITOS DO SPLIT PAYMENT SOBRE O CRITÉRIO TEMPORAL DO FATO GERADOR
resume: A Reforma Tributária do consumo, introduzida pela Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023, promove significativa reestruturação do sistema tributário brasileiro, destacando-se a criação do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e a adoção do split payment como mecanismo de segregação e recolhimento do tributo. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo analisa os reflexos do split payment sobre o critério temporal da regra-matriz de incidência do IBS, a fim de verificar se a sistemática interfere na configuração jurídica do fato gerador ou se constitui técnica de arrecadação juridicamente distinta da incidência. A pesquisa fundamenta-se na teoria da regra-matriz de incidência tributária, especialmente na construção doutrinária de Paulo de Barros Carvalho, bem como nos princípios da legalidade, tipicidade e segurança jurídica. Metodologicamente, adotou-se abordagem qualitativa, explicativa, bibliográfica e documental, com método predominantemente dedutivo. A análise demonstrou que a liquidação financeira possui relevância própria para a operacionalização do split payment, para a extinção dos débitos e para a dinâmica da não cumulatividade, mas não se confunde, no regime geral do IBS, com o momento juridicamente definido para a ocorrência do fato gerador. Conclui-se, portanto, que o split payment modifica significativamente a forma e o momento operacional do recolhimento, sem deslocar, por si só, o critério temporal da regra-matriz de incidência do imposto.
revue: Journal of Law and Sustainable Development

titre: SARS-CoV-2 and the Gut: From Viral Persistence to Post-Infectious Gut–Brain Disorders
resume: COVID-19 is a multisystem disease with important gastrointestinal (GI) involvement. Diarrhea, nausea or vomiting, reduced appetite, and abdominal pain are among the most frequently reported GI manifestations during acute infection, although their prevalence varies across populations, viral variants, disease severity, and study designs. The biological basis of intestinal involvement is supported by the expression of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) and host proteases required for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) entry into intestinal epithelial cells. Viral RNA and antigens have also been detected in intestinal tissues after respiratory clearance, indicating persistence of viral material in some individuals; these findings do not by themselves demonstrate replication-competent virus. Uncommon but potentially severe GI complications include acute mesenteric ischemia, ischemic colitis, gastrointestinal bleeding, ileus, intestinal perforation, and acute pancreatitis. Although COVID-19 is associated with worse outcomes in acute pancreatitis, direct viral causation remains uncertain. Persistent GI manifestations have also emerged as an important component of post-COVID disease. Studies using Rome criteria have identified new-onset disorders of gut–brain interaction, including irritable bowel syndrome, functional dyspepsia, functional diarrhea, and functional constipation. Candidate mechanisms include intestinal viral antigen persistence, epithelial barrier dysfunction, sustained immune activation, gut microbial dysbiosis, and altered tryptophan–serotonin signaling; most links remain associative rather than causally established. Altered microbial signaling may also contribute to mucosal inflammation and disturbances in gut–lung and gut–brain communication. Overall, current evidence supports GI involvement in both acute and post-acute COVID-19. Further studies integrating microbiome, metabolic, and immune profiling are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying post-COVID GI disorders and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

titre: Gut microbiota dysbiosis exacerbates radiation brain injury after FLASH whole-brain irradiation: insights from the microbiota-gut-brain axis
resume: The microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA)plays a critical role in neurological injury and repair, but its involvement in FLASH radiotherapy, a modality that minimizes radiotoxicity to normal tissues, remains unexplored. We found that FLASH irradiation alone injured the brain (neuronal necrosis, elevated TNF-α and IL-1β, oxidative stress) and disturbed the gut (colon shortening, colonic inflammation); however, the microbiota was remodeled, with increased diversity and expansion of Akkermansia and Muribaculum , and the serum metabolome was barely affected. In contrast, Antibiotics alone collapsed microbial diversity and reduced differential serum metabolites, yet the brain remained normal by all pathological, cytokine, oxidative and metabolic measures. When dysbiosis preceded FLASH irradiation, however, radiation brain injury was amplified and sustained: neuronal necrosis and edema extended into day 9, ZO-1 remained reduced, cerebral IL-1β and colonic TNF-α remained elevated, and early oxidative stress was aggravated. The serum metabolome was remodeled, with microbiota-driven bile-acid and kynurenine changes. Taken together, these findings indicate that gut dysbiosis exacerbates radiation brain injury after FLASH irradiation mainly by altering the composition of the blood reaching the brain, making the MGBA a candidate target for improving radiotherapy outcomes.

titre: Nutritional recommendations in gastroparesis
resume: Gastroparesis is characterized by delayed gastric emptying (in the absence of mechanical obstruction), nausea, vomiting, postprandial fullness, early satiety, abdominal pain, and, in severe cases, weight loss and dehydration. The prevalence of gastroparesis in the United States ranges from 24.2 to 267.7 per 100,000 people, creating a significant financial burden on healthcare. Aim of the review was to characterize the diet of patients with gastroparesis, to review recommendations for oral, enteral, and parenteral nutrition in gastroparesis to restore nutritional and hydration status. Material and methods . The search for sources was carried out in the peer-reviewed scientific literature databases eLIBRARY, PubMed/ MEDLINE, Google Scholar, CyberLeninka, from 1990 to 2025 using the keywords: gastroparesis, gastric emptying, diet, nutrition, enteral nutrition, bezoar. Results. Nutritional deficiency of patients with gastroparesis: on average 1.4 ± 1.0 meals per day, 64 % of patients have an energy value of the diet <60 % of estimated one, 30–86 % – a deficiency of carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins and minerals. Only 32 % of patients with gastroparesis were consulted by a nutritionist, 2 % of patients followed the proposed diet. Nutritional support for gastroparesis includes initial nutrition screening, nutritional assessment, individualized nutritional recommendations, hydration and nutrient correction. Patients with gastroparesis are recommended: in a sitting position to consume mainly liquid chopped food 4-8 times a day in small portions with low fat content (25-30 % of the total energy value of the diet), fiber (15 g / 1000 kcal), eat slowly (30 minutes), do not lie down immediately after eating, control weight, reduce excess weight, maintain oral hygiene, avoid caffeine, alcohol, tobacco, bezoar-forming products, wearing tight clothing, stress. Exclusive enteral or parenteral nutrition is required in 3.3 % of patients with complications of gastroparesis (sharp weight loss, severe vomiting). Conclusions. The diet for gastroparesis is deficient in energy value and nutrients. Individualized recommendations of a nutritionist are necessary to reduce the symptoms of gastroparesis, prevent complications, and improve the quality of life of patients. Modifications of oral nutrition are preferred, enteral or parenteral nutrition is used for complications of disease.

titre: Correlates of demoralization syndrome among patients with gastrointestinal tumors: A meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND Demoralization syndrome (DS) is a prevalent form of psychological distress among cancer patients, which adversely affects treatment adherence and quality of life.Correlates of DS among gastrointestinal (GI) cancer patients have yielded inconsistent findings across individual observational studies.AIM To synthesize observational evidence and identify psychosocial correlates associated with DS in patients with GI tumors via meta-analysis.METHODS We search for relevant literature on correlates of DS in GI patients in databases such as China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, China Biomedical Literature Database, Web of Science, PubMed, and EMBASE.The search period is from the establishment of the database to May 2026.Two researchers screened, evaluated, and collected data according to the literature inclusion and exclusion criteria.Meta-analysis was conducted using R (4.5.1) software. RESULTSThe pooled mean score was 35.01 [95% confidence interval (CI): 31.79-38.24]for the 24-item DS (10 studies, n = 1923) and 13.50 (95%CI: 8.89-18.11)for the 16-item DS-II (4 studies, n = 926).Social support factors showed a significant negative correlation with DS (summary r = -0.557,95%CI: -0.695 to -0.381;I 2 = 91.8%).Psychological resilience was also negatively associated (summary r = -0.722,95%CI: -0.938 to -0.103;I 2 = 96.8%).Among coping strategies, facing coping was negatively correlated with DS (summary r = -0.470,95%CI: -0.846 to -0.059;I 2 = 98.1%).Sensitivity analyses confirmed robust results for social support, psychological resilience and facing coping.No significant publication bias was detected. / 34CONCLUSION Social support and psychological resilience were associated with DS for GI cancer patients.These correlational findings may inform preliminary hypotheses for targeted psychological management.Nevertheless, findings should be interpreted with great caution given three key methodological constraints: All data are derived from Chinese cross-sectional studies, each correlational subgroup includes only 3-7 studies, and extreme heterogeneity is present for every pooled estimate.Causal evidence from longitudinal or interventional studies is required before clinical implementation.

titre: Artificial Cognitive Design: memory, time, interoception and continuity for long-lived AI agents
resume: We have automation bots that run for years with limited intelligence, and language models that solve hard problems but rarely last beyond a session. Between them is a gap that matters more each month as agents move from answering questions to doing jobs: agents that are intelligent and also last, working for months, acting on their own or controlling a physical body. Such an agent has to remember, understand time, sense its own condition, and remain itself. Today these are solved imperfectly, with patches. Upgrade the model underneath an AI agent and it may come back thinking and judging differently, with no established, thorough way to check, let alone ensure, continuity. I argue that these abilities should be deliberately designed, and I introduce artificial cognitive design (ACD): the design of cognition for artificial agents, starting from the goals they pursue and combining machine-native mechanisms with designs inspired by nature, human cognition above all, where nature does better. Intelligence is the foundation of this cognition, but the rest has to be designed. These abilities carry a responsibility. Agents that have memory, a sense of time, interoception and continuity, and that may even take part in their own design and growth, could come to be more than tools. ACD therefore considers ethics from the start, toward every intelligence, organic or machine.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Testing the Factor Structure and Psychometric Properties of the Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 Among a Sample of Individuals Diagnosed with Eating Disorders
resume: Abstract Alexithymia is implicated in eating disorder phenomenology. The Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 (TAS-20) is a commonly used measure of alexithymia, which has been used to investigate associations between alexithymia and eating disorders. However, the TAS-20 has never been validated among individuals across the eating disorder spectrum. The purpose of this study was to test the factor structure and psychometric properties of the TAS-20 in a sample of patients with eating disorders. Participants were 710 patients admitted to a partial hospitalization program for eating disorder treatment. Participants completed self-report instruments at admit and one-month into treatment. Analyses tested the three-factor structure of the TAS-20 using confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) and measurement invariance across eating disorder diagnosis. Next, analyses tested the psychometric properties (i.e., convergent validity, internal consistency and test-retest reliability) of this model. CFA determined that the original three-factor structure of the TAS-20 fit the data after removal of five items in the Externally Oriented Thinking factor. This structure was invariant across diagnoses. The TAS-20 showed strong test-retest reliability, good internal consistency (excluding Externally Oriented Thinking), and moderate convergent validity. This structure of the TAS-20 may be more appropriate to use in future clinical work and research among those with eating disorders.
revue: Journal of Psychopathology and Behavioral Assessment

titre: 脳のシステム工学・制御理論的観点から考察する精神病のメカニズム 第18報 その他の精神病治療法の検証/ An Examination of the Mechanisms of Psychosis from the Perspective of Brain Systems Engineering and Control Theory Report No. 18: An Evaluation of Other Treatments for Psychosis
resume: 【Abstract (English)】Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT/modified mECT), which has existed since before the widespread use of pharmacological treatments, is a therapeutic method that induces forced convulsive seizures by passing a physical electrical current through the brain. Essentially, it is a symptomatic treatment that utilises the ‘GABA-sedative response’—an excessive release of GABA triggered by the brain’s defensive reaction to extreme artificial stress (electric shock)—and is a dangerous approach that further accelerates the destruction and degeneration of frontal lobe synapses through the same mechanism as pharmacotherapy. On the other hand, whilst TMS (transcranial magnetic stimulation) is more readily accepted as it involves no physical invasiveness or severe stress, scientific evidence regarding its effects on neuroplasticity and synaptic regeneration remains scarce. Whilst counselling is one of the few effective methods that can contribute to the brain’s synaptic regeneration process, the current system in Japan contains a contradiction in that its use is premised on combination with drug therapy. Hypnotherapy, expensive molecular nutrition (supplement therapy) and traditional Chinese medicine also require a dispassionate evaluation, taking into account the scientific validity of their mechanisms and the risks of dependence and side effects. 【概要(日本語)】薬物治療が普及する以前から存在する電気けいれん療法(ECT/修正型mECT)は、脳に物理的電流を流して強制的なけいれん発作を誘発する治療法である。その本質は、極度の人為的ストレス(感電)に対する防御反応として脳が過剰分泌する「GABA・鎮静応答」を利用した対症療法であり、薬物治療と同一のメカニズムで前頭葉シナプスの破壊・変性をさらに加速させる危険なアプローチである。 一方、TMS(磁気刺激治療)は物理的侵襲や強いストレスを伴わない点で受容しやすいものの、神経可塑性やシナプス再生に対する科学的エビデンスは依然として乏しい。カウンセリングは脳のシナプス再生プロセスに寄与し得る数少ない有効な手段である一方、日本の現行制度では薬物治療との併用が前提となる矛盾を抱えている。催眠療法、高額な分子栄養学(サプリメント療法)、および漢方治療についても、メカニズムの科学的妥当性と依存・副作用のリスクを踏まえた冷静な評価が求められる。
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Mindfulness Based Intervention to Combat Stress, Anxiety and Depression among Elderly in Selected Community Area
resume: Mental health problems in older people and a significant cost to their quality of life. This is an emerging non-pharmacological approach to improve psychological wellbeing in this population, called Mindfulness Based Interventions (MBIs). The aim of the present study was to identify the effectiveness of a mindfulness-based program administered over an 8-week period aimed at the reduction of stress, anxiety and depression. Methods: The study used a randomized controlled repeated-measures study design which included 132 subjects. The participants were randomly assigned to both groups. The study group were offered the 8-week MBI for older adults. The program conducted for about 10 to 15 minutes per session. Psychological outcomes were measured using standardized instruments, including the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Geriatric Anxiety Scale (GAS-10) and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). Results: The study findings revealed a statistically significant reduction in depression, stress and anxiety in the study group compared to the control group following the intervention (p<0.001). The control group showed only slight changes, however. Conclusion: The findings emphasize the need to further integrate structured mindfulness programs in resource-limited, community-based and geriatric health care in order to improve mental health and promote healthy aging.

titre: Developing and implementing a web-based psychotherapy program to address anxiety and depression among patients receiving oncological and palliative care: An open-label, mixed-methods randomized controlled pilot trial (Preprint)
resume: BACKGROUND Cancer is a prevalent disease that commonly leads to comorbid mental health conditions that are often undertreated due to barriers to traditional psychotherapy. Online cognitive behavioural therapy (e-CBT) could be an effective way to reduce these barriers since it demonstrates efficacy in reducing depression and anxiety symptoms, but its effectiveness is understudied in oncological and palliative populations. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to develop a web-based psychotherapy clinic for individuals receiving oncological and palliative care to examine whether this program is an effective psychotherapy to address this population's needs. METHODS Sixty participants diagnosed with depressive disorder and/or anxiety disorder in the context of oncological and/or palliative care conditions were recruited in Kingston, Canada. Participants were randomly assigned to either 8 weeks of a Mindfulness-Enhanced e-CBT (MECBT) program plus treatment as usual (TAU; n=32) or TAU alone (n=28). Participants in the MECBT condition completed weekly pre-designed modules, homework, and were sent personalized feedback. Additionally, a survey was sent out to all MECBT participants to conduct a thematic analysis of their experiences with the program. RESULTS Both conditions demonstrated reductions in anxiety and depression symptoms over time, and a statistically significant difference in depression scores occurred when comparing treatments. Six main themes were identified during the thematic analysis. CONCLUSIONS Findings support the effectiveness of MECBT in reducing depression severity. Qualitative benefits included providing structure, flexibility, and accessibility. Constructive feedback included problems with time restraints, the need for continuity of care, technical challenges, and the need for human contact. titre: Digital interventions to reduce burnout, psychological distress and workload among nurses in acute care settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled studies (randomised trials, non-randomised controlled trials, controlled before-after studies and interrupted time series) evaluating digital interventions delivered to or used by nurses working in intensive care, emergency departments or inpatient wards. Interventions include psychological-support tools (mHealth, web-based, VR or chatbot programmes for mindfulness, CBT, resilience or stress management) and task-relief technologies (ambient AI or speech-recognition documentation, EHR optimisation, virtual nursing, tele-ICU, AI workload or monitoring tools). Primary outcomes: burnout and psychological distress (stress, anxiety). Secondary outcomes: workload and documentation time, job satisfaction, retention (intention to leave or stay, turnover), resilience and unintended effects. Random-effects meta-analysis (Hedges' g, REML, Hartung-Knapp), subgroup analyses by setting and mechanism (psychological support vs task relief), RoB 2, ROBINS-I and GRADE. Status at registration (disclosed for transparency): the review is underway. Searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were run on 5 November 2026, and AI-assisted (Claude, Anthropic) pre-screening and provisional data extraction from open-access full texts have begun. Formal dual independent human screening, verification of extracted data, risk-of-bias assessment and final analyses have not yet been completed. This registration supersedes an earlier unregistered narrative review by the same lead author.

titre: Theological Dimensions of Mental Health Treatment: Integrating Hospital Chaplaincy into Interdisciplinary Models of Care for Religious Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
resume: Abstract Purpose of Review Religious obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), also known as religiosity or scrupulosity, presents unique clinical and ethical challenges due to the presence of obsessive-compulsive symptoms that are entangled with sincerely held religious beliefs. Hospital chaplains can play a vital role in an interdisciplinary care framework that supports evidence-based OCD treatment while respecting religious beliefs and identity. Thus, this review examines the role of hospital chaplains in the provision of evidence-based OCD treatment and proposes formalized models of collaborative care. Recent Findings The current literature emphasizes the value of collaboration between hospital chaplains and mental health clinicians in delivering comprehensive mental health care to individuals with religious OCD. Structured interdisciplinary approaches may aid in the shared understanding of OCD psychopathology within the context of religiosity and help ensure values-driven living. Summary This paper argues for formalized collaboration between hospital chaplains and mental health clinicians as part of comprehensive, evidence-based treatment for religious OCD. It also proposes structured models of partnership to promote the preservation of sincerely held religious beliefs and improved treatment outcomes.

titre: Physical Exercise in Alzheimer's Disease: Impact on Functional Biomarkers and the Muscle-Gut-Brain Axis
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and involves systemic alterations beyond the brain, such as loss of muscle strength, chronic low-grade inflammation, and gut microbiome dysbiosis. Physical exercise is a promising non-pharmacological therapy, and velocity-based resistance training has proven safe and effective in older adults. However, the effects of performing resistance exercises at high versus moderate velocity in people with AD remain unknown, and human evidence on how exercise modulates the gut microbiome in AD is very limited. This study aims to assess and compare the effects of two velocity-based resistance training modalities (high load at moderate velocity and moderate load at high velocity) versus usual care on the gut microbiome, systemic inflammation, plasma biomarkers, biological age, and intrinsic capacity in older adults with mild-to-moderate AD, using cognitively healthy older adults as a reference group.

titre: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Effectiveness of Expressive Arts Therapy in the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether expressive arts therapy works to treat major depressive disorder in adults. It will also learn about the safety and feasibility of expressive arts therapy. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Can expressive arts therapy reduce depressive symptoms in participants with major depressive disorder? * Can expressive arts therapy reduce alexithymia in participants with major depressive disorder? * Can expressive arts therapy increase participants' positive psychological capital? Researchers will compare expressive arts therapy with a control condition (such as usual care or a waitlist control) to see whether expressive arts therapy works to treat major depressive disorder. Participants will: * Receive expressive arts therapy sessions two or three times per week for 4 weeks, or receive the control condition * Visit the clinic at scheduled intervals for checkups and assessments * Complete questionnaires about depressive symptoms, alexithymia, and positive psychological capital * Keep a diary of their mood and therapy-related experiences

titre: [Management of chronic constipation in primary care]
resume: Chronic constipation is a common reason for consultation in primary care. After excluding red flags and secondary causes, three main clinical situations should be distinguished: functional constipation, irritable bowel syndrome with constipation, and defecatory disorders. These conditions differ in their pathophysiological mechanisms and require appropriate management. Management is based on a stepwise approach combining lifestyle and dietary measures, targeted pharmacological therapy, pelvic floor rehabilitation for defecatory disorders and, more rarely, surgery.

titre: Multi-matrix metabolome and microbiome profiling in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome and ulcerative colitis in remission with IBS-like symptoms
resume: BACKGROUND: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)-like symptoms frequently persist in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) in remission. Whether UC in remission with IBS-like symptoms (UCR-IBS) represents functional overlap with diarrhea-predominant IBS (IBS-D) or a distinct metabolic phenotype remains unclear. METHODS: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, 39 patients with IBS-D, 21 with UCR-IBS, and 35 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum, urine, fecal, and colonic mucosal samples were collected. Untargeted metabolomics, targeted tryptophan profiling, fecal 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing, predicted microbial functional profiling, and microbe-metabolite association analyses were performed. RESULTS: Tryptophan-related metabolism was altered in both patient groups, but the patterns differed across biological matrices. Compared with IBS-D, UCR-IBS showed higher serum N-formylkynurenine (NFK) concentrations, and fecal findings suggested reduced concentrations of microbiota-associated indole metabolites. Microbiome differences were modest, but predicted nicotinate/nicotinamide metabolism was enriched in UCR-IBS. Exploratory network analysis identified associations between tryptophan-related metabolites and selected bacterial genera in each group. CONCLUSIONS: Multi-matrix profiling shows tryptophan-related metabolic differences between mesalazine-treated UCR-IBS and IBS-D, highlighting higher serum NFK concentrations in UCR-IBS. These findings provide a basis for investigating host-microbiota metabolic relationships across systemic and intestinal compartments during UC remission.This trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR; https://www.chictr.org.cn/) under registration number ChiCTR2200060224.

titre: When Will Constipation No Longer Be Idiopathic? A Review of Primary Constipation Pathogenesis, Diagnostics, and Emerging Treatments
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Chronic primary constipation is common and burdensome yet is often labeled idiopathic despite growing evidence of physiologic heterogeneity. This invited, clinically oriented review examines emerging mechanisms underlying chronic constipation and their implications for phenotyping, diagnosis, and treatment. RECENT FINDINGS: Microbial composition, methanogenesis, enteric serotonergic signaling, neuromuscular function, gut-brain interactions, and sex-related biological factors may contribute to distinct constipation phenotypes, although most associations lack validated biomarkers. Clinically, careful phenotyping remains essential, including exclusion of secondary causes, digital rectal examination, anorectal manometry with balloon expulsion testing, and, in a minority of patients, transit testing or defecography. Emerging diagnostic approaches, including artificial intelligence applied to anorectal testing and location-aware ingestible devices, may improve classification, but require prospective multicenter validation and demonstration of clinical benefit. Therapeutic options are also expanding: tenapanor is modestly effective for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation, vibrating capsules are authorized for chronic idiopathic constipation, and elobixibat provides proof of concept for ileal bile acid transport inhibition as a therapeutic target. Chronic primary constipation encompasses heterogeneous mechanisms that are incompletely captured by current diagnostics. Advances in physiologic phenotyping, novel diagnostic technologies, and mechanism-based therapies may enable more individualized management. Future progress will depend on phenotype-enriched trials that link reproducible mechanisms with actionable diagnostics and targeted therapy.

titre: The Gut Microbiota-Associated Metabolite Network in Ischemic Stroke: From Pathophysiological Imbalance to Potential Precision Intervention Strategies
resume: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a leading cause of death and long-term neurological disability worldwide, and current treatment options are constrained by narrow therapeutic windows and limited neuroprotective efficacy. Accumulating evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) in the development and progression of IS. Following cerebral ischemia, bidirectional communication between the brain and gut is disrupted, resulting in gut microbial dysbiosis, impaired intestinal barrier function, and altered production of microbiota-associated metabolites that influence neuroinflammation, immune regulation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Among these molecules, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), bile acids (BAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) have attracted particular attention. Importantly, these molecules differ in origin: SCFAs and several tryptophan-derived indoles are direct microbial products; TMAO is a host-microbial co-metabolite; primary BAs are host-derived and subsequently modified by gut bacteria; and LPS is a bacterial structural component. Rather than acting in isolation, these metabolites form an interconnected network characterized by synergistic, antagonistic, compensatory, and feedback interactions; however, only a subset of these interactions has been directly demonstrated in patients with IS or in experimental stroke models, and many remain inferred from studies in other cardiovascular, metabolic, or inflammatory conditions. At present, the strongest human evidence concerns associations of individual metabolites with stroke risk and outcomes, whereas the proposed network-level interactions remain largely inferential. This review therefore proposes "gut microbiota-associated metabolite network imbalance" as a conceptual, integrative, and hypothesis-generating framework for understanding IS pathophysiology, and summarizes current evidence on protective and injurious metabolite pathways, their crosstalk, and emerging therapeutic strategies. Metabolite-guided precision intervention remains largely investigational and will require prospective validation before clinical translation.

titre: Starch-chitosan composite particle-stabilized Pickering emulsions for oral celastrol delivery and gut-brain axis-mediated neuroinflammation therapy
resume: Celastrol (Cel) is a potent natural anti-inflammatory agent whose clinical utility is severely limited by its poor aqueous solubility and negligible oral bioavailability. Herein, we report a surfactant-free oil-in-water Pickering emulsion (C-PE/Cel) stabilized by composite particles of acid-hydrolyzed corn starch and chitosan for oral Cel delivery and gut-brain axis-mediated neuroinflammatory therapy. Controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis for 6 days was used to tune starch surface amphiphilicity for effective interfacial anchoring, while electrostatic chitosan coating at 1.0 wt% reversed the particle zeta potential from negative to positive, thereby enhancing intestinal retention. C-PE/Cel exhibited high encapsulation efficiency and good colloidal stability at 25 °C for at least 55 days when prepared at an optimized water-to-oil ratio of 3:1. In vitro, C-PE/Cel demonstrated enhanced cellular uptake by Caco-2 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cell monolayers and superior suppression of lipopolysaccharide-induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in the RAW 264.7 mouse monocyte-macrophage cell line. In a chronic LPS-induced murine neuroinflammation model, oral administration of C-PE/Cel restored intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating zonula occludens-1 protein expression and reshaping the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial taxa (e.g., Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter) while reducing potentially pathogenic Ruminococcaceae. Furthermore, integrated 16S ribosomal ribonucleic acid and brain transcriptomic analyses revealed that the therapeutic effects were mediated via the gut-brain axis, involving the downregulation of immunoglobulin-related genes and the upregulation of fatty acid β-oxidation markers. This study established a simple, green, polysaccharide-based Pickering emulsion platform for the oral delivery of hydrophobic therapeutics targeting central nervous system disorders.

fiche.titre_court: Émulsion orale et axe intestin-cerveau
fiche.conclusion_simple: Des pistes précliniques intéressantes sur le lien entre microbiote intestinal et neuroinflammation.

titre: Probiotics for Human Health: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Risks, and Next-Generation Microbial Therapeutics
resume: Probiotics are widely used live microbial supplements intended to promote human health, yet their clinical benefits remain inconsistent and often strain-specific. Most currently available probiotics are derived from Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Saccharomyces species originally isolated from fermented foods or human microbiota. Preclinical studies suggest that these organisms may influence host physiology through several mechanisms, including antimicrobial activity, toxin inhibition, strengthening of intestinal barrier function, modulation of immune responses, and signaling along the gut-brain axis. However, translation of these mechanisms into consistent clinical benefit has been limited by heterogeneity in probiotic strains, dosing, and study design. Emerging evidence also highlights potential unintended consequences of probiotic use, including rare infections in vulnerable patients, alterations of microbiome recovery after antibiotics, and possible interactions with host metabolism or medications. Recent advances in microbiome research have supported the development of next-generation probiotics and engineered microbial therapeutics, representing a shift toward more targeted and mechanistically informed live microbial therapies.

fiche.verdict: Revue sur les probiotiques : bénéfices cliniques incertains, hétérogénéité des souches, et axe intestin-cerveau suggéré par des études précliniques.
resultats_cles: Mécanismes précliniques : immunité, barrière intestinale, axe intestin-cerveau.
Bienfaits cliniques limités par l'hétérogénéité des souches et dosages.
Risques potentiels : infections rares, interaction avec le microbiote.
fiche.conclusion: Les probiotiques offrent un potentiel via l'axe intestin-cerveau, mais nécessitent des thérapies plus ciblées et validées.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Utile pour comprendre l'axe intestin-cerveau et les limites des probiotiques en gastro.
fiche.titre_court: Probiotiques et santé humaine
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les probiotiques influencent l'axe intestin-cerveau chez l'animal, mais leur usage clinique reste hétérogène et nécessite prudence.

titre: Modulation of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis by the FGF-FGFR axis: therapeutic implications and translational perspectives
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the neurodegenerative disease characterised by deposition of senile amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques. It is a progressive disease which results in cognitive impairment and memory loss. There is no promising cure available so far for this disease due to its complex pathogenesis. The complex pathogenesis of AD involves multiple interconnected mechanisms, including Aβ plaque accumulation, tau protein hyperphosphorylation leading to neurofibrillary tangle formation, and damage to cholinergic synapses that impair neurotransmission. Additionally, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, metal ion dyshomeostasis, glutamatergic excitotoxicity, disrupted autophagy processes, and alterations in the gut-brain axis contribute to disease progression. Emerging evidence highlights the potential role of Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) and their receptors (FGFRs) in neurodegenerative diseases. FGF-FGFR system is crucial for cellular proliferation, differentiation, migration, and survival. The FGF-FGFR system system plays significant roles in various biological processes such as wound healing, angiogenesis, tissue regeneration, and embryonic development. Numerous FGFs and FGFRs are expressed in the central nervous system, where they are believed to exert neuroprotective and neurotrophic effects. Emerging evidence suggests that modulating this pathway could offer therapeutic benefits in neurodegenerative diseases, including AD, by intervening in multiple pathogenic cascades. This review emphasizes the significance of the FGF-FGFR system in AD, exploring their roles in disease pathogenesis, the development of novel drug delivery routes, and advanced delivery systems for FGF-based therapeutics.

fiche.verdict: Cette revue analyse le rôle de l'axe FGF-FGFR dans la pathogenèse de la maladie d'Alzheimer et ses implications thérapeutiques potentielles.
resultats_cles: Implication de l'axe FGF-FGFR dans les cascades neurodégénératives et la neuroprotection.
Pistes thérapeutiques ciblant les récepteurs FGF pour la maladie d'Alzheimer.
fiche.conclusion: La modulation de la voie FGF-FGFR offre des perspectives thérapeutiques intéressantes dans les maladies neurodégénératives.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Hors champ clinique (maladie d'Alzheimer, biologie moléculaire).
fiche.titre_court: Axe FGF-FGFR et maladie d'Alzheimer
fiche.conclusion_simple: Revue moléculaire hors champ de la psychogastroentérologie.

titre: Advances in plant polysaccharide research for neurodegenerative diseases therapy
resume: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), Huntington's disease (HD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and multiple sclerosis (MS), represent a growing global public health burden with limited therapeutic options. Plant polysaccharides are natural, biocompatible, and multi-target bioactive macromolecules that have emerged as promising candidates for ND intervention. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in elucidating the structural characteristics, structure-activity relationships, and neuroprotective mechanisms of plant polysaccharides. Key structural features such as molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, glycosidic bond configuration, and spatial conformation critically modulate the biological activity of these molecules. Furthermore, we summarize the numerous protective effects of plant polysaccharides against NDs, including inhibiting abnormal protein aggregation, alleviating oxidative stress via the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway, suppressing neuroinflammation through the NF-κB and MAPK signaling pathways, regulating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the gut-brain axis. Clinical translation challenges, primarily blood-brain barrier penetration, structural heterogeneity, and insufficient clinical validation, are discussed. Future directions include developing advanced delivery systems, conducting large-scale randomized controlled trials, and exploring synergistic combination therapies. Collectively, plant polysaccharides show considerable promise as potential multi-target candidates for the intervention of NDs, although further studies are needed to clarify their therapeutic potential and facilitate clinical translation.

fiche.verdict: Revue sur les polysaccharides végétaux comme agents neuroprotecteurs agissant notamment via l'axe intestin-cerveau dans les maladies neurodégénératives.
resultats_cles: Effets neuroprotecteurs multiples (oxydation, neuroinflammation).
Modulation de l'axe intestin-cerveau identifiée.
Défis de translation clinique (barrière hémato-encéphalique, hétérogénéité).
fiche.conclusion: Les polysaccharides végétaux montrent du potentiel contre les maladies neurodégénératives, mais des essais cliniques robustes manquent.
limites: Absence d'essais cliniques à grande échelle
fiche.pertinence_raison: Trop éloigné de la pratique clinique en psychogastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Polysaccharides et neuroprotection
fiche.conclusion_simple: Ces molécules végétales modulent l'axe intestin-cerveau et l'inflammation, mais leur application clinique reste préclinique.

titre: Effects of Probiotics on Migraine in Children and Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Increasing evidence highlights a link between migraine, a disabling neurological disorder, and the gut microbiome. Probiotics, supplements containing colony-forming units of beneficial microbes, may influence migraine via the gut microbiome. A systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials was completed, and findings were synthesized narratively to evaluate probiotics for migraine prevention. RECENT FINDINGS: Of 676 studies screened, 7 were included involving 612 participants (N = 487 females, 79.6%) consisting of 5 adult and 2 pediatric trials. Probiotics demonstrated a reduction in migraine severity on a 10-point scale (mean difference - 1.11; 95% CI - 2.26 to 0.03), monthly attack frequency (- 2.06; 95% CI - 3.6 to - 0.52), and disability (standardized mean difference - 0.86; 95% CI - 2.33 to 0.6). Certainty of evidence was graded very low. Probiotics may reduce migraine severity and frequency; however, the heterogeneity of studies limits generalizability. Despite the very low certainty of evidence, probiotics are safe and may reduce migraine as an adjunct preventative therapy.

fiche.verdict: Méta-analyse suggérant que les probiotiques réduisent la sévérité et la fréquence des migraines, malgré des preuves de très faible certitude.
fiche.population: 612 participants (79.6% femmes, 5 essais adultes, 2 pédiatriques)
fiche.intervention: Probiotiques vs placebo
resultats_cles: Réduction de la sévérité de la migraine (différence moyenne -1.11; IC 95% -2.26 à 0.03).
Réduction de la fréquence mensuelle (-2.06; IC 95% -3.6 à -0.52).
Certitude de la preuve jugée très faible.
fiche.conclusion: Les probiotiques sont sûrs et peuvent réduire la migraine en thérapie adjuvante, malgré l'hétérogénéité des études.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour l'axe intestin-cerveau et les comorbidités douloureuses fonctionnelles.
fiche.titre_court: Probiotiques et migraine
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les probiotiques pourraient réduire la fréquence des migraines, mais la certitude méthodologique reste très faible.

titre: Inulin Combined with Rosmarinic Acid Alleviates D-Galactose-Induced Cognitive Impairment by Regulating Indoxyl Sulfate and the AhR/NF-κB/NLRP3 Inflammatory Pathway
resume: Age-related cognitive impairment is associated with oxidative stress, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and gut-brain axis disruption. This study evaluated how rosmarinic acid (RA), alone or combined with the prebiotic inulin, ameliorates D-galactose-induced cognitive impairment in mice. Male ICR mice received D-galactose for 6 weeks with RA, or RA plus inulin, followed by behavioral testing, histology, biochemical assays, 16S rRNA sequencing, serum metabolomics, molecular dynamics and inflammatory signaling analyses. RA ameliorated exploratory behavior and recognition and spatial memory, restored antioxidant enzyme (SOD/CAT/GSH-Px) activities, reduced lipid peroxidation (MDA), and attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury and glial activation. The RA-inulin combination exhibited additional protection, improving colonic barrier markers, increasing Lactobacillus and Lachnospiraceae, lowering indoxyl sulfate, and modulating AhR/NF-κB/NLRP3 activation. Meanwhile, the level of IL-1β/IL-18 (in the hippocampus) decreased by 15.96% and 24.41%, respectively. These findings suggest that the combined dietary intervention of RA and inulin mitigates aging-related cognitive impairment through the gut-brain axis.
revue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

fiche.verdict: L'association d'inuline et d'acide rosmarinique atténue les troubles cognitifs liés à l'âge chez la souris via l'axe intestin-cerveau et la voie inflammatoire.

fiche.intervention: Acide rosmarinique seul ou combiné à l'inuline (prébiotique) sous induction de D-galactose

Restauration de la barrière colique et modulation du microbiote (augmentation de Lactobacillus)
Baisse de l'IL-1β (-15,96 %) et de l'IL-18 (-18 %) dans l'hippocampe

titre: Special issue of autonomic neuroscience: Basic and clinical on the concept of visceral Interoception in health and disease
The neural basis of flavour-nutrient learning
resume: Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour-nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour-nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

fiche.verdict: L'apprentissage des associations saveur-nutriments repose sur une voie dopaminergique spécifique reliant l'intestin à l'amygdale basolatérale.
fiche.population: Souris et sujets humains (données comparatives d'activation)
fiche.intervention: Stimulation de neurones dopaminergiques et analyse des signaux post-ingestifs
resultats_cles: Libération de dopamine sélective dans l'amygdale basolatérale (BLA) suite aux nutriments post-ingestifs
Les capteurs intestinaux activent les neurones dopaminergiques exprimant la cholécystokinine
L'intégration des signaux gustatifs et post-ingestifs dans l'amygdale est indispensable à l'apprentissage
fiche.conclusion: Ces résultats établissent la base neurale de l'apprentissage des propriétés nutritionnelles des aliments via l'axe intestino-cérébral.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Fondement neurobiologique précieux de l'intéroception et des apprentissages alimentaires.
fiche.titre_court: Base neurale de l'apprentissage saveur-nutriments
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'intestin communique avec l'amygdale cérébrale via la dopamine pour nous faire apprendre la valeur nutritive des aliments.

titre: Learning safety through the observation of others: A proof-of-principle study on vicarious extinction of fear responses to respiratory threat
resume: Interoceptive fear-conditioning paradigms model the development and treatment of disorders involving fear of somatic sensations. While direct extinction can attenuate acquired fear, associations involving interoceptive sensations may be particularly resistant. Vicarious extinction, where individuals observe a model's safety experience, mirrors techniques used in exposure therapy. This proof-of-principle study aimed to characterize conditioned fear responses to interoceptive threat during and following a vicarious extinction procedure. Twenty participants completed a three-day differential extero-interoceptive within-subjects paradigm. On day one, participants were presented with geometrical shapes serving as conditioned stimuli (CSs), with a CS+ paired with an inspiratory resistive load (unconditioned stimulus), and a CS- left unpaired. On day two, participants observed a model responding calmly to the CSs, without exhibiting signs of dyspnea. On day three, extinction retention was assessed. Startle eyeblink response, skin conductance response (SCR), heart period, and US-expectancy were assessed. Differential learning was evident in US-expectancy ratings, as indicated by higher ratings for the CS+ than the CS- by the end of the acquisition phase. In SCR however, evidence for acquisition was not fully conclusive, as CS-differentiation emerged only at the beginning of the vicarious extinction phase. CS-differentiation was absent in startle response, and bradycardia emerged to both stimuli. During vicarious extinction, SCR decreased, while US-expectancy ratings decreased but remained elevated for the CS+. Spontaneous recovery and reinstatement of differential fear responses were observed in US-expectancy, but not SCR. Our results indicate that vicarious extinction may attenuate the subjective expectancy of threat. Thereby, this study suggests the feasiblity of vicarious extinction of fear of interoceptive threat and offers a starting point for future research on observational safety learning in the domain of fear of bodily sensations.
revue: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

fiche.verdict: L'extinction vicariante réduit l'attente subjective de menace respiratoire, mais avec récupération spontanée.
fiche.population: 20 participants
fiche.intervention: Observation d'un modèle calme (extinction vicariante) après conditionnement intéroceptif (charge inspiratoire)

Persistance d'une attente élevée du SI et récupération spontanée/rétablissement à J3.
Absence de différenciation sur le réflexe de sursaut.
