titre: Vitamin D Insufficiency as a Nutritional Stress Amplifier: An Evidence-Weighted Framework for Adaptive Reserve under Exercise and Energy-Deficit Stress
resume: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble secosteroid whose biological activity depends on conversion of circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D into calcitriol, the active ligand of the vitamin D receptor. Although vitamin D has often been discussed as a potential ergogenic nutrient, evidence for direct performance-enhancing effects in athletes remains inconsistent. This review proposes that vitamin D insufficiency, used here as a context-dependent descriptive label for low circulating 25(OH)D rather than as a universal diagnostic category, may function as a nutritional stress amplifier that narrows adaptive reserve when mechanical, energetic, endocrine, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine stressors converge. The strongest evidence derives from the vitamin D-calcium-phosphate-PTH-FGF23 axis, through which calcitriol-VDR signaling supports mineral homeostasis, skeletal remodeling, and resilience to repetitive skeletal loading. Emerging evidence suggests intersections with skeletal muscle repair, myokine and osteokine signaling, inflammatory regulation, and tissue adaptation, although athlete-specific validation is needed. Low energy availability and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport provide a translational model in which low circulating 25(OH)D may become more relevant because multiple nutritional, endocrine, skeletal, and recovery stressors coexist. Brain-related pathways involving fatigue, sleep, HPA-axis-related recovery, BDNF, monoaminergic signaling, and interoceptive processing are retained only as hypothesis-generating domains, not as evidence that vitamin D status modifies cognition, mood, motivation, behavior, or central recovery mechanisms in athletes. Future studies should move beyond static 25-hydroxyvitamin D assessment and unstratified supplementation trials toward dynamic stress-recovery phenotyping. This framework positions low circulating 25(OH)D status as a testable conditional modifier of stress-recovery trajectories rather than an isolated determinant of athletic performance or a primary clinical target.

fiche.verdict: Cette revue propose un cadre conceptuel reliant l'insuffisance en vitamine D à un amplificateur de stress nutritionnel chez l'athlète.
resultats_cles: La vitamine D agit via l'axe minéral et osseux face au stress physique.
Les liens avec la récupération centrale et l'intéroception restent hypothétiques.
fiche.conclusion: Le statut bas en vitamine D module les trajectoires de stress-récupération sans être un déterminant isolé.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Mention de l'intéroception mais ciblant les athlètes et le stress métabolique.
fiche.titre_court: Vitamine D et stress adaptatif
fiche.conclusion_simple: Cadre théorique sur la vitamine D et le stress physique, peu transposable en clinique digestive.

titre: Lexical-Semantic Properties of Freely Generated Everyday Emotion Labels and Self-Reported Alexithymia: A Preregistered Secondary Analysis
resume: Alexithymia-difficulty identifying and describing one's feelings-is thought to involve emotion language, and reviews indicate the two are related; however, the relation varies with what aspect of language is measured. Whether the meanings of the emotion words people spontaneously use in daily life relate to alexithymic difficulties remains unclear. In an existing dataset, 50 adults freely generated words for their current feelings across roughly 14 days of ambulatory experience sampling and completed the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) before and after. Labels retained by a preregistered lexicon filter were assigned external norm ratings of how strongly a word's meaning is typically experienced through sensations inside the body, plus action-effector strength, and concreteness. A corpus-based index of association with independently defined interoceptive terms covered a subset. These are properties of words, supplied by independent norming samples and corpora, not measures of participants' own interoceptive ability. Values were averaged within participants, weighted by how often each label was used, and related to the TAS-20 difficulty-identifying-feelings and difficulty-describing-feelings subscales, adjusting for vocabulary quantity, valence, and arousal. All eight primary estimates were negative, but none survived correction for multiple testing. The clearest concerned difficulty describing feelings; participants reporting greater difficulty tended to repeatedly use labels with somewhat lower norm-rated interoceptive strength (standardized β ≈ -0.27). Confidence intervals spanned associations close to zero as well as those of potentially meaningful magnitude. The pattern changed substantially when each distinct word was counted once rather than weighted by frequency of use, including changes in direction for the interoceptive-strength estimates. In this small sample, the meanings of everyday emotion labels showed a suggestive but uncertain relation to self-reported difficulty describing feelings. The findings describe properties of the words people use-not their capacity to sense bodily signals-and show that such conclusions depend on how vocabulary is aggregated.

fiche.verdict: L'alexithymie (difficulté à décrire ses émotions) montre un lien incertain et faible avec l'usage de mots émotionnels moins corporels.
fiche.population: 50 adultes
fiche.intervention: Évaluation par EMA sur 14 jours (mots spontanés pour les sentiments) et échelles TAS-20.
resultats_cles: Corrégations négatives non significatives après correction pour tests multiples.
Tendance pour la difficulté à décrire les émotions (β ≈ -0.27) avec des mots moins intéroceptifs.
Résultats sensibles au mode d'agrégation du vocabulaire.
fiche.conclusion: Les significations des étiquettes émotionnelles quotidiennes ont une relation suggestive mais incertaine avec la difficulté déclarée à décrire ses émotions.
limites: Absence de significativité après correction statistique
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien alexithymie et intéroception verbale chez le patient psychosomatique.
fiche.titre_court: Mots émotionnels et alexithymie

titre: Therapist-supported versus self-guided digital CBT for chronic pain with neurodevelopmental traits: A pilot feasibility randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Chronic pain frequently co-occurs with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). If these traits are overlooked, standard cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may be less effective. We developed a brief digital CBT program that adds psychoeducation on NDD traits to standard CBT for chronic pain. This study primarily examined its feasibility in adults with chronic pain and comorbid NDDs. METHODS: In this three-arm pilot feasibility randomized controlled trial, 44 adults with chronic pain and a self-reported diagnosis of ASD or ADHD were randomized to therapist-supported digital CBT (n = 15), self-guided digital CBT (n = 16), or a sham condition (n = 13; daily submission of the weekday and weather). The program comprised ten 15-min videos over two weeks. Primary outcomes were feasibility and pain catastrophizing; depressive symptoms were exploratory. Mixed models for repeated measures were used. RESULTS: Post-intervention retention was 90.9% (40/44). Of 31 participants allocated to CBT, 29 (93.5%) completed the program, all rating it as safe. Compared with sham, pain catastrophizing decreased significantly more in both the self-guided and therapist-supported groups (p = .006 and p = .035), with no clear difference between the two CBT formats. Depressive symptoms showed a similar pattern. Other outcomes did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: A brief digital CBT program for this population appears feasible and acceptable. Preliminary estimates favored both CBT formats but were imprecise because the trial was not powered for between-group comparisons. An adequately powered trial with follow-up and systematic assessment of negative effects is needed.

fiche.verdict: Essai pilote montrant qu'une TCC numérique brève adaptée aux TND réduit la catastrophisation de la douleur chez les adultes avec douleur chronique.
fiche.population: 44 adultes avec douleur chronique et autisme ou TDAH
fiche.intervention: TCC numérique avec thérapeute (n=15) vs autoguidée (n=16) vs condition sham (n=13)
resultats_cles: Rétention post-intervention de 90.9%.
Baisse significative de la catastrophisation de la douleur (auto et thérapeute vs sham, p=.006 et p=.035).
Pas de différence claire entre les formats autoguidé et supervisé.
fiche.conclusion: La TCC numérique adaptée aux TND est faisable et réduit la catastrophisation de la douleur, nécessitant des essais plus puissants.
limites: Absence de puissance statistique pour comparer les formats
fiche.pertinence_raison: Très pertinent pour la gestion de la catastrophisation de la douleur et l'adaptation aux profils neuroatypiques.
fiche.titre_court: TCC numérique pour douleur chronique et TND
fiche.conclusion_simple: Une TCC numérique courte adaptée aux traits neurodéveloppementaux réduit la catastrophisation de la douleur de façon prometteuse mais préliminaire.

titre: Pilot trial of a brief tailored online treatment for rumination and worry in premenstrual dysphoric disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) affects up to 8% of menstruating individuals and involves severe cyclical mood disturbance. Accessible psychological interventions are needed. Repetitive Negative Thinking (RNT; rumination, worry) is implicated in PMDD severity and represents a novel treatment target. METHODS: This open, single-group pilot trial examined the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a brief, clinician-supported online CBT intervention targeting RNT in PMDD. N = 37 Australian women with elevated premenstrual distress (91.9% [n = 34] of whom had provisional PMDD) and elevated RNT received the 4-module program over 4-8 weeks. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-treatment, and 5-week follow-up (one menstrual cycle post-treatment). Primary outcomes were PMDD symptom severity and impact (PSST). Secondary outcomes included RNT, rumination, worry, depression, suicidality, anxiety, distress, wellbeing, and functioning. Satisfaction and qualitative feedback were collected post-treatment. RESULTS: Satisfaction was good (93% mostly-very satisfied), and participants reported improved understanding of PMDD and gaining practical skills to manage RNT and premenstrual symptoms. Two thirds (64.9%) completed the program. Linear mixed models showed significant, large improvements from baseline to post-treatment and follow-up in PMDD symptom severity and impact (ps < 0.001; g = 1.18-1.81), as well as RNT, rumination, worry, depression, anxiety, wellbeing, and functioning (ps < 0.05; g = 0.52-1.82). CONCLUSIONS: This pilot supports the preliminary feasibility, acceptability, and positive outcomes of a brief RNT-focused online CBT intervention for PMDD. Future research should examine how to improve completion rates, and evaluate the program in a randomised controlled trial with prospective symptom charting to confirm PMDD diagnoses.

fiche.verdict: Étude pilote ouverte montrant qu'une TCC en ligne ciblant les ruminations réduit les symptômes du trouble dysphorique prémenstruel (TDPM).
fiche.population: 37 femmes australiennes avec détresse prémenstruelle élevée (TDPM provisoire pour 91.9%)

resultats_cles: Taux de complétion de 64.9%, forte satisfaction (93%).
Amélioration large et significative des symptômes du TDPM (g = 1.18-1.81, p < 0.001).
Réduction des ruminations, de l'anxiété et de la dépression.
fiche.conclusion: L'intervention en ligne ciblant les ruminations est faisable et réduit les symptômes du TDPM, à confirmer par essai contrôlé.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour le ciblage des ruminations et de l'anxiété, applicables aux troubles fonctionnels.
fiche.titre_court: TCC en ligne pour ruminations et TDPM
fiche.conclusion_simple: Cibler les ruminations via une TCC en ligne réduit la détresse prémenstruelle, mais nécessite un essai contrôlé randomisé.

titre: Effectiveness of psychosocial and therapeutic interventions for children and adolescents with adverse childhood experiences: A systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) are important risk factors for a range of mental health conditions among children and adolescents. This meta-analysis examined the effectiveness of psychosocial and therapeutic interventions on anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and psychosocial functioning among children aged ≤18 years with documented ACE exposure. METHODS: We systematically searched randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between January 1, 2000 and September 17, 2026 that evaluated psychosocial and therapeutic interventions and reported relevant mental health outcomes among children and adolescents with documented ACE exposure. Searches were conducted in eight electronic databases (PubMed, MEDLINE [Ovid], Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost). Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Pooled effect sizes (Hedges' g) were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted by intervention modality, duration, setting, country income level, and reported ACE exposure characteristics. RESULTS: After duplicate removal, 6087 records were screened, and 21 RCTs involving 2450 children from nine countries were included. Eleven studies were found to have low risk of bias, and 10 had some concerns, with no studies assessed as high risk of bias. Meta-analysis of six RCTs showed that cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), trauma-focused and resilience-building interventions significantly reduced anxiety symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.46; 95% CI -0.86 to -0.06). Particularly, trauma-focused interventions demonstrated significant reductions in anxiety in subgroup analyses (Hedges' g = -0.90; 95% CI -1.66 to -0.14). Meta-analysis of four RCTs indicated that CBT and resilience-building interventions lasting ≥8 weeks significantly reduced depressive symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.26; 95% CI -0.44 to -0.07). No significant pooled or subgroup effects were observed for PTSD or broader psychosocial outcomes. CONCLUSION: CBT-based, trauma-focused and resilience building interventions effectively reduce anxiety and depressive symptoms among children with documented ACE exposure. Integrating evidence-based psychological interventions with trauma-informed principles may strengthen the delivery of mental health care for children and adolescents with documented ACE exposure and mental health needs.

titre: The effect of a seven-week online mindfulness intervention on the relationship between menstrual symptoms and mental health - A non-randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Menstrual symptoms are common among physically active women and may affect their well-being and performance. Moreover, symptom frequency has been associated with mental health in previous studies. Although mindfulness-based interventions (MBI) have shown beneficial effects on psychological and physiological health outcomes, their potential role in the relationship between menstrual and mental health remains unclear. Therefore, this study examined whether participation in an MBI was associated with changes in this relationship. METHODS: 39 physically active students were split into an experimental group (EG; n = 14; 22.68 ± 2.23 years) and a control group (CG; n = 25; 22.76 ± 4.88 years), which conducted a baseline and post-intervention measurement, including a psychometric screening. The CG received no intervention during the study and was offered access to the intervention materials afterwards. Assessed constructs included the 21-item version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale and the Menstrual Symptom index (MSi). The MBI was developed based on mindfulness-based stress reduction, incorporating the dimensions of acting with awareness, non-judgmental acceptance, and present-moment attention. RESULTS: At baseline in the control group, MSi scores were positively associated with anxiety (B = 0.16; p = .004) and depression (B = 0.14; p = .012). No significant group × time interactions were observed for depression or stress. For anxiety, the group × time interaction was significant at the grand-mean MSi score (B = - 3.30; 95% CI [- 6.50, - 0.11]; p = .043), whereas the three-way interaction was not significant (p = .054). CONCLUSION: The results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. Participation in the MBI was associated with changes in anxiety over time. However, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of MBI for anxiety in menstrual health context. Future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered as 'Impact of an online mindfulness intervention on sleep quality in physically active students' in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the identifier DRKS00038462 on 13 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

titre: From Toad Venom to Drug Development: The Clinical Pharmacology of Mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) in Treatment-Resistant Depression
resume: Treatment-resistant depression affects about one-third of patients with major depressive disorder and remains a major unmet need. Mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine; 5-MeO-DMT), the principal psychoactive constituent of Incilius alvarius parotoid secretion and of several Amazonian plants, is a pharmacologically atypical serotonergic psychedelic in clinical development for this indication. This narrative review analyses its clinical pharmacology, drawing on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov and grey literature through 15 August 2026, supplemented by regulatory and sponsor disclosures. Mebufotenin is a non-selective serotonin agonist with high affinity at 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1A (5-HT1A, Ki 3.0 nM) and markedly lower affinity at 5-HT2A, with reported selectivity spanning approximately 30-fold to 300-fold depending on whether the 5-HT2A receptor is agonist- or antagonist-labelled. Clearance is dominated by monoamine oxidase A; the cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6)-derived metabolite bufotenine has a receptor profile comparable to the parent compound rather than a distinct 5-HT2A-preferring one, and was below the limit of quantification in the only human study to measure it. In the pivotal phase 2b trial (GH001-TRD-201), inhaled GH001 produced a day 8 placebo-adjusted Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) reduction of - 15.5 points (p < 0.001; d = - 2.0) and day 8 remission in 23/40 (57.5%) versus 0/41 (0%) with placebo, with 20/23 (87.0%) day 8 remitters in remission at 6 months under as-needed retreatment and no serious treatment-related adverse events. Median psychoactive duration was 9.0-14.0 min across doses, and 97.5% of patients were discharge-ready within 1 h. GH001 has been studied without protocol-mandated psychotherapy, although this does not establish that psychological support is unnecessary. Evidence rests principally on a single randomised trial, and replication in larger, more diverse phase 3 studies with formal blinding-integrity assessment is required.

titre: MBCT improves working memory and sustained attention in generalized anxiety disorder: A randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is a promising intervention for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). Although GAD is associated with cognitive impairments, it remains unclear whether MBCT benefits cognitive functioning in clinical practice. This study examined outcomes of MBCT among adults with GAD in a routine clinical setting. METHODS: In this assessor blinded randomized trial, 140 adults with GAD received 8 weeks of group-based MBCT or structured psychoeducation alongside stable pharmacological treatment. Anxiety, mindfulness, working memory, sustained attention, and inhibitory control were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Linear mixed models tested intervention effects, and within-group regression analyses examined factors associated with cognitive improvement. RESULTS: GAD patients receiving MBCT showed greater reductions in clinician-rated and self-reported anxiety and greater improvements in mindfulness, sustained attention, and working memory than those receiving psychoeducation. No between group difference in change was found for inhibitory control. Within the MBCT group, lower baseline cognitive performance predicted greater gains. Reduced self-reported anxiety was associated with working memory and subsequent sustained attention gains. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the effectiveness of MBCT in reducing anxiety symptoms and increasing mindfulness in adults with GAD. MBCT also improved sustained attention and working memory without significantly affecting inhibitory control. Cognitive gains varied with baseline performance, self-reported anxiety reduction, and improvement in related cognitive domains. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400090284.

titre: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access
resume: PURPOSE: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer. METHODS: Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample. RESULTS: At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group. CONCLUSION: Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels. CLINICALTRIALS: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04480203.

titre: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Symptoms in Adults With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Associations With Symptom Dimensions
resume: OBJECTIVE: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) share overlapping cognitive and neurobiological features, yet data on ADHD symptomatology in adults with OCD remain limited. This study aimed to examine the association between ADHD symptom severity and OCD symptom dimensions in an adult OCD sample. METHODS: Ninety-four adults diagnosed with OCD according to Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition criteria were recruited from an outpatient psychiatry clinic. OCD severity and symptom dimensions were assessed using the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). ADHD symptom severity was evaluated with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), including inattention and hyperactivity subscales. Correlation and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to examine relationships between ADHD symptom dimensions and OCD severity. RESULTS: Higher ASRS total scores were significantly associated with greater Y-BOCS total scores (r=0.40, p<0.001). Inattention symptoms were more strongly associated with total obsession (β=0.37, p=0.008) and total compulsion scores (β=0.41, p=0.003) than hyperactivity symptoms. Regression models indicated that inattention, but not hyperactivity, independently predicted OCD symptom severity. ADHD symptom severity was negatively associated with global improvement scores. CONCLUSION: ADHD symptoms, particularly inattention, were associated with greater OCD symptom severity within this OCD sample. These findings suggest that ADHD symptoms, particularly inattention, may be relevant in understanding variability in OCD severity within clinical samples. Further studies are needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.

titre: Neurobehavioral correlates of changing one's mind in ADHD and OCD
resume: Cognitive flexibility is an executive function that allows individuals to adjust behavior in response to changing environmental demands. We assessed volitional switching under uncertainty, without rule-based learning, in the "Change Your Mind" task. Nineteen patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), 19 patients with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and matched control participants (20 per group) completed the task while undergoing a functional MRI scan. The task was a two-alternative forced choice paradigm where each stimulus was presented twice successively, with spurious feedback following the first presentation. This allowed participants the opportunity to repeat or change their response. Participants with ADHD changed their response more frequently than controls following a previously correct response, associated with reduced accuracy on the second trial. This was accompanied with smaller differences between change and repeat trials in the superior frontal gyrus, paracingulate gyrus, and frontal pole compared to controls. Participants with OCD did not differ from healthy controls in their performance but exhibited greater activity on both change and repeat trials in the pre- and postcentral gyri than controls. These results point to distinct neurobehavioral differences in patients with ADHD and OCD underlying what is often termed more broadly inflexible behavior.

titre: Deep brain stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder: Why phenotype matters
resume: The history of neurosurgical treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has closely followed evolving concepts of how psychiatric symptoms arise from dysfunctional brain circuits. Early psychosurgical procedures rested on the premise that pathological interactions between frontal cortical and subcortical regions could be disrupted by surgical lesions. With the development of stereotactic functional neurosurgery, procedures such as anterior capsulotomy allowed increasingly precise, anatomically defined interventions.
revue: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

titre: A proposed decision-making tool for addressing OCD and co-occurring PTSD within a MED-DBT framework
resume: Co-occurring obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) are common and clinically consequential among adults with eating disorders (EDs), yet clear guidance for treatment prioritization and sequencing remains limited. This brief report introduces a structured decision-making tool designed to support Stage-2 prioritization of OCD versus PTSD treatment within a multi-diagnostic ED-dialectical behavior therapy (MED-DBT) program. The tool integrates readiness criteria, diagnostic confirmation, and decision points to guide clinicians in treatment planning. We describe the feasibility of integrating and delivering this structured decision-making tool within a MED-DBT program, along with preliminary clinical trends from a pilot sample. More than half of program admissions during the study period flagged for probable OCD/PTSD, though only a small subgroup met Stage-2 readiness criteria, consistent with patterns in higher levels of care. Among patients receiving protocol-based exposure and response prevention or trauma treatment, early symptom trajectories were favorable across ED, OCD, PTSD, and impairment domains. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of structured prioritization within MED-DBT and highlight pathways for future evaluation.

titre: Does a moral injury framework enhance our understanding of OCD?
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by intrusive thoughts that are appraised as signalling harm, evoking distress and efforts to reduce distress and/or prevent harm. It has long been observed that obsessions often reflect moral themes and that many people with OCD experience strong moral emotions, particularly guilt and shame. AIMS: Drawing on social functionalist models of moral emotions and the literature on moral injury (MI), we propose that in some people with OCD, symptoms can be conceptualized as an MI. METHOD: We reviewed leading theoretical models of OCD, moral emotions, and MI, and identified areas of overlap in phenomenology, development, and persistence. RESULTS: When an obsessional thought is itself a moral transgression, and/or failure to resolve the obsessional concern via the compulsion is viewed as a moral transgression, it evokes moral emotions and threatens social standing, reputation, and trust. This increases the stake in avoiding the obsession and in ensuring the compulsion is done properly. CONCLUSIONS: The integration of moral injury concepts with established cognitive behavioral models may enhance case formulation, reduce treatment ambivalence, and support recovery processes that extend beyond symptom reduction to restoration of moral coherence and self-trust. Clinical implications are discussed.

titre: Fecal Incontinence in Patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Narrative Review
resume: Fecal incontinence (FI) is the recurrent and uncontrolled passage of fecal material, in-cluding episodes of soiling or underwear staining. Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut-brain interaction characterized by recurrent abdominal pain or dis-comfort associated with altered bowel habits, including diarrhea, constipation, or a mixed pattern. Although these conditions have traditionally been considered sepa-rately, increasing evidence suggests that they frequently overlap, especially in patients with diarrhea-predominant IBS. In this setting, FI should not be regarded as a simple consequence of anal sphincter weakness. Loose stools, urgency, altered colonic transit, rectal hypersensitivity, anorectal sensorimotor dysfunction, pelvic floor impairment, and reduced continence reserve may interact and promote leakage. Additional struc-tural, iatrogenic, and patient-related factors may further increase susceptibility. The overlap is often underrecognized because many patients do not spontaneously report fecal leakage, despite its relevant impact on quality of life and daily functioning. A careful history, direct but non-stigmatizing questioning, physical examination, symp-tom assessment, and selective investigations are therefore essential to identify the dominant clinical phenotype and exclude secondary causes. Treatment should be indi-vidualized and progressive, combining optimization of bowel habits and IBS-directed strategies with anorectal rehabilitation and, when needed, more advanced FI-directed treatments. Recognizing FI as part of the clinical spectrum of IBS may improve diag-nostic accuracy, promote earlier treatment, and support a more integrated and pa-tient-centered approach to care.

titre: Histopathological and virus-associated features of Boid Inclusion Body Disease in Boa constrictor
resume: Boid inclusion body disease (BIBD) is a reptarenavirus-induced fatal disease of boid snakes that, while diagnosed with ease due to the pathognomonic intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies (IB), is not yet fully characterized pathomorphologically and with regards to its pathogenesis. The present study retrospectively investigated a random cohort of 50 captive male and female boa constrictors of variable age (neonate to 25 years) for histopathological changes and in situ viral protein (nucleoprotein, NP, and glycoprotein 2, GP2) expression patterns. IB formation and NP expression were scored semiquantitatively. The vast majority of snakes (42/50; 84%) exhibited histopathological changes; these mainly (39/42; 93%) represented inflammatory processes that most frequently affected the gastrointestinal tract. Overall, IB and NP scores were significantly higher in the more recent cases (2020-2025) compared to the older cases (2000-2003). NP scores did not differ between age groups or sex, but were lower in animals with clinical signs and higher in those with histopathological changes. No statistically significant association was found between NP scores and inflammatory processes, neither in general nor in individual organs. GP2 expression, as an indicator of virion assembly, was less consistent than NP expression and generally restricted to individual cells with and without IBs. There was no histological evidence of overt damage in infected cells. Jointly, the results indicate different phases of restrictive and systemic viral replication that are not directly associated with pathological processes and/or clinical signs.

titre: Neural Activation of Human Primary Intestinal Enteroendocrine L-cells
resume: Intestinal enteroendocrine L-cells play a central role in metabolic homeostasis by secreting the gut hormones GLP-1 and PYY, but whether and how neural signals regulate human L-cell function remains poorly understood. This gap reflects the limited availability of human model systems enriched for mature L-cells. Here, we establish a differentiation strategy that generates human donor-derived ileal organoids with markedly increased L-cell abundance, enabling functional interrogation of L-cell physiology in their basal state. Using this system, we show that cholinergic and adrenergic stimuli activate L-cells, triggering calcium influx and secretion of GLP-1 and PYY. Pharmacological analysis reveals that cholinergic regulation of human L-cells is mediated predominantly through M3 muscarinic receptors, while adrenergic regulation is mediated through the β1 adrenergic receptor. Neurotransmitter-evoked activation also initiates gap junction–dependent calcium waves that propagate across the intestinal epithelium; however, disruption of epithelial coupling by abolishing calcium propagation does not impair hormone secretion. Together, these findings identify L-cells as integrative hubs that couple neural signals to gut hormone secretion and epithelial calcium waves, providing mechanistic insight into the gut-brain axis and how the nervous system regulates intestinal endocrine function in human intestine.

titre: Work disability in patients with newly diagnosed inflammatory bowel disease: Results from the population-based IBSEN III cohort
resume: Background This study aimed to compare the proportion of Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) patients receiving work disability (WD) benefits with the corresponding proportion in the background population at diagnosis and after 1 year, and to assess associations between selected variables and WD. Methods Adults from a population-based inception cohort with WD data at diagnosis and/or 1-year follow-up were included. WD was defined as receiving work assessment allowance (AAP) or disability pension (DP). Relative risks (RRs) for AAP and DP were calculated vs. national registry proportions stratified by age and sex, overall RRs were age standardized. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between WD and selected variables. Results At diagnosis, risk of AAP was increased for UC (RR, 1.5; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.1-2.1) and CD patients between 30-39 years old (RR, 2.8; 95% CI, 1.1-5.8). AAP risk was increased at 1-year for both UC (RR, 1.6; 95% CI, 1.1-2.4) and CD (RR, 3.6; 95% CI, 2.4-5.2). DP risk was comparable with the background population. Higher general self-efficacy and health-related quality of life were associated with lower odds of WD, whereas disease-activity variables were not. Older age, comorbidities, and lower education were also associated with increased odds of WD in UC. Conclusions After 1 year, patients with UC and CD had increased risk of AAP. Lower general self-efficacy and poorer health-related quality of life were associated with higher WD, suggesting a potential window for targeted interventions to reduce AAP and prevent or delay DP.

titre: Oral hormonal contraceptive use and gastrointestinal symptoms in young women: a cross-sectional study
resume: Background Gastrointestinal symptoms may affect contraceptive tolerability, yet domain-specific symptoms associated with oral contraceptive use remain insufficiently described. Objective To compare gastrointestinal, physical, and psychological symptoms among young adults using no birth control, a combined oral contraceptive (COC), or a progestin-only pill (POP). Methods Participants aged 18-25 years completed a cross-sectional online survey. The sample included 669 participants: 427 using no birth control, 196 using a COC, and 46 using a POP. Outcomes included five PROMIS gastrointestinal domains, a study-specific regional abdominal pain sum, eight Cohen-Hoberman Inventory of Physical Symptoms (CHIPS) domains, and anxiety, depressive symptoms, and health anxiety. Race/ethnicity and current sexual activity were included as additional fixed factors in primary models. Results The multivariate PROMIS effect of contraceptive group was not significant. Constipation was the only PROMIS domain meeting the Bonferroni-corrected criterion, with higher adjusted estimated marginal means among COC users than participants using no birth control. COC users also reported higher regional abdominal pain scores than POP users. The CHIPS multivariate effect was not significant, but gastrointestinal subscale scores were higher among COC users than participants using no birth control. Psychological outcomes showed a small multivariate group effect, but no individual outcome met the Bonferroni-corrected criterion. Conclusion Oral contraceptive use was associated with modest, domain-specific gastrointestinal differences rather than a broad gastrointestinal or physical symptom profile. Because the study was cross-sectional and residual confounding remains possible, findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.
revue: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception

titre: Laparoscopic reduction of strangulated small bowel incarceration by controlled enlargement of a uterine perforation following manual vacuum aspiration
resume: Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is widely used for early pregnancy loss, but uterine perforation may cause serious intra-abdominal complications. Bowel incarceration through a uterine perforation can be difficult to recognize because clinical manifestations may be nonspecific. A 37-year-old woman underwent MVA for missed miscarriage at 6 weeks of gestation. After unsuccessful repeat suction for presumed intrauterine hematoma, she developed abdominal pain and vomiting. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed small bowel herniation through a posterior uterine wall defect with reduced enhancement, suggesting strangulation. Emergency laparoscopy confirmed bowel incarceration. Controlled enlargement of the uterine defect enabled atraumatic bowel reduction; ischemic intestine was resected, and the uterus was repaired laparoscopically. This case demonstrates that bowel incarceration may present with mild findings despite ischemia and highlights the importance of prompt CT and avoidance of repeated intrauterine instrumentation when uterine perforation is suspected.

titre: Rethinking Low Anterior Resection Syndrome: Higher Than Expected Pre-Surgical Incidence and the Role of Gut Microbes
resume: Background Low anterior resection syndrome, characterized by a constellation of defecatory dysfunction symptoms, is a frequent complication after low anterior resection surgery. However, the mechanisms underlying low anterior resection syndrome, including potential associations with intestinal microbiota, remain poorly defined. Objective To characterize the onset and progression of low anterior resection syndrome across the rectal cancer treatment pathway and to examine microbial community shifts in relation to low anterior resection syndrome development. Design Prospective cohort study with a nested subgroup undergoing repeated clinical and microbial assessments. Setting St Paul's Hospital, Vancouver, Canada. Patients Rectal adenocarcinoma patients undergoing curative-intent resection with restoration of bowel continuity. Interventions Prospectively collected cohort without intervention. Main outcome measures The primary outcome was presence of low anterior resection syndrome (score ≥ 21). Secondary outcomes included microbial diversity and composition changes. Results Pretreatment bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome-score criteria was present in 42% (30/71) of patients, without significant association with demographic or clinical variables. By the end of follow-up, 64% exhibited low anterior resection syndrome. New-onset low anterior resection syndrome correlated with lower tumor height (p = 0.04). Microbial beta diversity differed between no pretreatment bowel dysfunction and pretreatment bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome criteria at baseline (p Limitations Single-center design with small sample size. Conclusions Bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome criteria is common before rectal cancer treatment and increased postoperatively. Although baseline microbial profiles differed, no association between bacterial diversity and low anterior resection syndrome development could be demonstrated. Routine pretreatment bowel dysfunction assessment may guide patient counseling and quality of life. See Video Abstract.
revue: Diseases of the colon and rectum

titre: Intestinal molecular siphoning by engineered bacterial spores for non-systemic treatment of nicotine addiction
resume: Eradicating toxic small molecules from the body typically requires the administrations of therapeutic agents for systemic circulation and tissue distribution, resulting in inevitable adverse events from off-target effects. Here, we propose a “intestinal molecular siphoning” approach for treating diseases caused by toxic substances, in which enzymatic degradation of a toxic substance in the intestinal lumen serves as a driving force for the diffusion of the toxic substance from blood to gut, and continuous elimination of the toxic substance in the gut could effectively ease substance dependence. Using nicotine as a model substance, a live bacterial system was constructed by displaying a trypsin-resistant nicotine oxidase on the surface of Bacillus subtilis spores, and encapsulating in enteric-coated microspheres for gastric protection and targeted intestinal release. After oral treatments with the live bacterial system in mice, peak concentrations of nicotine in blood and brain were remarkably reduced compared to controls. Moreover, the live bacterial system could effectively attenuate nicotine addiction by suppressing dopamine reward surges to reverse withdrawal hyperalgesia, preventing the upregulation of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, and alleviating anxiety-like behaviors. These findings show the potential of “intestinal molecular siphoning” as a target-independent therapeutic strategy for lowering circulating toxic substances through non-systemic enzyme reprogramming. Significance Statement Currently, blood and tissue exposures are a critical measure on the efficacy for conventional therapeutics, including small molecules, biologics or therapeutic cells. To avoid various off-target-associated adverse events from such exposures, bypassing bloodstream to exert systemic therapeutic effects is a prerequisite to achieve target-independent treatments. Here, we describe the feasibility of implementing “intestinal molecular siphoning” approach for degrading toxic molecules in the body. When nicotine oxidase is displayed on the surface of probiotic B. subtilis , oral administration of the engineered live bacterial system exhibits desired efficacy and safety for nicotine addiction in murine models. Beyond the treatment of nicotine addiction, this approach also provides a versatile platform for non-systemically reducing other toxic molecules in the circulations.

titre: Effects of menstrual cycle phase on interoception: A daily experience sampling study across two cycles
resume: Abstract Interoception – the processing of internal bodily signals – has been related to numerous aspects of mental and physical health. Sex differences have been reported in objective interoceptive accuracy and self-reported interoceptive attention, yet the factors underlying such differences remain poorly understood. One theory is that these differences arise from increased amount of physical and hormonal change females experience across the lifespan. The menstrual cycle provides a compelling test of this hypothesis and here we present the first investigation of interoception across the menstrual cycle. Twenty females completed daily interoceptive accuracy and attention assessments across two consecutive cycles, alongside matched exteroceptive control tasks (ISRCTN registration: 99520723). Cycle phases were determined using the counting method, with ovulation confirmed via cervical mucus ratings and basal body temperature. Interoceptive accuracy was higher during the periovulatory phase compared with the perimenstrual phase. Interoceptive attention was highest during the perimenstrual phase compared to all phases, though fully explained by physical symptom burden. Cycle-related changes were unique to interoception and emerged only within a complete menstrual cycle, highlighting the potential role of between-cycle hormonal variability. These data provide the first evidence that interoception varies across the menstrual cycle, with implications for sex differences in interoception and mental health.

titre: The effectiveness of Schema therapy on Alexithymia, Cognitive flexibility, Body image, and Food craving in individuals with type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial
resume: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder accompanied by alexithymia, cognitive inflexibility, body image disturbances, and food craving. Schema therapy targets maladaptive cognitive-emotional schemas and may improve these psychosocial factors. We assessed group schema therapy for alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, body image, and food craving in adults with T2DM. Fifty adults were randomized to eight weekly 90-minute sessions of schema therapy or diabetes self-management education (DSMES), matched for therapist contact and format. Self-report measures (TAS-20, CFI, BICI, FCQ-T) were administered pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using intention-to-treat with multiple imputation. ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores. Schema therapy produced significant improvements over DSMES in alexithymia (adjusted means 49.31 vs 60.09; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.352), body image (32.92 vs 39.21; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.258), and food craving (92.30 vs 106.85; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.340). Cognitive flexibility total improved (100.81vs 94.47; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.085), but the Control subscale did not (p = 0.128). All subscales of alexithymia, body image, and food craving improved. Group schema therapy may be a useful adjunct for selected psychosocial barriers in T2DM, but sample size, no follow-up, and self-report measures limit conclusions. Trial registration: IRCT20251201068177N1 (registered 31 December 2025).

titre: Opposing Manipulations of Insular Projections to the Bed Nuclei of the Stria Terminalis Converge on Behavioral Passivity
resume: Adaptive stress coping involves flexible coordination of behavioral and neuroendocrine responses, yet how cortical regions orchestrate these outputs remains poorly understood. The insular cortex (IC) integrates interoceptive signals and projects to extended amygdala nuclei implicated in threat responses, including the anteroventral subdivision of the bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) and central amygdala (CeA). Here we used pathway-specific chemogenetics to bidirectionally manipulate IC-avBST projections in male rats during the shock probe defensive burying test, which naturalistically measures active versus passive coping. Inhibition of avBST-projecting neurons resulted in a passive coping phenotype of increased immobility and elevated corticosterone levels. Excitation of these neurons unexpectedly shifted behavior in the same direction, reducing defensive burying without altering immobility or corticosterone responses. This convergence suggested that the effects might not be mediated by the avBST projection itself, prompting us to examine collateral targets. Anatomical tracing revealed that avBST-projecting IC neurons send dense collateral axons to CeA, and ex vivo recordings confirmed functional synaptic connectivity. Chemogenetic excitation of CeA-projecting IC neurons also reduced defensive burying, as did optogenetic stimulation of IC terminals in CeA but not avBST, implicating IC input to CeA. These findings suggest that reducing IC excitatory drive on avBST promotes behavioral and hormonal features of passive coping, consistent with avBST's established role in constraining stress responses. In contrast, excitatory influences operate through collateral CeA projections suppress active defensive behavior without engaging neuroendocrine output, indicating that a projection's collaterals, not its defining target, can determine its functional impact.
revue: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

titre: Engineered Micro- and Nanoscale Delivery Platforms for Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Microbiota–Mucosal Immune Interactions and Translational Evidence
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome is a disorder of gut–brain interaction characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. Interactions among intestinal microorganisms and their metabolites, the epithelial barrier, mucosal immunity, and gut–brain signaling provide important insights into the heterogeneity of this condition. Engineered micro- and nanoscale carriers may improve the stability of orally administered bioactive agents and facilitate local intestinal delivery while modulating relevant pathological processes through protection of viable microorganisms, delivery of microbial metabolites, or direct regulation of host cells. This review examines major mechanisms underlying microbiota–immune interactions and summarizes advances in colon-targeted delivery, protective carriers for probiotics, plant-derived vesicle-like preparations, and microalgae-based hybrid systems. We further discuss the biological characteristics of different clinical subtypes and key translational challenges, including safety, quality control, and rigorous verification of therapeutic efficacy. In particular, evidence from direct irritable bowel syndrome studies is distinguished from findings in symptom-based models, other disease models, and fundamental mechanistic experiments.

titre: Reliability and readability of five large language models in answering patient-oriented questions about irritable bowel syndrome: a comparative study
resume: Background Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common gastrointestinal disorder requiring long-term self-management. Patients therefore need accurate, transparent, and comprehensible health information. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health information seeking, yet the quality, transparency, and readability of their responses remain insufficiently evaluated. This study compared five publicly accessible LLM-based platforms to inform their use in patient education. Methods This web-based cross-sectional study retrieved Google Trends queries from the preceding 5 years using the English MeSH term “Irritable Bowel Syndrome” and the “Worldwide” geographic setting. After screening, 12 patient-oriented questions were submitted in English to ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, and DeepSeek under a standardized single-turn, zero-shot protocol. Each configuration generated one English-language response per question, yielding 60 responses. Two gastroenterologists independently evaluated responses using DISCERN, the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) instrument, Global Quality Score (GQS), and Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria. Information-quality scores were compared using question-blocked Friedman tests, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests when the omnibus result was significant. Readability was assessed using ARI, GFI, FKGL, CL, SMOG, and FRES, with a sixth-grade reading level as the reference. Results Question-blocked Friedman tests identified differences in DISCERN, EQIP, and JAMA scores (all permutation P < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant difference was detected in GQS scores (permutation P = 0.600). Copilot and Perplexity had the highest median DISCERN scores (48.00), while Copilot had the highest median EQIP score (80.00), significantly exceeding ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek in Bonferroni-adjusted paired comparisons. Despite relatively higher JAMA scores for Copilot and Perplexity, all configurations had median scores of only 0–1, indicating limited fulfillment of the assessed transparency-related criteria. All configurations had a median GQS of 4. Median ARI, GFI, FKGL, CL, and SMOG scores exceeded 6, and all median FRES scores were below 80. Gemini had the highest medians for all five grade-level indices; Copilot had the lowest medians for ARI, GFI, FKGL, and SMOG, while DeepSeek had the lowest median CL and the highest median FRES. No model met the predefined sixth-grade readability standard. Conclusion All five LLMs generated IBS-related health information with educational value, but differed in treatment-related information quality, content completeness, and source transparency. Within the sampled responses, Copilot and Perplexity performed relatively well on selected measures, although transparency remained limited. Across all configurations, median readability scores indicated estimated reading levels above the prespecified sixth-grade reference, suggesting potentially demanding text. LLMs should serve as professionally reviewed adjuncts to patient education rather than independent sources for diagnosis, treatment, or clinical decision-making.

titre: IBS BAG
resume: The IBS BAG includes teams from IBS (Grenoble) and external groups from CEA-Cadarache (St Paul lez Durance), CEA-Grenoble, CERMAV (Grenoble) et IRBA (Brétigny-sur-Orge). We study the structure-function relationships of proteins and biological macromolecular complexes with a focus on human health, biotechnology and methodology. Most of the projects are a continuation of the MX-2686 proposal and can be grouped under the following themes: host-pathogen interaction, new therapeutic targets, fundamental cellular mechanisms, membrane proteins, biotechnological applications and methodology. Some of these projects use integrative approaches (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, SAXS and NMR) together with other biophysical and biochemical studies and, more recently, the use of AI (e.g. AlphaFold, Chai-1) to fully understand the complexity of the biological systems under study.

titre: Effectiveness of acupressure foot mats in older adults with functional constipation: protocol for a randomized controlled trial
resume: Background Functional constipation (FC) is a prevalent gastrointestinal disorder among older adults, significantly impairing quality of life. While pharmacological treatments are common, they are often associated with adverse effects and poor long-term adherence. Acupressure is a non-pharmacological alternative, but manual application requires trained practitioners. Acupressure foot mats offer an accessible, self-administered home-based intervention with the potential to support adherence. Objective This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of acupressure foot mats for treating FC symptoms in older adults. Methods This randomized controlled trial will recruit 192 adults aged ≥60 years with functional constipation from community health centers. Following a 14-day baseline diary period, participants will be randomly allocated (1:1) to use either an acupressure foot mat or a flat, non-textured control mat for 30 min daily over 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up period. The primary endpoint is the mean change from baseline in the weekly frequency of complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs) at week 8. The key secondary endpoint is the week-8 CSBM responder rate, defined as achieving both ≥3 CSBMs per week and an increase of ≥1 CSBM per week from baseline. Other secondary outcomes include diary-recorded rescue medication use, stool consistency, straining intensity, and abdominal symptoms, together with constipation symptom severity and quality of life assessed at baseline and weeks 4, 8, and 12. Conclusion This protocol outlines a rigorous methodology to determine whether acupressure foot mats can serve as an effective, home-based management strategy for FC in older adults, empowering patients and potentially reducing reliance on laxatives. Clinical Trial Registration International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry ( http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/ ), identifier ITMCTR2026001799. Registered on 31 July 2026 (prospective registration).

titre: SR Probiotik/Sinbiotik dan Gejala Psikologis pada IBS
Kiwifruit for constipation and gastrointestinal comfort: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and remaining research gaps
resume: Abstract Background and Aim Kiwifruit has been investigated as a whole-food intervention for functional constipation (FC), constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C), and gastrointestinal (GI) discomfort. However, previous reviews have not fully integrated recent clinical trials with contemporary fibre terminology and cultivar-specific mechanisms. This narrative review aimed to clarify the clinical evidence, plausible mechanisms, effective regimens, and remaining research gaps for kiwifruit as a dietary strategy for FC and IBS-C and their constipation-related symptoms. Methods PubMed and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications from January 1984 to June 2026. Earlier evidence was defined as publications up to December 2017, and recent evidence was defined as publications from January 2018 onward. Thirty-three publications were included in the narrative synthesis. Results The strongest evidence supports the use of two fresh green kiwifruits daily for approximately 4 weeks in adults with FC, IBS-C, or chronic constipation. Clinical studies report increases in complete spontaneous bowel movements, improved stool form, reduced straining, and better GI comfort, with generally favourable tolerability. Mechanistically, green kiwifruit combines bulking, fermentable, and gel-forming fibre properties with intrinsic water, sorbitol, polyphenols, microbiota-active substrates, micronutrients, and actinidin. Conclusions Kiwifruit is best positioned as an evidence-based, low-burden dietary option within individualised constipation care, rather than as a universal substitute for laxatives or dietitian-led IBS management. Further trials should define cultivar-specific effects, long-term adherence, clinically meaningful effect sizes, and comparative effectiveness.

titre: The Neuromodulatory Influence of the Gut Microbiota within the Bidirectional Gut-Brain Axis
resume: Gut-brain axis is a complex and dynamic bilateral channel of communication between the gastrointestinal tract and central nervous system via integrated neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic. The gut microbiota has in recent years been recognized as a major modulator of this axis, and has a central role in maintaining physiological balance and neurological activity. This variety of microorganisms that colonize the gut is highly influential on the brain functions through a number of ways which include synthesis of neurotransmitters, immune response, as well as the generation of biologically active metabolites like short chain fatty acids. Neuroactive compounds produced by microorganisms such as serotonin, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and dopamine are vital in the regulation of emotional states, cognitive performance and behavior patterns. In addition, the gut microbiota is in close contact with key regulating systems, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and the vagus nerve, thus regulating the response to stress and emotional stability. The immune-mediated mechanisms also play a role in this communication by impacting neuroinflammatory events and maintaining the structural and functional integrity of the blood-brain barrier. Dysbiosis, or disruption of the normal composition, and diversity of microbiota of the gastrointestinal tract, has been strongly implicated in multiple neurological and psychiatric disorders, such as depression, anxiety, autism spectrum, Parkinson, and Alzheimer diseases. These results highlight the important role of the gut microbiome in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of central nervous system diseases. This review will give an in-depth analysis of the neuromodulatory functions of gut microbiota in the gut-brain axis. It is, also, an overview of the current advances in microbiome studies and a description of new forms of treatment, such as probiotics, prebiotics, changes to the diet, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Greater insight into these interactions can be used to develop novel microbiome-based therapies that can be used to improve neurology and treat neuropsychiatric diseases.
revue: International Journal for Research in Management & Pharmacy

titre: THE INFLUENCE OF THE GUT MICROBIOTA ON NEUROTRANSMITTER SYNTHESIS AND NERVOUS SYSTEM PHYSIOLOGY
resume: The gut microbiota is a complex microbial ecosystem involved in digestion, metabolism, immune homeostasis, and communication with the nervous system. Evidence from microbiological, physiological, and biochemical research indicates that intestinal microorganisms can influence neuroactive compound production, neurotransmitter metabolism, and signalling along the microbiota–gut–brain axis. Serotonin, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), dopamine, noradrenaline, and glutamate are among the compounds and pathways investigated in this context. Microbial effects may involve amino-acid metabolism, short-chain fatty acid production, enteroendocrine-cell activity, immune mediators, the enteric nervous system, and vagal signalling. Importantly, neurotransmitters produced in the intestine do not necessarily enter the brain directly; peripheral and central neurotransmitter pools are regulated differently. This review summarizes key mechanisms linking the gut microbiota with neurotransmitter-related pathways and nervous system physiology, while distinguishing experimental findings from conclusions that remain uncertain in humans.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Gluten-free diet adherence and associated practical, socioeconomic, and psychological factors among Tunisian adults with self-reported celiac disease: a cross-sectional study
resume: Background Maintaining a gluten-free diet (GFD) is essential in celiac disease, but North African adherence data are limited. We described adherence classifications and explored associated factors in a selected Tunisian online sample. Methods The survey was conducted from 25 June to 30 September 2021 through one celiac-association Facebook group. Ninety-one adults reporting celiac disease and more than one year on a GFD were included. Telephone contact confirmed participant reports but did not verify diagnostic records. The combined operational classification required Biagi ≥3 and Celiac Dietary Adherence Test (CDAT) < 13. Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) scores assessed symptoms. Revised analyses used retained aggregate summaries; participant-level records and the original translated questionnaire were unavailable. Results Participants had a mean age of 33 years; 84.6% were women and 75.8% had higher education. The combined criterion was met by 32/91 (35.2%; Wilson 95% CI 26.1–45.4), compared with 40/91 (44.0%) for Biagi alone and 35/91 (38.5%) for CDAT alone. Eleven classifications were discordant. Anxiety symptoms occurred in 6/32 (18.8%) meeting the combined criterion and 36/59 (61.0%) not meeting it. Other comparisons were exploratory, unadjusted and subject to sparse cells, multiple testing and overlap with CDAT content. An unresolved label-reading count discrepancy prevented that association analysis. Conclusion The 35.2% figure is a sample-specific estimate using an unvalidated combined rule and translations without documented local validation; it cannot be generalized to Tunisian adults with confirmed celiac disease or directly compared with single-instrument estimates. Anxiety symptoms showed an unadjusted association with the combined classification. Selection, measurement and archival uncertainty require prospective confirmation.

titre: Parental Attachment and Positive Body Appreciation in Youth (10–19): Intolerance of Uncertainty and Interoceptive Awareness as Mediators
resume: This cross-sectional study examines how parental attachment relates to positive body appreciation in youth aged 10–19, with intolerance of uncertainty (IU) and interoceptive awareness (IA) as mediators. The current study collects a new sample aged 16–19 (self-consent) under PRIDE registration ID 26-0462, and pools it after a measurement invariance test with an existing sample aged 10–16 that was collected in a previous study under PRIDE registration ID 24-0079, using the same child/youth version battery. The confirmed primary analysis is a serial (sequential) mediation model, parental attachment → IU → IA → positive body appreciation, with gender, emotional symptoms (DASS-Y) and age (in years) as covariates. A parallel mediation model (IU and IA entered simultaneously, no imposed order) is reported as a secondary, sensitivity analysis for the ordering assumption. Indirect effects are estimated in R with 5,000 bootstrap samples (95% CIs); if the achieved sample is small, the study is reported as underpowered and preliminary; Bayes factors are reported as a complementary way to quantify the evidence. Target N = 220 (190 also acceptable).

resume: Uvod: Hipnoterapija je dopolnilna metoda priprave na porod, ki vključuje hipnozo, sproščanje, usmerjanje pozornosti, pozitivne sugestije, vizualizacijo in samohipnozo. Uporablja se lahko pri zmanjševanju strahu, tesnobe in subjektivnega doživljanja porodne bolečine ter pri krepitvi občutka nadzora in zaupanja v lastne sposobnosti. Kljub možnim koristim je med slovenskimi nosečnicami še vedno razmeroma nepoznana, prisotne pa so tudi različne predstave in predsodki o hipnozi. Namen: Namen diplomskega dela je bil raziskati poznavanje hipnoterapije med slovenskimi nosečnicami ter ugotoviti njihove izkušnje, pomisleke, predstave o možnih koristih in zanimanje za njeno uporabo kot metode priprave na porod. Metode dela: Uporabljena je bila kavzalno-neeksperimentalna metoda kvantitativnega raziskovanja. Podatki so bili zbrani s spletnim anketnim vprašalnikom, ki je vseboval 24 vprašanj. Anketiranje je potekalo prek spletne aplikacije 1KA od 4. 6. 2025 do 4. 7. 2025. V raziskavi je sodelovalo 127 nosečnic, pridobljenih s priložnostnim vzorčenjem. Literaturo smo iskali v podatkovnih bazah Medline, PubMed in Google Scholar. Rezultati: Za hipnoterapijo kot metodo priprave na porod je že slišalo 51 % anketirank, 49 % jih zanjo še ni slišalo. Večina (64 %) ni razlikovala med medicinsko in odrsko hipnozo, 83 % pa jih ni poznalo možnosti izvajanja hipnoterapije v nekaterih slovenskih porodnišnicah. Hipnoterapijo sta v nosečnosti uporabljali le dve anketiranki, obe sta svojo izkušnjo ocenili pozitivno. Pomisleke glede uporabe hipnoterapije je navedlo 14 % anketirank. Kot najpomembnejše koristi so izpostavile večjo sproščenost, manj strahu pred bolečino in bolj pozitivno porodno izkušnjo. Za dodatno izobraževanje o hipnoterapiji je bilo zainteresiranih 87 % anketirank, 79 % pa bi jo bilo pripravljenih preizkusiti, če bi bila brezplačno na voljo v porodnišnicah. Razprava in zaključek: Rezultati kažejo, da je hipnoterapija med slovenskimi nosečnicami še vedno razmeroma slabo poznana, vendar je zanimanje zanjo veliko. Ustrezno informiranje in vključevanje zdravstvenih delavcev bi lahko prispevala k boljšemu poznavanju te metode. Zaradi majhnega in priložnostnega vzorca rezultatov ni mogoče posplošiti na celotno populacijo. Smiselno bi bilo raziskavo ponoviti in jo razširiti na večji in bolj raznolik vzorec ter vključiti več žensk z dejansko izkušnjo hipnoterapije.

titre: Arquitetura da Mente, Volume I: Doze Termos-Chave da Experiência Mental (The Architecture of the Mind, Vol. I: Twelve Key Terms of Mental Experience): A Descriptive and Critical Self-Appraisal
resume: Abstract Background: The vocabulary of psychiatry is not neutral: terms such as delirium (Latin delirare, "to leave the furrow") and hysteria (Greek hystéra, "womb") carry within their etymologies the worldviews of the cultures that coined them—a historical freight that reaches, largely unexamined, into the consulting room. Arquitetura da Mente, Volume I: Doze Termos-Chave da Experiência Mental (The Architecture of the Mind, Vol. I: Twelve Key Terms of Mental Experience) addresses this freight through neuroetymology, using the trajectory of mental-health terms as a gateway to the evolution of clinical ideas. Disclaiming being either a psychiatry manual or a self-help guide, the book aims to illuminate the origins of clinical thought, humanize medical jargon, and destigmatize mental phenomena. Intended readers include neurologists, psychiatrists, residents, students, researchers, educators, and general readers. Objective and methods: This appraisal assesses the book's content, structure, and contribution against its stated aims and five criteria—theoretical coherence, evidentiary rigor, inclusive scope, pedagogical value, and destigmatizing program—acknowledging the reviewer's dual role as author of both the book and this appraisal. The book's analytical framework is a four-dimensional spiral applied to each of twelve terms: etymological, historical-clinical, neuroscientific, and poetic-philosophical—showing how the experience was lived, narrated, and represented. Results: The twelve terms were chosen for their high conceptual density, and together the chapters trace an arc from altered consciousness (hypnosis, coma, frenzy) to affective equilibrium (euthymia). Each term integrates the four dimensions and is anchored by a governing metaphor—the gate, the winter oak, the underground city, the stage, the broken mirror. Historical figures serve as interlocutors rather than objects of retrospective diagnosis, while clinical boxes translate erudition into communicational guidance. The central thesis—that mental phenomena are intelligible only at the intersection of language, biology, history, and lived experience—is sustained throughout, with etymology honestly framed as illuminating origins without explaining current concepts. References are current and abundant, and the hysteria chapter is exemplary. Limitations include some variable AI-generated illustrations and an exclusively Western, Greco-Latin selection of terms. Conclusions: The book succeeds in delivering a coherent, pedagogically promising framework for humanizing mental-health vocabulary. Its limitations are addressable in a future edition and do not undermine its contribution. Recommended for clinicians, residents, students, and educators; general readers will profit from it as essays.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Digital health for health outcomes: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials
resume: Abstract Background Digital health interventions offer unique strengths including wide accessibility, scalability, lower workforce dependence, and potential cost savings. Yet evidence on their effectiveness remains inconsistent, and existing evidence syntheses are fragmented, limiting clinical and policy guidance. This umbrella review aimed to address this gap. Methods We searched six databases from inception to April 2025 for meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials comparing digital health interventions with either inactive controls (eg, usual care, attention placebo or waitlist) or standard therapies (eg, face-to-face treatment). Methodological quality, evidence certainty, and credibility were assessed using AMSTAR 2, GRADE, and evidence classification criteria, respectively. Random-effects reanalyses used HKSJ correction, with effect sizes standardised so positive values indicate benefit. Results We included 232 publications encompassing 1133 unique outcomes across 12 condition categories and 559792 participants. Methodological quality was high in 37%, moderate in 12%, low in 32%, and critically low in 19%. Overall, 53 findings had high-certainty and 84 moderate-certainty evidence. Against inactive controls, telemonitoring reduced systolic blood pressure in hypertension (equivalent Hedges’ g 0.55, 95% CI 0.31–0.78). Other high-certainty findings showed telephone-based interventions reduced diastolic blood pressure (0.17, 0.09–0.24), Internet-based cognitive behavioural therapy reduced depression in insomnia (0.38, 0.23–0.54), and telemedicine reduced weight in type 2 diabetes (0.12, 0.06–0.17). Against standard therapies, specific virtual reality improved upper limb function after stroke (0.23, 0.06–0.40), whereas telemonitoring showed no statistically significant differences in hospitalisation, all-cause mortality, or stroke among patients with pacemakers; synchronous virtual consultations showed no difference in HbA1c in type 2 diabetes; and tele-exercise showed no difference in physical function in knee osteoarthritis. All had high-certainty evidence. Additional moderate-certainty findings concerned stroke, Parkinson’s disease, and musculoskeletal conditions. Surgical, maternal-neonatal, and older adult care outcomes included high and moderate certainty findings. Conclusions Digital health interventions are effective but show no superiority over standard therapies in cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, stroke and Parkinson’s disease, mental health, musculoskeletal conditions, postoperative care, maternal and neonatal health, and care for older adults, though effects vary by outcome. Future work should prioritise standardisation, optimisation and inclusive implementation to realise the equity and resilience potential of digital health. Trial registration PROSPERO, CRD42025645564.

titre: Effects of cognitive behavioral therapy on psychological and physical outcomes in adults with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
resume: Background Pain and functional limitations associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can substantially impair patients’ psychological and physical well-being. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may alleviate psychological and physical symptoms in patients with RA by modifying maladaptive cognitions and behaviors and promoting adaptive coping with the disease. However, the effect of CBT in RA patients has not been systematically established. Methods PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from database inception to July 9, 2026, for relevant studies. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were independently performed by two reviewers. Any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or adjudicated by a third reviewer. Meta-analyses were primarily implemented through random-effects models. Effect estimates were presented as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Twelve RCTs involving 1,538 participants with RA were incorporated. CBT was associated with lower levels of depression (SMD = −0.35, 95% CI: −0.55 to −0.14, low-certainty evidence), anxiety (SMD = −0.20, 95% CI: −0.32 to −0.08, moderate-certainty evidence), and fatigue (SMD = −0.44, 95% CI: −0.66 to −0.22, low-certainty evidence). At the 6-month follow-up, the pooled SMDs were −0.42 (95% CI, −0.63 to −0.20) for depression and −0.22 (95% CI, −0.43 to −0.01) for anxiety, based on six RCTs with available follow-up data. For sleep, the pooled estimate favored CBT, although this finding was based on only two studies and was supported by very-low-certainty evidence. No statistically significant between-group differences were noted for pain, physical function, or quality-of-life (QoL). Substantial heterogeneity was observed for depression and fatigue, and the 95% prediction intervals crossed the line of no effect for both outcomes. Exploratory subgroup analyses by CBT delivery format revealed no significant differences between subgroups. Conclusion The pooled estimates suggested that CBT may be associated with lower levels of fatigue, anxiety, and depression in patients with RA. However, substantial heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing the line of no effect, and low certainty of evidence limit the reliability of these outcomes.
