titre: Anterior insular cortex neurostimulation modulates sensory hypersensitivity and pain-related emotional behaviors in a rat model of chronic neuropathic pain
resume: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic neuropathic pain (NP) is frequently accompanied by anxiety- and depression-like behaviors that contribute to functional impairment. The insular cortex plays a central role in pain processing and interoceptive regulation, with the anterior insular cortex (AIC) critically involved in integrating sensory inputs with emotional and behavioral responses. However, whether direct modulation of AIC activity can simultaneously regulate sensory hypersensitivity and pain-related emotional behaviors remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of electrical neurostimulation of the AIC (eAIC) on chronic NP and associated affective disturbances. METHODS: Male Wistar rats were subjected to chronic constriction injury (CCI) of the sciatic nerve to induce NP or to a Sham procedure. Twenty-one days after surgery, an independent group of animals received a single session of eAIC neurostimulation delivered via stereotaxically implanted electrodes at low-frequency deep brain stimulation parameters (20 μA, 100 Hz, 15 s). Mechanical and cold allodynia, as well as anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, were subsequently evaluated using established behavioral paradigms. RESULTS: The eAIC significantly attenuated mechanical and cold allodynia in CCI rats. In parallel, eAIC reduced anxiety-like and depression-like behaviors without altering general locomotor activity. These effects were selectively observed in neuropathic animals and were not detected in SHAM-operated controls. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that AIC activity regulates both sensory hypersensitivity and pain-related emotional behaviors in chronic NP. By showing concurrent modulation of nociceptive and affective dimensions, this study provides physiological evidence supporting the AIC as a key cortical node linking pain processing to emotional behavior and underscoring its relevance for integrative neuromodulatory strategies.

titre: Interpretation bias is associated with differentiation of emotions between and within valence categories
resume: The ability to distinguish between discrete emotions, known as emotion differentiation, is often associated with favorable emotional outcomes, such as more effective and frequent use of emotion regulation and lower alexithymia. Here, we modified a novel task-based method of emotion differentiation, EmoMap, to assess valence differentiation-the ability to distinguish between positive and negative categories, particularly in the context of dual-valence ambiguity (i.e., stimuli that convey both positive and negative meaning). We validated this task in part by establishing its relationships with expected correlates of differentiation, including emotion regulation and alexithymia. We then examined how one's ability to differentiate between valence categories relates to valence bias, which represents one's tendency toward more positive or negative interpretations of emotionally ambiguous stimuli. Results revealed that less differentiation between ambiguous and clearly positive stimuli and more differentiation within these categories were associated with a more positive valence bias. These results highlight the role of differentiation in valence judgments by demonstrating a link between explicit judgments, in which participants categorize emotional stimuli according to valence, and incidental judgments, in which they are evaluating the similarity in feelings evoked by those emotional stimuli. Having rich conceptualizations of ambiguity and positivity that overlap may allow individuals to more readily produce positive interpretations of emotional ambiguity in daily life. titre: Beyond learning difficulties: Emotion regulation in children with specific learning disorder and its associations with maternal alexithymia and cognitive flexibility
resume: Children with specific learning disorder (SLD) frequently experience emotion regulation difficulties, yet the family factors associated with these difficulties remain poorly understood. This cross-sectional study examined maternal alexithymia and cognitive flexibility in relation to emotion regulation difficulties in 116 children with SLD without psychiatric comorbidity and 111 age- and sex-matched controls. Mothers completed questionnaires assessing alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, and their children's emotion regulation; Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Revised scores were recorded. Compared with controls, mothers of children with SLD reported lower cognitive flexibility and greater child emotion regulation difficulties, whereas maternal alexithymia did not differ. After adjustment for demographic and socioeconomic covariates, the difference in children's emotion regulation difficulties persisted, whereas among maternal measures only perceived control over difficult situations remained lower. Within the SLD group, maternal alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, and maternal age were each associated with children's emotion regulation difficulties in a covariate-adjusted model (R2 = .527; adjusted R2 = .455). Because all measures were mother-reported and obtained concurrently, the direction of these associations cannot be determined, and child-to-parent or bidirectional effects remain plausible. Longitudinal and intervention studies should test whether changes in maternal emotional awareness and cognitive flexibility relate to children's emotional functioning.

titre: The Impact of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Relapse Rates in Bipolar Disorder: A Meta-Analysis
resume: Purpose: To evaluate the efficacy of adjunctive cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for reducing relapse rates in bipolar disorder (BD), focusing on differential effects by relapse type (depressive vs manic) and treatment duration. Patients and Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, and SinoMed (inception to 25 August 2025). Ten randomized controlled trials (N=930) were included. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251109273). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2.0). Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, with prespecified subgroup analyses by treatment duration (≤ 6 vs > 6 months). This meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting standards for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Results: Short-term CBT (≤ 6 months) significantly reduced overall relapse rates (RR = 0.73, 95% CI: [0.55, 0.96], P 6 months), no significant benefit was observed for overall relapse rates (RR = 1.08, 95% CI: [0.90, 1.30], I 2 = 0, P > 0.05) or depressive relapse rates (RR = 1.07, 95% CI: [0.84, 1.38], I 2 = 0, P > 0.05). CBT also significantly improved depressive symptom scores on the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI; MD = − 2.54, 95% CI: [− 3.83, − 1.24], P < 0.05), Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Clinician Rated (IDS-C; MD = − 2.83, 95% CI: [− 5.53, − 0.13], P < 0.05), and Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; MD = − 4.10, 95% CI: [− 6.71, − 1.50], P < 0.05). By contrast, no significant benefit was observed for manic relapse rates or manic symptom scores on the Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results. Conclusion: Adjunctive CBT reduces overall and depressive relapse rates in BD but not manic outcomes. Limitations include long-term evidence limited to two confounded trials, heterogeneity limiting precision, high attrition in five studies, and performance bias from unblinding. Evidence on functional recovery and social cognition remains limited. CBT should be prioritized for depressive symptoms. Future trials should enhance manic-relapse prevention and address these gaps. Keywords: bipolar disorder, cognitive behavioral therapy, relapse prevention, depressive episode, manic episode, meta-analysis

titre: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy
resume: BACKGROUND: Evidence supporting psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) for treating posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and other historically difficult to treat mental health disorders is growing rapidly. Interest from the public and within the US government to provide access to these treatments has also grown. Considering the gap between discovery of effective treatments and implementing them in clinical settings, it is important to synthesize current knowledge of implementing these complex treatment modalities to aid efforts for systematic implementation going forward. OBJECTIVES: The specific objectives of this systematic review were to: (1) identify extant literature on implementation of PAP, and (2) synthesize and present findings to understand current implementation knowledge and inform future directions. METHODS: This systematic review followed the procedures outlined in Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. Six databases were searched using a string developed with the keywords "implementation," "psychedelic (methylenedioxymethamphetamine, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, ketamine)," and "psychotherapy" along with Elsevier expansions and synonyms. The study only included peer-reviewed research on PAP, which reported on the implementation of the interventions. The implementation science framework, the Practical, Robust, implementation and Sustainability Model, guided the data extraction and synthesis about implementation-relevant factors. RESULTS: A total of 2,406 articles were identified, and 2,074 of these were screened by title and abstract after the initial elimination of duplicates and sources that were not peer-reviewed research articles (e.g., gray literature). Forty-seven were retrieved for full text review, and 20 studies were included in the review. Most studies (15) were cross-sectional surveys and/or qualitative interviews assessing organizational perspective. The remaining (5) presented included aspects of patient perspective (2), infrastructure (2), and patient characteristics (1). CONCLUSION: There is a noticeable gap in implementation-focused research on best practices for translating PAP from academic settings into accessible clinical programs. Addressing this gap is essential to support the safe and effective implementation of PAP in real-world settings.

titre: Longer term impact of universal school-based mindfulness training compared with normal school provision on adolescent mental health and well-being, teacher mental health and school climate: results from the 2-year follow-up in the MYRIAD cluster randomised controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: The MY Resilience In ADolescence randomised controlled trial showed no superiority of universal school-based mindfulness training (SBMT) over social-emotional teaching as usual (TAU) regarding adolescents’ mental health and limited effects on teachers’ mental health and school climate at 1 year. OBJECTIVE: Explore 2-year impact of SBMT versus TAU. METHODS: 85 UK schools (cohort 1: 975 pupils, 104 teachers; cohort 2: 7401 pupils, 575 teachers) randomised 1:1 to continue TAU (43 schools; 4232 pupils) or include SBMT (42 schools; 4144 pupils). The cohorts were analysed separately. Key pupil outcomes were risk for depression, social-emotional-behavioural functioning and well-being (Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (WEMWBS)). Teacher outcomes were burnout (Maslach Burnout Inventory-Educator Survey (MBI-ES)), self-efficacy, mindfulness, mindfulness in teaching (Mindfulness in Teaching Scale), stress (Perceived Stress Scale (PSS)), depression, anxiety and school climate. Analyses used mixed-effects regression, allowing for correlation between observations from the same school and from the same class (pupil outcomes). FINDINGS: SBMT was not superior to TAU in reducing pupil risk for depression (cohort 1: p=0.51; cohort 2: p=0.47) or social-emotional-behavioural functioning (cohort 1: p values ranged from 0.20 to 0.99; cohort 2: p values from 0.09 to 0.97). SBMT enhanced only cohort 2 pupils’ well-being: adjusted mean difference 1.0 (95% CI 0.2 to 1.8, p=0.02, WEMWBS). SBMT did not impact cohort 1 teachers’ well-being (MBI-ES: exhaustion, p=0.19; depersonalisation, p=0.78; personal accomplishment, p=0.35), stress (PSS, p=0.68) or school climate (leadership and involvement, p=0.31; staff attitudes, p=0.09; respectful climate, p=0.87) but improved cohort 2 teachers’ well-being (personal accomplishment: −0.2, 95% CI −0.3 to −0.001, p=0.049), stress (−1.6, 95% CI −3.0 to −0.3, p=0.02) and school climate (leadership and involvement: 0.2, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.3, p=0.03; staff attitudes: 0.2, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.4, p=0.02; respectful climate: 0.2, 95% CI 0.1 to 0.4, p=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Longer term outcomes broadly replicated 1-year findings, with little advantage of SBMT over TAU for pupils but some benefits for teacher-reported well-being and school climate persisting over time. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: While social-emotional teaching in schools can be effective, with attention to wider context and individual differences, SBMT as delivered in this trial is not indicated for 11–14 year-olds. Small negative effects at 1 year washed out at year 2, and benefits for teachers largely persisted. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN86619085.

titre: Cost-Utility of Improving Access to Psychological Therapies compared with usual care in Norway: A Registry-Linked Randomised Trial
resume: OBJECTIVES: Prompt Mental Health Care (PMHC), Norway's adaptation of England's Improving Access to Psychological Therapies, provides cognitive behavioural therapy for adults with anxiety or mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms. We assessed cost-utility using registry-linked data. METHODS: This evaluation included 738 participants from a randomised trial (70:30 allocation) of PMHC versus treatment-as-usual (TAU). Registry data provided healthcare costs, prescriptions, sick leave and work assessment allowances. EQ-5D-5L was assessed through 36 months in PMHC and 12 months in TAU; TAU utilities at 24 and 36 months were model-projected. Presenteeism was assessed with the Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Cost-utility was estimated over 1-, 2-, and 3-year horizons from healthcare and public-sector perspectives. RESULTS: Over 1 year, incremental QALYs were 0.07 (95% CI 0.05-0.10), with incremental healthcare costs of €1,710 (95% CI €1,557-€1,865), yielding an ICER of €23,809/QALY (95% CI €16,272-€38,321). Over 3 years, model-based estimates were 0.24 incremental QALYs (95% CI 0.14-0.35) and €1,551 in incremental healthcare costs (95% CI €1,266-€1,837), yielding an ICER of €6,376/QALY (95% CI €4,055-€11,533). At €30,000/QALY, cost-effectiveness probability was 84% over 1 year and ≥99% over 2 and 3 years. Incremental public-sector costs over 3 years were -€296 (95% CI -€3,588 to €2,848) when sick-leave benefits and work assessment allowances were included alongside healthcare costs. Presenteeism gains equalled 0.25 full-productivity years. CONCLUSIONS: PMHC delivered sustained health gains at modest additional healthcare cost and was likely cost-effective, with ICERs below Norwegian and UK NICE thresholds. Incremental public-sector costs were close to zero over 3 years, although uncertain.
revue: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research

titre: Stepped-Care Internet Cognitive Behaviour Therapy for Childhood and Adolescent Anxiety: Parent Perspectives
resume: ObjectiveBy exploring parental views, we can better understand how stepped-care models with internet cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) interventions are experienced by young people and their families. A qualitative approach was used to understand parents' perceptions of the acceptability and appropriateness of a stepped-care ICBT intervention. Specifically, what elements were effective, what barriers existed and how treatment expectations could inform adjustments to enhance overall outcomes for young people.MethodsTwenty parents of children and adolescents (aged 9-16 years) who completed the BRAVE Stepped-Care randomised controlled trials for anxiety participated in semi-structured interviews informed by Proctor et al.'s implementation science framework. Data were analysed using deductive reflexive thematic analysis.ResultsFour overarching themes were identified, (1) comfort with stepped-care approach, (2) desire for support that feels personalised, (3) parental involvement perceived as helpful and (4) importance of family flexibility.ConclusionsThe self-directed component of ICBT was well received, particularly with parental involvement. Parents valued personalised support, especially via videoconferencing, and the flexible stepped-care ICBT approach suited busy family schedules. Finding suggest that stepped-care ICBT can be effectively implemented in routine care when parental engagement and flexible, personalised support are prioritised, potentially improving adherence, outcomes and scalability.

titre: Individual Therapeutic Approaches to Reducing Mental Health Symptoms and Risk of Future Violence Among Adults Involved in Intimate Partner Violence: Systematic Review
resume: Intimate partner violence (IPV) among adults is a major global public health concern associated with significant physical and psychological consequences. Although therapeutic interventions have increasingly been developed to address the mental health effects of IPV and reduce future violence risk, limited evidence exists regarding the effectiveness of individual therapeutic interventions for survivors and perpetrators across diverse populations. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on individual therapeutic interventions for adults affected by IPV, focusing on five outcomes: depression, anxiety, trauma symptoms, IPV victimization, and IPV perpetration. A comprehensive search without date restrictions was conducted across six databases in October 2024. Peer-reviewed studies were included if they evaluated an individual therapeutic intervention for IPV survivors and/or perpetrators and incorporated a control or comparison group. After screening 6,966 titles and abstracts, 29 studies published between 2000 and 2024 met the inclusion criteria. Most studies used randomized controlled trial designs and primarily focused on women survivors of IPV. Intervention approaches varied, with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) being the most frequently evaluated, followed by humanistic, advocacy-based, motivational, and trauma-focused approaches. Improvements were most consistently observed in depression, anxiety, and trauma-related outcomes, whereas IPV-related outcomes demonstrated more variable effects. CBT showed promise for reducing depressive symptoms, whereas smaller studies examining humanistic and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing approaches indicated potential benefits for broader mental health outcomes. Future research should prioritize long-term follow-up, culturally responsive interventions, and integrated approaches that address both psychological recovery and IPV-related safety outcomes overall.

titre: Depression burden and differential treatment effects in PTSD and substance use disorder comorbidity: findings from Project Harmony
resume: Background: Depression commonly co-occurs with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and substance use disorders (SUDs), yet it remains unclear whether depression meaningfully alters treatment response for individuals with PTSD/SUD. Prior studies have examined depression as an individual predictor with mixed findings but no studies to date have evaluated depression's moderating role across a broad range of PTSD/SUD treatment modalities using harmonised individual patient data (IPD).Objective: To determine whether baseline depression moderates within- and post-treatment changes in PTSD symptom severity, alcohol use, and drug use across trauma-focused, SUD focused, integrated and pharmacologic interventions in a large PTSD/SUD IPD treatment dataset.Method: Data were drawn from Project Harmony, an individual patient data meta-analysis of 36 randomised controlled trials. Latent PTSD, alcohol, and drug use severity outcomes were estimated using moderated nonlinear factor analysis. Treatment effects were evaluated longitudinally using multilevel models with propensity score weighting. Depression was examined as both an individual-level and study-level moderator.Results: Analyses did not detect moderation of individual-level depression across outcomes. In contrast, study-level depression burden significantly moderated selected treatment effects, such that the proportion of participants with depression within each original RCT shaped treatment response. In studies with higher depression burden, trauma-focused psychotherapy produced stronger post-treatment reductions in PTSD symptom severity and alcohol use but smaller in-treatment improvements. Integrated trauma-focused psychotherapy demonstrated comparatively better in-treatment PTSD outcomes. High-depression contexts yielded attenuated PTSD improvements and mixed effects on alcohol use for SUD-focused psychotherapy.Conclusion: Analyses did not detect evidence that baseline depression, as operationalised within this harmonised dataset, moderated treatment response at the individual level. In contrast, study-level depression burden was associated with differential treatment effects across treatment modalities. These findings suggest that characteristics of treatment populations may influence comparative treatment performance and warrant further investigation in implementation and comparative effectiveness research.

titre: The "sunshine vitamin" in obsessive-compulsive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analytical evaluation of its association with disease etio-pathophysiology
resume: INTRODUCTION: Decrements in the circulating levels of vitamin D (vitD) are frequently associated with psychiatric conditions, often correlating with disorder severity. However, whether hypovitaminosis D is linked to incidence and symptom severity of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) remains obscure. The purpose of this systematic review and comprehensive meta-analytical assessment was to evaluate the relationship between categorical and numerical parameters of endogenous vitD status and OCD etio-pathophysiology. METHODS: Using a systematic scheme, we retrieved clinical data from peer-reviewed journals indexed in scholarly online databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, and EMBASE) in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. First, we tested for the differences in vitD levels in OCD cases, compared to controls. Following this, the association between vitD deficiency (VDD) and OCD was examined using categorical data. Finally, we assessed correlation between vitD levels and symptom severity in OCD cases. RESULTS: Compared to the controls, circulating vitD levels were significantly decreased in OCD cases (standardized mean difference = -0.669 [95% CI: -0.943, -0.394]). Interestingly, VDD was associated with significantly enhanced odds of being diagnosed with OCD (odds ratio = 4.059 [95% CI: 1.984, 8.314]). Further, vitD levels correlated negatively with the subjects' total (pooled r = -0.361 [95% CI: -0.566, -0.157]), obsessive (pooled r = -0.383 [95% CI: -0.570, -0.196]), and compulsive (pooled r = -0.257 [95% CI: -0.456, -0.058]) symptoms. DISCUSSION: Our results indicate a significant relationship between endogenous vitD levels and OCD etio-pathology, with the diminished circulating levels of vitD correlating with OCD severity. While a causal relationship could not be established, the findings provide a research platform for future interventional trials to evaluate the effects of exogenous vitD supplementation in the management of OCD cases.

titre: Attitudes toward eating disorders among primary care physicians
resume: BACKGROUND: Eating disorders are severe conditions associated with high morbidity, mortality and socioeconomic burden. Primary care physicians are central in their early detection and treatment, but clinicians have been found to have limited knowledge and even negative attitudes toward eating disorder patients. Most studies have focused on anorexia nervosa (AN) and bulimia nervosa (BN), while less is known about attitudes toward binge eating disorder (BED) and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID). AIM: To examine primary care physicians' attitudes toward eating disorders and assess whether education and clinical experience predict comfort in management and willingness to work with affected patients. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among primary care physicians (n = 191) attending a mandatory seminar. Attitudes toward AN, BN, BED and ARFID were assessed using Likert-type items based on prior research. Ordinal logistic regression analyses examined associations between education, experience and selected attitudes. RESULTS: Overall attitudes were similar across diagnoses. Only 14-21% reported enjoying working with eating disorder patients. Education was consistently associated with greater comfort in management and enjoyment of working with these patients, whereas clinical experience was more strongly associated with comfort in management than with enjoyment. Familiarity with ARFID was low, reflected in reduced response rate (14.6%). CONCLUSIONS: Attitudes toward eating disorders were broadly similar across diagnoses, but positive attitudes toward working with affected patients were uncommon. Education was consistently associated with more favorable attitudes and greater confidence in management, highlighting the potential value of continuing professional education and support for eating disorder care in primary care.
revue: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

titre: Transforming Growth Factor-β1 as a Longitudinal Indicator of Treatment Outcome in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: While the immune system's role in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) pathogenesis has been increasingly recognized, cytokine studies have yielded inconsistent findings. This study assessed serum cytokine levels in patients with OCD and a control group at baseline and after 12 weeks of fluoxetine or group cognitive-behavioral therapy (GCBT), investigated associations with clinical parameters, and examined whether cytokine trajectories differed by treatment response. METHODS: The study included seventy patients with OCD enrolled in a 12-week clinical trial and eighty-eight control participants. Clinical and immune assessments were conducted at baseline (T1) and 12 weeks later (T2); patients with OCD received either fluoxetine or GCBT. Treatment response was measured using the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Serum concentrations of IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α, TGF-β1, and IFN-γ were measured, and longitudinal cytokine trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: No significant differences in cytokine concentrations were observed between patients with OCD and control participants at either baseline or 12-week follow-up, nor did longitudinal change in TGF-β1 differ significantly between groups (time × group interaction: p = 0.126). Among patients with OCD, transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) increased significantly over the 12-week treatment period (marginal time effect: p = 0.0033). Estimated marginal contrasts showed that the increase in TGF-β1 from T1 to T2 was significantly greater in non-responders than in responders (estimate = - 0.435, SE = 0.141, p = 0.0039; FDR q = 0.039). CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal changes in TGF-β1 were associated with treatment response in OCD, with greater increases observed among patients who did not achieve clinical improvement. These findings suggest that TGF-β1 may be more informative as a longitudinal correlate of treatment response than as a diagnostic marker of OCD. Replication in larger prospective cohorts is needed to clarify its biological significance and potential clinical utility.

titre: Adverse Childhood Experiences screening in pediatric primary care and concurrent health
resume: Objectives Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) are linked with a number of chronic health conditions. However, there are no large-scale data examining whether ACEs screening is also associated with these higher rates. The current study examined the rates of chronic health conditions for children with and without ACEs screening, and those with and without positive screens. Methods Data from a large integrated healthcare system captured 684,887 youth age 2-18 years old eligible for ACEs screening between June 2023 and August 2025. Chronic physical and mental health conditions from the electronic health records at the same visit as the ACEs screening included: abdominal pain, ADHD, anxiety, asthma, depression, headache, hypertension, and obesity. Logistic regression estimated the odds of each health condition for: 1) screened versus not screened, 2) positive versus negative screen, and 3a) Total score, 3b) Part 1 score (10 original ACEs), and 3c) Part 2 score (7 additional adversities), adjusting for covariates. Results ACEs screening (versus not screened) was associated with elevated odds for ADHD, asthma, and obesity but lower odds of anxiety and hypertension. Among the screened cohort (n=599,989), positive ACEs screening was associated with higher odds of every health condition except hypertension. For those with a positive screen (n=178,214), both Part 1 and Part 2 scores were significantly associated with 5 out of 8 health conditions, with Part 2 generally demonstrating larger effects than the Part 1. Conclusions ACEs screening in pediatric primary care is a critical component to assess health risks and address early intervention and treatment.

titre: Patient Expectations and Experiences With Postoperative Bowel Function
resume: Importance Postoperative constipation can affect quality of life and satisfaction in patients undergoing urogynecologic surgery. Objectives The objectives of this study were to compare preoperative expectations regarding postoperative bowel function to patients' actual experiences after surgery, and to examine patient-reported use and satisfaction with polyethylene glycol. Study design This was a prospective cohort study of women undergoing urogynecologic surgery. Before surgery, participants were asked to complete a survey on baseline bowel function and postoperative bowel function expectations, which included the validated Wexner constipation questionnaire. Participants were again surveyed at 1 week and 6 weeks postoperatively regarding their experiences with postoperative bowel movements and use of polyethylene glycol. Patient Global Impressions of Improvement were used to measure postoperative improvement in bowel function. Results Of 86 enrolled participants, 83 (96.5%) completed the 1-week and 77 (89.5%) completed the 6-week follow-up. Some participants reported improvement in bowel movements at 1 week (53%), and more at 6 weeks (65%). Presence of preoperative concerns about first bowel movement did not influence perception of improvement at 1 week (55% vs 45%, respectively, P=0.33) or at 6 weeks (62.2% vs 52.5%, P=0.37). At 6 weeks, those who continued to use polyethylene glycol were more likely to report postoperative bowel improvement (84.4% vs 50%, P=0.002). Conclusions Most patients experience improvement in bowel function after urogynecologic surgery. Preoperative concerns do not seem to affect self-reported improvement. Some patients taking polyethylene glycol experience improvement in bowel function as early as 1 week after urogynecologic surgery, with more improvement at 6 weeks.

titre: Cinnamon supplementation in broiler and laying hen diets: benefits, mechanisms, supplementation doses, and limitations - a review
resume: Cinnamon and its derivatives (bark powder, essential oil, extract, and nanoparticles) were used as phytogenic feed additives (PFAs) in the modern poultry industry possibly due to their antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and gut-promoting properties. The present review pools recent studies on the effects of cinnamon supplementation on broiler and laying hen performance, focusing on growth performance, carcass and meat quality, egg production, egg quality, and hatchability. Cinnamon bioactive compounds, particularly cinnamaldehyde, has been show to improve nutrient utilization through multiple mechanisms of action: direct stimulation of digestive enzymes, enhancement of intestinal morphology, and selective suppression of pathogenic bacteria and proliferation of non-pathogenic bacteria. In broilers, cinnamon supplementation has been indicated to enhance body weight gain (BWG), feed conversion efficiency (FCE), carcass yield, and meat quality traits, including water holding capacity (WHC), meat tenderness, oxidative capacity, and sensory attributes. In laying hens, studies suggest that cinnamon improve egg production, egg mass, internal egg quality, shelf life, and reduce cholesterol content in egg yolk. Supplementation doses are highly form-and context-dependent: 0.2-0.5% cinnamon bark powder (CBP) and 0.2-0.4% extract for broilers under thermoneutral conditions. For laying hens, evidence suggests an effective range of 0.75% to 1.0% CBP, while cinnamon essential oil (CEO) level remain less defined. Under heat stress conditions, 0.03-0.06% CEO or 0.06% cinnamon nanoparticles indicate superior performance. However, results of the effects of cinnamon supplementation on broiler and laying hen performance were inconsistent due to variation in dosage, cinnamon form, bird strain, age, and environmental conditions. High doses of (exceeding 2-3% CBP or 0.01% cinnamaldehyde) can reduce feed intake, elevate blood aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, and disrupt cecal microbiota balance. While cinnamon shows promise as a PFA in poultry nutrition, several challenges, including dose optimization, thermal stability in tropical climates, palatability, and long-term residue safety, require further research. Standardized, region-specific studies are also required to facilitate evidence-based commercial adoption of cinnamon in sustainable poultry production.

titre: Integrated Metabolomics Identifies Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Oxidative Membrane Remodeling, and Reduced Lipophilic Antioxidant Defenses in First-Episode Simple Dysmood Disorder
resume: Background Metabolomic abnormalities in major depression have largely been investigated at the level of individual metabolites. We hypothesized that coordinated metabolic pathways, rather than isolated biomarkers, characterize first-episode simple dysmood disorder (FE-SDMD). Methods Untargeted LC-MS metabolomics was performed in plasma from 44 FE-SDMD patients and 44 healthy controls. Differential metabolites were identified using Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction and integrated with complementary machine-learning approaches. Curated metabolites were grouped into biologically informed functional modules, validated using principal component analysis, and examined in relation to clinical phenome dimensions, adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), and negative life events (NLEs). Results Of 450 detected metabolites, 298 remained significant after FDR correction and 240 additionally met fold-change criteria. Complementary feature-selection methods yielded a consensus panel of 20 biologically relevant metabolites that discriminated FE-SDMD from controls across multivariate and machine-learning analyses. Six functional modules revealed increased oxidative membrane remodeling, gut–liver dysfunction, mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction, reduced lipophilic antioxidant defenses and glucocorticoid metabolism, and altered dietary phytochemical metabolism. ACEs, particularly emotional neglect, and NLEs were associated with greater abnormalities across all modules. Gut–liver and mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, NLEs, and/or ACEs explained substantial variance in overall depression severity (66%), physiosomatic symptoms (41%), and suicidal ideation (43%). Conclusions Functional metabolic modules provide a biologically interpretable systems-biology framework linking metabolomic abnormalities, psychosocial adversity, and clinical phenotypes, supporting the neuroimmune–metabolic–oxidative (NIMETOX) model of depression.

titre: Fucoidan as an anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory agent in humans: a systematic review of clinical evidence and translational potential
resume: Purpose : fucoidan is a sulphated polysaccharide from brown seaweeds, commonly used as a dietary supplement due to its proposed anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and potential tumour-related properties. However, despite substantial preclinical evidence, its clinical effects in humans remain unclear. This systematic review aims to evaluate and synthesise current clinical evidence on the effects of fucoidan on inflammatory, immune, metabolic, and tumour-related outcomes in humans. Methods : a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Human interventional studies evaluating fucoidan supplementation and reporting clinically relevant outcomes were included. Eligible populations comprised healthy adults, individuals with metabolic or inflammatory conditions, and patients with cancer. Outcomes included immune function, inflammatory biomarkers, metabolic parameters, tumour-related outcomes, quality of life, and safety. Risk of bias was assessed using the OHAT tool. Due to heterogeneity in study design and outcomes, meta-analysis was not performed. Results : five clinical studies met the inclusion criteria, including three randomised controlled trials and two open-label studies involving patients with cancer, with intervention durations of 2 to 24 weeks. Fucoidan was consistently well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. Individual controlled trials reported reductions in selected pro-inflammatory cytokines, sex-specific changes in NK cell activity, and changes in gut microbiota composition in individuals with metabolic risk. However, these findings were not consistently replicated across studies. Studies involving patients with cancer reported short-term reductions in inflammatory markers and stable quality-of-life (QOL) measures; however, tumour-related outcomes were inconclusive. Conclusions : current evidence suggests that fucoidan may exert modest anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects under selected clinical conditions; however, the available evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and inconsistent. Although oral fucoidan was generally well tolerated, the small number of studies, limited replication of findings, heterogeneity in study populations and fucoidan characteristics, and methodological limitations preclude definitive conclusions regarding clinical efficacy. Well-designed, adequately powered randomised controlled trials using well-characterised fucoidan and clinically meaningful outcomes are required to establish the clinical efficacy of fucoidan in humans.

titre: The effectiveness of a therapeutically applied Dungeons and Dragons group intervention in a community mental health setting – Protocol for a randomised controlled trial
resume: Objective The use of Therapeutically Applied Role-Playing Games (TA-RPGs) in mental health treatment settings has grown in popularity and early efficacy investigations appear promising. However, the use of TA-RPGs for the treatment of anxiety and depression has rarely been studied in people who present with comorbid complex mental health issues. While one recent waitlist-controlled trial has reported that a TA-RPG (Dungeons and Dragons with embedded CBT) reduced mental health symptomatology, this now needs to be replicated with a more robust experimental design. Publishing this protocol methodology before the study is completed aims to increase transparency and aid other researchers conducting similar research in this advancing field. Methods The authors propose a two-group randomised controlled trial testing the efficacy of a CBT-infused, therapeutically applied, 8-week Dungeons and Dragons group program. An active control group will play board games for a comparable amount of time. Participants will be consumers receiving care at a community mental health centre with complex care needs. Outcome measures for anxiety and depressive symptomatology will be collected before and after participation in both groups, with the intervention group also completing outcome measures at 12 months follow up. In this protocol paper the intervention will be outlined in detail. The trial is registered on the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry: ACTRN12625000296437.

titre: The SDI Model: Stabilization, Disconfirmation, Integration. Contact × Safety × Time as a Common Mechanism of Change in Anxiety Disorders, Phobias, and OCD
resume: Psychotherapy for anxiety-related conditions is described in the vocabulary of many schools: exposure, habituation, extinction, inhibitory learning, emotional processing, and memory reconsolidation. This paper proposes the SDI Model (Stabilization–Disconfirmation–Integration), a conceptual framework that treats these descriptions as accounts of a single process: the nervous system learns to respond differently to a stimulus that previously triggered fear, avoidance, or rituals. The model specifies three necessary conditions for this change: contact with the stimulus, a framework of safety, and sufficient time (summarized as Contact × Safety × Time). Under these conditions, threat expectancies are disconfirmed, new learning occurs, and the experience is integrated. The model further proposes a clinical principle of the precise stimulus: change is accelerated when contact targets the specific image, thought, phrase, or scene that actually triggers the response, rather than the general label of the fear. The framework is grounded in the inhibitory learning and expectancy violation literature and is offered as a clinically oriented integrative model. Its applications to phobias, panic, and obsessive-compulsive disorder are outlined, and directions for empirical testing are proposed.

fiche.verdict: Le modèle SDI (Stabilisation-Disconfirmation-Integration) propose un cadre conceptnel unifié pour les thérapies des troubles anxieux et TOC, fondé sur le triptyque Contact x Sécurité x Temps.
resultats_cles: Le changement repose sur trois conditions: contact, sécurité et temps.
L'efficacité est accrue si le contact cible précisément le stimulus déclencheur spécifique.
fiche.conclusion: Le modèle SDI intègre les différentes approches de l'exposition sous un mécanisme commun axé sur l'apprentissage inhibiteur et la violation d'attente.

titre: Reinforcement learning processes underlying the onset and maintenance of compulsive ritualistic behavior
resume: Compulsive rituals in OCD present a fundamental puzzle for theories of human learning. How can an action acquire value as a means of preventing harm even though the individual recognizes that the action has little or no causal influence on the feared outcome? We propose that this apparent contradiction can arise from automatic credit assignment, whereby actions that precede favorable outcomes are reinforced even when those actions are known to be causally irrelevant. When harm is anticipated but no adverse outcome occurs, the absence of harm may reinforce the preceding action, allowing an objectively ineffective behavior to acquire harm prevention value. We formalize this account using an actor-critic reinforcement learning model in which actions are performed under fluctuating states of subjective perceived threat. Simulations show that agents possessing such false credit assignment mechanisms develop persistent ritualistic behavior in an objectively uncontrollable environment. We find that ritualistic behavior is especially likely to persist when feared outcomes are rare and highly aversive, making the ritual appear consistently effective in preventing a catastrophe. We further describe the cost-effectiveness of ritualistic behavior, and provide a computational account of how compulsive rituals can emerge as goal-directed attempts to prevent harm, persist despite explicit causal knowledge, and subsequently acquire anxiety-reducing properties. This work may help explain the persistence of compulsive behavior and inform mechanisms through which therapy can reduce it.

fiche.verdict: Un modèle computationnel par renforcement montre que les rituels compulsifs peuvent émerger de fausses attributions causales face à la menace.

fiche.intervention: Modélisation actor-critic sous menace perçue fluctuante
resultats_cles: Persistance de comportements rituels inefficaces en environnement incontrôlable

titre: Effects of Bifidobacterium-based interventions on patients with irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
resume: Abstract Background: Bifidobacterium has showcased potential benefits in managing irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms. Methods: We systematically searched online databases up until 1 December 2025, to identify randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials investigating the efficacy of Bifidobacterium-based or Bifidobacterium-containing preparations in IBS patients. Pooled analyses of the effects of these interventions on IBS symptom relief were calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on different regions, doses, and treatment durations. Results: Eight RCTs encompassing 1,304 patients were identified. Bifidobacterium-based interventions demonstrated significant improvements in overall response rate (RR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.63–2.43; P < 0.00001), abdominal pain relief (RR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.36–3.24; P = 0.0009), and subjective relief (RR: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.28–2.05; P < 0.0001). Significant benefits were observed in both adult (RR: 1.94; 95% CI: 1.58–2.40; P < 0.00001) and pediatric cohorts (RR: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.33–6.15; P = 0.007). However, subgroup comparisons showed comparable efficacy between daily dosages of < 10¹⁰ and ≥ 10¹⁰ CFU (P = 0.65) and between treatment durations of < 8 and ≥ 8 weeks (P = 0.33). Conclusions: Bifidobacterium-based interventions effectively alleviate IBS symptoms, particularly abdominal pain and subjective discomfort, in both adults and children. However, current evidence does not demonstrate superiority for specific doses or extended durations, precluding definitive conclusions regarding optimal posology. titre: Prevalence of functional dyspepsia in the Middle East: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Review title: Prevalence of functional dyspepsia in the Middle East: a systematic review and meta-analysis Type and method of review: Meta analysis Stage of review at time of this submission: Review ongoing — the protocol has been finalised and the peer-reviewed search prepared; formal screening not yet started. Review question: In Adults in Middle Eastern countries, what is the effect of Functional dyspepsia by Rome criteria compared with None (prevalence estimate) on Pooled prevalence of functional dyspepsia? Searches: The following sources will be searched: Europe PMC (PubMed, MEDLINE & preprints), PubMed / MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Google Scholar. Additional records may be imported from other databases. No date or language restrictions are applied unless otherwise stated. The search strategy underwent peer review (PRESS) before execution. Condition or domain being studied: Adults in Middle Eastern countries Participants / population: Adults in Middle Eastern countries Intervention(s), exposure(s): Functional dyspepsia by Rome criteria Comparator(s) / control: None (prevalence estimate) Types of study to be included: Inclusion criteria: General-population, community or student samples in Middle Eastern countries; Functional dyspepsia by Rome II, III or IV criteria (or uninvestigated dyspepsia, analysed separately); Reports prevalence or data allowing its calculation; Cross-sectional or cohort studies; Full-text article published in English. Exclusion criteria: Samples recruited only from gastroenterology clinics; Populations outside Middle Eastern countries without separately reported data; Reviews, editorials, letters, case reports or conference abstracts; Overlapping samples (the largest or most recent report is kept) Main outcome(s): Pooled prevalence of functional dyspepsia Data extraction (selection and coding): Two reviewers will independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts, blinded to each other’s decisions, and extract data in duplicate using a standardised, piloted form. Disagreements will be resolved by discussion or a third reviewer. Risk of bias (quality) assessment: The risk of bias of each included study will be assessed independently by two reviewers using a study-design-appropriate tool. Disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Risk of bias in the review itself will be appraised with ROBIS. Strategy for data synthesis: Results will be synthesised narratively. Where studies are sufficiently homogeneous, effect estimates will be pooled in a meta-analysis using a fixed- or random-effects model as indicated by heterogeneity (I²). The certainty of the evidence will be rated using GRADE.

titre: QbD-Optimized Colon-Targeted Mucoadhesive Tablet for Enhanced Plecanatide Delivery in IBS-C Management
resume: Background: Plecanatide, which is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome constipation (IBS-C), is highly susceptible to gastric enzymatic degradation, impairing critical therapeutic efficacy and bioavailability. This work designed an improved site-directing, colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation to guarantee site-specific delivery and efficacy. Methods: Design-Expert software 13 was used in a systematic optimization system with different concentrations of Na-alginate, Carbopol 934, and Methocel K15M. Flowability and compressibility were evaluated by pre-compression analysis. To specifically target the distal colon, the in vitro dissolution kinetics and cellular activity against the HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells were assessed. They were in vivo studies that measured mucosal recovery, submucosal pathology, and systemic oxidative stress biomarkers (MDA and SOD). In the accelerated stability testing, the standardized periods were tested under controlled laboratory conditions. Results: Methocel K15M proved to be the best polymer. The formulation exhibited 24 h sustained release, which fit best in the Hixson–Crowell (r = 0.980) and Higuchi (r = 0.956) models. Cellular activity against the HCT116 cells was high (IC50 = 79.31 ug/mL), being ten-fold better than the raw API. In vivo, the mucoadhesive system demonstrated almost total inflammatory resolution of all the layers of the colon. As opposed to regular tablets, it had a tremendous impact in reducing MDA (p = 0.014) and raising the activity of SOD (p = 0.002). Accelerated stability testing (40 °C/75% RH for 6 months) showed a slight decrease in drug content from 100.85% to 96.78%, which remained within the acceptable pharmacopeial limits (90–110%), confirming formulation stability. Conclusions: The mucoadhesive Plecanatide formulation is a “site-directing colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation” that can effectively overcome the shortcomings of traditional therapy; i.e., it exhibits the potential for better compliance. This formulation mitigates inflammatory and oxidative stress, offering a stable, promising alternative for managing chronic IBS-C symptoms and enhancing patient health outcomes in contemporary clinical practice and pharmaceutical standards.

titre: The Gut–Brain Axis in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Anatomical, Functional and Microbiome Perspectives
resume: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic and relapsing disorder characterized by complex interactions among intestinal inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, immune responses, the enteric nervous system, and the gut microbiota. Increasing evidence indicates that these processes are integrated through the bidirectional microbiota–gut–brain axis, linking intestinal and central nervous system function through neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways. This chapter examines the anatomical and functional foundations of this axis, including bowel organization, enteric and autonomic nervous systems, intestinal barrier integrity, and neuroimmune communication. It further explores the role of the intestinal microbiota and microbial metabolites in maintaining gut–brain homoeostasis and discusses how dysbiosis, barrier dysfunction, altered neural signalling, and neuroinflammation contribute to the pathophysiology of Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. The chapter also considers the influence of stress, psychological distress, visceral hypersensitivity, and altered bowel function within the bidirectional gut–brain relationship. Finally, emerging therapeutic approaches targeting this network, including probiotics, psychobiotics, dietary interventions, faecal microbiota transplantation, psychological therapies, neuromodulation, and microbiome-guided precision medicine, are reviewed. By integrating anatomical, physiological, microbial, neuroimmune, and clinical perspectives, this chapter highlights current understanding, therapeutic opportunities, limitations, and future directions in IBD research and management.

titre: Unveiling the Gut–Microbiota–Microglia–Glioblastoma Axis: Pharmacological Strategies and Molecular Insights into Neuroinflammation-Driven Brain Tumors
resume: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary malignant brain tumour characterized by extensive cellular heterogeneity, diffuse invasion, metabolic adaptation, and profound immunosuppression. Despite maximal safe surgical resection followed by radiotherapy and temozolomide-based chemotherapy, disease recurrence remains a major therapeutic challenge. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can regulate systemic immunity, host metabolism, and inflammatory signalling through the microbiota–gut–brain axis [1–3]. However, the extent to which these mechanisms directly influence human glioblastoma remains incompletely established. This review examines the proposed gut microbiota–microglia–glioblastoma axis through an integrated framework encompassing microbial metabolites, peripheral immune signalling, blood–brain barrier regulation, microglial plasticity, and glioblastoma-associated macrophage (GAM) metabolism. Particular emphasis is placed on short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism, aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling, microbial-associated molecular patterns, and inflammatory pathways involving Toll-like receptors, NF-κB, NLRP3 inflammasomes, and colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R). Pharmacological opportunities include myeloid-cell reprogramming, selective inflammatory pathway modulation, microbiome-directed interventions, and rational combinations with standard anticancer therapies. Recent reviews published in 2025–2026 have further highlighted the potential relationship between microbiome-associated signals and glioblastoma immunobiology [4–8]. Nevertheless, evidence differs substantially across human observational studies, experimental models, and mechanistic investigations. Confounding by antibiotics, corticosteroids, diet, treatment exposure, and tumour-associated physiological changes remains important. This review proposes a translational framework integrating longitudinal microbiome profiling, metabolomics, single-cell analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and pharmacological target validation. Establishing whether microbial signals causally modify tumour-associated myeloid cells will be essential before microbiome-informed strategies can be translated into clinical glioblastoma management.

titre: A Scoping Review Protocol for Unravelling the Relationships Between Colonialism, Gut Health, and Neurodegeneration Among Indigenous Populations
resume: The gut-brain axis is an emerging topic of interest in modern understandings of human physiology and metabolism, connecting the nervous system, digestive system, immune system, and the trillions of microbes that reside within our gut and digestive tract. This emerging area of research can be used to broaden our understanding of wholistic brain health, yet a research gap remains in the application of these theories to understanding the prevalence of neurodegeneration in Indigenous populations. This scoping review protocol aims to produce a review that provides a broad understanding of the availability of literature and evidence that addresses our research question. Through this evidence synthesis, we aim to inform future research in neurodegeneration among Indigenous populations.

titre: Effect of Care Brochure and Progressive Muscle Relaxation on Heartburn and Quality of Life among Antenatal Women: A Quasi-experimental Study
resume: Introduction: Heart Burn is one of the most common gastrointestinal problems during pregnancy and it is mostly caused by physiological and hormonal changes. It can adversely affect maternal comfort, everyday activities, sleep, and general Quality of Life (QoL). Pregnancy-related discomforts can be safely and effectively managed with non pharmacological therapies. Aim: To evaluate the effect of care brochure and progressive muscle relaxation on heart burn and QoL among pregnant women. Materials and Methods: The present quasi-experimental study was conducted in the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Outpatient Department of Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, a tertiary care hospital, Kerala, South India, from October 2023 to June 2024. A total of 250 antenatal women with heart burn were selected using consecutive sampling, with 125 participants in each intervention and control group. The intervention group received a self-care brochure comprising lifestyle and dietary modifications along with training in progressive muscle relaxation, while the control group received routine antenatal care. Heart burn symptoms were assessed using the Gastro-oesophageal Reflux Disease Symptom Assessment Scale (GSAS), and QoL was measured using the QoL/GRAV Questionnaire before and after the intervention. The Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare two independent groups. Results: Baseline sociodemographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the intervention and control groups, with no statistically significant differences in most assessed variables, except occupational status (p=0.037). The findings indicated that women in the intervention group experienced fewer heart burn symptoms, with a median {Interquartile Range (IQR)} score of 4 (2), compared with 7 (2) among those in the control group. Heart burn-related distress was also lower in the intervention group, with a median (IQR) score of 1 (0.25), compared with 2 (0.488) in the control group. After the intervention, overall QoL improved substantially (p<0.05). The intervention group demonstrated better QoL, reflected by a lower median (IQR) QoL score of 26 (3), compared with 34 (2) in the control group. Conclusion: Self-care practices that include dietary and lifestyle changes, along with progressive muscle relaxation, are safe, effective, and affordable non pharmacological treatments for reducing heart burn symptoms and improving pregnant women’s QoL.
revue: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

titre: Interoceptive Pathways Linking Childhood Maltreatment to Adult Affective, Somatosensory, and Sleep Symptoms
resume: This study examines whether childhood maltreatment is associated with adult psychopathology symptoms through differences in the way individuals experience and interpret bodily sensations. The study uses existing data from the EPIC dataset to test a preregistered secondary-data analysis of the relationship between childhood maltreatment severity, interoceptive processes, and adult mental and physical health symptoms. The primary predictor is cumulative childhood maltreatment severity, assessed using the Maltreatment and Abuse Chronology of Exposure (MACE) measure. Two dimensions of interoceptive experience are examined as potential mediators: distress associated with bodily sensations, operationalized using the Body Signals Beliefs Questionnaire (BSBQ) (Stephenson, E. et al., in prep), and difficulty interpreting bodily sensations, assessed using the Interoceptive Sensory Questionnaire (ISQ) (Fiene et al. 2018). These processes are hypothesized to represent related but distinguishable pathways through which early adverse experiences may become associated with later psychopathology. Four adult outcomes are examined: depressive symptoms (BDI), anxiety symptoms (GAD), somatic symptoms (Common Mental Disorders Screening Questionnaire (CMDQ)), and sleep disturbance (PSQI). The primary analyses use parallel mediation models to estimate the associations of childhood maltreatment severity with each outcome through BSBQ distress and ISQ scores while accounting for age, gender, and difficulties in identifying feelings (Toronto Alexithymia Scale). Indirect effects will be estimated using nonparametric bootstrap confidence intervals. Missing data will be handled using full-information maximum likelihood, with complete-case analyses conducted as a sensitivity analysis. The primary hypotheses are that greater childhood maltreatment severity will be associated with greater interoceptive distress and difficulty interpreting bodily sensations, and that these interoceptive processes will in turn be associated with greater depression, anxiety, somatic symptoms, and sleep disturbance. The study will also test whether the associations between childhood maltreatment and adult outcomes are statistically consistent with indirect pathways through these two interoceptive processes. Additional exploratory analyses will examine whether socioeconomic status moderates associations between childhood maltreatment and interoceptive processes, whether other measures of interoceptive clarity and visceral awareness are related to the proposed pathways, whether momentary somatic-affective coupling in daily diary data is associated with individual differences in interoceptive experience and psychopathology, and whether different forms of childhood maltreatment show distinct patterns of association (MACE Subscales). Because the data are observational and the primary analyses are based on existing cross-sectional measures, the mediation analyses are intended to evaluate patterns of statistical association consistent with the proposed theoretical model rather than establish causal mediation. Confirmatory and exploratory analyses will be clearly distinguished, and all confirmatory analyses will follow the analysis plan specified in this registration.

titre: THE ROLE OF ALEXITHYMIA AND EMOTION REGULATION DIFFICULTIES IN PREDICTING PSYCHOSOMATIC SYMPTOMS AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
resume: Psychosomatic symptoms – Physical illnesses such as headaches, stomach and fatigue are common in the university students, associated with scientific impairments, and impaired quality of life, which are not fully explained by medical pathology. This document develops and tests a mediation model in which Alexithymia, a characteristic that is characterized by difficult identification and description of your own emotions, indirectly predicts psychosomatic symptoms through emotion regulation issues. Starting from the Process Model of Emotion Regulation (Gross, 1998), the deficit-in-emotional processing account from alexithymia (Taylor, Bagby, & Parker, 1997) and somatosensory amplification theory, this paper suspects that alexithymia impairs students’ capacity to regulate emotional experience and that this regulatory impairment is manifesting itself again as physical symptomatology. Based on the sample size of 250 university students and validated self-reporting measures (the Toronto Alexithymia Scale Sema20, the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale and the Patient Health Questionnaire Sema15), a mediation analysis (Hayes' PROCESS Model 4, 5,000 bootstrap resamples) indicated that alexithymia positively associated was emotion regulation difficulties (β = .77, p < .001) and that it is positively associated with psychosomatic symptoms (β = .46, p < .001). The indirect effect of alexithymia on psychosomatic symptoms through emotion regulation problems was significant (β = .36, 95% CI [26, .46]) and continued to have a significant direct effect (β = .33, p < .001) indicative of partial mediation. The complete model represented 55.4% of the psychosomatic symptoms variance. These findings underpin emotional regulation difficulties as an important mechanism link alexithymia of physical symptoms in university students and suggest that emotional regulation focused interventions could reduce psychosomatic complaints even among students who remain relatively alexithymic.

titre: The Adherence Paradox of Interoceptive Observation: Motivational Thresholds and Behavioral Constraints in Self-Directed Practice
resume: Background: Prior phenomenological accounts have described volitional fascial unbinding arising from prolonged interoceptive observation (Huang, 2026). However, phenomenological success does not guarantee sustained adherence in practice. Objective: This paper aims to analyze the behavioral and cognitive thresholds required for adherence to such endogenous observation protocols, rather than evaluating them as a therapeutic intervention. Analysis: We examine two primary behavioral barriers: the "motivation-intention gap" and the cognitive load of sustained attention. We propose that sustained adherence depends on the rare conjuncture of paired thresholds, following two distinct pathways: either exceptional baseline cognitive endurance alongside a powerful motivational catalyst, or targeted epistemic curiosity alongside substantial sunk costs. No single factor alone appears sufficient to sustain practice. We further explore trade-offs between "attentional anchoring" (suited for novices) and "targeted attentional focus with somatic relaxation" (an advanced strategy carrying greater risk of attentional drift). Conclusion: The protocol imposes substantial cognitive and motivational constraints, limiting its broader applicability across populations. These findings suggest that while valuable as a somatic practice, such observational approaches pose considerable challenges for widespread clinical referral, particularly given the apparent need for sustained external guidance during an ambiguous initial phase.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Fibromyalgia as a trauma-related functional syndrome: multimodal neurobiological basis, post-traumatic model, and interoceptive-emotional reprocessing
resume: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a heterogeneous condition that, in a substantial proportion of patients, resists a purely organic explanation. Following previous articles dedicated to diagnostic paradoxes, this work aims to develop a post-traumatic and functional therapeutic model. The central hypothesis is that, after excluding unrecognized organic conditions—primarily small fiber neuropathy, documented in approximately 40–50% of patients (Grayston et al., 2019; Marshall et al., 2025; Oaklander et al., 2013)—the residual core of what we call "fibromyalgia" may represent, in a significant portion of cases, the somatic expression of a trauma-related disorder or a post-traumatic spectrum. PTSD prevalence estimates in FM vary widely depending on samples and diagnostic criteria, from about 9% in large-scale retrospective studies up to over 70% in clinical samples selected for trauma (Gardoki-Souto et al., 2022; Rahangdale & Ferraro, 2025), but the direction of the association is constant. A 2025 review proposes that FM and PTSD share a common pathogenetic mechanism—salience network hyperactivity—and should be read as parts of the same spectrum (Luís et al., 2025). Early trauma would remain encoded in implicit memory, in limbic (amygdala) and interoceptive (right anterior insula) circuits, without sufficient integration with hippocampal and prefrontal circuits that allow contextualization and narration. This integration deficit produces a self-reinforcing circuit—metaphorically the "broken record," technically a self-sustained maladaptive attractor state—and finds correspondence in specific patterns documented by MRI, fMRI, EEG/MEG, and EMG. On this basis, the article presents an exploratory proposal for therapeutic integration combining targeted EMDR (validated technique) with Harmony Meditation and Analogic Meditation (meditative practices developed by the author, not yet validated by independent trials), discusses available evidence on meditation for chronic pain and central sensitization, and introduces the concept of the Incredulity Effect as an original construct—here proposed as an interpretative hypothesis—that can psychologically hinder remission.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Alexithymia and alexisomia in adolescents with functional neurological disorders: insights from brain network connectivity analysis – a study protocol
resume: Background Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a complex neuropsychiatric condition, characterized by diverse sensory and motor symptoms, and accompanied by significant pain and comorbidities. While previous research has explored FND primarily in adults, this study proposes to focus on adolescents, a critical developmental period where FND can emerge and impact various developmental milestones. The multifaceted nature of FND has led to the investigation of two underexplored compromised awareness traits: alexithymia (difficulty in emotional awareness) and alexisomia (difficulty in somatic awareness), and the relationship between them. Methods In the proposed study, we will apply a multidimensional model, to examine both subjective and objective aspects of alexithymia and alexisomia and their associations with FND symptoms. Finally, we will employ a comprehensive model of advanced neuroimaging techniques, including graph theory of both structural and functional connectivity, to investigate brain network patterns in adolescents with FND. Discussion By linking psychological constructs, such as emotional awareness, with neural connectivity, our novel theoretical and analytical approach will advance our understanding of the underlying neural mechanisms of awareness traits in adolescents with FND. This will assist in identifying potential biomarkers for early detection, refining diagnostic criteria, and informing the development of targeted interventions, contributing to potential improvement of clinical care and outcomes for adolescents with FND.

titre: The Mystery of Male-Female Perception: Two Dimensions of Vision, Body, Mind, and Love — A Conceptual Philosophical Study
resume: Human love, attraction, and interpersonal perception extend beyond visual beauty or mental constructs. They may involve bodily sensitivity, imagination, intellectual discernment, memory, conditioning, social environment, and the presence of another person. This conceptual philosophical study proposes two symbolic dimensions of perception: (1) vision-dominant perception—visual gaze → aesthetic perception → imagination → movement of desire; and (2) presence-dominant perception—proximity, gaze, voice, and demeanor → somatic perception → comfort, alertness, discomfort, or intimacy. The framework is placed in dialogue with Vedantic antahkarana, Samkhya, Tantric and Kashmiri Shaiva symbolism, Western phenomenology, and selected research on interoception. These dimensions are not universal gender laws, diagnostic categories, or claims of male-female psychological superiority. They are interpretive pathways that may appear in different people and contexts. The study distinguishes attraction from love, bodily response from reliable knowledge of another person’s intention, and comfort from consent. It argues that mutual dignity, autonomy, dialogue, and ethical discernment are indispensable to mature love. This paper is a conceptual philosophical inquiry, not an empirical experiment or a systematic review. Its proposed framework requires independent evaluation.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Exhibiting AI images: Unexpected outputs, linguistic inequalities, and curatorial possibilities
resume: Abstract Structured around latent data spaces that store masses of semantic associations, AI image generators have an intrinsic capacity to draw connections their users might not expect. Their outputs thus have the potential to engender characteristically anthropological epistemic shifts: subverting pernicious stereotypes, opening up horizons of possibility, and rendering the familiar strange. I demonstrate this with reference to World Hypnosis Convention , a collage of AI images that I developed for a public exhibition following long‐term fieldwork on the social imagination of hypnosis. While English‐language prompts generated highly standardized portraits of male stage performers, other languages elicited vivid, unexpected portraits that challenged rigid definitions of “hypnosis,” drew attention to the constitutive role of suggestion in social life, and invited critical perspectives on social institutions. World Hypnosis Convention thus demonstrates how AI images can support practices of anthropological exhibiting, while illuminating several limitations of AI image generation itself. In particular, it highlights the linguistic inequalities with which AI users can be faced: non‐English speakers may struggle to achieve the precision they may desire, whereas English speakers can miss out on lateral perspectives. Both issues warrant greater attention in critical anthropologies of AI and in future AI design.

titre: Erminio Di Pisa, il maestro della fascinazione istantanea. Biografia, metodo e testimonianze
resume: La monografia ricostruisce la figura di Erminio Di Pisa, ipnotista, astrologo e medium attivo a Milano nella seconda metà del Novecento (1° gennaio 1942 – 15 aprile 2002), specialista dell'ipnosi istantanea e della fascinazione, cioè dell'induzione di stati ipnotici soprattutto con lo sguardo. Il lavoro si fonda sulla lettura integrale dei suoi scritti conservati nell'archivio della Scuola – il Corso di ipno-magnetismo pratico (MEB, Torino, 1980), il Settenario di ipnosi superiore e L'ipnosi nel marketing, confluiti nel 2007 nel volume L'ipnosi dalla A alla Z (Anima Edizioni) – e sulla testimonianza diretta del dr. Marco Paret, suo allievo, che lo frequentò e ne osservò il lavoro. Si aggiungono la presentazione dello psichiatra Paolo Muzzana, i ricordi di amici e allievi raccolti nel 2026, il ricordo della famiglia in forma scritta e la tradizione della Scuola, trasmessa da Di Pisa al suo allievo, che collega Di Pisa al fascinatore belga Donato attraverso, con ogni probabilità, il suo assistente Jean-Lambert Pickman, un certo Morelli e il maestro milanese Dante Caravelli. Il testo descrive la vita di Di Pisa, il suo metodo (sguardo alla radice del naso, tre metodi di fascinazione, ipnosi istantanea, ipnosi «ad occhi aperti», magnetismo fisico con passi, imposizione delle mani e soffio, differenza fra l'ipnosi tradizionale del Corso e l'«ipnosi superiore» del Settenario, sedute a teatro, in radio e in televisione), le sue applicazioni terapeutiche e le cautele da lui stesso indicate. Quattro puntate del programma pomeridiano di Raidue «Segreti per voi», ottenute dalle Teche RAI e databili al 1993, documentano le sue dimostrazioni televisive. Le registrazioni di alcune serate in diretta su Telelombardia del 1999 mostrano l'applicazione dello stesso metodo al telefono, con i risultati dichiarati in diretta dai telespettatori, compresi i casi più difficili. Una sezione finale conclude con l'elenco delle fonti e delle ricerche in corso. La Scuola del dr. Marco Paret – ISI-CNV / Université Européenne (www.marcoparet.com) – porta avanti gli insegnamenti di Di Pisa d'accordo con la famiglia. This monograph reconstructs the profile of Erminio Di Pisa, a hypnotist, astrologer and medium active in Milan in the second half of the twentieth century (1 January 1942 – 15 April 2002), who specialised in instantaneous hypnosis and fascination, that is, the induction of hypnotic states mainly through the gaze. It is based on a comprehensive reading of his writings held in the School's archive – the Corso di ipno-magnetismo pratico (MEB, Turin, 1980), the Settenario di ipnosi superiore and L'ipnosi nel marketing, collected in the 2007 volume L'ipnosi dalla A alla Z (Anima Edizioni) – and on the first-hand testimony of Prof. Dr. Marco Paret, his direct student, who knew him and observed him at work. To these are added the foreword by the psychiatrist Paolo Muzzana, recollections of friends and students collected in 2026, the family's written remembrance, and the School's tradition, handed down by Di Pisa to Prof. Dr. Marco Paret, which links Di Pisa to the Belgian fascinator Donato, most probably through his assistant Jean-Lambert Pickman, a certain Morelli and the Milanese master Dante Caravelli. The text describes Di Pisa's life, his method (gaze at the root of the nose, three fascination methods, instantaneous hypnosis, eyes-open hypnosis, physical magnetism with passes, laying on of hands and breath, the difference between the traditional hypnosis of the Corso and the higher hypnosis of the Settenario, sessions in theatres, on radio and television), his therapeutic applications, and the precautions he himself recommended. Four episodes of the RAI 2 afternoon programme Segreti per voi, sourced from the RAI Teche archive and dating to 1993, document his television demonstrations. Recordings of live evening shows on Telelombardia from 1999 show the same method applied by telephone, with the results reported live by viewers, including the most difficult cases. A final section lists the sources and the ongoing research. The School of Prof. Dr. Marco Paret – ISI-CNV / Université Européenne (www.marcoparet.com) – carries on Di Pisa's teachings in agreement with his family.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
