titre: Gut dysbiosis and brain cancer: exploring the emerging role of sweeteners and food additives
resume: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most aggressive primary brain malignancy, with a median survival of approximately 15 months, and its rising incidence has increased interest in modifiable dietary risk factors. Despite growing evidence that food additives disrupt gut microbial ecology and that gut dysbiosis influences neuro-oncological pathways, no previous review has systematically integrated these findings through the gut-brain axis. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from studies on food additives, gut microbiome, and glioblastoma to identify shared mechanistic pathways. Across five additive categories (artificial sweeteners, food colorants, preservatives, nanoparticles, and emulsifiers), a common dysbiotic signature emerged, characterized by depletion of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, increased lipopolysaccharide (LPS) production, disruption of tryptophan metabolism, and impairment of intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity. These changes converged on neuroinflammatory, immunosuppressive, and oncogenic pathways, including NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and m6A-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. Among all additives reviewed, aspartame provided the most complete hypothesized mechanistic sequence linking gut dysbiosis, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and m6A-mediated upregulation of glioblastoma-associated genes, highlighting a plausible microbiome-epigenetic axis that warrants further investigation. These findings position food additives as biologically active modulators of the gut-brain axis with potential relevance to glioblastoma pathogenesis and provide a mechanistic framework to guide future microbiome-informed prevention, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic research.

titre: The efficacy and safety of dupilumab therapy in pediatric patients with refractory eosinophilic duodenal bulb ulcer: a retrospective cohort study
resume: BACKGROUND: Refractory eosinophilic duodenal bulb ulcer (REDU) is a rare and poorly characterized subtype of non-eosinophilic esophagitis eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease (non-EoE EGID). Standard therapies are often ineffective, and evidence for biologic treatment is limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of dupilumab in pediatric patients with REDU. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 13 pediatric patients with histologically confirmed REDU treated with dupilumab for 12 weeks between January and December 2025, followed by a 24-week extension period. Primary outcomes were endoscopic healing and histological remission. Secondary outcomes included symptom improvement, laboratory parameters, growth indices, and quality of life (EGGE-QOL). An exploratory cross-sectional transcriptomic analysis compared pretreatment REDU biopsies with healthy-control biopsies. RESULTS: All patients achieved marked clinical improvement after 12 weeks of treatment. The median duodenal eosinophil count decreased significantly from 95 (IQR 72.5-100.0) to 3.5 (1.5-10.0) cells/HPF (P < 0.001), with histological remission achieved in all cases. Peripheral eosinophil counts and hemoglobin levels were improved significantly (both P < 0.05). Endoscopic mucosal healing was observed in all patients, with 11 achieving scar-stage healing. EGGE-QOL scores improved significantly (61.85 ± 16.90 vs 32.31 ± 18.85, P < 0.001). Exploratory RNA sequencing of pretreatment REDU biopsies versus healthy-control biopsies identified 837 genes meeting the nominal screening criteria, including 472 with higher and 365 with lower expression in pretreatment REDU biopsies. The top-ranked functional annotations were related to immune responses and cytokine signaling. CONCLUSIONS: Dupilumab demonstrated promising efficacy and acceptable safety in pediatric REDU, with consistent clinical, histological, and molecular improvements. These findings support further prospective studies to validate its long-term efficacy in non-EoE EGIDs.

titre: A study on the temporal network characteristics of early post-chemotherapy core symptoms in colorectal cancer patients based on ecological momentary assessment
resume: BACKGROUND: Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) often experience multiple concurrent symptoms during the early post-chemotherapy period, and both symptom severity and inter-symptom associations may change over time. Previous low-frequency assessments may not adequately capture short-term fluctuations. OBJECTIVE: To characterize the dynamic trajectories and network features of early symptoms in patients receiving postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for CRC and to identify candidate symptoms for enhanced monitoring. METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) was performed three times daily for seven consecutive days after infusion in the first and second chemotherapy cycles and covered 13 symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models characterized symptom trajectories, and a multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) model estimated temporal and contemporaneous networks. Edge uncertainty, centrality stability, sensitivity analyses, and between-cycle differences were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients contributed 4,134 valid assessments (completion rate, 89.5%). All 13 symptoms showed significant time effects. Fatigue, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sleep disturbance fluctuated, whereas numbness/tingling and depression showed cumulative trends. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea had comparatively high outgoing temporal associations. The strongest individual temporal edge was modest (standardized coefficient approximately 0.12). No statistically significant between-cycle differences were found in overall network structure or global strength. CONCLUSION: Early post-chemotherapy symptoms showed dynamic changes and a broadly comparable network structure across the first two cycles. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea may be candidates for enhanced monitoring and future intervention research; the observational findings do not establish causal effects or intervention efficacy.

titre: Afferent Renal Nerves Extend the Landscape of the Kidney-Brain Axis in Health and Disease
resume: Emerging evidence suggests a pathophysiological crosstalk between kidney disease and several brain disorders, highlighting the importance of the kidney-brain axis and the potential consequences of its impairment. The kidney-brain axis is a dynamic, intricate bidirectional network essential for maintaining body homeostasis. This crosstalk is influenced by systemic factors such as accumulating endogenous waste products (uremic toxins) and chronic inflammation resulting from impaired kidney function. Beyond waste excretion, the kidneys function as interoceptive organs, detecting mechanical, chemical, and nociceptive stimuli through a dense network of afferent renal nerves. Signals are transmitted to the central nervous system to modulate sympathetic outflow, fluid and electrolyte balance, and blood pressure. Despite a general understanding of the renal innervation anatomy and interoceptive function via the inhibitory renorenal reflex, the specific intricacies of afferent renal nerves are still limited. Significant knowledge gaps remain regarding the phenotype of renal mechano- and chemoreceptors, the precise molecular transducers involved, and their maladaptive remodelling during kidney disease and potential involvement in brain disorders. This review defines the kidney-brain axis as an integrated neurohumoral communication network through which the kidney and brain coordinate and adapt to physiological stresses. We describe the anatomical distribution of efferent and afferent nerves within the nephrons, map the kidney-to-brain signal transmission, describe known molecular pathways, and examine the implications of altered renal afferent signalling in kidney-related comorbidities, including neurological disorders. We shed light on the therapeutic potential of targeting renal sensory nerves to mitigate renal and neurological decline in the context of an ageing global population.

titre: Psychedelic assisted psychotherapy (2020-2025): a scoping review of clinical evidence, mechanisms, safety, and ethics
resume: BACKGROUND: Clinical research on psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT) has expanded substantially in recent years, particularly for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depressive disorders. Contemporary studies have generally evaluated psychedelic administration within controlled therapeutic settings that include psychological support, preparation, and integration. However, variability in clinical response and methodological challenges have highlighted the importance of individual, relational, and contextual factors, often described as "set and setting," in understanding therapeutic outcomes. The role of psychotherapy and the broader therapeutic context therefore remains an important area of investigation. OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to map the contemporary evidence on PAT, characterize the clinical and psychotherapeutic approaches used with psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, and DMT, summarize reported clinical and safety findings, and identify methodological, mechanistic, ethical, and implementation considerations across existing protocols. METHODS: A structured search of PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted on 23 February 2026. Sources published or publicly available between January 2020 and November 2025 were eligible. The review included peer-reviewed and relevant non-peer-reviewed sources addressing psychedelic-assisted interventions, including primary clinical studies, reviews, clinical trial registrations, regulatory documents, and other relevant contextual sources. Records were managed using Zotero and screened against predefined Population, Concept, and Context criteria. Findings were synthesized descriptively according to source type and evidence domain. RESULTS: The mapped evidence was most developed for MDMA-assisted therapy in PTSD and psilocybin-assisted interventions for depressive disorders. Randomized clinical trials reported reductions in PTSD and depressive symptoms following MDMA- and psilocybin-based interventions, respectively, while emerging clinical evidence also investigated LSD-based treatment for generalized anxiety disorder. Evidence for DMT-assisted therapy remained comparatively preliminary, with several available sources consisting of trial registrations or industry-reported information. Across the literature, preparation, supervised psychedelic administration, and integration were common therapeutic components, although the structure and intensity of psychotherapy varied substantially. Functional unblinding, expectancy effects, heterogeneity of psychotherapeutic approaches, and limitations in long-term safety data were recurring concerns. Ethical issues included informed consent during altered states of consciousness, therapist competence and boundaries, cultural considerations, and equitable access. CONCLUSION: PAT represents a rapidly developing area of clinical research, but the evidence base remains heterogeneous across compounds, indications, therapeutic models, and levels of evidential maturity. Future research should improve the standardization and reporting of psychotherapeutic interventions, strengthen methods for assessing blinding and expectancy, establish consistent long-term safety monitoring, and develop robust ethical and equity frameworks. Clear distinction between peer-reviewed clinical findings and preliminary or contextual evidence will also be essential as PAT research progresses toward broader clinical implementation.

titre: Case Report: Severe depression and suicidality in a young patient with RYR1-related congenital myopathy
resume: BACKGROUND: RYR1-related congenital myopathies (RYR1-CMYO) are rare inherited neuromuscular disorders characterized by considerable clinical and histopathological heterogeneity. Although chronic physical disability may be associated with substantial psychological burden, psychiatric manifestations in patients diagnosed with RYR1-related disorders remain insufficiently characterized. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of an 18-year-old man with a longstanding RYR1-related congenital myopathy with an autosomal dominant family pattern, who was admitted for a severe depressive episode with active suicidal ideation and a suicide plan. The patient also met diagnostic criteria for obsessive-compulsive disorder and retrospectively reported psychotic symptoms of uncertain timing, duration, and diagnostic significance. No active psychotic symptoms were identified at the documented examination. The familial RYR1 p.Leu4579Arg missense variant had previously been identified in both the patient and his clinically affected mother, supporting segregation with the neuromuscular phenotype. However, patient-specific muscle histopathology was unavailable. A particularly salient psychosocial feature was marked resentment toward his mother, whom he perceived as responsible for transmitting the disorder, in the context of longstanding physical disability, reduced autonomy, and intrafamilial conflict. An individualized multimodal treatment approach combining pharmacotherapy, described family-oriented work, suicide-risk management, and multidisciplinary follow-up was associated with partial improvement in depressive symptoms and reduction of active suicidal ideation during follow-up. The contributions of individual interventions could not be separated. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the psychiatric and psychosocial burden of living with an inherited disabling neuromuscular disease in a young adult. Although a direct pathophysiological relationship between RYR1 dysfunction and major depressive disorder or an RYR1-specific psychiatric phenotype cannot be inferred, chronic disability, impaired autonomy, awareness of genetic transmission, and associated family dynamics may contribute to psychological distress. The case highlights the importance of systematic assessment of depression and suicide risk in patients with rare disabling neuromuscular disorders and supports the integration of psychiatric care, psychological support, genetic counseling, and family-oriented interventions within multidisciplinary management.

titre: Ganglion cyst of the posterior cruciate ligament associated with osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle: A case report
resume: Ganglion cysts arising from the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) of the knee are rare, and their aetiology remains unknown. In this case, we found a ganglion cyst of the PCL concomitant with osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the medial femoral condyle (MFC). We presume that unstable OCD fragments of the MFC repeatedly irritate the PCL fibres connected to the lesion, and that this repetitive minor trauma and subsequent continuous tissue reaction may account for the development of a ganglion cyst of the PCL. We thus performed arthroscopic excision of the ganglion cyst of the PCL and OCD lesion, and osteochondral autograft transplantation. No ganglion recurrence was observed on magnetic resonance imaging at 12 months postoperatively and no symptom recurrence was observed during the final follow-up at 24 months postoperatively. We thus speculate that the pathogenesis of ganglion cysts in the cruciate ligament involves repetitive minor trauma and a subsequent continuous tissue reaction.
revue: Asia-Pacific journal of sports medicine, arthroscopy, rehabilitation and technology

fiche.verdict: Un rapport de cas suggère qu'un kyste ganglionnaire du ligament croisé postérieur peut être causé par des microtraumatismes répétés liés à une ostéochondrite disséquante.

titre: Neurodivergent Characteristics and Treatment Outcomes for Patients and Carers: A Secondary Analysis of the TRIANGLE Trial for Anorexia Nervosa
resume: OBJECTIVE: Neurodivergent characteristics, such as autistic and obsessive-compulsive features, may be associated with poorer treatment outcomes in anorexia nervosa (AN). We used data from the TRIANGLE trial to examine rates of neurodiverse features and their associations with 18-month outcomes for patients and their carers. METHOD: Patients (N = 370) enrolled in TRIANGLE completed baseline screening for autistic (AQ-10) and obsessive-compulsive features (OCI-R) and self-reported lifetime comorbid diagnoses. Patient and carer outcomes were measured at intervals up to 18 months. RESULTS: 27.1% of patients reported high autistic features, 61.6% reported high obsessive-compulsive features, and 21.7% reported high scores on both measures; 5.4% self-reported Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis, and 16.2% self-reported Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) diagnosis. Patients with high autistic or obsessive-compulsive features had higher levels of eating and general psychopathology and poorer work and social adjustment at both baseline and 18 months later. However, those with high obsessive-compulsive characteristics had greater improvements on these outcomes over time. Carers of those with high autistic or obsessive-compulsive features reported similar caregiving skills and psychological distress at baseline. Over time, those supporting patients with high autistic features reported greater reductions in psychological distress. Those supporting patients with high obsessive-compulsive features reported greater improvements in caregiving skills. DISCUSSION: We observed high rates of neurodiversity in our large cohort of patients with AN, and in some cases, more robust improvement relative to those with lower scores on neurodiversity dimensions. Greater consideration of neurodiversity in AN treatment may enhance benefit for patients and carers.
revue: The International journal of eating disorders

titre: Cross-Ancestry Polygenic Prediction of Bipolar Disorder and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in India
resume: Most genetic studies of psychiatric disorders have been conducted predominantly in populations of European ancestry, limiting evidence for the transferability of polygenic scores (PGS) to other populations. This cross-sectional study evaluated the predictive performance of European-derived PGS for bipolar disorder (BD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in an Indian sample. Participants (N = 2531) included individuals with BD (N = 463), OCD (N = 554), and controls (N = 1514) recruited from hospital- and community-based samples. Genotyping was performed using the Illumina Global Screening Array. PGS were derived from the summary statistics of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies using two Bayesian methods, PRS-CS-auto and SBayesRC. Principal component analyses demonstrated genetic overlap of the study population with other South Asian populations. BD PGS showed significant predictive performance, explaining approximately 6%-7% of liability-scale variance with PGS-only AUCs of ~0.71. OCD PGS showed lower but significant predictive performance, explaining ~2%-3% of variance with AUCs of approximately 0.59. Bayesian approaches showed better predictive performance than conventional clumping-and-thresholding. These findings demonstrate that European-derived psychiatric PGS can retain predictive information in an Indian population, although performance differed between disorders. The application of Bayesian PGS methods in this Indian cohort supports their utility for cross-ancestry prediction, while reinforcing the need for larger genomic studies in South Asian and other underrepresented populations.
revue: American journal of medical genetics. Part B, Neuropsychiatric genetics : the official publication of the International Society of Psychiatric Genetics

titre: Short-Term Effects of a Low-FODMAP Diet, Adapted NICE Dietary Advice, and Adapted NICE Dietary Advice Combined with Intermittent Fasting on Symptoms and Quality of Life in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Three-Arm, Non-Randomized Controlled Dietary Intervention Study
resume: Background/Objectives: Dietary interventions are central to irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) management, but evidence directly comparing a low-FODMAP diet (LF), adapted NICE dietary advice (NICE), and adapted NICE dietary advice combined with intermittent fasting (NICE-IF) is limited. This study compared the short-term effects of LF, NICE, and NICE-IF on IBS symptom severity and disease-specific quality of life. Methods: In this prospective, three-arm, non-randomized controlled dietary intervention study, adults with IBS followed LF, NICE, or NICE-IF for two weeks. IBS symptom severity, disease-specific quality of life, and psychological status were assessed using the Irritable Bowel Syndrome Symptom Severity Score (IBS-SSS), the IBS Quality of Life questionnaire (IBS-QOL), and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), respectively, at baseline and after the two-week intervention; stool consistency was monitored using the Bristol Stool Form Scale (BSFS). Between-group differences were additionally examined using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) adjusted for baseline values. Results: Eighty-one participants completed the study. IBS symptom severity decreased significantly in all groups (all p < 0.001), with a significant between-group difference in change (p = 0.018); the reduction was greater with LF than with NICE (p = 0.017). IBS-specific quality of life improved significantly in all groups (all p ≤ 0.002). Although the overall change differed among groups (p = 0.012), pairwise differences were not significant. After adjustment for baseline values, no significant between-group differences remained for symptom severity (p = 0.294) or quality of life (p = 0.333). Post-intervention stool consistency did not differ among groups (p = 0.485). A significant within-group reduction in anxiety scores was observed only in the NICE group (p = 0.025). Conclusions: All three interventions were associated with short-term improvements in IBS symptoms and quality of life. The greater unadjusted reduction in overall symptom severity with LF than with NICE was not robust to adjustment for baseline severity, and no between-group differences in quality-of-life improvement were observed; these findings require confirmation in larger, fully randomized studies with longer follow-up.

titre: The role of comorbidities in comprehensive healthcare utilization among people with multiple sclerosis
resume: BACKGROUND: Many people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) live with comorbid conditions, which may contribute to more complex healthcare needs. While there have been several studies on their associations with increased hospitalizations and emergency visits, there has been limited investigation into other aspects of care (e.g., imaging) or composite indices have been used rather than individual conditions. OBJECTIVE: To determine If comorbidities in PwMS are associated with utilization of a wider range of healthcare services and which specific comorbid conditions are linked to those services. METHODS: Participants (n = 185) were PwMS who completed a series of questionnaires about their comorbidities and healthcare utilization over the prior 12 months as part of a larger study. Regression models were used to evaluate the relationships between healthcare utilization and specific comorbidities, controlling for age, gender, race, education, and annual income. RESULTS: PwMS with a comorbidity had higher utilization of several services, including more healthcare provider visits (p < 0.001), particularly with primary care (p = .041) and mental health providers (p = .003), unique providers seen (p < 0.001), active medications (p < .001), MRIs (p = .008), X-rays (p = .031), inpatient hospital stays (p = .038), and elective surgeries (p = .035). Several comorbidities, including anxiety, sleep apnea, autoimmune thyroid disease, and irritable bowel syndrome, were most frequently associated with increased service use. CONCLUSIONS: These findings expand upon the previous literature, demonstrating that comorbidities are associated with greater utilization of a wide range of services and the complex needs of PwMS living with multiple chronic conditions.

fiche.verdict: Les comorbidités, dont le syndrome de l'intestin irritable et l'anxiété, augmentent significativement l'utilisation des soins de santé chez les patients scléreux.
fiche.population: n = 185, patients atteints de sclérose en plaques
fiche.intervention: Évaluation par questionnaires des comorbidités et de l'utilisation des soins sur 12 mois
resultats_cles: Comorbidités associées à plus de visites médicales (p < 0,001), notamment en soins primaires (p = 0,041) et santé mentale (p = 0,003).
Le syndrome de l'intestin irritable et l'anxiété font partie des comorbidités liées à une plus grande utilisation des services.
Hausse aussi des hospitalisations (p = 0,038) et des chirurgies (p = 0,035).
fiche.conclusion: Les comorbidités sont associées à une plus grande utilisation d'une large gamme de services, soulignant les besoins complexes des patients.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien comorbidités, SII et santé mentale en contexte médical.

titre: CHARACTERIZATION OF PATIENTS TREATED AT A UNIVERSITY OUTPATIENT CLINIC WITH FUNCTIONAL DYSPEPSIA AND ITS CORRELATION WITH MENTAL DISORDERS
resume: BACKGROUND: Functional dyspepsia is a common gastrointestinal disorder in clinical practice, characterized by chronic dyspeptic symptoms in the absence of identifiable organic disease, and is currently classified as a disorder of gut-brain interaction. Evidence suggests a significant association between functional dyspepsia and mental disorders, particularly anxiety and depression; however, this relationship remains insufficiently explored in national studies. OBJECTIVE: To characterize the sociodemographic and clinical profile of patients treated at a university outpatient gastrointestinal care clinic with functional dyspepsia and to analyze its correlation with mental disorders. METHODS: This was a cross-sectional observational study based on the analysis of medical records of patients diagnosed with functional dyspepsia according to the Rome IV criteria, treated at a university outpatient clinic in the southeast of Brazil. Sociodemographic data, lifestyle habits, clinical comorbidities, presence of concomitant mental disorders, and information on clinical evolution were collected. Statistical analyses were performed to evaluate associations between functional dyspepsia, mental disorders and clinical variables. RESULTS: The sample consisted of 135 patients, predominantly women, with a higher prevalence of patients over 60 years of age. Most individuals were sedentary, non-smokers, and non-alcohol users, with systemic arterial hypertension being the most frequent clinical comorbidity. Mental disorders were present in nearly half of the patients, with generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder being the most prevalent diagnoses, either isolated or in combination. No statistically significant associations were observed between mental disorders and most sociodemographic or clinical variables, except for obesity. During outpatient follow-up, a substantial proportion of patients with functional dyspepsia and concomitant mental disorders showed partial or complete improvement of dyspeptic symptoms. CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate a high frequency of mental disorders among patients with functional dyspepsia treated at a university outpatient clinic, reinforcing the multifactorial nature of this condition. The observed association and the clinical improvement identified in a subset of patients undergoing multidisciplinary follow-up highlight the importance of integrating gastroenterology and mental health care in the management of functional dyspepsia, contributing to a more comprehensive and interdisciplinary care of the patient.

fiche.verdict: Près de la moitié des patients souffrant de dyspepsie fonctionnelle présentent des troubles mentaux, l'anxiété et la dépression étant les plus fréquents.
fiche.population: n = 135 patients (majoritairement des femmes > 60 ans) suivis en gastroentérologie
fiche.intervention: Analyse du profil sociodémographique, clinique et des troubles mentaux concomitants

Association significative entre troubles mentaux et obésité.
Amélioration des symptômes dyspeptiques chez une proportion notable de patients lors du suivi multidisciplinaire.
fiche.conclusion: Forte fréquence des troubles mentaux dans la dyspepsie fonctionnelle, confirmant l'intérêt d'une prise en charge multidisciplinaire.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Dyspepsie fonctionnelle, axe intestin-cerveau, anxiété, dépression.
fiche.titre_court: Dyspepsie fonctionnelle et troubles mentaux
fiche.conclusion_simple: La forte co-occurence des troubles anxio-dépressifs en dyspepsie fonctionnelle justifie une approche intégrée gastro-psy.

titre: Salicylic Acid as a Food-Derived Bioactive Constituent of Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction: A Potential Functional Food Ingredient to Restoring Gut Barrier Function in Constipation-Predominant IBS
resume: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) is a chronic gut disorder with limited dietary management options. Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction (TQDZD), composed of medicine-food homologous plant materials traditionally consumed for digestive comfort, represents a dietary strategy with functional food potential, yet its systemically bioavailable constituents and nutritional mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the orally bioavailable polyphenol profile of TQDZD and elucidate its barrier-protective mechanisms within a functional food framework. Using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) serum metabolite profiling, we characterized TQDZD's polyphenol composition and identified orally bioavailable constituents in rat circulation after dietary administration. Untargeted serum metabolomics coupled with orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) was performed to map metabolic network perturbations in an IBS-C rat model, and dietary bioactive pathways were predicted by comparing intervention-induced metabolic trajectories. IBS-C was induced in rats by ice-water enema, and an in vitro inflammatory model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated Caco-2 monolayers. Barrier function was assessed by fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-dextran flux; tight junction proteins, cytokines, and signaling pathways were evaluated by Western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and qPCR. To explore the mechanistic basis of the observed barrier-protective effects, Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) signaling involvement was assessed using siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-mediated overexpression as complementary pharmacological tools. A total of 1962 non-redundant compounds were identified in TQDZD aqueous extract, with phenolic acids and flavonoids as the predominant chemical classes. These polyphenol-rich profiles are characteristic of functional foods with gut-protective potential. In dosed rat serum, 257 systemically bioavailable components were detected, of which 150 (58.4%) were prototype constituents. Multi-criteria screening (treatment/control peak area ratio ≥ 2, top-20 abundance rank in the formula, coefficient of variation < 30%, and Level 1 identification confidence) yielded four core prototypes: salicylic acid, N-acetyl-L-phenylalanine, L-valyl-L-phenylalanine, and L-phenylalanyl-L-hydroxyproline. Among these, salicylic acid-a naturally occurring phenolic acid widely distributed in plant-based foods-was prioritized for functional validation. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that IBS-C rats exhibited profound dysregulation of a lipid-inflammatory network, characterized by disturbances in glycerophospholipid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, and sphingolipid signaling. TQDZD intervention remodeled this network in a dose-dependent manner; notably, the metabolic trajectory of the high-dose TQDZD group converged strikingly with that of the BTK modulator orelabrutinib. In vivo, TQDZD significantly reduced intestinal permeability (p < 0.001), restored colonic expression of tight junction proteins zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), Occludin, and Claudin-1 (p < 0.001), and suppressed mucosal and serum levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), IL-1β, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) (p < 0.001). Mechanistic studies demonstrated that Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction (TQDZD) inhibited the BTK-spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK)- phospholipase C gamma 2 (PLCγ2)-protein kinase B (AKT) axis, thereby blocking IκBα phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation. BTK knockdown potentiated, whereas BTK overexpression abrogated, the barrier-protective and anti-inflammatory effects of TQDZD. Salicylic acid alone fully reproduced TQDZD's phenotype in vitro and in vivo, and its effects were strictly BTK-dependent. TQDZD exerts its therapeutic effect on constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) via its core systemically bioavailable constituent salicylic acid. The biological activity of salicylic acid relies on the BTK signaling pathway, which blocks the non-canonical nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway, thereby restoring the intestinal epithelial barrier and suppressing low-grade inflammation. Given salicylic acid's abundance in edible plants and its long history of safe dietary exposure, these findings provide a mechanistic rationale for developing phenolic-acid-rich botanical blends as supportive dietary strategies for IBS-C and related barrier-centric gastrointestinal disorders.

Restauration des protéines de jonction serrée (ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-1, p < 0.001)

titre: Probiotics and Semaglutide Therapy: Mechanistic Perspectives and Potential Interactions in Gut Microbiota, Gastrointestinal Function, and Metabolic Health
resume: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Semaglutide is one of the currently widely used medications that have shown particularly strong effects on glycemic control and body weight in people with obesity and diabetes. However, gastrointestinal adverse effects are common during semaglutide therapy. Gut microbiota and probiotic supplementation have also attracted growing interest because of their potential effects on metabolic health and gastrointestinal function and their ability to support gastrointestinal health. METHODS: This narrative review article investigated the potential interaction between probiotics and semaglutide in relation to gut microbiota, gastrointestinal function, and metabolic health. RESULTS: Patients with metabolic disorders, including type 2 diabetes and obesity, commonly have gut dysbiosis, characterized by an imbalance in the composition and function of the intestinal microbiota. Semaglutide, as a currently important treatment for metabolic disorders, provides effective glycemic control and clinically meaningful weight loss; however, gastrointestinal adverse events are among the most frequently reported adverse effects of semaglutide treatment. Modulation of the gut microbiota may contribute to improved metabolic outcomes and gastrointestinal function. Probiotics may further modulate the gut microbiota by restoring microbial homeostasis, increasing the abundance of beneficial microorganisms, and improving microbial diversity. In addition, probiotic supplementation has been associated with improved metabolic outcomes, including better glycemic control in individuals with diabetes. CONCLUSIONS: Probiotics may potentially complement the metabolic effects of semaglutide and support gastrointestinal function and gut microbiota during semaglutide therapy. However, further studies are required to determine whether a clinically meaningful interaction exists between semaglutide and probiotics.

fiche.verdict: Revue narrative évaluant l'intérêt potentiel des probiotiques pour atténuer les effets secondaires gastro-intestinaux du sémaglutide.
fiche.population: Patients obèses ou diabétiques (type 2) traités par sémaglutide
fiche.intervention: Supplémentation par probiotiques en association au sémaglutide
resultats_cles: Le sémaglutide induit fréquemment des effets indésirables gastro-intestinaux.
Les patients obèses/diabétiques présentent une dysbiose intestinale préexistante.
Les probiotiques pourraient restaurer l'eubiose et soutenir la tolérance digestive.
fiche.conclusion: Les probiotiques pourraient compléter les effets métaboliques du sémaglutide et améliorer la tolérance digestive, nécessitant des études cliniques.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Éloigné de la pratique psychologique, mais éclaire la prise en charge globale des troubles métaboliques et digestifs.
fiche.titre_court: Probiotiques et sémaglutide en santé métabolique
fiche.conclusion_simple: Associer probiotiques et sémaglutide est une piste théorique séduisante pour limiter les effets secondaires digestifs, mais cela reste à prouver.

titre: Comparative efficacy of gut microbiota-targeted therapies for motor and non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Gut dysbiosis may contribute to Parkinson's disease (PD) through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Probiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) have been studied as potential treatments, but their comparative effects remain uncertain. METHODS: We searched trial registries and electronic databases from inception to April 1, 2026 for randomized controlled trials of gut microbiota-targeted therapies in PD. We performed a frequentist network meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, and confidence in the evidence was assessed with CINeMA. Treatment rankings were summarized using SUCRA values. RESULTS: Nineteen RCTs involving 1,156 participants and five treatment options (FMT, probiotics, synbiotics, routine care, and placebo) were included. Probiotics increased spontaneous bowel movement (SBM) frequency compared with placebo (MD = 1.93, 95% CI: 0.23 to 3.64; SUCRA = 88.3%). In the oral-administration subgroup, probiotics (MD = 2.01, 95% CI: 0.64 to 3.39) and synbiotics (MD = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.01 to 2.45) increased SBM frequency. No active treatment significantly improved MDS-UPDRS III scores compared with placebo, although synbiotics and FMT had higher SUCRA rankings. Evidence certainty was Moderate for oral probiotics on SBM frequency and Low to Very Low for motor function and quality of life. CONCLUSION: Oral probiotics improved SBM frequency in patients with PD. Evidence for motor function and quality of life was uncertain, and the higher rankings of FMT and synbiotics should be considered exploratory. Larger head-to-head randomized trials are needed. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/recorddashboard.

fiche.verdict: Une méta-analyse en réseau suggère que les probiotiques oraux augmentent la fréquence des selles dans la maladie de Parkinson.
fiche.population: 1 156 participants répartis dans 19 essais contrôlés randomisés (Parkinson)

resultats_cles: Probiotiques augmentent la fréquence des selles (SBM) vs placebo (MD = 1,93, IC 95% [0,23 ; 3,64]).
Pas d'amélioration significative des scores moteurs (MDS-UPDRS III) pour les traitements actifs vs placebo.
Niveau de certitude modéré pour les probiotiques sur la fréquence des selles, faible à très faible pour le moteur.
fiche.conclusion: Les probiotiques oraux améliorent la constipation dans la maladie de Parkinson, mais l'évidence sur la motricité reste incertaine.

fiche.conclusion_simple: Les probiotiques oraux peuvent améliorer la fréquence des selles dans la maladie de Parkinson, mais les effets moteurs restent incertains.

titre: Psychobiotic modulation of the microbiome-gut-brain axis: A systematic review of the literature
resume: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is incompletely explained by the monoaminergic model. The microbiome-gut-brain (MGB) axis may link gut microbial ecology to immune, metabolic, neuroendocrine and neural signalling relevant to mood and antidepressant response. OBJECTIVES: To synthesise recent evidence on (I) microbiota-targeted (psychobiotic) interventions; (II) the gut microbiome as a diagnostic and treatment-response biomarker; and (III) biopsychosocial and immunometabolic correlates of depression. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus and PubPsych were searched (January 2022 to February 2025) following PRISMA 2020. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, ROBINS-I and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Findings were synthesised narratively, stratified by population, intervention type and study design. RESULTS: Sixty-six studies were included: 36 in diagnosed depressive disorders, 10 in non-clinical samples, 15 in other medical conditions and 5 genetic or biobank analyses; most were of low or very low methodological quality. Depression was associated with lower abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa and with altered tryptophan, bile acid, inflammatory and barrier-related markers, largely in cross-sectional designs. In MDD, some strain-specific add-on probiotics were associated with greater symptom reduction than placebo, whereas others showed no benefit; prebiotic, dietary and faecal microbiota transplantation data were sparse or derived from non-MDD populations. Diagnostic and treatment-response models came from small samples and were rarely externally validated. CONCLUSIONS: The gut microbiome is a plausible contributor to depressive pathophysiology and treatment variability, but current evidence is heterogeneous, predominantly associative and of low certainty. Psychobiotic interventions and microbiome-based biomarkers remain investigational; adequately powered, strain- and dose-specific trials and independently validated models are required before clinical application.

fiche.verdict: Revue de la littérature sur les psychobiotiques et l'axe intestin-cerveau dans la dépression majeure, soulignant une hétérogénéité méthodologique.
fiche.population: 66 études incluant des patients souffrant de troubles dépressifs majeurs, échantillons non cliniques et autres pathologies
fiche.intervention: Interventions psychobiotiques (probiotiques, prébiotiques, régimes, FMT) ou analyse du microbiote comme biomarqueur.
resultats_cles: Dépression associée à une baisse de taxons producteurs d'acides gras à chaîne courte et à des altérations inflammatoires.
Certains probiotiques adjuvants réduisent les symptômes dépressifs vs placebo, d'autres non.
Qualité méthodologique globale des études jugée faible ou très faible.
fiche.conclusion: Le microbiote est un contributeur plausible de la dépression, mais les interventions psychobiotiques restent exploratoires.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Apporte un éclairage sur l'axe microbiote-intestin-cerveau et les psychobiotiques en lien avec l'humeur.
fiche.titre_court: Psychobiotiques et dépression : revue systématique
fiche.conclusion_simple: Le rôle du microbiote dans la dépression est plausible, mais les preuves cliniques des psychobiotiques restent préliminaires.

titre: [Alpha-gal allergy]
resume: Alpha-gal allergy is a tick-borne allergy caused by IgE antibodies against the oligosaccharide alpha-gal. Alpha-gal is found in meat from mammals and in mammal-derived medications. The allergy often results in a delayed reaction 2-6 hours after ingestion. Symptoms commonly include urticaria and abdominal pain, but may progress to severe anaphylaxis, often influenced by cofactors such as exercise, alcohol, or NSAIDs. Diagnosis relies on patient history, as no laboratory test offers both high sensitivity and specificity. Treatment consists of avoidance strategies and the use of adrenaline autoinjectors, as argued in this review.

fiche.verdict: Une revue détaille l'allergie à l'alpha-gal (liée aux tiques), provoquant des réactions retardées aux viandes de mammifères et médicaments.
fiche.population: Patients souffrant d'allergie à l'alpha-gal.
fiche.intervention: Éviction des produits mammaires et usage d'auto-injecteurs d'adrénaline.
resultats_cles: Réaction allergique retardée de 2 à 6 heures après ingestion de viande de mammifère.
Symptômes : urticaire, douleurs abdominales, pouvant aller jusqu'à l'anaphylaxie.
fiche.conclusion: Le diagnostic repose sur l'histoire clinique et le traitement principal consiste en des stratégies d'éviction.
limites: Revue narrative sans analyse méthodique formelle.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Pertinent pour les douleurs abdominales atypiques et l'allergologie en gastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Revue sur l'allergie à l'alpha-gal
fiche.conclusion_simple: L'allergie à l'alpha-gal provoque des réactions digestives et anaphylactiques retardées nécessitant l'éviction des viandes de mammifères.

titre: The gut-eye axis in inflammatory bowel disease: shared immune mechanisms and targeted therapies
resume: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is recognized not only as a disease confined to the intestinal tract, but also as a systemic immune-mediated disorder. Among its diverse extraintestinal manifestations, ocular complications, which range from self-limiting episcleritis to severe and sight-threatening uveitis and scleritis, represent a critical clinical challenge that profoundly impacts patient quality of life. This review synthesizes the epidemiological landscape and clinical spectrum of ocular manifestations in IBD, framing their pathogenesis through the emerging concept of the gut-eye axis. We critically examine the shared mechanistic pathways driving this bidirectional relationship, including the systemic dissemination of circulating inflammatory cytokines, aberrant lymphocyte homing, cross-reactive autoantibodies, shared genetic susceptibilities, and microbiota dysbiosis, which collectively compromise the blood-ocular barrier. Furthermore, we outline targeted therapeutic strategies, highlighting that while systemic anti-TNF agents remain the cornerstone for severe and refractory ocular inflammation, gut-selective biologics like vedolizumab necessitate careful application due to the risk of extraintestinal exacerbation. Finally, we underscore the indispensable role of multidisciplinary management and highlight future research trajectories.

fiche.verdict: Revue sur l'axe intestin-œil dans les MICI, soulignant les mécanismes immunitaires partagés et les stratégies thérapeutiques ciblées.
fiche.intervention: Synthèse de la littérature sur les manifestations oculaires des MICI.
resultats_cles: Implication de la dysbiose, des cytokines circulantes et du homing lymphocytaire.
Vigilance requise avec les biologiques gut-selective (vedolizumab) sur les atteintes extra-intestinales.
fiche.conclusion: Nécessité d'une prise en charge multidisciplinaire face aux complications oculaires des MICI via l'axe intestin-œil.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Intéressant pour la vision systémique des MICI, hors pratique psychologique directe.
fiche.titre_court: Axe intestin-œil dans les MICI
fiche.conclusion_simple: Les complications oculaires des MICI relèvent de mécanismes immunitaires et microbiens partagés nécessitant une approche pluridisciplinaire.

titre: Efficacy, safety and mechanism of Jinfeng pill in the treatment of perimenopausal syndrome: A protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Perimenopausal syndrome (PMPS) refers to a series of physiological and psychological symptoms caused by the fluctuation or decline of sex hormone levels during the pre- and postmenopausal periods. With the acceleration of aging society, more and more women suffer from symptoms of PMPS. Jinfeng Pill (JFP) is a classic Chinese patent medicine for gynecological diseases, but it lacks rigorous clinical evidence for the treatment of PMPS. METHODS/DESIGN: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial will be conducted across three hospitals in China. A total of 100 perimenopausal women will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive JFP or placebo for 12 weeks, followed by a 4-week post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is the modified Kupperman Index (KI), assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16. Secondary outcomes include the Hot Flash scale (HFs), the Menopause-Specific Quality of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire, the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), the Vaginal Health Index Score (VHIS), and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) symptom score. Mechanistic outcomes encompass serum sex hormones and estrogen metabolites, inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), faecal β-glucuronidase (β-GUS) activity, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations. CONCLUSION: This is the first multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the molecular mechanism by which JFP ameliorate PMPS by reshaping the gut microbiota structure, modulating β-GUS activity, optimizing SCFAs metabolism, suppressing inflammatory responses, and maintaining estrogen homeostasis. The results of this trial will help us to evaluate the efficacy, safety and possible mechanism of JFP in treating PMPS. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The protocol (Version 3.0, dated November 19, 2025) was approved by the Ethics Committee of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (approval number: TJ-IRB202512083). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conference presentations. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07606755 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07606755).

fiche.verdict: Protocole d'essai évaluant l'efficacité et les mécanismes (microbiote, SCFAs) de la pilule Jinfeng dans le syndrome périménopausique.
fiche.population: 100 femmes périménopausées
fiche.intervention: Pilule Jinfeng versus placebo pendant 12 semaines.
resultats_cles: Mesure principale : Index de Kupperman modifié à 12 semaines.
Analyses mécanistiques : microbiote fécal, β-GUS, métabolisme des AGCC.
fiche.conclusion: Premier essai évaluant l'efficacité et les mécanismes de la pilule Jinfeng sur le syndrome périménopausique via le microbiote.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Lien microbiote et symptômes de la ménopause, mais traitement de phytothérapie chinoise hors pratique.
fiche.titre_court: Protocole Jinfeng en périménopause
fiche.conclusion_simple: Ce protocole rigoureux évaluera l'effet d'un traitement traditionnel sur la périménopause et le microbiote.

titre: Interoceptive mechanisms of body image disturbance in anorexia nervosa: Study protocol of a randomized parallel-group trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Current treatments for anorexia nervosa (AN), a dangerous psychiatric disorder, show only moderate efficacy. Interoceptive processing dysfunctions (i.e., how the brain receives and processes body afferents), and body image disturbance (BID) are clinical features of AN. Floatation-REST (Reduced Environmental Stimulation Therapy) has been reported to enhance both subjective interoceptive experiences and BID. The proposed project works to establish (1) how interoceptive processing dysfunctions may contribute to BID and (2) how the combination of Floatation-REST with psychotherapeutic principles may enhance interoceptive processing and BID in AN. METHODS: In this randomized parallel-group ( NCT06332963 ), single-site trial, 102 women and girls with AN will be recruited from an inpatient program. After completing baseline measurements, participants are randomized on a 1:1 ratio to receive either the interoceptively focused treatment (IFT) or exteroceptively focused treatment (EFT) condition. Both conditions utilize acceptance- and mindfulness-based principles, however incorporate skills that focus on interoception or exteroception, respectively. Participants complete acute measures following each experimental therapeutic session, as well as post intervention, six-week and six-month follow-up. The primary outcome of the current study is acute changes in BID assessed by the Photographic Figure Rating Scale. Additional outcomes include acute changes in interoception, and longitudinal intervention effects on self-reported, behavioral, and neuroimaging measures of AN symptoms, BID, and interoception. DISCUSSION: If interventions demonstrate reductions in BID, mechanisms of BID will be further understood, informing the development of future therapies for BID in AN.
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

fiche.verdict: Protocole d'essai randomisé évaluant l'effet de la thérapie par flottaison combinée à une approche intéroceptive vs extéroceptive dans l'anorexie.

fiche.intervention: Floatation-REST + thérapie focalisée sur l'intéroception (IFT) vs thérapie focalisée sur l'extéroception (EFT)

Suivi post-intervention, à 6 semaines et à 6 mois (mesures comportementales, auto-rapportées et neuro-imagerie).

titre: Effects of combining virtual nature exposure and hypnosis on quality of life in patients with hematologic malignancies undergoing hematopoietic cell transplant: Protocol for an efficacy trial
resume: INTRODUCTION: Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is a key treatment for patients with hematological malignancies, but often results in adverse effects that impact both physical and psychological well-being. This calls for the development of interventions aiming at reducing psychosocial impact of HCT. Among interventions, nature exposure appears promising and efficient via virtual reality. Combined to techniques increasing attention resources allocated to positive elements such as hypnosis, it could represent an innovative solution to preserve quality of life. Following the ORBIT model for the development of non-pharmacological interventions, this study constitutes a Phase IIc efficacy trial. It aims to evaluate the relative efficacy of an intervention combining virtual exposure to nature and hypnosis in patients with a hematological malignancy treated with HCT compared to observation only. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The intervention will consist of 2 to 3 weekly 30-min sessions over 2 weeks during aplasia following stem cell infusion, with immersive virtual nature exposure to environments (beach, forest) combined with hypnosis. Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to an intervention or control group. Participants in the intervention group will receive sessions between day +7 and day +21 after HCT. Primary outcome will be the change in quality of life from T1 to T2. PERSPECTIVES: The results of this study will be highly relevant to determine the efficacy of a non-invasive and cost-effective intervention aimed at preserving QoL in patients treated with HCT. Demonstrating its efficacy will pave the way for further development and implementation of a future Phase III randomized controlled trial. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The project was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of Hôpital Maisonneuve-Rosemont (Project no 2026-4116). Participants will be asked to provide written consent for their participation. Results from this study will be shared through peer-reviewed publications, as well as oral and poster presentations at scientific events. The protocol for this study was preregistered on ISRCTN and raw anonymized data will be available on Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/n598j). TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN42049015 (date of registration: November 6th, 2025). PROTOCOL VERSION: 1 (01/11/2025).

fiche.verdict: Protocole d'essai évaluant l'association de la nature virtuelle et de l'hypnose pour préserver la qualité de vie en oncologie.
fiche.population: Patients atteints de malignités hématologiques traités par greffe de cellules souches (HCT)
fiche.intervention: Immersion en nature virtuelle combinée à l'hypnose (2-3 séances/semaine) versus observation seule
resultats_cles: Protocole d'intervention non pharmacologique ciblant le bien-être psychosocial en phase d'aplasie.
Mesure principale : évolution de la qualité de vie entre T1 et T2.
Intervention courte (30 min par séance sur 2 semaines).
fiche.conclusion: Cette étude déterminera l'efficacité d'une approche combinant réalité virtuelle et hypnose pour préserver la qualité de vie.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Très pertinent pour les applications cliniques de l'hypnose et de la distraction attentive en contexte médical lourd.
fiche.titre_court: Nature virtuelle et hypnose en greffe (Protocole)
fiche.conclusion_simple: Ce protocole teste l'intérêt d'associer hypnose et nature virtuelle pour soutenir les patients immunodéprimés.

titre: [Delayed diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome in a patient with psychiatric illness]
resume: In this case report, a 24-year-old woman diagnosed with psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, OCD and presumably a schizotypical disorder presented with symptoms of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The patient had a history of somatisation, which is why her symptoms were initially overlooked. After several contacts to the emergency department, the patient was hospitalised after finding bilateral lung embolisms. The patient deteriorated quickly and suffered shortly from hypoxic cardiac arrest. Whilst she was in the ICU, she was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome.

fiche.verdict: Un diagnostic de syndrome de Guillain-Barré a été retardé en raison d'antécédents psychiatriques (anxiété, TOC) et de somatisation.
fiche.population: Patiente de 24 ans avec troubles anxieux, TOC et antécédents de somatisation
resultats_cles: Symptômes initiaux de Guillain-Barré attribués à tort à des troubles psychiatriques
Détérioration rapide avec arrêt cardiaque hypoxique après embolie pulmonaire
Diagnostic posé secondairement en unité de soins intensifs
fiche.conclusion: Les antécédents psychiatriques peuvent masquer des pathologies neurologiques graves et retarder le diagnostic.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Rappel clinique sur le risque d'errance diagnostique en cas de comorbidité psy.
fiche.titre_court: Guillain-Barré masqué par des troubles psychiatriques
fiche.conclusion_simple: Attention au diagnostic hâtif de somatisation chez les patients anxieux ou TOC masquant une urgence médicale.

titre: Gut Microbiota Profiles in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome and Their Relationship to Clinical Efficacy of Hangeshashinto: The GMIBS-HA Study
resume: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify specific microbiota associated with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) and to evaluate clinical improvement in IBS-D according to changes in gut microbiota abundance following treatment with Hangeshashinto (HST), an anti-inflammatory Kampo medicine. METHODS: This post-hoc retrospective analysis included 20 IBS-D patients from a previous study in whom gut microbiota had been analyzed. Patients were enrolled at two affiliated institutions between March and December 2023 and received HST 7.5 g/day for 2-3 weeks. Gut microbiota of IBS-D patients were compared with those of 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Differences in microbiota before and after HST administration between effective and non-effective cases were also analyzed. RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, IBS-D patients showed significant differences in alpha diversity (Faith's PD, p=0.016) and beta diversity (unweighted p=0.006; weighted p=0.031). Taxonomic analysis demonstrated increased Escherichia-Shigella (p=0.003, q (Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction)=0.035) and decreased Faecalibacterium (p=0.005, q=0.035). In the comparison of pre-HST microbiota between 14 effective and 6 non-effective cases, significant increase of Escherichia-Shigella (p<0.001, q=0.014) and significant decrease of Fusobacterium (p=0.004, q=0.019) and Lactobacillus (p=0.002, q=0.014) were observed in non-effective cases. Regarding changes in bacterial abundance from pre- to post-HST administration, differences at the nominal p-value were observed for a decrease in Escherichia-Shigella (p=0.049, q=0.343) and an increase in Faecalibacterium (p=0.012, q=0.168) in non-effective cases compared with effective cases. CONCLUSIONS: Characteristic microbiota profiles of IBS-D were identified. Significant differences in bacterial abundance before HST administration were observed between effective and non-effective cases.
revue: Journal of the anus, rectum and colon

fiche.verdict: Le microbiote des patients IBS-D diffère des contrôles, avec des profils bactériens basaux distincts selon la réponse au traitement par HST.
fiche.population: 20 patients avec syndrome de l'intestin irritable à prédominance de diarrhée (IBS-D) et 20 contrôles sains
fiche.intervention: Médecine Kampo (Hangeshashinto, HST) 7,5 g/jour pendant 2 à 3 semaines
resultats_cles: Alpha et bêta diversité significativement différentes entre IBS-D et contrôles.
Augmentation d'Escherichia-Shigella et diminution de Faecalibacterium dans l'IBS-D.
Excès initial d'Escherichia-Shigella chez les non-répondeurs au traitement par HST.
fiche.conclusion: Des profils microbiotiques caractéristiques de l'IBS-D existent et diffèrent selon la réponse clinique à la phytothérapie HST.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Apporte des données biologiques sur le microbiote dans l'IBS-D, utile pour la compréhension globale de l'axe intestin-cerveau.
fiche.titre_court: Microbiote et réponse au traitement dans l'IBS-D
fiche.conclusion_simple: Le profil du microbiote intestinal varie dans l'IBS-D et pourrait influencer la réponse aux traitements anti-inflammatoires.

titre: Age- and Sex-related Differences in the Prevalence of Perianal Manual Compression Method Use and the Method's Clinical Effectiveness in Patients with Evacuation Difficulty
resume: OBJECTIVES: The perianal manual compression method (PMCM) is a form of pelvic floor support used to facilitate defecation. Although PMCM is included in the Rome IV diagnostic criteria for functional constipation as a manual maneuver to facilitate defecation, it has rarely been investigated. This study aimed to investigate age- and sex-related differences in the prevalence of PMCM use and to evaluate its clinical effectiveness in patients with evacuation difficulty (ED). METHODS: A retrospective survey of 1,400 patients scheduled for hemorrhoid surgery, stratified by age and sex, was conducted to assess the prevalence of PMCM use. In addition, the clinical effectiveness of PMCM was retrospectively evaluated in patients with ED. RESULTS: Of 1,380 eligible patients, 94 (6.8%) reported using PMCM. PMCM use was significantly more common in women than in men (9.1% vs. 4.5%, p = 0.0006) and increased with age, particularly in those aged >50 years. Sixty-two patients with ED (median age: 77 years; 30 men) received standardized instruction in PMCM. Of them, 55 were also prescribed laxatives, but 12 did not use PMCM because their symptoms improved with laxatives alone. Of the remaining 50 patients, PMCM was effective in 35 (70%), with 22 (44%) showing marked improvement. The median follow-up period was 2.0 months, and no adverse events related to PMCM were observed. CONCLUSION: PMCM is a simple and noninvasive maneuver that may represent a useful adjunctive therapy for patients with ED who are refractory to laxative therapy.
revue: Journal of the anus, rectum and colon

fiche.verdict: La compression manuelle périnéale est une technique simple et utile pour soulager les difficultés d'évacuation réfractaires aux laxatifs.
fiche.population: 1 380 patients inclus (dont 94 utilisateurs de PMCM et 62 avec difficulté d'évacuation traités)
fiche.intervention: Instruction standardisée à la méthode de compression manuelle périnéale (PMCM) pour les difficultés d'évacuation
resultats_cles: Prévalence globale de l'usage de la PMCM : 6,8% (plus fréquente chez les femmes : 9,1% vs 4,5%, p = 0,0006)
Efficacité de la PMCM chez 70% des 50 patients évalués (amélioration marquée chez 44%)
Aucun effet indésirable rapporté sur un suivi médian de 2 mois
fiche.conclusion: La PMCM est une thérapie d'appoint simple et non invasive pour les patients ayant des difficultés d'évacuation réfractaires aux laxatifs.
limites: Biais de sélection (patients de chirurgie proctologique)
fiche.pertinence_raison: Utile pour la prise en charge des troubles de la défécation en gastroentérologie.
fiche.titre_court: Compression manuelle périnéale et constipation
fiche.conclusion_simple: La compression manuelle périnéale est une option non invasive efficace pour certains patients souffrant de difficultés d'évacuation.

titre: Gut Microbiome Alterations in Alzheimer's Disease: A Shotgun Metagenomic Case-Control Study
resume: The gut microbiome has been proposed as a contributor to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis via the microbiota-gut-brain axis, but findings across cohorts are inconsistent and scarce data exist from Central Asian populations. We used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiome of AD patients and cognitively healthy controls from Kazakhstan. In a cross-sectional case-control study (35 AD, 39 Control), we profiled taxonomic and functional (HUMAnN pathway) composition, and compared alpha/beta diversity, individual taxa and pathways, and their association with clinical and demographic variables (Mann-Whitney U test, PERMANOVA/PERMDISP, OLS regression, all BH-FDR corrected, sensitivity analysis using ANCOM-BC2), with sensitivity analyses adjusting for age and BMI and applying Bonferroni correction. Within the AD group, circulating adiponectin-measured only in this group-was examined for associations with microbiome features in an exploratory analysis. Alpha diversity was lower in AD (q < 0.05). Community composition also separated by group on PERMANOVA (R2 = 8.6%, p = 0.001), and this separation held after adjusting for age and BMI. A total of 178 taxa differed significantly between groups (BH-FDR; 37 were also Bonferroni-significant), most prominently depletion of Faecalibacterium and enrichment of Eisenbergiella and Desulfovibrio in AD; 100 pathways differed significantly (20 Bonferroni-significant). Three clinical/demographic variables (total bilirubin, atherogenic index, BMI) were associated with specific taxa or pathways. Within the AD group, adiponectin correlated negatively with the pathway assimilatory sulfate reduction IV (rho = -0.60, q = 0.015). AD in this Central Asian cohort was associated with a less diverse, compositionally distinct gut microbiome, with depletion of butyrate-producing Firmicutes and enrichment of sulfate-reducing taxa, alongside other taxa whose direction of association differed from prior reports.

fiche.verdict: Le microbiote intestinal des patients atteints de la maladie d'Alzheimer présente une diversité réduite et des altérations taxonomiques.
fiche.population: 35 patients Alzheimer et 35 témoins sains
fiche.intervention: Comparaison du microbiote fécal par séquençage métagénomique shotgun
resultats_cles: Alpha-diversité significativement plus faible dans le groupe Alzheimer (q < 0,05)
178 taxons et 100 voies métaboliques significativement différents entre les groupes
Épuisement de Faecalibacterium et enrichissement d'Eisenbergiella et Desulfovibrio chez les patients
fiche.conclusion: La maladie d'Alzheimer est associée à un microbiote intestinal moins diversifié et compositionnellement distinct dans cette cohorte.
limites: Design transversal ne prouvant pas la causalité
fiche.pertinence_raison: Axé sur l'axe intestin-cerveau, mais ciblant la pathologie d'Alzheimer.
fiche.titre_court: Microbiote et maladie d'Alzheimer
fiche.conclusion_simple: Le microbiote des patients Alzheimer présente des dysbioses spécifiques, sans lien causal établi à ce stade.

titre: Sex-Related Differences in Regional Homogeneity and Intolerance of Uncertainty in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Resting-State fMRI Study
resume: BACKGROUND: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is a cognitive vulnerability associated with symptom severity in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Evidence also suggests that IU and OCD symptom profiles may differ by sex; however, the neural correlates of IU in male and female patients with OCD remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: In this cross-sectional observational study, 63 patients with OCD and 40 healthy controls (HCs) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Regional homogeneity (ReHo) was used to examine diagnosis- and sex-related differences in intrinsic brain activity. Imaging data were analyzed using a full-factorial model in SPM, with diagnosis and sex as factors and age, years of education, and mean framewise displacement (FD) as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 followed by cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction at p < 0.05. Significant effects were characterized using post hoc contrasts. Four exploratory partial correlations controlling for age, years of education, and mean FD were examined; their p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The final sample comprised 63 patients with OCD (37 males and 26 females) and 40 HCs (25 males and 15 females). Patients with OCD showed lower ReHo in visual processing regions, including the right calcarine cortex and right middle occipital gyrus, compared with HCs. Across diagnostic groups, the whole-brain factorial analysis revealed a significant main effect of sex, with males showing higher ReHo in visual and sensorimotor regions and females showing higher ReHo in prefrontal regions. No significant diagnosis-by-sex interaction was observed. Exploratory partial correlations showed that higher IU was associated with lower ReHo in the left inferior frontal gyrus in the female OCD, and that lower ReHo in the right middle occipital gyrus was associated with greater obsession severity in the overall OCD sample. These uncorrected associations are preliminary and hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest potential sex-related differences in regional neural synchrony in OCD and identify an exploratory association between IU and left inferior frontal gyrus ReHo within the female OCD subgroup. Given the cross-sectional observational design, these findings should be interpreted as associative and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of distinct sex-specific neural mechanisms.

titre: Impact of Climate Change on Gastrointestinal Health
resume: Climate change is increasingly endangering gastrointestinal (GI) health. Heat stress, rising temperatures, extreme weather, humidity changes, food insecurity, air pollution, environmental contaminants, and vector-borne diseases contribute to GI disorders through mechanisms like epithelial barrier dysfunction, immune activation, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Climate-driven changes in food and water systems increase the spread of enteric infections, viral hepatitis, and parasitic diseases, while disruptions to agriculture reduce food security and nutrient availability. Air pollutants, microplastics, heavy metals, and mycotoxins further impact GI health. These exposures are linked to inflammatory bowel disease, disorders of gut-brain interaction, GI cancers, and liver disease, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations.
revue: Gastrointestinal endoscopy clinics of North America

titre: Severe Chronic Constipation and Fecaloma in a Patient With Partial Agenesis of the Corpus Callosum: A Case Report
resume: Symptoms of functional constipation are associated with dysregulation of the brain-gut axis (BGA). BGA stands as a framework that accounts for the bidirectional interaction between the central nervous system (CNS), autonomic nervous system (ANS), and the enteric nervous system (ENS). Considering these interactions, the brain (CNS) becomes central to bowel movement/defecation. Consequently, it becomes evident why conditions of the CNS or impacts on the CNS could lead to functional constipation. This case report highlights the intricate relationship between the CNS and GI motility via the BGA. The clinical presentation of partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and refractory fecaloma demonstrates an association between structural neurological deficits and impaired visceral sensory processing, though further studies/investigation are needed to establish a causal link (direct) to the patient's disrupted ability or physiological urge to defecate. Acute management, such as manual evacuation, can be necessary in severe chronic constipation with fecaloma to prevent life-threatening stercoral perforation. Additionally, long-term management of neurogenic constipation should evolve beyond a standard approach. Individualized management strategies could be considered, which may involve transitioning from an urge-based to a time-based defecation routine, alongside adjuncts like prokinetic agents (e.g., prucalopride) and regular abdominal massage.

titre: Rationale and design of the Cardiac MRI and Biological Samples in the Acute Phase of ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction study (the CARAMBOLE study)
resume: BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) can lead to complications such as no-reflow/microvascular obstruction (MVO) and left ventricular remodeling (LVR), both with major prognostic impact. Inflammation is central to these mechanisms, and gut dysbiosis may amplify it through elevated trimethylamine N-oxide and lipopolysaccharides. A multiparametric strategy integrating cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), microbiome profiling and immuno-inflammatory biomarkers may improve the understanding and prediction of these complications. METHODS: CARAMBOLE is a prospective, single-centre translational cohort study. From March 2024 to July 2025, 150 consecutive STEMI patients at Poitiers University Hospital were included. Eligible patients (≥18 years, confirmed STEMI, informed consent, no CMR contraindication) underwent serial blood sampling and biobanking (plasma, serum, PBMCs, DNA, RNA) at admission, 24 h and 48 h. Faecal and urinary sampling for gut and genitourinary microbiome characterisation, standardised questionnaires (lifestyle, quality of life, cognitive assessment), echocardiography, and CMR were performed during the acute phase and repeated at 1-year follow-up. The primary objective is to identify clinical, biological and imaging biomarkers associated with 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, heart-failure hospitalisation), adjudicated by an independent blinded committee. Multi-omic analyses (shotgun metagenomics, targeted metabolomics, high-plex inflammatory proteomics) are pre-specified as exploratory and several are contingent on additional funding. CONCLUSIONS: This multiparametric, translational cohort will provide new mechanistic and epidemiological insights into the relationships among dysbiosis, inflammation, and CMR markers (no-reflow/MVO, infarct size, LVR), with the goal of generating prognostic biomarker hypotheses to be validated in larger, multicentre cohorts.
revue: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

titre: Interoception and the negative self-evaluation bias of one's own speech in adults who stutter
resume: BACKGROUND: Stuttering, a speech fluency disorder, is often accompanied by psychological difficulties, such as social anxiety. We hypothesize that adults who stutter (AWS) may experience a negative self-evaluation bias, where they over-focus on even minor disfluencies that listeners may not notice, resulting in an unfairly low self-rating of their speech. This heightened self-focus could be linked to interoception, the ability to perceive internal bodily states. This study aimed to quantitatively verify this self-evaluation bias and is the first to examine its relationship with interoceptive accuracy in this population. METHODS: Nineteen AWS and 39 fluent speakers (FS) participated. An evaluation gap (listener average score minus self-rated score) was calculated using a semantic differential scale for speech evaluation. Interoceptive accuracy (IAc), social anxiety, subjective impact of stuttering (OASES), and objective stuttering rate were also assessed. RESULTS: Both groups showed a significant evaluation gap (self < listener). Across the entire sample, IAc, social anxiety, rater group, and age were significant predictors of this gap. Specifically, the gap in AWS was associated with IAc, OASES, and stuttering rate, whereas in FS, it was related to IAc, social anxiety, age, and rater group. A subsequent path analysis showed that OASES mediated the effect of social anxiety and age on this gap in AWS. CONCLUSION: Higher interoceptive accuracy linked to negatively biased self-evaluation suggests that heightened accuracy in perceiving internal physiological cues-such as respiratory or articulatory effort-is associated with negative self-evaluation. This highlights the importance of interoception in the negative impact associated with stuttering.

titre: Take no risk!-Persistent avoidance after interoceptive fear conditioning
resume: Maladaptive fear and avoidance of interoceptive threat are central to many anxiety and somatic disorders, often persisting even after exposure therapy and thereby contributing to relapse. While fear conditioning paradigms have mostly focused on avoidance in response to external threats (e.g., electric shocks), less is known about avoidance in response to interoceptive threat. Therefore, the present study investigated fear acquisition of interoceptive threat and subsequent avoidance behavior. Healthy participants (n = 35) underwent a differential fear conditioning paradigm in which one cue (CS+) predicted restricted breathing (US), whereas another (CS-) signaled safety. In the subsequent avoidance phase, participants were informed that they could prevent the US by pressing a button. During the consecutive response prevention phase, the avoidance option was no longer available. Finally, an avoidance test assessed the persistence of avoidance after extinction. No US was delivered during avoidance and response prevention phases. Results suggests that participants successfully learned to discriminate between CS+ and CS-, as reflected in US expectancy, fear ratings, startle eyeblink response and skin conductance responses. Although participants consistently reported greater fear of the CS + than the CS-, differential responding in psychophysiological measures was no longer observed following the introduction of the avoidance option. Participants demonstrated high levels of avoidance to CS+ and CS-, with avoidance persisting even after extinction with response prevention. The findings indicate a "better-safe-than-sorry" strategy despite awareness of threat contingencies. The generalization and persistence of avoidance may contribute to the development and maintenance of anxiety and somatic disorders.
