titre: Effect of Adverse Childhood Experiences on Nonsuicidal Self-Injury in Adolescents With Mood Disorders
resume: BACKGROUND: Nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a severe global health concern, particularly among adolescents, and is closely associated with adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). However, the underlying mechanisms by which ACEs are associated with NSSI remain largely unknown, although peer attachment and alexithymia have been identified as potentially relevant to this relationship. This observational study aimed to test a chain mediation model examining the indirect associations among ACEs, peer attachment, alexithymia, and NSSI in adolescents with mood disorders. METHODS: A total of 363 adolescents with mood disorders were recruited from the outpatient clinical psychology department of a general hospital. Clinical interview tools and self-report questionnaires were used to evaluate patients' history of NSSI, ACEs, peer attachment, and alexithymia. Comparisons were made between groups of patients who did and did not meet the criteria for NSSI diagnosis, and peer attachment and alexithymia were evaluated for potential mediating effects. RESULTS: In total, 203 (55.9%) patients were included in the NSSI group. In the chain mediation model, ACEs were directly associated with NSSI, with a significant effect size of 0.246 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.088, 0.404), accounting for 64.2% of the total effect. Peer attachment and alexithymia had a total indirect effect of 0.137 (95% CI: 0.079, 0.221), accounting for 35.8% of the total effect. CONCLUSIONS: In addition to reaffirming the direct association between ACEs and NSSI, this study provides novel insight into a chain of indirect associations linking peer attachment and alexithymia to the ACE-NSSI relationship.

titre: Do you feel your body right now? Ecological momentary assessment of interoceptive intensity and valence across multiple domains in everyday life
resume: Researchers usually assess interoception (i.e., the perception of inner bodily states) under laboratory conditions, once, with a focus on one organ, mostly the heart. The present study expands this research and presents findings from two independent studies, demonstrating the reliability and validity of an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) approach to study interoception in different modalities at the very same time from a subjective perspective. We asked more than 250 participants to rate how intensely they feel their heart, gut, and breath at random moments in everyday life, as a measure of interoceptive attention. We further assessed the appraisal of these interoceptive body sensations by means of valence ratings. Across two samples (N1 = 141, N2 = 112), we demonstrated high reliability of this assessment at the between-person level and modest reliability at the within-person level. We further examined convergent and divergent validity for both subjective measures. The study findings highlight promising psychometric properties and applicability of this novel assessment of ambulatory interoception. This method enables large-scale field studies to investigate interoceptive attention and appraisal on a momentary basis to understand the role of bodily sensations in daily functioning and health.

titre: Comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in China (CAMPUS): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials
resume: UNLABELLED: University students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. This protocol describes the Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mental Health Program for University Students in China (CAMPUS), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal AI and multi-omics studies across seven Chinese universities. Longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at Henan Medical University in September 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. Multidimensional screening integrates psychological self-report (PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI, BSI-CV, and others), physiological measurements (EEG, MRI, fNIRS, HRV, eye tracking, facial-expression analysis, ERP, voice acoustics), and an exploratory biospecimen component for multi-omics profiling, potentially including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome analyses, subject to the finalization and approval of layer-specific protocols. Students identified through cohort screening as potentially eligible for an intervention trial will undergo trial-specific eligibility assessment. Those who meet the eligibility criteria and provide trial-specific informed consent will be individually randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or its comparator within one of eight separate two-arm, multi-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trials. A Transformer-based multimodal AI framework with SHAP-based feature attribution will be developed and internally evaluated for questionnaire-defined risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. The initial Henan Medical University cohort recruitment and university-student mental-health assessment were approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Henan Medical University (XYLL-20250484), and written informed consent is obtained from participants before enrolment. Each additional participating center will obtain local ethics approval before study activation. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences, and policy briefs, providing evidence that may inform the design and prospective evaluation of youth mental-health programs in other university settings. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The two clinical trials were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR). The registration details and URLs are as follows: ChiCTR2500113527: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298271; ChiCTR2500113613: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298268.

titre: Animation-assisted psychological intervention in pediatric care: mechanisms, clinical applications, and emerging evidence
resume: Children frequently experience fear, anxiety, and pain during medical encounters, and this distress can lead to poor cooperation, longer procedures, and lasting avoidance of care. Animation, delivered as cartoons, preparation films, applications, serious games, and virtual reality (VR) scenes, has become one of the most widely deployed non-pharmacological adjuncts in pediatric settings because it is inexpensive, non-invasive, and easily standardized. Drawing on a structured search of six databases through July 2026, this mini-review synthesizes randomized and meta-analytic evidence across perioperative anxiety, procedural pain, pediatric dentistry, chronic-disease self-management, and mental health promotion. It organizes the evidence around five psychological pathways: attentional competition, observational learning, exposure and inhibitory learning, narrative-affective processing, and self-efficacy. Additionally, it examines a sixth, non-psychological use in which animation is used to provide therapeutic visual stimulation. Evidence supports moderate short-term benefits for anticipatory anxiety and for needle- and dentistry-related distress, with weaker and less consistent effects for high-intensity procedures and physiological outcomes. We argue that the field's core issue is conceptual rather than empirical: animation refers to a delivery medium, not a treatment, and trials have compared media rather than mechanisms. This obscures three unresolved problems: discordance between self-reported and autonomic outcomes; an untheorized moderating role of the developmental stage; and a theoretical tension between distraction, which withdraws attention from the feared stimulus, and exposure, which requires engagement with it. Mechanism-matched comparators, core outcome sets, developmentally stratified designs, transparent intervention reporting, and follow-up across repeated procedures are prerequisites for cumulative progress.

titre: Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions for reducing dental anxiety and improving behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients: a systematic review with GRADE assessment
resume: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Dental anxiety affects an estimated 9%-20% of children and disproportionately impacts those with neurodevelopmental conditions. Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions, which intentionally modulate auditory, visual, tactile, olfactory, or proprioceptive input, have emerged as promising approaches for anxiety and behaviour management in paediatric dentistry, but no published review has applied formal GRADE certainty assessment across multiple sensory-based modalities. This review evaluated the effectiveness of sensory-based interventions for dental anxiety and behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients (≤18 years) and assessed certainty of evidence using GRADE. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: RCTs and controlled clinical trials involving paediatric participants (≤18 years) evaluating sensory-based interventions delivered during dental treatment or as pre-visit preparation, reporting dental anxiety, behavioural cooperation, or physiological stress, were eligible for GRADE assessment; eligible non-randomised, observational, pilot, feasibility, descriptive, and secondary studies were retained for narrative synthesis only. Studies of exclusively pharmacological or non-sensory cognitive-behavioural interventions were excluded. METHODS: MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus, Embase, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 27 July 2026, supplemented by manual reference screening and Google Scholar searches. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment (RoB 2), and GRADE assessment. Given substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. RESULTS: Of 2,002 records identified, 47 studies met inclusion criteria: 25 RCTs/controlled crossover trials contributing to GRADE assessment, and 22 non-randomised, pilot, observational, or secondary studies retained for narrative synthesis. Nine modalities were evaluated: sensory-adapted dental environments (SADE), audiovisual distraction/virtual reality (VR), music therapy, aromatherapy, weighted blankets, social stories, video modelling, visual pedagogy, and emerging sensory-based approaches. SADE, audiovisual distraction/VR, and music therapy showed the most consistent improvements in anxiety, cooperation, physiological stress, and pain, supported by moderate-certainty evidence for SADE and audiovisual distraction/VR; for music therapy, the direct paediatric primary-trial base is now a single GRADE-eligible RCT following reclassification of Chen and Hawkins (2021) to Tier 2 as a single-arm pilot without a concurrent comparator; certainty for music-therapy anxiety reduction is correspondingly rated low, supported by corroborating secondary meta-analyses. Certainty across modalities ranged from very low to moderate, limited by risk of bias, heterogeneity, inconsistent outcome measures, and imprecision. [Table: see text]. CONCLUSIONS: Sensory-based interventions show promising benefit for dental anxiety and behavioural cooperation in paediatric dental care, with the strongest (moderate-certainty) evidence for SADE and audiovisual distraction/VR, and low-to-moderate-certainty evidence for music therapy. Overall certainty remains low to moderate, supporting cautious, individualised clinical use rather than routine first-line implementation. Adequately powered trials with standardised outcomes, prospective registration, and GRADE-informed reporting are needed to strengthen the evidence base.Systematic Review Registration: identifier CRD420261456366.

titre: Effect of mindfulness breathing versus acupoint stimulation on anxiety, fatigue, and sleep quality among children undergoing stem cell transplantation: a three-arm randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Children undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) commonly experience anxiety, fatigue, and sleep disturbances, which may negatively affect their quality of life and recovery. Non-pharmacological interventions, including mindfulness breathing and acupoint stimulation, have emerged as supportive approaches for symptom management. AIM: This study evaluated and compared the effects of mindfulness breathing, acupoint stimulation, and routine care on anxiety, fatigue, and sleep quality among children undergoing HSCT. METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted at the stem cell transplantation unit of Tanta University Hospitals, Egypt. Ninety children aged 7-17 years were randomly assigned to three equal groups: control (routine care), mindfulness breathing, and acupoint stimulation. The assigned interventions were delivered once daily for seven consecutive days before transplantation and continued for one month after transplantation. Anxiety, fatigue, and sleep disturbance were assessed using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Children, Fatigue Severity Scale, and PROMIS Parent Proxy Sleep Disturbance Scale, respectively. Assessments were conducted at baseline, one week, and one month after intervention. RESULTS: Baseline sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were comparable among the three groups. Significant Group×Time interactions were observed for diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, pulse rate, anxiety, fatigue severity, and sleep disturbance scores (p < 0.001). Both mindfulness breathing and acupoint stimulation resulted in significant improvements compared with routine care. Mindfulness breathing demonstrated greater improvements across several physiological and psychological outcomes compared with acupoint stimulation and routine care. CONCLUSION: Mindfulness breathing and acupoint stimulation are promising complementary interventions for improving physiological and psychological outcomes among children undergoing HSCT. Mindfulness breathing showed greater improvements across several outcomes and may represent a useful supportive nursing intervention during the transplantation period. Further multicenter studies with longer follow-up are recommended to confirm the sustained effects of these interventions. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The Pan African Clinical Trial Registry PACTR 202407894821147. Date: 17 July 2024. www.http://pactr.samrc.ac.za.

titre: Baseline gut microbiota and short-term response to acupressure combined with thermal stimulation in maintenance hemodialysis patients with functional constipation: an exploratory responder analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Constipation is common in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), and individual responses to non-pharmacological interventions may vary substantially. This exploratory study investigated whether baseline gut microbiota characteristics were associated with short-term response to acupressure combined with thermal stimulation in MHD patients with functional constipation. METHODS: This responder analysis was based on a randomized two-sequence crossover study. Clinical data and fecal samples obtained immediately before each participant entered the 14-day intervention period were analyzed. Participants with an increase of ≥1 bowel movement (BM) per week were classified as responders (R), and those with <1 BM/week as non-responders (NR). Baseline gut microbiota were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and genus-level differential abundance were evaluated. ANCOM-BC2 was performed with adjustment for baseline BM/week, sex, and diabetes mellitus, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction and pseudocount sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Twenty-six participants were included, of whom 9 (34.6%) met the predefined response criterion. Across all participants, weekly BM frequency increased from 1.25 (1.00, 1.50) to 2.00 (1.00, 3.00) (P = 0.0003), while PAC-SYM total and stool-symptom subscale scores decreased (P = 0.0011 and P = 0.0013, respectively). Alpha-diversity did not differ significantly between R and NR groups, and beta-diversity showed no overall community separation (ANOSIM R=-0.044, P = 0.6751). Lactonifactor was nominally higher in responders in the unadjusted analysis (P = 0.015) but was not significant after multiple-testing correction (FDR = 0.86). In adjusted ANCOM-BC2 analysis, Veillonella (β=5.319, FDR = 0.0347) and Lactobacillus (β=3.621, FDR = 0.0459) were associated with responder status; however, neither association was robust to pseudocount sensitivity analysis. PICRUSt2 identified no significant between-group differences in predicted functional pathways. CONCLUSION: Baseline microbial diversity and community structure were similar between responders and non-responders. Veillonella and Lactobacillus showed adjusted associations with response, but neither was robust in sensitivity analysis. These findings should therefore be regarded as exploratory rather than predictive. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and determine their clinical relevance.
revue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

titre: Phenotype-informed selection of microbiota-directed interventions in irritable bowel syndrome: current evidence and limitations
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a heterogeneous disorder of gut-brain interaction in which bowel-habit subtype, dominant symptoms, post-infectious onset, bile-acid handling, visceral sensitivity, and diet-microbiota interactions may influence the treatment response. This narrative mini-review asks whether available clinical evidence is sufficient to select or sequence microbiota-directed and microbiota-modulating interventions according to Rome bowel-habit subtype and clinically observable dominant symptoms. Literature was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and major guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and pivotal trials published through June 2026. Evidence was interpreted at the level of the exact intervention or product, studied population, target outcome, consistency, independent replication, safety, and guideline position. Mechanistic data support plausible links through fermentation, epithelial barrier function, mucosal immunity, bile-acid metabolism, visceral sensitivity, and gut-brain signaling, but mechanistic or microbiome changes do not establish the clinical efficacy. Rifaximin has the clearest replicated and guideline-supported role in IBS with diarrhea, while soluble fiber has guideline support for global or constipation-associated symptoms. Evidence for individual probiotics, postbiotics, partially hydrolyzed guar gum, galactooligosaccharides, and fermented matrices remains product-specific or emerging and is rarely independently replicated. Symptom improvement with a diet low in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (low-FODMAP diet) does not establish microbiota mediation. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and microbiome-guided prescribing remain investigational. Current evidence, therefore, supports only limited phenotype-informed matching and does not establish a validated treatment sequence or microbiome-defined therapeutic phenotype.

titre: A Hairy Tail of Rapunzel Syndrome: A Video Case Report of the Laparoscopic Management of a Giant Trichobezoar Causing Gastric Outlet Obstruction
resume: Trichobezoars are rare gastrointestinal concretions formed by accumulated ingested hair, occurring predominantly in young women with trichotillomania and trichophagia. Extension beyond the pylorus into the small bowel defines Rapunzel syndrome, which may present with gastric outlet obstruction. We report a 25-year-old woman with a three-year history of progressive weight loss, early satiety, postprandial vomiting, and iron-deficiency anaemia. Oesophago-gastro-duodenoscopy and computed tomography revealed a giant gastric trichobezoar extending to the distal duodenum. After two unsuccessful endoscopic extraction attempts, laparoscopic gastrotomy with en bloc extraction of a 38-cm, 220-g trichobezoar (weighed without the retrieval bag or container) with a 14-cm duodenal tail was performed. Recovery was uneventful; postoperative contrast study showed no leak or obstruction. At three months, the patient was asymptomatic, gaining weight, and engaged in cognitive behavioural therapy. Laparoscopic gastrotomy is feasible for giant trichobezoars when adequate exposure and contained extraction can be achieved. Concurrent psychiatric assessment and ongoing psychological care are essential to prevent recurrence.

titre: Sodium oxybate with reduced-dose propofol for anesthesia induction in elective spine surgery: a randomized trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Sodium oxybate has an established sedative action, but its contribution to contemporary propofol-based anesthesia remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated induction hemodynamics, propofol use, bispectral index (BIS), and early recovery in elective spine surgery. METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial, 127 patients received propofol alone (P; n = 62) or propofol plus sodium oxybate (PS; n = 65). Planned induction doses were propofol 2.2 versus 1.2 mg/kg, with oxybate 30 mg/kg in PS; recorded propofol doses were lower in both groups. The primary outcome was the mean arterial pressure (MAP) trajectory across 13 induction landmarks. Maximum-likelihood mixed models were supplemented by unstructured-covariance and baseline-adjusted analyses. RESULTS: The primary group-by-time interaction was not significant (P = 0.607; unstructured covariance, P = 0.719). The baseline-adjusted average post-baseline MAP difference was 1.7 mmHg (PS minus P; 95% confidence interval [CI], -2.0-5.5). Systolic-pressure-defined hypotension occurred in 37/62 versus 32/65 patients (risk ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.60-1.14; risk difference, -10.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -26.8-6.7). Recorded total propofol use was 31.4% lower (751.3 versus 515.4 mg; difference, -235.9 mg; 95% CI, -366.0 to -105.9). Maintenance use was also lower under unblinded BIS-guided titration. Post-intubation BIS <40 occurred in 2/62 versus 22/65 patients. The mean surgery-end-to-extubation interval was 10.5 versus 13.6 min (difference, 3.1 min; 95% CI, 0.9-5.2), although both medians were 10 min. Vasoactive-treatment documentation was incomplete. CONCLUSIONS: The oxybate-containing strategy was associated with substantially lower propofol use, lower BIS values, and a longer mean extubation interval; hemodynamic superiority was not demonstrated. These findings define the observed effects and trade-offs of the combined regimen under BIS-guided care and inform further evaluation of dose selection, hypnosis monitoring, and recovery. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400080686.

titre: Dual-theoretical framework integrating the stress process model and family systems theory-based psychological intervention for caregivers of children and adolescents with mood disorders: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Globally, the prevalence of mood disorders among children and adolescents is rising, with the associated burden affecting patients, families, and society. Primary caregivers-mostly parents-experience sustained psychological stress and their mental health directly influences patients' treatment adherence and clinical outcomes. Despite this, research on interventions has predominantly focused on the caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. The caregivers of youth with mood disorders, particularly bipolar disorder, have been largely neglected. Moreover, theory-driven intervention programs for this population remain scarce. METHODS: Grounded in the stress process model and family systems theory, we developed a comprehensive psychological health intervention for caregivers of children and adolescents with mood disorders and designed a randomized controlled trial to evaluate its effectiveness. A total of 216 caregivers will be recruited and randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to either the intervention group receiving the theory-based program or the control group receiving routine psychological nursing and health education. Outcomes include anxiety, depression, parenting stress, coping style, family functioning, and self-efficacy. These will be assessed at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and at 1-month follow-up. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted within 2 weeks post-intervention to capture caregivers' lived experiences. DISCUSSION: Adhering to the SPIRIT guidelines, this protocol targets primary caregivers of children and adolescents with mood disorders, a critically important yet under-recognized population. Based on evidence synthesis, five caregiver needs identified in the scoping review have been consolidated into four theory-based intervention targets within the SPM-FST framework: cognitive adjustment and belief restructuring, emotion regulation and stress coping, parent-child communication and family functioning enhancement, and group mutual support and social support. The intervention will be delivered via face-to-face group sessions, and its effectiveness will be evaluated using a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative scales and qualitative interviews. If shown to be effective and feasible, this program may provide empirical evidence for developing multi-level family caregiver support systems. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2600123504.

titre: Exercise-induced hypoalgesia following HIIT: associations with cardiac interoceptive accuracy and the moderation by physical fitness
resume: INTRODUCTION: Exercise-induced hypoalgesia (EIH) refers to the reduction in pain perception following acute exercise, yet the roles of aerobic fitness and interoception in this response remain unclear. METHODS: This study investigated pain perception and cardiac interoceptive accuracy before and after high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in endurance athletes and non-athletes. Forty-one healthy adults (20 athletes, 21 non-athletes) completed a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test to determine VO₂max and self-report measures, including the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA). On a second study day, participants underwent pressure pain testing and a HBDT before and after HIIT. Training status was operationalized both categorically (athletes vs. non-athletes) and continuously (VO₂max). RESULTS: Athletes showed greater EIH than non-athletes, reflected in a significant reduction in pain following HIIT in athletes only and a larger pain change score compared with non-athletes. Higher VO₂max was likewise associated with greater pain reduction. Baseline cardiac interoceptive accuracy was positively associated with VO₂max, and interoceptive accuracy decreased significantly from pre- to post-exercise in both groups, with a more pronounced decline in athletes. MAIA scores showed no significant associations. VO₂max also significantly moderated the relation between post-exercise changes in cardiac interoceptive accuracy and pain reduction, suggesting that the link between interoceptive change and EIH differed as a function of aerobic fitness. DISCUSSION: From an adaptation-based, hormesis-informed perspective, the findings are compatible with a distinction between acute cost and longer-term adaptation: intense exercise may transiently reduce cardiac interoceptive accuracy, while repeated exposure may be associated with better baseline interoceptive accuracy and more effective post-exercise pain modulation.

titre: Dog-human gene network colocalization links synaptic signalling and ubiquitination to compulsive disorders
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is highly polygenic, and the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS), with 53,660 cases and 2,044,417 controls, identified only 30 loci, a small fraction of loci estimated to explain its heritability - too few to resolve biological pathways 1 . Pet dogs develop a compulsive disorder (dogCD) similar to OCD 2 . In a GWAS of dogCD with 2,584 dogs from the community science project Darwin's Ark, each dog locus explains at least 40-fold more phenotypic variance than each human OCD locus, giving power equivalent to the human GWAS with 80-fold fewer individuals. Combining the two GWAS identifies a 165-gene network undetectable in humans at current sample sizes. This network is enriched for genes expressed in neurons, particularly in the amygdala and cortex, and comprises four biological processes: excitatory-inhibitory synaptic transmission, axon guidance and neuron recognition, protein ubiquitination, and adenylyl cyclase-activating G-protein-coupled receptor signaling. Like most complex human traits 3 , dogCD risk is likely driven by regulatory variation: fine-mapped dogCD SNPs are non-coding, and dogCD loci are enriched in candidate cis-regulatory elements (cCREs) in a new dog epigenomic atlas spanning eight brain regions. The cross-species network implicates an inherited risk architecture largely outside current OCD pharmacotherapy, and establishes pet dogs as a model for gene network discovery, particularly for conditions underpowered in human studies.

titre: Recognizing Pelvic Venous Disease in Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Primary Care Case Report
resume: Chronic pelvic pain is a common and challenging condition with a broad differential diagnosis and a substantial impact on quality of life. Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay. A 42-year-old woman presented to a general and family medicine consultation with a six-year history of chronic pelvic pain, progressively worsening over the previous six months. She described persistent pressure-like pelvic pain, rated 7/10 in intensity, aggravated by prolonged standing and associated with severe deep dyspareunia, which prevented sexual intercourse, associated with low back pain radiating to the pelvis and both thighs, lower-limb heaviness, and significant sleep disturbance. She denied urinary symptoms or a relationship with the menstrual cycle. During the previous six years, she had undergone repeated medical assessments, with symptoms being attributed to recurrent gynecological infections, probable irritable bowel syndrome, and other non-specific causes. Previous investigations, including colonoscopy and emergency department assessments, had not identified a clear etiology for her symptoms. Physical examination revealed hypogastric tenderness and mild superficial lower-limb varicosities, without vulvar or perineal varices. Pelvic and lumbar computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral dilated periuterine veins measuring up to 13 mm, raising suspicion for a symptomatic pelvic venous disorder. The patient was referred to vascular surgery for further assessment; however, specialist evaluation remained pending at the time of manuscript revision. Pelvic venous disease should be considered in women with persistent pelvic pain, particularly when symptoms worsen with prolonged standing or sexual intercourse and are accompanied by low back pain or lower-limb heaviness. The absence of vulvar varices or previous inconclusive investigations does not exclude a possible pelvic venous etiology. This case illustrates how the non-specific presentation of pelvic venous disease may result in years of fragmented investigation and delayed recognition. Continuity of care in general and family medicine facilitated a longitudinal review of the patient's symptoms and previous investigations, allowing recognition of a pattern suggestive of pelvic venous disease. Greater awareness of pelvic venous disease in primary care may facilitate earlier consideration and appropriate specialist referral in women with otherwise unexplained chronic pelvic pain.

titre: Sedation and Gastrointestinal Adverse Event Reporting for Suzetrigine Versus Traditional Opioids: A Cohort-Restricted Disproportionality Analysis
resume: Background Suzetrigine is a non-opioid analgesic approved for moderate-to-severe acute pain. Whether its early postmarketing adverse-event reporting differs from traditional opioids is uncertain. We tested a prespecified respiratory-depression question and secondary sedation and gastrointestinal (GI) reporting domains. Methods We analyzed US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System/Adverse Event Monitoring System quarterly American Standard Code for Information Interchange extracts from 2025 Q2 through 2026 Q1. After latest-version deduplication, the main cohort comprised adult or age-missing US reports listing suzetrigine or exactly one of oxycodone, hydromorphone, morphine, or tramadol as the primary suspect; misuse/overdose-related reports were excluded, but the cohort was not indication-matched. The primary endpoint was the exact MedDRA preferred term "Respiratory depression," with minimum counts of 10 suzetrigine and 20 comparator reports. Secondary domains were sedation and GI events. Cohort-restricted reporting odds ratios (RORs) were stratified by calendar quarter. The prespecified acute/postoperative restriction was the most clinically aligned comparison; reporter-occupation restrictions were post hoc. No case-level causality assessment was performed. Results The cohort included 894 suzetrigine and 2,365 opioid reports. Respiratory depression appeared in 0/894 and 11/2,365 reports; the primary comparison was non-estimable. Sedation reporting was 33/894 versus 52/2,365 (Mantel-Haenszel ROR 1.77, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-2.76; Holm-adjusted p=0.0244), and GI reporting was 76/894 versus 157/2,365 (ROR 1.31, 95% CI 0.98-1.74; adjusted p=0.0688). The most clinically aligned acute/postoperative restriction attenuated sedation to ROR 1.03 (95% CI 0.56-1.89). In post hoc reporter analyses, consumer-only sedation occurred in 16 of 277 suzetrigine reports and 30 of 1,647 pooled-opioid reports (ROR 3.13, 95% CI 1.66-5.88). Sedation administered exclusively by health care professionals occurred in eight of 295 suzetrigine reports and 17 of 481 pooled-opioid reports, failing to meet the 20-event comparator threshold. Conclusions The respiratory comparison was non-estimable. Sedation reporting was elevated in the main cohort; consumer-only estimates were elevated for sedation and GI events. In the acute/postoperative restriction, both domain confidence intervals included 1. These patterns are compatible with reporting bias or channeling but establish neither their cause nor clinical equivalence. Zero respiratory reports do not establish safety. Denominator-based studies are needed.

titre: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Orforglipron for Weight Reduction in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review
resume: Obesity is a chronic disease associated with increased cardiometabolic risk, reduced quality of life, and higher mortality. Although injectable glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have substantially improved weight management, the requirement for injections remains a limitation for many patients. Orforglipron is a novel nonpeptide oral GLP-1RA currently under investigation for the treatment of overweight, obesity, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without T2DM. A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed and ScienceDirect from database inception through December 2025. Randomized controlled trials evaluating oral orforglipron and reporting weight-related, glycemic, or metabolic outcomes were included. Six randomized controlled trials involving 6,022 participants were included in the qualitative synthesis, with follow-up durations ranging from 12 to 72 weeks. Across studies, treatment with orforglipron was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in body weight ranging from approximately -4.5% to -14.7%, with greater reductions generally observed in longer-duration studies and at higher doses. Improvements in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting glucose, waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, triglycerides, and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol were also reported across several studies. Gastrointestinal adverse events, particularly nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation, were the most commonly reported safety outcomes and occurred more frequently during dose escalation and in higher-dose groups. Overall, current evidence suggests that oral orforglipron may represent a promising therapeutic option for weight reduction and glycemic improvement in adults with overweight or obesity; however, additional long-term randomized controlled trials are needed to further clarify optimal dosing strategies, long-term safety, and comparative clinical effectiveness.

titre: Dysbiosis of the gut bacteriome, phageome, archaeome, and mycobiome in multiple sclerosis: An in-depth review
resume: Recent advances in next-generation sequencing technologies have enabled comprehensive characterization of the gut microbiota in multiple sclerosis (MS), revealing significant alterations across the bacteriome, phageome, archaeome, and mycobiome compared with healthy controls. In this review, we discuss how MS is linked to the imbalance of gut microbial communities. Furthermore, we provide mechanistic insights into the interplay among dysbiosis, immunology, and microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids and toxins. Investigations have revealed diminished microbial diversity and shifts in critical immunomodulatory taxa in the gut microbiota of MS patients. It is evident that disruptions in these microbial communities influence the onset and progression of MS through the gut-brain axis. Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies, standardized methodologies, and detailed analysis of gut ecosystem dynamics. Understanding these complex microbial interactions is essential for improving MS management, suggesting that microbiota-targeted interventions may hold promise in future precision medicine strategies. Finally, we hope that this review will guide readers in keeping abreast of the latest research advancements in this field.

titre: Neuromodulation Therapies for Depression: Current Status and Future Directions
resume: Major depressive disorder is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and many patients fail to achieve sustained remission with first-line pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy. This unmet need has traditionally been framed as treatment-resistant depression (TRD), defined by an inadequate response to antidepressant treatment. Within this context, neuromodulation has assumed an increasingly important role by providing mechanistically distinct interventions when medication-based approaches are insufficient, poorly tolerated, or too slow. In this expert opinion article, we present a targeted, clinically oriented review of two established neuromodulation therapies for depression, electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), encompassing conventional repetitive TMS (rTMS), deep TMS, and theta-burst stimulation (TBS), as well as magnetic seizure therapy (MST), the most clinically advanced investigational convulsive modality. ECT remains the benchmark treatment for severe, urgent, psychotic, or otherwise refractory depression due to its rapid and robust efficacy, although its use is limited by anesthesia requirements, cognitive adverse effects, and associated stigma. TMS has the strongest evidence base among nonconvulsive neuromodulation treatments, with pivotal sham-controlled multicenter trials supporting conventional rTMS and deep TMS, while TBS protocols are improving feasibility, access, and scalability. MST is conceptually appealing as a more focal convulsive treatment designed to preserve antidepressant efficacy while reducing cognitive burden; recent Confirmatory Efficacy and Safety Trial of Magnetic Seizure Therapy for Depression (CREST-MST) data have strengthened its evidence base, but its routine clinical role remains to be defined through regulatory approval, durability data, and implementation evidence. We argue that future progress will depend not only on the development of new stimulation protocols but also on improved clinical sequencing, patient selection, and maintenance strategies that help sustain acute gains. The concept of difficult-to-treat depression (DTD) broadens the clinical framework beyond antidepressant nonresponse to include persistent burden, partial response, tolerability constraints, functional impairment, and patient-centered goals. This perspective may inform earlier and more strategic use of neuromodulation, although most randomized controlled trials remain focused on TRD. Further studies are needed to determine whether DTD-based approaches improve real-world outcomes. Advances are likely to arise from integrating protocol refinement, individualized targeting, scalable home-based approaches, depression-relevant extensions such as bipolar depression, and durable maintenance strategies rather than identifying a single universally superior modality.

titre: Digestive Aid as Adjunctive Therapy in Functional Dyspepsia: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
resume: Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal complaint. This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to determine the efficacy of a six-herb formulation (digestive aid) as a complementary therapy for FD. FD was confirmed based on Rome-IV criteria. Fifty patients were randomly assigned to receive either the digestive aid or a matching placebo for eight weeks, in addition to standard treatment protocols for FD. Dyspepsia symptoms were evaluated using the Leeds Dyspepsia Questionnaire (LDQ). The primary outcome was to compare changes in epigastric pain scores between the two groups from baseline to the end of treatment. The study included 30 (60%) female participants with a mean age of 40.8 (± 7.5) years. The comparison of mean changes in epigastric pain (-1.80 (-2.10, -1.50)), retrosternal pain (-2.12 (-2.40, -1.84)), regurgitation (-0.72 (-1.00, -0.44)), nausea (-1.40 (-1.70, -1.10)), early satiety (-0.88 (-1.16, -0.60)), belching (-1.00 (-1.30, -0.70)), dysphagia (-0.52 (-0.74, -0.30)), and vomiting (-0.40 (-0.64, -0.16)) showed significant improvement in the intervention group from baseline to the end of treatment. While a decrease in all dyspepsia domain scores was observed in the placebo group over the study period, the changes were not statistically significant. Between-group comparisons of mean differences revealed a significantly greater decrease in epigastric pain (-1.48 (-1.90, -1.06)), retrosternal pain (-1.96 (-2.40, -1.52)), regurgitation (-0.60 (-0.96, -0.24)), nausea (-1.32 (-1.72, -0.92)), early satiety (-0.76 (-1.14, -0.38)), belching (-0.84 (-1.24, -0.44)), and dysphagia (-0.40 (-0.68, -0.12)) in the digestive aid group compared to the placebo. The new formulation was well-tolerated with no major side effects during short-term use. Digestive aid, as an adjunct to standard therapy, may help alleviate symptoms in FD.

titre: Microbiome-Derived Metabolites in Multiple Sclerosis: Mechanisms of Immune Regulation and Therapeutic Potential: A Literature Review
resume: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune neuroinflammatory disease characterized by immune dysregulation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration of the central nervous system (CNS). Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota and microbiome-derived metabolites play important roles in the pathogenesis and progression of MS by modulating the gut-brain-immune axis. This narrative review examines the possible immunomodulatory effects of microbiome-derived metabolites in MS, with particular emphasis on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines, and evaluates their potential therapeutic implications. This review was conducted using the most recent available studies relevant to the topic. The search included PubMed, Google Scholar, and PMC databases. Eligible studies focused on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, reviews, and other publications that examined the role of microbiota and its metabolites in MS. The reviewed evidence indicates that MS-associated dysbiosis is accompanied by altered microbial metabolite production, disruption of regulatory T cell (Treg)/T helper 17 (Th17) balance, impaired barrier integrity, and increased neuroinflammation. SCFAs, tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines demonstrate immunoregulatory effects through modulation of T-cell responses, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory pathways. Microbiota-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modulation, and metabolite supplementation, have shown promising immunological and clinical effects. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, variable interventions, and insufficient long-term clinical validation limit definitive conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy. Future large-scale longitudinal and multi-omics studies are crucial for clarifying the underlying mechanisms and unlocking microbiota-targeted strategies to manage MS more effectively.

titre: Effectiveness of the Low Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols Diet for Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome Managed in Primary and Secondary Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
resume: The low fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (FODMAP) diet has emerged as a promising dietary intervention for managing irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the low FODMAP diet compared with various control conditions in adults with IBS. The pre-specified primary outcome was the Irritable Bowel Syndrome Symptom Severity Score, whereas adequate relief, abdominal pain, bloating, and quality of life (QoL) were the secondary outcomes. A systematic search identified English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from inception through 20 May 2026 that compared the low FODMAP diet with control conditions in adults with IBS. Statistical analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4 (Cochrane Collaboration, London, UK), with treatment effects expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic, and random-effects models were used for the primary analyses, with fixed-effect sensitivity analyses when heterogeneity was low. Twenty-three RCTs, encompassing 2,164 participants (1,852 completers), were included. Compared with traditional dietary advice, the low FODMAP diet significantly reduced IBS symptom severity score (SMD: -0.71; 95% CI (-1.02, -0.40)), improved adequate relief (OR: 2.15; 95% CI (1.54, 3.01)), reduced abdominal pain (SMD: -0.35; 95% CI (-0.54, -0.16)), decreased bloating (SMD: -0.45; 95% CI (-0.75, -0.15)), and improved QoL (SMD: 0.48; 95% CI (0.27, 0.69)). Similar benefits were observed against habitual diet comparators. Compared with other active dietary interventions, the low FODMAP diet did not significantly improve IBS symptom severity, adequate relief, or QoL, although it did modestly improve bloating. The low FODMAP diet is an effective intervention for reducing global IBS symptoms and improving QoL compared with traditional dietary advice and habitual diet; however, it does not appear to offer greater benefit than other structured active dietary interventions, aside from this modest, comparator-independent improvement in bloating. These findings suggest that structured dietary intervention and dietary support may contribute substantially to symptom improvement beyond FODMAP restriction itself.

titre: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder as a Prodromal Manifestation of Alpha-Synucleinopathies
resume: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia in which patients physically act out their dreams due to loss of the normal muscle paralysis that occurs during REM sleep. It is now recognized that isolated RBD (iRBD) is strongly associated with future development of α-synuclein-related neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). It is seen that most patients with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD eventually develop a clinically defined synucleinopathy, often after a long symptom-free interval. This long prodromal phase makes iRBD a unique clinical model for studying the earliest stages of neurodegeneration, before the onset of clear motor or cognitive disability. α-synuclein pathology frequently begins in the lower brainstem and autonomic nervous system, affecting REM sleep regulatory circuits early in the disease process. As pathology spreads, dopaminergic, cholinergic, and cortical systems become involved, leading to the gradual emergence of motor, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms. As a result, many individuals with iRBD exhibit subtle non-motor features such as hyposmia, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, anxiety, and mild cognitive changes years before a formal neurological diagnosis is made. Recent advances have improved the ability to identify patients at the highest risk of near-term phenoconversion. Quantitative measures of REM sleep without atonia, dopamine transporter imaging, autonomic testing, and emerging molecular biomarkers, including α-synuclein seed amplification assays, have shown promise in risk stratification. In addition, cognitive changes may occur earlier than previously recognized, particularly in patients with iRBD who also demonstrate hyposmia or dopaminergic dysfunction. Management of RBD remains largely symptomatic and focuses on injury prevention and sleep stabilization. While clonazepam and melatonin remain first-line therapies, alternative treatments including sodium oxybate, serotonergic agents, cannabinoids, and modulation of the gut-brain axis through probiotic supplementation have also been explored. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge regarding the clinical features, mechanisms, biomarkers, and management of RBD as a prodromal manifestation of α-synucleinopathies, with emphasis on its importance for early diagnosis and future disease-modifying research.

titre: Progressive Dysphagia Revealing Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy: A Diagnostic Challenge
resume: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy (OPMD) is a rare, late-onset myopathy often presenting with progressive dysphagia and delayed diagnosis. We report a 69-year-old woman with worsening dysphagia, ptosis, and proximal muscle weakness who underwent an unrevealing gastrointestinal evaluation, including upper endoscopy. Videofluoroscopic swallow evaluation (VFSE) demonstrated pharyngeal dysphagia. A strong family history prompted genetic testing, confirming a poly(A) binding protein nuclear 1 (PABPN1) trinucleotide repeat expansion consistent with autosomal dominant OPMD. This case highlights the importance of recognizing neuromuscular causes of dysphagia, particularly when structural evaluations are negative. Early identification can reduce diagnostic delay and allow appropriate supportive management, improving quality of life and reducing complications.

titre: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Prevalence of Capitellar Osteochondritis Dissecans in Preadolescent Baseball Players in Japan
resume: BACKGROUND: Capitellar osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) is considered to have a multifactorial cause, including repetitive microtrauma and other intrinsic factors. The COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 markedly restricted baseball-related physical activity in preadolescent baseball players, providing an opportunity to examine whether this restriction affected the prevalence of capitellar OCD. PURPOSE: To compare the prevalence of capitellar OCD among preadolescent baseball players before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional study; Level of evidence, 3. METHODS: The authors retrospectively analyzed data for 5006 preadolescent baseball players aged 9 to 12 years who had undergone elbow screening in Tokushima, Japan, before (2018-2019), during (2020-2021), and after (2023-2024) the COVID-19 pandemic. Screening consisted of questionnaires, physical examinations, and ultrasonographic evaluation of the throwing elbow. Players with abnormal ultrasonographic findings underwent radiography and, when necessary, magnetic resonance imaging. RESULTS: The authors examined 1935 preadolescent baseball players before the COVID-19 pandemic (prepandemic group), 1671 during the pandemic (pandemic group), and 1400 after the pandemic (postpandemic group). There were no statistically significant differences between the groups in characteristics, including school grade, school grade at the time of starting baseball, baseball experience, and playing position. There was also no significant difference in the prevalence of capitellar OCD among the prepandemic, pandemic, and postpandemic groups (1.9% [36/1935], 1.3% [21/1671], and 1.4% [19/1400], respectively; P = .283). All measures of elbow pain and physical examination findings were lower during the pandemic period than during the prepandemic period, and most increased again during the postpandemic period. CONCLUSION: The prevalence of capitellar OCD in preadolescent baseball players did not significantly decrease during the COVID-19 pandemic, despite temporal changes in the prevalence of elbow pain and positive findings on physical examination.

titre: Soluble Siglec-9 combined with exercise ameliorates HFD-induced metabolic and depressive-like phenotypes with gut-brain axis changes
resume: Long-term intake of a high-fat diet (HFD) induces gut microbiota dysbiosis associated with inflammation and is linked to metabolic abnormalities and depressive-like behaviors. The soluble form of sialic acid-binding Ig-like lectin-9 (s-Siglec-9) exhibits therapeutic effects against inflammatory diseases, and exercise is known to have antidepressant effects. However, the effects of s-Siglec-9 on HFD-induced depressive-like behaviors, alone or in combination with exercise, remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects of s-Siglec-9 combined with exercise in mice with HFD-induced metabolic dysfunction. Mice were fed an HFD ad libitum for 8 weeks, and interventions were conducted during the final 4 weeks. The induction of the anti-inflammatory phenotype by s-Siglec-9 was also investigated using primary microglia. The results revealed significant suppression of depressive-like behaviors in the intervention groups compared with the group fed only the HFD, with the effect being greater in the s-Siglec-9 with exercise group. Histological analyses showed reduced microglial activation and astrogliosis in the hippocampus and hypothalamus, together with increased hippocampal neurogenesis. Gut microbiota analysis showed a decrease in inflammatory bacterial genera and an increase in short-chain fatty acid-producing bacterial genera in the intervention groups. In vitro, s-Siglec-9 promoted a shift in primary microglia toward an anti-inflammatory and neurotrophic M2-like state in the presence of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans. Our study suggests the potential of combining administration of an anti-inflammatory substance with exercise as a therapeutic strategy for metabolic abnormalities accompanied by depressive-like behaviors, potentially involving coordinated changes across gut microbiota, inflammatory, and neural systems.

fiche.verdict: L'association d'un traitement anti-inflammatoire (s-Siglec-9) et d'exercice physique réduit les comportements dépressifs et les anomalies métaboliques induits par un régime riche en graisses chez la souris.

fiche.intervention: régime riche en graisses (HFD) avec administration de s-Siglec-9 et/ou exercice physique

titre: Neuroimaging-Guided Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
resume: Rates of response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) vary widely. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether neuroimaging-guided targeting personalization, from fixed-coordinate neuronavigation to individually connectivity-personalized targeting, moderates clinical response, safety, and neural mechanisms in OCD. Following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched through July 2026 for randomized and non-randomized studies of neuroimaging-guided transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in OCD. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using Cochrane RoB2 for RCTs (randomized controlled trials) and ROBINS-I (Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions) for non-randomized studies. Random-effects inverse-variance and risk-ratio models pooled Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) scores and responder rates; non-poolable data were synthesized narratively. Nine study cohorts across eight publications met inclusion criteria (five RCTs and four open-label/single-arm). Pooled analysis of four sham-controlled RCTs showed no significant benefit of neuroimaging-guided TMS on Y-BOCS total score (MD = -0.64, 95% CI = -3.60, 2.32) or responder rate (RR = 1.46, 95% CI = 0.68, 3.15), with moderate heterogeneity. However, trials using individually connectivity-personalized pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA) targeting consistently trended toward benefit, while fixed-coordinate neuronavigated trials trended toward null or sham-favoring results. A narrative synthesis of non-poolable and non-randomized studies showed larger, mostly positive within-group reductions in Y-BOCS scores (25%-48%), particularly among patients with moderate disease severity, alongside mechanistic evidence linking individualized connectivity-based targets to symptom improvement. TMS was well tolerated overall, with mild, transient headache being the most common adverse event and no serious safety concerns identified. Overall, neuroimaging-guided TMS showed no pooled benefit in OCD; however, individually connectivity-personalized targeting may be more beneficial than fixed-coordinate approaches, warranting adequately powered trials that directly compare targeting-personalization strategies.

fiche.verdict: La sTMS guidée par neuro imagerie ne montre pas de bénéfice global poolé dans les TOC, mais le ciblage personnalisé connectique promet.
fiche.population: Patients souffrant de troubles obsessionnels-compulsifs (TOC)
fiche.intervention: Stimulation magnétique transcranienne répétitive (sTMS) guidée par neuro imagerie versus comparateurs ou placebo

titre: Dietary Patterns and Practices Among Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Their Associations With Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Disease Activity: A Systematic Review
resume: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) often report food avoidance, restrictive eating, and dietary modification, although the association of these dietary behaviours with gastrointestinal symptoms and objective measures of inflammatory activity remains unclear. Clinically, it is important to distinguish dietary behaviours for symptom relief from dietary exposures associated with underlying inflammation. The aim of this systematic review was to synthesise evidence on habitual dietary patterns and patient-adopted dietary practices among patients with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or IBD-unclassified and to evaluate their associations with gastrointestinal symptoms and clinical, biochemical, endoscopic, or histological disease activity. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched for English-language observational studies published between January 1, 2016, and August 4, 2026. Eligible studies provided information on habitual dietary intake or diets used by patients in their daily practice or real-world situations. Prescribed therapeutic dietary interventions, supplementation studies, reviews, case reports, animal studies, and studies without IBD-specific outcome measures were excluded. The review was performed in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, and methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists for each design. Findings were synthesised narratively. Eleven studies were included in this review, with 2,242 participants who had IBD. Across disease states, food avoidance, dietary restriction, meal skipping, and symptom-driven dietary modification were common. Three studies reported positive screening rates for avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (10.2% to 32.5%). Dietary practices were restrictive and related to malnutrition risk and nutritional inadequacy, and low appetite and reduced food-related quality of life were also reported. Associations with dietary behaviours were more consistent for gastrointestinal symptoms than for objective measures of inflammatory activity, including C-reactive protein, faecal calprotectin, endoscopic activity, and validated disease-activity indices. No single dietary pattern or dietary total score was consistently associated with inflammatory activity. Dietary patterns and practices in IBD were more consistently associated with gastrointestinal symptom burden than with objective measures of inflammatory activity. Self-imposed dietary restrictions may be associated with nutritional and psychosocial consequences. Patients with substantial dietary restriction should undergo assessment of inflammatory activity and nutritional status, with referral to an IBD-experienced dietitian when appropriate. Future studies using validated dietary instruments and standardised clinical, biochemical, endoscopic, and patient-reported outcomes are needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships.

titre: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for anxiety: Translating brain-behavior models into scalable clinical tools
resume: Advances in affective and systems neuroscience have clarified how distributed brain networks encode threat processing, generate bodily arousal, and shape cognitive and behavioral features of anxiety disorders. However, this progress has not been systematically translated into patient-facing educational tools or clinical care. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation (NIPE) extends conventional psychoeducation by incorporating brain-based explanations of symptoms and treatment, while also structuring materials to engage attention, memory, and self-referential processing. Emerging work suggests NIPE may enhance insight, reduce stigma, and improve treatment engagement and adherence. NIPE aims to optimize both the content (what is taught) and structure (how it is delivered) of psychoeducation to engage emotional and motivational aspects of learning. Building on recent NIPE frameworks applied to other psychiatric conditions (e.g., addiction), here we extend this approach to anxiety disorders. We developed two cartoon-based NIPE posters within an anxiety disorders specialty clinic to operationalize core brain-behavior processes in anxiety. The first poster (10 Ways Anxiety Impacts Your Health) organizes anxiety symptoms into four domains: threat-related Alarms, maladaptive Beliefs, reinforcing Coping Behaviors, and broader Social Context. The second poster (10 Actionable To Do's) maps evidence-based cognitive-behavioral strategies onto corresponding brain processes, using a dial to emphasize symptom dimensions over dichotomies. These materials use visually engaging metaphor-based illustrations to translate abstract neural processes into intuitive, self-relevant representations emphasizing actionable brain-based learning over brain region labeling. This approach reflects a scalable framework for integrating neuroscience into psychoeducation with the potential to enhance patient understanding, engagement, and support behavioral change in anxiety disorders.

titre: Efficacy of transabdominal magnetic field therapy on constipation severity in chronic functional constipation: A randomized controlled trial
resume: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate transabdominal magnetic field therapy (MFT) for constipation severity and related outcomes in adults with chronic functional constipation. METHODOLOGY: This multicenter, three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted at Istanbul Medipol University and Istanbul Gedik University, Türkiye, from February 2019 to April 2026. Adults meeting Rome III criteria were randomized to MFT, sham, or standard care (SC) (n=75); 60 completers formed the per-protocol analysis (20/group). MFT was administered at 25-Hz and 30-Gauss for 30 minutes, twice weekly for eight weeks. Sham replicated the procedure without active stimulation; SC received standardized constipation management education. The primary outcome was the Constipation Severity Instrument (CSI) total score. Secondary outcomes assessed bowel habits, defecation time, stool form, and constipation-related quality of life (PAC-QOL). RESULTS: MFT reduced CSI more than SC (mean difference in change [MD], -20.55; 95% CI, -24.97 to -16.13) and sham (MD, -14.40; 95% CI, -18.82 to -9.98; both p<0.001). MFT also improved complete spontaneous bowel movements versus SC (ratio of rate ratios [RRR], 1.57; 95% CI, 1.20-2.05) and sham (RRR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.87-3.07), and reduced PAC-QOL versus SC (MD, -21.25; 95% CI, -24.09 to -18.41) and sham (MD, -11.60; 95% CI, -14.44 to -8.76; all p≤0.001). No adverse events were observed or reported among completers. CONCLUSIONS: Transabdominal MFT was associated with greater short-term improvements in constipation severity, bowel function, and constipation-related quality of life than sham treatment and standard care. Future studies should establish optimal stimulation parameters and evaluate long-term effectiveness and safety.

titre: Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction: All Roads Lead to Rome, Few Lead to Africa
[Advances in pharmacological research of TCM based on "Akkermansia and traditional Chinese medicine polysaccharides"]
resume: In recent years, the pharmacological mechanisms of TCM based on gut microbiota have received increasing attention. Among gut microbes, Akkermansia, a low-abundance functional gut bacterium, has emerged as a research hotspot due to its distinctive biological properties and key roles in immune and metabolic regulation. Polysaccharides, among the major active components of TCM, exhibit typical prebiotic properties. They can resist digestion in the upper gastrointestinal tract, reach the intestine directly, and are fermented by the gut microbiota. A large body of research indicates that, as prebiotics, TCM polysaccharides can selectively promote the proliferation and metabolism of Akkermansia, thereby treating diseases. However, the selective effect of TCM polysaccharides on Akkermansia is determined by their complex chemical structures, including monosaccharide composition, relative molecular mass, specific functional groups, glycosidic bond types, and spatial conformations. The interaction between the distinctive physicochemical properties of polysaccharides and the abundant carbohydrate-degrading enzyme systems of Akkermansia represents a research field that requires in-depth exploration in the microecological pharmacology of TCM polysaccharides. Based on the latest literature, the crucial roles of Akkermansia in maintaining the intestinal barrier and regulating immune responses and metabolism were systematically elaborated. Then, from the perspectives of the association between TCM polysaccharide structure and the Akkermansia enzyme system, the interaction mechanisms between TCM polysaccharides and Akkermansia were deeply discussed. By integrating the holistic concept of TCM with microecological principles, this review elaborated the TCM connotations of the pharmacological mechanism based on the "Akkermansia and TCM polysaccharides" from multiple perspectives, including the gut-targeted axes(mainly the gut-brain axis), TCM property theory, reinforcing healthy Qi to eliminate pathogenic factors, balancing Yin and Yang, and treating diseases based on the root causes. Finally, the limitations of the current research(e.g., unclear structure-activity relationships between TCM polysaccharides and Akkermansia, insufficient investigation of microbial synergistic networks, and a lack of clinical data) were summarized, and future research directions were proposed to provide a reference for in-depth research on the microecological pharmacological mechanisms of TCM.

titre: [Cardiac and psychological diseases: innovative understanding from TCM and treatment with classic TCM formulas]
resume: Cardiac and psychological diseases refer to a clinical syndrome with or without organic cardiovascular disease, characterized by cardiovascular somatic symptoms associated with adverse emotions. Modern medicine mainly adopts a regimen of foundational cardiovascular therapy combined with anti-anxiety and antidepressant drugs for this condition. While this approach can partially alleviate symptoms, clinical challenges persist, including frequent gastrointestinal adverse reactions, the potential for dependence on psychotropic drugs, and poor long-term medication adherence among patients. TCM, adhering to the principle of simultaneous cardiac and psychological treatment and simultaneous regulation of the body and spirit, holds unique advantages in managing this condition. However, the current clinical understanding of the TCM pathogenesis of cardiac and psychological diseases remains fragmented, and the treatment strategies using classic TCM formulas lack systematic organization and integration. Based on the theory of "the unity of the body and spirit" from the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, and integrating discussions from ancient and modern physicians with modern clinical practice, this paper systematically elucidated the TCM etiology and pathogenesis of cardiac and psychological diseases. It clarified that depression was the initiating factor, blood stasis was the core link, and deficiency was the key foundation for disease prolongation in pathological progression. The core disease location was the heart, closely related to the liver, spleen, and kidneys. Furthermore, with deficiency and excess as the overarching principles, a classic TCM formula-based treatment system centered on depression, stasis, and deficiency was constructed. For liver depression and Qi stagnation with pivot dysfunction, the treatment methods were soothing the liver to relieve depression and regulating Qi to adjust the pivot, using classic TCM formulas such as Chaihu Shugan Powder, Sini Powder, Xiaoyao Powder, and Danzhi Xiaoyao Powder. For combined phlegm and stasis and stagnant fire disturbing the heart, the methods were resolving phlegm, expelling stasis, unblocking the vessels, and calming the spirit, using formulas like Xuefu Zhuyu Decoction, Mengshi Guntan Pills combined with Huanglian Wendan Decoction, Banxia Houpo Decoction, Gualou Xiebai Banxia Decoction combined with Shixiao Powder, and Chaihu Jia Longgu Muli Decoction. For visceral deficiency and Yin-Yang imbalance, the methods were replenishing Qi, nourishing blood, and harmonizing Yin and Yang, using formulas such as Guipi Decoction or Yangxin Decoction, Zhigancao Decoction, Tianwang Buxin Dan, Suanzaoren Decoction, Baihe Dihuang Decoction, Ganmai Dazao Decoction, Shenfu Decoction combined with Yougui Pills, Huanglian Ejiao Decoction combined with Jiaotai Pills or Zuogui Pills, and Linggui Zhugan Decoction. The correspondence between formula and syndrome and key points for clinical application for each pattern were simultaneously clarified. By refining the TCM pathogenesis theory and the pattern differentiation and treatment principles of using classic TCM formulas for cardiac and psychological diseases, this paper aims to provide a systematic theoretical reference and actionable clinical practice insights for the standardized TCM diagnosis and treatment of cardiac and psychological diseases.

titre: Targeting the Gut via the Spine: Spinal Cord Stimulation for Chronic Idiopathic Gastroparesis-A Case Report
resume: BACKGROUND: Gastroparesis is characterized by delayed gastric emptying and can cause abdominal pain, nausea, impaired oral intake, and reduced quality of life (QoL). CASE REPORT: We describe spinal cord stimulation (SCS) in a patient with chronic idiopathic gastroparesis, intractable nausea, epigastric pain, severe food intolerance, and poor nutrition. She presented after multiple treatments, including gastric electrical stimulation, had failed to provide lasting relief. A celiac plexus block briefly improved her symptoms. High thoracic SCS was subsequently trialed and implanted, with reported improvement in pain, nausea, and oral intake at 1 month, and continued food tolerance without early satiety at 1 year post-implantation. CONCLUSIONS: SCS was associated with improvement in symptoms and quality of life in this patient. Longer follow-up and further study are needed to evaluate its role in refractory gastroparesis.

titre: A case of suspected IgE-mediated hypersensitivity to Menta piperita with identification of a possible allergenic protein through proteomic study
resume: BACKGROUND: Products derived from Mentha piperita (peppermint) and Mentha spicata (spearmint) are commonly used in cosmetics and food preparation, as well as in medications for treating various gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and respiratory disorders. CASE REPORT: A 41-year-old male patient of Italian origin was evaluated for recurrent symptoms of urticaria; he had a history of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis caused by house dust mites (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus and Dermatophagoides farinae). During the first episode, he reported generalized urticaria 20 minutes after taking mint-flavored granulated ibuprofen (Espidifen® 600 mg), requiring emergency medical attention. In the second episode, one month later, he experienced nasal obstruction, sneezing, and rhinorrhea after chewing mint-flavored gum. In the third episode, occurring weeks later, he suffered two bouts of contact dermatitis after applying an anti-inflammatory cream containing menthol and using a mentholated shampoo. All symptoms resolved upon complete avoidance of mint-containing products. Skin prick-to-prick testing (using fresh leaves) was performed with various species from the Lamiaceae family. Only the fresh M. piperita leaf elicited a positive reaction (5 mm wheal and 4 mm erythema). Tests with basil, oregano, and thyme were negative. Molecular diagnosis (specific IgE) confirmed the reaction to M. piperita (0.4 kU/L). CONCLUSION: Given the widespread use of mint derivatives in various forms, sensitization to mint may be underdiagnosed. Mint allergy should be considered-specifically regarding potential IgE-mediated reactions-in patients with unclear diagnoses following exposure to mint-containing products.

titre: Efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions for Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: OBJECTIVE: This meta-analysis aimed to systematically assess the efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions (TGDs) as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of Parkinson's disease (PD) using the latest clinical evidence. METHODS: Nine databases were searched from their inception to 31 August 2025 to identify eligible studies. Primary outcomes included the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Score (TCMSS) and clinical efficacy. Secondary outcomes encompassed the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), British 39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39), Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale (PDSS), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and adverse events. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to assess the quality of evidence. RESULTS: Thirty-four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving a total of 3049 participants were ultimately included. The results indicated that add-on therapy with TGDs significantly benefited patients with PD by reducing the UPDRS, TCMSS, PDQ-39, and HAMD scores, as well as IL-6, TNF-α and MDA levels, and by increasing clinical efficacy, the MMSE, MoCA, and PDSS scores, and SOD levels. TGDs also reduced the incidence of adverse events, including constipation, gastrointestinal reactions, and the on-off phenomenon. CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis provided up-to-date and supportive evidence for the efficacy and safety of TGDs as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of patients with PD. Given the generally low certainty of the evidence, more high-quality RCTs are recommended to confirm these findings.
