titre: Comparison of oncological outcomes between adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma after sublobar resection for T1a/bN0M0 non-small cell lung cancer: a propensity score-matched SEER study
resume: BACKGROUND: Sublobar resection is increasingly used for selected patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, whether adenocarcinoma (ADC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) have comparable survival outcomes after sublobar resection remains uncertain, particularly when competing causes of death are considered. This study aimed to compare survival outcomes between ADC and SCC after sublobar resection, incorporating tumor size stratification and competing-risk analyses. METHODS: Patients with one primary T1a/bN0M0 NSCLC who underwent segmentectomy (SEG) or wedge resection (WR) between 2004 and 2022 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Overall survival (OS) and lung cancer-specific survival (LCSS) were compared between ADC and SCC using propensity score matching (PSM), Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox regression, with hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Tumor size-stratified analyses were also performed. Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs), Gray's test, and Fine-Gray regression were used to evaluate lung cancer-specific death (LCSD) and other-cause death (OCD) as competing events, with subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) reported. Exploratory comparisons of SEG and WR were conducted within each histologic subtype. RESULTS: Among 4,198 patients (3,066 ADC and 1,132 SCC), 1,129 patients remained in each group after 1:1 PSM with well-balanced baseline characteristics. SCC was independently associated with poorer OS than ADC (adjusted HR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.20-1.51; P<0.001), with consistent associations in both tumor size subgroups. LCSS did not differ significantly after adjustment (adjusted HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.79-1.15; P=0.62) or within either size subgroup. CIF analysis showed no significant difference in LCSD (Gray's P=0.10), whereas the CIF of OCD was significantly higher in SCC (Gray's P<0.001). Fine-Gray regression yielded consistent findings: SCC was not significantly associated with LCSD (adjusted sHR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.71-1.02; P=0.09) but was associated with a higher subdistribution hazard of OCD (adjusted sHR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.44-1.91; P<0.001). These competing-risk patterns were consistent in both tumor size subgroups. Exploratory analyses showed no consistent adjusted survival advantage of SEG over WR within either histologic subtype. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with T1a/bN0M0 NSCLC undergoing sublobar resection, SCC was associated with poorer OS than ADC, consistently across tumor size subgroups. In contrast, neither LCSS nor LCSD was significantly worse in SCC, whereas the incidence of OCD was higher; these patterns were also consistent across tumor size subgroups. The poorer overall prognosis associated with SCC should therefore be interpreted in the context of competing mortality rather than lung cancer-specific mortality alone.

titre: Anorexia nervosa or pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndrome? A case report
resume: BACKGROUND: Pediatric Acute-Onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome (PANS) is a rare heterogeneous condition characterized by rapid onset obsessions/compulsions and/or food restriction with at least two accompanying acute-onset neuropsychiatric symptoms. PANS is currently considered an exclusionary diagnosis with considerable overlap with psychiatric disorders including obsessive compulsive disorder, tics, and eating disorders. Little is known about the crossover between eating disorders and PANS, and there is minimal guidance on diagnostic and treatment considerations for these patients. CASE PRESENTATION: This case report describes a 9-year-old female who presented for an initial assessment to a specialty outpatient eating disorder treatment center due to restrictive eating, fear of weight gain, body image disturbance, and obsessive-compulsive compensatory behaviors. She met diagnostic criteria for other specified feeding and eating disorder (OSFED)/atypical nervosa (AAN) and received family-based treatment (FBT) to target food restriction through parent-led refeeding. Despite weight stabilization and nutritional improvement in FBT, the patient experienced severe progressive functional deterioration. The patient was subsequently evaluated by an immune behavioral health (IBH) clinic and diagnosed with PANS. Treatment included gradual transition in care from the eating disorder clinic for AAN to IBH and sleep clinics for management of remaining neuropsychiatric symptoms. CONCLUSIONS: This report highlights a unique case of a patient with PANS features and body image/weight-driven food refusal. This case has potential implications for how eating disorder specialty providers asses for possible overlapping PANS. Criteria prompting consideration for PANS may include a combination of acute-onset restrictive eating, prepubertal body image disturbance, and progressive functional impairment and/or developmental regression despite weight restoration. This case also highlights implications of care coordination and triage across specialty clinics.

fiche.population: Une fillette de 9 ans présentant des restrictions alimentaires et des TOC

titre: Delayed Recognition of Autism Spectrum Disorder and Off-Label Lurasidone After Intolerance to Risperidone and Aripiprazole in a Latin American Child: A Case Report
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) can be difficult to recognize when co-occurring psychiatric symptoms are more clinically prominent, which may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a nine-year-old Latin American boy whose ASD and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) were not diagnosed until approximately 27 months after initial presentation with irritability, mood lability, anxiety, and, subsequently, hallucinatory experiences; these symptoms were initially managed as primary psychiatric conditions. During this interval, fluoxetine was discontinued due to symptom worsening, sertraline produced only partial benefit, and both Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved agents for irritability associated with autistic disorder were discontinued because of adverse effects: risperidone due to significant weight gain and aripiprazole due to nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. A detailed neurodevelopmental reassessment subsequently identified longstanding social communication difficulties, rigid routines, sensory sensitivities, and restricted interests, supporting diagnoses of ASD and OCD. Low-dose lurasidone (20 mg nightly) was initiated off-label alongside continued sertraline. Over the following year, the patient demonstrated sustained improvement in irritability, aggression, self-injurious behavior, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. Hallucinatory experiences resolved within approximately three months and did not recur, with no significant adverse effects observed. This case illustrates how more prominent psychiatric symptoms can mask ASD and describes the individualized use of off-label lurasidone after intolerance to approved agents. However, the temporal association with clinical improvement does not establish causality, and findings from a single case cannot demonstrate efficacy.

titre: A participatory study of information and presentation priorities for a digital interface for bowel self-management
resume: BACKGROUND: Difficulty controlling or emptying the bowel is a common issue with devastating physical and mental health impacts. Digital technologies supporting bowel self-management remain limited. We are exploring a system combining an implanted sensor with a digital interface to support bowel self-management. This paper reports on the digital interface. OBJECTIVES: To identify the information most valuable to adults living with bowel problems and the best ways to present it on the digital interface, informed by lived experience; secondarily, to gather their views on the sensor and implantation methods. METHODS: A participatory design approach was employed. Thirteen adults with IBD/IBS attended design sessions; five more with IBD/IBS and eight with other bowel problems attended evaluation sessions. Participants were primarily UK-based, female, and White. Design sessions explored interface priorities and lived experiences; evaluation sessions assessed usability and utility. Views on the sensor were gathered across both phases. Data were analysed using qualitative methods. RESULTS: Five themes were identified: balancing discretion, clarity, and stigma in presentation; balancing benefit and burden; encouraging engagement without exacerbating anxiety; supporting the move from data to information to knowledge; and supporting clinical communication and confidence. Ninety-two percent of participants were positive towards sensor implantation. CONCLUSIONS: This study addresses a gap in the literature on digital interfaces for bowel self-management in combination with implantable sensors. It highlights faecal incontinence as a key patient concern, identifies priorities for information and presentation, and informs future sensor development. The work may have some limited applicability to other implantable/wearable sensors with digital interfaces.

titre: A practical approach to dietary interventions in pediatric irritable bowel syndrome
resume: Pediatric irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a gut-brain axis disorder that negatively affects the quality of life of children and adolescents. Because up to 90% of children and parents report a direct correlation between the consumption of specific foods and symptom exacerbation, dietary intervention is a therapeutic challenge. However, the lack of nutritional guidance leads parents to self-manage their children's diets, thereby increasing the risk of dietary restrictions and nutritional deficiencies. This review analyzes current evidence on dietary therapy for pediatric IBS, focusing on efficacy, safety, and the risk of nutritional deficiencies. Traditional dietary advice is recommended as the first-line dietary approach, promoting a set of lifestyle and dietary recommendations; it demonstrates long-term clinical efficacy comparable to more restrictive diets while minimizing the risk of eating disorders. The Mediterranean diet serves as a protective and sustainable diet, offering anti-inflammatory effects and favorable microbiota modulation by prebiotic fiber and antioxidant compounds. By contrast, the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols diet is reserved for selected cases owing to its restrictive nature and potential for nutritional deficiencies. To date, the gluten-free diet approach remains limited and controversial in children. Moreover, reduction of ultra-processed foods is a further diet strategy for IBS symptoms; ultra-processed foods are often rich in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, polyols, and added sugars, leading to microbiota dysbiosis and symptom exacerbation. Overall, a multidisciplinary and family-centered approach is essential to control IBS symptoms in children, focusing on personalized diet and behavioral interventions.

titre: Post-COVID Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction: A Focus on Persistent Diarrhea
resume: Persistent gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection include diarrhea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, constipation, nausea, and other disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), but these entities should not be treated as interchangeable. In a meta-analysis of long-COVID studies, any GI symptom was reported in approximately 22% of patients and diarrhea in 10%, although heterogeneity was very high. In a large US Veterans Affairs cohort, post-acute COVID-19 was associated with incident diarrhea (hazard ratio {HR}: 1.58, 95% CI: 1.52-1.65; excess burden 7.99 per 1,000 persons at one year) and irritable bowel syndrome (HR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.28-1.86). Prospective Rome IV cohorts report lower absolute rates of formally diagnosed DGBIs; one study found persistent DGBI symptoms in 6.6% at six months, with functional diarrhea in 2.2% and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) in 2.5% at three months. Mechanistic evidence supports intestinal involvement during acute infection and demonstrates associations with epithelial/angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) perturbation, immune activation, barrier dysfunction, altered microbial taxa, and impaired microbial metabolite production. However, persistent viral RNA or antigen, dysbiosis, and gut-lung signaling remain proposed or associative mechanisms rather than established causes of chronic diarrhea. Treatment evidence specific to post-COVID functional diarrhea is sparse. A large synbiotic trial improved a broad "gastrointestinal upset" domain in post-acute COVID syndrome, but did not enroll a defined chronic diarrhea or Rome-positive population; probiotic and fecal microbiota transplantation trials showing GI effects were largely conducted during acute COVID-19. Therefore, current care should first exclude organic and medication-related causes, then apply phenotype-based management extrapolated from established diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) and functional-diarrhea practice while clearly acknowledging the limited post-COVID-specific evidence. Standardized definitions, pre-infection GI data, appropriate controls, functional microbiome measures, and dedicated randomized trials are priorities for future research.

titre: Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PET-CT) Diagnosis of Large-Vessel Giant Cell Arteritis Presenting as Pyrexia of Unknown Origin Without Classical Cranial Features: A Case Report
resume: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is a systemic vasculitis affecting medium and large arteries and is classically associated with cranial manifestations such as headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and visual disturbance. However, large-vessel GCA may present with non-specific constitutional symptoms, making diagnosis difficult and delaying appropriate treatment. We report the case of a 58-year-old man with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis, and irritable bowel syndrome who presented with a 5-6-week history of intermittent fever, night sweats, anorexia, weight loss, mild headache, and predominantly lower-limb myalgia. Extensive investigations for infection, malignancy, and autoimmune disease were unrevealing. Microbiological investigations including blood and urine cultures, viral studies, acid-fast bacilli testing, and fungal markers were negative. Autoimmune screening, including antinuclear antibodies (ANA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), rheumatoid factor, and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies (anti-CCP), was also negative. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of occult infection or malignancy. Despite empirical antibiotic therapy, the patient remained symptomatic with persistently elevated inflammatory markers, including an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 136 mm/hr and C-reactive protein of 196 mg/L. As part of the evaluation for pyrexia of unknown origin, fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (FDG PET-CT) was performed, which demonstrated increased uptake within the bilateral femoral, vertebral, and axillary arteries, consistent with large-vessel vasculitis. Following rheumatology assessment and specialist consultation, a clinical and radiological diagnosis of large-vessel GCA was made. High-dose oral prednisolone was initiated, resulting in rapid clinical and biochemical improvement, with marked improvement in inflammatory markers. A subsequent right temporal artery biopsy demonstrated histological features in keeping with GCA. This case illustrates an atypical presentation of GCA as pyrexia of unknown origin without classic cranial or visual symptoms. Several important learning points emerge. Firstly, clinicians should maintain a high level of suspicion for large-vessel vasculitis in patients over 50 who present with persistent systemic inflammation and non-specific constitutional symptoms, specifically prolonged fever, weight loss, and myalgia, even in the absence of cranial manifestations. Secondly, the case demonstrates the diagnostic utility of FDG PET-CT in identifying large-vessel vascular inflammation when initial standard workup for infection, malignancy, and autoimmune disease is unrevealing. Thirdly, in selected patients with suspected large-vessel vasculitis, FDG PET-CT can provide an important diagnostic clue and help guide timely specialist management.

titre: Attenuation of self-produced touch in the posterior insula reflects body image disturbances in anorexia nervosa
resume: UNLABELLED: Body image disturbance (BID) is a core feature of anorexia nervosa (AN), encompassing multimodal distortions in bodily self-perception. Affective touch, a gentle, emotionally salient tactile stimulus, is implicated in body ownership but has not been extensively studied in AN. Affective touch is processed in the insula, an area involved in interoception and bodily self-awareness which has been shown to be altered both structurally and functionally in AN. This study explored the neural mechanisms underlying BID by examining how individuals with AN process self-produced affective touch. Women with AN (n = 44) and age-matched healthy controls (HC, n = 40), participated in a self-other-object touch task during functional brain imaging and filled out questionnaires related to body image and eating disorder symptomatology. During self-touch, individuals with AN exhibited increased activation in the right posterior insula compared to object-touch, whereas HC did not. This insular activation correlated positively with body attitude (BAT) and body size estimation (FRS) scores in AN, but negatively in healthy controls, suggesting divergent processing of self-related tactile input. These findings suggest that posterior insular responses to self-produced touch may reflect disturbed sensory self-processing in AN, and that touch-based mechanisms contributing to body ownership in healthy individuals may operate differently in the context of AN. Broadening BID research beyond the visual modality opens new avenues for translational research and treatment. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-71154-5.

titre: Associations between interoceptive awareness and symptom clusters in patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy: A joint network analysis
resume: OBJECTIVE: To identify symptom clusters among patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy and examine associations and directional dependencies between multidimensional interoceptive awareness and these clusters. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at two campuses of a tertiary hospital in China. Interoceptive awareness and symptom burden were assessed using the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness-2 and the M.D. Anderson Symptom Inventory-Lung Cancer Module. Symptom clusters were identified via exploratory factor analysis. Gaussian graphical network analysis examined associations and bridge centrality, while Bayesian network analysis explored directional probabilistic dependencies. RESULTS: Among 514 patients, 56.4% were aged ≥ 65 years, and 89.5% had stage III-IV disease. Four symptom clusters emerged: psychological, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and neurocognitive. Network analysis showed the psychological and respiratory clusters were most strongly associated with the Not-Worrying (weight = -0.407) and Trusting (weight = -0.430) dimensions, respectively. Not-Worrying, Trusting, and drowsiness showed the highest bridge strengths in the psychological, respiratory, and neurocognitive symptom-level networks, respectively. Bayesian analysis identified connections between interoceptive awareness dimensions and symptoms in the psychological, respiratory, and neurocognitive networks, but no cross-community connections in the gastrointestinal network. At the symptom level, Not-Worrying was linked to pain and sadness within the psychological cluster; respiratory symptoms were linked to Trusting within the respiratory cluster; and multiple interoceptive dimensions were linked to drowsiness within the neurocognitive cluster. CONCLUSIONS: The Not-Worrying and Trusting dimensions emerged as key bridging dimensions for the psychological and respiratory clusters, respectively, while drowsiness was the key bridge symptom within the neurocognitive cluster. These findings highlight dimension-specific patterns linking interoceptive awareness to symptom clusters, offering hypotheses for future longitudinal and intervention research.

titre: Globus Pallidus Externus α-Band Activity Decreases After Deep Brain Stimulation in Clinically Responsive Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Patients
resume: BACKGROUND: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC) is an effective treatment for severe obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Identifying brain readouts of a positive response may guide further DBS optimization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We measured local field potential (LFP) changes from bilateral DBS leads in ten patients with OCD who were implanted at a uniform tractographic network target derived from prior DBS responders. We consistently stimulated dorsal lead contacts in the ALIC white matter while recording LFP from the ventral lead contacts in the grey matter of the anterior globus pallidus externus (GPe), a key node in the basal ganglia nonmotor indirect pathway. RESULTS: After six months of DBS, OCD symptoms decreased by 40% on average across patients, along with a significant decrease in α-activity across both hemispheres. Only one patient did not have an improvement in symptoms, and this was also the only patient who never exhibited a decrease in α in either hemisphere. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that therapeutic ALIC DBS coincides with a stable decrease in limbic-cognitive GPe α-power, which should be further investigated as a potential biomarker of sustained response.
revue: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society

titre: A comprehensive review of the two most commonly studied traditional Chinese medicines for treating Alzheimer's disease
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an age-related neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by progressive cognitive decline. Its pathological hallmarks include senile plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, chronic neuroinflammation, and widespread neuronal loss. Beyond aging, several major hypotheses have been proposed to explain AD pathology, including amyloid cascade hypothesis, tau hyperphosphorylation hypothesis, mitochondrial dysfunction hypothesis, neuroinflammation hypothesis, and microbiota-gut-brain axis hypothesis. These mechanisms often interact with one another, further complicating the disease process. While genetic factors contribute significantly to AD susceptibility, other modifiable risk factors-such as traumatic brain injury, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, and obesity-also play critical roles. Despite decades of intensive research, current drug development for AD remains largely inadequate. Traditional Chinese medicine, with its multi-component and multi-target approach, holds promise as a potential therapeutic strategy for this multifactorial disease. Comparing the biomedical hypothesis with traditional Chinese medicine theory, both frameworks recognize the multifactorial, systemic, and progressive nature of dementia. However, their theories are complementary, with concepts such as "Phlegm and dampness" in traditional Chinese medicine aligning well with amyloid plaques and lipid/protein aggregates. "Qi and essence deficiency" correspond to mitochondrial and metabolic dysfunction. This article reviews recent progress in the therapeutic mechanisms of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction and Liuwei Dihuang Decoction in AD, aiming to provide a reference for future research on AD and the development of traditional Chinese medicine treatment. Future traditional Chinese medicine studies should integrate syndrome-based therapeutic principles with modern systems biology approaches to establish mechanism-based, personalized, and clinically translatable strategies for AD management.
revue: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine

titre: Comparing the Efficacy of Ziziphus jujuba L. Product and Polyethylene Glycol in Elderly People with Functional Constipation: A Single-Blind Randomized Clinical Trial : Short title: Ziziphus jujuba L. and PEG in Elderly Constipation
resume: BACKGROUND: Constipation is one of the most common gastrointestinal disorders, especially among the elderly. The tendency to use food-based remedies is increasing due to their safety and availability. Jujube is a plant recommended for treating constipation. this study was designed to compare the effectiveness of Jujube paste with polyethylene glycol (PEG) in elderly patients with functional constipation (FC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-blind, randomized, active-controlled clinical trial was conducted with 60 elderly individuals aged 60 years or older who had FC. Participants were randomly assigned to either the Jujube paste group (two tablespoons twice daily) or the PEG group (10-20 g/day) and underwent treatment for 4 weeks. Constipation symptoms and stool consistency, as primary outcomes, were assessed using the Rome IV criteria and the Bristol Stool Scale, respectively. Additionally, quality of life, acceptance, and satisfaction were measured. RESULTS: At the end of the study, 26 participants in the PEG group and 25 in the Jujube paste group completed the trial. When comparing each group to their respective baseline, all clinical constipation symptoms, as defined by Rome IV criteria, showed significant improvement in both groups (P ≤ 0.002). Defecation frequency improved in both groups, with a significantly greater increase in the PEG group. This between-group difference remained significant after adjustment for baseline defecation frequency and education level (adjusted mean difference, 5.20 bowel movements/week; 95% CI, 1.53-8.87; P = 0.006). Quality of life improved in both groups, with a greater improvement observed in the Jujube group. Acceptance and satisfaction rates were significantly higher in the Jujube group compared to the PEG group (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Jujube paste may improve constipation symptoms in elderly patients with functional constipation and showed higher acceptance and satisfaction than PEG in this short-term trial. Larger, longer, and preferably blinded trials are needed to confirm efficacy.

fiche.verdict: La pâte de jujube améliore la constipation fonctionnelle des personnes âgées avec une meilleure satisfaction que le PEG, mais nécessite confirmation.

Acceptation et satisfaction significativement plus élevées pour le jujube (P < 0,05).
fiche.conclusion: Jujube paste may improve constipation symptoms in elderly patients with functional constipation and showed higher acceptance and satisfaction than PEG in this short-term trial.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Utile pour la prise en charge non pharmacologique de la constipation en gastro.

titre: Management of diarrhea in patients receiving liposomal irinotecan-based regimens: a narrative review of mechanisms, clinical impact, and evidence-based strategies
resume: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin (5-FU/LV) represents the standard second-line treatment for metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC) following progression on gemcitabine-based therapy. Despite its demonstrated survival benefit, diarrhea remains a clinically significant toxicity that can compromise dose intensity, treatment adherence, and quality of life. This review provides a comprehensive and updated overview of the pathophysiology, incidence, and evidence-based management of diarrhea associated with nal-IRI-based regimens. METHODS: A structured narrative review of the available literature was performed, including prospective randomized trials, supportive care guidelines, pharmacogenomic data, and emerging translational evidence. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and the limited number of nal-IRI-specific supportive care trials, a formal meta-analysis was not feasible. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Diarrhea associated with nal-IRI is mechanistically complex, encompassing acute cholinergic and delayed secretory components mediated by SN-38-induced mucosal injury and enterohepatic recirculation. Grade 3-4 diarrhea occurs in approximately 13-20% of patients across major pancreatic cancer trials. Evidence-based management strategies are presented, including pharmacologic interventions (atropine, loperamide, octreotide, fluoroquinolones), supportive care, and dose modification protocols. Emerging approaches-including gut microbiome modulation, beta-glucuronidase inhibitors, and novel antisecretory agents-are also reviewed. CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary, proactive management approach-beginning before the first nal-IRI dose-is essential to minimize diarrhea-related morbidity and optimize treatment outcomes. Integration of pharmacogenomic data and emerging biomarkers-particularly UGT1A1*28 genotyping and gut microbiome β-glucuronidase activity profiling-may further individualize risk stratification and management in this patient population.

titre: Prevalence and clinical correlates of obsessive-compulsive disorder in central nervous system autoimmune demyelinating diseases: A cross-sectional observational Study
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a disabling psychiatric comorbidity that may be underrecognized in multiple sclerosis (MS) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD). Evidence regarding its prevalence and associated factors in these populations remains limited. OBJECTIVES: To estimate the prevalence of OCD and examine its clinical and demographic correlates in patients with MS and NMOSD in an Iranian cohort. DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study. METHODS: This cross-sectional study (January 2018-December 2024) included patients with MS and NMOSD from Kashani Hospital and Hakim MS Clinic, Isfahan, Iran. MS and NMOSD diagnoses were made according to the 2017 McDonald and 2015 IPND criteria, respectively. OCD was diagnosed by certified psychiatrists per DSM-IV. Demographic, clinical, and neuropsychological data were extracted from interviews and medical records. Group comparisons were performed using t-tests or χ2 tests, followed by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Of 4,759 patients (mean age, 42.9 years; 77.1% female), 4,460 had MS (3,502 with relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS), 212 with primary progressive MS (PPMS), and 746 with secondary progressive MS (SPMS)), and 299 had NMOSD. OCD prevalence was 15.4% in MS, highest in RRMS (17.8%), and 12.7% in NMOSD. Across all participants, female sex (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.04-1.64), higher educational attainment, sensory vs. motor onset symptoms, migraine (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.16-1.83), and hypothyroidism (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01-1.65), lower EDSS (OR per 1-unit: 0.78, 95% CI 0.70 - 0.88), and shorter disease duration (OR per 1-year: 0.98, 95% CI 0.97 - 1.00) were significantly associated with higher odds of OCD. CONCLUSION: OCD is frequently observed among patients with MS and NMOSD and shows distinct clinical associations, including migraine, hypothyroidism, sensory onset phenotype, and lower disability. Recognition of psychiatric comorbidities in these disorders may facilitate more comprehensive and individualized clinical management.

titre: Neurocognitive Performance and Peripheral microRNA Expression in Schizophrenia and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Comparative Study
resume: INTRODUCTION: Schizophrenia and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) are two chronic psychiatric disorders associated with partially overlapping cognitive impairments and neurobiological processes. The aim of this study was to comparatively examine neurocognitive performance and the expression levels of selected peripheral microRNAs (miR-134, miR-137, miR-150, miR-502, and miR-1306) in patients with schizophrenia and OCD relative to healthy controls, and to exploratorily assess potential heterogeneity within OCD by considering autogenous and reactive subtypes. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 20 patients with schizophrenia, 20 patients with OCD, and 20 healthy controls matched for age, sex, and years of education. All participants underwent a standardized neurocognitive test battery assessing executive functions, attention, processing speed, and verbal memory. Plasma miRNA levels were measured from peripheral blood samples using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Within the OCD group, autogenous and reactive obsession subtypes were additionally analyzed. RESULTS: Both schizophrenia and OCD groups showed poorer performance than healthy controls in measures of attention, processing speed, and executive functioning. Verbal memory impairment was more widespread in the schizophrenia group, whereas it was more limited in the OCD group. After controlling for depression and anxiety levels as covariates, many neurocognitive differences remained significant. miR-134 levels were lower in the OCD group, while miR-502 levels were lower in both the OCD and schizophrenia groups compared with healthy controls. Exploratory analyses yielded limited findings suggesting a possible association between miR-502 and executive function measures. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest a more widespread pattern of neurocognitive impairment in schizophrenia, whereas OCD appears to involve a more selective cognitive impairment characterized predominantly by executive dysfunction, with verbal memory difficulties potentially related to executive processes. Alterations in selected miRNA levels may provide exploratory clues regarding shared and distinct peripheral molecular processes, while the potential relationship between miR-502 and executive functioning warrants confirmation in larger and longitudinal studies.

titre: Validity and reliability of the Turkish adaptation of the diagnostic interview for anxiety, mood, and OCD and related neuropsychiatric disorders: child and adolescent version (DIAMOND-KID)
resume: BACKGROUND: The Diagnostic Interview for Anxiety, Mood, and OCD and Related Neuropsychiatric Disorders: Child and Adolescent Version (DIAMOND-KID) is a DSM-5-based semi-structured diagnostic interview for the assessment of psychiatric disorders in children and adolescents aged 6-18 years. Despite its broad diagnostic coverage, evidence regarding the psychometric properties of the DIAMOND-KID across different cultural and linguistic contexts remains limited. This study aimed to examine the validity and reliability of the Turkish adaptation of the DIAMOND-KID in a clinical sample. METHODS: A total of 195 children and adolescents aged 6-18 years were administered the DIAMOND-KID and an independent clinical interview. Interrater and test-retest reliability analyses were conducted in subsamples of 22 and 51 participants, respectively. Participants and their parents/caregivers completed self-report measures assessing symptoms related to the disorders evaluated within the DIAMOND-KID. Diagnostic agreement was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficient. RESULTS: Agreement between the DIAMOND-KID and clinical interview diagnoses, evaluated across diagnostic categories with sufficient case numbers, ranged from good to excellent (κ = 0.61-0.93). Interrater reliability ranged from fair to excellent, while test-retest reliability ranged from good to excellent (κ = 0.70-1.00). Effect sizes obtained from comparisons of self-report measures related to current diagnoses were generally large. CONCLUSIONS: The findings support the validity and reliability of the Turkish adaptation of the DIAMOND-KID for assessing a broad spectrum of psychiatric disorders in children and adolescents aged 6-18 years in Türkiye.

titre: Efficacy and Neural Mechanisms of Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) for Depression: A Systematic Review and Qualitative Synthesis
resume: BACKGROUND: Depression is a psychiatric disorder characterized by mood disturbances and cognitive impairment. Existing treatments, such as pharmacotherapy and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), often present limitations, including delayed onset of efficacy and low adherence. Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), a psychotherapy originally developed for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), has shown potential in the treatment of depression. METHODS: This systematic review synthesized evidence from 27 studies (14 randomized controlled trials, 10 single-arm studies, and three controlled studies) published between January 1990 and December 2024, integrating both behavioral outcomes and findings on neural mechanisms. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. RESULTS: The findings indicate that EMDR demonstrates potential efficacy in alleviating depressive symptoms. The included studies involved diverse populations, including individuals with major depressive disorder, comorbid conditions, and trauma exposure, suggesting potential applicability across a range of clinical contexts. Preliminary neurobiological evidence has explored possible mechanisms involving modulation of prefrontal-limbic circuits and the integration of traumatic memories, providing initial insights into its therapeutic effects. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports EMDR as a promising intervention for depression. However, further large-scale, high-quality studies are required to confirm its generalizability, identify optimal target populations, and clarify its underlying neurobiological mechanisms.

titre: Effects of mindfulness-based childbirth preparation education on psychosocial outcomes in pregnancy: a randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Mindfulness-based interventions have been increasingly integrated into antenatal education programs to improve maternal psychosocial well-being. However, evidence regarding their effects on perceived stress, depressive symptoms, childbirth self-efficacy, and postpartum post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) remains limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Mindfulness-Based Childbirth Preparation Education (MBCPE) on psychosocial outcomes in primiparous pregnant women. METHODS: This study was designed as a prospective, randomized controlled trial. The study was completed with 74 pregnant women, including 36 participants in the intervention group and 38 participants in the control group. The intervention group received Mindfulness-Based Childbirth Preparation Education over eight weeks, while the control group received Information-Based Childbirth Preparation Education over four weeks. Outcome measures included the Perceived Stress Scale, Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, childbirth self-efficacy, and postpartum PTSD symptoms. Statistical analyses were conducted to compare group differences, with significance set at p 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Mindfulness-Based Childbirth Preparation Education appears to be effective in reducing perceived stress and depressive symptoms during pregnancy and the postpartum period. However, it does not appear to provide an additional benefit for childbirth self-efficacy compared with the control group. No significant between-group difference was observed in postpartum PTSD symptoms assessed at the fourth postpartum week. These findings provide preliminary support for the inclusion of mindfulness-based components in antenatal education to enhance maternal psychosocial well-being. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on November 1, 2023 (NCT06111716).

titre: Xifenghuashi formula ameliorates diarrhea predominant-irritable bowel syndrome by modulating the gut microbiota and the bile acid-FXR-FGF axis: A human trial and an animal experiment
resume: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Xifenghuashi formula (XFHS), a traditional Chinese medicine, shows promising effects in treating diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D), but its mechanisms are unclear. This study aims to confirm XFHS's efficacy in IBS-D treatment and its influence on the gut microbiota-bile acid-farnesoid X receptor (FXR)-fibroblast growth factor19/15 (FGF19/15) axis. EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted to assess XFHS's effectiveness. In animal experiments, IBS-D rat models were induced by oral gavage of senna along with restraint stress and divided into six groups: the IBS-D group, XFHS group (administered XFHS), antibiotic group (administered antibiotics), A + XFHS group (administered antibiotics and XFHS), FGF401 (a FGFR4 receptor inhibitor) group (administered FGF401), and F + XFHS group (administered FGF401 and XFHS). Human and rat fecal samples, along with rat liver and terminal ileum samples, were analyzed for bile acid concentration, 16S rRNA sequencing, and western blotting. RESULTS AND CONCLUSION: XFHS could enhance the abundance of bile salt hydrolase (BSH)-active bacteria and decrease the abundance of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs)-producing bacteria in the IBS-D patients to a certain extent, and the same trend was found in the IBS-D rats. XFHS reduced the concentration of total fecal bile acids (including primary, conjugated, and unconjugated bile acids) in IBS-D patients and rats. However, this effect was eliminated by fibroblast growth factor receptor 4 (FGFR4) blockade in IBS-D rats. Furthermore, XFHS increased the protein expression of FXR and FGF15 in the terminal ileum, FGFR4 in the liver, and decreased the expression of cytochrome P450 7A1 (CYP7A1) in the liver. Overall, XFHS alleviated symptoms of IBS-D and restored the homeostasis of the gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism by regulating the gut microbiota-bile acid-FXR-FGF15-FGFR4 axis.
revue: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine

titre: Rural-Urban Differences in Health Status of Black Women Veterans With Military Sexual Trauma in Primary Care
resume: PURPOSE: Investigate rural-urban differences in physical and mental health conditions and comorbidities of Black women Veterans with military sexual trauma (MST) to help inform recommendations for personalizing care and addressing access barriers. METHODS: Using Veterans Health Administration primary care data, we examined differences in diagnosed mental and physical health conditions and social drivers of health for 40,580 Black women Veterans with MST during fiscal years 2021 and 2022 across rurality (i.e., rural/highly rural [13.9%] or urban settings [86%]). Rural-urban differences were assessed using logistic regression models. FINDINGS: There were high rates of physical (88.4%) and mental health diagnoses (85.4%) and physical and mental health comorbidity (77.7%). Diagnosis profiles of rural and urban Black women with MST were largely similar, though there were small, significant rural-urban differences. Rural Black women had slightly higher odds than their urban peers of being diagnosed with endocrine and cardiac diagnoses. By contrast, rural Black women had lower odds than urban Black women of receiving diagnoses involving reproductive and gastrointestinal system conditions, and receiving a Z-code related to a social driver of health. CONCLUSIONS: Black women Veterans with MST experienced high rates of health diagnoses that likely affect their quality of life. Given small differences and high comorbidity among the groups, there is no clear indication that different approaches to care for rural and urban Black women Veterans with MST are warranted. Adequately screening, assessing, and treating physical and mental health concerns in this population is vital.
revue: The Journal of rural health : official journal of the American Rural Health Association and the National Rural Health Care Association

titre: Lethal and sublethal effects of Alexandrium affine and Alexandrium pseudogonyaulax on juveniles of the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas
resume: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) represent a critical threat to bivalve aquaculture. Some species of the genus Alexandrium can produce phycotoxins and/or bioactive extracellular compounds (BECs), which may adversely affect marine organisms, including commercially important bivalves in natural environments and aquaculture, particularly during early developmental stages. This study evaluated the effects of exposure to cells and cell lysates of Alexandrium affine and Alexandrium pseudogonyaulax on the survival, feeding behavior, and tissue integrity in juveniles of the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas. Bioassays were conducted to determine inactivity and mortality rates, median lethal concentration (LC50), and clearance rate (CR) while histopathological analyses were performed to detect tissue lesions. Cells of A. affine caused 85% mortality at 6000 cells/mL after 30 h, with a LC50 of 3696 ± 767 cells/mL. Juveniles maintained active filtration, with CR values similar to the control, resulting in severe tissue damage, including gill atrophy and degeneration of the digestive epithelium. In contrast, A. affine cell lysates caused no significant increase in inactivity relative to controls. Exposure to A. pseudogonyaulax cells induced avoidance response in juveniles, characterized by reduced CR, increased inactivity, and mucus production. However, A. pseudogonyaulax cell lysates were highly lethal, causing 100% mortality after 32 h, with an LC50 of 2499 ± 879 cells mL⁻¹ at 20 h, and anatomical disorganization. Overall, A. affine induced lethality through ingestion of intact cells, whereas A. pseudogonyaulax became more harmful after cell lysis, highlighting the risk of both species to oyster seed viability.

titre: Expert consensus on endoscopic diagnosis and treatment of insulinoma (2026)
resume: Insulinoma is a rare functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor characterized by excessive insulin secretion, which causes hypoglycemia. Recent advances in endoscopic technology have provided essential tools for the diagnosis and treatment of insulinoma. Early diagnosis and timely intervention, particularly endoscopy-guided intervention in selected patients, may improve clinical outcomes and quality of life. Although existing national and international guidelines mention insulinoma, standardized criteria for its endoscopic diagnosis and treatment remain lacking. Therefore, under the leadership of the Digestive Endoscopy Branch of the Chinese Medical Association, experts from related fields were invited to develop the Expert Consensus on Endoscopic Diagnosis and Treatment for Insulinoma (2026). The development process included a comprehensive review of recent national and international evidence-based literature, with the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations assessed according to the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system. This consensus emphasizes endoscopy-guided diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. It aims to provide practical recommendations and operational guidance for standardized endoscopic diagnosis and treatment of insulinoma, thereby advancing the quality of endoscopic care for this condition in China.
auteurs: Digestive Endoscopy Branch of the Chinese Medical Association

titre: Endogenous oxyntomodulin in metabolic homeostasis and clinical utility as a prognostic biomarker: a systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: While the role of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and its exogenous analogues in the obesity treatment is established, the physiology of endogenous oxyntomodulin (OXM), a dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist, remains poorly defined. This systematic review aims to synthesize the current evidence on OXM secretion, its dysregulation in obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and its clinical utility. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed and Web of Science was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261308863). Studies on endogenous OXM in humans in various metabolic states (healthy volunteers, obesity, T2DM) and after interventions (diet, bariatric surgery, pharmacotherapy) were included in the analysis. Particular attention was devoted to the reliability of the analytical methods employed to ensure accurate interpretation of concentration dynamics. RESULTS: Available evidence indicates that OXM is a nutrient-stimulated hormone whose secretion depends on the caloric load and macronutrient composition of the stimulus, with higher sensitivity to lipid, which induces a stronger and longer secretory response than glucose. A reduction in OXM secretion was suggested in post-pancreatitis diabetes and, less consistently, in T2DM, where the highest-quality (mass-spectrometry-referenced) data were mixed; its independence from body mass index (BMI) could not be firmly established. Bariatric surgery induces a strong and sustained increase in postprandial OXM con-centrations, and early postoperative OXM dynamics were associated with long-term weight loss, improved lipid profile, and changes in dietary preferences, and, in small cohorts, predicted weight loss at least as well as GLP-1 (a hypothesis-generating observation). CONCLUSIONS: OXM may act as a nutrient-sensitive signal, whose secretion appears reduced in metabolic dysfunction and increased after bariatric surgery. OXM shows promise as a candidate predictive biomarker of obesity-treatment response; a potential role in cardiovascular risk stratification remains to be validated in outcome-linked studies and is proposed here only as a future direction. Nevertheless, its implementation in clinical practice requires standardization of pre-analytical and measurement procedures.

titre: Structural integrity facilitates multi-layer modulation of the brain-metabolome-microbiota network by Lilium lancifolium-derived vesicles in depression
resume: BACKGROUND: Plant-derived vesicles (PDVs) have emerged as promising natural nanotherapeutics with multi-component cargo profiles and potential biological activity. However, their delivery behavior and mechanisms of action, particularly in complex neuro-immune-metabolic disorders such as depression, remain incompletely understood. This study investigates the therapeutic efficacy, biodistribution, and multi-layer modulatory network of Lilium lancifolium-derived vesicles (LLEs) in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced depression models, with a focus on vesicular structural integrity and brain-metabolome-microbiota associations. METHODS: LLEs were isolated from fresh Lilium lancifolium Thunb and comprehensively characterized in terms of morphology, particle size, zeta potential, particle-to-protein ratio, proteomic cargo and simulated gastrointestinal stability. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in CUMS mice and LPS-challenged neuronal cell models using behavioral tests, histopathology, immunofluorescence, and multi-omics approaches (hippocampal transcriptomics, serum metabolomics, and gut metagenomics). Cellular internalization was assessed using pharmacological inhibitors and fluorescent tracking. Brain-associated delivery was evaluated using an in vitro BBB Transwell model, ex vivo brain imaging, and LC-MS detection of LLEs-associated small molecules in perfused brain tissues. The contribution of intact vesicular architecture was assessed by comparing native LLEs with disrupted LLEs (D-LLEs) and single bioactive components. Integrative multi-omics analysis was used to construct an associative brain-metabolome-microbiota modulatory network. RESULTS: LLEs exhibited nanoscale vesicle-like morphology, a negatively charged surface, and partial environmental resilience, with stability in simulated salivary and gastric fluids but vulnerability to aggregation under simulated intestinal conditions. Proteomic profiling and western blot validation supported the presence of vesicle-associated protein components, including HSP70. Intact LLEs showed stronger neuroprotective, anti-neuroinflammatory, and antidepressant-like effects than D-LLEs, supporting the functional contribution of intact vesicular architecture. Cellular uptake assays suggested that macropinocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis may contribute to LLE internalization. In vitro BBB Transwell model, ex vivo brain imaging, and LC-MS tissue quantification supported the brain-associated delivery potential of LLEs. Multi-omics integration revealed LLEs-associated changes in brain inflammatory and lipid metabolic pathways, circulating metabolites, and gut microbial composition, suggesting an associative brain-metabolome-microbiota modulatory network. CONCLUSION: This study identifies LLEs as a class of plant-derived nanovesicles that integrate structural stability with intrinsic neuroprotective potential. The present study supports the importance of intact vesicular architecture and provides an integrated, evidence-calibrated framework linking LLEs treatment to central neuroimmune modulation, systemic metabolic shifts, and gut microbiota remodeling. These findings provide a basis for the future development of plant-derived vesicles as natural nanovesicle platforms for neuroimmune and metabolic modulation, while highlighting the need for further causal validation of the proposed multi-layer regulatory network.

titre: Role of small intestinal bacteria overgrowth in irritable bowel syndrome and anxiety: a retrospective Electronic Health Record (EHR)- based cohort study using triNetX
resume: AIMS: The goal of this study is to examine the relationship between small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with their subsequent risk of developing generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). METHODOLOGY: Data for this retrospective study was obtained through TriNetX, a global health research network that aggregates de-identified electronic health records from over 100 million patients across multiple healthcare organizations. Two cohorts of 7716 patients were identified. Cohort 1 consisted of IBS patients with SIBO and Cohort 2 consisted of IBS patients without SIBO. Patients included were aged 18 to 50 years. Patients with pre-existing diagnoses of GAD, panic disorder, or depressive episodes before IBS onset were excluded. Cohorts were matched for sex, race, ethnicity, gastroesophageal reflux disease, non-infective enteritis and colitis, and proton pump inhibitor use through logistic regression models. RESULTS: IBS patients with SIBO (Cohort 1) demonstrated a GAD incidence of 6.36% compared to 4.71% in those without SIBO (Cohort 2), yielding an absolute risk difference of 1.66% (95% CI: 0.938%-2.38%, p<0.0001). Logistic regression revealed an odds ratio of 1.377 (95% CI: 1.197-1.583) for GAD development in Cohort 1. Cox proportional hazards modeling demonstrated a hazard ratio of 1.301 (95% CI: 1.136-1.491, p=0.0008), indicating that IBS patients with SIBO faced a significantly elevated and persistent risk of GAD development over the 15-year observation period. DISCUSSION: IBS patients with comorbid SIBO have a significantly elevated risk of developing GAD compared to IBS patients without SIBO. These findings suggest that SIBO may amplify gut-brain axis dysfunction beyond what is observed in IBS alone.

titre: The RELIEF-trial for patients with upper abdominal pain: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial to investigate the effectiveness of a web-based self-management tool compared with usual care for reduction of healthcare utilization and improvement of patient-reported outcomes
resume: BACKGROUND: Dutch healthcare faces increasing demand with constrained resources. Upper abdominal pain (UAP) is a highly prevalent symptom leading to substantial healthcare utilization and costs, with over 100,000 related hospital diagnoses annually in the Netherlands. In most cases, UAP is attributable to functional dyspepsia, irritable bowel syndrome, or symptomatic gallstone disease The overlapping symptom patterns of these diseases, which generally affect similar populations, leads to difficulties in diagnosing and an increased risk of exposing patients to unnecessary interventions and increase in healthcare costs. Web-based education and lifestyle interventions are used in several high-prevalence disorders, but evidence supporting it is effectiveness for managing patients with UAP is lacking due to its heterogeneous diagnostic nature. This trial evaluates whether a web-based self-management tool can reduce healthcare utilization by improving patient education and diagnostic selection in UAP. METHODS: The RELIEF-trial is a multicenter, randomized, open-label superiority trial. Adult patients referred to hospital with UAP are eligible, except those with alarm symptoms. Participants are randomized to either usual care or the RELIEF intervention. Usual care is provided at the treating physician's discretion. The intervention group receives access to a web-based self-management tool prior to the first outpatient visit, providing structured information on UAP, treatment options, and lifestyle advice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients who will undergo diagnostic or treatment intervention within 12 months. Secondary outcomes include time to diagnosis, outpatient clinic- or emergency room visits, pain severity, imaging use (Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), morbidity and complications, and patient-reported outcomes. DISCUSSION: The RELIEF trial is the first randomized controlled trial comparing usual care with a web-based self-management tool in patients with UAP. It will assess whether web-based education improves self-management and safely reduces diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in patients without alarm symptoms. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06002516 (ClinicalTrials.gov), Date of registration: 2023-08-21.

titre: Use of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions: an evidence map of systematic reviews
resume: BACKGROUND: There is high- or moderate-certainty evidence that massage therapy is beneficial for certain painful conditions. Massage therapy has also been evaluated for a range of non-painful health conditions, but the extent and certainty of this evidence are less well characterized. We mapped the systematic reviews, conclusions, and certainty (quality or strength) of evidence for outcomes of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions. METHODS: Computerized search of PubMed, AMED, CINAHL, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Web of Science from July 2018 to July 2024. This evidence map updates a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) report that covered massage therapy reviews published through July 2018. Study selection included systematic reviews of massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions that formally rated the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting the conclusions. Systematic reviews of sports massage therapy, osteopathy, dry cupping/dry needling, and internal massage therapy (e.g., for pelvic floor pain), and self-administered massage therapy techniques (e.g., foam rolling) were ineligible. Main outcomes and measures include health condition, number of included studies, intervention, comparison group, conclusions, and certainty of evidence. RESULTS: A total of 13 systematic reviews of massage therapy for 8 non-painful adult health conditions were identified. Of 190 full-text reviews, 20 used a formal method to rate the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting their conclusions; 7 reviews overlapped in health condition, resulting in 13 included reviews. Across these, one conclusion about abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation was rated as high certainty of evidence. There were 4 conclusions from 3 reviews rated as moderate certainty of evidence: 2 conclusions in 1 review about acupressure and auricular acupressure for improving sleep quality in patients with cancer, 1 conclusion about acupressure for sleep latency and fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and 1 conclusion about massage improving depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia; all remaining conclusions were rated as low or very low certainty of evidence. Evidence on adverse events was collected by 7 of 13 (54%) reviews; serious adverse events attributed to massage therapy were not identified in those reviews, but adverse event data were often incomplete or inconsistently described. CONCLUSIONS: Only a small number of systematic reviews reported high- or moderate-certainty evidence supporting the potential benefit of massage therapy for specific non-painful adult health conditions. High-certainty evidence was limited to abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation, whereas moderate-certainty evidence indicated that acupressure and auricular acupressure may improve sleep quality in patients with cancer, acupressure may improve sleep latency and decrease fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and massage therapy may reduce depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia. For most other non-painful adult health conditions evaluated, available conclusions are supported only by low- or very low-certainty evidence. Additional high-quality research is needed to strengthen the evidence base for massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions, particularly for conditions and outcomes that currently lack at least moderate-certainty evidence.

titre: Probiotic-based sequential delivery system for gut-brain co-therapy against inflammatory bowel disease-associated anxiety/depression
resume: With the emergence of the gut-brain axis, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is no longer simply regarded as a localized intestinal disease but as a systemic disorder intimately associated with psychiatric comorbidities, including anxiety and depression. However, conventional therapeutic strategies predominantly target localized colonic inflammation, which often yields suboptimal outcomes. This highlights a critical need for gut-brain co-therapy to achieve comprehensive IBD management. Based on our observation that indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) possesses the potential to attenuate hippocampal neuroinflammation and subsequently modulate intestinal inflammation via the acetylcholine pathway, we engineered a gut-brain co-therapy delivery platform (CB-ASA/IAA/L). This system comprises Clostridium butyricum (CB) loaded with 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), encapsulated by a pH-responsive Eudragit L100-55 layer incorporating IAA. This microecological preparation is based on effective protection and delivery of CB, achieving the delivery of IAA to the brain and 5-ASA to the colon simultaneously. This sequential-release delivery system achieved intestinal barrier repair, promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, and restored Th17/Treg balance to recover intestinal homeostasis, while simultaneously alleviating anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in colitis mice. Importantly, the system demonstrated a robust ability to prevent inflammatory recurrence, a major clinical challenge in IBD treatment. This research offers a new avenue for the effective treatment of IBD-associated anxiety/depression by coordinating neuroimmune modulation with local intestinal repair.

titre: Relationship between fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and microbial SCFA pathways with depressive symptoms in Dutch adults
resume: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including acetate, butyrate and propionate, have been linked to depression. It remains unclear whether fecal SCFA levels or predicted SCFA synthesis and degradation are associated with depressive symptoms. We explored these relationships in a Dutch, non-clinical adult sample, considering systolic blood pressure (SBP) as a potential moderator. We studied 200 adults (<50 years old) from the HELIUS cohort with high or low SBP, matched on age, sex and BMI. Fecal SCFA concentrations were quantified by HPLC. SCFA synthesis and degradation pathways were inferred from 16S rRNA gene sequencing using PICRUSt and mapped to gut-brain modules. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Negative binomial regression was used to explore associations between depressive symptoms and SCFA measures, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates, with SBP as a potential moderator. In the high SBP group, higher depressive symptom severity was associated with lower acetate concentrations, but this association did not survive multiple-testing (IRR = 0.82, 95% CI [0.69-0.96], p = 0.016, p-adjusted = 0.063). No significant associations were observed in the low SBP group, and similarly no association was found in either group for other fecal SCFA ratios or predicted SCFA pathways. Our exploratory analyses do not provide conclusive evidence for associations between fecal SCFA concentrations or ratios, or SCFA pathways, and depressive symptoms in this non-clinical subsample, although the acetate finding suggests a potential signal influenced by metabolic status. Future research in clinical populations is needed to inform gut-targeted interventions in depression.

titre: Gut microbiome heterogeneity in autism spectrum disorder: immune-brain interfaces, behavioral phenotypes, and translational implications
resume: BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is clinically heterogeneous, and gastrointestinal symptoms, immune perturbation, microbial metabolites, and behavioral variation may intersect in biologically informative ways. The gut microbiome has therefore attracted substantial translational interest, although interpretation remains constrained by marked between-study heterogeneity, uneven phenotyping, and causal claims that often exceed the available evidence. MAIN TEXT: This review brings together human cohort studies, family-aware analyses, multi-omics datasets, preclinical mechanistic work, controlled interventions, and selected registered trials. We followed a transparent targeted narrative-synthesis approach, drawing on PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov searches performed on 2 July 2026 (bibliographic date range, 1 January 2012 to 30 June 2026), predefined inclusion criteria, and an explicit distinction between mechanistic layers and evidentiary strength. CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, the evidence supports ASD microbiome heterogeneity as a framework for translational subgroup stratification, rather than as a basis for diagnostic or therapeutic claims. The revised framework outlines how host susceptibility, ecological organization, barrier-immune-metabolic relay biology, endophenotype expression, and translational responsiveness may be tested prospectively while accounting for diet, bowel phenotype, medication exposure, sex, developmental stage, and safety outcomes.

titre: The relationship between birth trauma and perinatal mental health: a cross-sectional study
resume: BACKGROUND: Globally, 130 million live births occur annually, including 3.6 million in the U.S. in 2023. While many women anticipate a positive birth experience, approximately 45% report birth trauma-a subjective experience that can occur regardless of medical complications. Birth trauma may increase risk for perinatal mental health disorders (PMHDs) such as depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), bipolar disorder, and psychosis. Existing research primarily focuses on birth trauma and perinatal PTSD, with limited exploration of its relationship to other PMHDs. This study examined associations between birth trauma and five PMHDs. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in December 2024 using Amazon Mechanical Turk and REDCap. Participants (N = 249) were U.S.-based women, 4 weeks-7 months postpartum. Birth trauma was assessed using the City Birth Trauma Scale; PMHDs were measured with validated tools including EPDS, PASS, DOCS, and MDQ. Modified Poisson and linear regressions, adjusted for demographic and birth variables, examined associations. RESULTS: Birth trauma was reported by 21.3% of respondents. PMHD prevalence was high: depression (84.7%), anxiety (81.9%), OCD (93.6%), bipolar disorder (10%), and psychosis (3.2%). Birth trauma was significantly associated with increased risk for depression (RR = 1.15), anxiety (RR = 1.34), bipolar disorder (RR = 9.59), and psychosis; OCD risk increase was non-significant. Symptom severity scores were higher across all PMHDs among women reporting birth trauma. CONCLUSION: Birth trauma is positively associated with elevated risk and symptom severity of multiple PMHDs beyond PTSD. Findings highlight the need for integrated postpartum screening and trauma-informed interventions to improve maternal mental health outcomes.

titre: Gut microbiota heterogeneity is linked to social dysfunction in severe alcohol use disorder
resume: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Gut microbiota and social functioning are both substantially altered in individuals with severe alcohol use disorder (sAUD). However, it remains unclear whether inter-individual variability in gut microbiota composition identifies biologically and clinically distinct subgroups of patients, particularly in relation to social functioning. Based on previous investigations of gut-brain axis interactions in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other psychiatric disorders, we investigated whether gut microbiota-based stratification is associated with differences in social functioning and biological profiles in sAUD. The social dimension is crucial for relapse risk after detoxification. DESIGN: Forty-six sAUD patients undergoing detoxification were stratified into dysbiotic and non-dysbiotic subgroups based on gut microbiota β-diversity. Bray-Curtis distances were computed and principal coordinate analysis performed. Patients were classified as dysbiotic when their first-axis score deviated > 1.65 standard deviations from the healthy subjects (HS) distribution. Groups were compared with HS in a cross-sectional design. Metabolomic profiles, inflammatory markers, dietary habits, psychological symptoms, and social functioning were compared. We applied a comprehensive assessment of social functioning combining sociodemographic data, an emotional intelligence questionnaire, a social cognition task and personal social networks (evaluated through mapping techniques). RESULTS: One third of the sAUD patients exhibited microbial alterations. The non-dysbiotic subgroup showed an overall microbial composition more similar to HS than the dysbiotic subgroup. The dysbiotic patients were younger, leaner, and reported higher alcohol craving compared to the non-dysbiotic patients. The dysbiotic subgroup also displayed altered metabolomic and nutritional profiles and a higher plasma IL-8 level. Interestingly, we observed a coherent profile of severe impairments across social functioning indexes in the dysbiotic group: they had lower sociability scores, displayed impairment in social cognition (with greater difficulty in spontaneously considering another's perspective), were more often divorced/separated and unemployed, and had a smaller, less cohesive, and less diverse personal social network compared to the non-dysbiotic group. CONCLUSION: We found a significant relationship between gut dysbiosis and various aspects of social functioning in sAUD. These findings are associative and do not establish causality, but suggest that targeting the gut microbiota could offer a novel approach to address social impairments in sAUD. Video Abstract.

titre: Efficacy and safety of theta-burst stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: INTRODUCTION: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a prevalent psychiatric disorder characterized by intrusive obsessions and repetitive, compulsive behaviors that are difficult to inhibit. Several studies have evaluated the efficacy of theta-burst stimulation (TBS) for alleviating OCD symptoms, reporting potential outcomes in both symptom reduction and functional improvement. This study aimed to synthesize evidence from published randomized clinical trials (RCTs) regarding the clinical effectiveness of TBS in patients with OCD. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Embase databases. A total of eight RCTs and one open-label study were included, each comparing TBS with sham stimulation in relation to the severity of obsessive and compulsive symptoms. The primary measure was the Yale-Brown Obsessive-Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) between two groups from baseline to the endpoint (immediate effect) and from baseline to the end of follow-up period (long-term effect). The secondary outcome was depressive symptoms reported by The Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D). Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs), while the dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs). RESULTS: This review included eight RCTs and one open-label study, comprising a total of 305 patients. According to the immediate action of TBS, it showed significant improvement in only the obsession sub-scale (MD = -1.04, 95%CI [-1.87, -0.22], p = 0.01, I2= 0%). While according to the long-term action, TBS showed significant improvement in 'obsession' sub-scale (MD = -1.63, 95%CI [-2.81, -0.44], p = 0.007, I² = 31%) and 'compulsion' sub-scale (MD = -1.68, 95%CI [-2.57, -0.8], p = 0.0002, I² = 0%), respectively. Also, it showed a significant reduction of HAM-D (MD = -2.16, 95%CI [ -3.89, -0.43], p = 0.01, I2 = 15%). CONCLUSION: The results showed that TBS could be effective as an adjunctive treatment for OCD in relieving the obsessive-compulsive symptoms, especially the long-term action with well-tolerated adverse effects.

titre: Claims-defined hepatic steatosis compatible with MASLD and reproductive outcomes after the first observed embryo transfer: a Korean nationwide cohort study
resume: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly prevalent among women of reproductive age; however, its association with reproductive outcomes after in vitro fertilization (IVF) remains insufficiently characterized in population-level data. We evaluated pre-index claims-defined hepatic steatosis compatible with MASLD as the primary exposure of interest in relation to first claims-identified pregnancy and time to first claims-identified live birth after the first observed embryo transfer (ET). Inflammatory bowel disease, irritable bowel syndrome, and autoimmune hepatobiliary disease were included as gastrointestinal and hepatic comparators. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data from 2017 to 2024. Among 601,664 women with an infertility diagnosis (ICD-10 N97), 122,134 underwent a first observed ET between 2019 and 2023 after predefined exclusions. Exposures were ascertained from pre-index claims using disease-specific ascertainment windows. The co-primary outcomes were first claims-identified pregnancy and time to first claims-identified live birth after the index ET. Claims-defined pregnancy loss was a secondary outcome among women with a first claims-identified pregnancy. Associations were analyzed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW)-adjusted Cox and logistic regression models, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and E-value analyses. RESULTS: Among 122,134 women (mean age, 36.4 ± 4.2 years), 82.1% had a first claims-identified pregnancy and 62.7% had a claims-identified live birth during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, claims-defined hepatic steatosis compatible with MASLD was associated with a modestly lower hazard of first claims-identified pregnancy (hazard ratio [HR] 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.88-0.98; FDR q = 0.049) and first live birth during follow-up (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.82-0.94; FDR q = 0.0006). It was not associated with claims-defined pregnancy loss among women with a first claims-identified pregnancy. CONCLUSIONS: Pre-index claims-defined hepatic steatosis compatible with MASLD was associated with modestly lower hazards of first claims-identified pregnancy and first live birth during follow-up. Because body mass index, ovarian-reserve markers, clearly separated ovarian phenotypes, male-factor information, and cycle-level characteristics were unavailable, MASLD-compatible hepatic steatosis may represent a broader metabolic-reproductive phenotype rather than an independent hepatic effect. Given the modest E-values, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted causally or used alone to guide individual IVF counseling or treatment decisions.
