titre: Intersphincteric prosthetic implants for faecal incontinence: a systematic review and exploratory pooled analysis of clinically meaningful response
resume: BACKGROUND: Intersphincteric prosthetic implants have emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for faecal incontinence (FI), positioned between conservative therapies and more invasive surgical or neuromodulatory interventions. However, evidence supporting their effectiveness remains fragmented and largely nonrandomised. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review with exploratory quantitative synthesis was conducted. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to August 2025, with an updated search in January 2026 for nonrandomised studies evaluating intersphincteric prosthetic implants (GateKeeper® or SphinKeeper®) in adults with FI. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving a clinically meaningful response, defined as a ≥ 50% reduction in Vaizey (St Mark's) score at ≥ 12 months. Where feasible, exploratory pooled analyses of binary responder outcomes were performed using random-effects models. Secondary outcomes, including continence severity, quality of life and complications, were synthesised narratively. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Fourteen observational studies were included. Two studies reporting comparable binary responder outcomes at approximately 12 months (n = 75) contributed to the primary exploratory synthesis, yielding a pooled responder proportion of 49.3% (95% CI 38.2-60.5%). A sensitivity analysis incorporating three studies reporting study-defined clinical success (n = 129) produced a similar pooled estimate (51.9%, 95% CI 43.3-60.4%). Given the very small number of contributing studies, measures of statistical heterogeneity were uninformative, and interpretation was further limited by the nonrandomised study designs. Quality-of-life outcomes and complication rates were heterogeneous and could not be pooled quantitatively. No procedure-related mortality was reported. CONCLUSION: Exploratory quantitative synthesis suggests that intersphincteric prosthetic implantation may be associated with clinically meaningful symptom improvement in a subset of patients with faecal incontinence. However, the certainty of evidence is low, and pooled estimates should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. Prospective comparative studies with standardised outcome reporting are required to more clearly define the role of these implants within the treatment pathway. What does this paper add to the literature? This review brings together the fragmented evidence on intersphincteric prosthetic implants for faecal incontinence and, where definitions allowed, summarises clinically meaningful responder outcomes at medium-term follow-up. It shows how limited and heterogeneous the evidence remains and identifies where comparative data are most needed.

titre: Associations between early regulatory problems and long-term neurobiological and psychosocial outcomes
resume: UNLABELLED: Early regulatory problems (RPs, i.e. problems with crying, sleeping and feeding), are associated with increased susceptibility to avoidant personality traits and peer relationship issues in adulthood. RPs have been linked to intrinsic functional connectivity changes within the allostatic-interoceptive system, notably involving the insula, which integrates sensory and interoceptive signals. The current study investigated whether early RPs and psychosocial outcomes in adulthood are associated with the insula morphology. Using data of the Bavarian Longitudinal Study, we analyzed individuals with RPs (N = 47) and a matched never RPs group (N = 121), who, in adulthood, underwent MRI and completed the Young Adult Self Report and Life Course Interview, to derive avoidant personality and peer relationship quality scores. RP group showed increased gyrification in the left insula when avoidant personality traits were included in the model. Importantly, individuals with both RPs and higher avoidant personality scores exhibited morphological insula differences. No significant associations were observed in cortical volume, thickness, or sulcal depth, or with peer relationship quality. Morphological differences were largest in individuals with persistent RPs. The findings highlight associations between early RPs and long-lasting neurobiological and psychosocial outcomes, providing important insights for the planning and development of targeted prevention and intervention strategies. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-66979-z.

titre: Distributed structural and functional brain alterations associated with irritable bowel syndrome: a coordinate-based multimodal meta-analysis
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is increasingly recognised as being associated with distributed structural and functional brain alterations, yet existing neuroimaging syntheses lack an integrated multimodal approach across imaging paradigms. To address this gap, we systematically meta-analysed IBS-related brain alterations across structural, task-free functional, and task-based functional neuroimaging studies identified through Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, and Scopus in April 2025. Contrasts comparing IBS with non-IBS controls were synthesised using activation likelihood estimation (ALE), with sensitivity analyses restricted to standard IBS-versus-healthy-control comparisons, and robustness was evaluated through jackknife and within-paper combined-experiment analyses. In the decreased grey matter paradigm, two clusters emerged in the medial thalamus and caudate (8 contrasts, 61 foci, 380 subjects), and largely similar findings were observed in the exploratory combined grey- and white-matter analysis. Task-free analyses identified increased local-metric alterations in the postcentral gyrus (9 contrasts, 51 foci, 528 subjects), increased functional connectivity in insular and paracentral lobule/cingulate regions (15 contrasts, 104 foci, 1 187 subjects), and decreased functional connectivity in the inferior parietal lobule (10 contrasts, 56 foci, 825 subjects). Task-based analyses identified four clusters spanning cortical (insula, medial frontal gyrus) and subcortical (e.g., amygdala, putamen) regions (7 contrasts, 75 foci, 352 subjects). Together, these convergent multimodal findings indicate altered somatosensory, interoceptive, affective, and cognitive processing in IBS, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the distributed structural and functional brain abnormalities associated with the condition.

titre: The impact of cognitive behavioral therapy and third-wave therapies on the quality of life of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and third-wave therapies on the quality of life of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library databases, up until June 20, 2026, to identify randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that used quality of life as an outcome measure. Quality assessment was performed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Assessment Tool. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata 18.0 software, and subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses and tests for publication bias were performed. RESULTS: A total of 13 randomised controlled trials (N = 1,324) were included. The meta-analysis revealed that CBT and third-wave therapies improve quality of life in patients with OCD (SMD = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.29, P = 0.004), with no overall heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). The results of sensitivity analyses were stable, and the risk of publication bias was low. Subgroup analyses indicated that CBT and third-wave therapies were effective in improving quality of life in non-European countries, early studies (≤ 2020), short-term interventions (≤ 12 weeks), adult populations, standard CBT, third-wave therapies, active control groups, and subjective experience/satisfaction scales; however, statistical significance was not achieved in some subgroups. Since the differences between subgroups aren't significant, the subgroup analysis is just exploratory, so the results should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: CBT and third-wave therapies can improve the quality of life of patients with OCD to a certain extent, but the overall effect is modest. Future research should be larger in scale, multi-center, and prospective. It's also necessary to further clarify the mechanisms behind different intervention modules, optimize intervention plans, and improve long-term follow-up, so that we can provide stronger evidence to support clinical practice.

titre: Accuracy of Rome IV questionnaire: a population-based study on diagnostic definitions and clinical validity
resume: BACKGROUND: Rome IV questionnaire is widely used for diagnosing disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), but was developed in Western populations and may not generalize to other regions. This study aimed to validate the Persian version of this questionnaire and develop population-adapted diagnostic criteria for three prevalent DGBIs: functional dyspepsia (FD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and functional constipation (FC). METHODS: Using the Isfahan functional disorders (ISFUN) dataset, we developed two modified versions of Rome IV Diagnostic Criteria (R4DC): (1) the modified Iranian Criteria (mIrC), based on the 90th percentile of symptom frequency in the Iranian population, and (2) the Clinically-Adjusted Criteria (CAC), derived using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses with clinical diagnoses as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance, accuracy, and agreement with the reference standard were assessed. Convergent validity was also examined using the Somatic Symptom Disorder-B Criteria Scale (SSD-12). RESULTS: mIrC thresholds were similar to R4DC for FD but more restrictive for IBS and FC. R4DC overestimated FC prevalence (23.4% vs. 13.9%) but underestimated FD and IBS due to high specificity and low sensitivity. mIrC improved specificity (FD: 95.6%, FC: 93%) but lowered sensitivity, whereas CAC achieved the highest sensitivity (FD: 75.0%, IBS: 84.2%, FC: 96.8%) with strong negative predictive values. R4DC showed the best agreement and accuracy. SSD-12 scores were significantly higher (p-value < 0.001) across all diagnostic groups. CONCLUSIONS: The Persian Rome IV diagnostic questionnaire is valid for DGBIs diagnosis in Iran. However, locally adapted thresholds can improve diagnostic performance, with mIrC offers population-specific diagnostic accuracy while CAC provides high clinical sensitivity, suitable for screening.

titre: Synchronous gastric-type intraepithelial neoplasia and ectopic pancreas in the gastric antrum diagnosed by en bloc endoscopic submucosal dissection: a case report and literature review
resume: BACKGROUND: Ectopic pancreas is a relatively common submucosal lesion of the stomach and is generally considered benign. Emerging evidence, however, suggests that ectopic pancreas may coexist with synchronous neoplastic changes of the overlying gastric mucosa. Because submucosal protrusions can obscure subtle surface abnormalities during endoscopic examination, such coexistence may increase the risk of missed diagnosis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old woman presented with intermittent epigastric discomfort for more than 1 year. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (gastroscopy) revealed a persistent lesion on the greater curvature of the gastric antrum, characterized by an irregular mucosal elevation with central depression and erosion. Magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging demonstrated irregular microvascular architecture within the lesion, and targeted multi-site biopsies were obtained. Histopathology suggested gastric epithelial dysplasia; preoperative pathology and immunohistochemistry indicated indefinite neoplasia for glandular epithelium, and endoscopic submucosal dissection was recommended. The patient underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection. During the procedure, a whitish submucosal nodule was identified and removed en bloc together with the mucosal lesion. Postoperative histopathology demonstrated gastric-type intraepithelial neoplasia (focal high-grade dysplasia) coexisting with ectopic pancreatic tissue (acini and ducts). The two components were histologically independent without evidence of direct continuity. No postoperative complications occurred. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights that gastric-type intraepithelial neoplasia (focal high-grade dysplasia) can coexist with ectopic pancreas within the same antral region while remaining histologically separate. For suspected ectopic pancreas or other submucosal protruding lesions in the gastric antrum, careful and systematic assessment of the overlying mucosa with targeted biopsies is important to avoid overlooking superficial neoplastic lesions masked by submucosal elevation. Endoscopic submucosal dissection can provide a definitive pathological diagnosis and enable en bloc resection of coexisting mucosal and submucosal components in selected cases.

titre: Circadian syndrome and headache accompanied by stomach pain among middle-aged and older Chinese adults: associations and the mediating role of frailty
resume: BACKGROUND: Circadian syndrome (CircS) integrates metabolic abnormalities, short sleep duration, and depressive symptoms, and may reflect multidimensional circadian-related health dysregulation. Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder that is frequently accompanied by gastrointestinal symptoms, but evidence on the association between CircS and migraine-related symptom phenotypes in middle-aged and older adults remains limited. This study examined the associations between CircS and headache accompanied by stomach pain, a self-reported symptom co-occurrence phenotype, and explored the mediating role of frailty. METHODS: Data were obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. A total of 9,342 participants were included in the cross-sectional analysis, and 5,895 participants without headache accompanied by stomach pain at baseline were included in the longitudinal analysis. CircS was defined as the presence of at least four of seven components. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations of CircS with prevalent and incident headache accompanied by stomach pain, respectively. Sensitivity analyses included complete-case analyses, a 2-year lag analysis, age-restricted analysis, propensity score matching, and E-value analysis. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves and bootstrap mediation analysis were also performed. RESULTS: CircS was associated with higher odds of prevalent headache accompanied by stomach pain after full adjustment (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67, p < 0.001). During follow-up, 969 participants developed incident headache accompanied by stomach pain. CircS was associated with an increased risk of incident headache accompanied by stomach pain (HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.16-1.51), and the risk increased with greater CircS component burden. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the main findings. CircS showed numerically higher discriminative ability than metabolic syndrome and individual CircS components. Frailty explained 19.72% of the association between CircS and incident headache accompanied by stomach pain (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Among middle-aged and older Chinese adults, CircS was associated with prevalent and incident headache accompanied by stomach pain, and frailty partially explained this association. As the outcome was based on self-reported symptom co-occurrence, it should not be equated with clinically diagnosed migraine.
revue: The journal of headache and pain

titre: Evidence-Based Nursing Combined With Structured Psychological Intervention for Perioperative Anxiety in Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: Background: Perioperative anxiety is common in women undergoing surgery for ectopic pregnancy and may aggravate pain and delay recovery. This trial evaluated whether evidence-based nursing combined with structured psychological intervention reduces perioperative anxiety compared with routine nursing in women undergoing conservative laparoscopic surgery for tubal ectopic pregnancy. Methods: In this single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 124 women with tubal ectopic pregnancy scheduled for non-emergency conservative laparoscopic surgery were enrolled by convenience sampling and randomly assigned 1:1 to a control group (routine perioperative nursing) or an experimental group (evidence-based nursing plus structured psychological intervention). The prespecified primary outcome was the between-group difference in State Anxiety Inventory (S-AI) score on the day of discharge. Secondary outcomes were postoperative pain (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS) and short-term recovery outcomes. Results: The day-of-discharge S-AI score was lower in the experimental group than in the control group (32.61 ± 4.45 vs 38.24 ± 2.62; mean difference -5.63, 95% CI -6.92 to -4.34; P < .001), with a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). VAS scores at 2, 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery were lower in the experimental group (all P < .001). First ambulation time, length of hospital stay, antibiotic use time, and menstrual recovery time were shorter in the experimental group (all P < .001). Conclusion: Evidence-based nursing combined with structured psychological intervention was associated with lower perioperative anxiety and postoperative pain and with shorter short-term recovery outcomes in women undergoing conservative laparoscopic surgery for tubal ectopic pregnancy.

titre: Neurobiological and cognitive correlates of avoidant restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID): a systematic review
resume: OBJECTIVE: Avoidant restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) is a recently recognised eating disorder and is largely under-researched. Given the paucity of research examining the neurobiological and cognitive correlates of ARFID, the present systematic review aimed to synthesise and summarise existing ARFID data to highlight directions for future research. METHOD: Using PRISMA guidelines, five databases (Cochrane, Embase, Medline, PsycInfo, Web of Science), in addition to hand searches of reference lists and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, were searched for studies that investigated evidence relating to the neurobiological and cognitive correlates of ARFID. Twelve papers met inclusion criteria. RESULTS: Twelve studies met inclusion criteria for this systematic review with a total of n = 548 ARFID participants across all studies. Neurobiological studies (k = 6) highlighted differences in regions including orbitofrontal and prefrontal cortices, and, in acute cases, midline diencephalic regions. Cognitive studies (k = 6) findings highlighted impaired executive function, specifically related to cognitive flexibility, impulsivity, visual processing skills, central coherence and inhibition. CONCLUSIONS: Research into the neurobiology of ARFID is nascent. The results of this review contribute to improved understanding of the possible underlying neurobiological and cognitive differences within ARFID, which in turn will inform translational research aimed at better understanding and treating individuals with this illness.

titre: Urolithin A and its dietary precursors: mechanisms underlying the improvement of cognitive dysfunction
resume: Cognitive dysfunction, driven by psychiatric and functional factors, toxic factors, neurodegenerative diseases and cerebrovascular diseases, metabolic diseases, and other systemic diseases, represents a significant global health challenge with limited pharmacological interventions. Emerging evidence highlights Urolithin A (UroA)-a gut microbiota-derived polyphenol of dietary ellagitannins (ETs) and ellagic acid (EA) -as a highly promising neuroprotective candidate. Current research has found that UroA and its derivatives have an effect against cognitive dysfunction. However, there is currently a lack of comprehensive reviews. This review provides a comprehensive insight of aetiology and pathogenesis of cognitive dysfunction, with a specific focus on how UroA and its precursors intercept these pathological trajectories, while evaluating the source and metabolism of Urolithin A. And we deeply dissect its mechanisms against cognitive dysfunction, particularly its capacity to mitigate neuroinflammation, restore autophagy, modulate the gur-brain axis and so on. Moreover, we address current knowledge gaps and focus on future perspectives.

titre: The associations between job stress and physical and mental health in firefighters: a systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Firefighters are exposed to psychosocial stressors including interpersonal conflict, organizational injustice, and discrimination. This systematic review investigated the associations between work-related psychosocial stress and physical and mental health outcomes among firefighters. METHODS: A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from inception to May 2026. Original cross-sectional, longitudinal, and cohort studies examining associations between job stress and health outcomes in firefighters were included. The review focused on six outcome domains: (1) depression and suicidality, (2) non-depressive mental health problems (PTSD symptoms, anxiety, burnout), (3) alcohol use disorders, (4) sleep quality, (5) somatic disorders (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal), and (6) physical performance. Quality assessment was conducted using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). A thematic narrative synthesis was employed due to methodological heterogeneity. Findings were synthesized narratively, with key odds ratios (ORs) extracted and presented in summary tables. RESULTS: Thirty-four original studies involving 87,242 firefighters across Asia, North America, Europe, and South America were included. The strongest associations were observed for organizational system stress with self-reported depressive symptoms (OR = 8.03 in the longitudinal study), discrimination and harassment with self-reported PTSD symptoms (OR = 2.21) and anxiety (OR = 2.56) in female firefighters, and lack of reward with gastrointestinal disorders (OR = 2.17-2.39) and musculoskeletal disorders (OR = 2.39). Protective factors including social support, self-efficacy, and resilience consistently buffered stress-related health outcomes. Physical performance declined with age (12-13% decrease in strength and power), and less experienced firefighters demonstrated greater physiological stress responses. CONCLUSION: Job stress is associated with pervasive and clinically significant adverse health outcomes in firefighters. The available evidence, predominantly cross-sectional, suggests associations rather than causal effects. Organizational interventions targeting workplace fairness, conflict reduction, and anti-discrimination policies, alongside individual-level resilience training, are warranted. Protecting firefighter health through evidence-based stress prevention is an occupational health priority. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261417550.

titre: Outcome measurement in perianal Crohn's disease
resume: Perianal Crohn's disease (pCD) is a distinct and debilitating phenotype of Crohn's disease and an independent predictor of long-term adverse outcomes. Traditionally, outcome measurement has focused on fistula healing to assess treatment success; however, as we recognise distinct classes of patients and shift towards shared decision making, healthcare professionals are increasingly acknowledging the importance of assessing more nuanced outcomes such as downstaging, quality of life, sex and intimacy and the impact on family, education or work. Current challenges in outcome measurement include substantial heterogeneity in definitions, measurement tools and time points used. This review will cover the current landscape, reporting on historical measurement instruments, such as the fistula drainage assessment (FDA), perianal disease activity index (PDAI) and the collective move towards patient-centred and patient-developed tools, such as the Crohn's anal fistula quality of life scale (CAF-QoL). It will also assess the value of core outcome measurement sets, which provide a uniform but flexible framework to standardise outcome reporting across studies and support comparison of interventions in clinical practice. Importantly, the incorporation of patient perspectives within their methodology ensures that their recommendations reflect outcomes that truly matter to those with pCD. The contemporary need is for novel clinical and radiological tools to monitor perianal disease activity that are predictive, preventative and provide treatment thresholds, so that patients can live well with their fistulising disease, if it cannot be eradicated. There will no doubt also be a role for digital applications and artificial intelligence in enhancing outcome measurement further for perianal Crohn's disease.

titre: The association between emotion anthropomorphism and individuals' emotion regulation and mental health
resume: BACKGROUND: Anthropomorphism refers to the tendency to attribute humanlike mental capacities to nonhuman entities. Prior research has primarily focused on state-like anthropomorphism by manipulating the degree of anthropomorphic features in concrete object targets (e.g., toy, pet, money etc.). However, individuals can also have different levels of tendency to anthropomorphize, and they can anthropomorphize more abstract targets such as emotions. The present study aimed to provide a more refined understanding of anthropomorphism by introducing emotion anthropomorphism as a novel, trait-like dimension of individual differences. METHODS: Korean adults aged 19 to 39 (N = 500; 50% men and 50% women) completed measures of anthropomorphism toward animals, non-animal agents, and emotions. We also measured psychological functions, including emotion dysregulation, cognitive emotion regulation strategies, loneliness, depression, anxiety, and alexithymia. Factor analyses and structural equation modeling were conducted to examine the factor structure of anthropomorphism and its associations with psychological outcomes. RESULTS: The results supported a three-factor structure, as well as a higher-order factor representing general anthropomorphism. Animal anthropomorphism was negatively associated with multiple indices of emotion dysregulation and psychological difficulties (e.g., loneliness, depression, alexithymia), whereas non-animal anthropomorphism demonstrated positive associations with most of those indices. Emotion anthropomorphism was positively associated with cognitive emotion regulation strategies. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that emotions may be anthropomorphized at the trait level, and support emotion anthropomorphism as a facet of anthropomorphism towards abstract targets. Moreover, the results suggest that the subfactors of anthropomorphism may carry distinct psychological meanings, with emotion anthropomorphism showing a more selective association with cognitive emotion regulation strategies.

titre: Association between interoceptive sensitivity and impaired fasting glucose in early pregnancy: the mediating effect of dietary quality distance and food variety
resume: BACKGROUND: Early pregnant women often experience changes in their dietary patterns. Interoceptive sensitivity (IS), the ability to detect internal bodily signals, influences appetite regulation and dietary choices, potentially impacting glucose metabolism. Whether IS is a protective factor against elevated FBG in early pregnancy, and poor dietary patterns are linked to impaired fasting glucose (IFG), the relationships between IS, dietary patterns, and IFG remain unclear. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from December 2024 to June 2025. IS and FBG were recorded in early pregnancy; a three-day dietary diary was applied to record the number of consumed foods and was valued by Chinese Diet Balance Index for Pregnancy (DBI-P), which was used to assess dietary quality distance (DQD) and food variety which comprehensively reflect unbalanced diet and richness of food intake, respectively. Logistic regression analyzed association between IS and IFG. The mediation model test was employed to examine the mediating effect of dietary quality. RESULTS: A total of 215 patients were included in the study, and the prevalence of IFG was 17.2% (N = 37). The scores of IS and its subscale including Emotional Awareness, Self-Regulation, Body Listening, and Trust in IFG group were lower than those in normal group. IS was significantly associated with IFG (OR = 0.491, 95% CI: 0.287, 0.839, P = 0.009). The values of DQD especially in Low Bound Score (LBS) were higher in the IFG group, whereas the food diversity was less sufficient than that in the normal group. The DQD and food variety mediated the relationship between IS and IFG, (DQD: indirect = -0.101, 95%CI: -0.241, -0.018; food variety: indirect = -0.074, 95%CI: -0.207, -0.010). CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that IS is significantly associated with impaired fasting glucose in early pregnancy which is mediated by dietary quality, mainly diet quality distance and food variety. The pathway may be that an impaired interoceptive sensitivity drives less optimal dietary choices (high LBS, low food variety), which in turn negatively impacts fasting glucose levels. These findings offer a novel perspective on the potential value of interoception-oriented approaches. Integrating body-awareness training into early pregnancy may represent a promising avenue to improve dietary choices and achieve better glycemic outcomes for pregnant women at risk of metabolic dysfunction.
revue: Journal of health, population, and nutrition

titre: The gut microbiota dietary index reveals a modifiable diet-depression association varying by BMI and possibly linked to inflammation: a hypothesis-generating modified diet for future intervention research
resume: In the context of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, diet represents a critical yet still debated component of translational psychiatry. However, population-based evidence linking microbiota-supportive dietary patterns to depressive symptoms remains limited. This research leverages the Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) to examine the associations between a gut-microbiota-friendly diet and depression, providing a theoretical framework for future research on practical applications. Using data from 28,884 adults, this cross-sectional study evaluated the association between DI-GM and PHQ-9 using survey-compatible descriptive and conventional regression analyses, ordinary-weighted generalized additive models (GAMs), XGBoost with SHAP for exploratory feature ranking, and an exploratory mediation-type analysis of systemic inflammation. Participants with depression had lower DI-GM scores than those without depression. Model-based analyses suggested an inverse predicted pattern between DI-GM and PHQ-9, especially with the interaction GAM indicating significant BMI-related heterogeneity (a more pronounced inverse association at higher BMI). XGBoost with SHAP analyses identified fiber, refined grains, percent energy from fat and whole grains as dietary features with relatively larger contributions to model predictions. Exploratory mediation-type analysis suggested that inflammation may partially explain the DI-GM-PHQ-9 association. However, a high DI-GM diet lacks depression-related nutrients like vitamin D, omega-3 fatty acids, and zinc. Based on these hypothesis-generating findings, we propose a conceptual framework for a Modified Gut Microbiota-Friendly Diet (MGFD) with high DI-GM score, caloric control, and targeted nutrient supplementation, requiring validation via prospective cohorts, randomized trials, and gut microbiome/metabolomic studies.

titre: Underrecognized suicidality in higher functioning youth with autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
resume: OBJECTIVE: To examine factors associated with elevated risk of suicidal thoughts, behaviors, and death by suicide among high functioning individuals with autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, with particular emphasis on phenotypes characterized by high cognitive ability and delayed recognition. METHODS: A structured review of the literature was conducted across multiple electronic databases using controlled vocabulary and key terms including suicidal risk, autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, high functioning, and neurodivergence. After screening for relevance, duplication, and methodological rigor, 7 studies meeting inclusion criteria were synthesized from an initial yield of fifty publications. RESULTS: Across studies, individuals with ASD demonstrated a consistently elevated risk of STB and death by suicide compared with the general population, both over the lifetime and within shorter follow up periods. Risk was disproportionately concentrated among individuals without intellectual disability, with higher cognitive ability emerging as a vulnerability factor rather than a protective one. Communication differences, alexithymia, and impaired interoceptive awareness limited the sensitivity of caregiver and clinician assessments, contributing to under recognition of suicidality. Traditional protective factors such as educational attainment, employment, and relationship status did not reliably mitigate risk in ASD and ADHD populations. Camouflaging behaviors and diagnostic overshadowing frequently delayed identification, increasing exposure to cumulative psychosocial stress and untreated mental health conditions. CONCLUSIONS: High functioning individuals with ASD and co-occurring ADHD represent a concealed yet high risk population for suicidality. These findings underscore the urgent need for autism informed suicide risk assessment, early identification of neurodevelopmental traits in suicidal individuals, and prevention strategies tailored to cognitive profile, developmental history, and comorbidity. Advances in the current screening and intervention frameworks may mitigate adverse outcomes in this vulnerable group.

titre: Palliative care educational intervention versus cognitive behavioral therapy for health-related quality of life in patients with incurable cancer: a protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis
resume: BACKGROUND: Patients with incurable cancer prioritize health-related quality of life (HRQoL)-a key target of palliative care. But shortages of palliative care professionals create critical access barriers, leaving patients with unmet HRQoL needs. In addition to palliative care provided by professionals, non-pharmacological strategies such as palliative care educational intervention (PEI) and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) have been proposed to address these gaps. Recent studies about PEI have shown promise in improving HRQoL for patients with incurable cancer. However, it remains an emerging approach that has not been thoroughly and systematically evaluated, especially compared with CBT-an intervention with extensive systematic reviews. Furthermore, due to the scarcity of head-to-head comparisons between PEI and CBT, a network meta-analysis (NMA) is needed to clarify their relative effectiveness. METHODS: This systematic review and NMA will include randomized controlled trials evaluating PEI and/or CBT in adults (≥ 18 years) with incurable cancer. Electronic databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and CINAHL) and trial registers (ClinicalTrials.gov) will be searched from inception. The primary outcome is HRQoL (measured via validated scales such as the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Core Questionnaire [EORTC QLQ-C30]); secondary outcomes include symptoms (pain, fatigue, anxiety, depression) assessed by validated scales. Effect sizes (standardized mean differences [SMD]) will be calculated, and SMDs will be re-expressed to the EORTC QLQ-C30 global health/quality of life scale. NMA will estimate relative effects, with subgroup analyses (based on delivery setting, mode, etc.) and sensitivity analyses. The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) will assess evidence quality. DISCUSSION: Comparing PEI with CBT will offer evidence for palliative care professionals and policymakers. Clear PEI definition and comprehensive literature retrieval are foundational to this systematic review and NMA, while analyzing study and intervention details may address heterogeneity in HRQoL outcomes and guide development of more effective interventions. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251146822.

titre: From fear to bonding: a randomized controlled trial of CBT-based group counseling on the experience of becoming a mother in marginalized adolescent mothers
resume: BACKGROUND: Adolescent motherhood, especially in marginalized populations, presents psychological and emotional challenges that can affect maternal-infant bonding and maternal self-efficacy. This study evaluated the effect of cognitive-behavioral group counseling on the experience of becoming a mother among adolescent mothers in marginalized areas of Urmia through a randomized controlled trial. METHODS: This cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted between September and December 2024 in Urmia, Iran. Health centers were randomly allocated to intervention or control groups using a computer-generated random sequence. Eighty-eight adolescent mothers were recruited via census sampling. The Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21) was used to screen and exclude mothers with depressive symptoms before randomization. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group receiving seven weekly cognitive-behavioral group counseling sessions or to a control group receiving routine care. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the Being a Mother Scale (BaM-13). Statistical analyses included chi-square, independent t-tests, and repeated measures ANOVA using SPSS 20. RESULTS: The intervention group showed significant improvement in the experience of becoming a mother, with mean BaM-13 scores decreasing from 36.54 ± 2.20 at baseline to 15.30 ± 2.50 at three months post-intervention. The control group's scores remained stable. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significant effects of time (p < 0.001) and a time-by-group interaction (p < 0.001), confirming improvements were exclusive to the intervention group. CONCLUSION: Cognitive-behavioral group counseling effectively enhances adolescent mothers' experience of becoming a mother by fostering emotional closeness, positive child experiences, and personal growth. This intervention may benefit maternal health in marginalized populations. TRIAL REGISTRATION: IRCT20250126064520N1, The date of registration: 2-19-2025. Ethical approval code: IR.UMSU.REC.1403.134 Date: 4.8.2024.

titre: Nail biting in children with ADHD: exploring its clinical correlates, psychiatric comorbidities and association with other body-focused repetitive behaviors
resume: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether children with ADHD who engage in nail-biting (NB) differ clinically and cognitively from those who do not, focusing on body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs), psychiatric comorbidities, and cognitive profiles. METHODS: In this retrospective, cross-sectional chart-review study, 250 medication-naive children aged 8-12 years with ADHD were grouped by the presence (n = 100) or absence (n = 150) of NB. Co-occurring BFRBs, psychiatric comorbidities, cognitive performance (WISC-R subtest scaled scores) and symptom severity (RCADS-P, CPRS-R: S) were compared using Mann-Whitney U and chi-square tests, followed by multivariable binary logistic regression. RESULTS: Compared with children with ADHD without NB, those with NB showed higher rates of co-occurring BFRBs (thumb sucking, lip or cheek biting, bruxism), anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder and speech disorders, and substantially higher parent-rated internalizing symptoms (RCADS-P Total Anxiety and Depression, rrb = 0.55). They also obtained lower scores on selected WISC-R subtests, most consistently Vocabulary, Comprehension, Picture Completion and Picture Arrangement. In multivariable analysis, older age, higher internalizing symptoms and lower scores on these subtests were independently associated with NB. CONCLUSION: In children with ADHD, NB and co-occurring BFRBs were associated with a greater burden of internalizing symptoms and with lower performance on selected verbal and perceptual WISC-R subtests, and may correspond to a distinct clinical profile. These associations are cross-sectional and correlational and do not imply causality.

titre: Comparative effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in hemodialysis patients: a randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) face significant psychological challenges that affect their well-being. Nevertheless, no comparative investigation has yet examined the efficacy of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in this population. Hence, this study aimed to compare the effectiveness of CBT versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in HD patients. METHODS: This three-arm, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial was conducted from September 2024 to May 2025 with a sample of 135 HD patients. Participants were selected through simple random sampling and were randomly allocated to two experimental groups and one active control group. Prior to the intervention, all three groups completed the relevant questionnaires. The CBT and group-based optimism training programs were then implemented for the first and second experimental groups, respectively, each consisting of eight 90-minute sessions delivered once per week for eight consecutive weeks. The control group received standard educational interventions. Following the completion of the training sessions, the questionnaires were completed again immediately and again two and four-months later. The data were analyzed using SPSS software version 21. ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS: All procedures performed on human participants complied with the ethical guidelines of the relevant institutional and national research committees, as well as the Helsinki Declaration and its subsequent revisions, or equivalent ethical frameworks. RESULTS: Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant time × group interactions for anxiety (η²p = 0.068), depression (η²p = 0.085), optimism (η²p = 0.101), and hope (η²p = 0.073), all p 0.05). CONCLUSION: The findings indicated that both CBT and group-based optimism training were effective in reducing anxiety and enhancing hope. Nevertheless, a distinction emerged at long-term follow-up, as optimism training yielded more sustained reductions in depression and greater improvements in optimism. This suggests that, although CBT is effective for acute symptom reduction, optimism training may offer additional advantages for sustained psychological well-being. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: IRCT20240609062065N4, 2025-12-01, 'retrospectively registered'.

titre: Role of gut microbiota dysbiosis on the functional outcomes in ischemic and haemorrhagic stroke patients: a systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, yet the biological determinants of post-stroke recovery remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a key regulator of neuroinflammation, metabolic signalling, and immune response through microbiota-gut brain axis. However, the extent to which gut microbial dysbiosis influences neurological severity and functional recovery across ischemic and haemorrhagic stroke remains unclear. METHODS: This systematic review examined the relationship between gut dysbiosis and functional outcomes following stroke. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library identified eligible studies published up to July 2025. Twenty-three clinical studies comprising 2,951 participants were included. Microbiome diversity indices, microbial taxa, and microbiota-derived metabolites were evaluated in relation to standardized stroke outcomes, including acute neurological severity (NIHSS) and functional outcomes (mRS, Barthel Index. The study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Cochrane risk-of-bias framework. RESULTS: Across the included cohorts, stroke patients exhibited consistent alterations in gut microbial ecology compared with healthy controls. Alpha diversity analyses demonstrated a significant reduction in microbial richness and evenness in several cohorts, while beta diversity metrics revealed pronounced restructuring and clear separation between stroke and control microbiomes. Differential abundance analysis consistently identified depletion of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing commensals, including Roseburia, Faecalibacterium, and Coprococcus, alongside enrichment of opportunistic and pro-inflammatory taxa such as Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus, and Escherichia/Shigella. Metabolomic analysis further revealed a convergent disruption of key microbial metabolic pathways, including reduced SCFA production, increased endotoxin-associated signalling and trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) metabolism. These microbial and metabolic perturbations were significantly associated with greater neurological severity, higher disability scores, increased infection risk, and poorer functional outcomes following stroke. CONCLUSION: This systematic synthesis demonstrates that stroke is accompanied by a reproducible pattern of gut microbial dysbiosis characterized by ecological contraction, expansion of inflammatory pathobionts, and disruption of microbial metabolic signalling. These findings support the existence of a conserved gut-brain-metabolic axis influencing stroke severity and recovery trajectories. Integrating microbiome-derived biomarkers with clinical prognostic models may enable earlier risk stratification and the development of microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies to improve post-stroke outcomes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (Identifier: CRD420251106958).

titre: Neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio as a predictor of early treatment response in adolescent females with obsessive-compulsive disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical period for the onset of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), in which inflammatory markers such as the neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) may influence disease development. However, the impact of these markers on early clinical improvement remains unexplored. This study aimed to identify factors associated with early clinical improvement in adolescent females with OCD, with particular focus on baseline inflammatory markers. METHOD: This retrospective analysis included 99 female patients (aged ≤ 18 years) diagnosed with OCD and admitted between 2011 and 2024 at a tertiary psychiatric hospital in China. Clinical and demographic characteristics, medication usage, and baseline blood routine results were extracted from electronic records. Inflammatory markers including the NLR were calculated. Early treatment response was assessed using the Clinical Global Impressions scale. Variables with p < 0.1 in univariate analysis were entered into a binary logistic regression model to identify predictors of early treatment response. Bootstrap internal validation with 1000 resamples was performed to assess model stability. RESULTS: Among the 99 patients, 50.51% showed early clinical improvement at two weeks. Binary logistic regression identified baseline NLR (odds ratio = 0.173, 95% confidence interval = [0.060 to 0.496]; p = 0.001) and sodium valproate use (odds ratio = 0.056, 95% confidence interval = [0.005 to 0.581]; p = 0.016) as independent predictors of early clinical improvement. Bootstrap validation confirmed model robustness (optimism‑corrected C‑statistic = 0.803), the combined model incorporating NLR and sodium valproate achieved good discriminative ability (area under the curve = 0.823). CONCLUSION: Higher baseline NLR and sodium valproate use are associated with poorer early clinical improvement during the first two weeks of hospitalization in adolescent females with OCD. These findings highlight the potential utility of NLR as a prognostic marker and underscore the need for individualized medication selection in this population. Further prospective studies with larger samples are warranted to validate these results and clarify the underlying mechanisms. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400093247) on 29 November 2024.

titre: Effects of heat-killed Bifidobacterium longum KABP-042 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KABP-051 on cognitive performance in typically developing school-aged children: a placebo-controlled, randomized double-blind parallel-group trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Increasing evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis plays a critical role in cognitive and behavioral development. However, clinical evidence supporting cognitive benefit of probiotics and postbiotics in typically developing children remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of a postbiotic formulation containing heat-killed Bifidobacterium longum KABP-042 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KABP-051 on brain-related outcomes in school-aged children. METHODS: This study randomly allocated 60 typically developing children (aged 8-10 years) to receive either a daily jelly containing heat-killed KABP-042 and KABP-051 (5 × 109 cells each) or a placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoints were changes in working memory (digit span), inhibitory control (Go/No-go task), and cognitive flexibility measured by the Stroop test. Secondary endpoints included autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity, emotional and behavioral assessment, and gut microbiota composition. RESULTS: Participants who received the postbiotic intervention demonstrated significantly higher accuracy (p = 0.019) and lower error rates (p = 0.004) in the incongruent condition of the Stroop test at 12 weeks compared to placebo, while reaction time was unchanged. No significant between-group differences were observed in working memory, inhibitory control, ANS activity, emotional and behavioral outcomes, and gut microbiota composition, although changes in beta diversity were significantly greater in the placebo group (p = 0.049). CONCLUSIONS: Twelve weeks of postbiotic intervention was associated with enhanced accuracy-related Stroop task performance, particularly in the incongruent condition, in typically developing children, whereas other cognitive outcomes were unaffected. These preliminary findings suggest that supplementation with KABP-042 and KABP-051 may influence selected aspects of cognitive task performance in children. Further investigation into the underlying mechanisms and long-term outcomes is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN-CTR; ID: UMIN000058366).

titre: Sex differences in symptom-specific brain abnormalities across disease stages in depression
resume: BACKGROUND: The incidence and clinical manifestations of major depressive disorder (MDD) differ between sexes. This implies distinct neuropathological mechanisms. This study aimed to investigate sex-specific brain patterns in MDD by stratifying patients according to both sex and disease course. METHODS: We recruited 1170 participants (811 MDD patients and 359 healthy controls) who underwent T1-weighted and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. We explored duration-stage-related, sex-specific differences in gray matter (GM), amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF), and structural-functional coupling. We also used the structural covariance network (SCN) to assess morphological connectivity reorganization. Finally, we explored the relationship between key brain measures derived from the preceding multimodal analyses and clinical features. RESULTS: GM abnormalities in both sexes were observed first appeared in areas supporting sensorimotor and interoceptive functions, and later extended to areas involved in cognitive and emotional processing. Critically, we found distinct sex-specific epicentres of pathology. In male patients, the right postcentral gyrus (PoCG) exhibited early GM atrophy and decreased betweenness centrality within the SCN. In female patients, the left inferior temporal gyrus (ITG) showed early GM atrophy, increased degree centrality within the SCN, reduced ALFF values, and a two-stage evolution of structural-functional coupling with a transition lasting 3 years. Clinically, GM volumes of the right PoCG in male patients were negatively associated with insomnia-early, genital symptoms, and weight loss, while in female patients, GM volumes of the left ITG were negatively associated with depressed mood, work and interest, and psychic anxiety. CONCLUSIONS: This study shows a sex-specific neuropathological origin in MDD, with the left ITG serving as the core pathological area in females and the right PoCG in males. These conclusions not only advance our insight into the sex-dependent mechanisms underlying MDD but also provide a stage-informed framework for individualized interventions, suggesting that the early years of the disease may be a critical period for structure-targeted therapies.

titre: Evaluating the introduction module of Mentalization-Based Treatment: a naturalistic pre-post clinical cohort study
resume: BACKGROUND: Mentalization-Based Treatment Introduction (MBT-I) is a psychoeducational group module preceding long-term Mentalization-Based Treatment (MBT) for patients with borderline personality disorder (BPD). MBT-I aims to increase knowledge of mentalizing and BPD, prepare patients for treatment, clarify diagnosis, and assess mentalizing capacities. However, empirical evidence remains limited. This study examined whether MBT-I was associated with improved mentalizing capacity and attainment of its clinical goals. METHODS: A naturalistic, non-randomized one-group pre-post study was conducted in a Dutch mental health care institute. Patients attended ten weekly MBT-I group sessions. Of 60 patients included, 51 were analyzed. Most had a primary BPD diagnosis; others had personality disorders with comparable difficulties in relational functioning, self-image, and mentalizing. Mentalizing capacity was assessed using the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire, Interpersonal Reactivity Index, and Toronto Alexithymia Scale. MBT-I goals were measured using visual analogue scales. RESULTS: A trend was found for the TAS-20 subscale 'Difficulty Identifying Feelings'. No significant differences were found between pre- and posttest on the RFQ, IRI, and the remaining subscales of the TAS-20. Significant differences were found comparing pre- and post-VAS scores with regard to the goals of MBT-I. CONCLUSION: MBT-I was not associated with statistically significant improvements across the outcome scales on mentalizing, but a promising trend emerged toward improved emotional awareness. The brief module appears to strengthen early prerequisites for mentalizing and offers clear psychoeducational value by increasing patient knowledge, rather than inducing changes in mentalizing. Future controlled studies are needed to clarify its incremental clinical benefit.
revue: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation

titre: The mediating role of interoception in the relationship between anaemia-like symptoms and psychological distress in adults
resume: This study investigated the relationship between anaemia-like symptoms and psychological distress, examining interoceptive awareness as a potential mediator in adults. A cross-sectional online questionnaire was administered to 312 non-clinical participants (M = 38.26 years) from five countries (America, Britain, China, India, and Nigeria). Correlation analysis revealed significant positive associations between anaemia-like symptoms and psychological distress (r = 0.55, p < 0.001). Furthermore, mediation analysis demonstrated that interoceptive awareness, particularly the "Not-Distracting" dimension, partially mediated this relationship (β = 0.079). Individuals with higher anaemia-like symptoms scores reported greater avoidance of uncomfortable bodily sensations, which was in turn associated with greater psychological distress. A reversed mediation model testing psychological distress as a predictor of anaemia-like symptoms yielded a non-significant total indirect effect, suggesting the proposed model may better account for the observed mediation pattern. This study identified an association between physical symptoms and psychological outcomes through interoceptive awareness, particularly highlighting the role of avoidance of bodily sensations in the psychological well-being of individuals with anaemia-like symptoms.

titre: Defeating fear with exposure therapy delivered by mental health nurses in primary care for anxiety disorders in older adults: a protocol for a cluster-randomized controlled trial (DeFEAD65+)
resume: INTRODUCTION: Anxiety disorders are associated with a high disease burden throughout the life span. Anxiety disorders in older adults, however, remain frequently untreated, and when treated, pharmacotherapy predominates despite age-related risks and a preference for psychotherapy. Exposure Therapy is the most effective intervention for anxiety disorders and is a suitable treatment method to be delivered in primary care centres by mental health nurses. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the (cost-) effectiveness of ET delivered by trained MHNs compared to usual care in reducing anxiety symptoms and improving quality of life among older adults with anxiety disorders in primary care. The secondary objective is to examine secondary outcomes, including comorbid depressive symptoms and disorder-specific anxiety symptoms. We also aim to investigate potential predictors and moderators of treatment outcome, as well as possible mechanisms of change in exposure therapy for older adults with anxiety disorders. METHODS: A multi-centre cluster-randomised controlled trial conducted in primary care with two parallel groups: (a) exposure therapy, and (b) usual care, with one-year follow-up. Participants must meet the criteria for a primary Diagnostics and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition anxiety disorder. Exclusion criteria are earlier treatment for anxiety disorder, other somatic and/or psychiatric morbidity that could interfere with diagnostics or treatment, being terminally ill, and having a moderate to severe cognitive impairment and stable pharmacotherapy use. The intervention consists of eight 30-min ET sessions delivered over 12 weeks. Primary outcome measures are anxiety severity as assessed with the Geriatric Anxiety Inventory, societal costs as assessed with the Trimbos and iMTA questionnaire on Costs associated with Psychiatric illness, and quality of life using the EuroQol 5 Dimension 5 Level version. DISCUSSION: Even though participating in present study involves a time investment for patients, we expect that they will benefit from the offered exposure therapy in a more effective way than usual care, as we anticipate a beneficial impact on their anxiety symptoms. If proven effective, exposure therapy could represent a valuable addition to existing clinical guidelines for the treatment of anxiety disorders in older adults within primary care settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06770517) on 26 February 2025.

titre: Distinct dimensions of interoception modulate the link between cardiovascular reactivity and perceived stress
resume: Perceived stress, even when the stressor is the same, varies across individuals. Interoception-the ability to perceive and process internal bodily states-plays a crucial role in shaping the relationship between perceived stress and physiological changes in the body. We aimed to determine how interoception modulates the translation of cardiovascular reactivity into perceived stress during various stress situations. To examine this effect under varying degrees of external pressure, participants performed a speech task under two different themes: a higher-stress condition, in which they were informed that their content about social and political issues would be evaluated by professionals, and a lower-stress condition, in which they could speak freely about their personal experiences. During the tasks, we measured cardiovascular reactivity by using the hemodynamic profile (HP), which reflects the qualitative nature of blood pressure responses (i.e., myocardial-dominant vs. vascular-dominant). Following each task, participants reported subjective emotional states. To assess individual differences in interoception, we employed a Heartbeat Counting Task (HCT) and the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA). The results revealed that, in the higher-stress condition, excitement was negatively associated with HP among individuals with higher HCT scores, whereas it was positively associated with HP among those with lower HCT scores. In contrast, in the lower-stress condition, MAIA scores interacted with HP to affect excitement, which was negatively associated with HP among individuals with higher MAIA scores, and positively associated with HP among those with lower MAIA scores. We show that the interplay between interoception and cardiovascular reactivity substantially influences the perception of excitement as a subjectively positive aspect. These results provide important insights into the quality of perceived stress, highlighting its dependence on context and individual traits. Our findings offer a physiological anthropological insight into the mind-body connection, suggesting that interpreting cardiovascular reactivity as allostasis demonstrates how individuals utilize multidimensional interoceptive cues to adapt to environmental demands and reshape their physiological states into qualitative emotional experiences.

titre: Hippocampal subregion volume alterations at baseline and following antidepressant treatment in youth at high risk for bipolar disorder
resume: Understanding hippocampal neurostructural alterations at baseline and following antidepressant treatment in high-risk youth, particularly within distinct subregions, is critical for elucidating bipolar disorder (BD) pathophysiology and treatment planning. In this prospective randomized clinical trial, 105 high-risk youth with a first-degree BD-I relative(s) and moderate to severe depression and/or anxiety disorder, along with 51 healthy controls (HCs), were recruited. All participants underwent baseline structural MRI and clinical evaluations for depression, anxiety, and adverse events. High-risk youth were then randomized to receive psychotherapy and with either escitalopram or placebo. After 4 weeks of treatment, high-risk youth underwent repeated structural MRI and clinical assessments. These clinical assessments continued biweekly over the remaining 12 weeks of treatment (up to week 16). Volumetric measurements of hippocampal subregions were analyzed at baseline and 4 weeks. Compared to HCs, high-risk youth had significant baseline volume increases in the right cornu ammonis (CA)3, bilateral CA4, bilateral granule cell and molecular layers of the dentate gyrus (GC-ML-DG), and bilateral molecular layer, but reduced volumes in the bilateral fimbria and left parasubiculum. Volume reduction in the left hippocampal tail after 4 weeks of escitalopram treatment was associated with improvements in disinhibition and impulsivity symptoms from baseline to 4 weeks, and this association remained significant from baseline to 16 weeks. CA3-4 and GC-ML-DG enlargement may reflect adaptive changes, while fimbria and parasubiculum atrophy indicate vulnerabilities in BD-risk youth. Escitalopram-related volume reduction in the left hippocampal tail may reflect neural plasticity associated with emotional symptom improvement in BD high-risk youth. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: Mechanism of Antidepressant-Related Dysfunctional Arousal in High-Risk Youth; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ ; NCT02553161.

titre: Low cost app-based intervention DIALOG+ for anxiety and depression in outpatient psychiatric settings: a pragmatic multisite cluster randomized controlled trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Clinically diagnosed anxiety and depressive disorders are widely recognized as the most common mental health issues in India, affecting approximately 15% of the population. With notable gender disparities, Tamil Nadu has some of the highest depression rates in the nation. Despite the growing burden, countries such as India that fall within the low and middle-income countries (LMICs) continue to struggle with mental health services due to challenges in funding, a lack of qualified practitioners, and obstacles to putting evidence-based treatments like Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) into practice. Innovative, low-cost, and scalable approaches are required to address this gap. This multisite pragmatic randomized controlled trial (RCT) seeks to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and evaluate the effectiveness of DIALOG+ , a low-cost app-based solution-focused intervention designed to enhance quality of life and reduce mental distress. While previously validated for psychosis and other chronic psychiatric conditions, this study aims to evaluate its potential for individuals with anxiety and depression in outpatient psychiatric services in India. METHODS: A pragmatic multisite randomized controlled trial will be conducted across four outpatient psychiatric settings in Chennai and Puducherry to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness of DIALOG+, a low-cost app-based intervention. Adults (18-65 years) with anxiety and/or depressive disorders will be randomly allocated to receive either DIALOG+ together with treatment as usual (TAU) or the DIALOG Scale alongside treatment as usual (TAU) over a 6-month period. The key outcome of this study is the improvement in quality of life, evaluated using the Manchester Short Assessment of Quality of Life (MANSA). Secondary outcomes will include changes in depression and anxiety measured using the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Feasibility will be assessed through recruitment, retention, and intervention fidelity rates, and acceptability will be explored through interviews with participants and clinicians. Assessments at follow-up will be carried out at 3 and 6 months, and analyses will be performed using an intention-to-treat approach. DISCUSSION: If feasible, acceptable, and effective, DIALOG+ for clinically diagnosed persons with anxiety and depressive disorders could represent a transformative, scalable solution for improving mental health outcomes in India and similar LMIC contexts. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered with the Clinical Trial Registry-India (CTRI), and the registration number is CTRI/2025/08/092477. The registration was done on August 6, 2025.The URL of the trial registry record is https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/rmaindet.php?trialid=133110&EncHid=16149.91763&modid=1&compid=19 .

titre: Pharmacologic Treatment Response in Panic Disorder with Comorbid Medical Conditions: A Systematic and Narrative Review
resume: Panic disorder frequently co-occurs with medical conditions, complicating diagnosis and treatment. Although pharmacotherapy is a first-line treatment for panic disorder, pharmacotherapeutic evidence for patients with medical comorbidities is limited. Therefore, this review systematically evaluates the efficacy of pharmacologic treatments for panic disorder in adults with medical comorbidities and synthesizes clinical insights using a narrative approach. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through April 22, 2024, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Eligible studies compared pharmacotherapy with placebo or no treatment in patients with panic disorder and comorbidities. The review protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (registration number CRD42024544914). A hybrid approach combining systematic review methods with narrative synthesis was employed to enable broader interpretation. Two randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria. Both had small sample sizes and used different outcome measures, limiting cross-study comparability. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and benzodiazepines showed potential in alleviating panic symptoms among patients with irritable bowel syndrome or noncardiac chest pain. Narrative synthesis underscored the bidirectional link between panic disorder and medical conditions, challenges in pharmacologic treatment, and gaps in existing clinical guidelines. Current evidence on pharmacologic treatment of panic disorder with medical comorbidities is very limited, derived from only two small studies with heterogeneous designs. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and benzodiazepines showed preliminary signals of potential benefit, but definitive conclusions cannot be drawn. Individualized treatment and interdisciplinary collaboration are essential. Large-scale clinical trials and updated guidelines are needed to better support this population.
revue: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology

titre: Parastomal Hernia Repair Beyond Recurrence: A Narrative Review of Surgical Strategies with Special Focus on HyPER
resume: INTRODUCTION: Parastomal hernia is one of the most common late complications after stoma formation and may significantly impair quality of life, stoma care, appliance fit, and daily functioning. Despite numerous operative techniques, no universally accepted gold standard has been established, particularly for complex and recurrent parastomal hernias. AIM: The aim of this narrative review was to summarize current evidence on epidemiology, risk factors, prevention, classification, and surgical treatment of parastomal hernia, with particular emphasis on the Hybrid Parastomal Endoscopic Repair (HyPER) technique as a reconstructive approach. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Google Scholar, and reference lists of relevant articles. Publications addressing parastomal hernia prevention, classification, operative techniques, recurrence, complications, quality of life, stoma function, and appliance-related outcomes were analyzed. Particular attention was given to randomized trials, cohort studies, case series, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and expert reviews, published primarily within the previous 20 years. RESULTS: Conventional approaches, including local repair, stoma relocation, keyhole, Sugarbaker, sandwich, retromuscular, and Pauli-type repairs, have specific advantages and limitations. Their interpretation is limited by heterogeneous study designs, inconsistent recurrence definitions, variable follow-up, and insufficient use of standardized classification. HyPER combines laparoscopic adhesiolysis and mesh reinforcement with open peristomal reconstruction, including hernia sac excision, fascial narrowing, stoma revision or relocation, bowel loop shortening, and soft-tissue remodeling. CONCLUSIONS: Parastomal hernia repair should be evaluated not only by recurrence but also by functional outcomes and quality of life. HyPER may represent an important evolution toward comprehensive anatomical and functional reconstruction, particularly in complex and recurrent cases. Further multicenter comparative studies are needed.

titre: Experience sampling reveals habitual and transdiagnostic properties of compulsivity
resume: Both obsessive thoughts and an urge to act have been linked to compulsions cross-sectionally. However, prominent theories of compulsivity disagree quite fundamentally about whether compulsions are goal-oriented attempts to reduce or eliminate obsessive thoughts or are urge-driven and habitual. To shed light on this debate, we used multilevel vector autoregression modelling to analyse contemporaneous and temporal associations based on self-report symptoms and cognition from N = 179 individuals with and without diagnoses who performed compulsions. Six weeks of three-times daily timeseries data with a mean lag of five hours between assessments were gathered from a transdiagnostic sample who checked their phone compulsively, binge ate, or engaged in compulsions commonly seen in OCD (e.g. checking, cleaning). Across compulsions, the strongest within-person correlate of compulsions were urges (β = 0.61, pFDR < 0.001) and this was 3 times larger than obsessive thoughts and 4 times larger than anxiety. We found that urges predicted compulsions at the next assessment time point (β = 0.09, pFDR < 0.001), while compulsions themselves had a markedly low tendency to predict themselves (β = 0.04) compared to the other mental health symptoms sampled (0.12 < β < 0.23). Finally, like habits, compulsions occurred more often when executive functioning was low (β = 0.09, pFDR < 0.001). Based on real-time dynamics of compulsions, we find that urges, but not obsessive thoughts, predict compulsivity five hours later. Intriguingly, the associations were remarkably similar across compulsions, supporting the notion that transdiagnostically, a habit-like mechanism may underlie compulsive actions.

titre: Vanadium-based cathode materials for Zn-, Al-, Mg-, and NH4 +-based aqueous rechargeable batteries: modification strategies and energy-storage mechanisms
resume: Aqueous rechargeable batteries employing vanadium-based cathodes, including aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), aqueous aluminum-ion batteries (AAlIBs), aqueous magnesium-ion batteries (AMgIBs), and aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (NH4 +-IBs), have gained increasing attention as promising alternatives to conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) because of their improved safety, cost effectiveness, and environmental compatibility. In this background, vanadium-based cathode materials, owing to their multivalent redox capabilities (V2+ to V5+), diverse architectures (e.g., layered, tunnel-like, or three-dimensional frameworks), and elevated theoretical capacities, perform even more outstandingly. These characteristics can help overcome challenges, such as narrow electrochemical stability windows (∼1.23 V), sluggish ion diffusion, and cathode dissolution. A comprehensive analysis of vanadium oxides, vanadates, phosphates, sulfides, nitrides, and their composites across these aqueous battery platforms is given in this review. Various performance-enhancing strategies like ion/water intercalation, surface engineering, defect engineering, and heterostructure design were emphasized. Additionally, this review outlines future research directions for advancing these aqueous ion battery technologies toward practical applications in grid-scale storage and portable electronics. Focusing on the materials design and mechanism study, this review discusses the key challenges and opportunities for vanadium-based materials as a promising cathode in aqueous rechargeable batteries, both for fundamental research and practical applications. This study serves to promote future efforts toward the development of vanadium-based materials and related materials for applications in aqueous rechargeable batteries.

titre: Comparative pilot study using mucosal brushing and mucosal biopsy for detecting duodenal microbiome in functional dyspepsia
resume: BACKGROUND: Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a prevalent gastrointestinal disorder affecting quality of life, with recent studies suggesting a role of the duodenal microbiome in its pathogenesis via the gut-brain axis. The optimal specimen sampling collection method and the specific microbial features associated with FD remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This pilot study compared mucosal brushing and biopsy for duodenal microbiome sampling, with an exploratory secondary aim of assessing microbial differences between FD and non-FD controls. METHODS: Patients undergoing esophago-gastro-duodenoscopy (EGD) were recruited from February 2024 to May 2025. FD patients were identified using the Rome IV criteria, and non-FD controls without upper GI symptoms were included. Duodenal samples were collected via mucosal brushing and biopsy, followed by DNA extraction and 16 S rRNA sequencing of the V1-V2 region. α-diversity (richness, Shannon, Simpson) and β-diversity (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity) were assessed between FD and non-FD controls and between sampling methods. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests compared sampling methods, while linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and BMI compared FD and non-FD controls within each method. Microbial associations with FD were examined using generalized linear models, adjusting for age, sex, and BMI, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. RESULTS: Forty participants (FD n = 20; non-FD controls n = 20) were included, yielding 80 paired samples. Brushing showed higher retention of non-chimeric reads and lower filtering losses than biopsy (all p 0.05). CONCLUSION: Mucosal brushing collects luminal/mucus-associated microbiota and therefore yielded higher bacterial biomass and greater microbial diversity than mucosal biopsy. No significant differences in alpha or beta diversity were detected between FD and non-FD controls within either method, although the study was not powered to exclude such differences. Exploratory analyses suggested numerically higher Streptococcus abundance in FD that did not survive FDR correction. This hypothesis-generating finding requires validation in larger studies. GOV IDENTIFIER: NCT06326918.
