titre: Acculturation and Culturally Adapted CBT for Refugee Youth and Families-A Systematic Review
resume: UNLABELLED: Refugee children are exposed to stressors and events that can severely impact their psychological wellbeing. Additionally, the acculturation process during resettlement can greatly shape their mental health. Acculturation-informed culturally adapted Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CA-CBT) could provide refugee youth and families with psychological support that meets their complex needs. This review explores the effectiveness of acculturation-informed CA-CBT interventions for refugee youth and families, specifically in reducing trauma-related symptoms such as PTSD, anxiety, or depression as well as improving day-to-day functioning, effective coping skills, and resilience. 17 databases were systematically searched between April 2022 and June 2022. Search strategies such as keyword searching, phrase searching, Boolean logic, and truncation were all used during this stage to ensure relevant studies and literature were found and included. Moreover, due to this topic's niche nature, broad eligibility criteria were applied to ensure all relevant studies were included. 5 studies with acculturation-informed CA-CBT interventions for refugee youth were included. The studies indicate the use of acculturation-informed CA-CBT reduces trauma-related symptoms such as PTSD, anxiety, depression, and resource hardships while improving functioning, effective coping skills, treatment engagement, and resilience associated with acculturation. Comparing acculturation-informed CA-CBT with CA-CBT and treatment uninformed by acculturation was not possible due to study limitations. Although these are not well-established interventions, growing evidence supports their use. This review demonstrates how 5 acculturation-informed CA-CBT interventions have been designed and implemented to meet the unique needs of refugee youth. Studies on this topic are scarce and further research is needed before concrete conclusions can be drawn. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40653-026-00947-7.

titre: The gut, conductor of our health: putting the microbiota in the spotlight, a symposium report
resume: This report summarizes key takeaways from the 11th International Yakult Symposium held in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, in October 2024. It provides an overview of insights obtained by the latest basic and clinical research, meta-analyses, and omics research, underscoring the relevance of the exposome, the outer and inner factors to which our bodies are exposed throughout our entire lifespan, in shaping the microbiota. The symposium addressed external factors such as diet (including probiotics and novel fermented foods), additives, pharmacologic agents, and physical environment, as well as the internal crosstalk between tissue or organ-specific microbial communities and their interactions with immune mediators, metabolic and neuroendocrine hormones, and their receptors. Collectively, the data presented during the symposium reinforced the understanding that health and disease are the result of the (im)balance of a tightly interconnected network rather than isolated axes. This was illustrated using examples of inflammatory and infectious diseases of the brain, mouth, gynaecologic tract, lungs, as well as of metabolic and mental states. Finally, a roundtable discussion on the current state of clinical trials in nutrition, including challenges and solutions was featured. The conclusion indicated that there is room for new developments and that hurdles need to be overcome, requiring continued collaboration across scientific disciplines.

titre: Wounded Boys, Violent Men? Exploring Risk Factors for Intimate Partner Violence among Perpetrators with a History of Trauma
resume: One of the key challenges for enhancing the effectiveness of intervention programs for intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetrators is tailoring interventions to participants' specific risks and needs. A history of childhood or adolescent exposure to family violence as either a direct victim or witness has been consistently associated with an increased risk of IPV perpetration in adulthood. This study examined differences between 1,126 court-mandated male IPV perpetrators with and without a history of family violence exposure during childhood or adolescence across sociodemographic, individual, social-relational, attitudinal, and violence-related variables. The study also examined whether trauma history was associated with IPV recidivism risk beyond sociodemographic characteristics and after accounting for individual, social-relational, and attitudinal factors. Compared to perpetrators without trauma exposure, those with a trauma history were younger, had lower educational attainment, included a higher proportion of immigrant participants, and reported higher impulsivity, anger, depressive symptoms, alexithymia, and substance use. They also reported more stressful life events, lower perceived family and friend support, and higher hostile sexism and victim-blaming attitudes. In addition, they reported greater physical and psychological IPV, a more advanced stage of change, and higher risk of IPV recidivism at intake. Hierarchical logistic regression analyses showed that younger age, unemployment, higher impulsivity, and lower perceived family social support were the variables most strongly associated with trauma history. Hierarchical linear regression analyses further revealed that trauma history remained significantly associated with IPV recidivism risk after accounting for covariates. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating trauma-informed strategies into IPV perpetrator interventions.

titre: A Network-Informed Perspective on Targeting the Urge to Tic With Deep Brain Stimulation of the Centromedian-Parafascicular
resume: BACKGROUND: Premonitory urges precede tics in Tourette Syndrome (TS) and are usually transiently relieved after tic execution. Despite the proposal that premonitory urges arise through aberrant interoceptive signaling, relatively little is known about their underlying mechanisms or how they respond to treatment. The centromedian-parafascicular complex (CM-Pf) is a proposed target for deep brain stimulation (DBS) in medically refractory TS on the basis of the convergence of limbic and sensorimotor corticostriatal pathways. The CM-Pf also contributes to processing the affective and motivational dimensions of pain. METHODS AND MATERIALS: In this narrative review, we explore how the intersection between CM-Pf connectivity, pain-processing, and interoceptive function supports investigation of DBS at the CM-Pf complex as a potential modulator of both premonitory urges and tics in TS. RESULTS: Neural structures associated with premonitory urges overlap with interoceptive and pain-processing pathways and may be part of a broader "urge-for-action" network. On the basis of its structural and functional connectivity, the CM-Pf appears to link paralimbic and motor circuits, helping to facilitate the transition from internal bodily sensations (ie, urges) to action (ie, tics). Existing but limited evidence shows that CM-Pf DBS in TS can improve both urges and tics and that modulation of urge-related structures may be important to its mechanism of action. CONCLUSIONS: Premonitory urge-related circuitry is a relevant therapeutic substrate in TS. Further dedicated exploration of CM-Pf DBS in TS is warranted to better understand its capacity to address urge and tic symptoms and the mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects.
revue: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society

titre: Effectiveness and Safety of Cannabis on Anxiety Treatment Outcomes: A Systematic Review
resume: OBJECTIVE: We assessed controlled non-interventional studies and randomized clinical trials (RCTs) evaluating THC-containing cannabis' safety and effectiveness for anxiety. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, APA PsychInfo, and Cochrane databases in February 2023 for clinical studies that reported patient-level controlled quantitative assessments of anxiety outcomes following cannabis treatment. Exclusion criteria included: publication before 2000, in non-English language, assessment of topical treatment or containing <0.3% tetrahydrocannabinol, and FDA-approved products. We assessed risk of bias via RoB2/ROBINS-I, and rated evidence quality using the GRADE approach. PROSPERO:CRD42023411999. RESULTS: From 6,453 search records, 4 RCTs and 1 observational study met inclusion criteria. All studies involved patients with severe comorbid medical conditions, with anxiety assessed as a secondary outcome, limiting generalizability to primary anxiety disorders. Interventions included THC-rich cannabis oil for fibromyalgia, cannabinoids for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), cannabidiol (CBD)-enriched extracts for Parkinson's disease, nabiximols (THC:CBD 1:1) for multiple sclerosis (MS), and cannabis for chronic non-cancer pain. Anxiety was measured via self-reported scales. Due to heterogeneity in anxiety measures, results were synthesized narratively. Compared with placebo, the OCD RCT showed significant anxiety worsening [4.31 (1.70, 6.92)]; the Parkinson's disease RCT non-significant improvement [-0.82 (-1.97, 0.33)], and the fibromyalgia and MS RCTs show no significant effects [0.38 (-2.91, 3.67); -2.00 (-7.51, 3.51)]. The pain observational study reported no initial significant effect on anxiety -0.30 (-1.53, 0.93). Quality of life (QoL) worsened with THC in Parkinson's [-0.14 (-0.23, -0.04)] and showed non-significant improvement in MS [0.35 (-1.09, 1.79)]. The evidence quality was rated low to moderate. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on THC-containing cannabis' effects on anxiety is limited and inconsistent, with heterogeneous measures and mixed findings preventing meaningful quantitative synthesis. Across studies, no consistent evidence of benefit was observed. Higher-quality studies with standardized outcomes are needed to clarify their impact on anxiety and quality of life. Evidence quality was rated as low to moderate, driven by small sample sizes, short durations, and limited generalizability.

titre: Remission rates and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation in inflammatory bowel disease in adult patients: A systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is a chronic gastrointestinal disorder that substantially impairs quality of life. Conventional therapies are often limited by suboptimal efficacy, adverse effects, and diminishing response over time. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has emerged as a therapeutic strategy aimed at restoring microbial balance, reducing inflammation, and improving outcomes. OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate clinical remission rates and safety profiles of FMT in IBD. DESIGN: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials, controlled clinical trials, and observational studies, reported in accordance with the PRISMA-2020 guideline. DATA SOURCES AND METHODS: Searches were conducted in Google Scholar (November 17, 2024) and Scopus (November 19, 2024). Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, controlled clinical trials, and observational studies published after 2015 that reported remission and/or safety outcomes in adult IBD patients. Reviews, protocols, pediatric or animal studies, non-English publications, and non-peer-reviewed sources were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted Cochrane approach, with common concerns relating to blinding and subjective outcome assessment. RESULTS: From 309 records, 22 studies met inclusion criteria. Mean remission rates were 46.6% for FMT via colonoscopy (41.75% for CD and 47.17 for UC), and 58.13% for alternative routes (capsules, enemas, tubes), yielding an overall mean remission of 47.61%. Adverse events were generally mild gastrointestinal symptoms; serious events were rare, including infections and procedure-related complications. CONCLUSION: FMT, particularly via colonoscopy, appears effective and generally safe for IBD. However, heterogeneity in donor selection and protocols, limited long-term data, and English-language restriction constrain generalizability. Larger, standardized, and longer-term trials are needed to consolidate evidence. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered post-study at INPLASY registration number: INPLASY202620020, and no formal protocol was prepared; conducted as a coursework project but adhered to prespecified criteria and PRISMA-2020 reporting. Consequently, no amendments were made to the information provided at registration or in the protocol.

titre: Effects of bile acids and gut microbiota interactions on neurological and psychiatric disorders
resume: The gut-brain axis, as a bidirectional communication network connecting the gut microbiota to the central nervous system, plays a key role in a variety of neurological and psychiatric disease processes. In recent years, researchers have discovered that bile acids (BAs) are important signaling molecules that extend beyond their traditional role in lipid digestion and absorption. They are now known to play a significant role in regulating metabolism, immunity, and nervous system functions. Notably, gut microbes dynamically regulate BA profile through deconjugation, dehydroxylation, and other biotransformations, building a complex regulatory network of microbial-host co-metabolism, which in turn modulates gut-brain axis function through multiple receptors. Specifically, BAs precisely regulate neuroimmune homeostasis, dynamic balance of the blood-brain barrier, and neurotransmitter metabolism through the activation of membrane and nuclear receptors, such as farnesoid X receptor (FXR), takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5), pregnane X receptor (PXR), vitamin D receptor (VDR), and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 2 (S1PR2), a mechanism that provides a new perspective for elucidating the pathogenesis of neurological and psychiatric diseases. In this review, we systematically elucidate the microbial regulatory mechanisms of BA metabolism, focusing on the pathways through which BA-gut microbiota interactions affect neurological and psychiatric disorders via the neuroimmune pathway. By integrating the latest research evidence, we systematically sort out the key signaling pathways mediated by BA receptors and their neuroimmune regulatory networks, and provide a theoretical framework for the development of targeted intervention strategies for psychiatric disorders based on the regulation of the gut-brain axis.

titre: Development and Initial Clinical Evaluation of a Stress-Induced Computerized Bowel Sound Analysis System for Irritable Bowel Syndrome
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is diagnosed using symptom-based criteria because no established physiological test objectively supports the diagnosis. We developed and evaluated a computerized bowel sound analysis system incorporating a dichotic listening task as a psychological stress challenge in three phases. In Phase 1, a short-time energy (STE)-based bowel sound extraction algorithm showed high sensitivity and specificity in technical evaluation. In Phase 2, six individuals with IBS and 10 healthy controls underwent two dichotic listening conditions in a randomized crossover study. Bowel sounds and heart-rate variability were recorded during consecutive 10-min resting, stress-loading, and recovery periods. Despite no significant between-condition differences, the condition showing numerical LF and HF increases during stress loading in participants with IBS was selected exploratorily. Using this condition, Phase 3 evaluated 15 individuals with IBS and 38 healthy controls. The percentage change in STE from rest to stress loading (rest-to-stress ΔSTE) showed an AUC of 0.79 (95% confidence interval, 0.66-0.91), with 0.80 sensitivity and 0.68 specificity at an exploratory cutoff of 20.1%. Computerized bowel sound analysis during psychological stress showed preliminary potential as a non-invasive physiological adjunct for distinguishing IBS from healthy controls. Validation in larger independent cohorts is required. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 503-518, August, 2026.
revue: The journal of medical investigation : JMI

titre: Therapeutic Role of Probiotics in Regulating Mental Health: Gut-Brain Cross-Talk
resume: The gastrointestinal tract harbors a diverse microbial community, including bacteria, archaea, and protozoa, which play pivotal roles in maintaining host gut health. Probiotics, comprising nonpathogenic microorganisms administered in appropriate doses, have garnered attention for their therapeutic potential in promoting overall human health. They bolster antipathogenic defenses, enhance immune function, and ameliorate gastrointestinal disorders like irritable bowel syndrome. The intricate interplay between diet, gut microbiota, and mental health is well-documented, with numerous studies highlighting the impact of food consumption on stress levels and cognitive function. Preclinical and clinical investigations have elucidated the therapeutic effects of probiotics and prebiotics in managing various mental disorders, including depression, autism spectrum disorders, and fibromyalgia syndrome. Emerging research underscores the role of psychobiotics, a class of probiotic microbes with psychotropic properties, in alleviating psychiatric distress. Furthermore, synbiotics, combining live microorganisms with substrates, hold promise in modulating gut microbiota and mitigating stress, depression, and anxiety. This review aims to explore the intricate communication pathways between the gut and brain and their implications for disease pathology.
revue: Journal of environmental pathology, toxicology and oncology : official organ of the International Society for Environmental Toxicology and Cancer

titre: Probiotics, Prebiotics, Synbiotics and the Gut-Brain Axis in Precision Health
resume: The gastrointestinal system synthesizes a considerable proportion of the body's neurotransmitters and neuromodulators and is consequently increasingly acknowledged as the "second brain." Advances in high-throughput sequencing technology following the Human Genome Project have considerably expanded understanding of the gut microbiome, igniting increasing interest in microbiota-based medicinal approaches. Probiotics, defined as live microorganisms offering health benefits when provided in suitable doses, have proven potential in the management of chronic inflammatory and immune-mediated illnesses through immunomodulatory and barrier-protective pathways. The therapeutic efficacy of probiotics is strain-specific and influenced by dosage, host physiology, and environmental factors; consequently, strain selection prioritizes functional attributes such as gastrointestinal survivability, adhesion to intestinal epithelium, modulation of resident microbiota, and antimicrobial activity. Despite promising clinical and preclinical evidence, comprehensive elucidation of the systemic effects of probiotics and identification of novel symbiotic strains remain critical research priorities, underscoring the need for interdisciplinary collaboration between pharmacologists and microbiologists.Another highly integral aspect of nutrition and medical research involves prebiotics. Prebiotics are defined as selectively fermentable substances that promote the activity and number of beneficial microbes in the gastrointestinal region. Oligosaccharides and inulin are examples that add to the betterment of metabolic homeostasis and immune system functioning. The rising consumer education and innovation have led to large-scale expansion in the prebiotics industry, which strengthens the connection between microbiology, nutrition, and health economics.Synbiotics that combine both probiotics and prebiotics represent a cutting-edge strategy that can enhance the resistance and stability of gut microbiota, especially in the gut-brain axis (GBA) microbiota network. New multiomics approaches have revealed the intricate relationships that exist between the microbiota and the host that modulate neuropathological, metabolic, and immunological outcomes. There is a great variation in the microbial populations and corresponding metabolic products among different human subjects that clearly reveals the need to develop microbiota-targeting therapies.
revue: Advances in experimental medicine and biology

titre: The role of interoceptive and sensory engagement in mindfulness-based cognitive therapy
resume: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy's targeting of rumination follows the accepted neuroscience that characterizes depression vulnerability as due to increased activity in the brain's frontal regions, leading to overthinking and self-reference. Relying on frontal brain regions to solve emotional problems has the unintended consequence of limiting new information coming from our senses. While prefrontal brain function is certainly important, recent work suggests that it is precisely this sensory inhibition that locks our minds into states of suffering when alternatives are present. Sense foraging represents a framework for viewing interoceptive awareness as an important complement to the changes in cognitive processing that are associated with MBCT. Leveraging the ubiquity of sensory phenomena, Sense Foraging offers people multiple access points for engagement with contemplative mindsets and may seed sustained informal practices.

titre: Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Subgroup Analyses of Standard and Adapted Approaches
resume: Depression has ranked as one of the major complications after stroke, which reduced participation in rehabilitation, increased recurrence rate and mortality. Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) has been used in treating post-stroke depressive symptoms, although evidence regarding the effectiveness of CBT interventions for post-stroke depressive symptoms remains heterogeneous. Meanwhile, standard CBT typically involves structured cognitive restructuring and multiple therapeutic components, which may place considerable cognitive and practical demands on stroke survivors; several CBT-adapted interventions have been increasingly applied. Determining effectiveness of CBT intervention for post-stroke depressive symptoms and effectiveness of standard and adapted approaches for post-stroke depressive symptoms is warranted. This review was registered with PROSPERO (REG# CRD420251270950). PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched. Standardized mean differences (SMDs), and the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the random effects model. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool was used. Altogether, 11 studies with 994 participants with post-stroke depressive symptoms were included and analysed. CBT interventions were associated with a significant reduction in post-stroke depressive symptoms compared with control conditions (SMD = -1.00, 95% CI -1.61 to -0.39, p = 0.001), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 95%). In subgroup analyses, adapted CBT showed a significant pooled effect (SMD = -1.16, 95% CI -1.92 to -0.40, p = 0.003; I2 = 94%), whereas the pooled effect of Standard CBT did not reach statistical significance (SMD = -0.58, 95% CI -1.52 to 0.36, p = 0.23; I2 = 93%). However, the test for subgroup differences showed no statistically significant difference between standard and adapted CBT (p = 0.35; I2 = 0%). CBT interventions may help reduce depressive symptoms after stroke. Although adapted CBT showed a statistically significant pooled effect, the test for subgroup differences did not indicate a significant difference between adapted and standard CBT. Given the substantial heterogeneity across studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further well-designed randomized controlled trials are warranted.

titre: The Effects of Mindfulness-Based Programs on Pain-Related Cognitions in Individuals With Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
resume: OBJECTIVES: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is a complex condition influenced by psychological factors, including pain-related cognitions. This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials aimed to evaluate the effects of mindfulness-based programs on pain-related cognitions in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, psychological distress, pain intensity, disability, intervention adherence, and mindfulness-related adverse events. METHODS: Eight databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Evidence was synthesized using random-effects models and reported as standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk of bias tool. Evidence certainty was rated using GRADE. RESULTS: Fifty-one studies (n = 5997) were included and had a moderate-to-high risk of bias. Compared to no intervention, mindfulness-based programs reduced pain catastrophizing (SMD: 1.00, 95% CI: 0.56-1.45) and increased pain acceptance (SMD: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.31-1.92) post-intervention. They also reduced depression (SMD: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.50-1.38), anxiety (SMD: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.57-1.59), psychological distress (SMD: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.12-1.38), pain intensity (SMD: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.38-1.23), and disability (SMD: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.04-0.92) compared to no intervention. Minimal significant differences were observed between the effect of mindfulness-based programs and cognitive behavioral therapy on these outcomes. DISCUSSION: Mindfulness-based programs appear to be an effective self-management strategy for individuals with chronic musculoskeletal pain. However, the certainty of evidence is mostly low with intervention adherence varying. Future research should clarify the direction and nature of the relationship between adherence and outcomes. Reporting of mindfulness-related adverse events was insufficient to evaluate safety; future trials should incorporate comprehensive measurement.

titre: Effects of Group-Based CBT/ERP and ACT on Emotion Dysregulation, Sleep, Anxiety Sensitivity and Psychological Flexibility in Adults With OCD
resume: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention (CBT/ERP) is the recommended first-line psychological treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) has emerged as a promising alternative, yet treatment comparisons have primarily focused on symptom severity and even less is known about their effects on other domains. STUDY AIM: We examined the effect of group-based ACT and CBT/ERP on emotion regulation, anxiety sensitivity, insomnia and psychological flexibility in adults with OCD. METHODS: 176 adults with OCD were randomized to CBT/ERP or ACT and assessed with the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), Sleep Condition Indicator (SCI), Anxiety Sensitivity Index-Revised (ASI-R) and Acceptance and Action Questionnaire for Obsessions and Compulsions (AAQ-OC) at baseline, post-treatment, 6-month and 12-month follow-up and analysed with Mixed-Model Repeated Measures (MMRM). RESULTS: Both treatments showed similar improvements in the four domains across timepoints. CONCLUSIONS: In line with our hypotheses, our results indicated that ACT may be non-inferior to CBT/ERP for all secondary outcomes. However, as the trial was powered for the primary outcome (symptom severity) rather than for these secondary measures, our findings should be interpreted as suggestive. Nonetheless, these findings add to the growing evidence that ACT may be considered a viable treatment for OCD.

titre: Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders in the Middle East and North Africa Region: A Scoping Review
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive and related disorders (OCRDs) are often underdiagnosed and undertreated despite their negative impact. They include obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), hoarding disorder, trichotillomania and excoriation disorder. AIM: This scoping review aims to map the current evidence on OCRDs in the MENA region and identify research patterns and gaps. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted according to JBI and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, ProQuest, Embase, among other databases were searched from inception through June 2025, using OCRD and MENA-related terms. Eligible studies were those conducted in MENA countries and involved individuals with DSM-5-defined OCRDs and were published in Arabic or English. RESULTS: Of 6174 identified articles, 393 articles across 13 countries, published between 1991 and 2025, were included. Research was highly concentrated in Iran (n = 304). Most articles were cross-sectional, randomized controlled trials, or case-control studies. Sample sizes ranged from 6 to 29,858 participants (median ≈ 106.5, mean ≈ 407). OCD accounted for the majority of clinical samples, followed by BDD. Therapeutic studies (n = 142) encompassed pharmacological, psychotherapeutic and neuromodulation interventions, while epidemiological studies (n = 136) primarily examined OCD and BDD characteristics. Other emerging themes included cognitive mechanisms and symptomatology diagnostic, psychometric and qualitative studies. CONCLUSION: The evidence indicates a growing but uneven body of OCRD research across the MENA region. The evidence is substantially concentrated in Iran, highlighting important geographic disparities. Key gaps include generating evidence from underrepresented countries and conditions. In addition to culturally adapted diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks and region-specific policy development.

titre: [Multi-locus rTMS in Tourettic obsessive-compulsive disorder]
resume: We present the case of a 27-year-old woman with Tourettic obsessive-compulsive disorder (TOCS), a condition characterized by symptoms across the spectrum of tics and compulsions. Pharmacological treatment was associated with disabling side effects and, together with psychotherapeutic interventions, resulted only in temporary improvement. Given the treatment-resistant nature of the disorder and its substantial impact on the patient’s quality of life, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) was initiated using a symptom-oriented multi-locus protocol. Sequential stimulation was applied to the orbitofrontal cortex and the supplementary motor cortex. This approach led to an almost complete remission of TOCS symptoms, with stable effects maintained up to seven years after treatment initiation. This case highlights the potential of rTMS as an effective and safe therapeutic approach within the Tourettic-compulsive spectrum and underscores the relevance of symptom-targeted multi-locus rTMS protocols.

titre: [Empowering families in OCD treatment: a scoping review]
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder impairs social, academic, and family functioning. Cognitive behavioral therapy with exposure and response prevention is the most effective treatment, but many patients remain symptomatic. Family accommodation and maladaptive family dynamics influence treatment outcomes. AIM: An overview of the outcomes of interventions with family involvement and advice for families. METHOD: We searched the literature on 21 July 2024 to identify interventions with family involvement. Given the heterogeneity of the available literature and the exploratory nature of the research question, a scoping review was conducted. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies were included. All studies with family involvement reported statistically significant reductions in OCD symptom severity. Commonly used advice included psychoeducation, reducing family accommodation, supporting exposure exercises, reward systems, supportive and motivational approaches, open communication, emotion regulation, joint problem solving, improving family interactions and functioning, self-care, and relapse prevention. CONCLUSION: The strategies and advice used in the various studies often included the same components. More research is necessary to specifically evaluate the impact of practical advice, with detailed descriptions of how recommendations can be most effectively implemented.

titre: [Application of perioperative bundled nursing measures in robot assisted radical prostatectomy]
resume: Objective To evaluate the application effect of perioperative cluster nursing interventions in patients undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. Methods A total of 122 prostate cancer patients who underwent robot-assisted surgery from January 2023 to December 2024 were divided into the control group (routine care, 55 cases) and the observation group (cluster nursing, 67 cases) according to the nursing methods. The psychological status, surgery-related indicators, postoperative recovery, incidence of perioperative complications, and patient satisfaction were compared between the two groups. Results The observation group demonstrated a statistically significant decrease in postoperative anxiety and depression scores compared to the control group (P=0.034, P=0.005). The observation group exhibited shorter operative time and less intraoperative blood loss, with both differences being statistically significant (P=0.016, P<0.001). In terms of postoperative recovery, the observation group showed faster recovery of bowel function, shorter time for catheter insertion and postoperative hospital stay compared to the control group (P=0.010, P<0.001, P<0.001). In the observation group，the incidence of systemic postoperative infection was lower than that of the control group (4.5% vs 18.2%, P=0.015). The perioperative hypothermia rate in the observation group was lower than that of the control group (38.8% vs 60.0%, P=0.020). There was no statistically significant difference in postoperative urinary fistula rate between the two groups (P=0.477). The observation group achieved an overall patient satisfaction rate of 98.51%, with higher satisfaction scores compared to the control group (P=0.008).Conclusion Perioperative cluster nursing measures yield favorable outcomes in patients undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. It can not only shorten the operation time, promote the postoperative recovery of patients, but also reduce the anxiety and depression of patients and complications, and improve patient satisfaction.
revue: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology

titre: Therapeutic Alliance is Linked With Suicidality Trajectories in Psychotherapy for Late-Life Depression
resume: OBJECTIVES: Late-life suicidality is rapidly increasing; psychotherapy may reduce suicidality, but trajectories of change in suicidality remain unclear. A strong therapeutic alliance may protect against persistent suicidality. We examined the association of alliance with suicidality trajectories during brief, remote interventions for depression. METHODS: Sixty middle-aged and older adults with major depression were randomized to brief remote psychosocial interventions. Suicidality and alliance were assessed during treatment. Patients' suicidality trajectories were classified as: 1) absent; 2) improved; 3) persistent, based on pre- to post-treatment changes. All three groups were included in mixed-effects models to examine the association between suicidality and alliance. RESULTS: At baseline, 53% of patients endorsed suicidality, with 45% in the absent group, 45% improved, and 10% persistent. Patients in the absent and improved groups showed stable, strong alliance while the persistent group showed worsening alliance. CONCLUSION: Simple, remote psychosocial interventions are promising first-line treatments for late-life suicidality. A strong alliance may reduce suicidality and enhance outcomes, guiding timely, personalized interventions.
revue: The American journal of geriatric psychiatry : official journal of the American Association for Geriatric Psychiatry

fiche.intervention: Interventions psychosociales brèves et à distance pour la dépression
resultats_cles: 53% présentaient une suicidnalité au départ (45% sans, 45% améliorés, 10% persistants).
Les groupes sans suicidnalité et améliorés montrent une alliance forte et stable.
Le groupe persistant montre une dégradation de l'alliance thérapeutique.
fiche.conclusion: Une alliance forte peut réduire la suicidnalité et améliorer les issues thérapeutiques.
fiche.pertinence_raison: Souligne l'impact clinique crucial de l'alliance thérapeutique en visio/présentiel.

fiche.conclusion_simple: Maintenir une alliance forte est essentiel pour réduire la suicidnalité en psychothérapie.
